in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the european council of 8 and 9 december and on the new intergovernmental treaty under preparation. however, i have reservations about three points. firstly, i do not share the doubts about the need for the treaty. its main objectives - including the incorporation of the golden rule of budgetary balance into the domestic law of the member states - could not be achieved within the framework of the eu treaties. secondly, i fully agree that the implementation of the new treaty at union level should be left to the institutions themselves in accordance with the community method. but i cannot dismiss the constitutional problem of using the eu institutions, created by the respective treaties, to implement a treaty outside them, which does not bind all the member states. thirdly, i entirely agree with the idea that the treaty should provide for genuine budgetary union and genuine economic union, but i think that among the missing points (redemption fund, project bonds, financial transaction tax, road map for stability bonds) there should also be a minimum of tax harmonization, without which there can be no level playing field in the internal market.
in writing. − the pressure on the euro area makes it urgent to adopt measures to respond firmly, sustainably and effectively to the current economic, financial and social crisis. in this context, it is crucial that solutions are found that can restore market confidence while safeguarding the values, principles and institutional framework on which the european project is based. in this context, it should be recognised that the new treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union, which is to be agreed on 30 january and involves the leaders of all the member states except the united kingdom, is far from the ideal solution, as it represents a strengthening of the intergovernmental aspect to the detriment of the community method. however, it is important to maintain a constructive attitude here, and the european parliament should do everything possible to seek to deepen the community framework of this treaty and to extend its scope so that, alongside budgetary discipline, it can also include an agenda for growth and solidarity between the member states. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the food chain is not affected by the food crisis. i also thank all the political groups who supported this oral question and who worked diligently on the final text of this resolution. this resolution responds to the long-delayed expectations of farmers to counteract the growing imbalance in the food chain, both in terms of the bargaining power between the parties and in terms of the distribution of income. this has been caused by a high concentration of the largest distribution operators in europe and threatens the survival of farms and suppliers in general, with serious damage to the agricultural economy and rural societies. in this context, the proposed path is to unequivocally identify bad practices in the food chain, support their self-regulation by joint action by all those involved, require appropriate legislation by the european commission, without neglecting the necessary performance of the member states at this level, supervision and application of sanctions. the community legislation which is to be adopted must take account of previous decisions of the european parliament, both those which have been implemented and those which have not yet been implemented, together with the responses which are considered appropriate here in the context of the current situation in contractual relations between producers, suppliers and distributors. this resolution is not against any of the partners in the food chain, but is in favour of closer relations between them and the implementation of dialogue, so that everyone's contribution is required. this resolution opposes the unfair and abusive practices which are taking hold and is in favour of introducing appropriate community and national legislation where necessary and without distorting the proper functioning of markets. it is hoped that this will encourage greater organisational capacity among producers and the abandonment of dominant practices by the distributor, such as the unilateral imposition of contractual conditions or discounting practices, without increasing the price to the consumer, but rather contributing to a wider and better quality of effective choice for the consumer. we now have to wait for the european commission to take the necessary initiative.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the crisis. the numbers speak for themselves. according to eurostat, in the last decade, while factor costs have increased by 40%, prices have not exceeded 25%. but it is not just upstream that farmers are being completely crushed. farmers downstream are also obliged to accept prices, payment terms and other contractual conditions that are unimaginable given the disproportionate balance of forces in the trade chain. i give the example of my own country, where the cooperative sector has little expression. the five main groups account for about 65% of the marketing of food products, with much higher figures in some sectors, such as milk. just last week, in my country, authorities seized 400,000 litres of milk from a supermarket chain that was being sold below cost. as policy-makers, we need to ensure that agriculture remains a viable activity in europe, producing good quality food and raw materials at fair prices and good returns for farmers. this requires a good common agricultural policy, but also the guarantee of fair competition, as referred to in the treaty. i therefore urge the commission and the council to give urgent effect to the recommendations and suggestions made in the resolutions we are discussing here today and to put forward concrete proposals as soon as possible.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because i consider that it is intended to clarify in practical terms, both for passengers and for airlines, the rules on transit through the international areas of airports, in order to contribute to greater transparency and legal certainty. it is intended that third-country nationals holding valid visas or residence permits issued by a member state which does not yet apply the full schengen provisions should be exempted from the requirement of an airport stopover visa.
in writing. − a common visa policy is essential to facilitate legitimate travel by third-country nationals and to provide for the implementation of measures to facilitate the application and processing of visa applications, such as simplification of the issuing procedure, cost reduction, use of multiple-entry visas, provision of more appropriate validity periods, etc. the community visa code, established in 2009, was the decisive factor in bringing greater coherence to the common visa policy by allowing all the provisions governing the issuing of visas and decisions on refusal, extension, annulment, revocation and reduction of visas to be integrated into a single code. i support this proposal which introduces a mere technical amendment, but one of great practical relevance both for passengers and for airlines, aimed at clarifying the rules on transit through the international areas of airports in order to contribute to greater transparency and legal certainty. it is therefore envisaged that third-country nationals holding valid visas or residence permits issued by a member state which does not yet apply the schengen provisions in full will be exempted from the requirement of an airport stopover visa.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates the implementation of a community visa code which clarifies the rules on the movement of passengers making a stopover in the international areas of airports. this clarification, which is of a technical nature, removes the requirement for european passengers to have an airport stopover visa. these measures contribute to greater legal certainty and to the reduction of ancillary bureaucracy.
in writing. - this proposal is limited to a technical amendment involving the clarification of the pre-existing text so as to make it explicit that third-country nationals holding valid visas or residence permits issued by a member state which does not fully apply the common visa policy are covered by the vat exemption and that it also covers persons holding a visa when travelling to the third country issuing the visa, to any other third country, and when, having used the visa, returning from the third country issuing it. the result of the vote in committee confirms the consensual nature of this matter and reinforces my non-opposition to this amendment.
in writing. the report by mr louis michel is on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 810/2009 of 13 july 2009 laying down the community code on visas, commonly known as the visa code. the ep has been concerned to reduce the administrative and bureaucratic burden on european citizens, in particular by facilitating the mobility of people and eliminating the duplication of checks which do not jeopardise the safety of persons and property. the commission's proposal is limited to a technical amendment to clarify that third-country nationals holding valid visas or residence permits issued by a member state which does not apply the schengen acquis in full (the united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, bulgaria and romania) are exempt from the requirement to present an airport stopover visa, without changing the practices adopted by the member states. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report proposes a technical correction of practical importance for certain types of passengers, who will thus be exempted from a second check, unnecessary in the face of the previous check which entitled them to a visa. as a correction which does not change the practices in use by the member states but which is only intended to make life easier for passengers and to reduce the administrative burden on the member states, we voted in favour.

in writing. in this report, vital moreira analyses the recommendation on the draft council decision on the signing of an agreement between the european union and georgia on the protection of geographical indications (gi) for agricultural products and foodstuffs. although georgia only joined the world trade organisation (wto) in 2000, a partnership and cooperation agreement between the eu and georgia has existed since 1 july 1999. following an ancestral tradition, gi's aim to identify the origin, quality and characteristics of certain products, linking them to the land where they are produced, in order to guarantee their reputation. i voted in favour of this draft recommendation because i believe that both georgia and the eu, particularly its farmers, will benefit greatly from having the characteristics of their products (cheeses, fats, bakery and pastry products, fruit, vegetables, cereals, fresh meat and meat products, fresh fish and seafood, wine, spirits and beer) recognised and protected. i also welcome the strengthening of trade relations between the eu and georgia.
in writing. - geographical indications (gi) are an instrument designed to protect certain names which identify products with a special link to their territory of origin. gi indications are indications identifying a product as originating in a given territory, where a particular quality, reputation or other characteristic of the product can essentially be attributed to its geographical origin. in the current international context, marked by the deregulation and liberalisation of world trade, the standardisation of production methods, the intensification and homogenisation of production, the consequent loss of traditional production methods and products and the reduction of biodiversity in its many aspects, gi's are an instrument that can help to preserve and respect the characteristics and quality of certain local and regional productions. we support the establishment of gi for various agricultural products such as cheeses, fruit, vegetables, cereals, meat, fish and shellfish, bakery and pastry products, wines and spirits from various eu countries (23) and georgia. but it is important to remember that this instrument is not the panacea for the evils of trade deregulation. what is needed is to challenge the dogma of free trade. unfortunately, the rapporteur insists (even in this report) on opening the door to it.

in writing. the international civil aviation organization (icao) was established by the 1944 chicago convention as a specialized agency of the united nations. the signatory states shall cooperate in the fields of aviation safety, air traffic management and environmental protection. this memorandum of cooperation (moc) aims to formalise and enhance the relations between the european union and the international civil aviation organisation, ensuring greater harmonisation of standards and better coordination of their activities. the mc aims at a better use of available resources, avoiding duplication of effort and preserving the integrity of the parties. the parties agree to cooperate closely with a view to coordinating their activities in the field of security. this cooperation includes provisions for the eu to make specialised expertise and resources available to the international civil aviation organisation, and eu observers may participate in icao audit missions in eu states with the agreement of the latter and in the strictest respect of the confidentiality of audit missions. i therefore support this recommendation.

in writing. - i welcome the new rules on the collection and recycling of electrical and electronic equipment adopted today by the european parliament. these new rules will improve the collection and recycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment and prevent its illegal transfer to other countries. to this end, eu countries will have to increase the collection and recycling of waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee).
in writing. − i am pleased to note that the waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) directive 2002/96/ec has been subject to an extensive review to correct the inconsistent and contradictory elements contained therein. i consider the objectives identified by the rapporteur to be relevant and essential for the better performance of the directive. the review therefore aims to eliminate excessive and unnecessary bureaucratic burdens (technical, legal and administrative problems) which result in costly efforts by market players and member states, continuous environmental damage, reduced innovation in waste collection and treatment, lack of a level playing field or even distortion of competition. of the various objectives listed in the report, i would like to highlight those which carry the most weight, namely cost reduction through the elimination of all unnecessary red tape without compromising environmental safety; further efforts to make the weee directive more effective and applicable through an increase in the rate of compliance and reduction of parasitism; and finally reducing the impact of the collection, treatment and recovery of weee on the environment in order to maximise the net benefit to society.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in the european union. this revision was necessary for two main reasons which are explained in the report. firstly, the experience gained in implementing the directive since it entered into force and the fact that it identified some shortcomings in its architecture and implementation. secondly, waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) is the waste that has grown the most in the union and therefore faces a number of new challenges. the amendments now agreed will make the directive more effective, reduce red tape, increase its applicability and protect the environment, and for that i obviously voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on waste electrical and electronic equipment, because it contains important measures to better manage this waste and thus protect the environment and combat climate change, by setting high collection and recycling rates, as well as strict rules to combat illegal exports and hold producers accountable.
in writing. − waste electrical and electronic equipment has grown exponentially across the union and its treatment and conversion is now a particularly important problem in the european context. in addition to the environmental and public health concerns, which are of concern in themselves, the non-reuse of raw materials leads to inefficiency and additional costs for the production system, which could be offset by better use of the materials used in the equipment in question. i hope that the european union will make increasingly rational use of electronic and electrical machinery and equipment and that it will be able to reuse them in an environmentally safe and socially responsible way.
in writing. − the exponential growth of the market for electrical and electronic equipment (eee) in recent decades (especially mobile phones, computers and televisions), due to technological innovations and very aggressive promotional campaigns, has led to an increase in the tonnes of waste from this equipment, which, not being collected separately, end up in open landfills or exported illegally. this situation, in addition to the environmental problems it causes (threatening human health), is a huge waste of materials - some of them noble like gold, platinum and silver - that could contribute to the recovery of the world economy and reduce the extraction of natural resources. this recommendation for second reading, drawn up by mr karl-heinz florenz, concerns the council's position at first reading on the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on such waste. since it is imperative to implement measures to encourage the separate collection, recycling and/or recovery of these materials, i voted in favour of this report and i hope that the new directive will be implemented as soon as possible, thus helping to improve public health and prevent the illegal export of weee to countries where there is no environmental control.
in writing. − this is the final stage of the adoption of a directive laying down measures to protect the environment and human health by preventing or reducing adverse impacts arising from the generation and management of waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee). the reality is that waste flows are increasing across the european union and that it is therefore necessary to put in place approaches to waste collection and treatment with the aim of increasing recycling and reuse, particularly as regards secondary raw materials. the directive extends its scope to all eea states unless explicitly excluded; new definitions are added to increase legal certainty and consistency with other community legislation. as regards targets, within four years member states should achieve a collection rate of 45% of weee, taking into account eee placed on the market in the last three years. the targets for recovery and combined recycling/reuse are increased by 5% over the next 3 years.
in writing. the report aims to prevent the illegal export of waste electrical and electronic equipment. in recent decades, this type of waste has been the fastest growing in the european union, and is often illegally dumped in open landfills in developing countries. this scenario aggravates the eu's development at the expense of the consumption of natural resources and the health and environment of the poorest countries. this second reading version improves the proposed legislation by introducing an improved scope, more ambitious collection and recycling targets and more stringent export regulation. consumers will be able to take very small electrical and electronic waste, such as mobile phones, to various retail outlets without the obligation to purchase new items. for these reasons i voted in favour. however, i do not think that nanomaterials should be treated as normal as other compounds, because they are extremely hazardous to health and the environment and can be equally dangerous even in the recycling process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading with a view to adopting the european parliament and council directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee). i did so because i agree with the amendments tabled by the european parliament which, always duly reasoned, promote a more balanced directive.
in writing. − directive 2002/96/ec, in force since 13 february 2003, on waste electrical and electronic equipment, is currently under review. the aim is to overcome some of the difficulties which have arisen in the meantime in applying the directive (by delimiting more clearly, for example, the scope of the text) and to strike a balance between the need to ensure uniform application of the directive and the need to maintain flexibility to respond to the specific needs of each member state. the european parliament's position is part of this effort to find balanced and appropriate solutions to these objectives. i therefore voted in favour, taking into account the recommendation for second reading by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.
in writing. − this directive aims to contribute to the reuse, recycling and recovery of waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) by aiming at sustainable production and consumption of the goods concerned. i am voting in favour of this report because it supports the development of european standards for the collection and treatment of weee, the creation of ecodesign requirements to facilitate the reuse, dismantling and recovery of weee and the treatment of goods in good environmental conditions. finally, i believe that appropriate facilities should be set up for the delivery of weee, including public collection centres, where private individuals can make a positive contribution by delivering waste. it should be noted that the costs should be passed on to the price of the products, rather than being borne by european taxpayers.
in writing. - i am voting in favour because this report contributes, through the sustainable use of biocidal products, to the protection of human health, animal health and the environment. i think it is particularly positive that the union now has a list of active substances which do not present any risks. i also welcome the recommendation that under certain conditions, for example in relation to more vulnerable or protected ecosystems (the azores are very committed to protecting their ecosystems and will certainly take this into account), member states may have the autonomy to refuse the use of a given biocide.
in writing. − directive 98/8/ec of 16 february 1998 establishes a regulatory and harmonised framework for the authorisation and placing on the market of biocidal products. this regulation aims to eliminate the shortcomings of that directive as regards authorisations, the improvement of the authorisation procedure and a more streamlined decision-making process, while accompanying the development of a high level of protection. the introduction of a european union authorisation system is a decisive step towards a harmonised european market for biocidal products. this regulation will contribute to greater legal certainty and transparency in the use of active substances and to ensuring a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, and will improve the functioning of the internal market by harmonising the provisions concerning the placing on the market and use of biocidal products. this regulation will also contribute to improving the protection of european consumers. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. − the introduction of a union authorisation system is a decisive step towards a harmonised european market for biocidal products. for reasons of competition and the internal market, it is necessary to establish clear and transparent rules on fees for both the agency and the member states. on the other hand, a centralised authorisation system has a positive effect on the internal market, as it allows for consistent assessments and uniform application of requirements in all member states, thus contributing to improving consumer protection.
in writing. - i am pleased to support the proposal for a regulation to amend directive 98/8/ec on the making available on the market and use of biocidal products in order to eliminate inconsistencies and contradictions. the amendments proposed by the european parliament and accepted by the council are of a technical nature, in particular as regards consistency (both in the text as a whole and between this regulation and other eu legislation), simplification of the text and the elimination of overlapping legislative obligations. i admit that it is essential to introduce a european union authorization system. this is a decisive and vital step towards a harmonised european market for biocidal products. this will undoubtedly be the best and most efficient system for improving the availability of biocidal products, encouraging innovation and obtaining additional benefits for human health and nature protection. however, i believe that there is still considerable work to be done in terms of improvement to ensure that the objectives pursued are achieved, such as the elimination of the shortcomings of the authorisation directive 98/8/ec and a more agile decision-making process, accompanied by the development of a high level of protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation for second reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the making available on the market and use of biocidal products, which will bring together in a single document some of the currently scattered european legislation, eliminate unnecessary red tape, extend the scope of union intervention to products and materials treated with biocides (in particular so-called low-risk products). it also makes product information requirements clearer and more visible (e.g. through labelling), minimises the possibility of animal testing, increases the involvement of the european chemicals agency (echa) and ensures the uniform application of these rules throughout the european union. i also congratulate my colleague, christa klass, on the political commitment she has made to the other groups in parliament, the commission and the council. i share, however, your doubts about the authorization of active substances/biocidal products, which should gradually move towards greater centralisation at union level in order to avoid overlaps and increase safety. i also agree with the rapporteur that the training of the relevant target groups, in particular professional users, should be promoted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the placing on the market and use of biocidal products, as i considered that the commitment reached includes measures to ensure the protection of human and animal health and the safe and sustainable use of these products, in particular requirements with regard to environmental and health issues, research and innovation and the internal market.
in writing. − modern life requires an increasingly constant and intensive use of biocidal products. at the same time, these products are required to be increasingly effective and aggressive, which means that their handling becomes more dangerous. therefore, the approach to regulating the placing on the market and use of bio-food products must pay particular attention to the protection of consumers/users. once again, as i have said on other occasions, the rules on this matter must be uniform and valid throughout the eu, otherwise we will not be effectively ensuring the protection of all european consumers and, not least, environmental protection.
in writing. - this recommendation for second reading, by mrs christa klaß, concerns the council's position at first reading on the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the placing on the market of biocidal products, which, in the european market alone, amount to 90 000 tonnes. biocidal products, which are products used to control harmful organisms such as bacteria and parasites, can be used to protect both human and animal health and therefore require clear regulation at the level of a framework directive to enforce their sustainable use. although their use has a very important positive effect on our lives, we must be careful to eliminate carcinogenic or infertility-causing products as well as to counteract potential side effects. the measures now adopted improve the certification process, reduce red tape and consolidate the single market through standardisation. what is permitted in a country like italy or france will also be permitted in portugal or spain. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation because it will help to protect the health of citizens and animals and to create a better environment.
in writing. − biocides are used to prevent and protect against pests and other organisms that can threaten human health. however, their uncontrolled use can also be harmful to health and the environment. this report shows some improvements on the first reading, as a result of the compromise reached in the negotiations between the groups. among the positive aspects, there is a clearer concern to ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, as well as labelling issues with non-misleading consumer information, such as in the case of the possible use of nanomaterials. the information requirements on active substances and biocidal products should take account, as the rapporteur points out, of the latest methods to avoid animal testing. however, some doubts remain about the rules on fees, both for the european chemicals agency and for the member states.
in writing. − this document updates the european rules on the authorisation, marketing and use of biocidal products in the european union, making them more restrictive and safer for the environment, public and animal health. the most toxic products, including carcinogens, gene and hormone disruptors and fertility-damaging products, will be banned. exceptions to this rule shall be permitted only if the substance is absolutely necessary to prevent or control a serious danger to public or animal health or the environment. i believe that the rules governing biocides should be governed by the public interest, taking account of human and animal health and the environment, and i voted in favour of this.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the making available on the market and use of biocidal products because the safe use of these products requires the adoption of a framework directive on the sustainable use of these products. the positive effects of the framework directive on the sustainable use of pesticides recommend the adoption of an equivalent standard for biocidal products. it is important that professional users and consumers of such products are informed about their safe use and about possible alternatives.
in writing. the council's position at first reading on the adoption of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning the making available on the market and use of biocidal products contained about half of the amendments proposed by parliament. however, following the analysis carried out by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, there are still a number of technical points which need to be improved in order to ensure the adoption of a clearer legislative text and thus more suitable for introducing effective regulation. that being the spirit of the amendments proposed by parliament in the recommendation for second reading, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the regulation applies to biocidal products which, in the form in which they are supplied to the user, contain or generate one or more active substances. i agree with this regulation, as i believe that a list of active substances which are allowed to be used in biocidal products should be drawn up and regularly evaluated in order to take account of scientific and technological progress and to inform member states in advance of the availability of the products concerned by the companies. finally, i believe that this regulation will contribute to greater legal certainty and transparency in the use of active substances, ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment and improve the functioning of the internal market by harmonising the provisions on the placing on the market and use of biocidal products.
in writing. i am in favour of this because the increase in food prices does not automatically translate into an increase in agricultural incomes and this report expresses this concern. the progressive and very significant increase in production factors has not been passed on fairly throughout the food chain and has mainly affected farmers' incomes, which creates a feeling of permanent insecurity in the exercise of agricultural activity. the situation is of particular concern to farmers in isolated regions such as the outermost regions, which already incur additional costs due to the distances and remoteness of the regions. in this sense, it is essential to promote transparency so that we can identify what is driving this scenario, promoting resilience to price volatility. only in this way will a supply chain be provided which treats all the actors in the process, and in particular farmers and consumers alike, in a more equitable way from the top down.
in writing. - i welcome the proposed measures to increase the capacity of farms and to save energy in installations, farming practices and transport. to this end, it is essential to use energy efficiency programmes and to research renewable energy production on farms or locally (wind, solar, biogas, geothermal, etc.). given the importance of water in agricultural production, the eu should support member states in providing improved water storage systems for agriculture, including improved ground water storage and water collection capacities in dry areas, as a precaution against changes in rainfall patterns due to climate change.
in writing. - i support this new own-initiative report which, in a context of deep economic and financial crisis with growing repercussions for farmers, identifies problems upstream of agricultural production, with an impact on the increase in the costs of agricultural production factors purchased in the fields of energy, machinery, compound feed, fertilisers, pesticides, seeds and water. as regards the production sector, this report also mentions the impact on farmers, who are increasingly dependent on an industry of factors of production with an increasing concentration. the aim of this report, which suggests measures to be taken in the context of the next reform of the cap, is to analyse the structures and markets which are aimed at creating new strategies to assist farmers in reducing the costs of the factors of production, taking into account their autonomy and their incomes, leading to a more efficient and sustainable use of the means of production. i also agree with the rapporteur that farmers need to be supported not only to improve their performance in the agronomic and environmental fields, but also to better respond to the climate, environmental and economic challenges, in particular by adopting greening measures, and to focus on greater resilience to climate instability, better soil health and lower susceptibility to disease.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the supply chain for agricultural products because measures are needed to tackle excessive concentration and ensure transparency in agricultural markets, so as to promote competitiveness and avoid volatility in food prices.
in writing. - in view of the imbalances in the supply chain of agricultural products in the union, which threaten the viability of many farms, the european union needs to be able to monitor closely market developments, in particular as regards the prices of the costs of production factors, and to be able to monitor fluctuations appropriately and identify their causes. i think that this action to analyse and regulate the markets must be cautious and seek not to introduce additional distortions in a supply chain which has already identified marked asymmetries. that said, i believe that this assessment by the union and the defence of competition must take place, otherwise failure to do so risks jeopardising agricultural production in its territory and consequently reducing the supply of european agricultural products available to consumers. doing nothing would mean worsening the conditions of everyone in the medium term. agriculture is not just an economic activity. it has an important social and environmental function which must be taken into account and deserves protection.
in writing. - the report under review, by mr josé bové, focuses on the supply chain for agricultural products, in particular its structure and implications. at a time when the common agricultural policy (cap) after 2013 is being discussed, it is appropriate to discuss all the problems affecting this strategic sector of the european union in order to avoid the continued abandonment of agricultural activity, calling into question not only the lack of some agricultural products, but above all the ecosystems associated with this activity in rural areas and mountain regions. this is a very important and timely report which i support because it draws attention to the real problems in the supply chain for agricultural products and points out the measures that must be taken. it is not sustainable to have an economic activity whose factors of production have increased by 60% in a decade, while output has increased by only 25%, as has happened with energy costs. energy efficiency must be a priority in the new cap. finally, i welcome the recognition of the need to support farmers in the greening measures provided for in the new cap, so that they can meet the new environmental and competitive challenges.
in writing. - we appreciate, as the report says, the need to improve the transparency of agricultural production factor prices. we also consider it important to improve the analysis of the reasons for extreme market fluctuations and to seek to clarify the interactions between speculation and agricultural markets, as well as between energy markets and food prices. the fundamental point, however, has not been defended, since the report does not mention any substantive measures for the benefit of small and mediumsized farmers and the general population, which should be aimed at defining a regulation of the market and the distribution chains of agri-food products that will defend national agricultural production, agricultural employment, and thus combat desertification and reduce imports. this report makes little progress on concrete solutions to improve the current situation in this sector, although it raises some relevant issues in this area (such as those relating to the efficient use of resources, among others).
in writing. - in the area of seeds, the report exposes the dominance of three companies, which contributes to the maintenance of high prices and the negative impact on crop diversity. it therefore calls for the possibility - now threatened - of farmers using seeds produced on their own farms to be maintained. the report calls for incentives for farmers to organise collectively in order to increase their bargaining power, improve resource management and reduce vulnerability to price volatility. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. it also proposes energy-saving measures, reducing the use of fertilisers, pesticides, herbicides and fertilizers, and local production of crops for animal feed. in short, the report aims to reduce production costs by proposing measures to break up concentration in the agricultural market dominated by a powerful agro-industry. i voted in favour of the report, considering that it is only a step and that more measures are needed to ensure a supply chain for agricultural products that is fairer socially, economically and environmentally.
in writing. - in addition to the difficulties in marketing their products, exacerbated by their weakness in negotiations with distributors, farmers have been faced with a successive escalation in the prices of the factors of production. while producer prices have risen by about 25% in the last decade, energy costs have risen by about 60%, fertilisers and soil conditioners by about 100%, seeds and animal feed by about 30%, non-residential building costs by about 20% and plant protection products and other pesticides by 13%. the increase in the cost of industrial machinery is also noticeable. overall, costs for european farmers increased by 40% over the same period. it will therefore come as no surprise that since 2009, according to eurostat data, the level of agricultural incomes has fallen by 11.6% in the eu. the difficult obstacles facing farmers can only be overcome by a comprehensive response that helps restructure agricultural production by reducing its dependence on the volatility of demand and the market for production factors. in agreeing with this approach, i voted in favour of this report, in the hope that the next cap will provide an answer to these problems.
in writing. - agricultural products have been subject to high market volatility, mainly due to rising production costs which are not reflected in an increase in farmers' incomes, thus threatening the survival of several enterprises and the maintenance of jobs. i support the initiatives in this report, particularly those relating to greater transparency in the prices of production factors, increased competition throughout the food supply chain, new incentives for investment in renewable energy production and the promotion of rural development programmes with an increased focus on greening the common agricultural policy (cap). i also believe that it is crucial that special attention be paid to the outermost regions in order to ensure that the agriculture of the respective european regions is increasingly sustainable and competitive in the framework of the cap for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution which deals with a key issue for producers and consumers. as the title of the report well indicates, imbalances in the food supply chain persist unfairly. a significant part of the problems faced by farmers stem from highly punitive behaviour imposed by modern distribution operators. i am referring in particular to the abusive buying practices of dominant wholesalers and retailers. only with the political will to implement the solutions already put forward by the european parliament will farmers and consumers be spared the penalty, especially since much of the legislation in force needs to be properly applied.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on imbalances in the food supply chain, arguing that european legislation should be strengthened and properly applied in order to ensure transparency in agricultural product markets, promote competitiveness and avoid volatility in food prices.
in writing. - there are now clear distortions in food markets which have a negative impact on both producers and consumers. the former, in particular, have seen a growing increase in production costs and, at the same time, have lost bargaining power with distributors. this imbalance threatens to jeopardise the viability of many farms, and this is a matter of concern to policy-makers, particularly in europe, given the possibility of inland desertification and increased unemployment in traditionally less developed regions. this pressure on producers is particularly relevant in the outermost regions of the union. i would like to see a more equitable and transparent relationship between the various players on this market, without jeopardizing the fundamental freedom of the market, and to prevent abuse of a dominant position and to allow farmers greater stability and more healthy competition.
in writing. i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure and replacing the motions for resolutions tabled by the ppe, alde, greens/efa, s&d and gue/ngl groups, for the following reasons: 1. we all recognise that agriculture is a strategic sector in the context of the european union's economy and that, in order to respond to future challenges in terms of food, natural resources and the environment, a more or less thorough reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) is essential. 2. there are problems in the food chain from production to the consumer that need to be addressed, including unfair trading practices that are aimed only at depriving producers of income. i therefore welcome the commission's communication, in the context of the single market act, on the adoption of a communication on these commercial practices and misleading advertising. the commission has already taken a number of measures to help the poorest countries in the world to cope with the crisis. it is urgent to recognise the role of the farmer and to free him from the stranglehold he finds himself in between the costs of the factors of production and the exploitation by the marketing chains of his products.
in writing. - it was a pity that the majority in this parliament had missed yet another opportunity to seriously address the problem of farmers' incomes and the growing imbalances in the distribution of income along the food supply chain. it has done so by rejecting the proposals of our group which could really add concrete possibilities for solving the problem to the condoled speeches which recognise the problem but do nothing to tackle it. more than forums and high-level groups to establish what we have known for a long time, more than the cynical insistence on this miraculous idea of self-regulation, solutions were needed that would constitute a possibility of breaking with the current agricultural and trade policies, which generate the imbalances and injustices that we have once again seen here. we regret that the majority of this parliament, including the portuguese members of the psd, cds and ps, continue to reject measures such as the maintenance of the production quota system, the creation of effective regulatory mechanisms in the food supply chain, the establishment of ceilings for trading profit margins, particularly for large supermarkets and retail companies, with reference to the price paid to producers, and measures to stop dumping between member states.
in writing. − the food supply chain has been marked by profound imbalances between producers and distributors. because of their economic ascendancy, distributors have imposed abusive trading conditions on farmers in their contracts (see paragraph 10 of the resolution adopted). these practices undermine the normal functioning of the competitive market in that the exchanges, instead of being based on a negotiation that brings benefits to both parties (positive sum game), allowing a fair price to be found for the transaction, play a role of pure strengthening of the stronger party. it is therefore necessary to adopt measures to correct these disparities, such as the creation of mechanisms for monitoring prices at the various stages of the supply chain, from producer to consumer, the use of legal information services for producers and the promotion of official forums responsible for identifying problems and finding solutions to the imbalances in these trade relations. i voted in favour of this joint resolution because that is the direction it is taking.
in writing. − the european commission has produced the report better functioning of the food supply chain in europe, which aimed to identify the considerable imbalances in terms of inequality of bargaining power that translate into unfair trading practices, such as late payments or restrictions on market access. i am voting in favour of this resolution because i agree that concrete measures should be taken which are transversal to all the member states and which have an impact on the development of sound european legislation. in addition, it is essential to improve the european price monitoring tool, develop a user-friendly interface and clarify the application of competition rules in the agricultural sector. finally, i believe that an intensive information campaign should be carried out at european level to inform farmers of their contractual rights, with particular emphasis on workers in the outermost regions.
in writing. - i welcome the european parliament's unreserved support for the european gnss, implemented through the galileo and egnos programmes, which seeks to improve the daily lives of european citizens, ensure europe's autonomy and independence and win a significant share of the world market for high-technology satellite navigation. it is essential, in my view, that the commission develops a space policy specifically adapted to the various sectors of the sector, stressing in this context that the policy should be coordinated not only with esa and the member states but also with the european parliament. i believe that a strategy for research and innovation in the field of space policy is of fundamental importance, in order to ensure technological progress, industrial development and competitiveness in the european union and to create jobs in the eu.
in writing. − space policy is one of the key elements of the europe 2020 strategy, contributing to the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth by creating highly skilled jobs (currently employing over 31 000 people), stimulating innovation and improving citizens' well-being and safety (through enhanced transport safety, civil protection, the development of social services for the elderly and disabled, etc.). space is of strategic importance to europe and it is important to ensure a coherent european approach to space, which contributes to a strong, competitive and independent european space industry, and these proposals are a step in that direction. it is important to ensure appropriate and clear governance of space policy and programmes, with effective monitoring and coordination mechanisms to reconcile priorities and ensure the best management of eu and national resources. i support the development of an effective space policy that can respond to the major global challenges and which cannot fail to bring about the completion of the galileo, egnos and gmes programmes, bringing enormous benefits at social, environmental, economic and strategic levels. it is therefore necessary and urgent that the respective legislative and financial frameworks be completed in an appropriate manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support a european space policy that contributes to improving the daily lives of european citizens, promotes economic growth and fosters the potential for innovation. space solutions are key to addressing the major challenges facing today's societies, such as natural disasters, climate change or environmental management.
in writing. − it is important that the union has a defined space strategy with concrete priorities and that it is feasible. there are two flagship projects in question that are currently underway. the commission has also been involved in the development of the gmes programme, which will provide earth observation data to monitor climate change and global security via the sentinel satellites. both have valuable objectives and bring important gains for security, climate change monitoring and the european economy itself, and are therefore part of a strategic challenge for the european union.
in writing. − space exploration has always stimulated the imagination of europeans and the galileo project symbolises europe's capacity in this field in the face of the american giant. this report looks at the european union's space strategy in the service of citizens at a time of crisis when financial resources are scarce. however, it is essential that the eu continues to develop its space programme in a way that does not jeopardise scientific and technological progress, including flagship projects such as galileo and gmes. the rapporteur, aware that space policy is a key element of the europe 2020 strategy and that the european space industry employs more than 31 000 highly qualified people (with a turnover of more than eur 5.4 billion), calls on the commission to develop an international strategy of collaboration with the member states, strengthening the dialogue with strategic partners (the united states of america and russia) and involving emerging powers such as china, india, the republic of korea, brazil, among others. conscious that a better european space capability can contribute not only to boosting the eu economy but also to improving the lives of european citizens, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - space research is undoubtedly an area in which cooperation between member states, as well as with other countries in europe and beyond, can and should be deepened. such research should aim at exploiting the potential of space for exclusively peaceful purposes, deepening knowledge and thereby seeking new possibilities for solving current problems and needs of human societies. the report advocates a european space strategy based on a set of existing and developing programmes such as galileo, egnos, sesar and gmes. these are programmes with which we have known reservations, concerning their possible use for military purposes. this is the case of gmes, which aims at global monitoring of the environment and security, and whose scope includes earth observation and the extraction of accurate data useful for the development of military operations, even if disguised as border surveillance, support for the union's external action, as well as risk prevention, emergency management and coastal surveillance. this is a type of military use which raises serious concerns. the commission, like this report, not only does not exclude it, it opens the door to it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on a european union space strategy for citizens. the treaty of lisbon, in article 189, gave the european union an explicit mandate to develop a policy on the exploitation and use of outer space in order to promote scientific and technical progress, industrial competitiveness and the implementation of its policies. with this own-initiative report, the european parliament is making its contribution, and one of the reasons for doing so is that the european space industry generates a consolidated turnover of eur 5.4 billion and employs more than 31 000 highly qualified people.
in writing. - in the context of the policy on the exploitation and use of outer space (article 189 of the lisbon treaty), the european union has two central projects: galileo and gmes. in the context of the first project, satellite navigation, an initial open service, an initial public regulated service and an initial search and rescue service will already be provided from 2014. in the context of gmes, the aim is to collect earth observation data to monitor climate change and global security. this market is highly dynamic today: the commission has already adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. on the other hand, india and japan are developing regional systems. on the other hand, the economy is increasingly dependent on these services. it is therefore necessary to adopt an overall strategy to ensure that the european navigation system is both globally competitive and, above all, at the service of citizens.
in writing. − this global space strategy, inserted in article 189 tfeu and part of the flagship industrial policy initiative of the eu 2020 strategy, aims to boost the exploitation and use of space. there are many areas that will benefit from the technological development of the global satellite navigation system. the services and applications developed by the galileo and gmes programmes will have major benefits for the european economy and the daily lives of citizens. it is now necessary to maintain the leading edge in this area and to allow technological developments to create business opportunities for european industries. it is also necessary to ensure compatibility and interoperability between the galileo programme and the other in-orbit navigation systems. the potential this will bring requires the european commission to assume responsibilities, particularly with regard to the financing and coordination of this strategy with the research programmes of the member states. a clear signal of political approval is needed to increase the interest of private initiative.
in writing. - as regards space development, we are in no doubt about the importance of deepening cooperation between member states and other countries in europe - among which russia stands out, with its invaluable research heritage - and the rest of the world. such cooperation shall aim at using the knowledge acquired to solve current problems and needs for the development, social progress and well-being of mankind, always for peaceful purposes. the report advocates a european space strategy based on a set of programmes - galileo, egnos, sesar and gmes. the latter has as one of its objectives the overall monitoring of the environment and security, which will be carried out through the observation of the planet and the extraction of accurate and useful data and in the framework of border surveillance actions, support for the union's external action, maritime surveillance, complex emergencies, humanitarian aid and civil protection. the resolution also calls for the security component of the gmes programme to be strengthened. behind these words there is the real danger of using the control of information obtained from space for the development of military operations, as well as the clear intention of deepening the path of securitarianism by attacking the fundamental freedoms of citizens, reasons for which we voted against.

in writing. - knowing that an increasing amount of healthy and edible food - by some estimates up to 50% - is lost annually in europe along all links of the agri-food chain, including in some cases at the consumer level, turning into waste, it is in my view fundamental to support this memorandum so that this catastrophe can be avoided. i support this report in the sense that we must avoid reducing food waste. this is an important preliminary step in the fight against world hunger, in responding to the increase in demand estimated by the fao and in improving the nutritional level of the population.
in writing. - there are currently around 925 million people at risk of undernourishment worldwide. in the eu, 79 million people live below the poverty line, 16 million of whom survive on food aid provided by charities. if we consider that reducing food waste is an important step towards fighting world hunger and improving the nutritional level of the population, it is unacceptable that almost 50% of healthy and edible food is lost annually in europe, along all links of the agri-food chain. the growing trend in global food waste needs to be countered by additional preventive measures, guidelines and strategies to improve the efficiency and sustainability of the agri-food chain. thereby contributing to the achievement of the millennium development goals, in particular with regard to reducing poverty and hunger by around 50% by 2015. finally, food waste and the resulting production of food waste also represents an environmental and ethical problem, with economic and social costs and implications in the context of the internal market, both for businesses and consumers.

in writing. - according to european commission figures, there are 43 million people in the european union at risk of food poverty, making food waste an even more shocking reality. according to some figures from 1974 to the present, it is estimated that food waste in the world has increased by 50%, and the fao estimates that europeans and north americans waste between 95 and 115 kg of food per capita per year. this waste occurs along the entire chain from production to consumers. it is therefore urgent to improve the functioning of the food chain, allowing food that would otherwise be wasted to be used and to raise public awareness of this important issue.
in writing. - according to a study by the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations (fao), each european wastes on average 105 kg of food per year. this report by salvatore caronna looks at this issue, namely what strategies the european union should adopt to improve the efficiency of the food chain and thus avoid food waste. in addition to being ethically unsustainable, this problem, since there are 70 million people in europe living below the poverty line, is economically and environmentally unsustainable. excess food production has enormous environmental costs, from wasted energy, water consumption, depleted natural resources, to greenhouse gas emissions. as such, it should be given priority treatment in the european institutions, while safeguarding food safety at all times. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of. i welcome and support the proclamation of 2014 as the european year against food waste in order to raise awareness among the general public, and i hope that the proposed measures will be properly implemented in order to achieve the goal of halving food waste by 2025.
in writing. - this report addresses a growing problem, which is certainly worrying: food waste. the rapporteur seeks to take a holistic approach to the problem, covering the different links in the agri-food chain and putting forward proposals to increase the efficiency of the chain. the report contains some important gaps and even some misunderstandings. the scale of the problem of food waste today is inseparable from the capitalist mode of production, the intensification of agriculture and the increase in the size of the production and consumption chains. it is important to note that small and medium-sized farming, short supply chains, local production and consumption can reduce waste and increase efficiency. it is not possible, therefore, to put everything on the same level and it is important that this distinction be made. on the other hand, proposals such as the redistribution of food to the poor and the application of discounts to products that are nearing the end of their shelf life, in addition to the charitable and welfare dimension they contain, constitute, in the concrete context of the current food supply chains, a dangerous doorway to dumping and manipulation by the large distributors, which we cannot accept.
in writing. - in the eu, half of all edible food is wasted. each european citizen produces 179 kg of waste per year and it is estimated that by 2020 this figure could increase by 40%. the report sets out concrete measures to halve this waste by 2025. the double-expiry labelling (with the expiry dates for sale and consumption), the modification of the packaging size to better match the quantities, the possibility of bulk sales, sales at a discount for products that are close to expiry or damaged, awareness campaigns and education programmes at different levels of education are some of these measures. in public procurement, in the restaurant and hotel sectors, preference is also given to companies which distribute unsold products free of charge to less-favoured citizens. the report introduces measures to reduce food waste and increase the efficiency of food production, and i voted in favour of it. in the eu, 16 million people receive food aid. i think that resolving this situation should be a priority. support policies are important to lessen the impact of the situation, but more equitable and redistributive economic policies are needed to effectively resolve it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that food waste is becoming unacceptable and that we must do everything we can to change the current situation by adopting, on a voluntary basis, more sustainable behaviour and appropriate regulation to combat losses in harvesting, storage, transport under unsafe conditions, packaging errors and the bad habits of the final consumer in the purchase and use of food products. in a context of crisis at european level, in which waste of resources is unacceptable, of exponential growth in developing countries with new and increased food needs, and of climate change, which causes irreversible crop losses, the problem dealt with in this report must be a priority for the eu. it should also be stressed that, in addition to the environmental damage caused by the production of unused food, the costs of treatment and disposal of the resulting waste and the loss of revenue for the producing undertakings should also be taken into account.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i am very pleased that the commissioner has taken this opportunity to speak. since its launch in 1997, this programme has been a real success with the people involved, as well as in terms of the effectiveness of the projects that have been funded. the report we are now discussing on the progress made and future prospects for the daphne programme was adopted in the committee on women's rights by almost unanimous vote, with only one abstention. the cooperation with the other political groups has been very fruitful and i would therefore like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for the very positive contributions they have made to this report. the fight against violence against children, young people and women remains a priority and unfortunately still makes sense. it is sufficient to take into account the new forms of violence that have emerged more recently with the increasing use of online social networks, as well as violence in kindergartens, mistreatment of the elderly and sexual assaults among adolescents. in addition, given the current economic crisis and budgetary constraints, it is necessary to avoid the financial impact of this type of crime on the judicial system and on social and health services. the costs of domestic violence have been estimated at €16 billion per year for the european union, including direct medical costs, costs of judicial and police activities, and social and economic costs. last november, the european commission announced that, as of 2014, the daphne programme will be integrated into the rights and citizenship programme. we have to admit that we would and would prefer that the programme retained its independence and autonomy. in the absence of such a possibility, i would like to highlight three concerns: first, to safeguard the objectives of the programme for the period 2014-2020; second, to maintain its funding at the same level as previous programmes; and third, to ensure its visibility within the future rights and citizenship programme. it is essential for the continued effectiveness of this programme to ensure that beneficiaries, public authorities and non-governmental organisations continue to be properly informed of the means of funding and the conditions of access. small organisations, which are by their nature closer to the phenomena of violence and very often have administrative difficulties, should be able to participate widely as they play a key role in detecting these problems and in the innovative way of addressing them. the balanced distribution of projects across the different member states should be taken into account. on the other hand, it is useful to collect regularly comparable data on the different types of violence in the european union in order to determine the real extent of the problem and to find appropriate solutions. i would like to conclude by stressing the important role of raising awareness of the phenomenon of violence through the media in the fields of education, health, the police and the judicial system.
i would like to say that access to renewable energy must really be a european objective, but not just a european but also a global one. there's no question that we've made fantastic technological progress in renewables. this progress was unthinkable 20 years ago, and so setting 2015 as our target for access to renewable energy is absolutely right. we all know about the destruction of a part of the sub-saharan african forest, for the use of biomass as the only and exclusive fuel. new solutions must be found. but in europe too, we have based renewable energy and its financing largely on full user payment. this is now under attack by everyone, particularly because of the crisis we are experiencing and also because of the nuclear lobby. that is why we support the commission in these measures.
