in writing. - i approve the report. it is in the european union's interest to promote coordination with the brics and the emerging powers, given the growing importance of these countries in the world in various fields. just as there is already permanent coordination between them, the eu should, by way of example, promote the coordination of positions for meetings such as the united nations general assembly or strategic partnerships in other areas, provided that the interests of eu member states and their citizens are not compromised. as such, it will be appropriate to develop these diplomatic efforts through an institutional mechanism, perhaps from the eu external relations service, which can deal with these countries in a coherent and permanent manner.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to congratulate my party colleague and rapporteur, mr jacek saryusz-wolski, on the conciliation work carried out within the afet committee, which has resulted in a very comprehensive own-initiative report in terms of the subjects covered and very inclusive in terms of the involvement of the different parliamentary groups. although i prefer the division between the designations civet (colombia, indonesia, vietnam, egypt, turkey and south africa) and bric (brazil, russia, india and china) to designate the world's major emerging economies, i believe that, because i consider that this separation between the two groups of emerging economies brings greater precision to the strategic analysis of their relations with the eu, this report proposes a number of very important measures for the future of our relations with the brics (this designation includes south africa), which should obviously be taken into account by the union. first of all, because of the importance attached to multilateralism in international relations, but also because of the greater involvement of the brics in economic development policies on a global scale and the strengthening of the role of the european parliamentary dimension in relations with these countries, which i consider to be fundamental for the establishment of lasting ties at international level.
in writing. - the report under review, by mr saryusz-wolski, deals with the european union's external policy - objectives and strategies - towards the so-called brics countries (brazil, russia, india, china and south africa) and other emerging-economy powers. brics is not a homogeneous bloc, as they are located in different geographical areas, have divergent pasts and do not equally embrace the values of the european union. they represent 40% of the world's population, 17% of world gross domestic product and often take concerted positions. the eu, while upholding its principles and values, cannot ignore the increasingly important role of these emerging economies and must work together to tackle the problems affecting the planet, such as climate change, terrorism, sustainable development, access to raw materials, political stability and global security. i voted in favour of this report and i support the proposal by mr paulo rangel to set up a delegation of this parliament for brazil, as is already the case with other countries, not least because it is the only country that speaks an official language of the eu.
in writing. - recognising the growing importance of the brics in the world economy, the report affirms the need for the eu to strengthen relations with each of these countries. the concern is, however, to consider them separately. some of the reasons are clear: the growth and diversification of economic activity in the brics is challenging the traditional international division of labour, which is unfavourable to these countries. their role is no longer limited to that of producers of low value-added products and exporters of raw materials and agricultural products to the countries at the centre of the capitalist system. today, they are gradually becoming great world powers, rivaling the triad - the united states, japan and the european union. some of them are even going the opposite way of the eu in the fight against hunger and poverty. it is worth remembering that in a few years, in a process not without great contradictions, millions of human beings have been lifted out of extreme poverty in china, india and brazil. it is a fact that brics have been converging on a number of internationally relevant issues. the positions that the brics have been taking on the international stage, their concertation, is increasingly perceived as a threat to the influence and dominance of the triad. in particular, in the institutions of international capitalism (the world bank, the imf, the g20).
in writing. − the brics (brazil, russia, india, china and south africa) and other emerging economies have been gaining great foreign policy relevance on the world stage as their growth has increased. in a future global economic outlook, seven emerging countries (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, mexico and turkey) are expected to have economies larger than the g7 countries as a whole (usa, japan, canada, uk, germany, france and italy) by 2050. the creation of a common platform in terms of foreign policy is thus necessary, and the creation of a new system of global governance, sufficiently inclusive of the brics and other emerging powers and based on common values, is beneficial for this. it is therefore urgent to discuss the foundations of a new inclusive system of global governance and to make recommendations, identifying key areas for reform where the eu can make its action and institutional architecture more efficient, and thus increase its potential and effectiveness as a global actor.
in writing. − while i voted in favour of the report on the eu's foreign policy towards the brics and other emerging powers: objectives and strategies, as it is overall positive, i cannot, however, follow the passage where it is proposed to entrust the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy/vice-president of the commission (hr) with the coordination of foreign and security policy with other sectoral eu policies, such as external trade policy. i understand that this proposal makes no sense in the light of the treaty of lisbon. firstly, these are two very different policies, subject to very different regimes in the union treaties. under the treaty, the hr is only competent to conduct the union's foreign and security policy and not to coordinate the union's various external action policies, in particular its external trade policy. thirdly, if there is a need for such coordination, it is the hr, together with the commissioner for external trade, who has the responsibility for it, without this implying any authority or hierarchy of the former over the latter. the proposal will therefore represent an unacceptable change in the balance and distribution of powers between the institutions and bodies of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with its main objective, which is to discuss the foundations of a new system of inclusive global governance and to make recommendations, identifying crucial areas for reform where the eu can make its action and institutional architecture more efficient and thereby increase its potential and effectiveness as a global actor with the so-called emerging economies, which are, among others, the brics (brazil, russia, india, china and south africa).
in writing. − the brics (brazil, russia, india, china and south africa) and other emerging economies can become highly relevant in terms of foreign policy on the world stage. in fact, it is estimated that by 2050, these states, together with indonesia, mexico and turkey, will have economies larger than the g7 countries combined. this new political and economic weight of the brics and other emerging powers should be duly weighed by the eu in the design of its foreign policy: the economic rise of these states will necessarily lead to a redefinition of the model of world political and economic governance. it is therefore urgent to start thinking about the eu's strategy for the near future, seeking to place these states within the circle of the community's foreign policy and preserve the eu's place as a committed and influential actor in the multipolar system of global governance that is being envisaged. i therefore voted in favour of this report, particularly welcoming the fact that the door has been opened here for the creation of a european parliament delegation for relations with brazil. this is an objective for which we have fought so hard and i hope that it can now finally be achieved.
in writing. - the international relations we are witnessing today reflect a loss of dominance by europe and the usa as the supposed holders of economic, cultural, political and humanistic supremacy. the dynamics built and developed in terms of multilateralism, in particular the composition of the un and the cs and other international organisations, have been implemented and adapted to the existing international system. today, we have a set of countries that have created a common platform of understanding in the field of foreign policy, the so-called brics -- brazil, russia, india, china and south africa -- and other emerging economies like indonesia, mexico and turkey, that want a global, multipolar system of governance. in terms of international action, brics already has common positions on a number of current issues. the reform of the international institutional framework is beyond doubt. today's problems are transnational, so they require global, non-state solutions. for global stability and security, brics emerges as essential partners where close cooperation, consultation, dialogue and consensus are urgently needed.
in writing. the report recognises the growing importance of the brics in the world economy and the need for the eu to strengthen relations with these countries. the crisis of capitalism is not only made more serious by the contribution of these countries to world output. the european parliament has also called for the eu to be given a role in the negotiations on the future of the eu, and for the eu to be able to play a more active role in the negotiations on the future of the eu. they want to curb their growth and the diversification of economic activity, which calls into question the international division of labour and the role they wanted to give them as producers of low value-added products. today, the brics are becoming progressively major world powers, rivaling the triad, some of them taking a reverse course to the eu in the fight against hunger and poverty, which the wrong course and policies of the eu and the member states will increase among us. we, for our part, are in favour of establishing relations with all countries, refusing to classify them and regardless of differences in political, economic, social and cultural views, ensuring mutual interest.
in writing. - i approve the report because it is balanced. consistency in the application of restrictive measures to certain states and, consequently, their leaders is essential to the credibility of the eu's foreign policy. in this respect, we must continue to set an example for the world by applying non-violent coercive measures to those who violate human rights and democratic values.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a coherent policy towards regimes against which the eu applies restrictive measures, because i believe that a more coherent and effective strategy towards authoritarian regimes is needed, including measures to prevent authoritarian leaders from benefiting from the proceeds of corruption and the possibility of transferring funds.
in writing. - it is well known that many of the authoritarian leaders in other parts of the world, as well as their families and clients, have diverted assets from their own countries and made investments in europe. it is often seen as a potential haven and a safe place to invest and put savings. against this disturbing circumstance, a number of measures have been taken to sanction these practices and restrict the movement of persons and goods involved, which are clearly not consistent and have not produced the desired effects, particularly as regards the desired political change in the countries of origin. this position of the european parliament, which i welcome, cannot be successful if the member states do not understand the importance of effectively articulating their responses to such problems and if they do not involve the people and civil society organisations of the sanctioned states in order to contribute to a collective awareness of these problems and to a much-needed paradigm shift in governance and the management of public goods.
in writing. - the european union's territory and its banking institutions are often chosen by leaders of developing countries, where democracy is slow to take hold, to deposit large sums of money (hosni mubarak of egypt, 50 to 70 million deposited in the eu and the us; gaddafi of libya, billions of dollars in assets in the eu; omar al-bashir of sudan, 4 billion dollars in the eu; etc.) the report by graham watson is on a proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council for the eu to implement a policy of coherence with regard to schemes against which the eu applies restrictive measures when their managers have personal and commercial interests within the eu territory. i voted in favour of this report because those who rule authoritarian regimes and enrich themselves through corruption and exploitation of the people and resources of that country must be obliged to respect human dignity. they cannot act with complete freedom and impunity in the face of the impotence and often complacency of international institutions. the eu must set an example by confiscating these assets and returning them to democratically elected governments.
in writing. - the application of the principles contained in this report is contrary to international law and the charter of the united nations. the latter advocates, among other things, friendly relations between nations based on respect for the principle of equal rights and self-determination of peoples and international cooperation to solve international problems of an economic, social, cultural or humanitarian nature. these are the principles which should guide international relations. this report defines an approach based on interference in the internal affairs of states. sanctions are one of the instruments of this approach. on the other hand, the explicit advocacy of support for parties to the conflict, aimed at regime change or changes of political power in certain countries, constitutes unacceptable interference, which invariably carries with it undisguised ambitions to satisfy economic and/or geopolitical interests. as we have said on many occasions, changes in the political power of a country must be the result of the exercise of the sovereign will of its people and not of external impositions.
in writing. − the new article 21 teu, as introduced by article 1 (24) of the treaty of lisbon, recognises that the union's actions are based on the principles of democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law. sanctions are applied in pursuit of the objectives of the cfsp as set out in article 21 teu, which include the promotion of international peace and security, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, the rule of law, the consolidation of democracy and good governance. however, the application of sanctions or restrictive measures is only effective if it is part of a coherent and comprehensive human rights strategy of the european union and its member states. it is therefore necessary that, when imposing sanctions on states which do not promote international peace and security, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, the rule of law, the consolidation of democracy and good governance, the interests of each member state should not interfere.
in writing. − on the basis of an own-initiative report, the european parliament voted on 2 february 2012 in favour of a proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on a coherent policy towards regimes against which the eu applies restrictive measures when their managers have personal and commercial interests within the eu's borders. these measures are intended to prevent capital flight from these countries. it is estimated that over the past two decades some 150 billion dollars have flowed out of certain north african countries (algeria, morocco and tunisia) from authoritarian leaders and their circles, when restrictive measures were already in place by the european institutions. for the sake of consistency, it is called for the strict application of financial sanctions or restrictive measures by all member states to these countries.
in writing. − the european union is founded on the principle of the dignity of the human person, and its line of action includes the defence of political regimes based on the representativeness of citizens and respect for the fundamental rights of the person. the natural corollary is the rejection of authoritarian regimes which, instead of pursuing the common good of the peoples represented, are directed to the satisfaction of the personal interests of the holders of public offices. in this context, it is justified that any measures adopted by the european union clearly identify, on the one hand, the subjects who are subject to the sanction and, on the other hand, already at the time of determining the applicable sanction, that targeted measures are adopted for the subjects to be sanctioned, seeking to avoid, where possible, that peoples also suffer. any guidelines which may be found must also be taken up by all member states in order to ensure an effective foreign policy; the european union must also take account of the fact that a large part of the personal property of the leaders who are subject to sanctions is located in the european union, which opens the door to more effective action by the eu. that is the spirit of this recommendation, and i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the eu's external action must be based on the constituent principles, as expressed in article 2 of the eu treaty, and on a strategic, coherent, comprehensive and transparent policy, when imposing any type of sanctions, avoiding duplication of criteria. the imposition of general or selective sanctions should target those responsible and maximise the safeguarding of the most vulnerable population. i therefore support the content of this report when it states that economic and financial sanctions imposed on the relevant officials and/or legal persons and/or entities should also cover all financial and property assets established in eu territory. to this end, it is necessary to develop clear criteria for the application of sanctions and for the coordination of sanctions between member states in order to assess the assets of persons included in the sanctions list for the possible confiscation of those assets. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament be informed from the outset and throughout the sanctions procedure.
in writing. − the imposition of sanctions is a unilateral decision and therefore a negative principle for the dialogue-based resolution of conflicts. the establishment of sanctions means the cancellation of the space that could and should be used for dialogue, negotiation and diplomatic mediation. we do not accept acts of direct interference and meddling in the internal affairs of countries by supporting one of the parties to the conflict, which are often added to sanctions. the sad examples of recent times are varied, in which external powers have directly interfered in the political changes of a country, by various means of supporting one of the parties to the conflict in a country, without this being done, obviously, in a disinterested way. it is the peoples who must decide their own destiny and future, without being subject to pressure and interference from outside powers. the unilateral decision to impose sanctions is part of this logic which does not respect the sovereignty of the peoples. what is needed is scrupulous respect for international law, the charter of the united nations and the principles contained in it.

in writing. - the full functioning of the single market - one of the main objectives underlying the creation of the european union - despite the rights enshrined in the european treaties and regulations, still has many obstacles to overcome. the report under review, by evelyn regner, is about parliament's recommendations to the commission to move forward with a 14th directive on the right of companies to transfer their registered offices from one member state to another, which is already enshrined in eu regulations. once workers' rights are safeguarded, it is essential that companies can move their headquarters, as this can save time and money. however, legal uncertainties and bureaucracy which differs from one member state to another have prevented it from becoming a reality. the legislation must also prevent abuse and opportunism, such as the setting up of companies reduced to a simple e-mail box. because this is not the first time that the ep has pressed the commission to come forward with a proposal in this area and because i believe that this is a measure which will benefit the european economy, in particular small and mediumsized enterprises, by making them more competitive at world level, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report argues that crossborder migration of companies is one of the key elements in the completion of the internal market and that, at the level of employment, the transfer of headquarters should be guided by the principle of flexibility, with a view to a more flexible market. here is further proof that the majority in the ep is seeking to deepen the neoliberal orientation that has led to the current financial, economic and social crisis in the eu. the majority of meps want to keep the free movement of capital, tax havens and offshore companies untouched, which are the direct causes of the worsening of the current serious situation. the portuguese are well aware of the case of the company jerónimo martins, which moved its personal and family holdings to the netherlands in order to pay less tax. the solutions of the majority of the ep will only bring more unemployment, injustice and social tragedies to the workers and the people. for these reasons, we voted against.
in writing. - articles 49 and 54 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union guarantee freedom of establishment to all companies. we all know that crossborder migration of companies is one of the fundamental elements in the completion of the internal market. similarly, the lack of uniformity in the legislation on transfer and in the procedures for transferring the registered or actual seat of an existing company under national law from one member state to another within the framework of the single market, as well as the employment risk, administrative difficulties, costs, social implications and lack of legal certainty, delay the final establishment of an increasingly effective internal market. it is therefore very important that all member states harmonize in this area.
in writing. − this report makes recommendations to the commission on a 14th company law directive on crossborder transfer of registered offices. the european parliament makes seven recommendations, including one on workers' rights, namely that workers' participation rights should be preserved in the context of the transfer and that workers' participation should be governed by the legislation of the host member state. this will, in our view, avoid the transfer of jobs for the sake of reducing labour costs.
in writing. - this own-initiative report aims to lay the foundations for further harmonisation of tax laws within the european union, as a way of combating the attempts at tax fraud we have seen in recent times. this document is intended to ensure that the processes of crossborder transfer of head offices do not affect the rights of interested parties, such as minority shareholders, employees and creditors, existing before the transfer. this avoids, in the event of insolvency or any other similar proceedings, the escape of a company from its obligations. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - economic activity, from producer to final consumer, is based on a system of trade between trading companies. since the community is based on the recognition of the freedom of establishment of companies, company law must be a privileged subject of regulation, since in that context a number of barriers to the proper functioning of the internal market can be created. the european parliament therefore recommends that the commission submit a 14th directive on the crossborder transfer of registered offices. in this context, the interests of shareholders, who should not have their pre-transfer rights postponed by the relocation of the company's headquarters, the interest of the company itself and, finally, the interests of the employees and all those who interact with it, will have to be weighed. this is a step whose necessity was confirmed by the court of justice in the cartesio case. in this context, i voted in favour.

in writing. − the eu, together with the member states, is the world's largest donor of humanitarian aid with a total of €2957 million in 2010. maintaining this policy is essential to mark the role that the eu and its members play in achieving the millennium development goals. the largest share of humanitarian aid funding goes to the african continent, which is, according to 2010 data, 42%. the eu, from this amount and aggregated reserves, funds some 200 partners, ranging from ngos to international organisations such as the un's specialised agencies. this support is intended for humanitarian assistance and civil protection for victims of disasters and protracted conflicts. establishing control levels to ensure that funding is implemented and holding both donors and recipients accountable is key. on the other hand, there should be more coordination between the eu and the member states for a comprehensive strategy for planning, financing and implementing the available humanitarian aid.

in writing. - i support this report because it advocates the idea that justice should be accessible to all european citizens and because it calls on the commission to present complementary measures to ensure the full exercise of this right, particularly in the area of collective actions. in the european area of justice, citizens and businesses must enjoy effective and efficient protection of the rights guaranteed by eu law. it is therefore important to provide for strong safeguards against abusive litigation, as provided for in the commission's horizontal consultation, and to protect consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises with safeguard procedures, particularly in the competition or consumer sectors.
in writing. - the right to compensation for damage suffered (compensation) is essential in any legal system. this is already safeguarded in the various national jurisdictions. however, i think caution is necessary when it comes to class action. on the one hand, we do not want to open the door to a system like the american one, in which the abuse of rights is a common practice, putting the activity of thousands of companies in doubt. secondly, because in the area of competition, the existence of a class action will lead to consumers who have been harmed by an anticompetitive practice, punishable under the provisions of the tfeu, being able to claim damages in the future. this will lead to the simultaneous application of fines and compensation to consumers harmed by such practices. again, this could have dramatic effects on businesses. i therefore believe that we should proceed with caution on this matter and i prefer alternative dispute settlement mechanisms which are cheaper, quicker and, in many cases, more effective. finally, i think it is essential that the ep should continue to play an active role in this area.
in writing. - the present report, by klaus-heiner lehne, is about the european union's openness to a coherent approach to collective action and the need to provide for consistent safeguards to avoid abusive litigation. improving access to justice for european citizens has been a concern of the eu, which has adopted several regulations and directives on this matter over the past few years. it is not the legal tradition in europe to settle disputes between individuals by resorting to a legal body. given the complexity of the matter and the different modes of operation in the various member states, harmonisation between most branches of national law is essential and, in the absence of such harmonisation, it is preferable that defendants be tried in the courts of their place of residence and have the right to refuse to take part in a class action. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that, as justice is a matter which affects the lives of all citizens in a very profound way, this parliament must be actively involved in the whole ordinary legislative process until a solution is found which covers the whole of the european union.
in writing. − this report provides that compliance with national legislation cannot stand in the way of uniform application of european union legislation, making clear the intention to create a horizontal system that supersedes eu legislation over national legislation. we are not against a european approach to collective action, providing for strong safeguards against abusive litigation. but we disagree that, driven by an objective need that transcends borders, the transfer of more elements of national sovereignty to the eu should be promoted. we believe that the way forward could be different, namely through the establishment of agreements between countries to enable them to tackle this problem, while preserving their sovereignty and maintaining the elements which this proposal seeks to transfer.
in writing. − this report is about a european approach to collective action and the commitment to provide strong safeguards against abusive litigation. the report provides answers, in a good way, to some legal items which are crucial in view of the structure of this legal instrument. the document is against the idea of copying the us system, with the aim of not allowing excessive and abusive practices, and takes into account the systems of the 27 member states. many member states have recently created collective instruments which allow, to some extent, collective access to justice. this report also highlights the benefits of class action lawsuits in terms of lower costs. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − i believe that in the european area of justice, citizens and businesses must enjoy effective and efficient protection of the rights that eu law guarantees them. in the case of widespread or massive damage, victims of unlawful acts may therefore refrain from seeking compensation, since the costs of obtaining individual redress may be disproportionate to the damage suffered. however, particular emphasis should continue to be placed on the enforcement of eu law by european and national public authorities, since these authorities have public law investigative tools that cannot be extrapolated to natural persons, so that the enforcement of legislation by private individuals continues to take on a complementary character.
in writing. − in this report, concerns are raised about abusive class actions. it is a common legal instrument in the anglo-saxon countries. the legal tradition of the european union is more oriented towards the resolution of disputes between natural persons than towards resolution through a legal entity. with this own-initiative report, the european parliament is contributing to the horizontal consultation initiated by the european commission. this consultation demonstrates the commission's openness to a european approach to collective action and its commitment to providing robust safeguards against abusive litigation. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the regulation of legal and procedural matters is one of the most sensitive areas of community law. it is therefore understandable that community legislation has started by standardising the common criteria for determining the international jurisdiction of courts by establishing common criteria for determining the substantive law applicable to certain types of dispute, by supporting alternative means of dispute resolution or, furthermore, by introducing procedural models for small claims. the regulation of collective action at community level therefore represents a breakthrough in this field: in this context, there will be a type of litigation relationship mass litigation with uniform regulation throughout the community. this is a measure which may be resisted, since the legislation to be introduced may conflict with certain features of national procedural law. in any event, i believe that this reflection should be carried out and should be seen as an opportunity to rethink the law governing the organisation of the judiciary in the various member states.
in writing. − consumers face significant difficulties in terms of effectiveness and accessibility when they individually wish to bring a legal action, which is all the more relevant in the face of the increasing integration of european markets and the consequent increase in cross-border activities. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the european union must adopt an integrated and coherent approach to dealing with cases where consumers are unprotected, making the most of joint action by several citizens. i also consider it essential that the measures proposed are designed to reduce the costs of litigation and to increase legal certainty for applicants, defendants and the judicial system. however, it will be necessary to take account of the traditions and legal systems of each member state and the dissemination of good practice at european union level should be encouraged.
in writing. − this initiative makes explicit the intention to create a horizontal system and a uniform application of eu law, overriding national legislation. we are not against a european approach to collective action, providing for strong safeguards against abusive litigation. but we disagree that, driven by an objective need that can cross borders, the transfer of more elements of national sovereignty to the eu should be promoted. we believe that the way forward could be different, namely through the establishment of agreements between countries to enable them to tackle this problem, while preserving their sovereignty and maintaining the elements which this proposal seeks to transfer.
in writing. − i agree because nutrition and health claims must not be false, ambiguous or misleading. the opposition to this list of nutrition claims arises from the fact that the draft commission regulation is not compatible with the purpose and content of the basic act. the commission must submit an amended draft.
in writing. − according to article 3 of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006, nutrition and health claims must not be false, ambiguous or misleading. according to that regulation, those claims should be worded in such a way that the average consumer can understand them and, where comparable, the comparison term should cover a range of foods of the same category and of different brands. the motion for a resolution under consideration contains, pursuant to rule 88 (2), parliament's opposition to the draft commission regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 on the list of nutrition claims, on the grounds that it is vitiated by certain defects, such as contradicting the purpose and content of the basic legal act in that it is ambiguous, misleading and confusing for the average consumer. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution calling on the commission to submit a new proposal to the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this resolution which opposed the adoption of the draft commission regulation, which would amend another regulation, which relates to the list of nutrition claims. the proposed introduction of the claim now containing x% less of [nutrition name] violates the principle of comparative claims, which allows, among other things, the comparison of the nutritional values of a product with a previous version of the same product, regardless of the starting level concerned. there is also the problem that this type of claim discourages producers from reformulating their products more substantially, as it is easier to reduce 15% of a nutrient than the percentage needed to make the product light or low in content. in the end, with this proposal, which fortunately was rejected by parliament, it was the consumer who lost in terms of the clarity, relevance and objectivity of the information provided to him. the european commission is now invited to submit an amended draft of these measures.
in writing. − nutrition and health claims should not be false, ambiguous or misleading, and the use of nutrition and health claims should only be allowed if it is plausible that the average consumer will understand the beneficial effects expressed in the claim. therefore, comparative nutrition claims should compare the composition of the food in question with a range of foods in the same category, including foods from other brands. in this way, information on foodstuffs should not mislead the consumer as to the nature, properties and characteristics of the foodstuff.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution of 2 february 2012 stating the european parliament's opposition to the draft commission regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 as regards the list of nutrition claims. the european parliament considers that comparative nutrition claims should compare the composition of the food in question with a range of foods in the same category, including foods from other brands. furthermore, information on foodstuffs should not mislead the consumer as to the nature, properties and characteristics of the foodstuff. in this context, it considers that the new nutrition claim proposed by the commission now containing x% less of [name of nutrient] to be included in the annex to regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 is contrary to the purpose and content of the basic legal act, as it is ambiguous, misleading and confusing for the average consumer, and therefore requests the commission to withdraw it and to submit to the committee on the environment, public health and food safety an amended draft of measures.
in writing. − the commission has presented a draft regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 as regards the list of nutrition claims. following the examination of the proposed amendments to the draft regulation, the committee on the environment, public health and food safety identified a number of provisions which, if accepted, could mislead consumers as to the characteristics of products available on the market and therefore opposed the adoption of the regulation. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that, following the arguments put forward by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, these provisions would violate the fundamental principles of consumer protection.
in writing. − according to article 3 of european commission regulation (ec) no 1924/2006, nutrition and health claims must not be false, ambiguous or misleading and it is important to inform consumers about the nature, properties and characteristics of the foodstuffs contained in the products. however, the new nutrition claim proposed by the commission seeks to adopt a comparative measure as it now contains x% less of another nutrient, thus contradicting the purpose and content of the basic act in that it is ambiguous, misleading and confusing for the average consumer. i would also point out that the principle of comparing the nutritional values of a product with an earlier version of the same product could lead to unfair competition with other products available on the market, since a product which has not been reformulated but has a lower content of a particular nutrient than the reformulated product of another brand cannot make a nutritional claim. in this respect, i am voting in favour of this report which opposes the adoption of the draft commission regulation amending regulation no 1924/2006, and calls on the commission to submit a draft with new measures to the committee on the environment, public health and food safety of the european parliament.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the new treaty, the so-called budgetary pact, because i agree with it in general. i have three objections, however, although they are pointed. firstly, i think it is an exaggeration to say that virtually all the measures in the treaty could be achieved within the framework of the existing eu treaties and that this new treaty is therefore unnecessary. in fact, its most important points, namely the obligation for member states to include binding rules on budgetary balance in their internal rules, could not be the subject of union legislation. secondly, i agree that the treaty does not solve the present budgetary and economic crisis in the union. but that is not their aim either, but to prevent future crises. the present budgetary crisis cannot be overcome without assurances to creditors that such crises will not be repeated in the future. thirdly, while i fully agree that a genuine budgetary union is much more than budgetary discipline, including also the issuing of joint loans to both national budgets and the union budget, i think that the requirement of tax harmonization cannot be omitted. the very idea of the internal market is incompatible with tax competition and tax dumping.

in writing. - the report undeniably contains some good proposals. most of them are, however, vaguely stated, going little beyond the plane of good intentions. the role of sport in society is valued, in terms of integration, among other correct principles. it is proposed that the multiannual financial framework should include a specific and ambitious budget for sport policy, that sport should be integrated into the curricula of all types of schools and that gender issues should be duly taken into account. however, it is proposed that mass sport (a term used to distinguish it from professional sport) be supported by money from lotteries; proposes the existence of a database of supporters at european level; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the drafting of the new rules. approaches that we don't follow and distance ourselves from.
in writing. − sport promotes socialization and recreation and is one of the most important health factors in modern society. in recent decades, the practice of grassroots sports has been replaced by the mere attendance of professional sports events. a european approach is needed to promote grassroots sport, to regulate professional sport and to ban violence and doping in sport. this report goes in that direction, and i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - sport is an important phenomenon and a social good. for many, it is indeed one of the most important forms of recreation, both when participating and when watching sporting events. sport, at its best, brings people together, regardless of their background, background, religious beliefs or economic status. sport promotes the active participation of european citizens in society and helps to develop a sense of social inclusion. article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) confers a new competence on the eu in the field of sport, calls on the eu to contribute to the promotion of sporting issues and states that eu action should aim at developing the european dimension of sport. the commission's communication is the first policy document in the field of sport since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which gives the eu a mandate to support, coordinate and complement the sport policy measures adopted by the member states. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - this report arises in the context of the new competences of the european union in the field of sport, article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the treaty gives the eu a mandate to support, coordinate and complement the sport policy measures adopted by the member states. the commission's communication is the first policy document in the field of sport following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. before these powers were conferred, the european parliament had already promoted several documents in the form of a resolution on the subject, which the rapporteur uses to present parliament's proposals. i voted in favour of agreeing to the measures laid down for a large and fast-growing sector with a major impact on national economies and which directly or indirectly employs 15 million people.
in writing. − as well as being an important social phenomenon and good, sport is an integration vector that promotes the active participation of european citizens in society and helps to develop a sense of social inclusion, and represents a large and fast-growing sector of the economy that contributes significantly to growth and employment. in this context, it is crucial that the eu and its member states adopt policies and measures to support and promote sport that address the main challenges in this field, such as the fight against doping, violence and intolerance, the free movement of citizens and the nationality of sportsmen and the transfer of players (the legality of the acts and the transparency of the financing flows involved, the european social dialogue in the sector, as well as the integrity of competitions). i have voted in favour of this report because i see these concerns reflected in it.
in writing. - article 165 of the treaty gives the eu a new competence in the field of sport, and the eu should contribute to the promotion of sport issues and develop the european dimension of sport. in its first communication in this field, the commission proposes concrete actions with regard to the social role, the economic dimension and the organisation of sport. the european parliament supports the development of the european dimension in sport, stressing issues such as the resolution of major problems, the need for proper management, the importance of sport for tourism, the fairness of sporting competitions, the budget, traditional games and sports, opportunities and employment, training and mobility, cooperation with third countries and international organisations and the european identity of sport itself.
in writing. − free and universal access to quality sport is essential for the social and personal development of individuals and a right that must be guaranteed by each member state through public funding to sports organisations, schools and the grassroots associative movement. this last aspect is of particular importance in reports seeking to promote the european dimension of sport, as it cannot replace the cultural and sporting specificity of each country. this report contains positive measures (although mainly on the level of intentions) to promote mass sport and sporting activity (not forgetting gender issues), in particular by proposing a specific and ambitious budget for sport policy in the multiannual financial framework. however, we cannot but express our concern and disagreement with the proposal that amateur sport be financed mainly by money from gambling, the creation of a european fan database or the prohibition of any kind of political demonstration by athletes during the games.
in writing. - i regret that more ideas on environmental monitoring have not been adopted. the minimum reporting requirement therefore requires the commission to monitor more closely the transposition of the environmental protection directive by member states through criminal law in order to ensure that it is carried out promptly and effectively. it is important that comprehensive waste management plans are implemented within the framework of european legislation. in turn, public authorities are expected to be effective and rigorous, particularly when dealing with matters in the field of education and health such as this, not least because this is a subject that has been attracting an increasing number of petitions from european citizens.
in writing. − most european citizens expect public authorities to provide efficient and effective public services in the areas of health, education, transport and safety. however, one issue that is giving rise to an increasing number of petitions is the apparent inability of public authorities in many countries to deal satisfactorily with the problem of waste management. judging from the petitions received, this concern is growing in many local communities, indicating that waste management is becoming a serious political and social problem. the resolution calls on the member states to speed up the transposition of the waste framework directive into national law and urges the national authorities to implement the measures essential to combating illegal waste disposal. the commission is also called upon to monitor carefully the transposition of the environmental protection directive by the member states in order to ensure that it is carried out promptly and effectively. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the measures it contains will help to improve the implementation of waste management policy in the future.
in writing. − one of the issues that has been generating an increasing number of petitions is environmental issues, which is the main group of petitions received, with waste related petitions representing an important subgroup within these. this seems obvious to me, as the waste problem affects citizens across the eu very directly, particularly in the authorisation procedure for new waste management facilities or the operation of existing ones, followed by concern about waste management in general - the not in my backyard (nimby) syndrome! it also appears that the failure of public authorities in many member states to address the problem of waste management satisfactorily may be a factor in the increase. i voted in favour of this report which, on the basis of 114 petitions which fundamentally point to the existence of deficiencies in waste management and the frequent failure of member states to comply with their legal obligations, recommends that member states should in future improve the implementation of waste management policy and speed up the transposition of the waste framework directive into their national law, and that the national authorities should implement the necessary and appropriate measures to combat illegal waste disposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the application of the waste directive, because the member states must make every effort to transpose this directive as quickly as possible and to ensure full compliance with all its requirements and all the objectives set out in the framework of european legislation with a view to protecting the environment and public health.
in writing. - one of the great problems of our time is how to manage the waste generated by industries, hospitals, our homes and the whole dynamic of modern life. this waste, created every day, must be properly treated to allow for efficient and sustainable management that preserves the environment. although the responsibility for waste management lies with the states, there are wide discrepancies in the way it is handled in the eu, and the report recommends, and i think it is right, that european guidelines be adopted in this area, which will allow for greater harmonisation of waste management policies.
in writing. − in a modern society where the 'use and throw away' principle has gained ground, sustainable waste management is making progress, as was clear from the discussion and vote on the report on waste from electrical and electronic equipment in the previous plenary session. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of waste water and the use of water-based products. the citizens have a right to know how their waste is treated. human health and the environment are at stake. despite the strictness of european legislation, there are member states with problems, some of which have been the subject of infringement proceedings. in the context of economic crisis, we cannot waste resources. it is therefore imperative to reuse, recover and recycle waste. i voted in favour of this report because it has significant advantages both for environmental protection and for human health. it is not enough to have the best legislation in the world, it must be respected. we must look at recycling as an opportunity for job creation and economic value.
in writing. − the report addresses the problem of the application of the waste directive and related directives in the eu member states, starting from complaints and petitions submitted to the european parliament by groups of citizens, in particular from greece. the rapporteur makes a number of points which we consider to be positive, relating, in general, to waste management, environmental protection and public awareness. however, there are less positive aspects of the report which must be noted. the report makes it clear that waste control is a public responsibility, but is often undertaken by private parties. it is not a secret that there are two large companies that control this business in two thirds of the member states, making a lot of money. unfortunately, this model is not, as was claimed, clearly rejected by the report. the report also refers to the 2007 directive. however, this directive has a problem in not distinguishing between toxic waste and ordinary waste, which has led in some cases to situations where large companies produce toxic waste in ways that are not compatible with the overriding interests of public health and environmental protection.
in writing. − most european citizens expect public authorities to provide efficient and effective public services in the areas of health, education, transport and safety. however, one issue that is giving rise to an increasing number of petitions is the apparent inability of public authorities in many countries to deal satisfactorily with the problem of waste management. the european union has adopted a wide range of legislative measures, applicable in all member states, to ensure that the legal framework is in place to deal with the inevitable consequence of our modern lifestyle, in terms of all the things we throw away in our homes, our workplaces, our hospitals, our industries, etc. it is clear to everyone that not addressing these issues and not prioritising efforts in this direction has negative effects, not only on the health and well-being of people, but also on the viability of the planet and its environment in the broad sense. however, lessons must be drawn from these examples and the recommendations contained in this report should therefore contribute to improving the implementation of waste management policy in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on member states to speed up the transposition of the waste framework directive into national law and urges national authorities to implement essential measures to combat illegal waste dumping. in this european parliament resolution, on the issues raised by the petitioners relating to the implementation of the waste directive and related directives in the member states of the european union, the commission is also asked to monitor carefully the transposition of the environmental protection directive by the member states in order to ensure that it is carried out promptly and effectively.
in writing. - the european parliament has received several petitions, initiated by groups of community citizens, highlighting local problems in waste management. given that this area has already been regulated at community level, the effectiveness of union law in responding to the needs of the people on the ground must be questioned. it is therefore necessary to identify, following the field trips of some meps, the points where the waste directive can be improved and those where it has not been properly applied. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european parliament has been receiving a number of petitions, with environmental issues being the ones that arouse the greatest interest from citizens, in particular those directly related to waste management. following several visits to ireland, france, italy and spain, it was considered necessary to take a position on the matter in question. i agree with this report, as i believe that member states should implement an advanced waste management strategy and ensure greater compliance with existing legislation. i also believe that european governments should involve citizens living near waste management infrastructure, strengthen cooperation with local and regional authorities and establish strong links with european agencies with strong knowledge of waste management, such as the european commission's directorate-general for the environment, the european environment agency or the european network for the implementation and enforcement of environmental legislation.
in writing. - this report sets out some positive lines, notably by denouncing abusive situations, and at the same time presents proposals for reducing and implementing the so-called waste hierarchy. we stress, however, the wrong perspective of almost exclusive individual responsibility for the environmental situation we are living in (a panacea which does not solve, in itself, a problem which is systemic), arguing that waste management is a public responsibility for private profits (it is not unusual that it praises two multinationals responsible for this management in 2/3 of the member states, without relating the extraordinary profits they make and the increase in complaints throughout europe). the distinction between toxic and ordinary waste is still missing, which allows large companies to pollute without restrictions, based on studies that consider the average waste produced per individual, putting households and companies in the same case. waste management is fundamental to the protection of the environment and human health. but we must not forget that the serious environmental problems do not stem from isolated acts, but are rather the result of the capitalist system which, in its quest for maximum profit, looks no further than the means to achieve it.
in writing. - i approve the report. the daphne programme has been successful in all its editions and as such it makes sense to continue to support it, especially because this programme has supported small projects on subjects that deserve special attention from society and the ngos that apply them on the ground, such as raising awareness of the situation of victims of violence or the commercial exploitation of children. i think there will also be the possibility of including support for projects on gender equality, as my group has advocated.
in writing. - that since its inception in 1997, the daphne programme, promoted by the eu and carried out by several ngos in the member states, has proved to be an important policy instrument in combating violence against women, children and adolescents, who are, along with the union's older citizens, the most vulnerable groups in the population. while considered a success, the report proposes some adjustments to the daphne programme until 2013, following the mid-term evaluation report, with which i agree: increased participation in the programme by the newest eu members and other member states with a small number of approved projects; increased publicity for approved projects to promote benchmarking; and a better fit of programmes to eu priority objectives through the funding of a smaller number of larger projects. i would like to end by congratulating my party colleague, regina bastos, for her work on such an important matter, which requires the european institutions to be increasingly involved in combating and eradicating this incomprehensible and shocking form of violence against the most vulnerable groups of our population.
in writing. the daphne programme is the european programme to combat violence against women and children. this type of violence encompasses a range of serious violations of fundamental rights, such as sexual abuse, physical assault and domestic violence, psychological violence, harassment or coercion, trafficking in women and exploitation of prostitution, among many other forms of aggression, which must be strongly condemned by states. i condemn all violence, but especially that which is directed against those who are most vulnerable - physically, socially, economically or emotionally - such as children and, often, women. states should therefore seek to eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, including trafficking for sexual exploitation, violations of their sexual self-determination and offences against their physical integrity. finally, i should like to clarify that the designation of sexual and reproductive rights, according to the internationally accepted definition, includes abortion, which is why i voted against this reference in recital k.

in writing. - this report recognises, and rightly so, the importance that the daphne programme has had in combating violence against children, young people and women. the report also calls for the inclusion of the objective of ending violence against women in the future rights and citizenship programme, as there is a proposal for actions funded under this programme to be integrated into the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, and for the latter to be integrated with the objective of ending violence against women, continuing with the same level of funding as the daphne programme has had so far. we cannot but point out the risk that under the new conditions now proposed this objective will be diluted and eventually lost amidst so many others. we therefore believe that specific funding should be allocated to the daphne programme and that this funding should be higher than in the last programmes, in view of the existing needs. given the importance of women's organisations, trade union organisations and various other ngos in defending and promoting women's rights and combating violence against women, it would be important for the report to set out clear measures to enable these organisations to access the programme's funds.
in writing. - given that violence against women continues to persist and take on new forms, and that in an economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing today, it is women who continue to suffer most as a result of inequality, there is no doubt that there is a need to finance programmes that can combat all forms of gender-based violence or contribute to reducing inequalities between women and men.
in writing. − this programme, set up in 1997, has established itself as the only european programme to combat violence against women, children and adolescents. in 2000, the daphne initiative was transformed into a multiannual programme for the period 2000-03, with a funding of eur 20 million, and has attracted great interest both in the european union and in various international bodies fighting the commercial sexual exploitation of children. the daphne ii and daphne iii programmes were launched in 2004 and 2007 respectively, with an average annual budget of eur 10 million for daphne ii and eur 16.7 million for daphne iii. the general objective of the daphne iii programme is to contribute to the protection of children, adolescents and women against all forms of violence and to achieve a high level of protection of health, well-being and social cohesion by promoting the deepening of community policies, in particular in the fields of public health, human rights and gender equality, and by encouraging action to protect children's rights and to combat trafficking in human beings and sexual exploitation. with such initiatives, the eu is at the forefront of the fight against violence against women, children and adolescents.

in writing. - i approve the report because it brings to the fore, and in a very pertinent way, a very sensitive subject which deserves debate: the situation of women and also of children in armed conflicts. it is of course important to involve more women in conflict prevention, mediation and resolution, but also in the leadership of military and peacekeeping operations. perhaps this will help to reduce the vulnerabilities that are targeted in many war scenarios, as there are still many women who are victims of violence and sexual exploitation.
in writing. - the situation of women in areas of armed conflict, especially on the african continent, is intolerable. sexual violence against women continues to be used as a weapon of war. these crimes have disastrous physical and psychological consequences for the victims who are often rejected by their communities. this report strongly condemns these crimes and stresses the need for the national authorities to put an end to the impunity of the perpetrators and to strengthen their justice systems to prosecute these acts. it also stressed the need to promote education for women's empowerment and awareness-raising campaigns for respect for the dignity of women. it also stressed the importance of increasing the number of women in peace negotiation processes, as well as in military and peacekeeping operations, especially in leadership positions. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. for the reasons i have given, i have supported this report.
in writing. - the brutality of the most vulnerable is, unfortunately, one of the most striking features of armed conflict. despite all the international conventions on this subject, wars, by revealing the worst in human beings, demonstrate that the law is not enough to curb the destructive impulse and that, however much men may try to set limits to it, the hatred of the other present in such situations eventually overcomes reason and piety. the situation of women is particularly difficult in cases of armed conflict. psychological or physical violence (often of a sexual nature) and the multiple vexations to which they are subjected are used as weapons to demoralize the opponent and to destroy the social fabric from which he comes. this type of violence leaves deep and lasting marks and, by its very intimate nature, instills in the communities that suffer it an inevitable desire for revenge that is very difficult to quell. the european union must continue to be vigilant about this phenomenon, vigorously combat the disgusting and deplorable situations facing defenceless women and seek ways of helping them and raising awareness in society of the need to change attitudes in this regard.
in writing. - the reports we receive of human rights violations in the context of war are constant and almost always take on machiavellian contours according to the available information (conflict in the congo: 16 violations a day!). women and children, because of their fragility, are among the main victims. girls and women are often repeatedly raped in the face of their family's impotence. this, in addition to the physical and psychological consequences for the victims, brings enormous trauma to the husbands and children. it is therefore of the utmost urgency to adopt a code of conduct to be applied in the theatre of war and in refugee camps. moreover, it is essential that the perpetrators of such war crimes be arrested and brought to justice, so that they do not go unpunished. i support this report by norica nicolai, which calls for the protection of women from all forms of violence and for their greater participation in military negotiation processes - where they are less than 10% - as their presence is essential in dialogue with other women in conflict. the eu cannot miss this opportunity to put this issue on the foreign policy agenda.
in writing. - the subject of this report is important and relevant. the report should be appreciated as it draws attention to the specific issues of women in war situations, such as increased vulnerability in conflict situations, sexual violence and rape, among other aspects. some recommendations are made to address and avoid these dangers and to properly consider gender specificities in military conflicts. the report as a whole, however, is imbued with an unmistakably militaristic vision, which is well expressed in the call for better conditions for women in nato military and civilian missions. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council and parliament, and the council will be consulted on the matter. the commission's proposal is to be accompanied by a strong commitment to peace and the peaceful settlement of conflicts, an area in which women can indeed make an invaluable contribution.
in writing. - in the context of armed conflict, there are numerous crimes against women which go unpunished. it is therefore important, on the one hand, to strengthen the prevention of this type of crime and to ensure that there is no impunity. inequality between men and women must also be tackled in these scenarios, in particular by giving women a more active role, for example in peace negotiation missions and in the processes of political and democratic reconstruction in post-conflict countries.
in writing. − in my view, more women need to be involved in conflict prevention, mediation and resolution. in this regard, the eu and the member states should include more women in the armed forces, in leadership positions and in field operations. from the gender equality point of view, it is essential that there are more women officers in high-ranking positions, but it is also very important that women are present in civilian operations, as they have an easier time establishing better relationships with local women. in the peacebuilding phase, the participation of women is key, as as the pillars of communities, women are much more aware of social and practical needs than men, as it is women who spend more time in local communities, so they have a better knowledge of the practical needs to be included in peacebuilding projects, namely market infrastructures, health centres, accessible school systems, etc. that is why i am voting in favour.
