in writing. - widespread access to energy sources is not yet a reality worldwide. in many areas, people face serious difficulties in accessing and having access to energy in sufficient quantity and quality to ensure a comfortable life in which energy is no longer a major concern for households. the european union, the world's largest donor, must be aware of this inequality and contribute to helping to reduce it. to this end, it should seek to help the countries and populations most in need and not only provide access to energy but, where possible, enhance the possibilities for self-management and self-generation by aid recipients. without more and better access to energy, poverty in many parts of the world will be hard to eradicate. the european union must therefore be part of this collective effort, which the authorities of the assisted states themselves cannot ignore. they should be required to make good use of the funds received and to make efforts to extend access to energy to their citizens, in particular the most deprived.
in writing. - the western world considers access to energy as a right, like water. however, there are many countries where access to energy remains a mirage, especially in india and on the african continent. it is therefore imperative to adopt investment catalysts to achieve the 2030 objectives of universal access to energy. the report under review, by norbert neuser, focuses on the need for cooperation within the european union to achieve the above objective and could not be more timely, given that we are at the beginning of the year 2012, which has been designated by the un as the year of renewable energy for all. i welcome the measures proposed, in particular the encouragement of private investment and the inclusion of universal access to energy as one of the millennium development goals from 2015. the focus on energy efficiency and green energy production is key. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, and i hope that very soon the eu will finance the projects of private individuals for the installation of equipment for the production of energy from renewable sources.
in writing. - this report addresses the issue of promoting access to energy in developing countries, within the framework of the eu's cooperation policy. the report makes some pertinent remarks on the scale of the problem of energy poverty and the negative implications for the achievement of development objectives. the importance attached to the need to adapt energy supply solutions to the specific conditions of developing countries, by making use of decentralized solutions, renewable energies and the autonomy of these countries, seems equally correct to us. but unfortunately the great contradictions which run through this parliament also emerge quite clearly in the report. in the end, what prevails is a completely subversive view of the role of development cooperation, here transformed into business opportunities for eu countries. the attempt to interfere with the sovereign choices of developing countries by imposing models identical to those of the eu, of deregulation and liberalisation of markets (market-oriented reforms in the energy sector, public-private partnerships, etc.) is notorious, which has led to situations of exclusion from access to energy in europe. while recognizing the urgent need to intensify cooperation with developing countries in this area, we cannot support this report.
in writing. − the report considers that access to modern energy services is a fundamental condition for poverty reduction and sustainable human development and that without access to these services, entire communities are condemned to a life of poverty. it also considered that access to modern energy promotes school attendance and education, both by facilitating communication and by facilitating access to basic needs. modern fuels also improve environmental sustainability. better access to modern fuels reduces the physical burden of transporting wood and frees up precious time, especially for women, by broadening their employment opportunities. as the report addresses these problems, i voted in favour.
in writing. − access to modern energy services is a key condition for poverty reduction and sustainable human development. energy services impact on all aspects of people's lives and livelihoods, and without access to these services, entire communities are condemned to a life of poverty. the importance of access to energy requires greater attention from the international community. the two main mechanisms for eu cooperation on energy access are the european development fund (edf) and the eu energy facility. it should be noted that 90% of edf funds are allocated through the mechanism of national and regional indicative programmes (nip/rip), negotiated with the beneficiary countries and regions. the eu energy facility, established in 2005, is a co-financing instrument open to submission by governmental and non-governmental entities. it is crucial to step up political will and financial commitment if the eu is to play a key role in achieving universal access to energy by 2030.
in writing. − this report deals with the european union's development cooperation to achieve the goal of universal access to energy by 2030. access to modern energy services is a key condition for poverty reduction and sustainable human development. energy services impact on all aspects of people's lives and livelihoods, and without access to these services, entire communities are condemned to a life of poverty. the importance of access to energy requires greater attention from the international community. in this connection, and in view of the measures proposed in this document to pursue the objective of universal access to energy, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in september 2010, the goal of universal access to energy by 2030 was set by the united nations secretary-general ban ki moon. in fact, access to energy is a basic condition for the pursuit of many other millennium development goals. among the various obstacles to access to these services under universal conditions, financing difficulties emerge as the main cause of the supply gap. it is therefore justified that these objectives should be taken into account in the allocation of european funds available for development aid. on the one hand, because this makes it possible to harmonize the objectives of the community institutions with the objectives of the un, and on the other hand, because access to energy can, in so far as it improves the basic conditions of production, have, in general terms, a multiplier effect on the aid granted. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − access to modern energy services is a key condition for poverty reduction and sustainable human development, impacting on all aspects of people's lives and therefore requiring greater attention from the international community. the european union must cooperate and contribute to financing the poorest in access to energy. the energy facility is the eu's largest financing mechanism for energy cooperation. however, when compared to the funding gap in energy access or the funding of the necessary aid, the size of this fund is quite small. thus, if the eu shows and intensifies political will and financial commitment, it can play a key role in achieving universal access to energy by 2030.
in writing. - this report addresses the issue of promoting access to energy in developing countries, within the framework of the eu's cooperation policy. the report makes some pertinent remarks on the scale of the problem of energy poverty and the negative implications for the achievement of development objectives. it is also worth mentioning the importance attached to the need to adapt energy supply solutions to the specific conditions of developing countries, making the most of decentralised solutions, renewable energies and the autonomy of these countries. if these were the objectives of the report, we would agree with it. however, in the main, what ends up prevailing is a completely subverted view of the role of development cooperation, here transformed into business opportunities for eu countries. the attempt to interfere in the sovereign choices of developing countries by imposing models identical to those of the eu, of deregulation and liberalisation of markets, which have led to situations of exclusion in access to energy in several countries and have allowed states to be deprived of this important strategic sector, is notorious.

in writing. − this report is intended to be a tool for cooperation in developing initiatives to improve the single market and create a more competitive europe. it addresses tax problems faced by european citizens and businesses, and whose reform could help improve their daily lives. the report, which i supported, focuses mainly on the following issues: tackling problems of double taxation and difficulties in obtaining tax reductions, benefits and deductions; promoting better access to tax information and removing cross-border tax obstacles for the benefit of eu citizens; analysing areas where further tax coordination will be needed and where the eu can play a role; discussing the problem of removing discriminatory tax provisions in member states that are in conflict with the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the eu treaties; and solutions to prevent tax evasion, fraud and abuse and promote greater tax transparency. the report also stresses the need to assess the fiscal implications of the european semester and calls on the commission to present a report in 2012 on this matter.

in writing. - the report even makes positive initial considerations, such as that the function of tax systems is to finance public services (education, health, infrastructure, public transport), reduce social inequalities and ensure a fairer distribution of wealth, or that taxation remains a matter of national sovereignty and the tax structures of the member states should be respected. we also appreciate some of the comments on smes. but the few positive aspects of the report are insufficient to change a very negative overall view, which is even in direct contradiction to the initial considerations. the report therefore advocates the need for harmonisation of fiscal policies in the eu and increased control of budgetary procedures by the commission, defends fiscal federalism and highlights the european semester. in other words, it supports the subversion of the function of the tax system enshrined in some national constitutions, as is the case in portugal, by placing it at the service of the reproduction of inequalities, the accumulation and concentration of capital by the large economic and financial groups and justifying the retreat of the state in a number of areas of economic and social life. despite the contradictions noted, it is pure and simple neoliberalism that prevails. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. − the main functions of tax systems are to finance public services such as education, healthcare, infrastructure and public transport, to protect public goods by encouraging, in particular, the production and consumption of environmentally friendly products, to reduce social inequalities and to ensure a more equitable distribution of income and wealth. however, taxation remains a matter of national (and in some cases local) sovereignty and the different structures of member states' tax systems must therefore be respected. changes in the treaties will be necessary to transfer decision-making on tax policies from the national to the eu level. the increased scrutiny of budgetary procedures by the commission should therefore be reflected in greater democratic scrutiny by the european parliament.

the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common fisheries policy is based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is a principle which is also reflected in the common fisheries policy. the objectives of the motion for a resolution are clear: the first is to call for the recognition of the multifunctionality of fisheries. this implies an awareness that fisheries are not limited to their traditional extraction, processing and marketing activities, because, in addition to these activities and their socioeconomic value, fisheries play a significant role in the historical, cultural, recreational, tourist, scientific, energy, environmental, educational and other fields, producing public goods for the benefit of society and which must be taken into account in the cfp's financing. a second objective is to propose the notion of conditionality, i.e. positive discrimination for those who provide evidence of the implementation of good fishing practices, whether in the gear used, in the rejection of illegal fishing and in the effort to reduce by-catch. this measure will also have a positive impact in addition to the increased cooperation of shipowners and fishermen in the monitoring and control processes. a third objective is to highlight how fisheries as such and integrated into the integrated maritime policy contribute to the rio+20 summit objectives of job creation and poverty eradication and to the european union's 2020 strategy, promoting smart, sustainable and inclusive growth through its increasingly scientific basis, ecosystem structuring and vocational training. only this renewed, holistic, modern approach to fisheries can make it a real engine of development, which is slow to reach many coastal areas of the member states facing the sea, such as portugal, or maritime regions such as the islands and, specifically, the outermost regions such as the azores. we can't ask for less from the next reform.
the fisheries sector, apart from its strategic importance for the public fisheries supply and for the balance of the food balance of the member states, also contributes considerably to the socioeconomic well-being of coastal communities, local development, employment, the maintenance and creation of economic activities and jobs upstream and downstream of fishing. the european union's common fisheries policy has so far neglected the importance of the multifunctionality of the sector and with it the so-called production of public goods. the deep economic and social crisis affecting the fishing sector, the result of a policy whose central orientation has in many cases been reduced to the indiscriminate killing of vessels, jeopardises the release and full exploitation of the sector's enormous potential in a number of areas, such as the economic, social, historical and cultural, scientific, educational and environmental fields, among others. the question is, commissioner, whether the reform of the cfp under way will help to change this picture or whether it will maintain it or even worsen it. unfortunately, the signs given by the commission so far are not encouraging, we might even say disturbing. the advocacy of an increasing market orientation of the cfp and the gradual elimination of public support - the general philosophy that inspires the reform - forgets that the market does not recognise, and does not properly reward, many of the so-called positive environmental and social externalities for which less competitive segments of the fleet are responsible from a strictly economic point of view. it is well known that, in the general context of the fisheries sector, small-scale coastal and artisanal fisheries, which are largely the majority in many member states, are of particular importance for multi-functionality and the production of public goods. the importance of this segment of the fleet is not sufficiently recognised in the commission's proposal. on the contrary, the commission adopts a reductive and outdated definition of small-scale fishing, while at the same time proposing a change in the cfp management system based on the introduction, with mandatory status in all member states, of a system of transferable individual concessions which could seriously undermine small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing and, with them, the multifunctionality of the sector and the production of public goods. if this system is to continue, and we will do everything we can to ensure that it does not, none of the safeguard clauses already proposed by the commission will be able to stop the inevitable concentration of activity on the operators with the greatest economic and financial power, first at national level, but inevitably sooner or later at european level. it would be a further strong contribution to the decline of many fishing communities more dependent on fishing. these are guidelines that need to be bridged and reversed. there are other ways, alternative ways, which can reverse the decline of the sector and help to realize its great potential. this path involves proposals such as the linking of the new european maritime and fisheries fund with other instruments, notably cohesion policy, to promote the cohesion of the economic and social fabric of coastal communities most dependent on fishing. support for economic activities associated with fishing, both upstream and downstream, diversification, rather than replacement of fishing activities, with the development of complementary activities. priority should be given to projects with integrated solutions that benefit all coastal communities as widely as possible, rather than those that benefit only a small number of operators. access to these projects should be guaranteed to fishermen and families and not just to shipowners. promote the rejuvenation of the sector by encouraging young people to enter the labour market, ensuring that support is provided, inter alia, for meeting vocational training and entry-level needs. the value of activities carried out on land. recognition and appreciation of the role of women in fisheries. the development of a community programme to support small-scale fishing, which, by combining various instruments, particularly financial instruments, will respond to the specific problems of this sector and support sustainable management of the fisheries concerned. these are some of the proposals which we think the reform in progress should welcome, in order to recognise the multifunctionality of the fisheries sector and the production of public goods, among many other proposals in our resolution.

in writing. - the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy has been operating for some years. the observatory's mission is to detect and record infringements of intellectual property rights by making a statistical record of them - without any kind of personal data collection. in order to reduce the centre's operating costs, the european commission proposes to incorporate it into the office for harmonization in the internal market. this report is aimed at this alone, not at definitions of data collection or other such matters, but at transferring tasks from one institution to another. although the scope and practical effects of this report are therefore relatively small, we cannot but express our reservations and dissociation, both with regard to the conception of intellectual property rights in force in the eu, and shared by the majority of this parliament, and with regard to the role and objectives of the office for harmonization in the internal market.

in writing. the technological revolution we are witnessing has led to a redefinition of the notion of wealth: this concept, which was traditionally identified with the ownership of landed property, has become predominantly credit-related and is now being used to defend the exclusive exploitation of ideal-sized entities. it is not possible today to think of exclusive rights of use for certain goods without taking account of intellectual property rights, especially in their economic dimension: in fact, we have a great deal of incentive here to take up innovation and development activities. without this degree of protection, which offers the possibility of a return on investment, it is unlikely that firms would use the same degree of force to create new products and services. the proposal to integrate the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy into the office for harmonization in the internal market, seeking to add the activities of that body to the know-how and financial resources available to the office, is therefore to be welcomed. the aim is to strengthen the prevention and detection of piracy, which, in addition to its economic effects, may also jeopardize consumer protection. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the protection of intellectual property is covered by a large number of international conventions. the european union has two important institutions to fulfil this strategic desire, namely the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) and the european patent office (epo), which are responsible for the registration of community trade marks and designs. i support the commission's proposal to transfer some of the powers of the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy to the office for harmonization in the internal market, in particular with regard to certain tasks relating to the protection of intellectual property rights, such as trademarks, designs and models. i agree with this report because i believe that there is a need to take further measures in the area of intellectual property protection, thereby reducing the threats to european businesses and increasing consumer safety.
in writing. − the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy is responsible for detecting and recording infringements of intellectual property rights by keeping a statistical record of them - without any collection of personal data. what this report proposes is a measure to reduce the operating costs of the observatory, in this case it proposes to incorporate it into the institute for the harmonization of the internal market. this report is only intended to transfer tasks from one institution to another, not to change the system of defining data collection. we cannot but express our reservations and disagreement both with the conception of intellectual property rights that prevails in the eu and is shared by the majority of this parliament, and with the role and objectives of the office for harmonization in the internal market.
in writing. - i welcome this report, the main objective of which is to establish a european-wide platform for existing national business registers. this platform will be beneficial in promoting the exchange of simple information on business and thus benefiting potential investors, regulators, etc. as it will make information on this subject easier to access and understand throughout the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this initiative because this directive should not limit the rights of member states to levy fees for obtaining information on companies through the system of interconnection of registers, if national legislation provides for this. therefore, the technical measures and specifications for the system of interconnection of registers should allow for the establishment of payment arrangements. this directive should not affect any specific technical solution in this area, as the payment arrangements should be determined at the stage of adoption of the implementing acts, taking into account the widely available online payment facilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates important measures to strengthen legal certainty for businesses and consumers involved in crossborder activities. these measures contribute to the further integration of the eu economic area and its transparency.
in writing. - when we talk about the internal market, we must realise that one of its consequences is increased crossborder trade. this is desirable and should be encouraged, but it also entails the need to make official and reliable information available to the public about companies operating in the eu. the lack of uniformity in the data contained in the various trade registers creates legal uncertainty, which is not in the interests of businesses or consumers. the creation of a centralised european access, where the registration data of all member states are stored in a uniform manner, is therefore necessary. this increases transparency, efficiency and legal certainty, and strengthens the confidence of the 500 million european consumers, which is essential in the context of the exit from the crisis. finally, and once again, i stress the need for a new interconnection system that does not represent an additional administrative burden for european companies. this system should make life easier for all market players and not be a (more) red tape to overcome.
in writing. - new information technologies have made life easier for citizens and businesses, saving time and money. however, while much has been done, much remains to be done in this area and with a view to the full functioning of the internal market. this report, by kurt lechner, concerns the proposal for a directive of the european parliament (ep) and of the council amending directives 89/666/ec, 2005/56/ec and 2009/101/ec as regards the interconnection of central, commercial and companies registers. at a time when business internationalisation is becoming necessary in response to the needs of growth and the existence of national registers alone makes life difficult for companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises. it is a requirement of smes. this directive is therefore a fantastic tool for faster communication between citizens and businesses and a means of ending the fictitious existence of subsidiaries whose parent companies have disappeared. i voted in favour of this proposal because it represents a major step forward in the single market, bringing greater security and transparency to commercial transactions, and it is a key aid to companies wishing to open branches in another member state or to establish commercial relations with companies in other countries.
in writing. - this report proposes a technical link between existing national registers (trade and company registers). the proposal has no legal consequences as regards its harmonization. it is only intended to provide a platform that allows people to access such records more quickly, without altering or modifying them. amendments nos 10, 11 and 12, proposed by the rapporteur, are clear as to the objectives and scope of the report. in particular, it is noted that this directive is not intended to harmonise national systems of central, commercial and companies registers, and that no obligation is imposed on member states to amend their internal system of registers, in particular as regards the management, storage of data, charging of fees and the use and dissemination of information for national purposes. we have supported this report on the terms proposed.
in writing. − given the opportunities offered by the internal market, companies are increasingly expanding their activities beyond national borders. we are witnessing the creation of transnational groups, restructuring operations, mergers and divisions. in this context, the importance of access to information on companies in a transnational context becomes obvious. however, such information is not always easily obtainable and this legislative resolution is an important step towards further integration of the european economic area. in this respect, i voted in favour of this directive, considering further that the data set necessary for the proper functioning of the central platform should be defined from the system of interconnection of central, commercial and companies registers and that the provision of such data should be made in a careful manner and should not be made directly available to the public.
in writing. − trade registers are kept at national and regional level and consistently differ in de facto and de jure, particularly as regards their legal significance and the reliability of the data recorded. since i consider that the interconnection of business registers is an important measure to promote the integration of the economic area within the eu and to strengthen legal certainty for businesses and consumers, i voted in favour of this report, which aims at legal certainty and transparency in order to promote better interconnection of business registers, saving time and money for businesses.
in writing. − often overlooked, registers make a fundamental contribution to the security of transactions and the certainty of legal facts, helping to avoid situations of uncertainty and therefore litigation. it is therefore understandable that, in a context where the economies of the various member states are highly integrated, contributing to the emergence of international legal relations, there is a need for rapid access to the register data of the various member states. given the different structures of the register systems of the various member states - both in the value attributed to the facts recorded and in the evidence required for their recording - the proposed directive is intended only to create the conditions necessary for the exchange of information between the various member states by reducing obstacles to trade within the community market. on the face of it, this is a laudable initiative. i therefore voted in favour, following the amendments tabled by the committee on legal affairs.
in writing. − the interconnection of business registers is an important measure to promote the integration of the economic area into the european union and to strengthen legal certainty for its businesses and their consumers. the rapporteur believes that it is exceptionally justified to leave decisions to future legal acts, some of which will also take the form of implementing acts, with the full involvement of the member states. the interconnection of company registers will therefore only be successful if the commission and the member states cooperate closely. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. it is stated that: this directive is not intended to harmonise national systems of central registers, commercial registers and companies' registers, no obligation is imposed on member states to change their internal system of registers, in particular as regards management, data storage, charging of fees and use and dissemination of information for national purposes. the report therefore proposes a technical link between the existing national registers (trade and company registers) and not a harmonisation of their legal consequences. the aim is to provide a platform that will enable people to access these types of records more quickly, without altering or modifying them, and we voted in favour of this.

in writing. − on 17 march 2008, the council adopted regulation (ec) no 241/2008 on the conclusion of the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) between the european community and the republic of guinea-bissau for a period of four years, renewable by tacit agreement unless one of the parties denounces it. the app supported the presence of the eu fleet in west africa, created employment and generated additional revenues for the eu market. it has also proven to be relevant to the needs of guinea-bissau, both as an important contribution to macroeconomic and budgetary stability and in terms of the national fisheries policy, as it provides financial means for the implementation of important measures to support the economic development and sustainability of the sector. it therefore appears to be in the interest of both parties that a new protocol be concluded, and this resolution recommends that the european parliament give its consent to its conclusion. during the negotiations, concerns about the need for better monitoring of resources through the best available scientific advice, accelerating the work programme of the joint scientific committee, should be taken into account. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. - bearing in mind that the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and guinea-bissau, in force for the period 2007-2011, would expire on 15 june 2011 and the absence of agreement between the parties on a future new protocol, i am pleased to learn that the two parties have decided to conclude a protocol for at least one year, with the terms of the previous protocol being renewed with little change. i commend this protocol because it allows the activity of tuna (spain, france, portugal), shrimp (spain, italy, greece, portugal), fish and octopus (spain, italy, greece) fishing vessels in exchange for payments of eur 7 million per year, 35% of which will be used to help guinea-bissau develop sustainable and responsible fishing. i voted in favour of this cooperation agreement because it has proved its importance for guinea-bissau, particularly in seeking to contribute to the economic and fiscal stability of that country.

in writing. − on 15 june 2011, when the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) between the european community and the republic of guinea-bissau, which had been in force for four years, expired, a new protocol was signed for a period of one year, in order to prepare a new agreement during that period which would respect the provisions of the cotonou agreement. in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and in order for the council to conclude a new protocol, it is necessary for this parliament to approve this proposal for a protocol between the european union and the republic of guinea-bissau, which sets out the fishing opportunities for eu fishing fleets in guinean waters and the financial compensation to be paid by the eu. considering that the protocol under consideration renews the terms of the previous protocol, including only additional clauses for the suspension and revision of the payment of the financial contribution and for the suspension of the implementation of the protocol in the event of a violation of the essential and fundamental elements of human rights and democratic principles, as provided for in article 9 of the cotonou agreement, i voted in favour of this recommendation for the approval of the new protocol.
in writing. − the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and guinea-bissau, in force for the period 2007-2011, expired on 15 june 2011. in the absence of agreement between the parties on a future new protocol - due to the eu's refusal to accept guinea-bissau's position that the financial contribution should be increased - the two parties decided to conclude a protocol for a period of one year only, the terms of the previous protocol being renewed with little change. the 37 fishing licences for member states' fleets, of which 4 are for portugal, are thus retained. it should be recalled that the current agreement was temporarily suspended by the eu, which referred to problems with the absorption capacity of the funds related to sectoral support by the guinean state. it is also important to recall the calls we made at the appropriate time, and which we reiterate here, for increased eu support through the adoption of measures, discussed and decided jointly with guinea-bissau, aimed at improving the capacity to absorb community funds. unfortunately, the eu has done little in this area. this shows the fragility of these agreements in their development aid component. weaknesses that need to be looked at and urgently overcome.
in writing. − on 17 march 2008, the council adopted a regulation on the conclusion of the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) between the european community and the republic of guinea-bissau, in force for a period of four years, renewable tacitly, unless one of the parties denounces it. the gpa was accompanied by a protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution for the period from 16 june 2007 to 15 june 2011. since there is little time left for the conclusion of a new protocol before the expiry of the previous one, both parties decided to conclude a protocol for one year in order to have the time necessary to assess the feasibility of a future protocol with a longer duration. in order to allow european union vessels to continue fishing activities pending the completion of the procedures necessary for the conclusion of the new protocol, article 14 provides for its provisional application as from 16 june 2011. pursuant to article 14 (3), the parties shall endeavour to conclude negotiations for a future protocol by 15 march 2012 at the latest.
in writing. − the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) between the eu and the republic of guinea-bissau has enabled eu fleet segments from areas heavily dependent on fisheries to access fishing opportunities, supported their regional presence in west africa, created jobs, and generated additional revenue for the eu market. the agreement is estimated to contribute to the employment of 470 eu citizens. the ppp has also proven to be relevant to the needs of guinea-bissau, both as a significant contribution to macroeconomic and fiscal stability and in terms of the national fisheries policy, providing financial means for the implementation of important measures to support the economic development and sustainability of the sector (according to the evaluation report, it contributed on average to 7,3% of annual government revenues and to around 88% of budgeted fisheries expenditure), and having a particular impact on the reduction of unreported and unregulated fishing and on the sector's compliance with eu health conditions in terms of trade in fishery products, which are important conditions for the development of a national fisheries sector. i therefore vote in favour of the extension of the fisheries protocol in question.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 241/2008, adopted by the council on 17 march 2008, aimed at the conclusion of a fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of guinea-bissau. the agreement was accompanied by a protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution for the period from 16 june 2007 to 15 june 2011. however, as the previous protocol has ceased to apply, negotiations have begun with a view to its replacement. it was signed on 20 december 2011 and is currently awaiting approval by the european parliament. from the community's point of view, the ratio between the financial contribution paid by the union and the benefits received has been 2.2: for annual costs of eur 6,6 million, a total benefit of eur 14,5 million is indicated. the new protocol will also strengthen the eu's position as an external partner. on the other hand, this protocol also offers added value for guinea-bissau. in addition to being a general source of revenue, it supports the local fisheries sector (contributing to some 88% of the sector's expenditure), which is of great importance to the guinean economy. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − in 2008, the eu and the republic of guinea-bissau concluded a fisheries partnership agreement (fpa), accompanied by a protocol setting out fishing opportunities and financial compensation for the period from june 2007 to june 2011. in june 2011, another protocol was signed for a period of one year to allow time for further negotiations for a future protocol with a longer duration. this new protocol contains additional clauses, in the event of violation of human rights and democratic principles, which may lead to suspension or revision of the payment of financial compensation. the new financial compensation amounts to €7 million per year to support the fisheries policy and the sustainability of marine resources in guinea-bissau, and €500,000 to improve the health conditions in the fisheries sector. portugal has historical links with this african country and this new protocol means more fishing opportunities for portuguese vessels and at the same time a form of support for the development of the guinean fishing sector. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.

in writing. − traditionally, vaccination against bluetongue was carried out with live attenuated virus vaccines, which entailed a number of restrictions on vaccination in order to prevent the spread of the virus to unvaccinated animals. however, scientific developments have allowed the creation of new inactivated vaccines. unlike ' live attenuated vaccines', these can be used safely and without restrictions, as there is no longer a risk of circulating any active virus. in view of the serious consequences of bluetongue for livestock farming, all measures should be taken to make vaccination easier and more effective, in order to protect farmers from animal losses and ultimately to ensure food safety.
in writing. − the text under examination is a recommendation for a second reading, based on the council's position at first reading, and aims at the adoption of a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2000/75/ec as regards vaccination against bluetongue. bluetongue, also known as bluetongue, is a disease which mainly affects ruminants such as sheep, goats and cattle and can take the form of an epidemic when environmental and climatic conditions are favourable, in particular in late summer and early autumn. although there is no record of human contagion, it is necessary to implement measures leading to its eradication. in november 2010, the european union adopted a set of measures to eradicate it, including a vaccination plan using so-called live attenuated vaccines. however, in recent years so-called inactivated vaccines have been developed which, unlike previous vaccines, can be used outside restricted areas. i voted in favour of this recommendation because, taking into account technological and scientific innovation in veterinary medicine, it makes the vaccination programme against bluetongue more flexible and more efficient, reducing the costs of the agricultural sector from this disease.
in writing. − bluetongue is a disease affecting ruminants (cattle, sheep and goats) whose infectious agent - a virus - is spread by a vector insect from animal to animal, with severe consequences for the agricultural sector. the aim of this directive is to update the rules on vaccination against bluetongue by making them more flexible and by making them an instrument not only for controlling the disease but also for prevention. greater agility allows for wider use of the vaccine and lifting restrictions circumscribed to areas where the disease has occurred. in addition, the updates concerned also concern new technologies, in particular the available inactivated vaccines, which are safer than the previous ones, modified live vaccines or live attenuated vaccines, which have allowed the unwanted circulation of the virus in unvaccinated animals. these are very important reasons, and we have supported the report. the council agrees with the objectives proposed by the commission and incorporates most of the amendments proposed by parliament. this directive enters into force on the day following that of its official publication, which is important given the urgency of implementing the control and prevention of that disease and mitigating any consequences in the agricultural sector.
in writing. − vaccination against bluetongue was carried out with live attenuated virus vaccines, which entailed a number of restrictions on vaccination in order to prevent the spread of the virus to unvaccinated animals. however, recent technological developments have led to the emergence of new vaccines with the absence of live viruses. these new vaccines can be used with a higher level of safety and without any restrictions, as there is no longer any risk in the circulation of any active virus. in view of the serious consequences of bluetongue for livestock holdings, all measures should be taken to facilitate good vaccination practices in order to protect breeders from the loss of animals, which often leads to fatal losses for those holdings. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report following the agreement of the european parliament and the council at first reading, which updates the current rules on vaccination against bluetongue laid down in directive 2000/75/ec, making them more flexible. bluetongue is a disease affecting ruminants (such as cattle, sheep and goats) and is transmitted by vector insects which spread the virus from one animal to another, which has been affecting some european geographical areas, in particular portugal. the use of vaccines is, however, limited by the current rules provided for in directive 2000/75/ec, which provides for the use of vaccines only in areas where the disease has occurred and which have therefore been subject to restrictions on movements of animals. the new flexible rules provided for in the draft directive are based on the fact that inactivated vaccines are now available and can also be successfully used outside areas subject to restrictions on the movement of animals.
in writing. − better known as bluetongue, this disease has caused outbreaks in several member states, particularly in central and northern europe. bluetongue affects in particular ruminants such as cattle, sheep and goats and leads to a sharp increase in mortality and disruption of economic activity in the sector. since the frequent outbreaks since 2000, the eu has adopted specific disease control measures, in particular vaccination policies. inactivated vaccines are noteworthy, as they do not put at risk other communities not affected by the same disease. epidemic control within the eu is essential to avoid creating lock-out and embargo situations that will affect the economic sectors concerned.
in writing. - i welcome this report as it contributes to the well-being, greater protection and safety of consumers throughout the european union. the existence of efficient and secure payment systems is essential for the proper functioning of the internal market and for the conduct of economic transactions. as such, i believe that the creation of an internal market for euro payment services (single euro payments area, or sepa) is of great importance and should be considered.
in writing. − this report sets out the technical requirements for credit transfers and direct debits in euro. the proposal aims to create an internal market for payment services in euro (single euro payments area, or sepa), in which there are no differences in regulation between cross-border and national payments. the integration of european payment markets is expected to bring numerous economic benefits, including: • increased competition and innovation; • reduced fees (payment costs for consumers and businesses); • faster transfers (cross-border payments will be as easy as national payments). the aim of this regulation is to bring about harmonisation and a steady reduction in the fees to be charged on the market, to ensure a level playing field between payment service providers and to provide a more dynamic market, benefiting above all consumers and businesses. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i supported this report because the proposal aims at creating an internal market for payment services in euro (single euro payments area, or sepa), in which there are no differences in regulation between cross-border and national payments. i welcome the fact that this regulation is designed to bring about harmonization and a steady reduction in the fees to be applied on the market, ensuring a level playing field between payment service providers and providing a greater dynamism to the market, benefiting above all consumers and businesses. the regulation covers 32 european countries, including the 27 member states of the european union, switzerland, norway, monaco, iceland and liechtenstein, although for non-euro area countries its entry into force is only mandatory as of 31 october 2016.
in writing. the commission proposal for a regulation, which parliament voted in favour of today, amends the sepa regulation (single euro payments area or sepa) to create an internal market for payment services in euro, in which there are no differences in regulation between intra-european and domestic payments. this regulation covers 32 european countries, including the 27 member states of the union, switzerland, norway, monaco, iceland and liechtenstein. although the sepa direct debit and credit system has already been launched in 2008 and 2009 respectively, there is still a major problem with its actual implementation due to difficulties (resistance...? inertia...? both...?) in migrating to this new payment system. the commission's proposal therefore suggests a transitional period as short as possible, with a perfectly defined timetable (01/02/2014- euro area countries; 31/10/2016- non-euro area countries) and with no possibility of further derogations beyond those provided for in the regulation now adopted. with sepa fully operational, you will be able to use a single debit card throughout europe, for example, or receive your salary in your home country if you work in another european country.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it presents a set of measures which will bring economic benefits to the eu, increasing competition and innovation and reducing payment costs for consumers and businesses. from february 2014, it will finally be possible to make cross-border bank payments as if they were national payments, and for example, eu posted workers will be able to keep bank accounts in their home countries and enjoy their salary in the country where they are employed.

in writing. - this report aims at the creation of the single euro payments area (sepa). the commission's objective is to harmonise payment systems in the euro area in order to create an integrated market for payment services. the main argument for sepa is the benefits for consumers, who will be able to make payments in euro in europe in a simpler, cheaper and safer way, just as if they were doing it in their own country. between january 2008 and november 2009, the sepa credit transfer system (sct) and the sepa direct debit system (sdd) began to be introduced at eu level, including in portugal. by the deadline for migration to sepa instruments (february 2014), all national electronic payment systems for credit transfers and debit cards have to be abolished and replaced by those operating at eu level. despite some positive aspects, the report raises some reservations, both with regard to the specific difficulties that may be felt by some groups of the population, as acknowledged by the rapporteur himself, and with regard to the justification for the transition to sepa, to realise the potential of the single market for europe.

in writing. − section 7 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes the court of auditors as one of the european institutions. created in 1975, its objectives are to control the accounts and improve the financial management of the european union (eu). the court of auditors may carry out audits of any person or organisation responsible for the management of eu funds, and its findings are presented in writing in the form of reports, which are sent to the commission and the governments of the eu countries. member states shall submit a proposal to the council which, after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt the list of members of the court of auditors. i am voting in favour of the appointment of mr baudilio tomé muguruza, as he fulfils the conditions laid down in article 1 of article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, allow me to congratulate the european parliament, and in particular mr nicholson and the fictitious rapporteur for constructive cooperation with the council and the commission, who have enriched the commission's initial proposal and at the same time reached agreement at first reading. the differences in approaches initially expressed were overcome by an open discussion between the three institutions and a strong sense of responsibility which did not lose sight of the real purpose of the exercise, namely to give the dairy sector new instruments to ensure sustainability and to strengthen the organisation of producers in the dairy sector. the milk package is one of the first major agricultural legislative acts to be adopted at first reading under the ordinary legislative procedure introduced by the treaty of lisbon. i think this is a real success of the cooperation between parliament and the council, which shows that it is not the ordinary legislative procedure that prevents us from taking important decisions quickly and consistently. the milk package gives member states the possibility, as mr nicholson has mentioned, of making the milk delivery contract between producers and processors compulsory. the proposal also gives the possibility to milk producers who wish to organise themselves into producer organisations in order to assert their position in the food chain, in particular through collective negotiation of contracts for the delivery of their milk, which is clearly strengthened by this proposal. they will also be able to benefit from the possibility left to member states to impose the obligation on milk purchasers to offer milk producers a contract with a minimum duration of at least six months. the concern to take account of the specific nature of cooperatives, expressed by the high-level groups organized around experts from the member states, is also reflected in the final text. the milk package highlights the role that inter-branch cooperation can play in bringing producers, manufacturers, traders and consumers together to improve transparency in the milk supply chain and mutual understanding of the role of each link in the chain. in the same spirit of transparency, the milk package sets out the framework for monitoring milk deliveries after the expiry of the milk quota system by providing for the provision of the necessary data in a timely manner and thus enabling the commission to provide milk producers and milk market players with market information in a timely manner. the milk package will also play an important role in regulating the supply of quality cheese under a geographical indication, which brings benefits in terms of added value and sustainability, particularly in vulnerable regions. i conclude by saying that two meetings are planned to take stock of the implementation of the provisions introduced by the milk package, the first at the end of june 2014 and the second at the end of december 2018. at each of these dates, the commission undertakes to submit to parliament and the council reports on the development of the market situation in the milk sector. the effects on producers in less-favoured regions will be assessed in particular in relation to the general objective of preserving production in these regions. potential incentives to encourage farmers to enter into joint production agreements will also be assessed.
i would like to say that the commission is very pleased with the proposal for a regulation on the common organization of the market in milk and milk products. it is another step on the road to justifying the unacceptable and disastrous decision to end milk quotas in 2015 and for that reason alone it is unacceptable. the rest are illusions that those who are now preparing to pass this proposal are selling to the dairy farmers who see their situation worsening every day. the illusion that in a free and unregulated market, which they defend, it is possible to guarantee fair prices for production. the illusion that without instruments to regulate production it is possible to guarantee each country the right to produce according to its needs. what a delusion! this path will reinforce the power of the big economic groups, the big distribution and the big transformation. it will strengthen the concentration of production in some producers and countries, liquidating it in other countries, leading to the ruin of a significant part of their producers. it will continue to facilitate dumping between member states and the flooding of national markets with imported milk. it will continue to promote intensive, export-oriented production, which puts food safety and quality and environmental sustainability at risk. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. what is needed are instruments of regulation and intervention in the markets which ensure fair prices for the producer, taking into account both the cost of the factors of production and the prices charged to the consumer, in order to ensure a fair distribution of the added value along the value chain of the sector.
mr president, commissioner, the milk package which is presented here as an instrument for organising the sector, containing positive and important elements such as the strengthening of the role of producer organisations and inter-branch organisations and contractual aspects which in some member states may constitute a step forward in the relationship between producers and processors, nevertheless leaves us far short of the instruments which the sector needs to prosper in the coming years in the framework of an agriculture which we want to have in europe access to a fair distribution of value in the food chain, which does not turn into agriculture of large intensive farms concentrated in a few member states. if improving the conditions for self-regulation in the relationship between the actors in the sector is desirable, to think that this alone is enough is to commit a serious error which could lead to the exclusion of thousands of milk producers, dozens of regions and even some countries involved in the dairy sector. the debate on the regulation of the dairy sector in the perspective of an economically, socially, environmentally and territorially sustainable sector thus remains open. and we cannot abandon the milk quota system without ensuring that there are real instruments for managing supply.
the commission's proposal for the milk sector is insufficient, especially in view of the fact that it is a highly volatile sector, which is subject to cyclical crises and is undergoing restructuring with the announced end of quotas. this report, despite the meritorious work of the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs, does not do the miracle of making the proposal sufficient to guarantee the future of this sector. the milk package does not replace milk quotas. it doesn 't change much . the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the milk market is not affected by the new rules. the concentration limits are currently exceeded and there are no mechanisms in place to reverse the situation. without any significant new guidelines for the sector, with many producers still paying off the bank credit they used to buy a quota which seems worthless, with the selling price of milk falling, with dumping and cartels operating at the distribution level, what will be the future of regions heavily dependent on milk production as in the azores?

can the commission and the council continue to impose recessionary policies that squeeze the economies of the most vulnerable, openly discussing the possibility of sovereign states in the euro area going bankrupt when they know that firecrackers have never left the agenda? are the commission and the council fully aware of the explosive political and economic risk this speech poses to europe? yes, we need to radically overhaul the recipes. but that requires political will. until that will exists, out of respect for the citizens, let us stop saying that we are in favour of growth and employment, because it is not true. and the public cannot continue to be fooled.
mr president, i would first like to welcome the rapporteurs. it is now commonplace to say that we are experiencing the most serious financial, economic and social crisis since the creation of our modern international financial model. it is never too much to stress that unemployment rates in the european union have reached historic highs to demand that the fight against unemployment be the top priority. youth unemployment is dramatic. in my country, portugal, more than one in three young people are looking for work and have no prospect of finding it. our citizens are unbelievers. it is urgent to restore their trust. after years of reckless management of public finances, it is time to adopt budgetary reconciliation reforms and to get the books in order. but let us not delude ourselves, austerity without economic growth is only a partial solution. the creation of more and better jobs is the great european design. measures to ensure that young people do not have more than four months to go without a job or training offer, and to reduce the risk of poverty and social exclusion, must be a reality.
the policies contained in the european semester, in economic governance and in the budgetary pact are a reinforcement of the legitimacy and institutionalization of the so-called austerity measures, which we cannot accept. this recipe can never and cannot be reconciled with the principles of social justice, growth and the promotion of employment, because they call for the exact opposite, the reduction of wage costs, the increase in the exploitation of workers and the retreat of the state, the attack on acquired social and labour rights. these policies of so-called fiscal consolidation are causing real social tragedies and disasters, such as the increase in poverty, in addition to the fact that they are only deepening the path of economic recession and the increase in public debts. what is needed is a real break with this path. the construction of a europe of cooperation, whose main objective is to defend the interests of the peoples and to put an end to the processes of oppression and colonization by the major powers. last saturday, in the streets of lisbon, portugal, more than 300,000 people demanded an end to austerity measures and promised that the struggle would continue.
mr president, i would like to begin by congratulating the various rapporteurs on the documents we are discussing here today, in particular my colleague jean-paul gauzès, who in his report stresses the need to find solutions to the financial and sovereign crisis we are currently experiencing. it is also a matter of discipline, but also of strengthening medium- and long-term growth measures. doing everything at once and often in contradictory ways is not the solution. firstly, we must find short-term solutions to provide liquidity to the real economy, to solve the banking crisis we are currently experiencing, to solve the problem of the states. secondly, we must move towards a set of structural reforms which are clearly geared towards economic growth, and finally, we also need a set of institutional changes in the way the euro and the european union operate. finally, a clear political discourse is needed. we must all support it and i commend the way the council has done it here today.
in writing. - i support this recommendation, as it is essential to strengthen cooperation within the union, in this case with norway, switzerland, liechtenstein, switzerland and iceland, particularly with regard to one of the most important legislative acquis of the european union, the schengen treaty. at the moment we are going through, it is all the more important to promote the capacity for dialogue between countries and between countries and institutions in order for the union to function well and for the objectives of the treaties to be fully achieved.
in writing. − i welcome the conclusion of this agreement between the eu and the four schengen associated states, namely iceland, norway, switzerland and liechtenstein, which will enable these states to participate in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers in relation to the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis. in my view, this agreement is important because it aims to ensure greater coherence and at the same time to ensure that all associated states are treated equally. the participation of the associated states gives them the opportunity to express, in a timely manner, their ideas and concerns regarding the implementation or possible developments of the schengen acquis. the enlargement of the schengen area to non-eu countries has brought significant economic benefits to european countries as well as immediate practical results in the daily lives and movement of european citizens.
in writing. − i support the conclusion of this agreement between the eu and the four schengen associated states, namely iceland, norway, switzerland and liechtenstein, which will allow these states to participate in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers (comitology) in the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis. the conclusion of this agreement is of the utmost importance in order to ensure greater consistency and, at the same time, to ensure that all associated states are subject to the same form of treatment. the participation of the associated states gives them the opportunity to express, in a timely manner, their ideas and concerns regarding the implementation or possible developments of the schengen acquis. however, their participation is limited to possible contributions to the decision-making process and they cannot participate in the decision-making process itself, as they do not have the right to vote. they shall be subject to a set of rights and obligations which guarantee their effective participation as observers and shall also contribute financially to the administrative costs arising from their participation in the schengen comitology committees.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the participation of iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland and the schengen acquis, as i regard the agreement between the european union and these states as positive with a view to their participation in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers in the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis.
in writing. − the participation of the republic of iceland, the principality of liechtenstein, the kingdom of norway and the swiss confederation in the committees assisting the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers in relation to the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis is of the utmost importance for the full transparency of information and, as such, for the security of citizens of the states of the european union and of the countries cohabiting with the same community agreement.
in writing. - the draft council decision on the conclusion of an agreement between the european union, of the one part, and the republic of iceland, the kingdom of norway, the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein, of the other part, on the participation of those states in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the executive powers conferred on it in implementing, applying and developing the schengen acquis. the schengen agreement, which was initiated in 1985 and incorporated into eu law by the treaty of amsterdam in 1997, establishes a geographical area of free movement of persons, abolishing internal borders between the signatory states, and provides for cooperation and coordination between police services and judicial authorities. the agreement provides for the participation of the associated states as observers in the work of the current and future committees of assistance to the commission by means of certain rights and obligations, in particular the payment of a financial contribution. since the participation of the abovementioned states is provided for in the agreement on the european economic area or is based on the exchange of letters annexed to the association agreement with switzerland (the case of the swiss confederation), i am voting in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. the schengen agreement, created in 1985 and the convention implementing it adopted in 1990, had the following objectives: - to abolish internal border controls between the signatory states and to create a single external border with common visa rules; - to establish police and judicial cooperation and to set up a schengen information system. we have always criticised this approach to building a fortress europe, which simultaneously encourages and feeds the development of racism and xenophobia, as well as other forms of intolerance and authoritarian and anti-democratic practices. as we have already criticised the common immigration policy as being security-oriented, criminalising, exploitative and selective towards immigrants. we are in favour of an immigration policy which respects the rights of immigrants, particularly in terms of access to employment, health care and education. despite these longstanding positions, we believe that the decision to join schengen must be taken by a sovereign decision of the countries concerned (another longstanding position). that is why we abstained.
in writing. − these states, being parties to the schengen agreement, must also contribute to its development by actively participating in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers in implementing, applying and developing the schengen acquis. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the council has submitted to the european parliament a draft agreement between the european union and the republic of iceland, the principality of liechtenstein, the kingdom of norway and the swiss confederation concerning the participation of these states in the work of the committees which assist the european commission in the exercise of its executive powers with regard to the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis. i voted in favour of the agreement, since the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs has not raised any objections to the conclusion of the agreement, which can add value to the smooth functioning of the schengen area.
in writing. − this recommendation allows iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland to participate effectively in the work of the committees on which the ec exercises its executive power in the context of the implementation, application and development of the schengen acquis. i agree that the ep should endorse this recommendation, which allows the associated states themselves to have rights and obligations. the abovementioned countries have observer status in the schengen committees, their representatives cannot vote but must be informed of the acts and measures to be applied, and they contribute financially to administrative expenses. finally, a joint declaration was annexed which states that this agreement will not have repercussions on other matters. the development of the schengen area requires that the countries which are parties to it fully comply with their obligations, so that a genuine european area without frontiers can be achieved.
in writing. the schengen agreement, created in 1985 and the convention for its application adopted in 1990, aimed to abolish internal border controls between the signatory states and to create a single external border with common visa rules, to establish police and judicial cooperation and to create a schengen information system. we have always criticised this approach to building a fortress europe, which encourages the development of racism and xenophobia and other forms of intolerance and authoritarian and anti-democratic practices. the construction of fortress europe, the europe of schengen, is being carried out through a common immigration policy of a security-oriented, criminalising, exploitative and selective nature. and we are in favour of an immigration policy in which member states respect the rights of immigrants, particularly in terms of access to employment, health care and education. despite these observations, we do not consider that we should comment on the decisions of the countries concerned (iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland) in relation to the agreements signed with the european union.

in writing. − in accordance with article 145 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the member states and the community are working to develop a coordinated european union strategy for employment and for the promotion of a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce. the europe 2020 strategy puts the european union on the right track towards the desired sustainable, inclusive and multiplier-effect economic growth, which allows for a high level not only of employment but also of social cohesion, productivity and competitiveness. within the framework of the objectives previously set to increase labour market participation and reduce structural unemployment, to develop a skilled workforce and to promote quality employment and lifelong learning, to improve the performance of education and training systems at all levels and to increase participation in higher education, as well as to promote social inclusion and the fight against poverty, it is considered that these guidelines should remain unchanged until 2014 and that their update should be strictly limited after that date. i agree with the rapporteur and therefore vote in favour of this report.
