in writing. − the political agreement reached with this report on a multiannual radio spectrum policy programme will pave the way for a development that will enable the european union to take global leadership in broadband speeds, mobility, coverage and capacity. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it can be an essential foundation for the creation of a flexible and coordinated european radio spectrum policy, allowing for exponential growth in mobile data traffic through future reallocation and putting inefficient use of spectrum in the past. the studies indicate that the approval by member states of the proposal of the parliament and the council to open the 800 mhz band to electronic communications services by january 2013 will contribute to the creation of a pan-european telecommunications market, where new services can create opportunities and growth for a market of 500 million consumers.
in writing. − the legislative procedure for adopting a multiannual programme in the field of radio spectrum policy was launched with the proposal for a decision presented by the european commission on 20 september 2010. the european parliament therefore adopted its position at first reading on 11 may 2011, with a number of amendments. however, following five informal trilogues, the european parliament and the council reached agreement on the legislative proposal. following the work carried out in the course of a cooperation procedure between the various institutions, i voted in favour of the european parliament's position at second reading, in the hope that the regulation reached will contribute to the vitality and dynamism of the european economy.
in writing. − in september 2010, the european commission adopted three complementary measures to facilitate the deployment and uptake of fast and ultrafast broadband in the european union. in may 2011, the european parliament adopted its opinion at first reading, making 88 amendments to the proposal submitted by the european commission. among the amendments adopted, the commission emphasises the expansion of unlicensed spectrum allocations to allow for greater use of wi-fi technology and the guarantee of broadband access to all eu citizens at a speed of at least 30 mbps by 2020. i support the second reading proposal put forward by the european parliament because i believe it is an important means for the eu to take global leadership in broadband speeds, mobility, coverage and network capacity. i also believe that we will achieve exponential growth in mobile data traffic, which will enable the creation of a pan-european telecommunications market benefiting some 500 million consumers.
in writing. − this proposal sets out the policy guidelines and objectives for strategic planning and harmonisation of the use of radio spectrum by 2015. we agree that there is a need for planning and organisation of radio spectrum, and we consider it essential that this be done within the framework of cooperation between member states, preserving it as a public good and free from the commission's guidelines, in particular those relating to putting radio spectrum at the service of the eu 2020 strategies, the digital agenda for europe and the single market act. policies that claim to aim at improving the market, competitiveness and competition for the launch of the so-called digital single market have, in fact, contributed greatly to the worsening of the crisis of capitalism and its negative consequences for the populations. radio spectrum from low to very high frequencies is being contested and filled for multiple purposes, paving the way for the business of future digital services at union level and stimulating effective competition. however, it is essential to preserve and defend the space for public access and to prevent its total commitment to commercial purposes, which is the direction towards which the policies of the european union are inclined.
in writing. - i abstain on this report because i consider it a lost opportunity. it covers positive elements such as the strengthening of the role of producer organisations and inter-branch organisations and contractual aspects, but it could have gone further and taken advantage of the opportunity to achieve another ordering of the milk hierarchies in the eu. the need to go beyond improving the self-regulatory status of the relationship between actors in the area. this sector must be framed above all in terms of an agriculture which we want to see in europe having access to a fair distribution of value in the food chain and which does not become an agriculture of large intensive farms concentrated in a few member states.
in writing. - this report is important because it is primarily intended not to prejudice the effective functioning of cooperatives and for reasons of clarity it should be specified that where a producer, by virtue of belonging to a cooperative, is subject to an obligation, in respect of all or part of that producer's milk production, to deliver raw milk for which conditions have been laid down in the statutes of the cooperative or in the rules and decisions based thereon, those conditions should not be the subject of negotiation through a producer organisation. moreover, in order to maintain effective competition on the market for milk and milk products, this possibility should be subject to appropriate limits expressed as a percentage of the union production and the production of any member state covered by the negotiations. the limit expressed as a percentage of national production should first apply to the volume of raw milk produced in the member state of production or in each of the member states of production. the same limit should also apply to the volume of raw milk supplied to a member state of destination.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on contractual relations in the milk and milk products sector because it contains positive proposals, particularly as regards strengthening the bargaining power of producers. however, these are insufficient for the future sustainability of the sector and i therefore consider it necessary to ensure effective supply management instruments.
in writing. - the deep crisis in the dairy sector makes it urgent to adopt more effective measures to support producers and, i continue to advocate, to think very deeply about the abolition of milk quotas in 2015. as we've always said, this is a mistake and it's not too late to make amends. stabilisation of the milk and milk products market will not be achieved by one-off measures alone, but by medium-term solutions to maintain production in a sustainable way, without neglecting the right of consumers to a fair price. it is essential to give producers more power and to ensure the necessary price stability. i would point out in this connection the particular competitive weakness of the outermost regions, which are heavily concentrated on dairy activity, such as the azores.
in writing. - the cap reform which introduced a quota policy in milk production has not had the desired effect and we have farmers who have invested in buying quotas in short supply. with the end of the quotas announced - to which some member states are opposed - it is imperative to adopt regulatory measures to ensure the normal functioning of the sector and to guarantee producers a fair income so that they do not abandon their activity. while i am aware that this legislation will not solve all the problems of farmers, i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 as regards contractual relations in the milk and milk products sector, because i consider that farmers see their positions strengthened in relation to negotiation with distributors, being able to negotiate directly 33% of national production. in addition, member states may opt for a european contract, with a minimum validity of six months, negotiated individually or by cooperatives.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation does not solve the problems currently facing the sector. thousands of dairy farms continue to close, with the price of milk paid to the producer failing to compensate for the high costs of production. it is an illusion to think that this regulation - whose assumptions are based on the wonderful idea of the peaceful coexistence between the lion and the lamb - will solve the problems created by the decision to eliminate milk quotas, which led to their increase, with a view to the so-called soft landing - which has been anything but soft for thousands and thousands of farmers. what is needed is to reverse the decision to end production quotas in 2015, adapting them to the needs of each country and the relative level of development of its production capacity (allowing the relative evolution of the member states with the largest deficits). the commissioner's argument that the milk crisis of 2009 occurred with the existing quota system is regrettable, which shows its futility. the crisis is actually the result of a situation which, to some extent, already anticipates the end of quotas, given the decision to increase them. so the crisis is the result of the decision to end quotas and not the other way around!
in writing. − exceptional events in the milk and milk products sector were recorded between 2007 and 2009. in a first phase, extreme weather conditions in oceania caused a significant supply shortage, which led to a rapid and significant increase in prices. moreover, although global supply had started to recover and prices to normalise, the ensuing economic and financial crisis had a negative impact on eu milk and milk products producers, exacerbating price volatility. first, the costs of feed and other factors of production, notably energy, have increased significantly, reflecting higher raw material prices. in october 2009, in view of the difficult situation on the milk market, the high level expert group on the dairy sector was set up to discuss medium and long-term measures for the milk and milk products sector, due to the abolition of milk quotas in 2015. in the light of the results of the health examination, the high level group should work on the development of a regulatory framework capable of stabilising the market and producers' incomes and enhancing transparency. this is a sector of great importance to my country, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - as in the agricultural sector in general, the milk and milk products sector has been facing a number of difficulties, with a drop in demand and a sharp fall in prices in recent years. the high level expert group on the dairy sector was therefore set up in october 2009 and brought together professionals in the field with a view to finding solutions to bring the sector back into balance. in this context, one of the points that needs to be corrected most rapidly is the restoration of the balance of trade between producer and distributor. in fact, the profound disparity in economic power between the two sides leads in many cases to the suffocation of milk producers. in this context, the introduction of the possibility of concluding collective agreements, similar to that in labour law, between associations of producers and distributors is to be equated. it is therefore urgent to find solutions to restore the normal functioning of the market, otherwise the current weaknesses will worsen very substantially with the abolition of quotas in 2015. that being the spirit of the resolution, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the production and processing of milk and milk products in the european union varies considerably from one member state to another and within each member state there are large variations between operators and types of operators. the concentration of supply is reduced, resulting in an imbalance between producers and dairies in terms of bargaining power in the supply chain, which can lead to unfair trading practices. the rapporteur therefore put forward proposals on contracts, the bargaining power of producers, inter-branch organisations and transparency to improve the bargaining power of producers.
in writing. - this regulation will not solve the problems created by the decision to eliminate milk quotas which has affected thousands and thousands of farmers. thousands of dairy farms continue to close, with the price of milk paid to the producer failing to compensate for the high costs of production. what is needed is to reverse the decision to end production quotas in 2015, adapting them to the needs of each country and the relative level of development of its production capacity.
in writing. - i approve this report because of the low regard which the european institutions currently have for the european parliament's owninitiative reports, since they are not ordinary legislative procedures. the report stresses that the role of own-initiative reports is strengthened, that they are considered as strategic reports and that the way in which they are dealt with should be improved.
in writing. i voted in favour of this amendment because it will incorporate the following amendment into its rules of procedure: the motions for resolutions contained in the own-initiative reports will be considered by parliament in accordance with the short-setting procedure laid down in rule 139. amendments to these motions for resolutions may be tabled in plenary only if they are tabled by the rapporteur in order to take account of new information or by at least one tenth of the members of parliament. political groups may table alternative motions for resolutions in accordance with rule 157 (4). rules 163 and 167 shall apply to the committee's motion for a resolution and to amendments thereto. rule 167 shall also apply to the single vote on alternative motions for resolutions. this paragraph shall not apply where the subject of the report warrants a priority debate in plenary, where the report is drawn up in accordance with the rights of initiative referred to in articles 41 or 42, or where the report has been authorised as a strategic report.
in writing. - in order to respond to the need to improve the handling of own-initiative reports, especially as regards the plenary stage, a number of recommendations were adopted by the conference of presidents. this initiative aims to introduce the necessary amendments to the ep's rules of procedure to incorporate the decision taken by the conference of presidents that own-initiative reports drawn up on the basis of the annual activity reports and the accompanying reports (annexes 1 and 2 to annex xviii to the rules of procedure) should be considered as strategic reports, in accordance with the criteria set by the conference of presidents. as regards the application of rule 163 (partisan votes) to own-initiative reports, it is provided that this rule does not apply except in the case of reports provided for in the final part of rule 48 (2), i.e. where the report concerns a subject which is to be the subject of a key debate in plenary, where the report has been drawn up in accordance with rule 41 or 42, or where the report has been given a mandate to become a strategic report. it is also clarified that nominative voting requests, article 167, should only be allowed for the final vote, with the same exception as had been provided for in article 163.
in writing. − own-initiative reports are an important way of exercising parliamentary function and have enabled parliament to look in greater detail at matters that would otherwise have escaped its scrutiny. despite these unmistakable qualities, this house must resist the temptation to occupy most of its time with non-legislative reports. this resolution seeks to improve the regimental framework of this figure and its link with the conference of presidents. i hope that the proposed amendments will have the desired effect and that parliament's rules of procedure will become an increasingly important legal instrument to strengthen and inform the action of members and, consequently, less and less a bureaucratic obstacle to this action which is to be free, active and well informed.
in writing. the present report, drawn up by mr stanimir ilchev, concerns the amendment of rule 48 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure as regards so-called own-initiative reports. this proposed amendment follows the conference of presidents on 7 april 2011 where, with a view to improving the treatment of own-initiative reports, it was decided that own-initiative reports based on the annual activity reports and the accompanying reports (annexes 1 and 2 to annex xviii to the rules of procedure - decision no 202) should be treated as strategic reports within the meaning of the last sentence of rule 48 (2) of the rules of procedure.
in writing. these amendments to the rules of procedure, which are being promoted by the majority which dominates parliament - the holy alliance between the right and social democracy - do not reflect a democratic strengthening of the institution. quite the opposite. the amendment to rule 48 (2) for example seeks to limit the possibilities for political groups to intervene in the tabling of amendments, in separate voting requests and in roll-call votes on points included in own-initiative reports, when these are only briefly presented. the aim is to assert parliament's place in the interinstitutional dispute in the eu by making the own-initiative reports appear to be a consensus, which is thus a forged consensus. it is regrettable and reprehensible that they are trying to limit the intervention of the political groups and, in particular, of the group of the unitary left/nordic green left - which unquestionably embodies an alternative project to this eu: that of a social europe, of workers and peoples.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending rule 48 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure, which concerns own-initiative reports, thus clarifying the procedure for voting on commission motions for resolutions and amendments thereto, and defining what should be considered a strategic report.

in writing. − in view of the current unique situation of the euro area, with member states sharing a currency without a common fiscal policy and without a single bond market, and with increased concern about the ongoing tensions in the euro area sovereign bond markets, reflected in spreads of increasing amplitude and enormous volatility, i approve this report, considering that the prospect of stability bonds can boost medium-term stability in the euro area, and that the ratification of an emff treaty and/or eurobonds, as well as the joint management of sovereign bond issues, are essential.
in writing. − given the unique situation of the euro area, the sovereign debt crisis and the high interest rates faced by the weakest economies, there is a consensus on the importance of stability bonds as an element of stabilisation, confidence building, convergence and growth in the euro area. stability bonds would allow sovereign debt risks to be shared, market volatility to be reduced and the euro area to be put back on a path of greater integration, which will be the basis for a revival of economic growth. and there would be other advantages, notably in terms of lowering the cost of debt, affirming the euro as the world's currency of reference, making markets more efficient and reducing speculative attacks. this resolution, which i supported, stresses the need for swift action to resolve the sovereign debt crisis, calling on the european commission to take concrete action.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the euro as a currency in the euro area. it presents considerations on the importance of implementing the stability obligations and some notes on the green paper on stability obligations presented by the european commission. given the unique situation of the euro area, the sovereign debt crisis and the high interest rates faced by the weakest economies, there is a consensus on the importance of stability bonds as an element of stabilisation, confidence building, convergence and growth in the euro area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the introduction of stability bonds will contribute to the efficiency of the bond market and the euro area financial system in general. eurobonds are not a recipe for all evils, but they are an important component of the medium-term solutions. the common bond issue will also require greater budgetary coordination with a view to better economic governance.
in writing. the motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure, following the question for an oral answer by mrs sharon bowles and mrs sylvie goulard, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, concerns the feasibility of introducing stability bonds. the possibility of introducing stability obligations has given rise to several studies, including the commission green paper of 23 november 2011 and the interim report of president van rompuy of 6 december 2011 entitled 'towards a stronger economic union'. the euro area is the issuer of the second largest international currency, and member states should take full advantage of euro issues, as it has the potential to become a global reserve currency. considering that these bonds can contribute to the stability of the euro area and to the efficiency of its financial system, which is currently vulnerable to speculative attacks, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution as it will also contribute to the relaunch of the european economy.
in writing. - the designation now given by the european commission to the (long-standing) so-called 'eurobonds' - stability bonds - denotes their inherent prerequisite: the deepening of economic and budgetary governance, as it has been advocated and put into practice by the eu's governing board. that is to say, with unacceptable limitations on the sovereignty of countries and peoples in areas essential to the determination of their collective duty. the strategic objective here is not economic growth, job creation and the fight against social inequalities, but the affirmation of the euro as the world reserve currency, which is contrary to the interests of the peoples of the peripheral countries. this mechanism does not guarantee the end of speculative attacks, and it also maintains differentiations in the interest rates on financing in each of the countries. what is needed are not measures which years ago, in the context of a discussion of a profound change in the economic policies of the european union, could have served as shock absorbers for speculation. what is needed now is to reverse the course taken and to abolish economic governance, the euro plus pact, the new european treaty.
in writing. − the ongoing tensions in the euro area sovereign bond markets are worrying and are reflected in increasingly wide spreads, high volatility, vulnerability and speculative attacks over the past two years. the euro area, as the issuer of the world's second largest international currency, is partly responsible for the stability of the international monetary system. it is therefore in the long-term strategic interest of the euro area and its member states to reap as much as possible the benefits of issues in euro, a currency with the potential to become a global reserve currency. it should be noted that the us treasury bond market and the euro area sovereign bond market are of comparable size but do not have the same liquidity, diversity and price formation. however, it may be in the interest of the euro area to develop a common, liquid and diversified bond market and that, once a culture of stability is credibly established in the euro area, a stability bond market could offer a viable alternative to the us dollar bond market and establish the euro as a safe-haven currency. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on stability bonds, i.e. the issuance of public debt by eu member states with mutual guarantee of the other states, because i agree that this is part of a genuine budgetary union. as the resolution says, we have had a common currency without a common budgetary policy and without a common bond market. once fiscal integration is consolidated, there will be no reason not to have a mutually guaranteed government debt issue (which will still require a revision of the treaties). what could not be achieved, as some hastily claimed, were eurobonds without the establishment of a budgetary union. no state can be asked to take responsibility for the debt of another if there is no mutual control of their budgets. the recent budgetary pact is an important step forward in the right direction.
in writing. − this resolution is a preliminary response to the commission's green paper and will be followed by a more comprehensive resolution in the form of an own-initiative report. the report is presented as a contribution to the current discussion on stability obligations and their relevance as an important component in the resolution of the crisis in the euro area, and presents considerations on the importance of the implementation of stability obligations. given the unique situation of the euro area, the sovereign debt crisis and the high interest rates faced by the weakest economies, stability obligations are inevitable and must be combined with effective measures to promote growth and increase the competitiveness of the european economy.
in writing. the european commission, following a request to this effect from the european parliament, presented a green paper on the introduction of stability bonds. without prejudice to a more detailed analysis, which will be deferred to a later date, the document presented should be welcomed now, as it can form a relevant basis for work at a later date. if it is true that the euro is a central currency for the international monetary system and that it also has the potential to become a global reserve currency, it is also certain that this can only be the case if the monetary governance of the union is equipped with instruments to ensure the stability of the currency. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. i have to say that i am very pleased with the way the commission has handled this matter.
in writing. - over the past few months, the european institutions have been discussing the possible introduction of stability bonds, in order to solve the problems of the various member states which are faced with high interest rates when they wish to finance themselves on international markets. in november 2011, the european commission published the green paper on stability bonds to assess the feasibility of introducing eurobonds between the various euro area countries. i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that this is the appropriate way to strengthen economic governance, to promote the efficiency of the bond market and the financial system of the euro area and to ensure greater stability in the international monetary system. however, i believe that it is of paramount importance to strengthen the sustainability of public finances, as only in this way will it be possible to create the best conditions for the introduction of stability obligations. finally, i believe that bonds can contribute to greater medium-term stability in the euro area and that the european commission must now come forward with concrete proposals to solve the current sovereign debt crisis once and for all.
in writing. the euphemistic form in which eurobonds are called - stability bonds - is based on a prerequisite which we reject - the deepening of economic and budgetary governance, which will lead to a marked transfer of sovereignty to the great powers. the strategic objective here is not economic growth, job creation and the fight against social inequalities, but the affirmation of the euro as the world reserve currency, which is contrary to the interests of the peoples of the peripheral countries. this mechanism does not guarantee the end of speculative attacks, and it also maintains differentiations in the interest rates on financing in each of the countries. what is needed are not measures which years ago, in the context of a discussion of a profound change in the economic policies of the european union, could have served as shock absorbers for speculation. what is needed at this moment is to reverse the course taken and to repeal the economic governance, the euro plus pact and the budgetary pact. it will not be in the framework of the deepening of federalism that the process of extortion, colonization and exploitation that is under way in the process of capitalist integration of the european union will be broken.
in writing. - i support this report, considering that the budgetary consolidation approach must be based on social justice so as not to increase the risk of poverty and must take into account the necessary additional efforts made by households to combat unemployment and mitigate the social problems arising from the crisis. the main objective should be to promote growth in the short, medium and long term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that people on the verge of retirement, the longterm unemployed, third country nationals and low-skilled workers are among those most affected by the crisis. i know that the labour market situation is particularly critical for all young people, regardless of their level of education, that they end up accepting precarious employment contracts and unpaid traineeships, and that the difficult situation of young people is partly due to the mismatch between acquired skills and demand in the labour market, so i supported the report in question.

in writing. given that the level of data protection in the eu is much higher and more comprehensive than in the vast majority of third countries, it was important to enshrine the extraterritorial scope of the directive, so as to prevent european companies from being able to transfer personal data to their facilities outside europe, with offshore processing so as to render the application of the strict limits imposed by the directive unenforceable. the directive prohibits the transfer of personal data to any third country which does not have an adequate level of data protection. at present, the number of countries which the commission considers to meet this criterion is very small. it is unacceptable that cases such as swift can occur, where, in the context of internal company transfers, european personal data, because they are on american territory, have to be made available to american authorities, thus cancelling out the rights and guarantees offered by european legislation to citizens and businesses. it is necessary and urgent to adopt the necessary measures to ensure the effective application of european data protection rules and to prevent the law of third countries from taking precedence over community law in protecting the interests of european citizens and eu-based companies.

in writing. - i support this report because i consider it essential to protect the interests of citizens who put their life savings in banks. the guarantee system and the means of benefiting from it have made progress, but more needs to be done, both at the level of individual member states and at the level of the european union, as it is essential that people have confidence and trust in the credibility of financial institutions, otherwise the removal of depositors could jeopardise the financial stability of these institutions. the formulation of common applicable requirements allows member states to have conditions at a harmonised level that avoids distortion of competition, thereby protecting depositors and contributing to the stability of the financial system.
in writing. − currently, in the event of a credit institution's bankruptcy, deposit guarantee schemes (dgss) in place in the different eu member states compensate depositors up to the agreed coverage level of eur 100 000 per depositor. the repayment period is 30 working days at the most. this system guarantees the confidence of depositors, but if it is not sufficient to protect them credibly and guarantee their repayments, it is the states and taxpayers who bear the bankruptcies of credit institutions. this report, which i supported, proposes a differentiated approach by defining common requirements for all sgds, while maintaining sufficient flexibility as regards the specific aspects of their mode of operation. it also sets out concrete measures on common requirements for a wide protection of depositors and uniform conditions for the stability of dgss within the eu, the flexibility of preventive and stability support measures, realistic repayment terms for depositors, european dgss and the promotion of cooperation at european level. these measures aim to ensure common requirements for sgds that allow for uniform conditions of protection, the same level of stability and the absence of distortion of competition.

in writing. − in 2008, the bankruptcy of lehman brothers, the fourth largest investment bank in the united states, sent a tsunami through financial circles because of fears of defaulting on its obligations to its clients. as the global crisis worsened, other banks failed, and depositors were not always able to recover their savings. this has led to a certain degree of public distrust in financial institutions which needs to be restored. the report under review, by peter simon, deals with the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on deposit guarantee schemes at first reading. i welcome this proposal for a directive aimed at creating a deposit guarantee fund, because the taxpayer cannot be the one to pay for the financial problems of the banks. on the contrary, citizens should have guarantees that in the event of a bank failure, their deposits will not be affected and will be repaid in a timely manner. i voted in favour of this report because the new regulation will be an asset for the european citizen and society through guarantees and harmonization, thus contributing to the construction of a single market for financial services at european union level.
in writing. − this proposal for a directive on deposit-guarantee schemes (dgs) aims to establish common requirements in the different member states concerning the protection of depositors in the event of the bankruptcy of a credit institution. the proposal contains relevant and other aspects which give rise to our concern and serious reservations. the rapporteur proposes to increase the level of protection for depositors by establishing the legal right to a maximum refund of eur 100 000 and a faster refund period. on the one hand, this directive is another step towards the full realisation of the eu's internal market in financial services - a highly sensitive area for a variety of reasons at the moment. the rapporteur's proposal even leaves open the possibility of merging dgss from different member states and voluntarily creating their own cross-border systems. it does not specify which institutions are responsible for financing sgds. the state, i.e. the taxpayers, cannot bear the consequences of the bankruptcy of credit institutions when sgds do not have sufficient funding. this aspect should be ensured in the directive.
in writing. − in the event of a credit institution's failure, deposit guarantee schemes (dgss) currently in force in the different eu member states compensate depositors up to the agreed coverage level. during the financial and economic crisis, the amount of that coverage level was increased, under directive 2009/14/ec of the european parliament and of the council, initially from eur 20 000 to eur 50 000 and finally to eur 100 000 per depositor on 1 january 2011. at the same time, the repayment period in case of compensation was reduced to a maximum of 30 working days. the increased level of coverage enhances depositors' confidence and prevents the so-called deposit run, i.e. the withdrawal of large numbers of depositors. however, a higher level of coverage alone is not sufficient to protect depositors in a credible way. in order to avoid the danger of a run on deposits and a possible destabilisation of financial markets, dgss should also be provided with the necessary financial resources. the combination of measures provided for in this directive aims to enhance depositors' confidence and the stability of the european financial system, contributing to the completion of the single market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on deposit guarantee schemes (dgs) in the various eu member states. the system currently provides for compensation up to the agreed coverage level of eur 100 000 per depositor. the repayment period in the case of compensation shall be no more than 30 working days. this report recognises the heterogeneity of the different banking sectors in the eu and proposes a differentiated approach by defining common requirements for all dgss while maintaining sufficient flexibility in the specific aspects of their mode of operation. the aim is to ensure common requirements for dgss that allow for uniform conditions of protection, the same level of stability and non-distortion of competition, but also the greatest possible flexibility in the design of dgss so that they are adapted to the specificities of the financial markets in each member state. the aim being to ensure effective protection of depositors and the stability of the financial system, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − deposit guarantee schemes should be analysed from a two-fold perspective: the degree to which the rights of depositors are protected and the entities on which the responsibility for such protection lies. the report under review supports a line of action to strengthen the guarantees given to depositors, based on greater accountability of financial institutions, in order to provide the dgss with resources to cope with crises and to avoid that responsibility falling on taxpayers through public involvement. this is the fairest, most responsible and best way for the institutions to conduct their work. for these reasons, i shall vote in favour of the report.

in writing. − multiannual management plans are an important tool for the sustainable management of fisheries resources. this is what is recognized by this resolution. in the case of the western stock unit of carp (the most commercially important stock in european waters), the multiannual plan aims to maintain the biomass of this unit at a level that ensures its sustainable exploitation and the highest long-term yield. this objective is compromised by the institutional blockade that has been preventing the approval and effective implementation of the plan. we are facing a war between parliament and the council, in which parliament wants to assert its co-decision power, considering that the council cannot reserve the power to adapt unilaterally the parameters defined in the proposal for the fixing of total allowable catches, since these are essential components of the proposed long-term plan. the resolution adopted stresses that the existing interinstitutional deadlock must be resolved in the interests of the sustainability of fish stocks and to enable fishermen to plan their activities better. the council also called for the establishment of a european union-wide network of experts in the field of the environment.
in writing. − the multiannual plans are the cornerstone of the common fisheries policy and a key tool for its conservation, laying down the general provisions necessary for the pursuit of the objectives of the common fisheries policy, which in turn must be adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure, in accordance with article 43 (2) tfeu. those plans aim to maintain the biomass of the western stock of carp at a level that ensures its sustainable exploitation and the highest long-term yield. the control rule for the holding shall be based in equal parts on precautionary opinions and on the most recent total allowable catches, adjusted by a factor reflecting the recent evolution of the abundance of the stock measured through egg production. the rules on farm monitoring are therefore fundamental elements of the multiannual plans and should be decided under the ordinary legislative procedure.

in writing. - today we are examining the first democratic constitution of hungary after the communist dictatorship and the legislation related to it. they deserve respect as the emanation of the will of the representatives of their people. unlike the preamble to the draft constitution for europe, which attempted to erase the christian heritage from common european references, the text of the hungarian constitution takes on this heritage and the civilizational and human values that flow from it. it did so without closing itself off to other values and without seeking to make a tabula rasa of its history. it should be noted that, despite the attacks on questions of customs, tradition and christianity launched by a certain left - in whose midst the heirs and defenders of communism abound - it is those relating to the separation of powers which have been relevant to the european commission. the hungarian government has been receptive to answering all the questions put to it and has been ready to review the legislation adopted whenever this is justified.
in writing. - the political situation in hungary has been discussed several times in this parliament. in july 2011, a motion for a resolution was tabled and discussed but not voted condemning hungary for failing to guarantee compliance with the principles and values defended by the european union. on 18 january, hungarian prime minister viktor orbán was here to explain the government's policy options and his country's basic law, which incorporated the eu charter of fundamental rights in its entirety. the european parliament cannot interfere in the approval of a member state's constitution, which would be considered an interference in the sovereignty of a state (this is something that should be judged by the citizens of that country). the commission is responsible for dialogue with the hungarian government to overcome any possible non-conformity with the eu treaties. although the new hungarian constitution was voted for by a majority of the democratically elected hungarian parliament and replaced the communist constitution of 1949, i believe that the european commission, which is the guardian of the treaties, must ensure that they are strictly observed.
in writing. - we express our concern and disquiet at the undemocratic escalation of the hungarian government and the adoption of measures of a fascinating nature in various areas of social life. at the same time, we also express our full solidarity with the hungarian people and all those in hungary who are fighting for freedom, democracy, justice and social progress. but we cannot accept the interference of the european institutions in the internal affairs of a sovereign state, which others have been defending. nor can we accept that the european commission - the same commission which signs, imposes and applies the imf-eu aggression pacts in portugal, greece and ireland - should be given the role of guardian of freedoms and democracy. the way forward is not a choice between two versions of social regression - the hungarian government's and the eu's. it is clear that the european commission and certain sectors of social democracy are not concerned about the new hungarian labour code, the backsliding on workers' rights that it implies, the attack on social rights, the intervention of the imf, in short, the cruel demands for social backsliding that the so-called austerity measures are imposing.
in writing. − the new hungarian constitution was approved on 18 april 2011 by the hungarian parliament by a large and legitimate majority. this new constitution replaces the communist constitution of 1949, as hungary was the only country in central europe that had not yet adopted a new basic law since the fall of communism. this new constitution incorporated the charter of fundamental rights in full and created a fairer electoral system, which guarantees the representation of minorities in parliament. it is therefore necessary that union law respects the competence of the member states to adopt their constitutions in compliance with the principles and values on which the eu is founded; however, it remains necessary for the hungarian government to work closely with the commission to ensure that the new national legislation complies with union law and, if necessary, to make the necessary amendments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree with the european parliament's support for the european commission's role in ensuring that national legislation is in conformity with the treaties of the european union and with the fundamental european values and, only in this context, i support the commission's assessment of the new hungarian organic laws.
in writing. - following the adoption of the new hungarian constitution in april last year and numerous organic laws of the state, many voices indicated that there was a backsliding in hungarian democracy. the european parliament has voted in favour of the commission's proposal to amend the law on the protection of personal data. in the ec letter to the hungarian government, the commission expressed serious concerns, in particular with regard to the independence of the national central bank, the data protection authority and the judiciary. however, many ngos accuse the hungarian authorities of encroaching on freedom of expression, religion and sexual freedom. on the other hand, the hungarian government has passed several retroactive laws which violate one of the basic principles of european law. as hungary is a state governed by the rule of law and a member of the eu, i think it will be important for the laws that undermine the principles of democracy and freedom to be reviewed together with the ec. we cannot invoke certain principles and values in our foreign policy when we have states at home that do not comply with them.
in writing. the entry into force of the new constitution of hungary has provoked reactions of false indignation. those who were once the government are now the opposition (social-democracy) and those who were once the opposition are now the government (right). both sides are fighting for the hegemony of power, they fear the reaction of the people to the deepening of the crisis, they pretend to be fighting not for the content of policies but for the form. but both have shown themselves willing to submit their sovereignty and institutions to the eu treaties in order to safeguard the interests of the big capital they represent. it is not the hungarian people that the eu, the hungarian government and this (social democratic) opposition are concerned about. they do not even once refer to the new labour code and the backsliding on workers' rights that it entails, or to the intervention of the imf and the cruel demands for social backsliding that the so-called austerity measures are imposing. a great political and ideological distance separates us from the hungarian government and those who support it. we do not encourage interference in the internal affairs of hungary. we do not accept interference campaigns by those who have responsibility for the situation in the country with the aim of forcing changes from outside, changes which only the hungarian people can force.
in writing. − i approve this motion for a resolution, stressing my hope that the elections in march 2012 will be held in accordance with international standards. in my view, the reports that have come in about procedural violations, such as the lack of impartiality of the media, the lack of separation between party and state and the attempts to threaten independent monitoring, are worrying. all reports of corruption, fraud and intimidation must be thoroughly investigated and punished.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it urges the russian government to submit legislative proposals, in line with the osce recommendations, aimed at developing a genuinely democratic political system, so as to allow genuinely free and fair elections to be held as soon as possible.
in writing. - ivan krastev, mark leonard and andrew wilson in what does russia think? are particularly clear on one of the problems affecting europe as it tries to interact with russia: if we want to influence and deal with russia, we have to understand it. but if we want to understand russia, we must take an interest in it. in fact, there seems to be no genuine european interest in russia, or only a reactive and comparative interest in the face of our own standards, which, despite their importance, should not make us forget the geostrategic importance of the largest country in the world. russia is at the crossroads between liberal democracy and state capitalism and has recently shown signs of leaning towards the latter model, as seen in the recent veto on syria in the un security council. reports of free and fair electoral processes raise fears that the upcoming presidential elections may also fall short of international standards. russia would gain if it adopted these western standards of democracy, human rights and the rule of law, and the west would gain if it, in turn, became more interested in russian reality in order to better understand and influence it.
in writing. - the joint motion for a resolution tabled in replacement of the motions by the ppe, alde, greens/efa, s&d and ecr groups, deals with the presidential elections to be held in russia on 4 march and the results of the state duma (russian parliament) elections held on 4 december 2011. the presidential alternations between putin and medvedev in russia have raised some suspicions about the transparency of electoral processes in this country, as well as about respect for the democratic process. on 14 december 2011, this parliament adopted a resolution on the eu-russia summit, calling for the addressing of such problematic issues as energy, terrorism, corruption, respect for human rights and the holding of free elections. we have recently been confronted with the russian veto in the united nations security council when it voted on a motion condemning the syrian government for the massacres of civilians, which have already caused more than five thousand deaths.
in writing. - this resolution, like others which parliament has adopted in the past, does not avoid interference in russia's internal affairs. russia, despite its deep contradictions, is determined not to submit fully to the role which the eu powers, together with the usa, want to impose on it after the defeats of socialism in eastern europe. the european parliament's majority does not accept russia's veto of a set of resolutions proposed by the us and other powers in the un security council, including one aimed at speeding up a political transition in syria. they are thus using this resolution as a revenge, threatening it with intensifying support for the internal opposition and civil society. russia is a huge country with significant natural resources, abundant energy resources on which the eu is dependent and one of the world's greatest military powers. the majority in parliament acts with political, economic and diplomatic calculation, hostilizing it in order to try to subjugate it, a tendency that the crisis of capitalism accentuates with the confrontation between the main world powers, nato and regional powers such as russia.
in writing. − enhanced cooperation and good neighbourly relations between the eu and russia are of crucial importance for the stability, security and prosperity of europe; the development of a strategic partnership between the european union and the russian federation can only be based on shared common values. however, concerns remain about the russian federation's progress in respecting and protecting human rights and respecting generally accepted democratic principles, rules and processes. the russian federation is a full member of the council of europe and the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) and has therefore committed itself to respecting the principles of democracy and human rights. on 12 april 2011, the european court of human rights condemned the lengthy registration processes of political parties in russia, which do not respect the electoral standards set by the council of europe and the osce, and the limitations on the registration of political parties and candidates that restrict political debate and pluralism in russia. we must continue to encourage the russian leadership to adopt more democratic practices towards opposition parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution for condemning the police repression of peaceful demonstrations and agreeing with the call on the russian authorities to fully respect the freedoms of assembly and expression in accordance with the constitution of the russian federation.
in writing. - russia is a major player in the international arena, not only economically or territorially but also historically, and in particular for europe. the results of the evaluation of the last duma elections in december 2011 are therefore deeply concerned, as they reveal several violations of procedural rules essential for the validity of the election results. at the same time, outside the strict electoral period, there is a clear effort by the political power to control, beyond what should be its sphere of competence, the opponents of the regime, by adopting an authoritarian stance that is difficult to reconcile with the requirements of a state governed by the rule of law. against this background, i voted in favour of the joint resolution calling for a restructuring of the russian political and electoral system. only in this way, it seems, will russia be able to assume fully the role which is reserved for it in international reality.
in writing. - numerous violations were detected during the 4 december elections to the duma. the attacks on the electoral process by various ngos and the osce must not be repeated in the next presidential elections on 4 march, as stated by prime minister vladimir putin, who believes that russia needs to be democratized and to fight corruption in all areas of society. i think it is essential that the next elections be closely monitored, from the preparation of the elections to the electoral act itself, by the eu and international institutions, in order to avoid the recurrence of irregularities in the previous elections. however, it is necessary to ensure that election observers are not subject to pressure or blockage by local authorities. the russian people have already demonstrated that they want an open society in which values such as political pluralism, freedom of expression, assembly and the press are guaranteed as fundamental rights of a state governed by the rule of law. i would like to say again that i am looking forward to a democratization of the russian political system, so that it can have a voice and shape its future, giving expression to the capabilities of a country like russia.
in writing. - i shall abstain on this motion for a resolution. i believe that this agreement will be of benefit to the economic development of morocco, an important neighbour in the southern mediterranean which is going through a major process of democratization, and will allow the export of a number of european products with advantages. on the other hand, it is important to safeguard the interests of the regions of the european union, particularly at this time of crisis, which may be more vulnerable to this opening of the market, in particular those regions which have the most difficulty in getting their products out and which have these activities as the main sectors of their economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu-morocco agreement on the reciprocal liberalisation of agricultural and fishery products, because it could be an important instrument for the development of the southern mediterranean countries and help to alleviate the widespread poverty and unemployment which are at the root of economic, migration and security problems in the region.
in writing. - in view of what is happening on the southern shore of the mediterranean, it is essential that the european union gives clear signals that it intends to turn words into action and to strengthen its relationship with those countries. after the regrettable rejection by parliament of the protocol between the european union and the kingdom of morocco setting out the fishing opportunities and financial compensation provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the kingdom of morocco, i believe that the time has come not to close the door on the possibility of an understanding with one of the muslim countries which has recently shown the most moderation and reformist capacity. i am not unaware of the reservations that such liberalization raises, particularly among european agricultural and industrial producers. i hope that the practical application of this decision will be monitored in detail and that clauses will be provided to safeguard them in cases of special need. nevertheless, i believe that a significant opening up of these markets could lead to more opportunities for european investment and employment and greater consumer access to products produced in the southern mediterranean that meet the same strict hygiene and safety requirements as those imposed in the eu.
in writing. - cooperation between the european union and the kingdom of morocco dates back many years. since 1 march 2000, an association agreement between the eu and morocco has been in force, which provides for the gradual adoption of measures to liberalize reciprocal trade in agricultural and fishery products. the recent political developments in some countries in the southern mediterranean require a swift and effective response from the eu in terms of cooperation, so as to contribute to the deepening of the democratic process, while strengthening bilateral relations. this new agreement translates into more financial benefits for small moroccan farmers and improves the quality of products by introducing new phytosanitary requirements. although i consider it important to strengthen bilateral relations between the eu and the kingdom of morocco, which demonstrate our confidence in a country that is embarking on a process of democratic reforms, i abstained from voting on the report because i am not sure that small farmers in southern europe, particularly in portugal and spain, will not be harmed by this agreement.
in writing. - i declare that, by the way, i voted in favour in the final vote when i intended to abstain because i had doubts as to the possible impact of this liberalisation on portuguese agriculture and fisheries, despite indications to the contrary resulting from the technical opinions to which i had access (in particular from the committee on international trade) and from the recognition of the importance of the agreement for the political stabilisation of the mediterranean and for relations between this region and the european union.
in writing. - this resolution is more a profession of faith in free trade. it is stressed that the opening up of markets and progressive integration into the eu's internal market can be powerful tools for the development of the southern mediterranean countries and help to alleviate the widespread poverty and unemployment which are at the root of economic, migration and security problems in the region. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this includes within the eu itself, where the opening up and capitalist integration of the markets of economies with a very different degree of development has led to deepening inequalities. moreover, the rhetoric of the arab spring is not lacking here, let alone the repression which the moroccan regime continues to exercise against the sarawi people. forgetting the illegal occupation of the territory of western sahara. forgetting that even other countries, such as the us, which have signed similar trade agreements with morocco, explicitly provide for the exclusion of products originating in western sahara which the eu does not do. it is significant that right-wing meps from portugal, spain and italy (the countries whose farmers will be most affected) voted against this agreement. even though we have also, on other occasions, also the wonders of free trade...
in writing. - i voted against the eu-morocco agreement on the reciprocal liberalisation of agricultural and fishery products for two reasons. firstly, because i cannot accept that western sahara, one of the last territories in the world to be under colonial occupation, is treated as if it were under moroccan administration. secondly, because i believe that the agreement deepens an agricultural model which fails both sides, namely by destroying jobs, lowering the quality of production and subordinating food security.
in writing. - portugal is going through a difficult period, and the success of the fight against the crisis will depend to a large extent on national production and exports. the agreement in question will have an immediate impact, particularly in the southern european countries, including portugal, with competing products produced in the same plants, at the lowest cost, taking into account the price of the factors of production, without forgetting the need to safeguard food safety by the absence of plant protection products prohibited in the european area. that is the reason for the vote against, which does not invalidate the recognition of the importance of this and other agreements to be concluded with the kingdom of morocco, portugal's strategic partner, provided that all reciprocal guarantees are ensured.

in writing. - the political turbulence affecting the maghreb countries (in particular tunisia, egypt and libya) requires the attention of the community institutions, because of their geographical proximity to continental europe, in order to protect the common space. in the light of the experience of the european communities, economic cooperation, by introducing links of dependence and interrelationship between peoples, is a privileged mechanism for pursuing some of the central aims of the community project, such as the defence of the fundamental rights of individuals, the rule of law and the democratic legitimacy of government. the increase in economic relations between the two areas should, however, lead to a rapprochement of the moroccan development model, based on respect for people and the environment.
in writing. this motion for a resolution on the eu-morocco agreement on liberalization measures for agricultural products and processed agricultural products, fisheries and fishery products, sets out the points which explain my negative position on the conclusion of the agreement. i believe in the democratization reforms that morocco has been implementing, but the recent events that resulted in the arab spring have shown that the eu approach would have to be substantially modified. i also believe that trade liberalisation and the progressive integration of morocco into the eu will serve as instruments for the development of the economies of the southern mediterranean. however, i cannot support an agreement where no environmental, social and economic impact assessment has been carried out, where the same phytosanitary conditions are not required and where numerous cases of fraud in tariff agreements have been reported. on the other hand, there is the dispute over the western sahara region within the un, which should not be included in the un, since it is not moroccan territory. i abstained on this motion for a resolution because i am not against the liberalization of trade in agricultural products, but against this agreement itself.
in writing. − the fisheries sector, including aquaculture, generates an estimated €34.2 billion in annual revenues and supports more than 350 000 jobs in the eu. with the agreement with morocco, which has recently undertaken major democratic reforms, europe is giving concrete support to the development of the euro-mediterranean countries. this agreement represents an open door for the neighbouring countries that participated in the arab spring and the beginning of the development of the economic reforms needed in europe to create safer and fairer trading areas in the mediterranean. with this agreement, the european union will open its market to the mediterranean regions affected by the arab revolutions, which need investment and economic support in the transition to democracy. european farmers will be able to market and export their products to the euro-mediterranean markets and safeguard clauses provide for guarantees in the event of excess products on the markets.
in writing. - as a matter of principle and as an alternate member of the committee on international trade, i am in favour of all agreements aimed at closer approximation between the eu and third countries which commit themselves to approximate to our legislative standards. as president of the european parliament's delegation to morocco and vice-president of the eu-morocco friendship group, i welcome all agreements between the eu and the kingdom of morocco. that said, i would like to make it clear that i reject all forms of unfair competition with european businesses, whether it takes the form of dumping, abuse or illegality, in the light of the agreements signed. therefore, following the doubts raised in the agri committee (regarding the control of timetables and tariff quotas; respect for community legislative standards; geographical indications, problems of competitiveness and the unseasonality of imports from morocco), i decided to ask the commission and the council for clarification on this agreement, by means of a written question sent two weeks ago, in order to clarify whether there is any (disaggregated) economic impact study in the eu on this agreement. how does the commission intend to monitor compliance with community standards, the control of tariff quotas and the timetable? when will we have an agreement on the gis?
in writing. - despite the asymmetry in the liberalization of access to the european and moroccan markets and the difficulties that some producers may encounter in the face of increased competition, i believe that this agreement, on the whole, will be beneficial for european businesses, workers and consumers as it will allow easier access to an expanding market full of opportunities. politically, this will be another sign that the european union is not only proclaiming good intentions but is capable of committing itself effectively to the progress of north africa and of seeking to establish with it a partnership which will allow it not only to project its interests but also its soft power there. i understand the fears of european farmers, fishermen and industrialists, but i believe that the european union, for its own sake, has a duty to seek to strengthen its relationship with morocco and the other arab countries and to build a profitable and lasting trade relationship on which to build a stable and balanced relationship based on respect for the values of human dignity, human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. the recommendation under consideration concerns a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the kingdom of morocco concerning reciprocal liberalisation measures in the field of agricultural products and fisheries, replacing previous protocols and agreements. this new agreement will liberalise trade in fish, agricultural products, processed agricultural products and fishery products, which account for 45% of eu exports to morocco and 55% of eu imports from morocco. the committee on agriculture and rural development expressed serious reservations about this agreement and even voted against it. i voted against the agreement because i believe that small farmers in the eu could be harmed.
in writing. - the eu-morocco agreement adopted today means the immediate liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fisheries products. there were at least two strong reasons for the rejection of this agreement. on the one hand, it will be harmful to european producers, especially small and mediumsized producers of typically mediterranean crops, particularly in the fruit and vegetable sector, since this agreement will accentuate the pressure already felt to lower production prices and the difficulties felt by many producers in selling their products. portuguese farmers will be particularly targeted. on the other hand, family farming is losing out, facing competition from intensive, export-oriented production models. models that threaten environmental sustainability, the viability of regional and local markets, food sovereignty and that degrade food quality and safety. for these reasons, they also lose consumers and populations. the biggest beneficiaries will be the large european economic groups, the exporting multinationals, which will thus conquer new markets and gain access to cheap labour, as well as the possibility of better circumventing social, labour and environmental standards in force in european countries. finally, we cannot accept that the commission continues to ignore the question of western sahara, illegally occupied by morocco, in total disregard for international law.
in writing. - i voted against the eu-morocco agreement for the reciprocal liberalisation of agricultural and fishery products, not because it does not support the development of trade relations between the eu and morocco, which i consider crucial to encourage reforms in morocco's political and economic governance and thus meet the democratic aspirations of the moroccan people. i voted against, however, because i believe that the terms of this agreement are not in accordance with international law, because they ignore the need to establish a specific regime for trade in agricultural and fishery products produced in western sahara, a territory occupied by the kingdom of morocco since 1975. since parliament rejected the two amendments proposing the establishment of a regime specifically to take account of the rights and interests of the saharawi people within the framework of this agreement, i had no choice but to refuse to be complicit in an agreement which, as it stands, violates international law and the most elementary rights of the people of western sahara to dispose of their own resources.
in writing. - portugal is going through a difficult period, and the success of the fight against the crisis will depend to a large extent on national production and exports. the agreement in question will have an immediate impact, particularly in the southern european countries, including portugal, with competing products produced in the same plants at the lowest cost in terms of the price of the factors of production, without forgetting the need to safeguard food safety by virtue of the absence of plant protection products banned in europe. that is the reason for the vote against, which does not invalidate the recognition of the importance of this and other agreements to be concluded with the kingdom of morocco, portugal's strategic partner, provided that all reciprocal guarantees are ensured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the eu-morocco agreement on the liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fishery products because i believe it is a mutually beneficial agreement. the alleged negative impact on european farmers is being grossly underestimated. while not forgetting the benefits the agreement will bring to european exports, it is important to bear in mind that it provides for various safeguard clauses (quotas, prices, etc.) which limit any negative impacts of moroccan imports. i also believe that the question of western sahara has been satisfactorily resolved through clear commitments by the moroccan government and the european commission. finally, the political dimension of enhanced cooperation with morocco must be taken into account as a sign of the union's support for the political and constitutional developments leading to a democratic transition in that country.
in writing. - recognising the importance of good political relations with third countries, in particular with our neighbour the kingdom of morocco, and committed to good commercial relations, i cannot accept another step towards a so-called joint liberalisation which in fact creates a situation of profound inequality of competition between european and moroccan producers. europeans are bound by stringent and burdensome standards of quality and food safety, as well as by agrienvironmental and animal welfare standards, which considerably increase the cost of production, without the certification and labelling provided for protecting them sufficiently or leading the consumer to prefer their products to those produced to lower standards and at lower costs. the liberalization of 55% of morocco's exports to the eu and the increase in concessions in the fruit and vegetable sector would deal a severe blow to these productions in southern europe, particularly in portugal, but also in spain, italy and greece - all member states in difficulty that need to bet on their productive sectors and not, once again, see their agriculture sacrificed to other interests.
in writing. the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco aims to introduce reciprocal liberalisation measures for agricultural products, processed agricultural products, fish and fishery products. as it is expected that products imported from morocco will be able to enter directly the community market, a transitional period of gradual liberalisation applies to products exported from the eu to morocco. despite the reservations expressed by the rapporteur and the committee on agriculture and rural development, the agreement was approved overall following the positions of the committee on fisheries and the committee on international trade in the light of the current situation in which a cooperative approach between the european union and the north african states is required.
in writing. − the eu-morocco agreement on agricultural products, processed agricultural products, fish and fishery products will bring enormous competitive disadvantages to moroccan farmers. under this agreement, morocco automatically liberalises the agricultural sector, covering some 45% of eu exports, reaching 70% in 10 years. the eu, for its part, liberalises some 55% of the value of exports with the approval of the agreement. although the opening up will be more favourable to morocco in the long term, there are several points which put the eu at a disadvantage. firstly, i would like to stress that we must impose the same plant health measures and take into account that the cost of labour in morocco is substantially lower than in the eu. these two factors alone make agricultural products from the eu too expensive. secondly, there is the question of the western sahara region, which is included in the agreement and which, as a disputed territory in the un, should not be applied. finally, i would like to stress that this agreement will only benefit the large landowners, leaving out 90% of moroccan farmers. i believe that morocco is in the process of genuine democratization. however, i do not agree that agreements should be made at the expense of european agriculture.
in writing. - the eu-morocco agreement adopted today means the immediate liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fisheries products. the greatest losers from this agreement will be european producers, especially small and mediumsized producers of typically mediterranean crops, since this agreement will accentuate the pressure already felt to lower production prices and the difficulties felt by many producers in selling their products. family farming will lose out, having to compete with intensive, export-oriented production models. it should be stressed that the commission continues to ignore the problem of western sahara, illegally occupied by morocco, in total disregard for international law.
