in writing. − on 15 december 2011, i stated that despite the promises made by bashar al-assad at the time regarding a new constitution, free elections and individual and association freedom, the reality shows that, so far, these have been nothing but meaningless statements, which cannot but be regretted. the recent events in the city of homs demonstrate the lengths to which the syrian regime is prepared to go to secure its power and make even more glaring the urgency of an international response to put an end to such atrocities and ensure a consistent transition to democracy and the rule of law. i cannot but regret the blocking of an international action at the united nations security council by russia and china. this inaction, as the top human rights officials in that organization and many other credible institutions keep saying, leads to the maintenance of this unacceptable state of affairs in which entire populations are being sacrificed. the european union must remain firm in its condemnation of the syrian regime and in its search for a political solution that will bring an end to the hostilities and lead to the safety of the population and respect for its rights.
in writing. the political situation in syria is shocking the international community, which is watching helplessly as the syrian people are being slaughtered for more than 11 months, with more than 5 000 people dead. this parliament has not been indifferent and has repeatedly condemned the bloody repression ordered by president bashar al-assad. however, the sanctions adopted by the ep, the arab league and the un security council have not taken effect. the european union is also calling on the syrian authorities to take all necessary measures to ensure that the syrian regime is not subject to any further violence. the syrian opposition needs international support to bring about regime change, democracy and bring those responsible for human rights violations to justice. i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution, which replaces the proposals from the ecr, s&d, ppe, greens/efa and alde groups, because, in addition to condemning the veto of russia and china in the unsc, it calls for an end to the atrocities against the syrian people and for the creation of a humanitarian corridor to enable aid to be provided to all syrians who are suffering greatly.
in writing. the veiled threat of military aggression against syria is gradually taking on a clearer shape. the consequences of this choice could be dramatic and further destabilise the already unstable middle east region. we are facing the same pattern of operations that led to nato's military aggression in yugoslavia, iraq, afghanistan and libya, with the fomenting of internal divisions, the interference of secret services and special forces, the financing and arming of the opposition, with a campaign of vile media manipulation. none of these interventions have had positive consequences for these peoples. in addition to the thousands of dead and the destruction of important infrastructure, they have opened up political space for the most reactionary and backward forces in these countries. the majority in parliament, with this resolution, is blocking the way to the peaceful solution that was needed. it is in line with the disregard for the sovereignty of the syrian people and refuses to support national dialogue and diplomatic efforts within the un framework to stop the escalation of the internal situation. it is siding with the nato powers and the obscurantist and reactionary monarchies of the region in financing and supplying arms to groups which have attacked civilian populations, public buildings, kidnapped and killed innocent civilians.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution in which i underline the european parliament's support for the european commission's decision of 3 february 2012 to provide humanitarian assistance worth eur 3 million to alleviate the suffering of the people, both in syria and in neighbouring countries.
in writing. - the european parliament has, over the past few months, insistently drawn attention to the situation in syria. at this point, it's estimated that there have been over 5,400 deaths. the city of homs, for its part, has been continuously bombed, fearing that the syrian armed forces are moving towards a final solution of destroying the city. on the international level, despite the arab league's condemnation of the conduct of the syrian government bodies, the un security council, through the veto exercised by russia and china, chose not to take any position on syria. pressure must therefore be maintained on the syrian political establishment to change its political course soon, so that at some point it can change the course of events once and for all. i therefore voted in favour of the joint resolution.
in writing. the european parliament also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external relations are not jeopardised by the threat of a nuclear war. i hope that the violence against the syrian people will end, and i hope that the arab league will also make efforts to that end.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution, stressing the importance of the eu member states maintaining common positions on key issues to be discussed in the un human rights council, including freedom of expression on the internet, children's rights, torture and arbitrary detention in syria, libya, the democratic people's republic of korea, burma/myanmar, iran and the ivory coast. i would stress the importance of the member states agreeing positions in mini-councils on foreign policy, so as to ensure that the european union always has a single point of view in the international sphere. i believe that the credibility of the european union depends on its ability to speak with one voice. beyond this tactical question, it is important to highlight the question of the principles underlying these discussions: human dignity and human rights must always be paramount and should guide the eu's stance in international politics.
in writing. - human rights are part of the common heritage of the west but have long since moved beyond this to assert themselves as tending to be universal and to be invoked at all latitudes. the european union is therefore right to put them at the centre of its external action and, in particular, the european parliament is right to involve itself directly in the most important fora concerning it. i hope that at the 19th session of the un human rights council the union will live up to its history and contribute to affirming the human rights agenda in the global context. i would, however, wish that we could collectively moderate the generous impulse to label any and all rights as human or fundamental, or else we would be stripping those who are actually human of dignity and importance. i believe that a hypertrophy in these categories of rights does not contribute to its affirmation, but rather risks trivializing it.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution tabled under rule 110 (2) of the rules of procedure and following a statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, catherine ashton, on the position to be taken by the european parliament (ep) at the 19th session of the united nations human rights council (unhrc); respect for human rights is one of the most relevant issues debated in the ep, which is currently reviewing its position on human rights. in all its proposals for agreements or partnerships with third countries, this issue must be required as a sine qua non for the implementation of the proposed support. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, as it reflects the ep's concern on this matter, by pointing out the relevant issues to be addressed at the 19th session of the unhrc, the political situation in some countries of the so-called arab spring and in others where fundamental human rights are not respected. finally, i would like to welcome the presence of a delegation from the ep at the 19th session of the unhrc, which is bearing our concerns.
in writing. − this resolution supports the european union's priorities for the 19th session of the unhrc. the eu's hypocritical human rights agenda is nothing new; it points the finger at countries where the eu has an interest in economic, geostrategic, political or diplomatic dominance, leaving aside friends or human rights violations within its own borders. and there is a lot to be said about these violations in and/or in the eu. they hypocritically speak in favour of the indivisibility and universality of human rights, but they reveal a restrictive conception of them, promoting sordid imf-eu plans that call them into question, imposing an unprecedented social setback, compromising their right to sovereignty and the development of peoples. also notable is the lack of clear references and in some cases any reference to the systematic violation of human rights carried out by the us at the illegal guantanamo base, the killing of thousands of civilians by nato in afghanistan, pakistan and libya, the occupation and violation of the rights of the people of western sahara, or the maintenance of israel's apartheid policy on the palestinian people and the maintenance of the blockade on gaza, among many other examples.

in writing. the 19th session of the united nations human rights council has burma/myanmar, the democratic people's republic of korea, syria, libya and iran as its core issues. as we can see, the protection of human rights is still of the greatest relevance today: on the one hand, old conflicts persist; on the other, new difficulties are emerging - situations which threaten the dignity of the person, a little bit all over the world, on which the european parliament has spoken at various sessions. these internal sessions are intended to promote the fundamental interpretation of the european area on the international political scene, in particular on the protection of human rights: the joint resolution seeks to summarise this by offering the european parliament's main positions on the main issues affecting the protection of the individual today, with a view to the 19th session of the un human rights council. that being the scope of the resolution, i voted in favour.
in writing. − human rights are a fundamental issue in the acquis of the european union, which must govern its external policy in line with the internal and external policies of the member states themselves. the eu's relations with third countries must embody these values through example and influence in the world. in the event of violations, the eu should, together with international organisations and countries, call for their restoration and safeguarding. the 19th session of the un human rights council (unhrc), the specialised body for the debate of these issues, should highlight the safeguarding of the fundamental human rights by their protection and respect throughout the world. i think it is extremely important that the eu continues to provide financial assistance and technical support to this unhrc, alongside the member states' own contributions. there are many cases of human rights violations that we could look at, from sudan to somalia, the countries of the arab spring, and even european countries, where there are serious violations of the rights of expression and sexual freedom. i think, however, that it is our duty to show a strong international community against any kind of attack on human dignity.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the eu to be given the right to take action in the fight against terrorism. this is not new: it is a recurring political position of those who want to point the finger at countries where the eu has an economic, geostrategic, political or diplomatic interest, leaving aside friends or human rights violations. and there is a lot to be said about these violations in and/or in the eu. they hypocritically speak in favour of the indivisibility and universality of human rights, but they have supported the cruel demands of the eu, the imf and the national governments of countries such as portugal or greece on their people, imposing a setback in the right to work and workers' rights, the right to health, education and housing, compromising their right to sovereignty and development. it is also hypocritical to make no clear reference - and in some cases no reference at all - to the systematic violation of human rights by the us at the illegal base in guantanamo bay, cuba, to the killing of thousands of civilians by nato in afghanistan, pakistan and libya, to the occupation and violation of the rights of the people of western sahara, or to the continuation of the blockade of gaza.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution. it is important to avoid negative discrimination against disabled people and, given that around 95% of published works are never converted into accessible formats such as braille, large print or audio recording, we can clearly state that this is a data point that tells us that there is work to be done in europe in this area. i believe that the european commission and the council are taking swift action in this way to support the legally binding wipo treaty on copyright applicable to books and other printed matter for the blind and visually impaired.
in writing. − blind and visually impaired people in the european union have severe restrictions on access to books and other printed products, as 95% of published works are not converted into accessible formats such as braille, large print or audio. at present, no international legal standard provides for an exception to copyright in the cross-border distribution of formats adapted for visually impaired persons. the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is drafting an international treaty to improve access to books for the blind and other visually impaired. this motion for a resolution calls on the council and the commission to support the above-mentioned wipo treaty, which is intended to be binding. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the measures it contains will make a decisive contribution to combating discrimination against blind and visually impaired people.
in writing. − it is important to ensure that books and other printed products are accessible to visually impaired and/or dyslexic people, and therefore there is a need for conversion of these into accessible media, such as braille, enlarged characters or audio. in the vast majority of member states, exceptions to the copyright law allow the production of books in accessible formats. unfortunately, the number of books published that are converted is still quite small, about 5% in the richest countries and less than 1% in the poorest countries. moreover, even this small percentage of books is legally prevented from crossing borders and cannot be distributed in other member states. i therefore believe that an international treaty should be adopted within the wipo framework, creating legally binding international rules to create clear rules on copyright applicable to books and other printed products, in order to improve the opportunity for these people to have access to them. i hope that both the council and the commission will reconsider their traditional position on this matter and join parliament in thus reinforcing the fundamental right to prohibit discrimination against people with disabilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on access to books for blind people, because i believe it is essential that the council and the commission support a legally binding international treaty on copyright applicable to books and other printed matter for blind and visually impaired people, with a view to improving access to books for these people.
in writing. - currently, only 5% of books published in the european union are accessible to the blind. to date, there are no international legal standards that allow for a specific copyright derogation for the transnational dissemination of formats adapted to persons with disabilities who cannot access printed products. the committee on copyright of the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is considering the possibility of adopting an international treaty to improve access to books for blind and visually impaired people, an idea which i believe the european union should join.
in writing. - this motion for a resolution was tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure and following a question with a request for an oral answer by mr dan pescod, on behalf of the european blind union (ebu) /royal institute of blind people (rnib), on access for blind people to books and other printed matter, which in the european union is only 5%. the reasons for such a low fee are the lack of international legal standards to facilitate transnational dissemination because of copyright, and the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization is working on an international treaty to solve this problem. the lack of access to these goods by these citizens means marginalisation and negative discrimination which prevents them from accessing the culture to which they are entitled. i welcome the measures proposed in this resolution - which is why i voted in favour - because i believe they will help to improve the quality of life of blind and visually impaired people, preventing their social marginalisation and facilitating access to cultural heritage, all in compliance with international treaties and in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - this resolution defends access for blind and visually impaired people to books and other printed products through copyright policy. of course we support it. we believe it is essential to put an end to social injustices and to intensify the specific discrimination to which these people are often subject. we are in favour of ensuring their equal participation in economic, social, cultural and sporting life. but these rights can only be guaranteed if they are enshrined in an integrated way. the policies now being implemented by the european union - and supported by the majority of this parliament - are putting at risk the most basic rights of various sections of the population, including citizens with disabilities. if we want to defend the rights of disabled people, we must of course defend them in all areas of their lives, without forgetting, for example, that the so-called austerity programmes serve as cover for wage cuts, the closure of essential public services for these people, as is happening in portugal, greece and other countries, putting at risk access to basic public services such as health, education, transport, among others.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution to allow blind people access to books and other printed products. indeed, to date there are no international legal rules allowing for a specific copyright derogation in favour of the transnational dissemination of formats adapted to persons with disabilities who are unable to access printed products, which inadmissiblely constitutes a factor of social exclusion and discrimination contrary to the provisions of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, in particular articles 21 and 30 thereof, and the european charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i consider that the measures it contains contribute to combating discrimination against blind and visually impaired people. the resolution seeks to promote not only the conversion of books and other printed products into accessible formats such as braille, large print or audio, but also to promote their transnational marketing. the european parliament has called on the commission to present a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. in a matter of this nature, it is justified to introduce a special scheme to facilitate the making available of these works in accessible formats, in an attempt to alleviate the difficulties of the blind, which could be achieved at the outset by a different regulation of copyright. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution, calling on the council and the commission to support a world intellectual property organisation treaty aimed at introducing a binding copyright instrument for books and other printed matter for the blind and visually impaired.
in writing. - about 95% of published works are not converted into other types of formats (e.g. braille, audio recording), making them unreadable by people with severe visual impairments. to this end, it will be necessary to adopt concrete measures to facilitate access to books or other printed documents for visually impaired persons. i agree with the intention of the european parliament to support the creation of a treaty drawn up by the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization which applies to books and other printed products intended for blind or visually impaired people. i believe that this is the only way to reduce the barriers faced by blind citizens and to increase their literary and intellectual training.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's security is not compromised. i would stress that this resolution seeks to respond to these demands by building on the partnership for democracy and shared values with the southern mediterranean, by bringing together the various instruments in order to simplify and enhance south-south trade cooperation and to contribute to economic growth and integration among the southern mediterranean states. however, concerns about the implementation of the eu-israel association protocol dealing with products originating in israeli-occupied territories should be noted, and a new commitment is needed.
in writing. - parliament has given its agreement, and i believe it has, to the conclusion of this convention on preferential rules of origin applicable to the pan-euro-mediterranean region. i believe that the european union cannot fail to see its southern neighbours as potential partners and to seek to encourage trade with them. despite the tension experienced by some of the countries concerned, the union should have a long-term view in mind when adopting such legal instruments and should aim at the effective establishment of faster and more reliable means of ensuring an increase in trade.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin. the european union has always sought to promote trade integration between the countries of the southern mediterranean, as international trade can promote economic growth and poverty reduction. after the so-called arab spring, this integration is even more important and an essential factor in the consolidation of the emerging democracies in these countries. it will also allow the unification of a series of about 100 trade agreements and facilitate trade between the south and the north. imports from israeli settlements on palestinian land, which cannot benefit from preferential rules, will also be prevented. i voted in favour of this proposal because, as the commissioner has said, this convention is not only the first response to the arab spring but will also allow the pan-mediterranean region to be integrated into eu trade.
in writing. the aim of this convention is to simplify the provisions relating to the determination of the country of origin of a product. if approved, it will replace more than 100 bilateral protocols. it is intended to promote the creation and consolidation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. although the rapporteur argues that this convention will serve as an incentive for south-south trade, lead to economic growth and poverty reduction, as well as to better regional integration of the economies of the region, we know well how different the reality is. small and medium-sized producers will suffer from trade liberalisation because they are unable to compete with intensive production models. the large economic groups will be favoured, as they will gain access to new markets and cheap labour. the most controversial issue is the legal uncertainty about assets originating from settlements in occupied territory. there is a possibility that these goods may enter the eu market as israeli products. our group has therefore tabled an amendment calling for a sustainable and satisfactory solution, which explicitly excludes the possibility of products originating in the illegal israeli settlements in the occupied territories entering the eu market before the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin can be envisaged.
in writing. the aim of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin is to create a euro-mediterranean free trade area. the adoption of this convention also aims to make the pan-euro-mediterranean system of preferential origin cumulation extended to the western balkan countries, facilitating eventual expansion to new members. this new legal instrument will help to stimulate economic growth, foster economic diversification and poverty reduction and enable the democratisation of the region, as well as to promote social, commercial and economic integration between the countries of the southern mediterranean. it is essential that each signatory exporting country applies uniformly and correctly the provisions on administrative cooperation and the issuing of certificates of origin and that each importing country has sufficient technical, budgetary and information resources to carry out effective customs controls, so as to avoid any preferential deviation. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and stress the need for the european commission to draw up an impact assessment after three years to assess, inter alia, the benefits of adopting this convention and the impact of cumulation caused by this document on business practices.
in writing. − the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin brings together in a single document the rules of origin for goods under the treaties concluded between the european union, the countries participating in the barcelona process, the efta states, the faroe islands and the states participating in the stabilisation and association process. this document replaces the rules which have hitherto been based mainly on bilateral protocols (more than 100). the convention, while providing an incentive for trade between these states and reducing the difficulties faced by the international trading system, is also likely to run into a number of problems of international law because of its broad subjective scope. the european parliament has already expressed its views on the situation in the middle east. the resolution seeks to set out a series of lines of action in this matter, which must be reflected upon, and i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - the approval of this convention with the euro-mediterranean region will bring a set of advantages to the countries of the southern mediterranean, providing for their regional integration, towards the creation of a genuine free trade area. at the same time, this convention will replace some 100 bilateral agreements on preferential rules of origin, making it easier for companies to work and to identify abuse and evasion. one of the points i consider to be fundamental in this motion for a resolution is the need to establish clear criteria for preferential rules of origin so that none of the products originating in the illegally occupied palestinian territories benefit from this rule. i agree with the commission's proposal to draw up a list of the settlements, to be sent to all the customs authorities in the member states, so that each one can take the necessary measures, ensuring that none of the products coming from the settlements has cumulative preferential measures. we must not close the door on the countries of the southern mediterranean; we must export our example of economic integration, showing that the union will bring benefits to all partners.
in writing. the creation of the convention is intended to promote the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. with this convention, small and medium-sized producers will suffer from trade liberalisation because they are unable to compete with intensive production models, thus favouring large economic groups that conquer new markets and access cheap labour.
in writing. - the adoption of a convention such as the convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin opens the way to increased trade between the two shores of this ancient inland sea of classical civilization and the cradle of what we now know as europe. the fact that the applicable rules of origin have been brought together in a single instrument contributes to their intelligibility and to their quicker use, which will benefit not only those directly involved in trade but also consumers themselves. i welcome this step towards greater euro-mediterranean integration and hope that in future it will include initiatives of a social and cultural nature, in addition to the very relevant and necessary initiatives in the economic field.
in writing. the recommendation under consideration, drawn up by emílio menéndez del valle, concerns the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin. this is a convention which will not only facilitate pan-euro-mediterranean trade rules but also catalyse the creation of a common market between the member states of the european union and the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean. the eu has always sought to promote trade integration of the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean, as international trade can promote economic growth and poverty reduction. after the so-called arab spring, this integration is even more important and an essential factor in the consolidation of the emerging democracies in these countries. it will also allow the unification of a series of about 100 trade agreements and facilitate trade between the south and the north. imports from israeli settlements illegally occupying palestinian land, which will not be able to benefit from preferential rules, will also be prevented. i voted in favour of this proposal because, as the commissioner has said, this convention is not only the first response to the arab spring but will also enable the pan-mediterranean region to be integrated into eu trade.
in writing. the report approves the conclusion of the convention aimed at promoting the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. this trade liberalisation will harm small and medium-sized producers who will suffer from trade liberalisation because they are unable to compete with intensive production models, thus favouring large economic groups who conquer new markets and access cheap labour, as well as the possibility of better circumventing social, labour and environmental standards in force in european countries. the most controversial issue in this convention is the legal uncertainty over property originating in israeli settlements in the occupied palestinian territories. the commission does not deny the possibility that these goods may enter the eu market as israeli products which is unacceptable. for these reasons, we voted against this report.
in writing. the objective of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin is to create a euro-mediterranean free trade area. the adoption of this convention also aims to make the pan-euro-mediterranean system of preferential origin cumulation extended to the western balkan countries, facilitating eventual expansion to new members. this new legal instrument will help to stimulate economic growth, foster economic diversification, reduce poverty and enable the democratisation of the region, as well as to promote social, commercial and economic integration between the countries of the southern mediterranean. i voted in favour, aware that for effective operation it is essential that each signatory exporting country applies uniformly and correctly the provisions on administrative cooperation and the issuing of certificates of origin and that each importing country has sufficient technical, budgetary and information resources to carry out effective customs controls to avoid any preferential deviation.
in writing. − the association agreements between the eu and its mediterranean partners were the first steps towards this convention, which promotes the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. the aim of this convention is to take advantage of these agreements by adopting this new, simpler and more effective legal instrument, which can serve as a possible incentive to stimulate south-south trade and contribute to economic growth, economic diversification, poverty reduction and democratisation in the region, as well as to promote social, commercial and economic integration between the countries of the southern mediterranean.
in writing. − the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin brings together in a single document the rules of origin for goods under the treaties concluded between the european union, the countries participating in the barcelona process, the efta states, the faroe islands and the states participating in the stabilisation and association process. this document replaces the rules which have hitherto been based mainly on bilateral protocols (more than 100). in so far as this convention can be translated into an incentive to trade between these states by lessening the difficulties posed to the international trading system, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. − the new regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin promotes the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area and brings together all the rules of origin of goods traded under the relevant trade agreements concluded between the various parties. this important step must be accompanied and consolidated by other ambitious plans to improve and promote trade in the region, starting as soon as possible with the updating of pan-euro-mediterranean rules of origin, in order to take full advantage of the more favourable political and economic environment in our southern neighbours.
in writing. the report approves the conclusion of the convention, which is intended to promote the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. this trade liberalisation will harm small and medium-sized producers, who will suffer from trade liberalisation as they are unable to compete with intensive production models. this convention favours the large economic groups, which in this way conquer new markets and gain access to cheap labour, and are able to circumvent social, labour and environmental standards in force in european countries. we cannot accept this situation, which will mean the end of small and mediumsized production.
in writing. - i approve this resolution, which is intended to take forward one of the european union's most emblematic programmes worldwide, namely gmes. i think that the lack of financial provisioning could jeopardise a significant development in the technological age we want to lead, and it is regrettable that the weak proposals for intergovernmental funding that have been put forward only deteriorate the quality of the programme. earth observation technology should be adequately funded and should be linked to the network of european regions using space technologies, which could promote economic, technological and territorial cohesion, and open up new opportunities for innovation-based development, as called for in the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution because it gives due weight to the renewal and extension of the term of the gmes given its increasingly important role in the area of the environment. gmes has been implemented to observe the planet earth, i.e. to monitor developments in climate change and forest degradation, greenhouse gas measurement, environmental sustainability, civil protection and security, and economic opportunities that may arise from research and development and innovation. i admit to being concerned about intergovernmental funding for gmes beyond 2013, as advocated by the commission. this not only raises doubts about the real interest of the eu in the programme, but it could also have a possible regression towards a programme that would lack a greater european dimension and include deficiencies in its transparency and full, open and equal access for all. consequently, i agree that it is necessary to urge the commission to come forward with a legislative proposal addressing all the problems mentioned above, namely to announce the management, the funding supported by the multiannual financial framework and a roadmap for the operation of the gmes programme, thus ensuring a safe and proper implementation and full operationality from 2014.
in writing. - as the resolution points out, uncertainty about the future of the gmes programme and its funding is detrimental to the development and commercialisation of gmes services and applications, which have the potential to generate economic growth and jobs in europe. i therefore support the recommendation that a proposal be made for the management, financing and operation of the gmes programme which ensures the objective of full operation from 2014.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) follows a question with request for an oral answer by mr norbert glante, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on the future of the global monitoring for environment and security (gmes) programme, one of the european union's most emblematic space initiatives. although it is an instrument that, in addition to enabling the observation of planet earth, is also essential for combating climate change, civil protection and security, crisis management and sustainable economic development, the current budgetary constraints have led the european commission to withdraw its funding from the multiannual financial framework from 2013 and to place it in an intergovernmental financing plan. as this new financing system does not guarantee the full continuity of the programme, rendering it unfeasible or drastically reducing its operability, i voted in favour of this proposal for the commission to present a legislative proposal to ensure long-term financing, in particular under the mff, so that gmes can fully continue and, from 2014, fulfil the functions for which it was created.
in writing. - gmes is the name given to the global monitoring for environment and safety programme. this joint project has applications and potentials of undisputed public interest. however, it also contains aspects which give rise to reservations. several authors and researchers have reported that under the guise of alleged civil protection and security, mobility and crisis management, emergency management and humanitarian crisis response, gmes has been serving possible military purposes/uses. that has been the reason for our abstention, which we repeat once again. in addition, the political and strategic objectives in the field of security are clearly stated, particularly as regards border control, maritime surveillance and support for the union's external action, as referred to in its regulation, which we are also unable to follow. these concerns are all the more pressing the more the european union is deepening its security and military dimension. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud, and it is not surprising that the commission has taken a number of measures to combat fraud.
in writing. the gmes initiative, earth observation, is a project of considerable importance for the future of the european union. this is a union infrastructure which makes it possible to manage the environment better and to increase the safety of citizens. this programme can serve as an example of the will to create a genuine european industrial strategy in the space industry and will create more benefits for society. it will lead to more jobs, more security and environmental protection. it will open up a significant market niche for smes. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the fight against crime requires a reinforcement of dialogue and action between the judicial authorities of the member states. judicial cooperation in criminal matters is based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions of the member states, which implies the approximation of the relevant national laws and the application of common minimum rules. thus, by applying almost all the provisions contained in the 2000 convention on mutual legal assistance between member states and its protocol adopted in 2001, judicial cooperation between the eu member states and norway and iceland becomes a reality. the agreement in question includes provisions of major importance such as those relating to the hearing of witnesses, experts and defendants by telephone or videoconference, to surreptitious deliveries, to covert investigations and joint investigation teams and to requests for information on bank transfers, bank accounts and their monitoring in the context of the fight against crime in general and organised crime in particular. the adoption of this agreement represents a considerable step forward in the creation of an effective area of cooperation with countries outside the union, with positive repercussions within the union itself, allowing the creation of an ever-growing area of freedom, justice and security.

in writing. − there are still many obstacles, directly or indirectly, which continue to hinder the free movement of people within the eu and the ability of citizens to fully benefit from the advantages of the single market. the cross-border obstacles to succession at european level affect some 50 million people (e.g. citizens living in a member state other than their member state of origin, holding assets in a member state other than their member state of residence, mixed couples, etc.) and also have a direct impact on their heirs. this is the first time that a union instrument has been adopted in the field of succession law, which is by its nature a very sensitive area and intrinsically linked to the national forum. we are facing a very important and complex initiative which brings clear benefits to citizens, not only in terms of clarity and legal certainty, but also by avoiding fragmentation at the level of succession and by making a significant contribution to reducing bureaucracy and costs. it will allow for the free movement and recognition of succession decisions and the creation of a european certificate of succession, which will allow citizens to prove their status and exercise their rights throughout the eu.

in writing. − the present proposal does not seek to harmonise the substantive law applicable to succession, but rather to establish harmonised rules for the settlement of international jurisdictional conflicts. this means that we are working within the framework of private international law and not within the substantive framework of the law of succession, where each state will continue to have its own laws. with the increasing globalisation of personal and family relationships, it is important to ensure legal certainty and security for the parties when several jurisdictions are involved. the proposal aims to establish common rules on the law applicable and the court having jurisdiction in matters of succession. i cannot but consider it an important step towards the construction of an area of freedom and justice in which the free movement of persons is effective to give greater legal certainty to the resolution of international disputes in the field of succession law, in particular by creating the european certificate of succession.
in writing. − the achievement of the objectives underlying the creation of the european union, namely the functioning of the single market and the free movement of persons and goods, has encouraged the mobility of europeans, who increasingly emigrate to other member states where they settle, work, marry, divorce, acquire property and die. this report, drawn up by mr kurt lechner, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and authentic instruments in matters of succession and the creation of a european certificate of succession. this is a cross-border legal regime which is an important step forward in this area and will allow for more effective application of the law in response to the concerns of families. in fact, after a decision has been taken, there are no limitations on the enforcement of the judgment due to the european certificate of succession. i welcome the adoption of this report, which is good news for thousands of european citizens who will benefit from this initiative which will end many conflicts. i regret, however, that it was not possible to obtain the agreement of the united kingdom and ireland.
in writing. - it is regrettable that this report was not made available in time, like the others, in all the language versions. in particular, the portuguese version was not available in digital format at the time of the vote. unfortunately, this is not the first time this has happened. these are situations which call into question respect for the principle of multilingualism in the european parliament and the equality of members, regardless of their country of origin and their mother tongue. the report proposes unified rules on jurisdiction, applicable law and recognition of courts in situations where citizens of one member state reside in another member state, in order to clarify situations in succession law which are often in doubt today. the european commission's proposal, which the report endorses, proposes the creation of a european certificate of succession. we believe that it is clearly necessary to protect citizens against the shortcomings of the current legal framework, the existing framework for the free movement of persons between member states. it should be borne in mind, however, that the law of succession and all relevant provisions in this field must result from an expression of national sovereignty, which must be respected. the solutions to concrete problems that exist today must therefore respect this framework.
in writing. − the union has set itself the objective of maintaining and developing an area of freedom, security and justice in which the free movement of persons is ensured. in order to gradually create such an area, the union should adopt measures in the field of judicial cooperation in civil matters having cross-border implications, in particular where this is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. it is appropriate to facilitate the proper functioning of the internal market by removing obstacles to the free movement of persons who currently face difficulties in exercising their rights in the context of a succession with cross-border implications. in the european area of justice, citizens must be able to organise their succession in advance. the rights of heirs and legatees and other persons close to the deceased, as well as of the creditors of the succession, need to be effectively guaranteed. in order to achieve those objectives, this regulation should group together the provisions on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition or, as the case may be, acceptance, enforceability and enforcement of judgments, authentic instruments and court settlements, as well as the european certificate of succession. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - 450 000 crossborder successions are opened in the european union each year, representing an estimated value of over eur 120 billion and about 10% of all successions. this proposal for a regulation aims to avoid legal conflicts and lengthy proceedings for heirs when the application of the laws of more than one member state is at stake. one of the innovative measures is the creation of a european certificate of succession designed to clarify the legal position of the testator and safeguard the rights of heirs and other parties, including creditors. i believe that these measures can contribute to greater efficiency and speed in these procedures, and i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in october 2009, the european commission presented a proposal for a regulation to the european parliament and the council with the aim of establishing the conditions for residents of the european union who own property in several member states to be able to organise their succession in advance and effectively guarantee the rights of heirs and/or legatees and other persons related to the deceased as well as the creditors of the succession. in order to achieve a solution across all member states, it is essential that single reference criteria are defined for the rights of succession, in particular the return, administration or liquidation of the assets of the rightful owner. i agree with the proposal that has been put forward, which guarantees greater legal certainty for citizens residing in the european union, since the criterion of habitual residence is now applied to the court having jurisdiction to apply its own law. finally, it should be stressed that for citizens who are habitually resident in their country of origin and have property in that country, no changes will be made to the normal succession procedure. the rules of the country of residence will also apply to property held by citizens outside their country of origin.
in writing. − the report proposes to unify rules on jurisdiction, applicable law and recognition of courts in situations where citizens of one member state reside in another member state, in order to clarify situations in succession law which are currently in doubt. the european commission is therefore proposing the creation of a european certificate of succession. it is necessary to protect citizens against the shortcomings of the current legal framework, the existing framework for the free movement of persons between member states. however, it is necessary to ensure that the right of succession and all relevant provisions in this area result from an expression of national sovereignty, which must be respected. we also regret that this report was not made available in time, as were the others, in all the language versions, particularly the portuguese version. these situations call into question respect for the principle of multilingualism in the european parliament and the equality of members, irrespective of their country of origin and their mother tongue.

in writing. − although gender equality is one of the eu's fundamental principles, the problem of inequality persists. the commission has put forward numerous proposals to tackle this inequality, notably for strategy 2020, but unfortunately progress has been too slow. in times of economic crisis it is even more evident that the strengthening of women's position in the labour market and their economic independence is not only a moral imperative but also an economic necessity. today, 60 percent of recent graduates are women. however, they are very unlikely to enter the workforce with their training, and there is a pay gap (which needs to be reduced) where women earn on average 17.5% less than men. it is also essential to strengthen measures to reconcile work and private life. particular attention should be paid to the most vulnerable groups of women, who are at a higher risk of social exclusion, poverty and extreme human rights violations. i call on the member states and all the parties concerned not to merely advocate the achievement of gender equality in words but to make the necessary efforts and actions to make it a priority in both their social and economic strategies.

in writing. - the principle of equality is, alongside freedom, one of the pillars of democratic states governed by the rule of law. it is because i believe in the importance of the principle of equality that i understand that men and women deserve equal opportunities and should have the same conditions that allow them to rise to management and leadership positions in the business world. this should be achieved by removing the remaining barriers to women - such as the negative impact of motherhood on career progression - and not by imposing quotas definitively by regulation. as i have said on several occasions, quotas, if they are not temporary, only reduce the number of women rather than guaranteeing them equal access to the profession, to public office or to management and leadership positions in companies. moreover, in the area of private initiative, the imposition of quotas may be an intervention which restricts the freedom of shareholders and, as such, may even infringe article 16 of the charter of fundamental rights which lays down the principle of freedom of establishment. i therefore advocate the adequacy of these essential principles.

in writing. - this report starts from the fact that women are under-represented in elected and appointed positions, in the bodies of national sovereignty and in the european parliament itself, and in what it calls 'top positions' in general. to solve this problem, it advocates the legal imposition of quota systems that promote parity in these areas. the approach adopted by the rapporteur is reductive and lacks the essential elements for a correct understanding of the problem on the one hand and for a fair solution on the other. women's civic and political participation at various levels - associational, trade union, cultural and other - is hampered by limitations in access to education, culture and public services, and by economic difficulties which are a direct result of the wage inequalities they suffer and the precariousness of their jobs. these are issues that underlie gender discrimination, which cannot be ignored and which limit women's social, political and cultural involvement. it is these structural inequalities - the expression of class inequalities - that must be combated. the solution cannot be simply to establish artificial, formal, administrative equality, forgetting and keeping untouched the real problems of the overwhelming majority of women. we also reject any interference in the internal life of the parties.

in writing. - this own-initiative report, by sven giegold, deals with the status of the european cooperative society (sce) as regards the involvement of workers in this form of trade which we can call social. there are currently over 160 000 cooperatives in europe, employing some 5.4 million people and providing local supplies, mainly in rural areas. in the current economic and financial crisis, when we are witnessing an unprecedented cut in public spending and a significant increase in unemployment rates, a social economy model based on cooperativism is an asset to society. in fact, cooperatives not only provide goods and services at more competitive prices - they are not for profit - but also promote education, vocational training, continuing training and entrepreneurship programmes. i therefore welcome the proposal to the commission for the launch of the european year of the social economy and welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, which not only recognises the role of cooperatives in economic growth and job creation, but also encourages the extension of their scope and number with a view to achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the report focuses on advocating for an improvement in the participation rights of employees in cooperative societies, with the integration of this issue in the revision of the regulation on the statute of the european cooperative society (sce), and not just in the directive 2003/72/ec on employee involvement. the promotion of the social economy and the cooperative sector will be important in strengthening production systems, particularly those linked to local and regional needs and realities. on the other hand, the ways in which cooperative management operates must incorporate concerns for a fairer and more equitable redistribution of the proceeds of these organisations to their members and workers. in this respect, we welcome the fact that the report stresses the importance of the member states transposing certain articles of the directive on workers' rights and of taking measures to encourage the development potential of cooperatives, especially in a period of economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing today. however, we do not share the view that the future status of sce should encourage the development of the eu internal market in the concrete context in which it is currently developing, namely free capitalist competition.

in writing. - a few days before the bologna process ministerial conference, progress is being made in the area of access to education, which is a right of all citizens. european universities have reorganised their teaching activities within the three-cycle framework established by the bologna process towards the so-called third mission of the higher education system. the recognition and standardisation of education systems across the european union encourages the mobility of learners, fostering european integration in general and growth and employment in particular. with only a few days to go until the bologna process ministerial conference, it is therefore necessary to formulate concrete measures to promote the full implementation of its objectives in all universities in all member states, to the ultimate benefit of vocational training and european competitiveness.
in writing. the university of bologna, founded in 1088 and whose motto is alma mater studiorum, is the oldest university and celebrated its 900th anniversary in 1988, and remains a centre of university excellence. in 1998, on the occasion of the 800th anniversary of the university of paris, a number of european ministers signed the sorbonne declaration, with the aim of harmonising the european higher education system. on 19 june 1999, 30 european states signed the bologna declaration, which aimed to establish by 2010 a coherent, compatible, competitive and attractive european higher education area for european and third-country students, an area that promotes european cohesion through knowledge, mobility and employability of graduates, thus ensuring a better and more positive performance of europe in the world. the bologna process, through the mutual recognition of academic qualifications between the various universities of the signatory countries, allows for greater mobility of people in general and of students in particular. i welcome the adoption of this report and am confident that it will be a strong incentive to continue this process and contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the education and training 2020 programme and the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. the rapporteur's apologetic view seeks to conceal or minimize some of the most serious consequences of the bologna process. these include: the creation of economic barriers to access to and attendance at higher education, the commodification of education (which excludes those who have less economic conditions to buy the products that today's higher education courses have become), the attack on the social function of the state in this field (which, in states such as portugal, is constitutionally enshrined, although not respected). education has been called into question as a right that should be guaranteed to everyone, regardless of their economic conditions, the role of the education system in overcoming social inequalities has been called into question, in order to create a knowledge market and a new business opportunity, which ensure the reproduction of social inequalities. these are some of the consequences of the bologna process! the stated objective of student mobility has been blocked, as the report itself acknowledges, by low rates of mobility. the harmonization of curricula ignores the specificities of the educational system of each country, in a trend towards vocational training rather than integral training. quality is declining and many students are forced into debt to access a fundamental right.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the contribution of the european institutions to the consolidation and progress of the bologna process. in fact, the creation of a european higher education area represents the final stage in the ambitious system launched by the bologna process. the broad structural reform of the european higher education system has not been as successful as expected and desired, but it is nevertheless a major objective to be achieved to enable the growth set out in the europe 2020 strategy, an important requirement for the full integration of the eu market and one of the only tools available to challenge the economic and financial crisis europe is going through. i call for greater involvement of all stakeholders, as the lack of respect by some european universities for the guidelines of the process demonstrates the need to implement new teaching strategies and to identify new measures to support this process.
in writing. − the bologna process has made it possible to make higher education systems in europe compatible and to remove remaining barriers to cross-border mobility, to enable studying in another country and to make european higher education more attractive. however, its application has not been uniform or successful in all member states, either because of the current economic crisis or because of the absence of information, monitoring and support mechanisms for all higher education actors. i voted in favour of this report, which provides for measures to strengthen this process. this is an essential process for achieving the europe 2020 objectives and requires the involvement of all member states, both through budgetary reinforcement and the full implementation of existing european programmes.
in writing. − the creation of a european higher education area is an essential goal for establishing a true european society based on knowledge and innovation, as expressed in the eu2020 strategy. to this end, the bologna process was launched in 1999, which aims to give a student enrolled in a european university the right to graduate and have his or her qualifications recognised throughout the eu. the system launched by the bologna process, which created three cycles and the credit transfer and accumulation system, faces several institutional and applicability obstacles. intergovernmental cooperation needs to be strengthened, as well as the involvement of the main actors in the process, universities, students and businesses. it is therefore necessary to look at physical, horizontal and vertical mobility, the recognition of qualifications and the framework for formal, non-formal and informal qualifications, quality assurance of institutions, the inclusion and social cohesion of university education, school/enterprise cooperation and the involvement of universities in creating innovation. unlocking the above points will make europe a place of teaching excellence.
in writing. - this report attempts to remedy or conceal some of the most serious consequences of the bologna process - the difficulty of access to higher education for those who are less economically able and who cannot afford the products that the higher education cycle packages have become today. the paradigm of education as a right that should be guaranteed to all people has been reversed to become a knowledge market and a new business opportunity. the much-touted objective of student mobility has been put on the back burner, because, as the report itself acknowledges, mobility rates are low. the aim is to harmonize the structure of knowledge and even of content, ignoring the specificities of the educational system of each country, in a trend towards vocational training rather than integrated education. the quality of education is declining, while many students are forced into debt to access a fundamental right. what is needed, as we have argued in our motion for a resolution, is cooperation between member states in higher education, but this must be done by guaranteeing the right of everyone to free, quality public higher education.
in writing. − i approve this report, agreeing to the progressive harmonisation of the statistical review measures and their codes of conduct, in order to bring more transparency, less discrepancies between member states and to give credibility to the european statistical system. all these efforts are important because the statistical sector qualifies governance by providing it with decisive analytical tools for decision-making.
in writing. − this report emphasises the need for rigorous, reliable and high-quality statistics, as they are an essential information basis for decision-making and the adoption of economic, social and territorial policies adapted to reality, both at european, national and regional level. it is agreed that the existence of accurate statistics is fundamental for the formulation of appropriate policies and that their impartiality, objectivity and independence must be guaranteed. the report sets out the assumptions that should be taken into account in the production of quality statistics and denounces the shortcomings and deficiencies found in both their production and governance. it stresses the need for statistics to be standardised, to be submitted in good time and for eurostat to play a central role in their aggregation and provision. it also suggests making statistics available in an easier and more intuitive way so that all citizens have simplified access to all data. i support this report as it is an asset for european citizens and policy-makers, making a clear contribution to improving decision-making, particularly in the context of implementing the europe 2020 priorities.
in writing. − this own-initiative report is intended to complement the six-pack, highlighting the importance of the quality of the figures in the statistics provided by the member states. in fact, the lack of knowledge of the real figures, or at least of absolute certainty in their collection methods (to allow reliable comparisons) between certain statistical variables, macro or microeconomic, in each of the member states, is a reality that unfortunately exists within the union, as recent events have well proved. this reality must objectively be stopped! it is clear that reliable and accurate statistics are essential for the formulation of effective economic and budgetary policies by member states and at union level, as can be seen from the report. it is also clear that these statistical bodies must be independent and have more powers, particularly in the field of research. and that the internal and external audit mechanisms will have to be strengthened. and that eurostat should support member states which so request. i therefore welcome this own-initiative report and its rapporteur, and i have obviously voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it argues that eurostat should continue, together with the main data providers and users, its efforts to modernise the methods of producing european statistics in order to provide reliable information to citizens.
in writing. − in the current context of the economic crisis in the euro area, the discussion on the quality and reliability of data provided by member states has become a major and central theme of the six-pack. it should be recalled that the presentation of statistics is an essential element of the european semester framework and that one of the six-pack directives sets out the requirements applicable to the budgetary frameworks of the member states. i therefore support the rapporteur on the need to ensure the independence of the national statistical councils from political power, the need to harmonise, as far as possible, the methodologies for obtaining and presenting results, and the need to strengthen the audit mechanisms so that we can ensure the highest possible quality and transparency of government financial statistics.
in writing. statistics is an essential technique for the substantiation of most scientific work and for sound decision-making. if we have the best information on a given subject, we can make a more correct and assertive decision. this report, by edward scicluna, analyses the document on the quality management of european statistics. member states and the european union need reliable and accurate statistics to enable them to adopt correct and effective social, economic and budgetary policies. the eurozone crisis has shown the inadequacy of existing data and in some cases statistical fraud. it is therefore imperative that member states scrupulously comply with the recommendations and legal provisions on this matter in the interests of good governance. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, because i believe that the measures envisaged, in addition to modernising the data collection system, introduce protective mechanisms and barriers, avoiding failures and making statistics independent of the political process. the success of the economic governance package and the europe 2020 strategy for growth and jobs requires statistics of the highest quality.
in writing. − the report focuses on some correct objectives and principles in the processing and collection of economic statistics, such as independence and autonomy, giving states responsibility for the accuracy and authenticity of statistical data. but the rapporteur does not avoid being caught in the web of his own contradictions, particularly when, while stating the need to safeguard the independence of the statistical services in relation to the threat of possible political interventions, both at national and european level, he ends up arguing that statistics should produce the data needed to monitor the results of economic governance and the six pack, which are nothing more than serious political impositions and attacks on the sovereignty of states in areas which are fundamental to determining the collective future of their peoples. we believe that statistical indicators should be used to provide the fullest possible knowledge and description of social and economic realities. moreover, they should not be selected with a view to pursuing political objectives which are, moreover, totally contrary to the defence of development, welfare and social progress.
in writing. − the existence of reliable statistical data is essential for the monitoring of macroeconomic imbalances. in order to ensure the existence of sound and independent statistics, member states should ensure the professional independence of national statistical authorities in accordance with the european statistics code of practice established by regulation (ec) no 223/2009. in addition, the availability of sound budgetary data is also important for the monitoring of macroeconomic imbalances. this requirement should be ensured by the rules laid down in this respect by regulation (eu) no [.../...] on the effective application of budgetary surveillance in the euro area, in particular article 6a thereof.
in writing. − this report sets out objectives and principles for the processing and collection of economic statistics, in particular that their production be independent and separate from the political process, giving states responsibility for the accuracy and authenticity of statistical data. i am sure that this principle will make the results more certain and more accurate, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european commission has published a communication which aims to define a strategy to provide the european union with the framework for its management of the quality of statistics needed for enhanced economic policy coordination. in this respect, i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that a systemic approach to the quality of european statistics should be adopted, that greater proactivity in the management and evaluation of public finance data should be encouraged at an early primary stage and that greater statistical rigour should be emphasised at all levels of government. i also believe that eurostat should modernise the methods of producing european statistics in order to maintain cost-effectiveness and ensure that accounting and publication systems are uniformly established across the member states, with supervision through internal and external audit mechanisms. finally, i would like to stress the need to develop a coherent system for research into socioeconomic processes in crossborder areas, including the outermost regions, with a view to obtaining a reliable, complete and accurate economic framework for regional development.
in writing. − the report sets out the objectives and principles we advocate with regard to the processing and collection of economic statistics, namely that their production should be independent and separate from the political process, giving states responsibility for the accuracy and authenticity of statistical data. the report also mentions the need to safeguard the independence of statistical services from the threat of possible political intervention, both at national and european level. it is, however, true that several other premises of the report are totally contradictory to these principles, in particular when it says that statistics should produce the data that serve to monitor the results of economic governance and the six pack, which are nothing more than political guidelines associated with those who run the european institutions and the governments that defend them. we believe that statistical indicators should be based on a full knowledge of social and economic realities and should not be selected in order to pursue political objectives which are, moreover, totally contrary to the defence of the development of social progress.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i have to start the debate on two related but different subjects. the first is the 2010 international cocoa agreement, for which the consent of the european parliament has been requested, and the second is a draft resolution on child labour in the cocoa sector. i am the rapporteur on the agreement for the committee on international trade and i am the author of the draft resolution which the committee on international trade is putting before the house. as regards the first, the committee on international trade unanimously proposes that parliament authorise the council to conclude the 2010 international cocoa agreement for three fundamental reasons: first, the agreement strengthens the capacity of the international cocoa organisation to act in this sector; second, the agreement provides greater clarity and transparency about how the organisation operates and increases the participation of civil society in the work of the organisation; and third, the international cocoa agreement introduces new provisions aimed at promoting good labour relations and a sustainable cocoa economy. the agreement requires the contracting parties to improve working conditions in accordance with the internationally recognised rules and principles of the international labour organisation. it also encourages the same contracting parties to promote the sustainable development of the cocoa economy and to implement programmes and projects aimed at achieving these objectives. as one of the largest importers of cocoa, the european union has an increased responsibility to ensure that cocoa production and trade are carried out in the most transparent and sustainable way possible. the international cocoa agreement, which is already provisionally in force, is our best ally in this respect. as regards the resolution to which i have referred, i believe that the issue of child labour in cocoa plantations is too serious to be ignored when we give our consent to the international cocoa agreement. that is why i proposed, and the committee on international trade adopted, the draft resolution expressing our concern at the continued use of child labour on cocoa plantations, particularly in west africa. the growing awareness of consumers and producers, as well as of policy makers, has, over the last ten years, led to the welcome mobilization of the international cocoa industry to work with all stakeholders, such as international institutions, trade unions and ngos, to eliminate at least the worst forms of child labour in cocoa production. still, there's a lot to do. children working in cocoa fields are exposed to serious health risks. there are no reliable data on the extent of the phenomenon. estimates range from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the issue of child labour must be addressed in a comprehensive way, involving policy makers, stakeholders and, of course, the union institutions. i look forward to hearing the commission's comments, to which we are putting concrete questions and for which we would like to have concrete and satisfactory proposals on how it thinks the union should respond to this question.
