i am very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative. these are, in fact, numbers of an epidemic. that is why i think it is justified to make a specific resolution on diabetes, especially since this is the first time that this parliament has dealt with this subject. it is the result of collective work, and it is work that does not undo the work done so far on chronic diseases, but rather reinforces it and reinforces this capacity that we have to intervene together. we have about 325,000 deaths a year associated with diabetes because we know that diabetes is the leading cause of, for example, heart attacks, blindness, amputations, vital organ failure. and given this data, we have two options, in my view. the first is to say that it's not that serious, that we can live with it and that each government can take care of itself. the second is to say that the absence of a european strategy in this area is part of the problem. i understand that we have a lot of work to do on this side. and we have a lot to do in early diagnosis, in coordination, in investment in research. that is why this resolution is a start and a joint effort in this direction.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, the economic and financial crisis in the european union has taken on different forms in the various member states. this reflects the differences and imbalances that exist, it reflects the inequalities that exist between member states. these inequalities are expressed in multiple dimensions. one of them concerns the ability to access and use community funds. the countries with the weakest economies, which need the most community funds, are also often the ones that have the most difficulty in accessing these funds. for years this was largely the result of restrictions on public investment imposed under the guise of the stability pact, which made it difficult to mobilise the required national effort. today, these restrictions are greatly aggravated by the imf and european union programmes under way in countries such as portugal, greece or ireland. the policy choices embodied in these programmes are leading these countries targeted for intervention and their peoples into a dramatic and deep economic recession, with a major destruction of part of their economic and social fabric, affecting both the capacity for private investment, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, and public investment which is has been reduced, in some cases, to historically low levels. the coastal communities most dependent on fishing are not exempt from this general picture. the problem is compounded by the fact that in this particular case, to this general picture are added years of decline and disruption as a result of the specific developments that have taken place in this sector. the commission's proposal to increase community co-financing for these countries, and the corresponding reduction in national effort, has long been seen as a necessity. two years ago the european commission itself pointed to a serious under-implementation of the european fisheries fund. you've actually identified the causes of this underperformance. this proposal was therefore long overdue and unfortunately comes too late. the urgency of its adoption is therefore clear, and we consider it important that it be adopted at first reading. but we are not forgetting the limitations of the proposal, which are also obvious. i would like to mention a few of them here, and i hope that the commission will take them into account. we believe that the commission should assess to what extent this amendment actually provides the member states with the funds needed to support projects and to restore their economies, as stated in the commission's proposal. it should be noted that the restrictions on investment imposed by the assistance programmes may, under the new conditions, continue to make it difficult to mobilise the required national effort of 15% and 40% for the regions eligible and non-eligible respectively under the convergence objective. the commission should therefore, in our view, consider the need to remove restrictions on investment on the one hand, but also the possibility of further reducing national co-financing. it should also be stressed that the commission proposal does not increase the budget available to each country. the practical result of this option, as a result of the reduction in the national effort of these countries which are in greater difficulty, will be the channelling of a comparatively smaller overall amount of investment funds into the sector than was initially envisaged. the growth prospects opened up by investments in these member states will therefore be further reduced. once again, the principle of cohesion may be at stake, and the commission should therefore consider increasing the funds available to these countries. moreover, the rules for the clearance of government deficits should separate investment expenditure from other government expenditure, and not take account of the former, so as not to override the budgetary consolidation with economic growth, without which any consolidation would become unviable in the medium and long term. i would like to ask you, madam president, why the regulation laying down the financial measures for the implementation of the cfp was not included in the commission's proposal. this regulation finances very important areas, such as the collection of data and scientific advice, and the percentages of community co-financing in this area are generally low, at a maximum of 50%. why was this regulation and the measures it finances not also included in the commission proposal?

on behalf of the s&d group, mr president, it is high time that parliament brought the existing legislation on the union's external trade policy into line with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts resulting from the lisbon treaty. and we recall what the treaty says: firstly, that the european commission can only have legislative powers by means of delegated acts, by decision and under the control of the two legislators of the union; secondly, that the executive power is normally vested in the commission and not in the council, under the control of the member states and not under the control of the council itself. in the case of the common foreign trade policy, it should be stressed that this is a policy, an exclusive competence of the union and no longer of the member states, and a policy which follows the community method, that is, the initiative of the commission, approval of the two legislators. and so we have to be particularly demanding in applying the new rules of the lisbon treaty, and that means two things: parliament must maintain full control over all the union's legislative production, so we have to qualify as delegated acts all cases where the commission is entrusted with supplementing or amending legislative acts of the union; secondly, in the case of implementing acts, we cannot allow member states to have a veto power over the commission's executive power, precisely because it is an exclusive competence of the union. the application of the examination procedure, which gives the member states a veto power over the commission's implementing powers, cannot therefore be the rule but the exception. let me end by congratulating the rapporteur, our colleague mrs quisthoudt-rowohl, on the excellent work she has done and on the spirit of compromise she has achieved in this report.

in writing. - we agree with the measures proposed in the report: a higher rate of absorption of the eff funds by the member states, a reorientation of the priorities of the eff itself, directing it primarily towards support for productive activity and the development of coastal communities; support for the rejuvenation of the sector; employment and vocational training; the renewal and modernisation of the fleet and infrastructure supporting fishing activity. despite some of the limitations of the report, we consider the measures set out here to be urgent and decisive, and we therefore voted in favour.

in writing. the proposal aims to amend a proposal for a regulation opening a tariff quota for imports of high-quality beef from the united states and canada with a view to ending the long-running transatlantic dispute over meat hormones. the proposal for a regulation implements the measures contained in the memoranda of understanding signed with the united states and canada on the import of meat from animals not treated with certain growth promoting hormones. the solution to the trade dispute is for the eu to gradually increase the tariff quota for high-quality beef not treated with growth hormones, and the us and canada to gradually reduce or lift sanctions on eu products. i am voting in favour of this report because the adoption of this regulation by the european parliament and the council will bring mutual benefits, strengthen transatlantic trade links and re-establish confidence by improving market access on both sides of the atlantic.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the autonomous tariff quota for high-quality beef imports, as it includes proposals to end the dispute between the eu and the us and suspend sanctions on eu products, while ensuring that beef imports are made in accordance with strict eu standards.
in writing. − the eu/us/canada conflict over hormone-treated meat demonstrates the extent to which two trading blocs with similar references and concerns about food quality and safety can disagree in a lasting and counterproductive way for both. the length of the conflict and the severity of the sanctions have shown that it is in the interests of the community to seek a negotiated solution before taking excessive positions. the unilateral suspension of sanctions against the european union by the united states and canada is a positive sign which deserves an appropriate response by the eu adopting an autonomous tariff quota for imports of high-quality beef. that said, i believe that the union must not compromise when it considers that the safety of its citizens is at stake and must seek to make its partners aware of the need to adopt procedures and forms of consumer information which will enable consumers to be adequately and fully informed about the nature of the products they consume. i hope that the european union and the two american countries will continue to make efforts to integrate their economies more closely, which would greatly benefit both businesses and consumers.
in writing. - for more than two decades, the european union on the one hand and the united states of america and canada on the other have been involved in a dispute over hormones in meat, which has adversely affected transatlantic trade relations. the eu's ban on imports of beef and beef products treated with certain hormones, due to the need to protect consumers in terms of food safety, has been met by the us and canada with the imposition of customs duties on a number of european products. with the approval of the report by godelieve quisthoudt-rowohl, and consequent validation of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 617/2009 opening an autonomous tariff quota for imports of high-quality beef from the usa and canada, the above-mentioned dispute is over. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which not only deepens transatlantic trade relations but also suspends all sanctions against the eu on european products in trade terms.
in writing. - this report is based on the dispute over the ban on the importation of beef from the usa and canada treated with certain growth hormones, on the grounds of consumer protection and food safety. in order to put an end to the dispute, an agreement was reached providing for the gradual lifting of sanctions on eu agricultural products by the us and canada in exchange for an autonomous, duty-free tariff quota of high-quality non-hormone-treated beef. this opening of the european market to hormone-free beef is mainly due to the economic and trade pressure and threat from these two countries, and may have positive consequences for the export of various products from the eu, such as beef and pork products, which will benefit the major exporting countries. the sanctions imposed on european products are clear evidence of this. in addition to our concerns about the quality and food safety of meat from the usa and canada, given the known intensive and very intensive production methods used in these countries, we also have reservations about the consequences of opening this quota for the production of countries such as portugal.
in writing. the dispute over hormones in meat has adversely affected transatlantic trade relations in agricultural products for more than two decades. in 1988, the european union banned the import of beef and beef products treated with certain growth hormones for reasons of consumer protection and food safety. in 1996, the united states of america and canada challenged the ban under the wto dispute settlement system and were subsequently authorised to impose trade sanctions on agricultural products imported from the eu. since 1999, the united states and canada have imposed retaliatory customs duties on a wide range of european products, amounting to usd 116.8 million and cad 11.3 million annually, respectively. it should be noted that the final settlement of the dispute over hormones in meat should give a new impetus to the strengthening of economic and trade integration between the eu on the one hand and the united states and canada on the other. the adoption of this regulation by the european parliament and the council will result in mutual benefits, strengthen transatlantic trade links and restore confidence by improving market access.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the agreement is very important in that it encourages the production of european beef for export, thus making an important contribution to the agricultural sector, while protecting the consumer, because the increase in imports of american beef will be made without resorting to hormone-produced meat. the united states agreed to a complete suspension of all sanctions against the eu in may 2011 if the eu would honour its part of the agreement in a timely manner. if the agreement is not reciprocally implemented by the european union, we risk additional retaliatory measures by the united states, which must then be compensated for the damage caused by the non-compliance with wto rules.
in writing. − the present commitment by the eu, the united states and canada provides for the gradual lifting of sanctions imposed on eu agricultural products by the us and canada in exchange for an autonomous, duty-free tariff quota of high-quality non-hormone-treated beef. this agreement will help to strengthen transatlantic trade links, restore confidence and improve access to markets on both sides of the atlantic, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − over the past few years, the european union has been banning the import of beef and beef products, and the united states of america and canada have responded by introducing trade sanctions on agricultural products imported from europe. in 2009, the bilateral negotiations between the eu, the us and canada led to a solution for the removal of the barriers and the respective sanctions adopted. the talks eventually resulted in the conclusion of two memoranda of understanding. i agree with this report, which will enable the european union to respect the commitments it has made to the other countries concerned with a view to resolving the dispute. the mou will ensure that beef products imported under this quota will continue to meet the strict food safety requirements laid down in eu legislation. it should also be noted that the rapid adoption and entry into force of this regulation will contribute to strengthening transatlantic trade relations in this sector of economic activity.
in writing. - we remain concerned about the quality and food safety of meat from the usa and canada, given the known intensive and very intensive production methods used in these countries, but our concerns also concern the possible consequences of opening this quota for the production of countries such as portugal. we know that the opening up of beef imports could have positive consequences for the export of various products from the eu, such as beef and pig products, but it will mainly benefit the large exporting countries.
in writing. - i approve this report as omnibus i and omnibus ii, documents relating to the new systems of delegated and implementing acts that this report covers, aim to bring the european union's trade policy into line with the provisions of the lisbon treaty. this is important because it strengthens the powers of the european parliament, which must therefore be respected, while it is politically important to keep parliament united around this wish.
in writing. - this is a very technical report, reflecting the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon in the union's common commercial policy, and seeking to amend certain regulations as regards the procedures for adopting certain measures. the report now adopted at first reading was not the subject of major divisions between the parliamentary groups, as its vote with only one vote against and two abstentions in the committee on international trade shows, and it is now being submitted to the european commission for examination. the amendments now proposed seek to make the trade policy of the european union (which has just become the european economic community) more effective and more efficient, and as a committed europeanist i cannot but strongly support this report.

in writing. - this proposal amends certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy as regards the procedures for adopting certain measures (omnibus i) and aims to adapt 26 regulations relating to the common commercial policy to the treaty of lisbon. this proposal for a commission regulation aims to replace the procedures for deciding on implementing measures established by 26 regulations by means of delegated or implementing acts. the regulations concerned are mainly regulations allowing the adoption of trade policy safeguard measures. the amendments are designed to make the commission's exercise of implementing powers more effective and efficient and to contribute to a better common commercial policy.
in writing. the report by mr godelieve quisthoudt-rowohl deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending certain regulations as regards the procedures for adopting certain measures relating to the common commercial policy. this is the adaptation of 26 regulations to the new primary law provisions of the lisbon treaty as regards the legal concept of delegated acts. until now, trade policy has been outside the comitology process, depending exclusively on council decisions. i welcome the progress made in this area, particularly with regard to the codecision procedure, because it is not acceptable that the council and the commission can decide without the prior agreement of the european parliament, which is responsible for monitoring these acts. in the case of implementing acts, i agree that member states cannot have a veto right in a general way, but only exceptionally. i regret that the united kingdom and ireland do not approve this regulation, which i voted for, which would contribute to a genuine free movement of people and goods throughout the eu and a more effective fight against commercial dumping.
in writing. the report aims to bring 26 regulations on the common commercial policy (cpc) into line with the lisbon treaty. the treaty provides that trade policy is an exclusive competence of the eu. following its entry into force and the adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011, the commission now has the exclusive power to implement the rules on trade policy. the definition of trading partners, trade and the objectives to which trade must be subject are an important instrument of economic sovereignty. the disposal of this sovereign instrument has, for example, resulted in very serious losses for portugal in numerous sectors of economic activity and for the country in general. trade policy has been directed towards maximising the profits of the large economic groups of the major eu powers, to the clear detriment of countries such as portugal and weaker sectors of economic activity, which have been exposed to fierce and destructive competition. free trade has been one of the main instruments of the ccp, guiding it towards a logic of capitalist competition rather than complementarity and mutual benefit. our profound disagreement with the cpc is therefore an assumption which we cannot fail to take into account in the analysis of this report.
in writing. - this proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy as regards the procedures for adopting certain measures (omnibus i) aims to adapt 26 regulations relating to the common commercial policy to the new primary law provisions of the treaty of lisbon. this is in particular to adapt the rules to the provisions of articles 290 and 291 tfeu and to the provisions of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council, as a consequence of article 291 (3) tfeu, laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. the report specifies the substance of the commission proposal for all 26 regulations, weighs the pros and cons of the use of delegated acts and implementing provisions and compares the advisory and examination procedures. the result is a balanced position between the various legal instruments, which takes into account the material and legal interests of all stakeholders, the legislation in force since 1 december 2009 and the institutional interests of the three european institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy. the aim is to adapt the rules laying down the general rules and principles governing the mechanisms for monitoring by the member states of the commission's implementing powers. the aim is to introduce the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon in this area, taking account of the material and legal interests of all those concerned and the institutional interests of the three european institutions.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and the adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011, executive decisions on trade policy, as in the case of other eu policy areas, are taken by the commission alone, either by delegated or implementing acts. this document thus aims to amend all regulations under this policy in order to promote an adaptation of the regulation to the provisions of the primary law of the lisbon treaty, in particular articles 290 and 291 tfeu. for these reasons i voted in favour of the european parliament's document.

in writing. − it is recognised by the eu that poverty and outdated farming techniques, but also and above all child labour, are widespread features of the cocoa sector. as the world's largest importer and consumer of cocoa, and home to the largest chocolate processors and manufacturers, the eu has and should absolutely take responsibility for making this sector more sustainable. numerous reports reveal that cocoa farmers continue to use child labour on their farms. although much child labour is carried out within the family, the situation is worrying and therefore urgently needs to be addressed.
in writing. - according to the international labour organisation, more than 215 million children worldwide are victims of child labour, of whom 115 million are engaged in tasks considered dangerous. the majority of these situations occur in the so-called developing countries, and to put an end to this scourge it is essential to eradicate the situations of poverty that give rise to it. the motion for a resolution tabled by mr vital moreira on behalf of the committee on international trade, pursuant to rule 110 (2), deals with child labour in the cocoa sector. 70% of the world's cocoa production is in west africa and some 7.5 million people are employed there, the vast majority on family farms, making it easier to use child labour in a society where there are no alternatives to wealth creation and no opportunities for young people outside of school. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the primary right of children is education and their place in school. this is the only way to end poverty in societies that consider child labor as just another source of resources.
in writing. the resolution's main objective is to draw attention to and condemn the use of child labour in cocoa fields and all forms of child labour. the resolution is a roll of good intentions and good practice in the fight against child labour. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of workers' rights and the protection of the environment. it is concealed, however, that many of the clauses complained of in some agreements are merely a dead letter, never put into practice and always relegated to the background in favour of business and profit. the real reasons for the use of child labour are not focused here. in particular, the socioeconomic conditions of the farmers and workers on these cocoa plantations. the resolution makes pertinent findings concerning the pressure to reduce labour costs in cocoa fields. but unfortunately, few solutions are put forward to counteract these pressures and to promote the necessary increase in the wages of these workers.
in writing. - following the international cocoa agreement, the european parliament, while acknowledging the importance of this sector, does not dismiss one of the major problems associated with it: child exploitation. as the european union is the world's largest consumer of chocolate, this resolution is of considerable importance, as it is intended to implement measures to achieve greater sustainability in the sector and also to raise awareness among all those involved of the problem of child labour, which unfortunately still occurs in this and other sectors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on child labour because it strongly condemns the use of child labour in cocoa fields. child labour is one of the most dramatic forms of violation of children's rights, which jeopardizes not only their future but also the future of the community to which they belong.
in writing. − at a time when the european parliament is called upon to approve the 2010 international cocoa conclusion, it is curious that a status report is being made here on initiatives to combat the worst forms of child labour on cocoa farms in west africa. in this respect, it must be recognized that, although progress has been made, much remains to be done. it should therefore stress the need for the authorities to assume their responsibilities in the fight against the trafficking of children and all forms of forced child labour and to promote the full implementation of the un convention on the rights of the child and the relevant ilo conventions. similarly, initiatives tending to involve the various actors - governments, industry, producers and civil society - aiming at eradicating child labour, improving the lives of children and adults working on cocoa farms and ensuring that cocoa is grown in a responsible manner should be welcomed.
in writing. − in the process of approving the 2010 cocoa agreement, knowing its importance for the producing countries, i voted in favour. however, i leave my concern about reports of the use of child labour subject to inhuman conditions in the production and harvesting of cocoa beans. it is therefore necessary that this issue be seriously discussed within the cocoa ilo and that answers be found to combat it. all stakeholders, from national governments to businesses, civil society, exporting countries and non-governmental organisations, should be involved in the process to raise awareness of this issue. finally, if the practice by a company and/or the state is systematic, we should not rule out the possibility of imposing sanctions on it.
in writing. - this resolution makes important findings concerning the pressure to reduce labour costs in the cocoa fields, but does not put forward solutions to counteract these pressures and to promote the necessary increase in the wages of these workers. the main reasons for the use of labour are the difficult socioeconomic conditions of the farmers and workers on these cocoa plantations. we believe, however, that it is important to be alert to the use of child labour in cocoa fields and condemn it, as well as all forms of child labour.
in writing. - i support this report because i believe that the international cocoa agreement can be an opportunity to address the issue of child labour. it is important that the different actors in the fight against child labour develop a strategy that enables them to identify the roots of this problem. the european union can and must play a vital role, because when it adopts its policies it can also use them to deal with the problem. one of the immediate solutions is for the commission to try to trace goods that are produced through child labour.
in writing. - since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, all agreements in areas covered by the ordinary legislative procedure are subject to the approval of the european parliament. this is the case with the eu's common trade policy, of which the 2010 cocoa agreement is an integral part. this international cocoa agreement 2010 replaces the 2001 agreement and aims to create conditions for fairer and more sustainable world cocoa trade through enhanced international cooperation between producers and consumers within the framework of the international cocoa organisation. improve market transparency by promoting the role of the international cocoa organisation in the collection, processing and distribution of data and its cooperation with industry and ngos. this new agreement sets clear objectives aimed at a sustainable cocoa economy, recognising the importance of economic viability and social and environmental responsibility at all stages of the value chain. it also recognises the need to ensure fair prices for cocoa and fair incomes, as well as to promote cocoa quality and develop food safety procedures. i therefore support this recommendation for parliament to approve this agreement.
in writing. − the 2010 international cocoa agreement is of major importance in the context of international trade and the global cocoa economy. the agreement is valid for 10 years, so it is essential that there is an appropriate space for discussion of all cocoa-related issues between the signatory governments as well as with the private sector. the 2010 international cocoa agreement is fundamental to the viability and development of cocoa producing countries, contributing to the sustainability of these economies by facilitating fair prices that allow for equitable revenues for producers and consumers and ultimately promoting the transparency of the global cocoa economy.
in writing. the recommendation under consideration, drafted by vital moreira, concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion by the european union of the 2010 international cocoa agreement. the conclusion of this agreement has been delayed due to the large-scale use of child labour in this sector. 70% of the world's cocoa production is in west africa and some 7.5 million people are employed there, the vast majority on family farms, making it easier to use child labour in a society where there are no alternatives to wealth creation and no opportunities for young people outside of school. most of the chocolate consumed in europe is produced by child labour. the eu is a stronghold of values, including human rights and children's rights in particular, and cannot establish commercial links with organisations or countries that exploit child labour. i voted in favour of this resolution because it not only strongly condemns the use of child labour in cocoa fields but also calls on the governments of the countries concerned to ratify and/or comply with the un convention on the rights of the child and the ilo conventions.
in writing. − the international cocoa agreement 2010 will replace the 2001 agreement, which in turn replaced the 1993 agreement. the first was established in 1972. the eu is party to this agreement. the stated objectives of this new agreement are: to promote international cooperation within the world cocoa economy; to contribute to the strengthening of the national cocoa economies of the member countries; to seek fair prices that will provide equitable revenues for producers and consumers; to advocate the removal of barriers to trade; to promote and encourage the consumption of chocolate and cocoa products and to encourage members to improve the quality of cocoa. without prejudice to the positive aspects associated with this multilateral forum, it is worth highlighting a background finding. in the various forms that this agreement has taken over the years, it has always been based on a vision - and a reality! - of an international division of labour that is profoundly unfavourable to developing countries, seen as mere producers and exporters of cheap raw materials, prevented from progressing in the value chain of the sector and keeping economies highly dependent and poorly diversified. the defence of free trade in the objectives of the agreement does not help to alter this fundamental view, but rather reinforces it.
in writing. − the new agreement, which replaces the 2001 agreement, aims to: promote international cooperation within the world cocoa economy; provide an appropriate forum for discussion of all cocoa-related issues between governments as well as with the private sector; contribute to strengthening the national cocoa economies of the member countries; seek fair prices that provide equitable revenues for producers and consumers; encourage an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy; promote transparency in the world cocoa economy through the collection, analysis and dissemination of relevant statistical data and the conduct of appropriate studies; advocate the elimination of trade barriers; promote and encourage the consumption of chocolate and cocoa products; and encourage members to improve the quality of cocoa. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, all agreements in areas covered by the ordinary legislative procedure are subject to the approval of the european parliament. this is the case with the eu's common commercial policy, of which the 2010 cocoa agreement is an integral part.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this new agreement on cocoa, which has as its main objectives the promotion of international cooperation within the world cocoa economy, through an appropriate forum for the discussion of all cocoa-related issues between governments as well as with the private sector, thus contributing to the strengthening of the national cocoa economies of the member countries. these measures are intended to achieve fair prices that allow for equitable revenues for producers as well as consumers, to encourage an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy and to promote transparency in the global cocoa economy.
in writing. − as part of the eu's common commercial policy, this document aims to make the cocoa sector fairer, more transparent and more sustainable. this sector, which is the livelihood of 50 million people worldwide, is essential to the eu's own economy, as the european chocolate industry is the largest in the world. the promotion of international cooperation within the world economy in this sector, the elimination of trade barriers and the promotion of an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy are some of the objectives set out in this agreement, the achievement of which deserves my support.
in writing. − the 2010 cocoa agreement, which replaces the 2001 cocoa agreement and was adopted in 2010 at the un cocoa conference, brings together the main cocoa producing and consuming countries of which the eu is a member. the aim of this agreement is to create fair, equitable and sustainable conditions for world trade in cocoa by strengthening international cooperation within the international cocoa organisation, which is strengthening its powers under this agreement. i am voting in favour of the agreement because i think it is important to establish rules and rethink strategies for this sector, on which 50 million people depend for their livelihoods.
in writing. - while we believe that there are a number of positive aspects associated with this international agreement, which has been in place for several years, we would like to make it clear that it has always been based on an international division of labour which is profoundly unfavourable to developing countries, seen as mere producers and exporters of cheap raw materials, prevented from progressing in the value chain of the sector and keeping economies highly dependent and poorly diversified. it was important, in order to counteract the strengthening of this path, that free trade was not advocated, as is done, in the objectives of the agreement.

in writing. - diabetes is the most common of the non-communicable diseases, affecting more than 32 million citizens of the european union - about 10% of the total population - with the significant increase in this disease in children and young people in portugal being of particular concern. type 2 diabetes reduces life expectancy by 5-10 years and type 1 diabetes reduces life expectancy by about 20 years, and overall is responsible for 325 000 deaths annually. in most member states, the implications of diabetes account for more than 10% of health expenditure. reducing risk factors such as habits and lifestyles is increasingly critical to achieving incidence reduction. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the measures it contains will make a positive contribution to the prevention and reduction of the incidence of diabetes among the citizens.

in writing. − diabetes is the most common of the non-communicable diseases, affecting more than 32 million eu citizens, or about 10% of the total population, and its current progressive trend is of particular concern. in the case of portugal, there is also a significant increase in its incidence in children and young people. unfortunately, the participation of people with diabetes in their own care accounts for 95% of all people with the disease, with obvious consequences for psychosocial and their own quality of life. as a doctor and a legislator, i believe that prevention is essential, not just research. and not just for diabetes, but for other diseases of the same kind like hypertension and cardiovascular disease. it is therefore essential that member states, with the support of the commission, develop, implement and monitor national programmes for diabetes, aimed at health promotion, reduction of risk factors, prediction, prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of diabetes, which also aim at reducing inequalities and optimising resources. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the measures it contains can make a positive contribution to reducing the incidence of diabetes in the european union.

in writing. − according to the world health organisation, 86% of deaths in europe are caused by non-communicable diseases, with diabetes being among the most common. while it cannot be said lightly that this is a behavioural disease, the truth is that it is associated with unhealthy lifestyle habits - tobacco, poor diet, lack of physical activity and alcohol. it is therefore urgent to develop sectoral policies that contribute to the prevention of diabetes and to avoid its complications and the economic and social costs of this disease. it is therefore up to the states, and the union can play an important role in this respect, to reduce the prevalence, if not the prevalence, at least the mortality associated with diabetes. this must be done not only through prevention - coupled with campaigns to promote healthier lifestyles - but also through a very serious focus on the early diagnosis, detection and treatment of diabetes, factors which we know are essential to reducing its mortality.

madam president, piracy is a serious problem, but it is not the only one, nor the most serious, off the horn of africa. to combat it effectively, the european union must build a comprehensive strategy for the region. this implies attacking the source of piracy, which is not located at sea but on land. it is the lack of a state, of governance, of representative institutions that defend the interests of the somali people. it is because of its lack of integration into such a strategy that operation atalanta, despite its importance as a naval mission in the csdp framework, is unable to achieve its objectives. worse, piracy became sophisticated and rampant, and al-shabaab grew, armed and radicalized. atalanta's primary mandate is to protect international shipping along the somali coast. but what does the european union do about the many other maritime crimes committed by foreign vessels in the same waters, from illegal fishing to dumping of toxic waste? what information does brussels have on this subject, sent by atalanta over the three years it has been operating, in compliance with its mandate also on this subject on fishing within 200 miles of the somali coast? can this data be provided to this parliament? has the european union submitted this data to the un and asked the security council to take it into account? somalia and the region need a strengthened and concerted political, diplomatic, economic and military effort on the ground, and not just at sea involving the un, the african union, the united states, the european union, india, china and other powers, but focused on the concept of human security in order to meet the survival and development needs of the somali people, which are at the core of the piracy industry. an effort that produces results in the building of representative institutions in somalia, which are clearly no more than the artificial tfg supported by invading troops from neighbouring ethiopia, and an effort that does not continue to neglect the potential for governance that can be expanded from the autonomous areas of puntland and somaliland, with which the european union has to work. (the speaker accepts the answer to a question on the 'blue card' (rule 149 (8)).)
blue-card answer. – madam president, i do not think that private security firms are the solution, but the eu, i would agree, can be. this is not a problem that can be solved overnight. it is a problem that has existed since at least 2005. the eu should have an autonomous strategy for somalia. if we look at how much money we have spent in the whole operation and at the results, including in fighting piracy, these are quite limited, because our objectives cannot be achieved until the core question of the governance in somalia is addressed. the effort is too big for the eu alone. it has to act in concert with others in the international community. how much money could have been saved, though, if something more meaningful had been done for governance in somalia. nothing has been done so far. our strategy has been to follow the us totally in a very non-critical way. that is why we are where we are and unhappy with the results, including in fighting piracy and hostage taking. until we address the question of the governance in somalia – and not with a fake institution like the tfg, the transitional government – we will not improve the situation for ships passing through those waters.
madam president, it is clear that the problem of maritime piracy must be tackled. however, under the pretext of combating maritime piracy, imperialist plans for controlling international waters, controlling geostrategically important regions, for gaining access to natural resources or controlling their flow, as may be the danger in the case of the horn of africa, must not be put into practice. what is decisive in combating maritime piracy is to combat the causes associated with it, namely to combat the poverty to which the peoples of the african countries have been voted in the framework of the capitalist system, which has always used these countries to supply the central countries with raw materials at low cost. what is needed is a genuine development policy which respects the sovereignty of these countries and peoples. what is needed is the rejection of the militarization of the european union, respect for international law, the charter of the united nations, the principles of sovereignty and non-interference, and the development of more equitable and fairer international economic relations.
madam president, commissioner, maritime piracy is today a phenomenon that is becoming more widespread and frequent, more organized and profitable, more audacious and violent, to which no vessel seems to be immune, from fishing boats and merchant ships to yachts and cruise ships. there are 1,500 pirates operating off the coast of somalia alone. the safety and freedom of persons are seriously affected, all maritime activities and the economy suffer enormous losses, in addition to the costs of rescues, insurance, diversion, pursuit, etc. in 2012 alone, there were 22 reported robberies, and in february alone, somali pirates captured 17 vessels and took 251 hostages. in 2009, the commission systematised its action in two stages: prevention, deterrence and repression, and also tackling the causes of piracy. but it persists and grows, which requires reinforced action by both the commission and the member states. the commission should extend its military action beyond 2012 and step up its diplomatic action to obtain effective cooperation from third countries hosting pirates. the member states will have to make efforts both in the field of criminal investigation, especially as regards the tracing of ransom money, and in the legal field, especially as regards the establishment of conditions for the trial of pirates. these concerted actions by the commission and the member states, but also with other countries and regions of the world, are urgently needed to restore safety on the seas, which, as far as fishing is concerned, affects both industrial fleets and small local vessels, affecting the economy of the european union, but also the livelihood of local communities, worsening their poverty and throwing the population into piracy, in a cycle that is intensifying successively and which must be cut off once and for all.
for the gue/ngl group i would like to give an example. in portugal, with public funds and european money, we have managed to ensure that today there is 98% coverage in water supply and 90% coverage in sanitation. this investment was paid for by portuguese and european taxpayers, and now what is going to be done is to privatize water in portugal. why do i bring this example to this house? because it is the clear example of what we are doing wrong in the field of water - whether in portugal, in europe or in the world. we're treating water like a commodity. well, water is a public good, not a business. water is a scarce commodity, it's not a competitive commodity. water should be for everyone, not just those who can afford it. water and water resources are for conservation, not for disruption or contamination. water is a right - that's it, it's a fundamental human right. and trying to make a profit from water is as reasonable as starting to sell air in plastic bags. it's not reasonable. there are millions of people in the world without access to water.
mr president, in july 2010, at the culmination of a long battle, the united nations general assembly adopted a resolution recognizing the right to safe drinking water and sanitation as a human right essential to the full enjoyment of life and all human rights. the resolution calls on states and international organisations to step up efforts to provide safe, affordable and accessible drinking water and sanitation for all people. it was not easy to secure the adoption of this text. it is no coincidence that some countries, including some member states, initially vetoed it, but then abstained in the final vote. it is that the un text is strong and clear, while others prefer the partial and ambiguous approach that gives way to the multimillion-dollar water and sanitation businesses. the effective guarantee of the right to water and sanitation is irrevocably confronted with the greed of the water transnational cartel. the effective guarantee of this right requires public ownership and management of this precious commons.
mr president, it is essential to discuss the quality and quantity of water and the impacts of climate change which are already being felt in rainfall levels. in my country, portugal, at the end of february, 68% of the territory was in severe drought and 32% in extreme drought - a calamity. droughts and floods kill more people than any other natural disaster. the so-called water crisis, both in terms of quantity and quality, is also the result of abuses, and not just of natural causes. the problem is also one of management. the un itself recognizes the need to develop ethically sound water management systems. europe continues to waste about 50% of its water due to inefficiencies. water is a public good, but scarce, which should be accessible to all at fair prices. it is not a commodity subject to speculation. we must reduce consumption and combat waste... in writing. - i approve this report. on the one hand, the objective of achieving a low-carbon economy by 2050 will help to tackle the main problems posed by climate change. on the other hand, it is an opportunity for the economy, as it is an added value for the eu to focus on a globally efficient and innovative knowledge economy, meeting the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. − at a time when the debate on greenhouse gas emissions has become unavoidable and when maintaining the current energy dependence on oil and its derivatives is unsustainable, it is important that more environmentally friendly and equally reliable energy alternatives are found. it is also essential that europe finds, within the eu2020 strategy, innovative ways to promote sustainable and greener growth. the 2010 data are not encouraging, however, with a 6% increase in carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it is therefore urgent to ensure the development of a low-carbon economy which is nonetheless competitive and does not harm the already weakened european economy. we cannot set ourselves such high emission targets that they create conditions of unfair competition with the rest of the world and undermine european competitiveness.

in writing. - this report is a paradigmatic example of the mercantilist approach that has presided over the much-touted transition to a low-carbon economy. the reaffirmation of the belief in emissions trading, despite its widely demonstrated perversity and ineffectiveness, the excessive focus on the issue of energy sources without giving due attention to consumption patterns and the underlying economic model are some of the most obvious shortcomings and weaknesses of this report. issues such as current production and trade models, free trade and its impacts on the delocalisation of production vis-à-vis consumption, and on energy consumption flows and patterns are insufficiently addressed. in the field of transport, for example, the defence of a modern, efficient public transport system with wide coverage and low prices for the population - in contrast to what is currently being done, for example, in portugal under the eu-imf programme - gives way to the market, liberalisation and charges in the various modes of transport. the focus on individual transport (which is certainly to the liking of the car industry), the defence of the single european sky and the inclusion of the sector in the emissions trading scheme are illustrative examples of the approach that inspires the whole report.
in writing. - the debate on emissions of polluting gases is becoming increasingly important, but we cannot continue to be hostages to our energy dependence on oil and its derivatives. we must therefore find energy alternatives that are more environmentally friendly and equally reliable. europe is obliged to find, by taking advantage of the eu2020 strategy, innovative ways to promote economic growth without further affecting the environment. however, data from 2010 tells us that there was a 6% increase in carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere. however, as this report points out, europe is responsible for only 11% of global co2 emissions and our actions in isolation are not enough to stop the process of increasing co2 emissions. this has to be a joint effort by all the powers, particularly the brics, which are increasingly responsible for co2 emissions. what is required of all is the development of a low-carbon economy which is still competitive and does not harm the european economy, which is currently very weakened by the world crisis. on the other hand, we cannot demand of ourselves what others do not fulfil, and thereby lose our competitiveness on world markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on a roadmap for the transition to a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050 because it has the ambition of a europe with cutting-edge, high-tech industry and highly skilled professionals who create the products we need using fewer resources and emitting less co2 in manufacturing them. the measures presented in this report contribute to a genuine green economy.
in writing. - this roadmap for the transition to a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050, presented by the european commission, deserves my applause. although it will require a large investment in sectors such as green technologies and transport, infrastructure (e.g. smart electricity grids) and environmental protection, this programme will always be a long-term added value. it is our responsibility to take the lead in reducing co2 emissions, even if our actions alone are not enough to stop the warming process. we must therefore aim for a high-tech, high-end industry in europe with highly qualified professionals who create the products we need, using fewer resources and emitting less co2. finally, there is a need to review the emissions trading system so that prices recover to the levels envisaged when the legislation was adopted and to avoid the so-called carbon leakage, i.e. the possibility for some companies to leave europe to avoid higher costs resulting from measures taken to reduce co2 emissions.

in writing. − the presidential elections in russia have made clear the centrality of vladimir putin's role in shaping the country's destiny, confirming the secondary role that had been attributed by many observers to former president medvedev. as in previous elections, these elections were marked by doubts from the international community about the whole process which, if not credible in calling into question who would win, may at least call into question the magnitude of putin's victory. the commission is therefore calling for unambiguous adherence to the best international standards. russia faces a major strategic challenge, and it is expected that it will have to choose between the recent alignment with china and a rapprochement with europe. despite the recent russian-chinese partnership in defending the syrian regime, i believe that in the medium and long term russia will not fail to recognize that its interests will be best served by choosing to move closer to the west. i hope that this will be the case and that the commission will endeavour to adopt standards and practices which coincide with this desirable future alignment.
in writing. - in the face of serious suspicions of electoral fraud in the 1996 presidential elections, neither the eu nor the us failed to praise russian democracy and the election of the candidate they wanted at the time - boris iletsin. today's criticisms, including those which are missing from this resolution, highlight the eu's well-known policy of double standards. the eu, like the us, has already realised that the russian government is not ready to submit fully to its interests. the russian government, which cannot hide its role in the service of the national plutocracy, has been holding back the advancement of the interests of these two blocs by protecting national wealth, particularly energy, from foreign interests. more recently, russia's veto in the un security council of military intervention in syria has led the us and the eu to see their expansionist ambitions blocked. in short, what concerns the eu and the us is not the defence of democracy but their desire to see russia have a government more likely to satisfy their own undeniable interests and ambitions for imperial domination.
in writing. − enhanced cooperation and good neighbourly relations between the eu and russia are of crucial importance for the stability, security and prosperity of europe. the development of a strategic partnership between the european union and the russian federation can only be based on shared common values. however, concerns remain about the russian federation's development in respect for and protection of human rights and respect for generally accepted democratic principles, rules and processes. the russian federation is a full member of the council of europe and the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) and has therefore committed itself to respecting the principles of democracy and human rights. on 12 april 2011, the european court of human rights condemned the lengthy registration processes of political parties in russia, which do not respect the electoral standards set by the council of europe and the osce, and the limitations on the registration of political parties and candidates that restrict political debate and pluralism in russia. we must continue to encourage the russian leadership to adopt more democratic practices towards opposition parties.
in writing. − the eu-russia political dialogue is of paramount importance to both sides. this motion for a resolution sets out the european parliament's observations on the presidential elections in russia. i voted in favour because i consider the comments made constructive and in line with the demands of the russian people, who have called for further reforms through peaceful demonstrations, which are frequent and involve an impressive number of citizens.
in writing. - the allegations of irregularities in the duma elections and the recent presidential elections are likely to raise the greatest concerns about russia's respect for human rights and democratic principles. it is therefore essential that russian political leaders engage in a constructive dialogue with the opposition and adopt the necessary reforms to ensure effective competition and political pluralism, by promoting, to this end, the simplification of the rules governing the registration of political parties, the resolution of problems concerning freedom of the press, assembly and expression, and the deepening of the rule of law and democratic transparency.
in writing. − the cooperation agreement between the european union and the russian federation was concluded in 1997 and extended until 2010, when it was replaced by a new agreement which established a comprehensive framework for bilateral relations. in addition to the agreements concluded, the european union remains deeply concerned about the protection of human rights and respect for democratic and electoral principles in russia. i am voting in favour of this report because i agree with the electoral observation mission which found irregularities in the preparation and conduct of the elections and the fact that the choice of voters was limited, and that it is important to adopt reforms in the existing political system. finally, i also regard the growing civic participation in the election campaign as extremely positive, which should allow for a serious and transparent analysis of the irregularities detected, in order to strengthen the democratic rules for future elections.
in writing. the criticisms which are implicit in this motion for a resolution on the results of the presidential elections in russia only demonstrate once more that the european union has two weights and two measures. it is a fact that, during the various suspicions of electoral fraud in the 1996 presidential elections, neither the eu nor the us failed to praise russian democracy and the election of the candidate they liked boris yeltsin. the us and the eu have already understood that the russian government is not ready to submit fully to their imperialist interests. this has been demonstrated by the russian government through a certain economic and political independence and defence of its national wealth, particularly energy, and the role of the state in certain strategic sectors. more recently, russia's veto in the un security council of military intervention in syria has led to the us and eu seeing their expansionist pretensions blocked. the question that concerns the eu and the us is not the defence of democracy, but their desire to see russia have a government that is more in line with their interests.

in writing. − there are several reports of the continuing violation of human rights in kazakhstan, casting doubt on the implementation of political reforms being carried out by the government of this country. abuse of power, detention of political opponents and journalists, of activists who were present at the demonstration in the city of zhanaozen last december, religious repression, violation of freedom of the press and the basic principles of the rule of law. i think it is important to clarify the government's actions towards the zhanaozen protesters and to await the investigation of the national commission established with the un monitoring. on the other hand, in parallel with the negotiations for a strengthened eu-kazakhstan agreement, the eu must show its concern at the dilution of fundamental and democratic rights and alert the authorities to the need for reforms. stability and development of kazakhstan are fundamental to the socioeconomic growth of central asia and international relations as a whole.

in writing. - i approve this resolution, reinforcing the message that water is a precious and public good and must be accessible to all mankind. the european union must therefore focus its position on promoting free access to water for all people, on efforts to conserve and manage it, taking account of the threats of climate change and greater coordination at regional, national, european and global levels in the interests of water quality.
in writing. - drinking water, an element we all take for granted, is not, however, accessible to the entire world population. however, it plays a key role in public health and environmental protection and as such these should be priorities for any appropriate water management policy. this is why the proper protection of drinking water resources is so important for human health and for combating water pollution by limiting the amount of dangerous substances entering the environment and areas with drinking water resources. in this new millennium, water must be seen as a genuine fundamental right of all citizens and as such deserves the appropriate protection of national, european and international legislators.
in writing. - this resolution amalgamates some commonplace notions about water with incorrect generalizations, which serve as a wrapper for a set of quite serious mercantilist objectives. the document distorts the text of the un resolution on the human right to water and sanitation, failing to faithfully reproduce the content of what was a very important decision of the un assembly. on the other hand, it does not take on, as was required, the clear and unequivocal defense of public ownership and management of water, creating the ambiguity that is conducive to business and privatization. the rejection of our amendments in this respect is indicative of the intentions of the majority of this parliament. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat illegal immigration and to ensure that the rights of the child are respected. the entire document is based on the collection of funds to be made available to eu-based transnational corporations, in particular water and sanitation companies and related service providers. the model is known. the funds are made available as aid to developing countries, are collected by these transnational corporations and are considered to be the debt of these countries, and privatisations are associated with the process.
in writing. - contrary to what it may seem, drinking water, an element we all take for granted, is not, however, accessible to the entire world population. water is, however, fundamental to public health and environmental protection and therefore an appropriate water policy should be a priority for all. proper protection of drinking water resources and the fight against water pollution are essential if we are to safeguard areas where drinking water resources exist. water should be accessible to all citizens, as a fundamental right, and thus deserving of adequate protection by national, european and international legislators.
in writing. − water is a common good of mankind, so access to it must be universal and constitute a fundamental right. i voted in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament welcomes the recognition by the united nations of the human right to safe drinking water and basic sanitation, which derives from the right to an adequate standard of living. i support the call for all necessary efforts to be made to ensure that the most deprived people have access to water by 2015.
in writing. − water is a commodity that is increasingly under threat, given the current demographic growth, urbanisation and the most diverse types of pollution. to make matters worse, it is a commodity that is not available to everyone. as a result, millions of people die each year from water-related diseases and from poor sanitation. in order to ensure the well-being of all, water must be considered a common good of mankind and not a source of profit. access to water should therefore be a fundamental and universal right. in addition, all countries are expected to set a quantitative target for reducing chemical and biological pollution from urban wastewater and soil-related activities by 2015 in order to protect and restore water quality and support the sustainability of water resources and ecosystems. finally, at the economic level, it is important to encourage public and private investment in research and development of innovative technologies in all water sectors.
in writing. − a significant proportion of developing countries lack basic sanitation infrastructure to enable effective management of water resources, a key precondition for poverty reduction. it should be noted that over 800 million people annually consume water from unsafe sources, which ultimately leads to the death of approximately 2.5 million children. i agree with this report, since it is necessary to ensure that access to water is a fundamental and universal right and should not be a source of profit but rather contribute to improving the quality of life of the population. i therefore believe that public and private entities should invest increasingly in the research and development of innovative technologies in all water sectors, encouraging the use of new technologies in agriculture with a view to producing sufficient and safe food. i believe it is essential that member states commit themselves increasingly to the achievement of the millennium development goals set by the united nations and also take into account the relevant outcomes of the rio+20 conference on sustainable development.
in writing. - this document distorts the text of the un resolution on the human right to water and sanitation, failing to faithfully reproduce the content of what was a very important decision of the un assembly. nor does it take a clear and unequivocal stand for public ownership and management of water, creating the ambiguity that is conducive to business and privatization. other aspects that we have not reviewed are the recommendation of the polluter-pays principle, the prospect of another water and sanitation tax, and the raising of funds to be made available to eu-based transnational corporations, including water and sanitation and related service providers.
