the rapporteur. - mr president, sometimes we have to remember where we came from: if you look at the history of international refugee law, you see that the aknur constitution in 1949, the geneva convention on refugees in 1951, and the first major refugee resettlement effort, which was in 1956 after the revolution in hungary, all of them were aimed at european refugees. europe was then the continent of refugees. and we europeans often forget that today, when we see refugees coming from the rest of the world. we also have to think about the world we're in. refugees are the most vulnerable population in the world. of the few million refugees who exist, most want to return home to their countries of origin. another part may stay in transit countries with which they sometimes have cultural or linguistic affinities. but a small portion of refugees, which aknur estimates at about 200,000 a year, can neither return home, where their lives would be at risk, nor stay where they are, in countries that are often not signatories to the geneva conventions. we must therefore give them access to a new life in a third country. the resettlement of refugees is a global, orderly and peaceful effort in which we must all play our part, and europe must play its part precisely by remembering where it came from and its history. today, europe resettles about 5,000 refugees a year, compared to about 100,000 resettled by other countries: the united states, primarily, canada, australia, or even new players like brazil and chile. we must then get down to business, and we have done so in recent years. the codecision on the european refugee fund, which we voted on in this house two years ago, introduces new humanitarian priorities with clearer categories, strategic priorities in the european union's neighbourhood where we can act to help resolve critical humanitarian emergencies, and modulation between the support given to member states so that we can attract new member states and get to 27, because when we started this process, only 10 were resettling and now we are going to 13 who want to resettle. it hasn't been easy to make this journey for two years now. since it was initiated under the swedish presidency and until it was finally completed under the danish presidency. there have been in these various presidencies various obstacles and there have been various moments of anguish when lives have been lost and when people have waited in refugee camps longer than we would have liked. in my view, and i believe in the view of european citizens and many people in this house and in the institutions, this is not the way to make a law in a matter of life and death. the lisbon treaty, which introduced the codecision procedure, must be followed by an interinstitutional agreement which provides for clear deadlines for the adoption of such legislation. we can't take two years to make a law in a life-or-death situation. i should, however, like to thank the danish presidency for its activity and the hard work it has put into this dossier, which has enabled us to close this procedure, especially since denmark, because it has an option on these matters, does not have access to the money from the european refugee fund. it was selfless and noble work, as indeed was much of the work done here in this parliament. the refugees, it is not too much to remember, are not the ones who vote for the members who are here, are not the ones who pay their salaries through their taxes or are not the leaders of our political parties, but from greek communists to british conservatives, there has been a huge alliance in this house to get this dossier to a good end and i am very grateful for that. and i would like to end by remembering the commission itself, where the process was initiated, and, on behalf of many commission officials, i would like to mention a person who worked for two years on this dossier and who unfortunately passed away after the agreement was reached and even before it was adopted here: our colleague and friend stéphanie pasqueti, whose work, like the work of many people who worked on this dossier, will be extended as long as we succeed in resettling one more refugee family, doubling or tripling the number of refugees resettled in the world. thank you very much and i thank everyone who has collaborated on this dossier.
mr president, i congratulate the rapporteur, mr rui tavares, on his excellent work and on finally reaching an agreement. it was a process that took too long because of an inexplicable deadlock at council level. an agreement which, in my delegation, has already been applauded by mr carlos coelho, is inexplicable, especially for the thousands of refugees who are living through a humanitarian tragedy, waiting in camps, in the most chaotic of cases in subhuman conditions and at risk of becoming the food for human trafficking networks. the urgency of the situation is revealed in the figures: during the year 2011, there was an increase of 15% compared to the previous year. the european union, with its 27 member states, has received almost 280 000 asylum applications. the european refugee fund should make it possible to finance actions of interest to the european union as a whole, but also actions of a transnational or purely national dimension, in the light of the establishment of a joint european union resettlement programme. the reception and protection systems of several member states have been severely tested by the unexpected arrival of large numbers of persons in need of international protection, in particular from countries such as afghanistan, libya, syria, tunisia and côte d'ivoire. it is therefore essential that this community financial support can be used by member states to improve their reception systems and to encourage resettlement.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, thank you for this debate. i agree with all of you who said that we hope more member states will engage in the programme once it is in place. we are definitely willing on the commission side to try to organise, facilitate and also fund this. as we all know, there are many people in the world who are desperate to run away from suffering, and from oppression and violence, many who have no other hope than to be resettled in europe. these are the most vulnerable people in the world. while we are, of course, aware that we have an economic crisis in the european union, we also have a long tradition of solidarity; that is part of one of the most important values of the european union. sometimes when i look and listen to the debate in the european union, in different member states today, solidarity does not seem to be very fashionable. but this is a chance to show solidarity not only in theory but also in practice. it is a chance to give people a life, hope for the future, and i would like to thank parliament for making this possible.
the rapporteur. - thank you, mr president, and thank you to all the members and commissioner malmström for their speeches. i would now like to say a few words about the future of the refugee resettlement programme in the european union. i am very pleased to see that the next financial perspective for the european union, as proposed by the commission, has adopted a good many of the ideas we have been discussing in recent years. the modulation between member states in order to attract more member states to resettle, the creation also of a resettlement unit located in the european asylum support office and the inclusion of some intelligence and sensitivity, i would say, in resettlement policies which cannot be based on a budgetary fund alone. and of course i fully support the commission in using article 80 on solidarity as a legal basis. we cannot accept that some member states in the council do not want to see article 80 cited as the legal basis for such instruments. i have to ask, who is afraid of solidarity in the european union? i now use this remaining minute to ask the citizens to do their part too: on the one hand, to persuade their member states and tell them that there is now extra money for resettlement, there are new rules, there is help at the european level to do things that individually would be expensive but that done together are much cheaper, that resettle more refugees. secondly, i would ask you to support the ngos and the unhcr that work in this area and i would also ask you to learn more about the way in which legislation is made in the european union and to do something to put an end to this codecision process by which european law is sometimes blocked between parliament and the council. without deadlines, a codecision is not a codecision, it is just an excuse to use a tacit veto. and finally, remember that, like us in our european history who have been refugees so many times, a refugee is a normal person in very difficult circumstances, someone who has already risked his life when he was expelled from his home, we will not let him do it again, even more falling into the hands of human trafficking, and please help us also to do the job of soon doubling or tripling the number of refugees resettled in the european union.
i would also like to acknowledge the efforts made by the rapporteur to ensure that we have strong controls in this house's budget for next year. the forecast increase of 1.9% is lower than the rate of inflation and that is a positive thing, but the left considers that this 1.9% should be considered as a ceiling and that this ceiling should be kept down until the final approval of the figures. we will make proposals to that end, ensuring in any case that the rights of workers and the right to multilingualism are fully respected. where are our reserves? firstly, we await the report from the presidency on the reduction of travel expenses for members of the european parliament. the sum involved is 12 million euros. secondly, we consider that the freezing of the various forms of indirect pay for these same members of the european parliament is not sufficient. another 10 million euros are at stake. thirdly, we disagree with the increase planned for the headings relating to the media. you can do better, with more imagination, but without more money. fourthly, we disagree with the above-inflationary increase foreseen for european foundations and parties. i am at ease because i am the leader of a european party, but there is one thing i do not want to do, and that is to arouse the demons of primary anti-europeanism. and finally, we must discuss the question of the single seat with an open mind, because that means discussing both brussels and strasbourg and at the same time finding alternatives to the one that is being overlooked.

mr president, the social situation of poverty is unacceptable in the european union today. in 2010, some 23.4% of the population, or 115 million people, were at risk of poverty, and even for employed workers the risk of poverty remains. according to eurostat itself, this risk of poverty is closely linked to low-paid, low-skilled, precarious and part-time employment. the so-called budgetary consolidation measures adopted in this house will certainly make this situation worse. it is therefore unacceptable to make any proposal which, in such difficult times, deprives the population and workers of the food aid which guarantees a minimum of dignity of life, which guarantees their right not to live in food poverty. it is clear to us that if the annual funding of at least eur 500 million is not maintained, and it would be desirable if it were increased, the so-called spirit of solidarity of the european union would be further compromised.
i congratulate you on the announcement that the commission has finally succeeded in adopting measures which make it possible to use the budget available to help the most needy people. in this time of widespread economic crisis, and when the european union is making substantial funds available for various cross-border support, it would be incomprehensible for the european citizen not to secure the 500 million euro needed to maintain the programme in 2012 and 2013. i am concerned, however, that this is only a short-term aid, as the continuation of the programme is not assured after 2013. i appeal to my colleagues in the member states who have argued that food bank aid should be provided by each country, to make their governments aware of the need to support the poorest and to promote equity, primarily within the geographical, economic and political space we share and which should be more socially fraternal.
in writing. we will not accept any proposal from the european commission which, in a time of enormous social and economic difficulties, deprives people and workers of the food aid which guarantees a minimum of dignity in their lives, which guarantees their right not to live in food poverty. we support the extension of this programme until 2020 and that the annual funding of at least eur 500 million be maintained and, if desirable, increased. today, in the european union, some 115 million people are at risk of poverty. if the so-called budgetary consolidation measures are already a cause of the worsening of this situation, it would be inhuman and unacceptable for the european union to withdraw this aid from the populations when they need it most.
poverty in the union is overwhelming, with a middle class falling into hidden poverty and at risk of social exclusion. in 2010, some 115 million people in the eu were living below the poverty line, equivalent to 23.4% of the european population. this situation requires member states to impose social support measures for the most vulnerable, in particular children and the elderly. the effects of austerity have led to high unemployment rates, which make it impossible for the quality of life in the countries to improve. public policies need to be created to support food distribution and to end food waste in public restaurants and canteens. on the other hand, in the eu's terms, in addition to the implementation of sectoral policies, in particular cohesion policy, the eu must continue to support the food aid programme which benefits 13 million people through food surpluses. i therefore consider it important that member states do not cut support for this programme in the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
in writing. this report seeks to define and apply what is called european citizenship, as if it made sense to designate the nationals of each country as, first and foremost, individuals of a european nation. it also proposes a number of harmonisations, particularly at the tax and social security levels, and the promotion of the digital single market, which confirms the federalist character of the report. it also advocates unacceptable interference in the internal workings of political parties, arguing that membership of a european political party can be proposed more often when joining a national party, and that citizens' more direct participation should be promoted through european political parties, on the basis that all parties share the same way of functioning and the same ideology. it is a question of establishing a single political and ideological thought. but there are voices that are deeply opposed to this, even though the majority of the ep tries to ignore it.
rapporteur. − madam president, the legal act that we are adopting today deals with questions of life and death for the most vulnerable population in the world: refugees. i should be happy but i am not, because it has taken us two years to reach this compromise. treaties call this a ‘codecision’ procedure, but it is nothing of the sort. without a deadline at first reading it is at best a ‘co-indecision’ procedure and at worst a tacit veto given to council. dear colleagues in parliament, dear colleagues in the council, a simple interinstitutional agreement will do. let us do away with this co-indecision procedure and find a true, fair and efficient way to do law in the european union.
in writing. - according to the contacts made by the rapporteur, the statutes and the rules of procedure of the international rubber study group seem to meet all the requirements. as such, parliament should accept the council's proposal, while at the same time suggesting that it would be important to try to attract all the world's major rubber producers to this group.
in writing. the international rubber study group (irsg) is the only inclusive international platform bringing together both rubber producing and rubber consuming countries. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry was not able to benefit from the measures in force. the fact that some of the world's largest rubber producing and consuming countries are not members of the irsg undermines the authority of this organisation and calls into question its objectives, credibility and representativeness. the united states of america, the third largest consumer, and thailand, the largest producer of rubber, left the gis in mid-2011.
in writing. the irsg is an intergovernmental organisation set up in 1944 in the united kingdom to discuss all aspects of the supply chain between rubber-producing and rubber-consuming countries. the purpose of the irsg is to collect and disseminate comprehensive statistical information on the global rubber industry, which is a key activity to increase transparency in the markets and to better understand and ultimately control the volatility of rubber prices. it is therefore appropriate for parliament to give its consent to the conclusion by the council, on behalf of the european union, of the amended statutes and rules of procedure of the international rubber study group.
in writing. the european council welcomes the commission's proposal to establish a european research area (era) to support the development of the european union's research and technological development activities in the field of biotechnology. the gis is an international organisation established in the united kingdom in 1994 (transferred to singapore in 2008) which aims to establish itself as a platform for debate between the rubber producing countries and the rubber consumers. the effectiveness of this organisation is compromised by the withdrawal of some countries considered to be the largest producers of rubber and the major consumers such as china and the united states of america are also not participating in this platform. in recent times, increased demand, especially from china, and the drop in production due to natural disasters and reduced planting of rubber trees have boosted the price of this raw material. i voted in favour of this recommendation because the eu is the second largest consumer of rubber in the world and despite its shortcomings i believe that the irsg is the only forum where member states, through their representatives, can demand more transparency in this market and ensure fair, predictable and more affordable access.

in writing. - in europe, hundreds of millions of flights are made every year. passengers are often faced with cancellations, denials or long delays of flights for a variety of reasons (strikes, weather, breakdowns, etc.), which cause them enormous disruption and loss. the report under consideration, which was prepared by keith taylor, focuses on the operation and enforcement of the rights acquired by air passengers following the commission's communication on the application of regulation (ec) no 261/2004 laying down rules on compensation and assistance to air passengers. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that all passengers have access to inside information, which is communicated in a simple and accessible way and is available from the moment a passenger decides to book his ticket. in addition, it is essential that there are effective and independent bodies responsible for ensuring full compliance with european standards as regards the right to complain and to resolve disputes and/or to guarantee assistance, reimbursement or compensation. finally, there is the need to guarantee the right of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility to travel in safety and comfort.
in writing. - this report reflects, in general, concerns about the rights of air passengers, which we consider to be justified, but which are designed in the competitive framework of the process of liberalization of this sector, which itself calls into question one of the fundamental rights of these same passengers: the right to public transport and to quality and safety. we value the right of passengers to compensation and reimbursement in the event of lost, delayed or damaged luggage and in the event of flight delays or cancellations. the same applies to the rights of passengers with reduced mobility, pregnant women and children. but on the other hand, we are concerned that the aim is to standardise a set of services in order to create conditions of fair competition, in particular through the official establishment of a european network of national enforcement bodies with a clear mandate for better cooperation in the exchange of information, best practices and also their databases. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the use of the term 'commercial flight' in the present case is justified.
in writing. − this report seeks to take account of the recent commission communication on the application of regulation (ec) no 261/2004 laying down common rules for the compensation and assistance of air passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights and the commission report on the operation and effects of regulation (ec) no 1107/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 5 july 2006 on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility in air transport. in addition, this draft report also seeks to cover the wider context of air passenger rights at european level, as passenger rights are addressed in several eu laws. accountability and transparency are desirable, existing rights should be clarified and strengthened and consumers should be clearly informed.
in writing. − this report seeks to take account of the recent commission communication on the implementation of the regulation laying down common rules for compensation and assistance to air passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights and the commission report on the operation and effects of the regulation on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility in air transport. this report identified the need for increased legal certainty, greater clarity of interpretation and uniform application of the regulations throughout the european union. the incorporation of the european court of justice judgments on the subject in the next review was also identified. i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to increase accountability and transparency, to promote the clarification and strengthening of existing rights and to ensure that consumers are clearly informed of their rights.
in writing. − this own-initiative report is intended to serve as a basis for the revision of regulation 261/2004 on compensation and assistance to air passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or long delay of flights. it also aims to bring about greater legal clarity and interpretation of the legislation, as well as its full application and uniformity in the member states. finally, it gives special attention to the rights of persons with reduced mobility, which include families with children, and of persons with disabilities. price transparency and compensation in the event of the bankruptcy of airlines should be uniform rights in the various member states. the triple choice - refund, rerouting and rebooking in the event of disruption - should be offered to all passengers immediately. in addition, the information should be accessible and a permanent point of contact should be available for possible changes after the reservation. i think it will also be important to consider protective measures against lost and delayed baggage and to allow the consumer to change, free of charge, booking errors or cancel an online reservation within two hours.

in writing. the report, drawn up by bernhard rapkay, deals with the request for the defence of the privileges of the italian mep luigi de magistris. luigi de magistris, elected member of the european parliament (mep) in 2009, was summoned to appear before the court of catanzaro, italy, by maurizio mottola di amato, for having published, in early 2011, on his website, two legal documents that were part of a criminal case when luigi de magistris was a magistrate of the public prosecutor's office. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. lugi de magistris claims that as a member of the european parliament he had an obligation to inform the italian public about what was happening at the cantazaro court and that the documents, which have since been removed from his website, were not confidential. the fact that the facts of the case show that the information published by luigi de magistris has a direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament and taking into account the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, i am voting in favour of the defence of the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. luigi de magistris' request concerns a subpoena against him in the court of catanzaro, on behalf of maurizio mottola di amato, in relation to two articles published by luigi de magistris on his website in early 2011. the articles were published on the website at a time when luigi de magistris was a member of the european parliament following the 2009 european elections. by publishing those articles, luigi de magistris was acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. i am therefore in favour of maintaining the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris.
in writing. - mep luigi de magistris was summoned to appear before the court of catanzaro by maurizio mottola di amato in the context of two articles published by luigi de magistris on his website in early 2011, in which he attached a copy of court documents. luigi de magistris considers it entirely appropriate to inform italian citizens about court documents (which were not covered by any obligation of confidentiality). this was the case after luigi de magistris became a member of the european parliament. it is concluded in the committee on legal affairs that luigi de magistris was acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament and it was therefore decided to uphold the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris. on the basis of the foregoing, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. the report, drawn up by bernhard rapkay, deals with the request for the defence of the privileges of the italian mep luigi de magistris. luigi de magistris, elected member of the european parliament (mep) in 2009, was summoned to appear before the court of milan, italy, by giancarlo pittelli, on the grounds that he had published, in april 2010, a book entitled assalto al pm, storia di un cattivo magistrato, in which, on pages 27, 58-60, 88-90 and 113-114, he questions the legal capacity of giancarlo pittelli to defend a defendant in the shock criminal case. giancarlo pittelli considered the statements extremely defamatory because they labelled him 'as a member of a white collar mafia with inappropriately close relations with personalities in the judicial, business and political spheres'. luigi de magistris claims that he has only expressed his opinion on important issues of public interest and that the book is the expression of the political activity of an mep. considering that the statements contained in the book have no 'direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties' of a member of the european parliament and taking into account the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, i am voting in favour of not defending the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. the request by luigi de magistris concerns a summons against him in the court of milan, in the name of dr giancarlo pittelli, relating to statements made by luigi de magistris in his book entitled assalto al pm, storia di un cattivo magistrato (assault on the public prosecutor's office history of a bad magistrate), published in april 2010. the facts of the case, as set out in the summons and in the written observations submitted by mr de magistris to the committee on legal affairs, show that the statements made have no direct and obvious connection with the performance of the duties of mr de magistris as a member of the european parliament. in publishing that book, luigi de magistris was not acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. so i am in favour of not defending the privileges and immunities of luigi de magistris.

in writing. - i support the proposal to postpone, once again, the deadline for transposing the 2004 directive on the minimum safety and health requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from electromagnetic fields. the first postponement was justified by concerns that the exposure limit values for electromagnetic fields set out in the directive could disproportionately limit the use and development of medical applications of magnetic resonance imaging, which play a key role in the diagnosis and treatment of a range of diseases. following the in-depth analysis carried out, the technical complexity of the matter did not allow an agreement to be reached which ensures a high level of protection of the health and safety of workers without disproportionately restricting the pursuit and development of medical activities. the only possible solution is therefore to postpone the transposition by two more years in order to avoid legal uncertainty and negative legal consequences for member states after april 2012, the deadline for transposition, and thus to allow sufficient time for agreement to be reached in the negotiations.

in writing. − in 2004, the parliament and the council adopted directive 2004/40/ec on occupational health and safety to protect workers from the risks of electromagnetic fields (emf), which was to have been transposed by member states into national law by 30 april 2008. however, there has been a strong campaign by mri equipment manufacturers and radiology associations to exclude the medical sector with mri equipment (mri scanner) from the scope of the directive. it was argued that mri devices could not meet the limit values set out in the directive and that therefore patients would be deprived of the early detection of various diseases, such as cancer. in this context, the commission proposed in 2007 to postpone the deadline for transposition of the directive by four years. now it renews the same proposal, this time postponing the matter until 2014. our group voted against the postponement of the date of transposition to 2012, which is now consistent with the position taken at that time. this is because it is considered that many workers are being deprived of the health and safety protection at work relating to electromagnetic fields to which they are entitled. that right should be guaranteed and enforced.
in writing. − the technical complexity of the issue requires lengthy discussions with national experts, with highly divergent views on some key provisions of the proposal, and it is therefore unlikely that the european parliament and the council will complete the adoption process before 30 april 2012, as originally planned. in these circumstances, a new directive postponing for the second time the date of transposition of directive 2004/40/ec will be necessary. it is appropriate to avoid a very uncertain legal situation that will arise after 30 april 2012, when all member states will have to transpose directive 2004/40/ec if no further measures are taken. i am therefore in favour of the new date of 31 october 2013 for member states to be obliged to transpose directive 2004/40/ec.

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the existence of different taxation for consumer products creates cross-border problems for member states and implies additional work for customs authorities. the ideal, of course, was a european tax union. until that is possible, good administrative cooperation is essential to prevent the evasion of these taxes. i voted in favour of this report and hope that its implementation will help to improve the fight against fraud and tax evasion.
in writing. the commission's proposal aims to modernise the current common framework for administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties between member states. the regulation focuses on the importance and need for administrative cooperation, particularly in the case of crossborder irregularities, and does not aim at harmonising national laws on the management of special movements of consumption or the taxation of consumer goods, both of which are covered by other legal acts. the commission proposal correctly addresses some important aspects, such as the simplification of some bureaucratic procedures, while considering (and rightly so) that the processing of personal data should be the responsibility of each member state. unfortunately, it is the rapporteur who is seeking to distort the approach to respect for national laws, powers and sovereignty in this area. we therefore regret amendment no 1 tabled by the rapporteur, which calls for the creation of a european tax union. we also reject unjustified references to the internal market and its promotion.
in writing. − the creation of a european tax union must include a broad, fast, efficient, user-friendly and, as far as possible, automatic exchange of information between member states in order to improve the fight against tax evasion. administrative cooperation between member states in the field of excise duties is therefore essential. i think this draft resolution is a good step in that direction. give my vote in favour.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 2073/2004 establishes a legal framework for administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties. the introduction of the system for computerizing the movement and control of excise goods requires a revision of the system. the new regulation will provide the legal basis for the introduction of a new system with new statistical features which could reduce the administrative burden on member states' administrations and at the same time improve the quality of statistical reporting. i therefore voted in favour of this report, since it is a regulation aimed at greater efficiency and transparency in the union.
in writing. − article 113 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that the european parliament is to give its opinion on provisions relating to the harmonisation of excise duty legislation as it is essential to ensure the establishment and functioning of the internal market and to avoid distortions of competition. i am voting in favour of this regulation, which aims to improve the exchange of information between member states, to improve the fight against tax evasion and to lay down specific provisions for the collection of statistics. i also believe that it is essential to improve feedback in order to ensure an efficient and continuous improvement in the quality of the information exchanged and to simplify bureaucratic procedures. finally, i believe it is important to set up a forum on vat and excise duties to analyse and discuss progress in the process, and that the commission should report to the european parliament and the council on the application of this regulation.

in writing. - the report under review, by alain lamassoure, deals with the amendment of the rules of procedure in the light of the evolution of the european parliament's (ep) relations with the institutions representing national governments following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which significantly increased the legislative role of the ep. however, by creating new institutions on the government side such as the european council and its president, as well as the high representative and the eurogroup - institutions which have assumed increasing political responsibilities - the political influence of the ep has been diminished, whereas the opposite is desirable. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the rapporteur that, although the council and the ep exercise their legislative and budgetary functions on an equal footing, the question period for the council should be maintained, since the council, in accordance with the second sentence of article 16 (1) of the treaty on european union, has policy-making and coordination powers which it must inform the ep about.
in writing. - the end of the question time to the council (already established in practice), as it was conceived, is the result of the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty. it is now proposed to create a new specific question period on matters which are within its competence and which are not relevant to the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions. the institutional changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon, often praised for the increased powers of the european parliament that they entailed, have in fact resulted in a weakening of national parliaments and in structures of legislative power closer to the citizens, which they can better control. the national parliaments have in fact been relegated to the secondary role of prior monitoring of the principle of subsidiarity in the process of drawing up european standards. in portugal, the assembly of the republic has lost its own decision-making power in key areas, increasing only its role as an advisory body, but without the right to veto community decisions with which it disagrees. only in very hypothetical and exceptional cases (of which there is no record yet), and always in conjunction with other national parliaments, can it create some difficulty for the european commission by delaying the legislative process.
in writing. - following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament became the european union's co-legislator and has the same powers as the council with regard to the ordinary legislative and budgetary procedures. in view of this new reality, there is no reason to keep question time to the council on the agenda of the plenary session in its present form, that is, at each part-session. it is however appropriate to maintain the possibility of organising question periods not only for the president of the commission but also for the vice-president/high representative and the president of the eurogroup. in view of the above, however, we think it is useful to continue to have the possibility of asking the council, during a specific question period, questions on matters which are within its competence but which are not relevant to the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions.
in writing. - the present case concerns the abolition of the question period to the council, as it was conceived until now, by reason of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. after lisbon, the two institutions are on an equal footing as regards legislative and budgetary functions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. in view of these arguments, i have voted in favour of the present procedure.

in writing. − the objective to be achieved with the instrument proposed in this report is clear: to create better conditions for interference in the internal affairs of sovereign countries, to better serve the interests of the eu powers and their economic and financial groups. the similarity of this instrument to the one existing in the united states for the same purposes is, moreover, obvious and very significant. new interferences are looming, new violations of international law and the un charter, to add to so many other violations of instruments that the eu hypocritically claims to respect. with this instrument, they want to overcome the insufficiency of resources, the restricted mandate of the so-called instrument for democracy and human rights (iedhr), its limitations and its lack of flexibility to promote change. what change do you want to promote? what happened in libya, afghanistan, iraq or honduras? what democracy can be promoted by an eu which itself attacks democracy within its own borders, which wants to enshrine in its constitutions the golden rule of neoliberalism, attacking the historical and civilizational rights and achievements of workers and peoples?
in writing. − the idea of a european endowment for democracy emerged from the eu's debate on the analysis of eu policies and actions in promoting democracy, following the events in the southern mediterranean. the aim is to create a semi-autonomous body that can support democracy advocates and democratic developments worldwide in a non-bureaucratic way and that is not directly related to eu diplomacy or the european commission. this idea was put forward in may this year by the eu high representative and vice-president of the commission catherine ashton and commissioner štefan füle in the new proposal for the european neighbourhood policy. it is now up to parliament to contribute constructively to the debate which has proceeded rapidly and to ensure that it will be involved in the establishment, governance structure and monitoring of a possible european fund.
in writing. − in may 2011, following the events in the southern mediterranean, eu high representative and vice-president of the commission catherine ashton and commissioner stefan füle put forward the idea of a european endowment for democracy (edd). the aim is to create a semi-autonomous entity that can support democracy advocates as well as democratic developments around the world. the creation of this new fund is a more appropriate and effective means than a review of existing instruments, in particular the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr). in view of the above, i have voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the creation of a more transparent, stable, reliable and accountable business sector in the eu. it is essential to ensure that the business sector takes account of social, ethical and environmental concerns in its practices and that it takes responsibility both towards employees and shareholders of companies and towards society at large.
in writing. − the proper functioning of the internal market depends to a large extent on good corporate governance rules and, consequently, on the trust placed in companies by european citizens and consumers. it is important to use the current crisis as an opportunity to improve corporate governance and a proportionate and flexible approach to corporate governance should be applied, given the diverse nature of existing national frameworks and of the companies themselves. such rules can never be taxable and compulsory, but they are standards to which companies voluntarily adhere. i would also remind you that, although more uniform and perhaps more stringent rules in this area are desirable, the commission should avoid the temptation to create excessive bureaucratic burdens, taking into account the need for growth and competitiveness of european companies.
in writing. − on 5 april 2011, the commission launched the green paper on the european union framework for corporate governance. this report focuses on the corporate governance framework for european companies. we are aware of the importance of smes in the economic recovery of the eu, particularly in terms of economic growth and job creation. the creation of a more transparent, stable and reliable european business sector is therefore essential. in addition to the important contributions of the green paper, there are other aspects of good governance that need to be addressed urgently, such as the accountability and independence of directors, the constitution and decision-making of boards of directors, as well as conflicts of interest and stakeholder involvement, in particular of minority shareholders. we need companies with an eye to the future and not just thinking about immediate profit for the satisfaction of shareholders, but looking to ensure the stability and financial sustainability of the company. i voted in favour of this report because the eu needs a new legislative framework which, in addition to encouraging women's participation in the corporate bodies, sets out a set of measures to promote good governance.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the proper functioning of the internal market depends to a large extent on good corporate governance rules and, consequently, on the trust placed in companies by european citizens and consumers. in this context, it is important to use the current crisis as an opportunity to improve corporate governance and a proportionate and flexible approach to corporate governance should be applied, given the diverse nature of existing national frameworks and of the companies themselves. such rules can never be imposed and made mandatory, but can be constituted as standards to which companies can voluntarily adhere.
in writing. − on 5 april 2011, the european commission published the green paper on corporate governance which aims to assess the effectiveness of the current european business model and how to improve its governance. i support this report because it aims to encourage a growing relationship between the management bodies of companies and all stakeholders (e.g. shareholders, suppliers, customers), to include independent personalities on the boards of directors, to adopt transparent methods and criteria of merit in the field of human resources in order to value the skills and talents of employees and to safeguard the appropriate reconciliation of work and family life. i agree with the rapporteur that there should be no rules too rigid for corporate governance, but that a number of basic measures should be established in all companies, while always safeguarding their size, complexity and type of business activity. financial audits and external evaluations should be carried out periodically as they are useful tools for assessing the effectiveness of corporate governance practices. i take this opportunity to point out that i disagree with the proposal for quotas for women on company boards, because i believe that they do not need this subterfuge to demonstrate their skills, qualifications and business knowledge.

in writing. the european investment bank (eib), set up by the treaty of rome in 1958, aims to contribute to the development of the single market and to reduce the asymmetries that persist in the territory of the european union (eu). its priority areas of action are therefore territorial cohesion, social and economic convergence, the implementation of the knowledge economy, support for small and medium-sized enterprises, the development of transport networks, environmental protection and the promotion of sustainable energy. the document under review, prepared by iliana ivanova, is based on the 2010 annual report of the eib. i would like to congratulate the eib's management on the results achieved, which allow the bank to maintain its triple a rating, guaranteeing credibility and being a sine qua non for obtaining loans at reduced rates. i also welcome the creation of the european progress microfinance facility. i welcome the support of the eib and the eif to smes and hope that these banking institutions will continue and if possible increase their level of support, given the importance they play in the economic recovery of the eu, in particular in terms of economic growth, innovation and job creation.
in writing. - this report gives great importance to the need to maintain the eib's annual reports. it calls for greater transparency and accountability in relation to the global loan programme. it also supports the eib's efforts to ensure greater support for smes. the 2010 annual report focuses on climate-related project finance in areas such as energy efficiency, renewable energy, transport, forestry, innovation and climate change adaptation. another key point in the report is the call for the eib to be subject to a discharge procedure by the european parliament in the context of the deployment of public funds drawn from the eu budget or the european development fund and managed by the eib. however, we have doubts, reservations and some disagreements about a number of aspects raised throughout the report. this is the case with reference to public-private partnerships, alignment with the eu2020 strategy, the implementation modalities of the so-called project bonds and the increased role of the eib in the balanced and regular development of the internal market.
in writing. - the eib is undoubtedly one of the most important european instruments to support the real economy and should be encouraged to continue to develop its policies successfully at european level. the bank's strong commitment to being the european bank and to playing a key role in reviving the european economy and supporting growth is recognised. it should be noted that in 2010 the eib increased the available finance for climate-related projects to eur 19 billion, compared to eur 16 billion in 2009. this focus of the bank on climate change is very important. it would, however, be relevant for the bank to stop financing certain types of projects which have a catastrophic environmental and social impact. the eib should also do its utmost to fully align the bank's operations with the eu's objectives for a swift transition to a low-carbon economy. the eib should continue to support the europe 2020 strategy by acting as a lever for the structural funds and making greater use of innovative financial instruments. the project obligations set out in the eu 2020 strategy are very important in this context.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which highlights the fact that the european investment bank should continue to support the europe 2020 strategy by leveraging the structural funds and making greater use of innovative financial instruments. this is indeed a key support during the deep economic crisis we are experiencing, which is also a liquidity crisis in the member states, to support these projects.
in writing. the european investment bank (eib) was set up in 1958 by the treaty of rome and its main objective is to contribute to the development of the single market and to reducing regional development disparities. in 2010, it lent €72 billion, of which €8.5 billion went to developing countries. in line with this activity report, the eib, which has provided 32% of its lending for the trans-european transport network, has helped to stimulate the implementation of the 7th framework programme for research and development (fp7), lent over eur 30 billion to enterprises and supported some 115 000 smes by providing credit lines worth eur 10 billion. the lack of capital from the markets has made it difficult for the european union, the member states and companies to invest. in this connection, i believe that the governors of the eib should be asked to give their consent to a significant capital increase, by deepening the bank's activity in the area of productive investments that will enable it to boost rapid economic growth, generate wealth and create jobs.
in writing. - this report refers to the need to maintain the eib's annual reports. the 2010 annual report calls for the eib to make a greater contribution by financing climate-related projects in areas such as energy efficiency, renewable energy, transport, forestry, innovation and climate change adaptation. it also advocates greater support for smes. it is also positive when it calls for the eib to be subject to a discharge procedure by the european parliament on the deployment of public funds taken from the eu budget or the european development fund and managed by the eib. however, we do not follow some of the positions such as the defence of the eib's regulatory control by the ecb, the financing of public-private partnership projects, the eib's support for the europe 2020 strategy, or a greater role for the eib in promoting a balanced and orderly development of the internal market.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this own-initiative report because it gives a precise analysis of the eu citizenship 2010 document on removing obstacles to eu citizens' rights, published by the commission. i would point out that the commission has consulted civil society and has in fact listed the most important obstacles that citizens face in exercising their rights across borders. it is important to keep a close eye on the 25 points that have been highlighted, especially as the commission is already presenting a number of solutions to help individuals, consumers, residents, students, tourists, professionals or political actors. like the s&d group, i insist on respect for values, such as those defined in the charter of fundamental rights, criticising for example the mass expulsions on ethnic grounds, such as that of the french gypsies, by the conservative government.
in writing. − in its 2010 report entitled citizenship of the union - overcoming obstacles to eu citizens' exercise, the european commission presented the main obstacles faced by eu citizens in different aspects of life. this report analyses the solutions proposed by the commission, taking into account the petitions received by the committee on petitions. there are still a number of obstacles, including freedom of movement and residence, the exercise of social security rights, the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications, double taxation and the lack of information for citizens on their rights, including the right to petition. this report, which i supported, calls for better coordination between member states in the application of existing legislation and asks the commission to improve the provision of eu information and to ask citizens how they would prefer to be informed. it also supports the preparation of a new report in 2013 and welcomes the commission's proposal to declare 2013 the european year of citizenship.
in writing. − in 2009, the number of european citizens living in a member state other than their own was around 12 million. however, one in five european citizens still encountered several obstacles to the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member state. in addition, citizens face obstacles to the exercise of social security rights and to the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications. on the other hand, many citizens do not have complete and accurate information about their rights, in particular to study, work, retire or live in another member state. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for better coordination between member states in the application of existing legislation and calls on the european commission to improve the provision of information on the european union to its citizens.
in writing. − the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states is the most tangible expression of the benefits associated with citizenship of the union. although in 2009 almost 12 million union citizens were living in a member state other than their own, one in five encountered too many obstacles to the exercise of this right, in particular as regards their right of entry, permanent residence, the rights of their family members, access to social security benefits, recognition of professional qualifications and diplomas, among many others. however, the biggest obstacle to the active exercise of union citizenship is the lack of awareness of the rights of eu citizens. it is essential to make available to citizens who wish to study, work, retire or live in another member state clear, practical and country-specific information on their rights if they wish to remain there. at the same time, there should be better coordination between member states (in taxation, social security, etc.), which should also remove the legal and administrative obstacles that still remain, in order to facilitate the exercise of these rights and eliminate any contradictions that still exist between national and european legislation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that, although citizens' rights are clearly enshrined in the eu's legal instruments, they are not always put into practice. we live in difficult times and many people are disillusioned with the european project. the european institutions must put citizens at the heart of their activities and keep them informed of their rights and the mechanisms at their disposal, including the right to petition, to find rapid solutions to their problems.

in writing. − the right to free movement of persons and goods is one of the main advantages of all citizens of the member states (ms), who benefit from a regulatory framework that protects them. however, not all ms fully apply the legislation to protect citizens. the 2010 report on the performance of citizenship in the union points to the need to remove obstacles to the exercise of the rights of citizens of the european union. one of the most frequent complaints concerns the limitations some feel on their right to mobility, particularly in relation to the bureaucratic and administrative burden they have to deal with, especially when it comes to relatives and people in their relationships. i welcome the proposal to make 2013 the european year of citizens, although i think that the allocation of €1 million is clearly reduced, as are all the measures to simplify the bureaucratic burden, such as the your europe portal and the registration process for motor vehicles already registered in a member state. finally, i would like to call for an information campaign on the eu charter of fundamental rights to be developed, since 85% of european citizens are not familiar with it.

in writing. − the 2010 eu citizenship report is more comprehensive than the previous reports, which essentially consisted of a descriptive summary, as required by article 25 tfeu, of the main developments in eu citizenship over the three-year period. this report identifies 25 obstacles that citizens face in different aspects of their lives (as individuals, consumers, residents, students, tourists, professionals or as political actors) and proposes solutions to overcome them.
in writing. − in its 2010 report entitled 'citizenship of the union - overcoming obstacles to union citizenship', the european commission presented the main obstacles faced by eu citizens in different aspects of their lives. obstacles to freedom of movement and residence, the exercise of social security rights, the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications, double taxation and the lack of information to citizens about their rights, including the right to petition, were identified. this report calls for better coordination between member states in the application of existing legislation and asks the commission to improve the availability of eu information and to ask citizens how they would prefer to be informed. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the full exercise of rights by eu citizens is essential to the realisation of the european project.
in writing. − the aim of this report on european citizenship is to remove obstacles, through legislative and non-legislative proposals, to ensure that european citizens enjoy their rights in the member states as workers, students, tourists and, above all, as european citizens with political rights. this initiative, with 25 measures, is the result of a compilation of petitions by european citizens who, among other things, highlight the violation of the directive on freedom of movement, the ignorance of their rights, double taxation, the non-implementation of the qualification directive and the lack of information and cooperation of the authorities themselves in relation to social, civil and political rights. since 2013 will be the year of european citizenship, i believe that this report, in addition to pointing out the obstacles felt by citizens, presents measures to ensure the full implementation of the rights of european citizens.
in writing. - this report delves into the federalism of the european union, openly confronting a number of aspects of national legislation with european legislation. it seeks to define and apply what is called european citizenship, as if it made sense to designate the nationals of each country as, first and foremost, individuals of a european nation. the report also proposes a number of harmonisations, particularly in the areas of taxation and social security, and the promotion of the digital single market, which confirms the federalist character of the report. it also advocates unacceptable interference in the internal workings of political parties, arguing that membership of a european political party can be proposed more often when joining a national party, and that citizens' more direct participation should be promoted through european political parties, on the basis that all parties share the same way of functioning and the same ideological ideology. it is a question of establishing a single political and ideological thought. we voted against it, of course.

in writing. − i approve this proposal, taking into account the need for regulation (ec) no 883/2004 and regulation (ec) no 987/2009 to be adapted to keep up to date with changes in national legislation and developments in social reality, which influence the coordination of social security systems. in addition, relevant proposals were received from the committee responsible with a view to improving the said coordination system. these proposals, together with other technical adaptations of the text, are incorporated into the present proposal. another positive aspect is that this proposal also updates and amends the references to national legislation in certain annexes to the regulations. although the proposal focuses on crossborder issues in relation to social security for selfemployed workers and commercial aviation, it is an essential step towards not only the coordination of national social security systems, but also a first step towards a single justice for workers across the european union, who currently face serious differences between member states. i think it is important to advocate greater harmonization in this area.
in writing. −it is up to the member states to organise and finance their social security systems. social security coordination thus focuses on crossborder situations where no member state can act alone. to simplify this coordination, eu legislation has been adopted, replacing the various bilateral agreements that existed. however, given the frequency with which member states tend to introduce amendments to their social security legislation, it is natural that references to national legislation in eu legislation coordinating social security systems, in particular regulations 883/2004 and 987/2009, may become outdated, creating legal uncertainty for stakeholders when applying the regulations. i therefore support the present initiative to update these regulations to take account of changes in national legislation and changes in social realities affecting the coordination of social security systems, such as the recent developments in crossborder mobility. i also consider the amendments proposed by the administrative commission to update, clarify and complete the content of certain provisions to be important, as this is the only way to ensure greater transparency and security for the parties concerned and to provide more complete protection for citizens who have opted for mobility.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to ensure adequate coordination of national social security systems at eu level, in order to adapt to the latest developments in crossborder mobility and free movement of workers. the aim is to guarantee the right to unemployment protection for selfemployed crossborder workers and the rights of aircrew, who should be entitled to the benefits due at the headquarters or branch of their respective airlines. these seem to me to be appropriate and proportionate measures, especially at the present time of crisis in europe, which has led hundreds of thousands of europeans into unemployment and further difficulties.
in writing. - the enlargement of the european union, particularly to the east, has contributed to greater movement of people and goods, thus consolidating the construction of a genuine european single market. the movement of people, especially workers, has raised some problems with regard to the recognition of their social security rights. it is therefore urgent to clarify this situation. the report, drawn up by milan cabrnoch, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 883/2004 on the coordination of social security systems and regulation (ec) no 987/2009 laying down detailed rules for the application of regulation (ec) no 883/2004. i welcome the adoption of this report which recognises one of the eu's basic rights: the right to live and/or work in any member state. all crossborder workers, including those in the air, maritime and selfemployed sectors, are guaranteed their social rights, even if they did not have them in their country of origin. equal treatment in the case of equal work is thus enshrined, irrespective of the member state.
in writing. − this legislative report aims to amend regulations 883/2004 and 987/2009 to incorporate recent changes in some member states in the field of national social security. another objective concerns the consideration of certain provisions of the regulation which have been amended, in particular the transferability of unemployment benefit for self-employed workers and the introduction of a special provision for air transport workers. the report argues that a selfemployed frontier worker who becomes unemployed is entitled to unemployment benefits in the competent member state if they do not exist in the member state of residence. this is an important and sensible measure. it is important, however, not to ignore the problem of the fake selfemployed, who in fact keep subordinate employment relationships in a hood. in some member states, this problem is of considerable proportions. air transport workers are covered by the social security scheme of the area in which they are employed.' we believe that it is essential to have a check on the registration of the registered office so that companies are not established in countries where social security costs are lower.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to ensure the necessary coordination at european level of the various social security systems. this is an update of the existing rules, in particular regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 which take into account legal developments at member state level and cross-border mobility.
in writing. - this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council promotes the updating of the regulation on the coordination of social security systems. the last amendment to these regulations, which entered into force on 1 may 2010, ensured the coordination of social security systems in all member states. the references made in those regulations to national legislation over time and the changes introduced by member states in their national social security systems have resulted in the outdated nature of this legal instrument and the potential legal uncertainty for stakeholders as regards the application of the regulations. the aim of this amendment is to reflect these changes in legislation at national level and changes in social reality. i voted in favour of this report, as the changes will facilitate the effective application of european union legislation on the coordination of social security schemes and improve the protection of people moving within the union.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to update regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 in order to ensure adequate coordination of national social security systems at eu level. the proposal reflects changes in national legislation and takes into account the latest developments in cross-border mobility. the aim is to improve and modernise eu law in the light of the constantly changing social reality. the main purpose is, first, to ensure that an unemployed frontier worker receives benefits if he has completed periods of insurance as a selfemployed person recognised for the purpose of granting unemployment benefits in the competent member state and there is no unemployment benefit scheme in the member state of residence covering such workers and, second, to protect the rights of airline crew. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − this report is purely technical and aims to update european legislation in terms of ensuring appropriate coordination between the social security systems of the member states. in accordance with article 153 tfeu, the eu should support the member states in the field of social security in order to achieve a harmonisation of social systems that safeguards the protection of european citizens. this amendment concerns specifically the selfemployed crossborder workers and civil aviation workers as regards the basic rule of secondment. the aim is to ensure that selfemployed persons in crossborder regions are covered by the country in which they last worked, even if they no longer live there. they will thus be entitled to unemployment benefit if the member state in which they reside does not provide for it. i think it is important that this legislation should be revised in two years' time to take account of the changes that member states are making. we must ensure that european citizens are guaranteed their rights, regardless of their nationality.
in writing. − the primary objective of this report is to amend regulations 883/2004 and 987/2009 to incorporate recent changes in some member states in the field of national social security. a second objective relates to certain provisions of the regulation which have been amended, in particular the transferability of unemployment benefit for self-employed workers and the introduction of a special provision for air transport workers specifying that their base of assignment should be considered as the registered office of their employers or the place of work, in order to identify the member state where they should pay social security contributions. the report argues that a selfemployed frontier worker who becomes unemployed is entitled to unemployment benefits in the competent member state if they do not exist in the member state of residence. this measure may be important if it is not applied to fake selfemployed workers, in order to legitimize their use. with the second amendment, workers are enrolled in the social security system of their base of employment. we think, however, that there should be a check on the registration of the registered office so that companies are not established in countries where the costs of social security are lower.

in writing. the treaty to which this report refers - the treaty of friendship and cooperation in south east asia (tac), which came into force after the original members of asean signed it in 1976, sets out principles that we hold dear, such as mutual respect for independence, sovereignty, equality, territorial integrity and national identity and the right of every nation to its own government free from outside interference, subversion or coercion. however, the signatory countries of the treaty created a free trade area in 1992 (completed in 2008). the population of asean countries is 600 million people. asean together generates a gdp of about usd 1.5 trillion and is the third largest trading partner outside the eu, with over eur 206 billion in trade in goods and services. if we support the signing of this treaty, for the principles enshrined in it, the truth is that we have no illusions about the reasons why the eu is signing it. this is a political and diplomatic manoeuvre aimed at creating better conditions for its objective of establishing a free trade area between the eu and asean.

in writing. − the european council of 19 june 2009 noted the various concerns of the irish people, including those related to fiscal policy, the right to life, education and the family, and the traditional policy of military neutrality. in this context, and in order to restore confidence and give assurances to the irish people, the european council adopted three annexes to the treaty, annex 1 being a legally binding decision of the heads of state or government, which should take effect from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. it was also agreed that, when a subsequent accession treaty was concluded, the provisions of the decision would be laid down in a protocol to be annexed to the treaties. following the signature of the treaty of accession of croatia on 9 december 2001, it became necessary to add the protocol. given that the substance of the proposals contained in the draft protocol has already been discussed and reached political agreement within the european council in 2009, i see no reason why a convention should be convened to add this protocol to the teu and the tfeu. i therefore support the recommendation to approve the european council's proposal not to convene a convention.
