in writing. − in the light of the irish referendum result, the european council in 2009 considered it necessary to create three annexes to the lisbon treaty. thus, on 19 june 2009, the european council considered the concerns of the irish people, including those related to tax policy, the right to life, education and family, and the traditional policy of military neutrality. in this context, and in order to restore the confidence of the irish people in the treaty of lisbon, the european council adopted three annexes to the treaty, annex 1 being a legally binding decision of the heads of state or government, which was to take effect upon the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. considering that the proposals contained in the draft protocol have already been widely discussed and deserved political agreement at the european council in 2009, i do not see the need to convene a convention to proceed with the addition of this protocol to the teu and the tfeu. i therefore agree with the european council's recommendation not to convene a convention.
in writing. − on 19 june 2009, the heads of state or government of the 27 member states of the european union, meeting within the european council, adopted a decision on the concerns of the irish people on the lisbon treaty, as regards the right to family life, education, taxation and security and defence. the inclusion of a protocol on the concerns of the irish people on the treaty of lisbon requires a review of the treaties. however, the heads of state or government also stated that this would only happen when the next accession treaty was concluded. in accordance with that decision, on 20 july 2011 the irish government submitted to the council a draft revision of the treaties with regard to the inclusion of a protocol on the concerns of the irish people on the treaty of lisbon. the analysis of the content of the said protocol shows that none of the concerns expressed in the protocol conflict with the text of the treaty of lisbon and that they concern ireland only. i therefore voted in favour of the european council's decision to examine this proposed amendment to the treaties.
in writing. - i am very pleased to see this report on the concerns of the irish people regarding the lisbon treaty adopted by a large majority. the irish protocol is a document which sets out the concerns expressed by ireland on issues relating to the right to life, the family, education, taxation and also security and defence policy. however, this protocol is a mere clarification of the treaty of lisbon and concerns only the irish situation, having been previously negotiated at the european council of 19 june 2009 in order to provide the necessary legal guarantees to respond to the concerns expressed by the irish people following the 'no' vote in the 2008 referendum. i therefore felt that parliament should support a decision by the european council to consider this amendment to the treaties.
in writing. − since the negative outcome of the ratification process of the lisbon treaty in ireland called into question the unanimity rule required for the entry into force of the new treaty, a protocol was added to the treaty on european union and the tfeu. i support this report because i believe that the content of the protocol does not affect the union's competences and the values of solidarity which the member states are committed to.
in writing. - what is certain is that the rejection of the treaty of lisbon by the irish people has been an obstacle to the attempt to impose a proposal for a treaty which was previously rejected, disregarding and seeking to override the will of the french and dutch peoples, who rejected this treaty in referendums. the adoption of this report will now be aimed at the undemocratic imposition of the treaty of lisbon. the so-called additional protocol to respond to the concerns of the irish people is an attempt to legitimize a process that is full of undemocratic coups. in contrast to this whole process, we defend as inalienable national sovereignty and the role of national institutions in promoting a genuine democracy.
in writing. − the process of ratification of the lisbon treaty by the irish government was a delicate one, with a referendum in june 2008 leading to the treaty, and a further referendum approving an amendment to the constitution which finally allowed ratification. furthermore, the heads of state and government, at the european council of 19 june 2009, agreed to provide ireland with the necessary legal guarantees as regards the protection of the right to life, family and education, as well as taxation, security and defence. this agreement with ireland thus entails the conclusion of a protocol stipulating that nothing in the treaty of lisbon affects the scope and applicability of the protection of the right to life, the protection of the family and the protection of the rights to education provided for in the constitution of ireland, as well as the provisions on taxation and the independence of the security and defence policy of the irish state.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the rangel reports on the protocol on ireland, not only because it merely incorporates into the constitutional law of the union the political commitment made by the other member states to the irish government before the referendum on the treaty of lisbon, but also because the report is explicit in the sense that the protocol has no effect except on the rights and obligations of ireland within the union. it is thus emphasized that the protocol, while it may involve a specific derogation from the treaties in respect of ireland, does not imply any restrictive interpretation of the treaties (in particular in the field of security and defence policy) as is apparent from the explanatory memorandum in the draft protocol. no other member state can therefore take advantage of the special treatment which the protocol accords to ireland as if it were a mere interpretation of the treaties. with effect restricted to ireland, the protocol leaves the interpretation and application of the treaties fully open to the other member states.
in writing. - i support this proposal, considering it essential and a priority to take account of the specificities of the outermost regions of europe in the design of future cohesion policy, as these regions are subject to permanent constraints mainly due to their isolation and distance, which justifies the adoption of measures by the european union. we must remember that the special situation of these regions and the need to adapt european policies to their particularities are enshrined in article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, since when this does not happen, their distance from the economic and social cohesion advocated by the eu is exacerbated. the eu 2020 strategy is an opportunity to pay attention to the ors in their priority areas and to use the added value they have to offer.
in writing. - the specific legal status of the outermost regions laid down in the treaty clearly demonstrates the need for differential treatment of these regions, in order to take account of their physical characteristics and structural peculiarities. the consequences of the economic, social and financial crisis have had an impact on all regions of the eu, but with a particular impact on the ors, further accentuating the structural gaps in their economies and their dependence on the outside world. european investment in these regions is not just a policy of recovery of delays and compensation. they also seek to create the added value needed to meet the challenges of sustainable development and increased competitiveness, in particular, of this region and of europe in general. i therefore support the excellent report by mr nuno teixeira, who wants to make an active contribution to finding a more balanced response from european action to the challenges facing the outermost regions in the context of the eu 2020 strategy objectives. this requires particular attention to the definition and implementation of cohesion policy and the establishment of a renewed strategy for the eu's outermost regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the role of cohesion policy in the outermost regions of the european union in the context of europe 2020, because i believe that the specificities of the outermost regions must be taken into account in the definition of the future cohesion policy, so that these regions can respond to the challenges they face and achieve the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. the outermost regions suffer from geographical isolation and have to make extra efforts to keep pace with the development of the mainland. strategy 2020 is therefore an opportunity to bridge the gap and work on differentiated policies that are appropriate to the characteristics of the ors, in particular at the level of cohesion policy. finally, i would like to congratulate my colleague who has been working so hard on this mandate and with fruitful results on this matter of the outermost regions.
in writing. − article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) (the council, on a proposal from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt specific measures designed in particular to lay down the conditions for the application of the treaties to these regions, including common policies) provides for the application of a special status to the so-called outermost regions (orr), which, by reason of their geographical situation (remoteness, difficult topography and climate or insularity), constitute a specific group. the report analyses the role of eu cohesion policy towards the ors in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, i.e. how these regions can achieve the defined objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the priorities mentioned by the rapporteur: positive discrimination against these regions and development strategies aimed at greater competitiveness, growth and employment; special attention to specific areas such as fisheries, agriculture, renewable energy, information technologies, tourism, etc.; the promotion of these regions in the context of the european neighbourhood policy, by strengthening their relations with third countries through more effective governance and better integration into the eu.
in writing. − the outermost regions of the european union are a group of regions which, by reason of their particular characteristics linked to their physical and structural constraints, resulting from their remoteness and insularity, difficult terrain and climate, form a specific group of regions, recognised by article 349 tfeu. it is therefore necessary and appropriate to examine, with regard to the future cohesion policy in the ors, how the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as set out in the eu 2020 strategy, can be achieved in these european regions, which have particularities and permanent constraints resulting mainly from their remoteness and which justify the adoption of specific measures by the european union. i am voting in favour of this report because it is important for the development of the outermost regions of my country, in particular the autonomous regions of the azores and madeira.
in writing. - this report, initiated by my fellow madeiran mep nuno teixeira, whom i congratulate on the excellent work he has done, is of the utmost importance in that: (1) it constitutes the first specific statement of this parliament's legislature on the outermost regions/uprs, (2) it is designed to influence the communication that the european commission is to present next may on the outermost regions, as a commitment of this college of commissioners to these regions. i therefore put a lot of effort into the final drafting of this report, working closely with the rapporteur and also with the psd/azores to introduce responses tailored to the specific needs of the azores, in particular with regard to a future posei transportes and also to the extension of the protection zone for access to azorean waters. these two aspects were safeguarded, although it had called for a more forceful expression in the case of posei transportes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally sensitive areas. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the eu's outermost regions (ors) are a group of regions which, because of their particular characteristics, linked to their physical and structural constraints resulting from their remoteness and insularity, difficult terrain and climate, have a special status in the treaty. in calling for a territorial approach, this report aims to examine, with regard to future cohesion policy in the octs, how the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as enshrined in the eu 2020 strategy, can be achieved in these european regions. the priorities to be taken into account in this context are: the need for differentiated and comprehensive treatment of the octs in the eu, taking into account their specificities and taking advantage of their potential; the adaptation of the implementation of european policies in the octs in several strategic areas; and better integration of the octs into the eu, which implies more effective governance, territorial continuity to improve access to the benefits of the single market and the development of their integration in the context of regional neighbourhood plans. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with this approach.
in writing. − the outermost regions are a group of regions of the european union which, because of their insularity, remoteness, small size and high dependence on a large number of products, have been granted a special status which allows for differentiated treatment with regard to the european union's actions and policies in these regions, as provided for in article 349 of the tfeu. this report, which i have written, is intended to present the european parliament's proposals for a future renewed strategy for the outermost regions, taking into account the important role of cohesion policy in the outermost regions and its contribution to the achievement of the eu-2020 objectives. these measures reveal the main needs of these regions, which the european parliament has today recognised as deserving of special treatment.
in writing. − the main problem of this report is a fundamental one - the framework for defending the specificity of the ors based on compliance with the guidelines for the eu2020 strategy or the internal market, a strategy which we consider harmful to the development of the ors, exacerbating many of the constraints on these regions. however, we cannot fail to note some positive considerations, in particular the clear advocacy of differentiated treatment for the outermost regions (ors) in accordance with their specificities and permanent natural constraints, the criticism of the commission's proposal to reduce the cohesion fund and the erdf, the advocacy of an 85% co-financing rate for all support instruments, and the advocacy of a framework for state aid that is neither time-limited nor degressive. we also agree that the criterion of gdp per head should be complemented by other indicators of human and social development.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering it necessary to reinforce the idea that the european union cannot have different or duplicated criteria between human rights and other external policies, between its internal and external policies, and in the conduct of its relations with third countries. the same principles should underlie all political action. i also advocate the need for a more systematic approach, which should include individual efforts by each country and a human rights strategy that includes clear deadlines, actions and responsibilities that can be implemented. i also regret that some of the s&d group's proposals were rejected at first reading, particularly as regards the reference to minorities and gender equality.
in writing. − eu policies must not only be consistent and exemplary within the eu, but also be coherent and in line with the eu's fundamental values and principles, in order to enhance the eu's credibility in the world and the effectiveness of the implementation of its fundamental rights policies. over the past decade, profound changes have taken place, from 9/11 to the arab spring, raising new challenges that highlight the vital importance of human rights and democracy. it is essential to redefine and strengthen the eu strategy and the instruments used in order to be able to respond more effectively and comprehensively to the challenges currently facing human rights and democracy worldwide. i call for rapid, transparent and inclusive progress towards an ambitious common strategy for the eu with clear actions, timetables and responsibilities, and for it to be created with the full contribution of all stakeholders. i also hope that the ep can be given a greater role in promoting transparency and accountability in the implementation of the eu human rights strategy, as this annual report is not in itself an accountability mechanism.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to be more active in the fight against terrorism and to promote the fight against organised crime. it should therefore avoid double standards in human rights and relations with third countries. it also calls for speed and transparency in the development of a common human rights strategy within the eu.
in writing. − this resolution is parliament's response to the annual report on human rights in the world and the union's policy on the matter published by the european external action service, which contains a broad overview of how the european union deals with and engages in these particularly sensitive issues, as well as an assessment of the activities of the main european institutions and actors in this regard. this evaluation could be very useful not only as a means of assessing best practice and defining the best criteria for solving the problems raised by the union's strategic approach to human rights, but also as a means of pointing out ways and solutions. and to reaffirm the centrality of human rights to the european union. the european union has been increasingly committed to putting democracy and human rights on the world agenda. it is right for you to evaluate whether you are handling the problems presented to you well and not neglecting others. a union which is willing to show itself capable of questioning itself and seeking to improve its responses could emerge from this exercise strengthened.
in writing. − one of the flags of the european union (eu) which has won the recognition of many countries and states is the uncompromising defence of human rights. since 1983 the european parliament has been examining a report on human rights in the world. the report under consideration, by mr howitt, analyses the annual report on human rights in the world and the eu's policy in this field. never have human rights been so important and led to so many changes as the arab spring, where men and women, young and old, were willing to give their lives in defense of human rights. however, much remains to be done, particularly within the un, to bring an end to certain human rights violations, such as the death penalty. we must also prevent the freedom achieved by muslim-majority countries from turning into persecution and massacre of minority communities such as christians. at a time when we are faced with news of the nationalization by the argentine government, with which the eu has cooperation agreements, of the capital of a spanish company, it is essential to review the eu's strategic policy in this area.
in writing. - the report contains some positive points - for example, on guantanamo or the recognition of eu complicity in certain regimes (not by chance, already disgraced in the eyes of their people) - which do not erase its overall very negative sense. once again, we are faced with an unacceptable exploitation of human rights, seen as a political weapon, used in the interests of the eu's great powers and their economic and financial groups. in the wake of the previous annual reports, there is no mention of the flagrant violations of human rights in palestine, iraq, afghanistan, occupied cyprus or western sahara. violations with the open complicity of eu countries and/or their allies, such as the usa, israel, turkey or morocco. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. the new and strengthened instruments of open interference in the internal life of sovereign states, contrary to the letter and spirit of the un charter, are being defended, along the lines of similar mechanisms long used by the usa. the european union is a country of the european union, and it is a country of the european union.
in writing. - credibility in the field of external relations is essential. to do this, the european union (eu) must act consistently, in accordance with the treaty and the obligations of the acquis communautaire. the eu should thus avoid inconsistencies in human rights and other external policies, between internal and external policies and in the conduct of its relations with third countries. appropriate measures should be taken to ensure that individual rights and fundamental freedoms are not affected or restricted in times of economic crisis. the union's policies must not only be consistent and exemplary within the european union, but also be consistent and in line with the fundamental values and principles in order to enhance the credibility of the european union in the world and the effectiveness of the implementation of its human rights policies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the howitt report on eu human rights policy, which honours the european parliament for its ambition and clarity. i do not agree with one particular point, however: the proposal to include a human rights chapter in all international trade treaties, which seems to me to be unreasonable and excessive. the defence and promotion of human rights is not a specific objective of the union's external trade policy. it must certainly be consistent with the other dimensions of foreign and domestic policy, starting with human rights policy. we cannot therefore conclude a trade agreement with a country which is characterized by systematic violations of human rights, such as china or belarus. but we cannot make international trade conditional on the union's high human rights standards. what we can and must demand is that trade agreements have a positive, not a negative, balance. i fully support the proposal to strengthen the chapter on labour and environmental standards, which is already part of the union's external trade treaties. the aim here is to defend the union's own economic and commercial interests by combating social and environmental dumping in trade relations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with its approach, particularly as regards the european union's duty to ensure that its actions in the field of development policy promote and strengthen peacebuilding, conflict prevention and international security.
in writing. − this report is in response to the eu annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2010, published by the european external action service, and provides an overview of eu policy on the subject. the main points covered by this report are: eu action in the context of the united nations and the international criminal court (icc); eu policies to support democratisation; human rights dialogues; consultations with third countries; and other issues such as the death penalty, arms control and torture. the fact that a more effective approach is envisaged, in which development cooperation plays a key role, and that human rights issues are intended to be extended to all eu policies is to be welcomed. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − human rights are indivisible values enshrined in the eu's founding treaties. the eu's policy, both external and internal, should therefore take account of the persecution of these people and should be applied uniformly, showing the eu's role as an example in safeguarding human rights. of course, the flaws still remain. however, it is through them that the eu and the member states must work towards the reformulation of their policies and strategies. this report covers a number of key issues, including the eu's policy action at the un, the icc, policies to support democratisation and their financial support instruments. what i would like to stress is the need to include this topic across the various eu policies. we also see shortcomings in the eu's approach to foreign policy. finally, i consider it extremely important that we continue to support democratisation and development. more technical, financial and political support is needed for the various programmes under implementation. we cannot provide the support due to third countries if the means are scarce. this is a subject of unparalleled importance, which allows the development and improvement of the quality of life of citizens, where transparency of criteria should be an element present in the annual reports.
in writing. − this paper focuses on the 2010 annual report on human rights in the world. the document's focus is on deepening the eu's policies of interference, on instrumentalising the idea of human rights in favour of eu interests, on silencing crimes against human rights (which we understand to be also social, cultural and economic) by the us and eu allies, and on advocating the strengthening of mechanisms that allow the eu to rapidly deepen its interference. in the wake of the previous annual reports, there is a complete absence of reference and denunciation of the flagrant violations of human rights in palestine, iraq, afghanistan, occupied cyprus or western sahara, perpetrated by eu countries and/or their allies, such as the usa, israel, turkey or morocco. on libya, they only regret not intervening earlier and they praise the arab spring. the position of interference in the internal affairs of countries is blatantly shown when it is stated that the transition to democracy needs to be promoted through various forms of support, including financial support, in order to support the capacity of civil society to make democratic opposition (...) in a mutually secure and, if necessary, confidential manner. we have, of course, voted against this hypocritical use of the concept of human rights.

in writing. − the european union and azerbaijan are currently negotiating an association agreement to succeed the partnership and cooperation agreement currently binding them. this new agreement will aim to deepen and strengthen the union's political and economic relations with azerbaijan. the energy chapter remains unaddressed and thorny issues such as nagorno-karabakh and the human rights situation remain. i hope that this rapprochement between the union and azerbaijan, which is crucial in the framework of the eastern partnership, will be achieved and that azerbaijan will be able to see in the european ally an example of consistency and a model of voluntary submission to western values and that it will be able to commit itself to converging with them.

in writing. − this report concerns the eu-azerbaijan association agreement in the framework of the eu's eastern partnership. the eu's eastern partnership is the political framework that strengthens bilateral relations through association agreements, taking into account the specific situation, mutual benefits and the eu's strategic interest in the stability and democratic development of the region. azerbaijan has played an important role in the eastern partnership and in addressing the eu's energy security challenges, due to its remarkable economic growth. the eu and azerbaijan have signed a new agreement on the settlement of the disputes between the two countries. we cannot, however, fail to appeal to the azerbaijani authorities to ensure greater respect for both the rule of law and the freedom of expression of political opponents, so that we can say that we are indeed facing a genuine democratic process in progress.

in writing. − armenia is a nation with a long history, tradition and culture having been the first country in the world to adopt christianity as its religion. it is a people which suffered for a long time under ottoman and soviet rule, and which is now taking steps towards the institutionalisation of a democracy and a western-style rule of law. the association agreement will help bring armenia closer to the european model and bring it closer to the union. it is up to the armenian leadership and the armenian people to persevere on this path and the european union to support this effort, which we hope will be concrete and fruitful. the next presidential elections will be an important test of the strength of armenia's european option and its adherence to the values of freedom, democracy, human rights and the rule of law. as in the case of azerbaijan, there are still thorny issues such as nagorno-karabakh, in which both states are involved and which will not be resolved definitively without the commitment of both sides.
in writing. - one of the european union's (eu) concerns has always been its neighbourhood policy. since its foundation, the eu has made peace and political and social stability strategic priorities, and has therefore sought to establish cooperation agreements with peripheral countries. this report, drawn up by tomasz piotr poręba, contains the european parliament's (ep) recommendations to the council, the commission and the european external action service (eeas) on the negotiations for the eu-armenia cooperation agreement. armenia has shown a certain openness and interest in its approximation to eu values throughout the negotiation process. however, much remains to be done, particularly in the fight against corruption and organised crime, the violation of human rights and the armed conflict in the nagorno-karabakh region where it has its troops. it is essential that the two countries, armenia and azerbaijan, adopt the minsk group initiatives as a matter of urgency. i voted in favour of this report and i urge the armenian authorities to continue with the reforms, particularly in the areas of human rights and freedom of expression, by holding free and fair elections as early as next may.

madam president, mr president-in-office of the council, commissioner, i have no doubt that the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the united states on pnr data is the best solution, as opposed to the conclusion of bilateral agreements, to ensure a coherent approach and a higher degree of legal certainty and protection for our citizens. i appreciate the effort made by commissioner malmström in these negotiations with the united states, but the final result is far from what i think we can and should approve. i shall therefore abstain, for the following reasons in particular: firstly, there is no protection for european citizens. some claim that rights related to access, rectification and deletion of data or the possibility of judicial or administrative redress have been improved. as article 21 of the agreement itself states, these rights could only be conferred to the extent that they are already enshrined in american law, this agreement could only confer new rights if there was an involvement of the american congress, which is not the case. secondly, the use of the pull system. the agreement with australia clearly provided for the push system, unlike the present agreement which still allows for pull extraction. i fully agree that the united states, as a sovereign state, has the right to request information on people who want to enter its territory, but i do not agree with the possibility of entering the airline databases to extract the data it needs, it is one thing for us to sign an agreement in which we commit ourselves to providing data, it is quite another to allow the use of our computers and databases by security forces of third countries. thirdly, the use of sensitive data, the 2004 agreement prohibited its use, while this agreement allows its processing. fourthly, data retention, whereas on the one hand there is an improvement in the anonymisation of data, on the other hand there is an extension of the retention for an indefinite period. madam president, a final word to thank the rapporteur, mrs veld, and my group's shadow rapporteur, mr voss, for their work.
the pnr agreement which the commission has negotiated with the united states has serious problems. we are particularly concerned that european citizens do not have the right to judicial review in the united states, that is, they do not have the means of appeal available to americans. however bad it is, this agreement is far better than the 2007 agreement that applies today and it is far better than the agreements that have been negotiated by european governments bilaterally with the united states. in the case of my country, portugal, such an agreement was subserviently ratified by the national parliament against the serious warnings of the national data protection authority. if the european parliament does not give its consent to this text, the bilateral agreements are much more burdensome and will enter into force, if the european parliament gives its consent to this agreement, nevertheless, european citizens will be more protected and parliament will be able to monitor the application of the agreement in accordance with the commitment made by the european commission. that is why i am voting in favour of this agreement.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank everyone for this very good debate. i also appreciate the good cooperation i have had with the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, with the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs. let me quickly answer a few questions. firstly, scope. the scope of this is to fight terrorism and serious cross-border crime, which carries a penalty of three years. customs, migration and border controls are not additional purposes. the reference to vital interests applies to life-and-death matters and communicable diseases. this arose in only four cases during the review we did on the current agreement from 2007 to 2010. that is four cases, none of which involved european pnr data. secondly, court orders. in the us constitution and some european constitutions, a court can ask for pnr data to be used to prove whether someone has been on a plane or not, for instance. this only happened once in our evaluation, so these cases are extremely rare and they are all logged. thirdly, ‘push’ and ‘pull’. in this agreement – in contrast to the current one – ‘push’ is the norm. this has been welcomed by the association of european airlines and the international organisation of airlines. a vast majority of carriers already use this method and will be able to comply with the requirement to have ‘push’ capacity within two years. fourthly, redress. it is spelled out in the agreement that anybody can appeal to the court against a decision to refuse access because of his or her data under the freedom of information act. the us privacy act does not give these rights to eu citizens, but the traveler redress inquiry programme is available for all decisions made by the us government that may be subject to judicial review. it is also possible to claim compensation. finally, the content of the data. the data registered are the data you give when you book an airline ticket. you do not say if you are a member of a trade union. you do not say in that booking what you intend to buy at the airport. the data is registered. i do not know how well informed passengers are about this (as was mentioned in the debate with mrs foster and others), but we say in the agreement that the us must inform passengers about this. this is a major improvement. profiling is prohibited by article 7 and article 9. as has been said, the united states has the right to ask for data from an individual who intends to land on its territory, as does any country. they do it today, they have done it in the past, and they will do it in the future, as most of our member states do. we are currently negotiating eu pnr, which i am looking forward to debating with you later. why? because our member states think that this is a valuable and important tool to fight terrorism and – even more importantly – drug smuggling and people smuggling. what we are here to do is to make sure that the transfer of data is used in a proportionate, limited way, with the strongest protection possible when it comes to fundamental rights and integrity. this is our collective duty. you asked the commission to renegotiate the 2007 agreement in force today. we all did that with strong support from the parliament, clear directions in your resolution and with the support of the council as well. it is not perfect. you did not get 100% of what you asked for. however, on all points it is a better agreement than the one we currently have. this is why we are asking for your agreement. we attach great importance to this agreement, as you all do. we will review it, and in the review, mrs sippel, there will be data protection experts present. i undertake – as i did earlier in my declaration – to be fully transparent and to report to you at all stages of these evaluations and reviews.
president of the council. i would like to thank you again for the opportunity to take part in this debate today. it is an important subject which we have discussed here today and the debate has again shown today that it is a matter to which we all attach very great importance. it is not an easy matter, as the debate today has shown, and many of the concerns raised today have been discussed in depth. but i would like to say, as commissioner malmström has said, that the presidency believes that the agreement we have today is better than the one we have. and that is the fundamental question that needs to be answered. the agreement is and will be better than what we have and it will give us better opportunities to strengthen the fight against serious crossborder crime. it is very understandable that some of you still have reservations about the draft agreement. but i hope that both myself and commissioner malmström have been made quite clear that we take the reservations and questions very seriously. at the same time, you should know that many of the issues raised today have also been the subject of discussions in the council. i would also like to conclude by emphasizing that this agreement does not mark the end of the transatlantic dialogue on the use of pnr data. the provisions of the agreement on evaluations will enable us to ensure that the provisions of the agreement on limitation of purpose are respected in practice. i therefore think it is important that we see this agreement as a good step towards a new framework for the use of pnr data - in writing. most people using air transport will be unaware of what the pnr - the passenger name record - is. moreover, you will not know the use that is made of this register today. the pnr may contain various information, such as name, address, passport number, credit card number, or information about other accompanying passengers, travel routes, etc. it is this roll of personal data, relating to any passenger, which is now being sent by airlines to the united states department of homeland security, now and forever, in the name of the so-called fight against terrorism - the pretext for all kinds of stampedes and gross violations of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. all this with the complicity of the european commission. as the rapporteur has pointed out, tens of thousands of passenger records are sent to the us authorities every day, without the passengers' knowledge. that has been the case in recent years. these data may also be sent to third countries. this genuine big brother will now be backed by the european parliament, supported in the committee on civil liberties (irony of ironies) by the usual stooges: the right and the social democrats. that is an unacceptable decision. justifying outrage, reporting, mobilizing and fighting.
human trafficking is the modern form of slavery and the second most lucrative activity for organised crime worldwide, affecting millions of people. i look forward to the strategy that the commission will present to us shortly, providing a more comprehensive approach that can deal more effectively with this type of crime and, at the same time, strengthen the aspect of prevention and protection of victims, with special attention to children and other groups at risk. the directive adopted in 2010 represented an important step forward in creating common minimum standards and closing the existing legal gap. it is now up to the member states to transpose it in time - by april 2013. i welcome the creation of an eu anti-trafficking coordinator who should contribute to a more coherent and coordinated anti-trafficking strategy by outlining general strategic guidelines and guidelines to be applied in cooperation with third countries. it is also positive that the commission has set up a working group to combat trafficking and that the council has set up a network of reports and equivalent mechanisms to analyse this phenomenon and collect reliable data.
in writing. - i support it because i believe that a partnership tool can improve forest governance. the partner countries and the european commission will have to coordinate for an effective implementation of this agreement. the establishment of this partnership is another step towards protecting the quality standards required of europeans for products imported from third countries, most of which do not comply with the same legislation as european producers. in this sense, it is an agreement which may lead to the establishment of other agreements with third countries, which should cover different economic sectors of activity.
in writing. − the exploitation and trade of illegal timber undermines the competitiveness of legitimate forest industries in both exporting and importing countries, limiting the ability of these industries to carry out operations that promote sustainable forest management as well as sustainable development, with the central african republic (car) being one such example. the voluntary partnership agreement which is voted on today and which i support is of great importance in that it provides a tool to tackle this problem, improves regulation, governance and enforcement in the forestry sector, and commits the car to implementing systems for verifying legal compliance and traceability throughout the supply chain from slaughter to the issuance of flegt export licences. while sustainable forest development wins, the eu also strengthens new market opportunities for car's wood products. 60% of the timber is exported to europe in a sector that represents 4% of the rca's gdp. i would stress that in implementing this agreement, efforts must nevertheless be made to promote fair solutions which do not have an impact on the most deprived sectors of society, such as the rural populations who make a living from this activity, leaving the most powerful unharmed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that voluntary partnership agreements are the basis of an eu action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt), as they establish partnerships with timber producers and exports between countries with the intention of stopping illegal logging. i consider vpas to be a partnership instrument that promotes better forest governance.
in writing. the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the central african republic (car) is imperative for the importation or non-importation of precious timber from that african country. the car has over 30% of its territory covered by tropical forests. it is not surprising, then, that timber exports account for about 40 percent of that country's exports. the partnership agreement comes at a good time to discourage illegal timber trade, as well as the unjustified destruction and irreparable loss of forests that are devastated by informal and illegal producers and traders. the agreement will also provide a guarantee to eu countries that they are buying timber harvested in a sustainable and balanced way and that they are not contributing, even unintentionally, to the destruction of tropical forests.
in writing. - climate change, which in recent decades has affected the planet through unexpected natural disasters, has put the problem of large-scale deforestation on the agenda, especially in the amazon region, considered the lungs of the planet, and on the african continent. the text under discussion concerns the draft council decision on the signing of a voluntary partnership agreement (vpa) between the european union (eu) and the central african republic (car) on forest law enforcement, governance and trade in timber and timber products imported into the eu under the flegt (forest law enforcement, governance and trade) action plan. this is an eu initiative to prevent illegally harvested timber from entering europe. the eu-car voluntary partnership agreement, signed on 28 november 2011, needs to be approved by the european parliament in advance in order to enter into force. i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider it essential that there should be legislation to promote the sustainability of the forestry sector and to prevent indiscriminate logging. in addition, this vpa will contribute to the overall and sustainable development of the car.
in writing. − the objectives of the flegt voluntary partnership agreement with the central african republic (car) are to combat the problem of illegal logging and to help improve regulation, governance and enforcement in the car forestry sector. illegal logging contributes to the destruction and degradation of ecosystems of great importance, both from the functional point of view and from the point of view of the natural values they contain. but a correct approach to the causes of this problem requires recognition that it is inextricably linked to the enormous weakness of these countries' economies, as well as to the significant levels of poverty among their populations, this activity sometimes being the sole source of income for many families. the rapporteur herself states that many indigenous communities living in the rainforests of the car depend on the use of forest resources. it follows that the end of illegal or unsustainable logging will only be possible if the dire social and economic situation in countries such as the car is properly addressed and resolved, and if an economic model based on the high dependence on logging and export of a limited number of raw materials to industrialized countries is reversed.
in writing. − in 2003, the eu developed an action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt). it provided for partnerships with timber producing and exporting countries to ensure that only legally harvested timber was traded and to promote sound forest governance. like the flegt voluntary partnership agreements, the agreement with the central african republic provides an instrument to address the problem of illegal logging, to help improve regulation, governance and enforcement in the country's forest sector, and to enhance market opportunities for central african timber products in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the draft council decision on the signing of a voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the central african republic on forestry law enforcement, governance and trade in timber and timber products imported into the european union (flegt). i did so because i believe that this partnership instrument aims to improve standards of management, sustainability and accountability in the forestry sector and because it is expected that the vpa will contribute positively to overall development and growth in the central african republic, including by safeguarding revenues generated by timber exports to the eu and other international markets. the instrument also provides that in future the tax revenues from industrial forestry will increasingly benefit the local economy and communities.
in writing. − the partnership agreement with the central african republic (car), signed on 28 november 2011, comes within the framework of the 2003 eu action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt), which provides for the establishment of partnerships with timber producing and exporting countries to ensure that only legally harvested timber is traded and to promote sound forest governance. this agreement is an instrument to address the problem of illegal logging, to help improve regulation, governance and enforcement in the country's forest sector, and to enhance market opportunities for central african timber products in europe. in addition to being a partnership instrument to improve management standards, sustainability and accountability in the forestry sector, the vpa is expected to contribute positively to overall development and growth in the central african republic, inter alia, by safeguarding revenues generated by timber exports to the eu and other international markets. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − in addition to being a partnership instrument to improve management standards, sustainability and accountability in the forestry sector, the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the central african republic is expected to contribute positively to overall development and growth in the latter, in particular by safeguarding revenues generated by timber exports to the eu and other international markets. it should be noted that although the voluntary partnership agreement provides for measures for better forest governance and has gained wide support, the main challenges now lie in its effective implementation. the eu's technical and financial support for the implementation of the vpa will be crucial to this end.
in writing. − the main purpose of the flegt voluntary partnership agreement with the central african republic (car) is to combat the problem of illegal logging by helping to improve regulation, governance and enforcement in the car forestry sector. but how does one really solve the problem of illegal logging in the forestry sector of these countries? by combating the fragility of these countries' economies, in particular by eradicating poverty, which is one of the causes of the illegal logging of forest resources, the only means of subsistence for many families and communities. to do this, it is imperative to reverse the economic model based on the high dependence on the exploitation and export of a limited number of raw materials to the industrialized countries, which robs these countries of their main wealth.
in writing. - i approve this report. forests require partnerships for better management of their resources. it is important that, like the agreement with the central african republic, the european union should adopt strict criteria for importing products from third countries, so that they meet the same quality standards as those required of europeans. this agreement can serve as a good model for other partnership projects with third countries in various sectors of activity.
in writing. − the exploitation and trade of illegal timber undermines the competitiveness of legitimate forest industries in both exporting and importing countries, limiting the ability of these industries to carry out operations that promote sustainable forest management and sustainable development. in the case of liberia, it is particularly important because for a long time the country was subject to un sanctions on timber imports because of the sector's involvement in financing the civil war. it is noted that approximately 45% of the territory is covered by forests, allowing this voluntary partnership agreement with the eu to allow liberia to simultaneously address the problems associated with illegal logging and trade, improve forest sustainability and expand market opportunities with the union in the timber sector. i also welcome the fact that the partnership agreement with liberia has been a multilateral approach with a high level of involvement of civil society, industry and forest communities, with particular attention to the new legality verification system, independent audits, transparency of the process and exchange of information and the creation of a joint implementation committee to oversee the agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that these voluntary partnership agreements are the basis of an eu action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt). liberia presents a very particular context, as approximately 45% of its territory is covered by forest. the efforts of this country to reform the forestry sector should be recognised and encouraged.
in writing. - given that about 45% of the republic of liberia is covered by forest and that the country is home to half of the remaining tropical forests in west africa, and given that much of these forests were cleared during the 14 years of civil war to finance the war itself, i can only welcome the efforts of the current president of liberia to structure the forestry sector and create a legal framework to allow the sustainable marketing of that country's timber. in this context i welcome the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of liberia on wood products.
in writing. − some 45% of liberia's territory is covered by tropical forest, the timber of which was used to finance the armed conflict between 1997 and 2003, leading the un security council to decree an embargo on timber from this country until 2006. the text under consideration concerns the draft council decision on the signing of a voluntary partnership agreement (vpa) between the european union (eu) and liberia on forest law enforcement, governance and trade in timber and timber products imported into the eu under the flegt (forest law enforcement, governance and trade) action plan. this is an eu initiative to prevent illegally harvested timber from entering europe. the eu-liberia voluntary partnership agreement, signed on 27 july 2011, needs to be approved by the european parliament in advance in order to enter into force. i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider it essential that there should be legislation to promote the sustainability of the forestry sector and to prevent indiscriminate logging. in addition, this vpa will contribute to the overall and sustainable development of liberia.
in writing. - this report recommends the conclusion of the flegt voluntary partnership agreement (vpa) with liberia. as with the other flegt agreements, the aim is to tackle illegal logging, help improve regulation, governance and enforcement in the forestry sector in these two countries and strengthen market opportunities for wood products in europe. the vpas aim to provide third countries with national regulations to implement systems for verification of compliance and traceability throughout the supply chain, slaughter standards and controls of consignments for export. the eu thus ensures favourable access to timber products from liberia. this whole approach is not without its contradictions. these agreements are not in themselves the solution to the problem of illegal logging. liberia, like other african countries, is an extremely poor country. for this reason, it is important first of all to promote the development of these countries by supporting the diversification of their economies, by reversing an economic model based on a high dependence on the exploitation and export of a limited number of raw materials to the industrialized countries, by maintaining neo-colonial relations of dependence and subjugation, which lead to the exhaustion of resources.
in writing. − in december 2005, the council authorised the commission to negotiate a series of voluntary partnership agreements (vpas) with timber producing and exporting countries, in order to promote the marketing of legally harvested timber to the eu market and to improve forest governance in partner countries. these bilateral agreements are a cornerstone of the eu's forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt) action plan to end illegal logging. the vpas oblige partner countries to market only products from legally verified wood to the eu. the agreements establish a framework, institutions and systems for a licensing regime to verify the legality of timber exports, and also define supply chain controls, a framework for legal compliance control and independent audit requirements. the partner countries develop, under the terms of the gpas and with the support of the eu, their systems for verifying the legality of their timber exports to the eu. this agreement with liberia is another step towards ending the import of illegal timber from african countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of liberia on forestry law enforcement, governance and trade with regard to timber products imported into the european union. i did so because i believe that this partnership instrument will contribute positively to liberia's overall development and growth and because it is expected to enable liberia to put an end to illegal deforestation and forest degradation, which contribute to climate change.
in writing. − these bilateral agreements are a cornerstone of the eu's action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade to end illegal logging. as in previous voluntary partnership agreements, the agreement with liberia is expected to help improve governance and law enforcement in the forestry sector in the country. in addition to creating a partnership instrument to enable liberia to end illegal deforestation and forest degradation, which contribute to climate change, the vpa should improve market opportunities for liberian timber products in european and other international markets. in this way, and because i believe that the agreement can contribute positively to liberia's overall development and growth, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of liberia should help improve governance and law enforcement in the country's forestry sector. in addition to creating a partnership instrument that enables liberia to end illegal deforestation and forest degradation, the agreement should improve market opportunities for liberian timber products in european and other international markets. the main challenges now lie in their effective implementation and monitoring, as capacity building is a critical issue for liberia, for which the support of the eu and its member states is needed.

in writing. - there are currently several countries receiving aid from the european union and the international monetary fund. the aim of this revision of the regulation, the third since the start of the economic crisis, is to ensure the continuation of the implementation of programmes co-financed by the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund in the context of economic recovery in the member states under financial assistance. the aim is to create a temporary derogation under these two programmes by creating a risk-sharing mechanism to avoid the total suspension of infrastructure projects due to the lack of private co-financing. it should be noted that only projects for which the european investment bank or similar institutions have taken a favourable position will be eligible for funding under the risk-sharing mechanism, thus ensuring that only revenue-generating and economically viable projects are covered. finally, i congratulate the initiative which i hope will be as successful as previous initiatives of a similar nature.

in writing. the resolution under consideration, tabled by mrs cornelia ernst on behalf of the gue/ngl group, concerns a request for an opinion from the court of justice on the compatibility with the treaties of the eu-us agreement of the use and transfer of passenger identification records to the us department of homeland security. after the tragic events of september 11, 2001, all airlines have increased their security levels. as regards travel between europe and the united states of america (usa), the latter began to require a set of passenger data which, to a certain extent, violated the right to data protection in force in the european union, specifically with regard to personal data (banking, health conditions, etc.), as referred to in the opinion of the european court of justice. however, in recent years there has been a great deal of convergence between the us and the eu position. moreover, given the urgency of the matter, the new conditions are the best possible and do not compare with those which could be the subject of bilateral agreements. i therefore believe that the new agreement is better than the bilateral ones and that is why i voted against this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - this resolution, proposed by our group, critically questions the legitimacy of the pnr agreement. the gue/ngl calls on the european court of justice to rule on the legality of this. it should be recalled that in the past this body has ruled that the first agreement concluded by the commission was illegal. in our view, this agreement is another act of submission by the eu to the us. the country, under the pretext of the so-called fight against terrorism, is deepening a disturbing trend towards security and persecution, which is not unrelated to attempts to criminalise the struggle and social protest, especially at a time of deepening of the crisis of capitalism and its effects. most people who use air transport will be unaware of what the pnr is - the passenger identification record. moreover, it will not know the use which is made of this register today and the use to which this agreement opens the door. the gue/ngl is thus making an invaluable contribution by its outstanding intervention in this debate to the denunciation of the content and consequences of this agreement - something which is essential to the dynamisation of the necessary fight and rejection of this intolerable attack on the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens.

in writing. the eu and the us pnr agreement, which allows the us department of homeland security to have access to a panoply of personal data of all passengers travelling to and from the us or making a stopover in the us, is one of the documents this parliament has approved that most attacks the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens. the eu/ngl resolution critically questions the legitimacy of this agreement, including from the perspective of the protection of individual data, and requests that the european court of justice rule on the legality of the agreement. in our view, this agreement is another act of submission by the eu to the us, which, under the pretext of the so-called fight against terrorism, is deepening its security and surveillance drift, which can lead (and leads) to the persecution of all those who do not align and fight us imperialism, who differ in their way of thinking, and even share ideals of social progress that go against us interests. we reiterate that we will do everything to stop and prevent the implementation of this shameful agreement.

in writing. − international judicial cooperation and transatlantic cooperation are essential in the fight against terrorism. the existence of a long-term agreement on the processing and transfer of personal data and passenger identification between the european union and the united states of america is therefore to be welcomed. but such an agreement must not unduly affect the rights of european citizens. the legal requirements for fair, necessary, proportionate and lawful processing of personal data should therefore apply in all circumstances. this agreement between the european union and the united states seems to seek to strike a reasonable balance between the protection of the rights of european citizens and the necessary security guarantees which ultimately benefit us all. i therefore vote in favour of the text of this agreement and i believe, as commissioner malmström has said, that this is the best possible agreement - and the one that best protects european citizens - and should therefore deserve the support of this house.
in writing. − the tragic events of 11 september 2001 in the united states of america (usa) have raised the need for governments and airlines to strengthen their security levels and thus prevent acts of terrorism that could destroy thousands of human lives. since 2007, the european union (eu) has been seeking to negotiate an agreement with the us on the use and transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data to the us department of homeland security. however, the keeping of passenger data on file and the requested information of a personal nature (health, financial situation, etc.) have been the subject of the greatest reservations due to violations of data protection standards. the conclusion of an agreement between the union and the united states on the use and transfer of passenger name records (pnr) is the best solution, as opposed to the conclusion of bilateral agreements. this proposal represents a major us approximation to the positions advocated by the eu. however, this agreement does not guarantee any more protection for european citizens. note that a push system is allowed instead of a pull system. in this way nothing guarantees that there can be no debauchery of our computers and databases. i therefore abstained on this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − the approval of this us-eu pnr agreement allows the us department of homeland security to access a vast array of personal data of all european passengers travelling to and from the us or making a stopover in the us. information to which the us may have access, for example, includes hotel and car reservations, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses, private and business addresses, credit card numbers, personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin. but also, as various voices have warned, data on political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, union membership, as well as other data concerning health or sexual orientation. this agreement, which is always invoked under the pretext of fighting terrorism, undermines the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens by breaching basic data protection rules. this agreement may still be unilaterally modified by the us department of homeland security at any time. this data may be used for unspecified purposes and will be kept for 15 years. we are facing a real big brother, justifying indignation, denunciation, mobilization and struggle.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the fight against terrorism to be crucial if we are to live in a world of peace and prosperity. when we think about the us demands when it comes to the entry of citizens into their country, we cannot forget that the us was attacked on its own territory and the weapons used were aircraft. i therefore agree that the information needed to prevent this from happening again in the future should be provided, even if it may appear to be inadequate or exaggerated. every citizen can be sure that his rights, freedoms and guarantees will never be affected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the eu-us agreement on the transfer of passenger data to and from the united states for the following reasons: (a) the agreement regulates and limits the obligation to provide data arising from us law by imposing commitments on the us vis-à-vis the eu; it is much better than the 2007 agreement, than existing bilaterals, and than no agreement at all. (b) passenger personal data are an essential tool in the fight against terrorism and other transnational crimes (drug and human trafficking). (c) the right to the safety of passengers and of persons in general is no less important than the right to the protection of personal data; the personal data concerned do not involve sensitive data; the agreement strikes a satisfactory balance between the right to security and the right to the protection of personal data and is not, in my view, incompatible with european law in this area. (d) the agreement gives european and member state security authorities access to data and research from us authorities, which helps european security itself while the union does not have its own system for collecting and processing passenger personal data.
in writing. - i abstained because i believe that voting no, by promoting the absence of an eu-us agreement, could open the door to bilateral agreements between the us and each of the member states, weakening the eu-us negotiation, but at the same time i believe that i cannot vote in favour because that would be accepting an agreement which in many respects represents a setback compared to the first agreement of 2004. the rights of european citizens could and should have been better protected.
in writing. − the european union and the united states of america face a number of common challenges in ensuring an effective fight against international terrorism as part of a broader global agenda. in this joint effort, the exchange of information, particularly in the area of the transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data by air carriers operating flights between the eu and the us, serves the purpose of countering the threat to international peace and security. the purpose of the processing of pnr data is limited to the prevention, detection and repression of terrorist acts and serious transnational crime. in addition, the period of data retention is limited, the disclosure of pnr information is subject to legal limitations and the push data export method is considered the regular mode of transfer. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. the text under discussion, for which marianne thyssen is responsible, deals with the proposal for a council directive on the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb). in a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing, it is important that reforms are undertaken that improve the economy and stimulate growth. the proposal for a directive, although not binding on member states, is a very important step towards creating a more favourable competitive environment for businesses and the revival of the economy. this is a more transparent system which eliminates double taxation, has less red tape (the member states will apply their taxation through a single point of contact) and less tax evasion. the existence of a review clause allows member states to verify whether the application of this directive is positive or negative for the pursuit of a market economy generating growth and job creation. i voted in favour because it is an optional system, free of charge for businesses, which will contribute to economic growth within the eu.
in writing. the proposal proposes to regulate the taxation of income of companies and groups of companies operating in more than one member state. it proposes a distribution formula which will determine the distribution of the collectable matter among the member states. this formula, which takes as factors the value of sales, the number of employees and the value of personnel costs and the value of fixed assets, is inaccurate because it abstracts from concrete factors which may be of considerable importance. on the other hand, consideration of the wage bill or the value of labour also has the harmful consequence of disproportionately distributing profits to the countries where labour is more expensive. the commission notes that the tax system in force in the netherlands is based on the principle of the arm's length principle, which is the principle of the arm's length principle. the mcccis is optional, but it cannot be applied to smes, only to european companies and european cooperative societies, which will give multinationals an advantage over domestic companies.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the thyssen report on the common corporate tax base (irc in portugal) because i consider it an important step towards tax harmonisation and transparency in the union, making life easier for companies operating in more than one country and allowing comparison of the effective taxation of companies in the member states. moreover, a common tax base is a necessary condition for future convergence in corporate taxation, starting with the establishment of a minimum rate. that is why i voted in favour of the gue's proposal. in fact, without harmonization of corporate taxation, the current system of tax competition - which is contrary to the very idea of the single market - will persist, allowing for tax dumping and favouring the race to the bottom of corporate taxation and tax revenue for the state.

in writing. − the council directive on a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) introduces common rules for calculating the tax base of companies operating in the eu. the harmonisation brought about by that directive concerns only the calculation and allocation of the taxable amount, since the determination of the rate of tax to be applied is the responsibility of each member state. nor does the directive affect national rules on financial accounting. the introduction of the ccctb brings numerous benefits, such as increased tax transparency, which will make the tax system more equitable and effective, reducing enforcement costs and red tape, making the eu more attractive to foreign investors, as well as reducing tax evasion and avoidance and double taxation. i therefore voted in favour.
