in writing. − finding the optimum balance between climate and environmental policy objectives and energy and industrial policy objectives is a complex exercise and, with rare exceptions, difficult to agree on. if we add a third objective to these two, namely an internal market based on the free movement of goods and services, the exercise underlying the calculation of taxation - based on the principle of equal treatment for energy consumers irrespective of the source of energy used - becomes extremely complex. however, the european union has made many efforts to find this balance. this directive therefore aims to find a new method of calculation, with the final taxation being based on two components: co2 emissions and general energy consumption taxation. an important point for portugal that this directive seeks to ensure is the safeguarding of the right of member states to apply a general level of taxation of energy consumption, which may go down to zero, to energy products and electricity used in agricultural, horticultural or poultry farming and forestry work. i would also like to congratulate my colleague on her work in such a sensitive area.
in writing. - this report, by astrid lulling, deals with a highly controversial subject. the proposal is a council directive amending council directive 2003/96/ec, which aims to restructure the community framework for energy products and electricity. over the last decade, european citizens have been confronted with continuous increases in the price of energy products, which have led to a substantial increase in the cost of factors of production and, consequently, to a rise in the cost of living. at a time when the global crisis is increasing unemployment, freezing wages and extending the retirement age, any measure that increases the price of these products can have very negative social effects. while i understand the need to move to a low-carbon economy to avoid climate change, this process has to be gradual and not suffocating for the economy and, above all, for people. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the energy taxation adopted in 2003 is outdated in the face of the new co2 reduction rules in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, but i cannot help but draw attention to the social problems arising from penalties for consumers.
in writing. - this proposal for a directive on the taxation of energy products and electricity provides that the part of the tax relating to energy consumption and the part of the tax relating to co2 emissions together form the tax on a given product. in addition, member states will be free to set their own rates, provided they are above the minimum rates set by the eu, and they will also be able to create their own tax structure, reproducing the relationship between the minimum levels of taxation for the different energy sources. in view of the perennial upward trend in the price of the various final energy sources, the energy taxation framework now proposed, in the context of the persistence of neoliberal policies in this sector, will not fail to penalise consumers in general and the least competitive countries, which already have serious competitive difficulties due to the costs of the factors of production related to their particular contexts. we cannot help but note it with concern. the environmental objectives must certainly be pursued and deepened, but in the context of a distinct economic and social formation, which puts the strategic sector under public control in the service of the general interest.
in writing. − the current energy taxation directive, adopted in 2003, aims to avoid distortions of competition in the energy sector in the internal market. the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. minimum rates are established, mainly on the basis of the amount of energy consumed, for fuels, fuels and electricity. in addition to these minimum rates, member states are free to set their own national tax rates. this new proposal for a directive adapts the structure of energy taxation to support the objective of a low-carbon economy that is equally energy efficient and to avoid problems in the internal market. the proposal aims to make energy taxation consistent with the eu's commitments to combat climate change by introducing a co2 element. i am in favour of this new form of taxation because it will help to reduce co2 emissions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the lulling report on the taxation of energy and electricity for two fundamental reasons: a) because this legislation is going in the right direction towards fiscal harmonization in the union, which, as i have long argued, is a key element of the very idea of a single market without internal frontiers, which is not compatible with fiscal dumping to gain competitiveness. (b) because taxation of fuels and electricity is a crucial part of the efficient use of resources in which the union is highly deficient, as well as of the european policy of reducing co2 emissions and combating climate warming.

in writing. − the current energy taxation directive, adopted in 2003, was mainly intended to avoid distortions of competition in the internal market in the energy sector by establishing common rules for the products subject to taxation, the timing of taxation and the exemptions allowed. however, the revised proposal for a directive adapts the structure of energy taxation to support the objective of a low-carbon economy that is equally energy efficient and can avoid problems in the internal market. the proposal aims to make energy taxation consistent with the eu's commitments to combat climate change by introducing a co2 element. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be of great importance for the implementation of the european 20-20-20 strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. − the european commission has put forward a proposal to restructure the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity, with the aim of aligning the directive more closely with the european union's energy and climate change objectives. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the taxation of energy in the union must take account of environmental policy as well as the objectives of energy policy and industrial policy, in order to help create a common strategy that will enhance the internal market and make it more efficient. it should be noted that the implementation of the new tax structure should not entail an increase in the tax rate on diesel in order to align the price with that of petrol, allowing the automotive industry to continue to focus on the production of cleaner, energy efficient and co2-reducing combustion engines. finally, the primary objective of energy taxation is to encourage consumers to use energy more efficiently and from cleaner sources, and to ensure a natural process of adaptation of the industry that will be in place by 2025.
in writing. − with this directive, the part of the tax relating to co2 emissions and the part of the tax relating to energy consumption will together form the tax on a given product. in addition, member states will be free to set their own rates, provided they are above the minimum rates set by the eu, and may also create their own tax structure, reproducing the relationship between the minimum levels of taxation for different energy sources. this voluntary narrowing of european policy on climate and environmental issues to the detriment of energy and industrial issues will have a very strong negative impact on consumers. at a time when the prices of the various end-use energy sources have been showing a perennial upward trend and the introduction of renewable energy is not relevant, it is worrying that, in the context of climate concerns, it is proposed to introduce an energy tax framework which will continue to penalise consumers in general and countries with less competitive economies, which already have serious competitive difficulties due to the costs of production factors related to their particular contexts. despite the positive reasons put forward by the rapporteur, the final product of the report remains negative for what would be the desirable development of europe.

in writing. − at present, several, if not all, member states are making a major effort to consolidate their budgets and rebalance their public accounts. inevitably, such efforts need a fiscal policy geared to increasing revenue and reducing public expenditure, while ideally trying to find, through fiscal policy, measures to attract investment from firms and job creators. however, member states have encountered a number of obstacles in pursuing this objective, with tax fraud and evasion having increased considerably in recent years. it is therefore essential to adopt a number of measures which can effectively combat tax fraud and tax evasion simultaneously. it is essential that member states make their tax systems more effective and adopt measures of cooperation with each other, and that the commission should study ways of minimising the situation and negotiate on behalf of the union bilateral agreements with third countries in tax matters.

author. - madam president, commissioner malmström, ladies and gentlemen, regulation 2252 adopted in 2004 was an important step towards improving and harmonising the rules on the protection of passports and travel documents. we introduced biometric identification elements to establish a more reliable link between the document and its true owner. but the security of passports is not limited to the passport itself, the whole process is relevant, it starts with the presentation of the documents necessary for the issuance of passports, what are technically called the breeder documents, followed by the collection of biometric data and ends with the verification and matching at border control posts. there is little point in increasing the level of security in passports if we allow weak points in the other elements of the chain. this is the case, for example, of the recently published news that some 10% of biometric passports circulating in france are fake, having been obtained on the basis of forged documents, or of a study presented during a hearing in the dutch parliament, which revealed that the results of a test carried out by a local government prove that more than 20% of the fingerprints collected could not be verified, thus revealing their uselessness. freedom of movement in the schengen area is undoubtedly one of the greatest achievements of the european construction, but it requires a high level of security. the existence of secure passports and documents that function effectively and efficiently contributes to this. it is therefore imperative to find solutions to the problems that may exist, first, in the reliability of the biometric data collection process, second, in the reliability and usefulness of fingerprints according to age groups, in particular for children and the elderly, third, in the disparities between member states in the documents that may serve as the basis for the issuance of passports, breeder documents and fourth, in the way fingerprints are matched. the commissioner knows that the council was responsible for sending a questionnaire to the member states to enable an analysis to be made of possible failures in the identification systems and of the error rates recorded, in order to assess the need to introduce a european system. these concerns were present in the review of the regulation that we did in 2008 and for that reason parliament introduced a three-year review clause in order to allow the necessary studies to be done by the commission and to receive the results of that questionnaire. the question i have to ask, commissioner, is whether the commission has the results to present to us and whether, in view of them, it is planning to present any legislative proposal that might be necessary.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the agricultural sector is not left to the detriment of the environment. we want to preserve biodiversity, we want to prevent forest fires, we want better water management and better soil protection. it is not, therefore, the concept of this kind of support that we are discussing here today, what we are discussing here today is of a very practical nature. we members who are currently responsible for drawing up reports on the reform of the cap will have to decide, we will have to legislate without having the slightest information on the real impact of the application of the new criteria on the territory. at this point the council should have informed us, the member states should have made available all the information on the real impact of these new criteria in each of the member states, and so the question i would like to leave to the council is whether it is in a position to provide this information and, if so, when? and i would remind you that in a month's time the rapporteurs will be submitting their work for translation, and therefore if this information is not available it is practically impossible, it is even impossible, to legislate responsibly. so, since the responsibility for this matter lies with the member states, i would very much like the council to tell us in a very clear and very concrete way whether and when it will be in a position to provide us with this information which is essential for our work as co-legislators.
the commission has long proposed to review the delimitation of lessfavoured areas on the basis of biophysical criteria alone, but to date no information has been made available on the process under way, which is particularly important when parliament is discussing the future cap. the identification of less-favoured areas is absolutely essential to the achievement of the european model of agriculture that the cap represents, since it establishes aid levels based on positive discrimination in order to make agricultural production viable and to promote it throughout the union. this also ensures the vitality of rural areas and prevents abandonment and depopulation of land. at the same time, the assessment of less-favoured areas, to be carried out on the basis of simulations carried out by the member states, should be very detailed, taking into account the high level of subsidiarity in the definition of criteria which may not only be biophysical but also have socioeconomic implications, considering limits of values adjusted to the characteristics of each member state and respecting the specificities of its regions. the criteria established should also consider the possibility of cumulative biophysical parameters, combining physical (soil, climate), geographical (isolation, distance), production, proportion of pastures, density of animals, etc. unfortunately, the commission proposal shows a complete absence of reference to geographical disadvantages such as isolation, the dispersion of farms, distance from the centres of consumption, distance from the centres of decision-making and services, aspects which are very relevant for a country like portugal, which has a continental territory in the far west of europe and two outermost regions in the middle of the atlantic ocean, such as the azores and madeira.
as you know, as the author of this question i have two minutes, so i ask you how much time i have for this speech. i would like to begin by making a reference which will help to frame this debate. the requalification of disadvantaged areas proposed in 2005, by excluding socioeconomic criteria, harms some of the poorest regions in the european union. small and mediumsized farms and family farming are obviously hit even harder. the european commission insists in various ways on denying them the role they need to play in the future of agriculture in europe. the concept of a disadvantaged area has been overturned. the current definition ignores a whole dimension, in addition to the biophysical dimension, which cannot be ignored, the socioeconomic dimension, otherwise the inequalities and injustices in the distribution of cap funds between countries and between producers will worsen and it would therefore be necessary not only to maintain but also to broaden and diversify the socioeconomic criteria, for example, in terms of indicators of desertification and rural exodus, among others. as regards the biophysical criteria, the commission has given a panel of experts the task of defining them, but has failed to include in this role, as required, representatives of the various member states, as it acknowledged in a question i addressed to it in 2010. no portuguese expert or institution was included in this panel, as were the overwhelming majority of member states. the dangers are obvious. in view of the diversity of situations, the complexity of the task of defining uniform criteria may once again result in the benefit of some to the detriment of others. there is one essential question in this reform of the cap which remains unanswered, namely the need to ensure a fair distribution of the cap funds which guarantees each country its right to produce and its right to food sovereignty.
this is a debate of great importance and timeliness. the current agricultural and trade policies have promoted export-oriented intensive production models, while at the same time devastating local production and small and mediumsized farming in numerous countries. these models are unsustainable and irrational, whether from an environmental, economic or social point of view. they have reduced the diversity of food, increased the food dependence of many countries and contributed to the desertification of vast rural areas. the promotion of local production and consumption by encouraging short supply chains and reducing energy flows associated with food production and distribution is thus a pressing need. small and mediumsized farmers play a very important role in this context, which should be recognized and valued. all this requires a fundamental change in the current cap and its market orientation. it calls for the withdrawal of agriculture from the wto, it calls for an agricultural policy which recognizes the right and the importance of each country and each region to produce according to its possibilities and taking into account its potential.
the definition of what is locally produced and, above all, the requirement that products are actually marketed as such can be important for producers and consumers. for producers because it stimulates production by ensuring that it is sold at a more profitable price. for consumers because they have access to fresher products whose origin and production methods they know better. it is also about boosting the economy and rural life with benefits for all european citizens. protect and value local products, but don't complicate or bureaucratize it because otherwise we'll kill you.
mr president, the effectiveness of development aid is a matter of the utmost importance and there are issues that go far beyond the aspects of management, decentralized or not, for the commission delegations, as the rapporteur has also mentioned. the question of the necessary coherence between the sectoral policies of the european union and the declared objectives in the field of development aid. the question of the much needed appropriation of aid, which requires a large involvement of the country, its authorities, institutions and social organisations in the design and implementation of policies. in this area, the european union must genuinely support and not dictate, it must empower and not impose, it must respect the specificities, the options, the sovereign will of the developing countries, it must not lose sight of the importance of south-south cooperation which must be encouraged. development aid should promote the full development and full exploitation of the endogenous potential of developing countries and not perpetuate their dependence which means that a substantial part of aid today is returned to the countries of origin, for example in the form of the purchase of goods and services, among other forms.
in portugal, the so-called bologna process and, in a broader sense, the modernisation of the higher education system, had disastrous aspects. instead of widespread student mobility, what has happened is an elitisation of higher education by dividing it into two cycles, which has increased the costs of higher education for most students. today, there are students who drop out of universities because they have no money to pay for tuition, to pay for their housing, or for all the other costs associated with being in higher education. for these students, the modernization of the higher education system is just a mirage.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on her report. mrs kiil-nielsen has made an interesting and well-structured report. good cooperation with the shadow rapporteurs has enabled a broad consensus to be reached. the effects of climate change are not gender neutral. climate change does not equally affect men and women, rich and poor, developed and developing countries. the effects of climate change are greatest in the poorest regions and can exacerbate social inequalities. women are victims of multiple discrimination. they are particularly affected by poverty. 70% of the poor are women and they are also more vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and natural disasters. the elimination of inequalities and the fight against climate change are linked. there will be no climate justice without true gender equality. natural disasters have a significant impact in the medium and long term in terms of education, health, structural poverty and displacement of populations. children and the elderly are particularly vulnerable to the effects of natural disasters. where more disasters occur, the schooling rate is lower, droughts and water shortages due to climate change force women to work harder to secure water, food and energy, and often girls drop out of school to help their mothers with these tasks. measures are therefore needed to integrate the gender dimension into natural disaster risk prevention and management strategies. on the other hand, women are accustomed to managing natural resources, which gives them a potential that should not be neglected in the upgrading of climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies.
on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur on the quality of his report, on the good work he has done, and to reiterate that only with ambition, political will and adequate funding can we meet the objectives of the biodiversity strategy 2020. the protection of biodiversity must be integrated into all eu policies, in particular in the context of the current reforms of the common agricultural policy and the common fisheries policy. the next financial framework must provide the resources needed to finance the strategy. this funding will be offset from an environmental and economic point of view, as the cost of biodiversity loss could reach 7% of gdp by 2050. the benefits associated with the natura 2000 network are estimated to be around eur 200-300 billion per year, in addition to creating millions of jobs. the commission and the member states should make available sufficient resources to finance the natura 2000 network and should also ensure the implementation of european legislation, in particular the birds directive and the habitats directive, as well as the marine strategy framework directive. equally important are the initiatives to be developed in relation to green infrastructure and genetic resources, as well as legislation on invasive alien species, whose proposals we look forward to from the commission. the objectives of the biodiversity strategy require concrete, integrated and ambitious actions, and adequate funding is also needed. it should be borne in mind that biodiversity encompasses all interactions of the living world, species and ecosystems, in direct connection with human activity, food, clothing, health care, heating of buildings depend on biodiversity. biodiversity is the guarantee of life.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, in 2001, the european commission set itself the objective of halting biodiversity loss by 2010. ten years later, it recognized that this goal has not been achieved and that global biodiversity is also under serious threat. the biodiversity strategy to 2020 is now being discussed. once again, goals and objectives are set. some questions therefore arise: have the lessons of past failures been learned? in 10 years, won't we be seeing another failure? what has been done to correct the course? what does success or failure depend on in this case? a strategy is made up of short, medium and long-term objectives, and it is also made up of the means to achieve these objectives. this strategy has shortcomings in one and another area, for example: on the one hand, there are still shortcomings in the funding, as in the next multiannual financial framework, and in the mechanisms for monitoring and correcting the implementation of the strategy. on the other hand, some of the sectoral policies with the most relevant effects on biodiversity remain essentially unchanged. this is the case with agricultural and trade policies, which promote intensive production models geared to exports, deregulation and trade liberalisation, and the weakening of local production and consumption. it is not enough to give these policies a greener look, keeping their fundamentals unchanged, keeping their so-called market orientation unchanged. the commission is enthusiastic about the business and biodiversity approach. we are afraid that we are dealing with a business-as-usual strategy in biodiversity.

in writing. the report under consideration, presented by my colleague francesca balzani, concerns draft amending budget no 1/2012 of the eu for the financial year 2012, section iii commission, in relation to the financing of the iter (international thermonuclear experimental reactor) programme. iter is a unique scientific programme in the world on fusion energy, also known as star energy, involving the world's leading nuclear experts, and which may be the future energy solution. it was initiated in 1995 by a future energy commitment between the presidents of the united states of america and the soviet union, ronald reagan and gorbachev. the european union (eu) has been one of its main drivers since its launch. during the debate on the 2012 eu budget, given the importance of the programme in question, the issue of its under-financing was raised and the commission left the guarantee of its resolution. i therefore welcome the presentation of this report, which substantiates the council's position on this draft amending budget, and i welcome the agreement reached between the three european institutions which has made it possible to overcome this problem. however, it is necessary to provide for its future financing.

in writing. - i approve of this report, considering it essential to propose an initiative which, on the one hand, proposes a quality framework for higher education and, on the other, a rapid harmonisation of qualification systems at european level, so that there is a real european area of education and research and so that conditions are promoted so that the new generations are in a position to integrate professionally not only into national labour markets but also into the european labour market. in view of the economic crisis which is responsible for unprecedented high levels of youth unemployment in europe, our s&d group proposal to support the creation of higher education entry mechanisms for citizens who have completed secondary education but have not continued their studies, and on the other hand to create a quality framework for traineeships and the use of the structural funds to support students' entry into the labour market, is also welcome. in short, the modernisation of higher education must ensure that people of all ages and social backgrounds can have the opportunity to attend higher education so that the focus on knowledge can serve the challenges facing europe in the 21st century.
in writing. − in a post-crisis europe, recovering and growing, the importance of higher education and vocational training plays a crucial role. it is imperative to give young europeans the tools they need to compete in a globalised world and to enter the labour market through their knowledge and skills. (we must not forget that, all over europe, the figures for youth unemployment are staggering.) but we must not ignore the fact that more training often does not equal more opportunities on the labour market. the eu is seeing a growing number of young graduates who, with full training and postgraduate training, have no job and no prospect of getting one. training must be geared to market needs and must prepare young workers. this paradigm shift and the modernisation of systems to bring them closer to the labour market will, in my view, be fundamental to halting the growth of unemployment among young people and to guarantee them a future with more possibilities.
in writing. - the future of a country lies in its youth. the more competent and better prepared the new generations are, the better their future will be. the report on the modernisation of higher education systems in europe by lászló tőkés is of great importance not only for the countries of the former iron curtain but also for the other member states. for the former, because it is an opportunity to continue democratic reforms, to combat past crises and to modernise their education system; for the latter, because it is an opportunity to help overcome the current crisis by boosting economic growth and promoting skilled youth employment. it is true that the bologna reform, with its division into two cycles, has brought an increase in costs and not everyone is able to complete their courses. in addition, and unfortunately, the economic and financial crisis, especially in the member states with financial assistance programmes, has forced cuts in education budgets. it is therefore essential to work with the social partners to ensure that disadvantaged people have the opportunity to learn. only in this way will we contribute to the pursuit of the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - as many have warned, the bologna process and the so-called harmonisation of the european higher education system served the purpose of attacking the right to education and the social role of the states in this field, which is enshrined in the constitution of the portuguese republic. the consequences are now visible in many countries, such as portugal, where there is a sharp rise in the cost of attending higher education, especially (but not only) in the now-designated second cycle. there is a notorious elitisation of higher education. what has happened is the distinction between those who can or cannot access higher education, but also between those who can or cannot attend the second cycle, which has enormous tuition costs. countless news reports have noted that every day thousands and more students are dropping out of higher education because of lack of financial resources. the commercialisation of higher education was bologna's primary objective. this is the fundamental objective of a certain modernization that many have been calling for. the same applies to this report.
in writing. − europe has some 19 million students and over 4 000 higher education institutions, but although 35% of all jobs in the eu will require highly qualified workers by 2020, only 26% of the workforce currently has high-level qualifications. the responsibility for higher education remains primarily with the member states and the higher education institutions themselves. eu actions (such as erasmus study abroad grants) complement and coordinate member states' efforts. the european higher education area and the european research area form the framework for eu higher education policy. given the challenges facing european societies, it is crucial that higher education institutions continue to be adequately funded, even as societies are dealing with the current economic crisis. in order to meet future skills requirements, more people will need to complete higher education and workers will need to update their knowledge and skills continuously while remaining active in the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a policy of improving european higher education and placing eu educational institutions among the best in the world is a policy of economic growth. the percentage of highly skilled workers is currently below the 2020 targets, and all efforts to achieve this are essential. it is essential that higher education institutions continue to be adequately funded, even in the current economic crisis. the quality of education is a central aspect in widening access to higher education, which is why the rapporteur's intention to include this factor in the related rankings of educational institutions seems pertinent.
in writing. − the eu has only 75 higher education institutions among the top 200 universities worldwide and only 26% of the workforce has a qualified degree. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to strengthen the role of higher education institutions as a key driver of the development of countries. the entities of the science and technology system should increasingly focus on the development of activities of scientific excellence, stimulate entrepreneurship, adapt academic training to the labour market and enhance programmes that allow for increased international mobility during the period of study or work. i also believe that it is urgent to define a european system for the mutual recognition of qualifications acquired. finally, i believe that there should be greater equality of opportunity in young people's access to quality education and training, and it is crucial that member states consider education as the main investment in the future of their nations. in this regard, i advocate that higher education expenditure on investments in university infrastructure and people be included in the eu budget for the period 2014-2020 in order to achieve the investment target of 3% of gdp.
in writing. − this report highlights the process of harmonising the higher education system in the eu, even recommending that this process be further developed, particularly in terms of the standardisation of educational content to meet the needs of the labour market. the reinforcement of the european higher education area and the bologna process is advocated on the grounds that this facilitates student mobility between eu higher education institutions. but what happened in portugal with the implementation of the bologna process? nothing less than the elitisation of higher education, the distinction between those who can or cannot access higher education, but also between those who can or cannot attend the second cycle, which has enormous tuition costs. today, in portugal, there are numerous cases and testimonies of students who abandon higher education for lack of financial resources. for these students, expressions such as modernisation of the higher education system are only rhetorical concepts with no practical application. we will continue to fight for a free, quality public education for all. we have voted against this report.
in writing. − i support this report because i believe that today eu citizens and businesses, especially smes, still often face insurmountable barriers when carrying out crossborder activities in the eu, when they should be able to benefit particularly from online public administration, as it entails reduced administrative costs and burdens, increases productivity, efficiency, competitiveness, transparency, openness, policy effectiveness, accessibility and streamlining of procedures. it should also facilitate the creation of synergies and the sharing of resources and skills between companies, thus enabling a more collaborative business environment for smes. national and european authorities also need to promote the innovative use of public sector information through academia, including students, and the general public, as well as for research and business development, thus enhancing transparency.
in writing. − the existence of a competitive digital single market is becoming more important and more inescapable in our society. technological developments, especially in terms of the provision of information, content and knowledge on the net, have been extremely rapid and, in just over a decade, have dramatically changed the digital landscape with the massification of the internet and mobile communications. it is therefore important to look to the future and to think about how these new facilities of the digital age can be put at the service of citizens and businesses, by modernising administrations and bringing them closer to those who are administered.
in writing. − one of the pillars of the europe 2020 strategy, namely smart growth, is based on the so-called digital agenda. according to the report by colleague silvia-adriana ţicău on a competitive digital single market with online public administration as a driving force, the implementation of an interoperability strategy will not only improve communications between member states but also bring about cost savings that are essential for the recovery of economies. in this process of digital modernisation, public administration plays an important role as a driver for achieving the objectives. there are, however, some problems that need to be solved, such as the absence of ultra-fast broadband throughout the eu. this is a sector with great potential, representing some 5% of gdp, which must be freed from all obstacles. i voted in favour of this report and hope that the measures it advocates, such as electronic invoicing, digital signatures, mutual recognition, online contracting and the renewal of infrastructure, will be implemented quickly in order to make life easier for businesses and to make the public service more efficient and citizen-friendly.
in writing. the report focuses on the digital single market, which aims to be competitive, without barriers and without distortions of competition. it also addresses the issue of the implementation of online public administration. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. we believe that advances in science and technology, such as new technological platforms, associated with the internet, can open up possibilities for social and civilizational advancement. when introduced into public administration services, they can help to make them more efficient, improve the comfort and well-being of citizens and workers in those services, while opening up prospects for diversification, improvement and expansion of public services themselves. we must not forget, however, that the current context is marked by various attacks on public administration and the social functions of the state. and in this context, the introduction of new technologies has sometimes been used as a pretext to reduce costs and functions, without any improvements for citizens or public officials, quite the contrary.
in writing. − the adoption of the eu 2020 strategy in 2010 sought to create smart, sustainable and inclusive growth by improving economic governance. one of the flagship initiatives of the eu's growth strategy is the digital agenda for europe, a strategy that seeks to harness the potential offered by the rapid advancement of digital technologies. e-government is the use of tools and systems provided by information and communication technologies (ict) to deliver better public services to citizens and businesses. in most member states, the development of online public administration is considered to be based on the one hand on bureaucracy, the network of interconnectivity between public administrations, and on the other hand on the development of the right digital content and applications. the application of ict in public administration is very important for the provision of a better service to all citizens, hence my vote in favour.
in writing. − the eu 2020 strategy was adopted with the aim of creating smart, sustainable and inclusive growth by improving economic governance. one of the 7 flagship initiatives of the eu's growth strategy is the digital agenda for europe, a strategy that seeks to harness the potential offered by the rapid advancement of digital technologies. i voted in favour of the view that the project for the development of online public administration by the european union is a sign of union and effective development, while ensuring that it is based on cooperation between public administrations, in full respect of the principles underlying european public services.
in writing. − the european commission has defined the seven action lines of the europe 2020 strategy, one of which is the digital agenda for europe, which aims to extract sustainable economic and social benefits from a digital single market, based on fast and ultra-fast internet and interoperable applications. after drawing up a number of strategy papers and opinions submitted by various european bodies, the european parliament decided to give its opinion on the importance of public administration in the implementation and development of the digital single market. i support this report because i believe that it is necessary to define an action plan for online public administration, to promote the adoption of public procurement and to implement the e-invoicing initiative. i also think that the importance of the telecommunications sector for the european union's industrial policy, the digital single market and research and innovation activities should be stressed. however, i believe that special attention should be paid to the specific features of the outermost regions and that a programme should be set up in the area of transport, energy and telecommunications, similar to posei for agriculture and fisheries.
in writing. - this report advocates, on the one hand, the creation of a competitive digital single market, i.e. without barriers and distortions of competition, and, on the other hand, states as its objective a greater implementation of online public administration, while reducing the cost of public services in exchange for greater efficiency and competitiveness, in particular for the digital single market, but also saving public resources. the question of the single market, whether digital or not, retains the same principles, objectives and interests as the single market, which is responsible for the dismantling of national productions, the destruction of jobs, the increase in external dependence and the imbalance in the trade balance, which results in the constant deficits and the weakening of the economies of the most vulnerable countries. we recognize, however, that new technological advances, such as the internet, are an important tool and asset to society, as are the conveniences and efficiencies they can bring when applied to public administration services, while complementing the existence of normal departments and their staff. we cannot, however, accept that the pretext of using this tool is to continue to pave the way for the weakening of public services, allowing and encouraging privatisations, brutal attacks on the jobs, rights and wages of public administration workers.
