in writing. − as the world's leading donor and seeking to use the soft power this gives it to promote democracy, freedom, the rule of law and the development of the least-favoured peoples and nations, the european union cannot but pay particular attention to how it spends its taxpayers' money and to evaluate the results of the commitment of resources and people to those purposes. i support european involvement in this worldwide effort to promote development and that it be made increasingly transparent and scrutinized by european citizens as well as by the citizens of the countries receiving aid.
in writing. - the strategy of decentralising the management of the commission's external aid from grants, as referred to in the court of auditors' report, has proved to be a very positive initiative. moreover, the effectiveness of aid to developing countries is of the utmost importance in helping them to overcome their economic and social situation. improving development aid through good management of funds is in the interest of the beneficiary states. i welcome the commission's intention to improve the recommendations of the court of auditors, particularly as regards the development of human resources not only in africa but also in other regions, and, taking advantage of the experience of officials, to change the duration of contracts from 3 to 6 years. i therefore agree with the proposals put forward by mr kaczmarek, both in relation to the recommendations of the court of auditors and in relation to the need to increase the coherence between the objectives of the european union and the real needs of the countries receiving support. i therefore voted in favour of this report, aware that decentralisation helps to reduce the cost of aid.
in writing. − the report considers that the decentralisation of external aid management has improved the efficiency of the provision of funds, making progress with recommendations with which we generally agree, such as: more actual workers and fewer contract agents; reduction of bureaucracy to distribute funds; promotion of local consultations. the rapporteur makes an important warning: the crisis must not be used as an excuse to do more with less, in order to contain or reduce external aid and the costs of its operationalisation. it also draws attention to the work still to be done in the area of the millennium development goals. there are, however, aspects of the report from which we distance ourselves (for example, the considerations on the european external action service) and also some omissions which we consider important. as we said during the debate, effective appropriation of development aid requires a strong involvement of the country, its authorities, institutions and social organisations in the design and implementation of policies. the european union must support, not dictate. it should empower, not impose. it must respect the specificities, choices and sovereign will of the developing countries (note the bad example of the imposition of the so-called economic partnership agreements, despite the resistance of the acp countries).
in writing. − a decentralised approach is beneficial as it brings decision-making closer to the realities surrounding such provision and to situations where more efficient coordination and harmonisation of donors develops in operational terms, with due regard to the need for local ownership. the ultimate objective of the decentralisation and wider reform of external aid managed by the commission is to increase the speed, rigor of financial management procedures and the quality of aid in partner countries. the results of the evaluation by the european court of auditors should only serve to further efforts to increase the effectiveness of aid delivery.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the european parliament's call for the commission and the member states to work towards better links between eu delegations and bilateral agencies and partner governments and other development groups such as think tanks, universities, foundations, ngos and subnational authorities, as these closer links will maximise the comparative advantages of the decentralisation process and of the different actors in the national context, while avoiding unnecessary duplication of effort.
in writing. - article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union stresses that the primary objective of the union's external aid policy is the reduction and, in the long term, the eradication of poverty. in implementing policies which may affect developing countries, the union shall take account of the objectives of development cooperation. it should be noted that 74% of the eu's external aid comes from its own eu budget and the european development fund (edf), implying a decentralised approach by the 136 existing european delegations. i agree with this own-initiative report because i believe that the european commission should contribute to the definition of a long-term strategy for development aid policy, promote the involvement and consultation of local authorities and carry out systematic monitoring visits to existing projects. as bill gates said in the european parliament in brussels, the eu should take the lead in analysing and identifying opportunities to increase the resources of development aid programmes, involving the eib and other international bodies.
in writing. − the report argues that the decentralisation of external aid management has helped to make the funds available more efficiently, suggesting a number of positive recommendations: the commission is also proposing to increase the number of staff in the central services, to improve the assessment of the provision of funds, to increase the number of workers and to reduce the number of contract staff, and to reduce red tape in the distribution of funds. it is also urging that the crisis should not lead to a reduction in resources and that this should not lead to a reduction in staffing levels. but two questions arise the social and economic development of the peripheral countries will only be truly sustainable when they are no longer dependent on powers such as the eu, when they can exploit and develop their own capacities and do not have to watch their resources being continually plundered. we also reiterate that eu external development aid must never, under any circumstances, be associated with the agenda of so-called defence actions with militaristic and interventionist intentions on the part of the eu. development aid must never be used as a pretext for interfering in the internal affairs of countries, in particular by exerting political influence and creating destabilising environments that undermine the sovereignty of the peoples.
in writing. − i welcome this report as the inclusion of gender issues provides an opportunity to strengthen efforts to combat climate change. this report should thus serve the purpose of addressing inequalities and addressing their root causes, to increase women's capacity for financial autonomy, not only by supporting women in critical situations, but also by harnessing their potential to fight climate change.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on women and climate change because the effects of climate change do not affect men and women, rich and poor, developed and developing countries equally. women are more affected by poverty (70% of the poor are women) and are more vulnerable to the impacts of climate change.
in writing. − regardless of the gender perspective, any climate change policy, especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis, must seek economic efficiency and sustainability, putting innovation and research at the service of new techniques and new solutions that are more environmentally friendly and equally efficient and competitive. the focus should be on clean energy, more efficient use of natural resources and strong investment in research and more environmentally friendly technologies in order to maintain european competitiveness and enable job creation in a sustainable development framework.
in writing. the resolution under consideration, drawn up by mrs nicole kiil-nielsen, draws our attention to a new problem, namely the awareness of the influence that the gender dimension can (or does) have on climate change. the role played by women in many societies gives them an importance in the management of some natural resources with a direct impact on environmental sustainability. in fact, they are the largest users of water (cooking and cleaning) and of forest products as a source of energy on a daily basis. this matter is of particular relevance when we consider that, in the event of environmental disasters, about 85% of the victims and 75% of the refugees are women. it is therefore essential that they participate in discussion forums and decision-making bodies where their experience can be of value in the adoption of measures to minimise this situation. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i am confident that more responsible and conscious climate action can contribute to improving the quality of life of people in many parts of the world, and particularly in the most disadvantaged regions.
in writing. - this report addresses the issue of climate change from a gender perspective. it is recalled that, as the report states, the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) has confirmed that the impact of climate change varies according to gender, age and social class, with the poorest people being the most affected. we agree with the integration of the gender dimension into all policies, including climate policies. we also agree that gender equality and justice objectives should be set in all policy areas, including this one, so that developments in this area do not exacerbate inequalities between men and women. the report also highlights the positive aspects of the development of implementation plans and evaluation of policies and projects; the adaptation of evaluation and action development tools for environmental protection, with reference to local projects on specific issues and with a focus on women; and the gradual, new and additional increase in funding, calling for the integration of gender equality as a horizontal issue in all climate funds and instruments.
in writing. − women represent approximately 50% of the world's population, yet in relative terms they continue to assume greater responsibility for daily consumer choices, childcare and household activities. given the differentiated roles of men and women, the impact of women on the environment is not the same as that of men, and their access to resources and ways of positioning and adapting themselves can be affected by discrimination in terms of income, access to resources, political power, education and household responsibility. climate change can increase inequalities, and there is a risk that climate change policies, if they do not address gender discrimination from the outset, could have a negative impact on gender balance and women's rights. this report deals with this problem in a balanced way and deserves my support.
in writing. − this report focuses on the effects of climate change on increasing inequalities between women and men. the rapporteur believes that climate change will have a disproportionate impact on women, as this gender inequality is present in all areas of society. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i think it is important that gender is not excluded from the eu's major priorities, so that it becomes a cross-cutting issue in its policies and strategies. it is therefore necessary to change mentalities and to value the role of women in all dimensions of society. however, i disagree with the need to introduce quotas in eu climate diplomacy, as they are an undervaluation of the genre itself.
in writing. - it is pertinent in this report to consider that dangerous climate change should be the eu's top priority. we reaffirm, however, that more than climate change, it is the capitalist system and its mode of production that by its nature depletes natural resources, jeopardizes the survival of man, and deepens inequalities in access to the quality of life between the working class and the bourgeoisie. the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) itself has confirmed that the impact of climate change varies according to gender, age and social class, with those most affected being mainly segments of the population living in poverty. we welcome the recommendation to mainstream gender in all phases of climate policies and to set gender equality and equity targets in all policy areas, so that climate action does not exacerbate inequalities between men and women. we do not, however, support the point on the introduction of quotas in the relevant delegations and bodies, since these measures only mask and make invisible the real inequality between men and women in various economic and social areas.
in writing. - i approve this report, recognising that infrastructure construction, urbanisation, industrialisation and physical interventions in the landscape in general are among the most significant factors in the deterioration of ecosystems and habitats. local, regional and national administrations, in the context of planning regulations, implementing measures and within their respective competences, should consider these factors, which sometimes pose a threat to ecosystems and habitats, in planning and urban planning projects, both large and small-scale. the pressures and needs at local and regional level, which require substantial economic development, are understandable, and so i think it is important to point out to local and regional authorities that they should be aware of the necessary balance between development and the need to protect biodiversity and natural habitats. for example, the azores are at the forefront of biodiversity protection, seeking to implement energy plans, tourism activities, etc. that value and protect their biodiversity. as such, regional and local development policies should induce biodiversity benefits and halt further habitat loss.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on our life insurance and our natural capital - eu biodiversity strategy to 2020 because biodiversity is not incompatible with development. biodiversity is a guarantee of life.
in writing. − within the framework of the eu biodiversity strategy, the union as a whole, and with particular attention to all areas covered by community policies, must find a sustainable strategy for the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of ecosystems. i believe that this is particularly relevant in the area of agriculture and fisheries, which is why i am following the reforms of the cfp and the cap with particular attention, since the proper and sustainable preservation of biodiversity, while essential and desirable, cannot be a brake on the sustainability and development of agricultural and fisheries activities.
in writing. − the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020 is part of the flagship initiative for a resource-efficient europe and aims to provide the opportunity to take the necessary measures to secure nature and ecosystem services for future generations. this is the right time to mainstream biodiversity in all policy areas as major european policies are currently being reviewed. the common agricultural policy, cohesion policy, common fisheries policy and the european roadmaps for energy, transport and resource efficiency will be transposed into legislation. it is now time to show that the warm words about biodiversity also translate into concrete policy measures. it is important that the european commission and the member states commit themselves to adopting integrated strategies which will make it possible to recognize, in each geographical area, the natural values and the characteristics of its cultural heritage, as well as the conditions necessary for its preservation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that political support for biodiversity must now be translated into effective and integrated policy measures in all policy areas.
in writing. - this report has been considerably improved from its initial version. we are pleased that several of the amendments we proposed in the committee on the environment have been adopted. examples of amendments are those relating to: funding issues, including the life programme; invasive alien species; the study of the impact of agrofuels; the reduction of the diversity of cultivated species; or some limitations and distortions of the european commission's greening proposal for the next cap. however, other important amendments we proposed were rejected, which we regret. as a consequence, the report contains some serious omissions on the one hand and, on the other, views and guidelines that we do not share, such as those on the european commission's proposals for reforms of the common agricultural policy and the common fisheries policy (which we welcome), or the whole of the so-called business and biodiversity aspect. we stress the amendments concerning the financing of the natura 2000 network, the criticism of the current agricultural and trade policies and the need for their radical change, the fisheries policy (proximity management, more means for data acquisition), the monitoring of the implementation of the strategy, among others. it is not enough to set ambitious goals, we must look after the means of achieving them. the report is flawed at this level.
in writing. − the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020 gives us the opportunity to take the necessary steps to secure nature and ecosystem services for future generations. all we need is political conviction, courage and commitment to avoid failure. the main objective is to mainstream biodiversity in all policy fields. and this may be the right time, because all the major european policies are currently being reviewed. the common agricultural policy, cohesion policy, common fisheries policy and the european roadmaps for energy, transport and resource efficiency will be transposed into legislation. the objectives set out in the eu biodiversity strategy by 2020 can be achieved. all we need is a transposition into policy measures of the political support for biodiversity expressed by many world leaders.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that european natural capital is a major asset which needs to be invested and maintained and from which a genuine cohesion policy can be derived. the objectives set out in the eu biodiversity strategy by 2020 can be achieved through the transposition of policy measures to support biodiversity.
in writing. − the safeguarding of biodiversity must be a cross-cutting element in the eu's sectoral policies. in parallel, the eu diversity strategy to 2020 should be present in the eu's external policy as a way of calling on third countries to provide an appropriate and timely response to ensure the sustainability of natural ecosystems. i regret that the objectives of the 2010 strategy have not been fully achieved, and therefore i consider it key to mainstream biodiversity in all eu sectoral policies in order to achieve one of the pillars of the eu 2020 strategy. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (aema) is a step in the right direction. at the same time, member states should cooperate in the protection of the natural heritage, including it in their national programmes and projects. we cannot but stress that our natural heritage is an inexhaustible resource. the use and abuse we make of it will have repercussions on our way of life, and consequently on our quality of life as citizens.
in writing. − the report contains positive aspects which we value, particularly in the parts concerning the funding of the life programme, invasive alien species, the study of the impact of agrofuels, the reduction of the diversity of cultivated species. there are, however, some recommendations that we could never follow up, in particular those concerning the european commission's proposals for reforms of the common agricultural policy and the common fisheries policy, and all the emphasis placed on the idea of business and biodiversity. environmental concerns should never be seen as an 'opportunity' for business to be set up for profit. they must be taken into account as matters of principle.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the seventh environment action programme (eap) should provide the appropriate framework to ensure sufficient funding, in particular for innovation, research and development, and that the funding of environmental objectives, in synergy with the life programme, and that the full integration of environmental protection should be an important part of the next multiannual financial framework, the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap), the common fisheries policy (cfp), cohesion policy and the horizon 2020 programme. i believe in particular that the eu should allow new sources of funding for the eap to be created. i believe that the seventh eap should provide a comprehensive framework to enable us to address recurrent and emerging environmental and sustainability challenges, taking due account of existing and planned measures and taking into account the outermost regions, which are seen as an added value in terms of environmental value and can make this programme an opportunity to promote the sustainable development of these regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the review of the sixth environment action programme and the setting of priorities for the seventh environment action programme, because i consider it essential to ensure a rapid transition to the next programme and to avoid any gaps. the continuity of the environment action programmes should be ensured as a guiding framework for eu environmental policy and with a view to further integrating environmental objectives into all sectoral policies.
in writing. − the sixth environment action programme will end in july 2012 and the final evaluation, published on 31 august 2011, concluded that overall it has provided a comprehensive framework for environmental policy, during which environmental legislation has been consolidated and completed in a significant way, and that adoption through the co-decision process has increased its legitimacy and helped create a sense of ownership for subsequent policy proposals. the priorities for the seventh programme must now be set, at a time when the environmental challenge is of the utmost importance and is far from being met. by 2050, improving global environmental performance is urgently needed and this requires a commitment to a greener and more sustainable economy in a framework of competitiveness, employment and job creation.
in writing. − the sixth environment action programme has provided a comprehensive framework for environmental policy, during which environmental legislation has been consolidated and supplemented in a significant way. the adoption of the environment action programme through the co-decision process has increased its legitimacy and helped to create a sense of ownership for subsequent policy proposals. however, the present situation as regards the environment is far from satisfactory. scientific data clearly show that we cannot maintain the current situation, as it puts too much pressure on the ability of the planet to support the demand for resources and services linked to ecosystems or to absorb pollution. i therefore consider it important to adopt a seventh environmental action programme which ensures the strengthening of environmental legislation, which addresses environmental policies in a transversal and integrated manner and which has an international dimension in environmental protection.
in writing. − the sixth environment action programme ends on 22 july 2012, so this report takes stock and redefines priorities for the subsequent programme. the report makes positive points, including the advocacy of an appropriate framework to ensure sufficient funding for innovation, research and development; the advocacy of funding for environmental objectives taking into account the protection of biodiversity and forests; efficient and sustainable use of resources, providing the necessary synergy with the life programme; the provision of sufficient resources for the conservation of the natura 2000 network; and the full integration of environmental protection as an important part of the next multiannual financial framework (mff). but as we know, the proposal for a mff under discussion does not guarantee that. some improvements were also proposed in the objectives of the new programme, notably the removal of the mention of the market. citizen responsibility has been relaxed to place more emphasis on producer responsibility. it should be borne in mind that the future environment programme, in addition to a framework to ensure coherence between the various environmental policies and actions, lacks coherence between the objectives proclaimed in the field of the environment and the other sectoral policies, a coherence which does not exist today.
in writing. − a healthy environment and a high level of environmental protection are the conditions for ensuring the quality of life and preserving the stability of ecosystems. environment action programmes have guided the development of eu environmental policy since the early 1970s. they have been an important driving force for the adoption of strong community environmental legislation, particularly in areas such as air, water, waste and climate. environmental protection enhances quality of life, including by protecting ecosystems and their services, halting biodiversity loss, ensuring better air quality, reducing noise, creating jobs and growth, and ensuring the well-being of current and future generations. however, given that the environment is not in a satisfactory state, we must immediately start the seventh environmental action programme.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur when he says that the seventh environment action programme must provide a strong comprehensive framework to ensure coherence. it should ensure that all current 2020 environmental objectives in the different policy areas are included and analysed together and should also provide a clear and ambitious vision for 2050 in order to offer a long-term perspective to all stakeholders. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − environment action programmes aim to define the environmental policy of the european union, playing a central role in the legislative guidance in the environmental areas of air, water, waste and climate. the sixth environment action programme ends in july 2012 and a thorough evaluation and the definition of strategic priorities for the subsequent programme is needed. i agree with the present report that it gives a positive assessment of the action of the sixth environmental programme, but it also considers that many of the objectives set have not been met and should therefore continue to be a priority in the future programme. i believe that the seventh action programme should establish a rigorous environmental policy and be closely aligned with the economic development of nations, set concrete targets for 2020 and define an ambitious long-term vision that will make it possible to achieve a sustainable future and improve the quality of life of the people. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the european union's international role in the area of climate change, efficient and sustainable use of resources, biodiversity, forests and environmental quality needs to be strengthened.
in writing. − the report makes positive points: advocating an 'appropriate framework to ensure sufficient funding' for innovation, research and development; advocating that funding for environmental objectives take into account the protection of biodiversity and forests, an efficient and sustainable use of resources, providing the necessary synergy with the life programme; providing sufficient resources for the conservation of the natura 2000 network; and fully integrating environmental protection as an important part of the next multiannual financial framework (mff). one of the positive changes is the removal of the mention of the market and the responsibility of producers. we reiterate, however, that there is an incompatibility between the economic policies of the european union in general and the stated objectives of environmental protection.
european economies were caught in the almost criminal irresponsibility of the global financial sector when they were already on a downward trend, due in part to changes in the distribution of wealth between the west and emerging economies. we have not questioned the rules of the game and have allowed countries with high social protection systems to be penalized. where we were supposed to have social market economies, we have declining living standards, more inequality and a greater share of the profits of big business in national income at the expense of wages. in this debate on the future of europe, it is important that we defend an alternative of hope for europe, stressing the need for more europe, with a coherent economic approach based on shared responsibility, growth and equality. the management of budgets must be based on public expenditure control, reproductive investment and a fair tax system, with the private sector contributing its fair share to the collective effort, with a total fight against evasion, fraud and tax havens. social justice is now essential to europe's recovery.
in writing. today we celebrate europe day, a european construction project which began more than 50 years ago, based on a pact between sovereign nations determined to share a common destiny and to exercise together an increasing share of their sovereignty. a europe based on common values and seeking to ensure peace, security, human dignity, democracy, justice, solidarity, sustainable development and quality of life for its 500 million citizens. at a time when the crisis is confronting us with new challenges and difficulties, it is important to strengthen the common project because nationalist illusions would lead us to isolation and failure. on the contrary, we must increasingly seek a genuine common voice, restore dignity to the principle of european solidarity, face the problem of population decline and, at the same time, the enormous growth of migratory pressures, combat the ongoing economic crisis, increase the levels of economic growth, ensure the sustainability of the european economy and strengthen the single currency by reducing the high levels of unemployment, with particular emphasis on the younger age group. the europe we want to be proud of is the europe that puts people first, that is not limited to the common market, the europe of the citizens and respect for human rights.
in writing. increasingly, the european union is demonstrating its true nature, the nature of capitalist integration which is only intended to benefit the big economic and financial groups, an integration which satisfies their expansionist drive to conquer new markets, to have easier access to cheap labour and resources, to liberalise areas such as public services in order to pass them into the hands of the private sector. in the face of the crisis caused by capitalism through financial speculation, what solution does the eu have to offer the people? what an imperialist bloc can offer: the increase of the exploitation of labour and the creation of mechanisms that transfer the wealth created by the workers to monopoly capital. the so-called austerity measures are nothing more than that. the direct transfer of wages, pensions, social supports and subsidies, the gigantic profits that the privatized public services and sectors can offer directly into the hands of capital. the workers and the people want a different future for europe, and they have shown this in massive social struggles.
i would like to begin by congratulating mrs niebler on her excellent work and to point out how coincidental it is that on europe day we are debating and tomorrow approving measures which are contrary to the legitimate aspirations of our citizens. the aim of this regulation is to impose limits on mobile phone charges charged to european consumers when roaming, with the overall aim of ending roaming in the european union by 2016. our citizens will benefit from a sharp drop in prices for calls, sms and data. if today there are operators who charge three euros per mega, from july the maximum price they can charge is 70 cents per mega, increasing this amount to 20 cents in 2014. as for incoming calls, the maximum price that can be charged will be eight cents this year and five cents in 2014. in july 2012, a family with two mobile phone users will save, as the commissioner said, two hundred euros on their bill. second benefit: better quality of information for consumers. as of the summer, operators are obliged to inform consumers of the prices charged when they travel outside the european union. until now, the obligation was only within the european area. third advantage: the possibility of more operators entering the market, which means increased competition which will stimulate better services and better prices. finally, in the near future, the consumer may, if he so chooses, have two contracts: one for services in the national territory and the other for services abroad, keeping the same mobile number and having only one invoice. the consumer, our citizen, will also be given the opportunity to contract with any european operator offering him the best price. this report is the perfect example of a people's europe, a europe of freedom of movement and freedom of establishment.
this report states that the european union will now be in a much better position to develop its foreign policy and its national trade agreements with the countries of the southern mediterranean. but it is worth remembering that the nature of the previous regimes has not upset the european union up to now, nor have its governments, which have established such deep relations. the report, following the european commission, advocates the concept of a "plus for plus", i.e. that democratic reforms and individual freedoms should be reflected in a process of economic liberalisation and trade liberalization through the consolidation of the euro-mediterranean free trade area. but is it liberation or pre-colonization? the free trade agreements have only proved to date that they have meant the loss of sovereignty of peoples, the appropriation by multinational companies of natural resources and biodiversity, the increase in external dependence on third countries and the disaster in productive sectors in some member states. what is needed is the establishment of fairer and more equitable economic relations at the service of the people and not free trade agreements which benefit certain economic and financial groups.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, in recent months, more than 70,000 people and some 300 organizations have given a very strong voice to a campaign against seed patenting. this broad movement, anchored in several national campaigns, has drawn attention to the way patent legislation has been applied in the european union, paving the way for the patenting of plants and animals, genetic material, biological processes essential to life. this unacceptable course has led, for example, to the creation of genuine monopolies in production processes in the agricultural sector. two multinationals control and divide the market between themselves at the expense of the ruin of very small and medium-sized producers, the reduction of the diversity of production and the possibilities of choice for consumers. the ethical, social and political implications of this issue are profound. we therefore welcome the citizens and organisations who have been involved in this campaign. it is one thing to invent processes of genetic modification using molecular biology, and quite another to invent the products, the living organisms, that come from these technologies. the existence of intellectual property rights in these organisms is just as unacceptable as the patenting of conventional genetic selection processes, of crossbreeding processes or of the resulting breeding products, such as new plant or animal varieties, or of laboratory-assisted selection processes involving whole genomes. in this respect, this resolution brings some clarity where it was needed.
regional airports and regional aviation, if properly integrated into comprehensive regional development strategies aimed at fully exploiting the endogenous potential of the regions in which they are located, can be an important instrument to support such development by helping to combat regional asymmetries. this requires a proper connection with other modes of transport, such as rail or maritime transport, ensuring conditions for the mobility of people and goods, which take into account essential environmental sustainability criteria. but the development of these services, according to a logic of the prevalence of the public interest, is not compatible with the process of liberalization under way in the sector and with the dogmas of the free market which guide the project of the single european sky and which subject the necessary state intervention and regulation, even in matters relating to security, to sacrosanct free competition. a word about the worrisome deterioration of working conditions in the sector. the ongoing liberalization has been facilitating social dumping by the multinationals in the sector, forcing precarious employment and lowering working conditions. low-cost companies have an indispensable role to play here.
in writing. - i support this report because it advocates more fair trade relations between european producers and world producers who do not respect the same rules as our own producers. according to the study prior to this report, it is concluded that article 9 (5) of council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 of 30 november 2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community (the basic anti-dumping regulation) was in breach of articles 6.10, 9.2 and 18.4 of the wto anti-dumping agreement and article xvi:4 of the wto agreement. article 9 (5) of the basic anti-dumping regulation provides that individual exporting producers in non-market economy countries which do not benefit from market economy treatment in accordance with article 2 (7) (c) of the basic anti-dumping regulation will be subject to a countrywide duty unless such exporters can demonstrate that they meet the conditions for individual treatment set out in article 9 (5) of the basic anti-dumping regulation (rl's finding on article 9 (5) of the basic anti-dumping regulation).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 of 30 november 2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, as i consider it of the utmost importance that the european community's provisions on this matter respect the obligations it has assumed before the wto.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which proposes to implement a legislative proposal recommended by the world trade organisation's dispute settlement body so that european legislation is in line with what has been agreed with the wto.
in writing. − this legislative proposal, following the european communities final anti-dumping measures on certain iron or steel fasteners from china proceeding, aims to implement the recommendations of the world trade organisation dispute settlement body and to set a reasonable timeframe for this to occur, as agreed between the european union and china on 19 january 2012. i believe that it is the union's interest to resolve this conflict and to bring its legislation into line with the agreements concluded and in force within the wto.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr vital moreira, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 of 30 november 2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european union (eu). this proposed amendment follows the adoption by the dispute settlement body (dsb) of the world trade organization (wto) of the report of the appellate body on the european communities definitive anti-dumping measures on certain iron or steel fasteners from china case, which pointed to the existence of non-conformities between regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 and the wto anti-dumping agreement. given that on 19 january 2012 the eu and china agreed on the deadlines for implementing the recommendations and decisions of the dsb and that the committee on international trade has already adopted this draft resolution under the simplified procedure method, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the proposed amendment to this regulation, which the committee on international trade decided to adopt under the simplified procedure, aims to incorporate into eu law, and in particular into the basic anti-dumping regulation in question, the decision of 28 july 2011 of the dispute settlement body of the world trade organisation (wto). the eu-china dispute arose from the fact that eu legislation discriminates against individual exporting producers in 'non-market economy countries' which is contrary to the rules of the wto itself and in particular its anti-dumping agreement. it means... the provisions requiring, for example, that in the exporting producer companies in question 'the majority of the capital is actually held by private individuals' are thus eliminated. although this report is aimed at an adaptation which seeks to bring eu legislation into line with the rules of the wto - an organisation whose actions and principles we disagree with - it is nevertheless significant and interesting to see how, in this case, the eu surpasses the wto itself in commercial glamour and neoliberal fundamentalism.
in writing. - european companies have to comply with a number of requirements imposed by european legislation, which often puts them in an unfair competitive situation when confronted with other countries outside the european community, which practice various types of dumping. with the adoption of this report, companies importing from countries which do not respect the rules and practice various types of dumping will be forced to pay higher tariffs at europe's borders. this is a very important and necessary measure to protect our companies against serious distortions of competition. the industry in my country, portugal, suffers from this type of unfair competition, particularly with the import of textiles from pakistan, a situation i have been warning about for a long time.
in writing. − given the importance of ensuring legal certainty, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 of 30 november 2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, so that the european community's provisions on this matter respect the obligations assumed under the wto.
in writing. - this report calls for greater control and protection against dumped imports from countries outside the european community. due to the import of certain iron or steel fasteners from china, it was found that the basic anti-dumping regulation of the council was not in conformity with the provisions of certain provisions of the wto anti-dumping agreement. in order to facilitate the eu's compliance with the deadline for implementing wto recommendations and decisions, more specifically through its dispute settlement body (dsb), the international trade committee approved the draft settlement under the simplified procedure. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'commercial'. this regulation adopts the legislation of the european union in the light of russia's accession to the wto. the european commission estimates that this regulation is equivalent to approximately eur 107 million per year in exports and that the competitiveness of the eu steel sector will increase due to the reduction of export duties. the application of this legislation will thus bring economic opportunities for european producers, which is essential at a time of crisis and especially in a market which is close to us geographically.
in writing. - restrictions on russian steel imports no longer made sense after russia joined the wto. the lifting of these restrictions will also allow trade with russia to increase, in particular the export of european steel and iron to that country. any failure by either party to comply with the applicable wto rules may be resolved through existing wto dispute settlement mechanisms. for these reasons i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposes to lift the restrictions on imports of certain steel products from russia. the current application of the restrictions no longer makes sense now that russia has joined the world trade organization.
in writing. - russia's accession to the world trade organisation means that the tariff quota for imports into the european union of steel originating in russia will be abolished. its maintenance would imply a breach of wto rules by the union and would make it subject to legal action by russia. further liberalisation of access to the russian market can benefit the union and should be extended to other areas of trade within the wto framework, which is considered to be the best means of ensuring the viability of a multilateral trading system.
in writing. − the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and russia, of the other part, entered into force on 1 december 1997 and led to the establishment of an agreement on trade in certain steel products originating in the russian federation, in accordance with council regulation (ec) no 1342/2007. this report, by robert sturdy, deals with a new proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing the above regulation and on the administration of certain restrictions on imports of certain steel products from the russian federation. although russian steel imports to the eu are significant, representing 24% of total imports of steel products, the acp provided that if russia acceded to the world trade organisation (wto) it would have to be withdrawn and the quota abolished. so, without questioning the interest in strengthening eu-russia trade relations, i agree with the rapporteur that the wto remains the best guarantor of a rules-based multilateral trading system and therefore i voted in favour.
in writing. − the european union and the russian federation have since 2007 established an agreement on trade in certain steel products, concerning the administration of certain restrictions on imports of certain steel products originating in russia. however, as russia became a member of the wto in december 2011, the european union lost the right to apply the above mentioned quota. the maintenance of this regulation and the consequent preservation of the quota for imports of steel products would constitute a violation of wto rules and would expose the eu to legal action by russia. the eu must therefore revoke the agreement currently in force. the rapporteur believes that the entry of the russian federation into the wto will bring benefits to the eu as it will have more liberal access to the russian market. the report is essentially a technical adaptation, but the philosophy and the guidelines underlying it are those of compliance with the wto rules and the international trade vision which inspires it, with which we disagree.
in writing. − with russia's accession to the multilateral trading system based on wto rules, the eu could benefit from more liberal access to the russian market. the increase in additional exports could amount to approximately eur 107 million per year in the iron and steel sector alone. from now on, even if there are any obstacles to bilateral trade in steel products, they will be minimal and will apply only in the exclusive domain of wto rules governing such matters as tariffs, applicable trade defence measures, technical standards, specific customs procedures, etc. with this accession, greater control and careful removal of any remaining trade and investment barriers by russia is required. it is my conviction that the wto remains the best guarantor of a rules-based multilateral trading system; i therefore hope that both its new member, russia, and the eu will fulfil all their wto commitments. i would also like to see the eu-russia trade relationship developed with a view to full compliance with the provisions agreed jointly in various bilateral agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the lifting of restrictions on russian steel imports, since they no longer make sense after russia's accession to the wto. the lifting of these restrictions will also allow trade with russia to increase, in particular the export of european steel and iron to that country. any failure by either party to comply with the applicable wto rules may be resolved through existing wto dispute settlement mechanisms.
in writing. − under the 1997 partnership and cooperation agreement between the european community and the russian federation, the agreement on trade in certain steel products was concluded in 2007. this agreement was implemented in the eu in the form of a regulation which, in addition to fixing a quantitative limit on steel imports, also laid down the condition that if the russian federation acceded to the wto before the expiry of the agreement, the agreement would have to be terminated. due to russia's accession to the multilateral system based on wto rules, the maintenance of the regulation in european law and consequent preservation of the quota for the import of steel products would constitute a breach of wto rules and would expose the eu to possible legal action by russia. however, the eu can expect to benefit from more liberal access to the russian market, which would stimulate competition and subsequently lower consumer prices. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − as russia became a member of the wto in december 2011, the european union lost the right to apply the agreement on trade in certain steel products, concerning the administration of certain restrictions on imports of certain steel products originating in russia. the maintenance of this regulation and the consequent preservation of the quota for imports of steel products would constitute a violation of wto rules and would expose the eu to legal action by russia. the eu must therefore revoke the agreement currently in force. we do not agree with the political principles underlying the report, namely the wto rules and the whole philosophy of international trade that is implied.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. today, virtually all users consult only the electronic version of eu legal acts. the fact that electronic versions of legal acts are not legally binding is in itself unacceptable and creates uncertainty as to the exact content of eu legal acts currently available in the eur-lex database. furthermore, consulting the printed version of the official journal is a time-consuming and costly process and few users do so. the reform will therefore enhance legal certainty and reduce the costs of access for citizens and businesses. all these reforms should be warmly welcomed in the eu. a less bureaucratic, more facilitated and more accessible european union will only promote economic progress.
in writing. − it is essential that european citizens have simple and reliable access to the legal acts of the european union. the electronic version of the official journal allows this kind of access and is a crucial information tool of the european union. consulting the printed version of the official journal is a time-consuming and costly process which few users resort to. the circumstance that electronic versions of legal acts are not legally binding has to be overcome as it creates uncertainty as to the exact content of eu legal acts. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it contributes to legal certainty and to reducing the cost of access to legal acts of the european union for citizens and businesses.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider that the council text presupposes a positive reform of the way the official journal of the european union is published, contributing to improving the access of european citizens to eu legislation.
in writing. − the present proposal aims to make the electronic edition of the official journal of the eu (oj) as an official version authentic, up-to-date and complete. these amendments are purely technical in nature and, in my view, welcome. the official and authentic nature of the electronic edition of the oj will improve citizens' access to eu legislation, increase legal certainty and reduce access costs for citizens and businesses, as online consultation of an official and authentic edition will always be free of charge.
in writing. − the transmission of data and the circulation of official information via the internet and the environmental awareness of the need to reduce the felling of trees for the paper industry have led many companies and public bodies to reduce their paper-based communications by opting for electronic means. however, as regards the legal validity of these notifications, several voices expressed reservations because there was no legislation to allow this. a 2007 judgment of the european court of justice states that rights are not enforceable and obligations cannot be enforced on the basis of the electronic version of the oj (official journal of the european union). to overcome this problem, the commission put forward a proposal on 4 april 2011 to increase legal certainty by broadening access to eu legislation and allowing the use of the electronic edition of the oj as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version by anyone. i voted in favour of this proposal for a council regulation on the electronic publication of the eu oj, as the amendments are technical in nature, they increase legal certainty and allow citizens better access to eu legal acts.
in writing. − this report proposes that the electronic edition of the official journal (oj) of the eu should be the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version, as opposed to the printed edition which would have legal value only in exceptional and temporary cases of unforeseeable disruption of electronic publication. the proposed regulatory amendment now strengthens legal certainty. today, most users only consult the electronic version of eu legal acts. the rapporteur notes that the fact that electronic versions of legal acts are not legally binding is itself problematic and creates uncertainty as to the exact content of eu legal acts currently available in the eur-lex database. in addition, consulting the printed version of the official journal is a time-consuming and costly process, and few users do so. the proposal also has an undeniable environmental advantage. while positive, this amendment does not remove the need to continue improving access of the entire population to relevant official public documentation, taking into account the difficulties and limitations that still persist at this level.
in writing. − this recommendation, by allowing anyone to use the electronic edition of the official journal of the eu (oj) as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version, enhances legal certainty and security. it also promotes greater access to legislation, allowing citizens better access to european law and, consequently, to the european union itself, thus reinforcing european citizenship. i voted in favour of all of this.
in writing. - i fully support this new regulation, as it strengthens legal certainty and provides better access for citizens to legal acts of the european union by making electronic publication equivalent to a legally valid publication of the official journal. this text promotes better public access to european legislation, recognising the important role played today by new information technologies, including the internet, in the dissemination of european law. this innovation also introduces significant savings and reduces the environmental impact of the activities of the european institutions.
in writing. − transparency is a key value for the success of the european project and for the involvement of citizens in this cause. it is essential that european citizens have quick and reliable access to the legal acts of the european union. the electronic version of the official journal allows this kind of access and is a crucial information tool of the european union. in order to make progress in this process, it is important to overcome the fact that electronic versions of legal acts are not legally binding. this creates uncertainty as to the exact content of the legal acts of the european union. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because of the facts which have been pointed out and because i consider that this regulation is intended to contribute to legal certainty and to reducing the costs of access to legal acts of the european union for citizens and businesses.
in writing. - the report deals mainly with the proposal by the committee on legal affairs that electronic publication should be equivalent to a legally valid publication of the official journal, and that only in exceptional and temporary cases of unforeseeable disruption to electronic publication, only the printed edition should have legal value. it should be noted that the background to the intention to make this amendment dates from 2007, when the cj gave a judgment declaring that the rights are not enforceable and that the obligations cannot be enforced on the basis of the electronic version of the oj. this is a positive reform of the way the oj is published, as it increases legal certainty and provides better access for citizens to legal acts of the european union, especially since virtually all users nowadays consult only the electronic version of eu legal acts. furthermore, consulting the printed version of the official journal is a time-consuming and costly process and few users do so. the reform will therefore enhance legal certainty and reduce the costs of access for citizens and businesses.
in writing. − this report proposes changes of a purely technical nature, so that the electronic edition of the official journal of the eu will now be the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version, as opposed to the printed edition which will have legal value only in exceptional and temporary cases of unforeseeable disruption of electronic publication. this new procedure could be positive in terms of ensuring greater public access to information, in this case to legislation produced by the eu.

in writing. − this report, by cecilia wilkström, concerns the request for defence of the immunity and privileges of corneliu vadim tudor, mep, lodged on 14 april 2011 following a case brought against him by the public prosecutor's office before the high court of cassation and justice of romania. mr tudor is charged with contempt of court, conduct contrary to public morals and disturbing the peace for threatening a judicial officer and police officers when they were trying to enforce a court decision in connection with proceedings for the eviction of the romania mare party from its premises in bucharest. the rapporteur considers that the circumstances surrounding the dismissal of the romania mare party are exclusively in the sphere of civil and criminal matters and therefore have no relation to the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament and that, in these terms, articles 8 and 9 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union cannot be invoked. in this connection, and in the light of the report by the committee on legal affairs, i am voting in favour of the report recommending that the immunity and privileges of corneliu vadim tudor should not be upheld.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. however, the facts of the case relate to criminal proceedings in which the member is accused of threatening a judicial officer and some police officers, of committing acts of violence against them, insulting them and in general attempting to obstruct the execution of a judicial decision in the context of the eviction of the romania mare party from its premises in bucharest on 4 january 2011. in these criminal proceedings corneliu vadim tudor is accused of contempt of court, of behaviour contrary to public morals and of disturbing the peace. the expulsion of the romania mare party and the circumstances surrounding it are in fact civil and criminal matters respectively which have no direct and obvious connection with the exercise of the duties of member of the european parliament, and i therefore voted in favour of not defending the immunity of corneliu vadim tudor.
in writing. - mr tudor has asked the european parliament to uphold his parliamentary immunity in the context of the proceedings brought against him by the public prosecutor's office before the high court of cassation and justice of romania. considering that the circumstances of the case at hand, the eviction of the romania mare party from its premises, are a matter of civil and criminal law without a direct and obvious connection with the exercise of the functions of a member of the european parliament, i voted, following the opinion of the juri committee, for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of vadim tudor.

in writing. − regional aviation can play a crucial role in achieving free movement within the eu by providing better connectivity for citizens, businesses and products from different regions of the eu, especially in the case of the most remote regions with the least access or the outermost regions, thus contributing significantly to the territorial cohesion and social and economic development of these regions. in particular, in a time of economic crisis, if it is important to avoid a proliferation of regional airports that would not meet either efficiency or sustainability criteria, it is also essential to maintain and strengthen existing links with regions affected by less favourable geographical conditions and to promote better links between regional airports and neighbouring cities, which could bring clear benefits in terms of reducing congestion at central airports. it is essential that the necessary measures be taken to improve the operational and economic efficiency of regional airports and to improve the conditions offered to passengers using these infrastructures and services. a clear and concrete definition of the concept of regional airport should be adopted and the criteria for obtaining grants and public funds should be set out in a clear and transparent manner.

in writing. − regional airports, when properly located, with safety conditions and a network of connections to other means of transport, play a key role in territorial, economic and social cohesion within the european union. it is easy to understand that not every city can have an airport. however, there are regions, especially the outermost, peripheral and/or island regions, where these airports are the only effective means of connecting these regions to the rest of europe. the eu's policy in this area should be to promote the provision of rigorous public services - with a focus on safety - to prevent the proliferation of regional airports, to accelerate the implementation of the air traffic management system (sesar) and the clean sky initiative and the implementation of the single european sky legislation, to create an intermodal system that makes the market more competitive and to promote regional development. i voted in favour of this report because, in the context of the economic crisis and the efforts to consolidate the budget we are going through, it appeals to common sense to achieve a balance between the social and territorial needs of a given region and the need for competitiveness and financial balance of each airport.
in writing. - this report recognises the importance of regional airports and aviation for the economic development of the regions, especially (but not exclusively) in the case of the outermost regions. it also recognises, to some extent, the role of public policies in promoting this development. but it also soon defends the supremacy of the market, reducing the scope for manoeuvre of the states and even calling into question their intervention and regulation - which are essential in the organisation of these services and in their articulation with a logic of public interest and promotion of development. the defence of the single european sky and the underlying approach to liberalising the sector are very revealing. the apology for sacrosanct free competition and the resulting limitations on state intervention is repeatedly mentioned throughout the report. and even safety issues are subject to the principle of free competition - measures in this area are limited to respecting this principle (paragraph 37). it is a view which we cannot accept for the reasons we mentioned during the debate. some remarks on the role of low-cost airlines and some positive proposals in this area do not erase the more negative aspects of this report.

in writing. - the report under consideration, by mr boguslaw liberadzki, deals with the discharge for implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section i european parliament. the court of auditors' audit of the ep's administrative expenditure in 2010 concluded that all institutions had satisfactorily complied with the supervisory and control procedures required by the financial regulation. while i believe that there is a need to improve the transparency rules so that it is very clear which institutions, whether natural, legal or public, are benefiting from eu funds, and whereas the secretary-general certified on 16 june 2011 that the ep budget has been correctly implemented and that the principles of sound financial management have been respected, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the rapporteur considers that there is sufficient assurance that the european parliament's budget has been implemented in accordance with the principles of sound financial management. the report does, however, make some specific criticisms and suggestions which deserve our general agreement, notwithstanding some pointed differences - which we noted during the votes - and a different view on some of the issues included in the resolution. the references to savings made possible by a greater rationalisation of missions between the three workplaces (brussels, luxembourg and strasbourg); the delays and considerable cost increases of the new ep visitor centre; the costs and lack of clarity associated with the house of european history project; and travel agency costs are noteworthy. the rapporteur proposes abolishing prizes such as the lux prize for cinema, and also refers to the end of the journalism prize, but says nothing about the future of the sakharov prize - which is the prize with the highest expenditure value and which since 2009 has increased by €352 348.
in writing. − all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and by all bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as assessed by the audits known to us, we can say that the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds made available and are meeting the objectives proposed. it is in this sense that the vote in favour of the report on discharge to the general budget of the eu is appropriate.
in writing. − having regard to the court of auditors' audit of administrative expenditure in 2010, which concluded that all institutions had satisfactorily implemented the supervisory and control systems required by the financial regulation and that 93% of the 58 payments audited were free from material error, and to the fact that the secretary-general of the european parliament, on 16 june 2011, certified that he was sufficiently satisfied that the budget of the european parliament had been implemented in accordance with the principles of sound financial management and that the control system provided the necessary guarantees as regards the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, i voted in favour of the clearance of the accounts presented by the european commission and thus discharge the accounts for 2010. in fact, by giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament declares that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and terminates its budget. if the implementation did not comply with the existing rules, the european parliament could refuse or postpone discharge, which did not happen in the present case where the eu accounts for the financial year 2010 were discharged, section i european parliament.
in writing. - i support this report, considering that the main concern should be the entry of the european development funds in the budget of the european union, since, as they are not integrated, it is not possible to analyse them fully, and in the same way as other expenditure. the message should be the call to the european commission to integrate the budget of these funds into the discharge report. the principle of transparency should never be imposed on the european union, which aims to be a political bloc promoting a highly advanced democracy and setting an example to the world.

in writing. - the european development funds (edf) remain the main instrument available to the union for the purpose of providing development aid to the acp states and, despite the repeated requests of this parliament, they are still not integrated into the commission's budget. it is therefore urgent that it be integrated into the union budget in order to allow for greater democratic control, accountability and transparency of funding. it should be noted that the court of auditors considers that coding errors are still very frequent and although they did not have a significant influence on the 2010 annual accounts, they may affect the reliability of europeaid's financial management data. the commission should therefore continue its efforts to improve europeaid's control and supervision systems in order to achieve positive results in terms of accountability, efficiency and effectiveness.
in writing. - the report under consideration, drawn up by martin ehrenhauser, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the budget for the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds (edfs) for the financial year 2010. the edf is the european union's main financial instrument for development cooperation with the african, caribbean and pacific states. i welcome the good financial execution of the edf, especially in terms of gross payments and the commitment rate of close to 50%, but i cannot help but express my concern, in the light of the court of auditors' report, about the way in which budget support payments were processed in the first half of 2011. in these terms, and in the light of the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinions of the committees concerned, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - the report criticises the fact that the edf - the european development fund, the eu's main financial instrument for development cooperation - is not integrated into the eu budget. the rapporteur calls on the commission to propose including the edf in the eu budget when the next multiannual financial framework is discussed - which is not the case with the commission's current proposal. this amendment has been long sought, providing the eu's development cooperation and aid policy with more robust and predictable means, as well as being more easily scrutinised by the institutions responsible for approving the budget. however, we do not follow the references to the european external action service, considering that it should "fully exercise its political role by actively participating in the development of the political objectives of the beneficiary countries (...) ". nor can we accept paragraphs which say that 'stable and effective trade relations in accordance with the principles of the wto are crucial' for the social and economic development of developing countries, calling on the commission to resolve outstanding disputes over the economic partnership and free trade agreements between the eu and the acp region.

in writing. − a clear and coherent legal framework for the protection of personal data is essential to ensure that every individual can have his or her fundamental rights and freedoms, including his or her right to privacy, respected throughout the eu. the european data protection supervisor is the independent body with supervisory powers whose primary objective is to ensure that the community institutions and bodies respect the right to privacy and data protection when processing personal data and developing new policies. in practice, the activities of the authority can be divided into three main strands: supervision, consultation and cooperation. it is therefore essential that it has sufficient resources to carry out its mandate in the most appropriate way. i supported this report on the basis of the court of auditors' findings that the accounts of the european data protection supervisor for payments and other expenditure for the year ended 31 december 2010 as a whole are free from material error and that the systems for the supervision and control of administrative and other expenditure have been effective in ensuring the regularity of payments.

in writing. - i welcome the conclusions of the court of auditors' audit, which states in its annual report that the audit found no material errors. i support the report in suggesting that the edps should prepare annual budgets corresponding to its needs (since in 2010 only 75% of title 1 was used) and that it should strive for better budget implementation in the future.
in writing. − due to information highways, citizens' personal and professional data circulate vertiginously in the corridors of the internet. the european data protection supervisor (edps), established in 2001, aims to ensure that all eu institutions and bodies respect the right to privacy of individuals when using their personal data. the report under examination, drawn up by inés ayala sender, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section ix european data protection supervisor. the court of auditors, in its 2010 report, concluded that the payments for the year ended 31 december 2010 were free from errors. the recommendations of the court of auditors and the commission for the financial year 2009 had also been implemented. following these recommendations, a number of improvements were made, particularly in recruitment. therefore, and taking into account the opinion of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, i am voting in favour of this report to give the edps discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for the year 2010.

in writing. − the report under review, by monica luisa macovei, is on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european union agencies for the financial year 2010: performance, financial management and control of the eu agencies. the european union, in order to support the member states and their citizens, has set up specialised and decentralised agencies to respond to europe's territorial dimension and to meet new technical, scientific and legal competences. the number of eu agencies has increased exponentially from 3 in 2000 to 24 in 2011, and their costs have almost doubled from 2007 to 2010. i welcome the establishment and work of the interinstitutional working group on agencies, whose objective is to review their role, position, structure, operation, supervision and management. i agree with the rapporteur that in the crisis we are living in, we need to be sure that the almost €1.7 billion that the agencies cost every year is absolutely necessary and justified by improving the quality of life of eu citizens.
