in writing. - the report under review, by monica luisa macovei, deals with the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european environment agency, eea, for the financial year 2010. the eea, which was set up in 1993, currently has 32 members: the 27 member states of the european union plus norway, switzerland, liechtenstein, iceland and turkey. its aim is to help the eu and national governments make informed decisions on the environment. the court of auditors, in its report on the accounts of the eea, considered that it had obtained reasonable assurance that the annual accounts for the financial year 2010 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. i welcome the high levels of budget implementation in terms of committed appropriations (100%) and payment appropriations (90.75%) and, while i understand the need to improve its performance, in particular in the inclusion of measurable objectives and indicators, i am voting against this report, as i believe that, as with other agencies, the executive director of the eea should also be given a discharge for the implementation of its budget for the year 2010, in accordance with the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.
in writing. − we support the rapporteur's position to postpone the discharge to the european environment agency (eea) for the financial year 2010. we believe that the conflicts of interest involving senior officials of the agency, as well as the uncertainties about the real value of the reports produced by the agency, should be clarified. these conflicts arise from the accumulation of management positions in organisations with projects funded by the eea. we also support the call for greater transparency in the prevention and fight against conflicts of interest. some of the proposals made by the rapporteur are in this direction, such as the proposal to publish the declarations of interests of the eea's senior officials on its website.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as can be seen from the audits that have been carried out, the institutions concerned are using the funds allocated correctly and are meeting the objectives set. in this particular case, the court of auditors has some doubts about the performance of the european environment agency. it is in this sense that i am voting in favour of postponing the discharge for the implementation of the agency's budget.
in writing. - i would point out the conflicts of interest identified in the european parliament's resolution and hope that the doubts raised will be cleared up. on the basis of these assumptions, i voted in favour of approving the accounts presented by the european commission, thus giving discharge to the 2010 accounts of the european environment agency.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that six very important recommendations of the sai still need to be implemented and that three of these recommendations have already been postponed for another 12 months. in particular, to stress that these delays concern the following aspects: information security management, contract renewal process and transparency of the decision-making process and classification and archiving policy; therefore, this report calls on the authority to address these shortcomings as quickly as possible and to inform the discharge authorities of the results obtained.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 2010 discharge: european food safety authority, because i believe that this agency carries out vital work to strengthen food safety in the eu. it is also important to acknowledge the efforts made to address issues of potential conflict of interest.
in writing. - the report under review, by monica luisa macovei, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2010. efsa was established with the aim of improving food safety across the european union by ensuring a high level of protection for consumers so that they have confidence in european food products. it therefore plays a role throughout the food chain, from the safety of food for animals intended for human consumption to plant protection and plant health. the court of auditors, in its report on the accounts of efsa, considered that it had obtained reasonable assurance that the annual accounts for the financial year 2010 were reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. therefore, despite the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, and taking into account the recommendations of the ombudsman, i am voting in favour of this report to postpone the discharge to the executive director of easa for the implementation of its budget for the year 2010.
in writing. − we support the rapporteur's position to postpone the discharge to the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2010. we consider that the reporting of possible conflicts of interest and in particular a 'turn-key case' mentioned by the european ombudsman in his annual report are sufficient grounds for requesting a deferral of discharge until these cases are fully clarified. the report 'stresses that the ombudsman concludes that the authority had not carried out a full assessment of the alleged potential conflict of interest and asked the authority to improve the application of its rules and procedures in future revolving door cases; furthermore, underlines that the ombudsman also indicated that negotiations by an incumbent staff member regarding a future job that could represent revolving door situations would in itself constitute a conflict of interest and recommended that the authority strengthen its rules and procedures accordingly; requests the authority to inform the discharge authority of the concrete measures taken and the respective deadlines, in order to deal appropriately with the ombudsman's findings. for these reasons we voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report by approving the closure of the accounts of the european institute for gender equality for the financial year 2010. despite my vote in favour of granting discharge, i would like to make it clear that i do not support a possible merger of this institute with the fundamental rights agency of the european union on the grounds of cost reduction. the work carried out by the institute is recent and has enormous potential for the promotion of gender equality in the european union, and it is therefore necessary to maintain its autonomy.
in writing. − social and legal equality between the sexes, which, while different, are complementary, is essential for a balanced society. efforts to achieve this are worthwhile and should be followed up by the european union. i note that the office has not yet communicated the results of the ex ante evaluation it commissioned to the discharge authority.
in writing. − equality between men and women has shown significant progress in recent times and is considered a fundamental right. the report under examination, drawn up by monica luisa macovei, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european institute for gender equality (eige) for the financial year 2010. the eig is a european agency whose objective is to support the member states and the european institutions in promoting equality between men and women. to do this, it collects and analyses data, develops methodologies and promotes the sharing of good practice. as 2010 is the first year of the eig's operation, i welcome the fact that the court of auditors, in its report on the eig's accounts, has declared all financial transactions to be legal and regular, and i hope that its performance will continue to improve despite the difficulties the eu is facing. in view of the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i therefore vote in favour of this report, in order to give the director of the european institute for gender equality a discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for the year 2010.
in writing. - in times of crisis, such as the one the peoples are currently experiencing, it is essential that the rights won by workers and peoples are defended. these rights must be strengthened, because the only way to overcome the predicament that the crisis of the capitalist system has brought us is through progress and social justice, by ensuring a fair distribution of wealth among those who create it. equality between women and men is an essential element and objective of this struggle. unfortunately, it's still a long way from being reached. the way forward must be to combat inequalities and to strengthen the conditions under which this struggle is carried out, on all fronts. we therefore disagree with the rapporteur's proposal to merge or abolish the european institute for gender equality. it is necessary to strengthen working conditions on this front, particularly as regards the recruitment of qualified staff, to ensure that it fully functions and continues to follow the principles for which it was created.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as can be seen from the audits that have been carried out, the institutions concerned are using the funds allocated correctly and are meeting the objectives set. it is in this sense that i vote in favour of the report by the european institute for gender equality.
in writing. − the european institute for gender equality acquired administrative and financial autonomy on 15 june 2010. in a time of economic crisis and austerity, it is vital that the institute is economical in its expenditure without compromising the good performance of its important mission. the first audit of the internal audit service will be carried out in 2012. in this context, and on the basis of the council's recommendation and the reports of the european court of auditors, i voted in favour of approving the accounts presented by the european commission, thus giving discharge to the 2010 accounts of the european institute for gender equality.
in writing. - in times of crisis, such as the one people are currently experiencing, it is not only essential that workers' rights are defended, but also urgent that they are strengthened: only the path of progress and social justice can put an end to the swamp situation that the capitalist system has brought us. in this context, equality between women and men is an urgent objective, but unfortunately it is still a long way off. the way forward must be to combat these inequalities and to strengthen the conditions under which this fight is carried out, on all fronts. we are therefore against the proposal to merge or dissolve the european institute for gender equality and in favour of strengthening the conditions, particularly as regards the recruitment of qualified staff, which enable it to function as it is intended to.

in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament declares that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and terminates its budget. if, on the other hand, the institution has not complied with the existing rules, the european parliament may refuse or postpone discharge. the members of the european parliament, on the recommendation of the council, take decisions on the basis of the reports of the european court of auditors, and the european parliament may make recommendations to the european commission to take action in a particular direction. in this particular situation, i voted in favour of the decision to postpone the granting of discharge to the executive director of the european medicines agency for the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2010.

in writing. the aim of this joint venture is to modernise the european air traffic management system and to pool the community's research and development efforts under the sesar (european new generation air traffic management system) project. the safety of citizens who increasingly use the services of airlines and of their employees justifies a particular effort to find the best solutions for managing this type of traffic, as well as the monitoring and comparison of the methodologies already applied in the various member states, with a view to the joint adoption of best practices and safe, cost-effective and innovative solutions. i therefore recognise the importance of the european commission and the member states improving the effectiveness of the application of the single european sky regulations in order to increase the effectiveness of investments in the sesar project.

in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament declares that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and terminates its budget. if, on the other hand, the implementation has not complied with the existing rules, the european parliament may refuse or postpone discharge. the members of the european parliament, on the recommendation of the council, decide on the basis of the reports of the european court of auditors, and the european parliament may make recommendations to the european commission to take action on certain matters. as regards the discharge for 2010, i am voting in favour of the discharge presented by the european commission.
in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament declares that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and terminates its budget. if, on the other hand, the institution has not complied with the existing rules, the european parliament may refuse or postpone discharge. the members of the european parliament, on the recommendation of the council, take decisions on the basis of the reports of the european court of auditors, and the european parliament may make recommendations to the european commission to take action in a particular direction. in this particular situation, i voted in favour.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the 2010 annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests fight against fraud, as it alerts the commission to irregularities and cases of suspected fraud. the report calls on the commission to exercise its right of legislative initiative by requiring member states to provide all information on the level of irregularities, so that the scale of fraud in the different countries can be reliably determined.
in writing. − fraud is voluntary irregular behaviour which constitutes a criminal offence, and an irregularity means a breach of a rule. it should therefore be severely penalized in order to limit its occurrence as much as possible. i find it serious that in 2010 irregularity reports increased in all sectors except for pre-accession funds and traditional own resources. the report says that in 2010 the financial impact of irregularities in the area of expenditure increased to €1.8 billion. this means that there are still funds that are being misused and mismanaged, and therefore measures must be taken to hold member states more accountable for irregularities and to improve the mechanisms for preventing and detecting irregularities. these are worrying data that lack urgent and effective corrective and punitive measures, such as immediate suspension of payments in cases of fraud and effective sanctions in cases of misuse of funds.
in writing. - the report in question, by zigmantas balčytis, deals with the protection of the european union's financial interests fight against fraud - annual report 2010, more specifically the topic of the risk of double funding in cohesion policy, as previously agreed between the commission and the member states (ms). according to the report, during 2010 irregularity reports increased in all sectors except for pre-accession funds and traditional own resources. despite the implementation of an irregularity management system (ims) managed by the european anti-fraud office (olaf), some member states do not update their data, which reduces the effectiveness of this system. it is therefore necessary for the commission to adopt the necessary measures, if necessary a legislative initiative, in order to be able to know in good time the level of irregularities and fraud in the member states. because the commission's annual reports cannot be based on inaccurate data, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the report notes that in 2010, the overall financial impact of irregularities detected by control systems amounted to eur 2193 million, an increase on 2009. according to the ect, control systems are only partially effective in ensuring the regularity of payment. the ecj considers that in most cases the member state authorities had sufficient information to have detected and corrected at least some of the errors before the payments were made. so there is room for improvement. the main criticism of the rapporteur is the lack of reliable statistical data on the extent of fraud and corruption, as well as on tax and customs evasion and the misuse of community funds by organised crime (data which the european parliament has repeatedly requested from the commission). this means that the commission is unable to assess the real extent of irregularities and fraud in the eu, and confuses the two. despite the positive aspects of the report, some issues are not sufficiently addressed and some of the proposed solutions lack greater context and some caution. we did not support the proposals concerning the suspension of payments and the application of sanctions to the member states.

in writing. − this report contains the latest information on irregularities and suspected fraud reported by the member states. there was an increase in the number of irregularity reports in 2010 in all sectors except for pre-accession funds and traditional own resources. the fact that the irregularities management system (ims) is not being used by all member states has led the european parliament to urge the commission to take all necessary measures to ensure that member states comply with their reporting obligations and to provide reliable and comparable data on the level of irregularities and fraud in the member states. i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is essential that all the necessary data should be made available in good time so that the true scale of fraud in the member states can be determined.

in writing. - the mobile phone has become a fundamental and irreplaceable means of communication for millions of citizens. today, in addition to calling and texting, mobile phones are also a preferred means of accessing the internet and data services. however, despite the geographical mobility and the free movement of persons and workers guaranteed by the treaties, most citizens continue to switch off their mobile phones when abroad in order not to have to pay roaming costs. the excessive cost of roaming and the consequent reduced use of mobile phones outside the home country do not benefit european consumers or the european economy. that is why it is urgent that measures be taken to bring down roaming charges. i therefore vote in favour of this report and congratulate the rapporteur on her work.
in writing. - information technologies have taken over our everyday lives. just look at the passers-by on a busy street in any european capital or watch students entering and/or leaving schools. young and old alike can't live without their mobile phones, their ipads, their smartphones, pens, tablets, etc. data transfers are a constant and the market is constantly evolving. it is essential that european citizens, whether at home or when travelling, can access these services quickly and at competitive prices. the cost of data transmission, especially when moving from one member state to another, is now almost prohibitive. we are in a europe without frontiers, building a single market. it is essential that this market also applies to new information technologies. we all have to win: consumers and businesses. i welcome the creation of a roaming regulation which will limit the tariffs of operators outside their member states, making it possible to hire foreign operators, with significant savings in the cost of roaming. i voted in favour of this report by mrs angelika niebler because i believe that the recommendations will promote mobility in the european area, benefit consumers and make businesses more competitive.
in writing. - we certainly appreciate the intention to reduce the price of mobile communications for roaming services, whose cost is now very high and unjustified. there are, however, other aspects of this proposal for a regulation which cannot be dismissed lightly in the face of this wish. the liberalization proposed for the sector, with the completion of the internal market in this field, will inevitably lead to the concentration of supply in a few large transnational operators. the consequences of this monopolistic concentration are known in other sectors and, here too, foreseeable: price concertation and even price increases at later stages of the process; pressure on the working conditions of workers in the sector. we also express some concern about the evolution of the use of the radio spectrum, a public good of great importance, limited, whose increasing occupation (and domination by private interests) lacks a multi-level impact assessment, which has been neglected.

in writing. − this report on roaming on public mobile communications networks in the union contains measures that meet the legitimate wishes of our citizens. the central issue in this proposal for a regulation is the imposition of limits on mobile phone charges charged to european consumers when roaming. this is the first step in a process which ultimately aims to end roaming in the european union by 2016. another essential aspect has to do with the quality of the information provided to consumers. as of the summer, operators are obliged to inform consumers of the prices charged when they travel outside the european union. in addition, the consumer may, if he so wishes, have two contracts: one for services in the national territory and the other for services abroad, keeping the same mobile number and having only one invoice. finally, it is advocated that operators should be able to enter the market more easily, which means increased competition which in turn will stimulate better services and better prices for the consumer. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on exports and imports of dangerous chemicals because i believe that the agreement reached with the council introduces important provisions for the protection of human health and the environment by applying the prior information and consent procedure provided for in the rotterdam convention.
in writing. the commission has proposed a recast of the regulation implementing the rotterdam convention on the exchange of information on chemicals placed on the market (the pic regulation). the main aim is to allow chemicals produced in the european union, which meet all eu environmental and health legislation standards, to be allowed to enter world markets, and to be replaced by chemicals with lower quality standards. in doing so, the european union ensures not only the export of its chemicals, protecting the european chemical industry, but also a high degree of environmental protection.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 689/2008 (the pic regulation) applies the rotterdam convention in the european union, but goes beyond it in that it covers a wider range of chemicals. in addition, the regulation applies the pic procedure to all countries importing listed chemicals from the eu and not only to countries that are party to the convention. i support the involvement of the european chemicals agency (echa) in the application of the regulation in order to take the greatest responsibility for its implementation. the chemicals listed in parts 2 and 3 of annex i to the pic regulation are banned or severely restricted in the eu because they often pose risks to the environment and/or human health. it is important to take special care when exporting these chemicals to third countries to ensure that we do not do so against their will. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the derogations should be limited to the pic procedure, as it is the eu's responsibility to ensure that the chemicals we export do not cause unnecessary harm to humans or the environment.
in writing. - the report seems to us to be generally positive and we have therefore supported it. the pic regulation applies the rotterdam convention in the eu, promotes the exchange of information on chemicals placed on the market and applies the prior information and consent procedure when chemicals covered by the convention are exported. the mechanism thus ensures that chemical exporting countries formally obtain the consent of importing countries before exporting. the commission proposal, supported by parliament, clarifies some definitions and involves the european chemicals agency in their application. therefore, care should be taken that manufacturers of chemicals banned or restricted in the eu, who normally choose to export, in particular to countries with more permeable legislation, can only do so by formally certifying that, when exporting these products, the third countries receiving them are not against their reception, given that certain chemicals entail a risk to public health and the environment, which is the central issue of this regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i think that, compared with the commission's proposal, it contains better provisions to protect public health, the environment and the economy itself. i believe that we should not facilitate the export of chemicals which are banned or heavily restricted in the european union to third countries. i could not therefore agree to the extension of the possibility of derogations in this area. the failure to respond to an export request for these products may be due to a number of factors, including inefficient administration, economic weakness or the belief that the general law covers the case. the absence of a reply cannot therefore be considered as acceptance of the import of those chemicals. the eu's role should not be to facilitate the export of chemicals banned in europe to countries whose legislation or administration is more permeable. the eu must be committed to safeguarding public health and the environment, not the profits of european manufacturers of chemicals banned in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the regulation of trade in dangerous chemicals, because it is concerned with ensuring the safety of citizens and the protection of the environment. this report introduces changes, such as requiring prior consent from importing countries to trade in these dangerous products, even when these countries are not part of the european union. the adoption of this regulation safeguards the international obligations assumed by the european parliament under the rotterdam convention.
in writing. − it is the eu's responsibility to ensure that the chemicals it exports do not cause unnecessary harm to humans or the environment. for this reason, and because i believe that the eu should continue to be a leader in environmental legislation, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − this report concerns the recasting of regulation (ec) no 689/2008 (the pic regulation) concerning the export and import of dangerous chemicals. although this regulation was created as a result of the rotterdam convention, it is true that its scope goes beyond that, covering a wider range of chemicals. the commission has now proposed a recast of this regulation, in particular to clarify certain definitions, bring the regulation into line with recently adopted legislation on chemicals, involve the european chemicals agency (echa) more closely in the application of the regulation and amend the rules of the prior information and consent procedure to make it easier for exporters to export chemicals covered by the pic regulation in cases where no response is received. it should be stressed that we must remain cautious about the possibility of applying derogations from the pic procedure with regard to exports of chemicals considered harmful or dangerous to third countries, as it is the eu's responsibility to ensure that the chemicals we export do not cause harm to humans or the environment. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon brought a change in the comitology procedure, transforming it into a new system for the adoption of delegated and implementing acts (articles 290 and 291 tfeu). the implementation of article 290 was the subject of a non-binding agreement between the eu institutions. the common understanding on article 291 tfeu provides for the adoption of a regulation 'establishing in advance the general rules and principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers'. the report suggests changes to the comitology rule. the new article 87, in combination with the revised article 88, establishes the standard procedure to be followed. the rapporteur proposes the creation of a procedure that more clearly defines the rules for cases requiring rapid adoption of a delegated act or its implementation - which is a positive thing. another positive element of this proposal is the possibility for a political group or 40 members to challenge the decision of the committee responsible on the substance. it is important that there should be increased control of the commission's implementing powers. it would therefore be essential that the same could also be exercised by the national parliaments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending rules 87a and 88 of parliament's rules of procedure, which provide for a procedure which clarifies the procedures for adopting a delegated act or an implementing act, making the procedure more efficient and speedier.

in writing. − the purpose of this report is to adapt the rules of procedure to the new system introduced by the treaty of lisbon for the exercise of implementing powers, which is now based, in accordance with articles 290 and 291 tfeu, on the adoption of delegated and implementing acts. more specifically, this concerned the need, already identified by the president of the european parliament, to provide for a procedure to clarify the modalities for the rapid adoption of a delegated act or an implementing act (whether for cases where there is only one competent committee, whether in the framework of procedures of associated committees or joint meetings of committees), adapting further, in the latter case, the rules of procedure to the provisions of the recent regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 february 2011 laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. i voted in favour.

in writing. − in recent years, the mobility of european citizens has increased exponentially, both because of their longevity and because of the enlargement of the european union to the east. along with this increased mobility, the data of each of us also knows fewer and fewer borders. the internet, particularly through social networks, puts our personal, professional and social data at the click of a mouse. if this situation makes it easy for the media, which can invade the privacy of many people without leaving their workplace, it makes citizens much more vulnerable. in fact, there is an increasing number of cases of international defamation and it is imperative to specify the legislation to be applied. the report under review contains recommendations to the commission on the amendment of regulation (ec) no 864/2007 on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations (rome ii). while i understand that these amendments may have a negative impact on freedom of expression, i voted in favour of them because there must be a balance between the right to privacy and the right to information. i also welcome the proposal to create an alternative system for the settlement of disputes by mutual agreement.
in writing. - this report proposes an amendment to the regulation on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations (rome ii), which basically seeks to clarify what legislation applies in cases of infringement of personality rights through content placed online or in print, if a person who considers that his rights have been infringed chooses to bring a civil liability action. the issue alleged for this need is the ease today for the complainant to choose to bring a defamation action in the jurisdiction which is considered most likely to produce a favourable outcome, the so-called defamation tourism. this appendix sets out clearer rules such as that the applicable law is the law of the country where the most significant element of the damage occurred, the law of the country where (in the case of a printed publication) the publication is mainly issued. the inalienable and non-transferable right of every individual to control the use of his or her body, name, image, privacy, etc., must be protected and guaranteed. it is noted that the addendum also contains a recital stating that this regulation does not prevent member states from applying their constitutional rules on freedom of the press... in writing. − this report contains some recommendations to the commission on the amendment of regulation (ec) no 864/2007 on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations (rome ii). infringements of personality rights through content posted on a website are particularly concerned. in this way, a person who considers that his rights have been infringed has the option of bringing an action for civil liability for all the damage caused, either before the courts of the member state in which the publisher of that content is established or before the courts of the member state in which the centre of his interests is located. the aim is to add to the rome ii regulation a provision which defines the law applicable to a non-contractual obligation arising from violations of privacy and personality rights, including defamation.
in writing. − this report proposes an amendment to regulation no 864/2007 seeking to clarify the applicable legislation in cases of infringement of personality rights (the inalienable and non-transferable right of every individual to control the use of his or her body, name, image, privacy, among others) through content placed online or in print, should the person who considers that his or her rights have been infringed choose to bring a civil liability action. this need is justified by the ease with which the complainant can choose to bring a defamation action in the jurisdiction which is considered to be most likely to produce a favourable outcome, the so-called 'defamation tourism'. this addendum sets clearer rules, such as that the law applicable in the event of a legal complaint is the law of the country where the most significant element of the damage occurred, the law of the country where (in the case of a printed publication) the publication is issued in the largest number of copies and where it will have the greatest impact. the content of the report can help to clarify judicial procedures in these cases, while safeguarding the laws specific to each member state.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates a new eu trade and investment strategy for the southern mediterranean, taking into account the socioeconomic changes brought about by the arab spring revolutions. trade and investment policy is an exclusive competence of the eu which must provide innovative instruments to achieve the goals of democracy, prosperity, stability and peace in the region.
in writing. the so-called arab spring was a breath of fresh air that swept through most of the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean. civil society, imbued with a yearning for freedom and social justice, carried forward a revolution that overthrew various totalitarian regimes. however, in some countries we are beginning to see the floodgates of religious intolerance being opened by the muslim majority in defiance of the rights, freedoms and guarantees enshrined in the un declaration of human rights. it is intolerable that we should see negative discrimination against christians by the muslim majority when they used to live side by side. this report focuses on the eu's trade and investment strategy for the southern mediterranean following the arab spring revolutions. although the negotiations with morocco have not progressed as far as would be desirable, the fact is that an acp memorandum was approved last december with the countries of the southern mediterranean, with the aim of integrating them into the single market. the eu should continue to support these countries, in particular with regard to the implementation of the democratic process, the promotion of entrepreneurship and student mobility. but it must also demand absolute respect for human rights.
in writing. − the report aims to address the challenges for eu trade and investment policies in the wake of the democratic movements in the middle east and north africa. the rapporteur characterises the movements as an unparalleled historical event and as an opportunity to open up the economies of the region and create a true market economy, whether or not this is the choice of the peoples concerned. the report makes a slight criticism of the role of the eu and its member states in maintaining relations with the dictatorships of the regions for decades (dictatorships, yes, but market economies too, according to the criteria in force). the report points to the fragility (social, economic as well as democratic) of the situation in the different countries, but at the same time explains that the eu is the largest consumer market in the world, to which access should only be granted if the partner countries are seriously committed to bilateral market opening. the idea is that the global and deep free trade agreements are the right way forward for the social and economic development of these regions. the whole report is inspired by the neoliberal vision of free trade. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. − the arab spring is the biggest political transformation in the european neighbourhood since the fall of the berlin wall and provides the eu with the opportunity to align its foreign policy and trade interests with its core values of human rights, democracy and a free society. the arab spring is a unique opportunity for the eu to make a serious commitment and show political leadership. it only obliges us to continue to make a more determined effort to liberalize trade and to create investment opportunities. this strategy should be fully aligned with policies in other policy areas, in order to create training opportunities for entrepreneurs, promote participation in eu programmes and facilitate access to visas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the arab spring to be an unparalleled historical event, prompted by the aspirations of the peoples for freedom, democratic rights and improved living conditions. i welcome the fair and transparent elections that have taken place in several north african countries, accompanied by economic, legal and social reforms that make it possible to envisage the unity of these countries through the building of democratic and pluralist institutions, thus creating the basis for greater stability and development. however, i could not help but reflect in my vote the rejection of paragraph 15 of the report, because i believe that the margin for negotiations on agriculture between the eu and this group of countries must be properly weighed up, otherwise there will be too much political enthusiasm on the part of the eu which will unduly penalize european agricultural producers.
in writing. − the arab spring is the biggest political transformation in the european neighbourhood since the fall of the berlin wall and has provided the eu with the opportunity to align its foreign policy and trade interests. in this way, the results achieved in terms of democratic reforms and individual freedoms should be reflected in a similar process of economic liberalisation. this is where the eu will have an important role to play, provided that the appropriate political, social and environmental commitments are made and implemented by the countries of the southern mediterranean (sme). some of the proposals in this report concern both the eib and the ebrd. the first is essential in helping smes by providing micro-credit. the second must draw on the experience gained in eastern europe to make its contribution. the creation of the euromed free trade area and the facilitation of knowledge and direct contacts through the exchange of both students and european business communities and smes are also part of the set of objectives to be achieved. as this is a unique opportunity for the eu to show its political leadership, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to play a more effective role in the fight against terrorism. but it is worth remembering that the nature of the previous regimes has not bothered the eu so far, nor have its governments, which have established such deep relations with them. it should be remembered that ben ali's party was, until it was overthrown by the struggle of the tunisian people, a member of the socialist international. the european commission says the report advocates the concept of 'more for more', i.e. that democratic reforms and individual freedoms should be reflected in a process of 'liberation' in the economic and trade spheres, through the consolidation of the euro-mediterranean free trade area. it therefore advocates the use of the infamous free trade agreements, which have proved to this day that they only mean the loss of the sovereignty of peoples, the appropriation by multinationals of natural resources and biodiversity, the increase in external dependence on third countries and the disaster in productive sectors in some member states, particularly those like portugal which have a more fragile economic situation.
in writing. − i welcome this report, starting with the recognition of the important role played by the eip in supporting innovation, competitiveness and economic growth in europe and that patents favour the dissemination of valuable technical information and are an important instrument for technology transfer. however, the commission, in coordination with the member states, should address in its next report the issue of the potential repercussions of the granting of patents on plant breeding methods and the consequent impact on the plant breeding sector, agriculture, the food industry and food safety.
in writing. − intellectual property rights are essential to stimulate the development of new plant varieties and plant-related innovations and are a necessary precondition for boosting growth and innovation, as well as helping european businesses, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), to cope with the economic crisis and global competition.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution, tabled following a statement by the commission pursuant to rule 110 (2), deals with the grant of patents relating to essential biological processes. each year some 800 patent applications are filed, which in a few years amounts to thousands. although there are provisions for the registration of patents, we need greater legal clarity in this area. patents should obviously be protected, since such registration protects the inventor, encourages research and stimulates the economy. however, not everything about genetic manipulation should be allowed. natural products such as plants and animals should not be patentable and only crossbreeding by traditional methods should be allowed. it's the future of the planet at stake. we need a climate of honesty, because life cannot be patented. i voted in favour of this report because i am in favour of greater transparency in the process - companies cannot falsify data or use tricks - and only something that is new and relevant to humanity should be allowed to be registered.
in writing. - we do not fully follow some of the considerations made in the resolution concerning intellectual property rights, as well as the reference to the eip and its framework in the field of competitiveness. but overall this resolution is positive, and indeed contains important clarifications. it aims to prevent abuses of the rules on patenting living things and processes involving the improvement of living things or parts of living things. the defence of the non-patentability of agricultural processes such as the breeding of species and of newly created varieties is of great importance, seeking to ensure that farmers can continue to use age-old breeding processes and have access to their products without being dependent on multinationals. it is necessary to ensure the free flow of scientific information and to prevent the obtaining of disproportionate profits from biological processes or from their manipulation. the exclusion of the possibility of patenting essentially biological processes and the results of such processes is also positive, calling for reflection on the consequences of patenting. the resolution recalls the commission's lack of responsibility for reporting on the evolution and implications of patent rights in the field of biotechnology and genetic engineering, the frequency of which is defined in directive 98/44/ec as annual... (parliament adopted the legislative resolution)
in writing. - i believe that essential biological processes are natural heritage, the heritage of mankind, and therefore can never be patented or declared to be the property of private individuals. the resolution is mainly aimed at excluding from patentability several of these processes, namely essentially biological processes for obtaining plants (or animals) as well as products derived from conventional breeding and all conventional methods of breeding, including breeding using advanced reproductive technologies and markers (smart or precision breeding), as well as genetic material used for conventional breeding. that is why i voted in favour. i should add, however, that i consider patents to be often a hindrance to the transfer of technology.
in writing. - considering that intellectual property rights are essential to stimulate growth and innovation and that patent protection which is too broad is likely to constitute an obstacle to innovation and progress, i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament resolution on the granting of patents relating to essential biological processes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider that intellectual property rights are essential to stimulate the development of new plant varieties and plant-related innovations. indeed, such recognition is a necessary precondition for boosting growth and innovation.
in writing. the resolution is concerned with the granting of patents on essential biological processes. intellectual property rights are essential to stimulate the development of new plant varieties and associated innovations. they are also a necessary precondition for boosting growth and innovation and helping european businesses to cope with the economic crisis and global competition. however, patent protection that is too broad is likely to constitute an obstacle to innovation and progress and to harm small and medium-sized livestock breeders by blocking access to animal and plant genetic resources. in order to treat differently what is different, i believe that patents can be granted in the field of genetic engineering, but that the prohibition of patents relating to plant varieties and animal breeds must be safeguarded, considering that the production of plants is essential to the security of food supply and, to some extent, to the supply of energy. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the resolution aims to prevent abuses of the rules on patenting living organisms and processes involving the improvement of living organisms or parts of them. the defence of the non-patentability of agricultural processes such as the breeding of species and of newly created varieties is of great importance, seeking to ensure that farmers can continue to use age-old breeding processes and have access to their products without being dependent on multinationals. it is essential to ensure the free flow of scientific information and to prevent the obtaining of disproportionate profits from biological processes or from their manipulation.
in writing. - i welcome this report, stressing the importance of close cooperation with the imo on naval capacity building with the work being done towards the conclusion of an eu-imo strategic partnership to combat piracy throughout the horn of africa. i also believe that the use of private armed guards is a measure which cannot replace the necessary global solution to the multifaceted threat posed by piracy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution for urging the eu high representative to make more efforts to secure the release of the more than 200 hostages currently held in captivity, victims of piracy off the coast of somalia and in the western indian ocean. the union should actively contribute to the establishment of an international tribunal specialised in combating maritime piracy.
in writing. the joint motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 110 (2) and (4) of the rules of procedure, replacing the motions for resolutions tabled by the following groups: alde, ecr, s&d and ppe, on maritime piracy. the transport of goods by sea remains the most widely used mode of transport worldwide. however, in recent years we have witnessed a phenomenon that takes us back to the 16th and 17th centuries, to the time of the discoveries: piracy. piracy has been a major risk at sea for centuries and continues to pose a danger and insecurity to many ships sailing the oceans. we all remember the recent phenomenon of piracy off the coast of somalia. the european union has taken measures and is taking part in actions to prevent this phenomenon, which we can call maritime terrorism. i voted in favour of this report because, in addition to recommending that the member states protect their fleets, it seeks to tackle the problem at its source, that is, in the ports from which pirates depart, by promoting the economic development of these regions, since these are very poor communities with a high rate of emigration.
in writing. - the majority of this parliament reiterates its unacceptable militarist and openly meddling positions in this resolution. the resolution supports the extension and strengthening of the eu operation eunavfor atalanta and 'enhanced coordination' with the nato operation to combat piracy. but it does not explain the real causes of this phenomenon. it ignores the responsibilities of several european countries, the usa and nato for the serious problems facing the people of somalia and other countries in the region, which are at the origin of the so-called piracy. we know the interest that the region arouses. it is rich in natural resources, particularly in fisheries, and is important for international trade, the horn of africa and the gulf of aden connect the suez canal to the indian ocean, making it the fastest route between asia and europe. the solution to the problems of the region lies in respecting somalia's sovereignty over its resources and its eez. for the immediate withdrawal of the eu and nato mission. the break with the so-called structural adjustment policies of the imf and the world bank, which from the 1990s onwards led to the collapse of the country's fragile economy, putting its sovereignty and food security at risk.
in writing. − piracy is a threat to international security and regional stability and should be seen as an international organised crime, but also as an economic problem, since it threatens international commercial sea lanes and has a considerable negative impact on international trade. in this connection, i welcome the motion for a resolution in which i voted in favour, stressing the need for immediate and effective measures to crack down on and punish persons suspected of acts of piracy and for third countries and eu member states to transpose into their national law all the provisions of the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the united nations convention for the suppression of unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation in order to combat the impunity of pirates.
in writing. - maritime piracy is now a phenomenon that is becoming more widespread and frequent, more organised and profitable, more audacious and violent, to which no vessel seems to be immune, from fishing boats and merchant ships to yachts and cruises. the safety and freedom of persons are seriously affected, all maritime activities and the economy suffer enormous losses. in 2009, the commission systematised its action in two stages: prevention, deterrence and repression, and also tackling the causes of piracy. the commission should extend its military action beyond 2012 and step up its diplomatic action to obtain effective cooperation from third countries hosting pirates. the member states will have to make efforts in the area of criminal investigation and justice, particularly in establishing conditions for the prosecution of pirates. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution and i hope that concerted action by the commission, the member states and other countries and regions of the world will restore safety at sea, which, as far as fisheries are concerned, affects both industrial fleets and small local vessels, affecting the economy of the european union.
in writing. the resolution calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's military presence in somalia is not compromised. the majority of meps reiterate militaristic and interventionist positions to promote the domination of big capital and the eu's major powers over the region's natural resources, particularly in the fisheries sector, and over one of the most important regions for international trade (the horn of africa and the gulf of aden link the suez canal to the indian ocean, which is the fastest route between asia and european countries). we stand for the sovereignty of somalia, including over its eez, and for a peaceful political solution to the internal conflict, free from any external interference. we are in favour of the immediate withdrawal of the eu and nato mission, of which portugal is also a member. we defend the right of peoples to food sovereignty and food security, rejecting the so-called trade liberalization in the framework of the wto or other instruments such as the epas, and the structural adjustment policies imposed by the imf and the world bank.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr barnier, for the work he has done in general. a fully functioning internal market ensures more jobs, more trade transactions, enables more informed consumers with access to a greater variety, quality and reliability of goods and services, and small and medium-sized enterprises more robust and better able to face globalisation. to this end, the role of the member states is crucial, not only at the legislative production stage, which must be appropriate, innovative and inventive, but also at the transposition stage into the internal legal orders. and that's where the problems come in. member states sometimes take the transposition deadline much longer than the two years stipulated, which seriously undermines the functioning of this market of 500 million citizens and makes it impossible for rules to enter into force. other member states have incorrectly or insufficiently transposed directives, which causes enormous problems of interpretation and application of the rules in the european market. the 2011 internal market governance communication brings together the governance life cycle in a single document. the holistic approach has long been advocated by parliament, particularly in the grech report, and it now allows us to have a fuller and more comprehensive view of the obstacles to the full functioning of the internal market. the resistance of the member states, the inertia and sometimes the lack of commitment to good transposition must be actively combated by the european commission, the european parliament and by active scrutiny by the national parliaments, let us not forget. solvit, which has a crucial role in the extrajudicial resolution of problems faced by citizens and businesses as a result of the malfunctioning of the internal market, must be given as soon as possible a legal basis to enable it to exploit its full potential and to respond fully to challenges, complementing the work of the european commission in the field of infringement proceedings. the annual governance report, alongside the internal market forum, which was initially suggested by my colleague mr grech and was crowned with success at its first edition in krakow in october 2011, should henceforth be a benchmark for the development of the internal market. this forum, or, as commissioner barnier has now called it, single market week, which it is desirable to organise, is of enormous importance in assessing progress and the obstacles to the development of the internal market. in addition to the data that the governance report provides us with, it brings together in the same physical space a number of actors, legislators, consumers, business people and other stakeholders who will thus be able to audit the functioning of the internal market and have a better understanding of their rights and developments in this area. finally, i would like to express my surprise at a proposal by the rapporteur, which came out on the eve of the vote in committee, after a fruitful debate lasting more than six months, which advocates the creation of an independent body from the commission which would be responsible for infringement proceedings in the internal market and would be competent to initiate infringement proceedings after approval by the college of commissioners: an internal market prosecutor. this is a very complex proposal which requires a thorough debate, which has not yet taken place, and clarification of the legal nature of this body, its powers and its modus operandi. we regret that this complex proposal has come so late, making it impossible to debate it, and that our receptivity in these circumstances is therefore limited in this respect.
madam president, this report makes some very interesting points. it says, for example, that the success of the internal market is a key driver for increasing competitiveness and growth and one of the best ways to solve the economic crisis. these considerations may be interesting but they are only interesting from the perspective of large economic and financial capital. these considerations have certainly not taken account of the economic and social development of the peripheral countries and their peoples. it is because these countries are experiencing the greatest difficulties today, in a period of crisis, as a result of their economic weakness, to which the construction of the internal market has contributed greatly, which is a surprise. the internal market, i.e. the policies of liberalization, privatisation and deregulation of the economy, have meant for the economically most vulnerable countries the destruction of their productive capacity, the decline of their exports, the increase of imports in sectors such as energy and food, which have left them in situations of extreme external dependence. what were the consequences of the internal market for countries like my own, portugal? the increasing number of enterprises closing, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, the destruction of thousands of jobs, the increase in levels of poverty, exclusion and inequalities, the loss of workers' rights and the generalization of precariousness in labour relations, the privatization of energy, transport, postal, telecommunications, banking, insurance sectors, the liberalization of essential public services. it is that in the perspective of the internal market there is no freedom for people to have social rights and a dignified life. from the perspective of the internal market, and those who defend it, there is only the free movement of goods and capital. the workers of the various european countries have been fighting courageously for their freedoms, for their social and economic rights and demanding a different direction from the current policies.
mr president, on june 17th the greek people will vote: it's your future, your life that you're going to choose. it is on this freedom that europe is built. trichet's statements at the g8 meeting are therefore unacceptable. in practice, the former president of the european central bank proposed that a people could lose the right to vote, that a democratically elected government which refuses austerity could be replaced by a constellation of commissioners from brussels. the blackmailing of the budgetary treaty is equally unacceptable. for us, europe is democracy, it is solidarity between peoples. it is not, and cannot be, the forced impoverishment of populations. that is why i ask all of you, ladies and gentlemen, whether you are prepared to accept this colonial regime. the answer from the european citizens will certainly be democracy.
mr president, in recent weeks portugal has experienced yet another social and civilizational setback. with the sponsorship of the european union and the imf and the signature of the national parties that accept, defend and implement a genuine pact of aggression against the country and its people. the amendments to the labour law strike at historic achievements of the workers and deal another severe blow to an already fragile democracy. facilitation of dismissals, reduction of compensation, reduction of additional pay and days off, reduction of holiday days and abolition of holidays, i.e. forced and unpaid work, attempt to generalize precarious contracts and to dismantle collective bargaining. it will be millions of euros more than will be extorted from portuguese workers. at the same time, more jobs are being eliminated, possibly more than 90,000, at a time when unemployment is already at historic levels. it's not too late to break from this path. now is the time to do it. the thousands of people who will again be filling the streets of lisbon next saturday will confirm this once again.
i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. much can be said about the importance of small and mediumsized enterprises in helping economic growth and job creation. whatever one says, what is certain is that the application of the so-called austerity measures leads daily to the strangulation, suffocation
