in writing. − the new crime landscape is characterised by the existence of highly mobile and flexible criminal networks operating in various criminal jurisdictions and sectors, aided by new technological trends and the widespread use of the internet. the eu must be prepared to respond appropriately as security threats emerge and evolve, with the involvement of the ep in defining policy guidelines and in implementing and evaluating results, and with the need for cooperation between member states to deal effectively with these challenges greater than ever. five priorities have been identified for the next five years: the fight against organised crime, terrorism, cybercrime, strengthening border management and the eu's resilience to crises and disasters. it is important not only to strengthen the instruments at the eu's disposal to combat crime, but also to implement and apply those already in place, e.g. member states still do not fully implement the instruments for the exchange of information; the various instruments of police and judicial cooperation have not yet been ratified and applied by all member states; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it clarifies the importance of a comprehensive approach to the eu security strategy, based on a holistic concept of human security anchored in human rights, freedom, democracy, the rule of law, good governance and peace. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the internal security strategy should include a parliamentary dimension and not be limited to an intergovernmental policy issue, as both european and national parliaments have an active role in setting priorities and evaluating eu policies.
in writing. − we live in a complex world with diverse and varied threats, such as terrorism, serious international crime, the mafia, cybercrime, economic crime, money laundering and corruption, and natural disasters themselves, and failures in existing infrastructure. all these threats, although very different, call into question the security of european citizens and that is why the institutions must have a clear strategy to ensure that the eu remains an area of freedom and justice, but also of security. as the report says, the charter of fundamental rights must be the basis of a sound internal security strategy, in accordance with the principles enshrined in the treaty, the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. - this report is based on the guidelines of the stockholm programme and the path opened up by the lisbon treaty in this field. it is considered that eu security policy must be anchored in a specific eu legal order, subject to supervision at european level. this is the starting point for developing an eu internal security strategy, which protects the eu from terrorism and other threats. in the present context, many of the possible implications of this view are evident. this is all the more so when we consider that any security policy must include a preventive element, which is particularly indispensable at a time when economic and social inequalities are worsening. . . . but it goes on to suggest that eu security measures ... [should] focus on enforcing specific legislation and on intelligence-based activities with proven capacity to reduce crime rates and prevent terrorist attacks. despite some statements on human rights and the principle of subsidiarity, the whole report is geared towards a security and repressive approach which does not help to tackle the causes of terrorism effectively. the gue/ngl has long been opposed to this view. we voted against it.
in writing. − the internal security strategy (iss) for 2010-14 identified five priority areas where the eu can add value, namely in the fight against and prevention of serious and organised crime, terrorism and cybercrime, in strengthening external border management and in building resilience to natural and man-made disasters. in any case, i believe that freedom, security and justice are objectives which must be pursued in parallel, and that the implementation of the eu charter must therefore form the basis of any sound internal security strategy. to succeed and achieve freedom and justice, security must always be guaranteed in accordance with the principles enshrined in the treaty, the rule of law and the union's obligations in respect of fundamental rights. it is the pursuit of these objectives that will make the european union's internal security strategy a success.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's proposals on the internal security strategy of the european union, stressing the need to recognise parliament as a full-fledged institutional actor in security policy matters and therefore entitled to participate actively in defining the characteristics and priorities of the internal security strategy and the eu security model and in evaluating these instruments, in particular through regular monitoring exercises on the implementation of the internal security strategy, carried out jointly by the ep, national parliaments and the council.
in writing. − any security policy must integrate a preventive dimension and in a period of increasing economic and social inequalities this preventive aspect is particularly important. despite the financial constraints in the context of the crisis we are living in, i stress that it is essential to include in the multiannual framework 2014-2020 adequate financial resources for the implementation of this strategy through the respective fund.
in writing. − the european commission's proposal lists the most urgent challenges to the internal security of the european union which should be integrated into a strategy for the coming years. this strategy is based on five main objectives to combat large-scale crime, organised crime, cybercrime, natural disasters and border security. in this context, the fight against terrorism also remains a high priority for the eu's internal security. it also sets out specific actions for the period 2011-2014 in addition to those already under way, which it is hoped will also contribute to strengthening cooperation and the link between the internal and external dimensions of european security. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - this report takes account of the provisions of the stockholm programme and the treaty of lisbon, in particular the considerations that eu security policy must be anchored in a specific eu legal order, subject to what they call democratic oversight at not only national but also mainly european level. it thus establishes an eu internal security strategy that is said to protect the eu from terrorism and other threats. although the document is tempered with some statements that human rights and the principle of subsidiarity must be respected, the report in general is aimed at creating a security and repressive strategy, with little emphasis on prevention, focusing on strengthening the conditions of punishment, which often means, in the eu, the criminalization of all social movements and forces that do not allow themselves to be guided by the dictates of the eu, and also a control of the lives of citizens, undermining their fundamental freedoms and guarantees. we voted against it, of course.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that criminal law is different from many other areas, which by definition restricts certain human and fundamental rights of the accused. this report sets out principles and parameters to be taken into account in the development of criminal law, with interinstitutional mechanisms to make it more efficient and with respect for the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the united nations, and in my view the european union can and should be the bulwark of the defence of human and fundamental rights in the world.
in writing. - the coordination between the council, the commission and parliament in matters relating to criminal law is essential. in the future these institutions will certainly establish a common framework which may include a set of principles which will serve as a basis for any criminal law instrument. this framework may contain precise guidelines for the internal procedures adopted in each of the institutions with a view to ensuring a coherent approach. i voted in favour of this report because it is in line with what i said earlier.
in writing. − criminal law is a sensitive area where differences between national systems remain substantial. however, given the cross-border nature of many offences, it is essential that criminal law measures are adopted at eu level to prevent criminals from hiding behind borders or taking advantage of differences in national legal systems. the existence of minimum rules also contributes to the strengthening of mutual trust between member states which is essential not only for good cooperation between their authorities but also for the effective functioning of the principle of mutual recognition. we must take advantage of the new possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty to develop a uniform, coherent and transparent eu criminal law that brings real added value to our citizens, by strengthening their confidence in exercising their right to free movement and to acquire goods or services from other member states. i therefore support this report, which contributes to the debate on the development of a genuine common eu legal culture in the fight against crime, which, without replacing national legal traditions, can complement them and strengthen mutual trust.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the question of criminal law in the eu context. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, criminal law becomes part of the eu's competences. unfortunately, parliament does not have a coordinating role and is not competent to deal with all legislative proposals containing criminal law provisions, since these have to be transposed into national law. i welcome the principles and parameters set out in this report to be taken into account in the drafting of criminal law: the creation of mechanisms to facilitate interinstitutional cooperation, full respect for the eu charter as well as other international human rights instruments, and the creation of checks for human rights solidarity campaigns.
in writing. - for many years criminal law was considered to be the exclusive competence of the member states, which was only changed by the maastricht treaty in 1992. since then, the eu has been creating a set of criminal rules which do not always fit together in the way that would be most appropriate. at present, eu criminal law includes a wide range of rules that are not just jha policy instruments, but that range from the financial sector to fraud, counterfeiting, serious breaches of eu data protection rules, customs offences, environmental offences and certain aspects of internal market policies. these are, as you can see, very diverse policy areas and it is nevertheless essential to ensure consistency and quality for effective application of eu criminal law.
in writing. - there is a lot of ground to cover in the field of judicial cooperation, criminal investigation and the fight against crime in general. some steps have been taken in this area, but others could and should still be taken. the increase in the movement of people and capital, as well as the various forms of cross-border crime, including economic crime, makes this necessary. cooperation between member states should also be extended to the area of policies to prevent high economic crime, an area where the political will to do more and better has been lacking. but the report goes beyond this approach, proposing a harmonization in criminal matters, which we find unacceptable. this is an area in which the member states should retain their sovereignty. we do not accept the harmonization of criminal policies or the establishment of common criminal codes. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. − the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has brought new challenges to the development and integration of criminal law into eu law. in the case of criminal law, a field of law which may restrict the rights, freedoms and guarantees of the accused and/or the convicted person, we must always take account of the procedure for verifying the necessity. the eu will therefore have to act with great caution in developing additional provisions or revising existing criminal provisions to ensure that certain human rights and fundamental freedoms are never affected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the de jong report on 'a european perspective on criminal law' because it provides a good analysis of the stage of construction of a european criminal law, to which the treaty of lisbon has given renewed importance. indeed, the growing european integration not only in the economic field but also in the field of 'freedom, security and justice' cannot do without a dimension of integration of criminal law and criminal procedural law. the charter of fundamental rights of the union, which protects european citizens against the union itself, may also need criminal instruments of protection. the progressive establishment of a 'federal' criminal law is also an essential pillar in the construction of a genuine european 'political community', the basis for the constitutionalisation of the european union.
in writing. − i agree with the rapporteur's concern that there is a risk that the adoption of new legislation will not lead to better control, undermining the credibility and efficiency of substantive eu criminal law. the eu will therefore have to act with great caution in developing additional provisions or revising existing criminal provisions. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, a basis has been created for the development and integration of criminal law into eu law. this is a very sensitive area and it is essential that the eu institutions improve their internal structures and agree working principles and methods in order to ensure the quality and consistency of the eu's approach to criminal law. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european communities and the european investment bank is based on the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. − the eu has not developed a distinct area for criminal law provisions, and these do not only integrate instruments in the area of justice and home affairs, but also many other policy areas of the union. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the pillar structure disappeared and a basis was established for the development of criminal law as an integral part of eu law. it is therefore important to know how to ensure consistency and quality in a legal area which seems to integrate such diverse policy areas. to ensure the high quality and consistency of the eu's approach to criminal law, not only would the internal structures in each of the three eu institutions need to be improved, but the relevant working principles and methods would also need to be agreed between them.
in writing. − this report lists a number of general principles governing criminal law and stresses that harmonisation measures should be proposed to support the application of the principle of mutual recognition, supporting the creation of a common legal culture in the eu in the fight against crime. in our view, criminal matters are an area which is exclusively a matter for the sovereign action and policies of the various states. we therefore do not advocate the harmonization of criminal policies and the establishment of common criminal codes. in this respect, there are other avenues to be explored in the fight against crime, such as judicial cooperation, cooperation in the investigation and fight against crime. on the other hand, the promotion of policies that lead to the reduction of social inequalities and the promotion of important social, economic and labour rights would be fundamental to the prevention of crime. this has definitely not been the way forward in the european union.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that a new consumer protection agenda, which emphasises the protection of vulnerable consumers in the european union, is urgently needed. in taking into account the different needs, skills and circumstances of consumers, in fact, in my view, it is imperative to consider consumer vulnerability as a key task of this new agenda, and more consumer information and awareness campaigns should be provided.
in writing. − the european union's consumer policy should be ambitious and provide a high level of protection, with particular attention to vulnerable consumers. this report, which has my full support, calls on the european commission and the member states to introduce specific measures in their legislation to ensure adequate protection for vulnerable consumers. in addition to the authorities, companies and suppliers should be involved in order to make contractual balancing more transparent and less opaque. the report also draws attention to the vulnerability of older consumers in the context of the digitalisation of services. the establishment of a strategy to strengthen the rights of the most vulnerable consumers will contribute to their social inclusion and to progress towards a fairer and more tolerant society, as well as to ensuring a more dynamic, secure and competitive internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the creation of a strategy to strengthen the rights of the most vulnerable consumers, enabling them to participate in the single market, contributing not only to their social inclusion and to progress towards a fairer and more tolerant society, but also to ensuring a more dynamic, secure and competitive internal market.
in writing. - there are 500 million consumers in europe, where consumer spending represents 56% of eu gdp. consumers in full use of their rights, properly protected and able to benefit from the single market can make a significant contribution to stimulating innovation and growth in the context of a more dynamic, efficient and fair internal market. it is essential that eu consumer policy can pay particular attention to the specific needs of the most vulnerable consumers, through a specific strategy to strengthen their capacity to make effective and autonomous decisions. it should be borne in mind that all consumers are liable to become vulnerable consumers throughout their lives, and this may result from temporary or permanent causes inherent in their physical or psychological situation, or from external causes such as lack of knowledge of the language, use of new technologies, etc. in this way, the issue of consumer vulnerability should be subject to a horizontal approach and take into account their different needs, capacities and circumstances. specific measures should be adopted to ensure adequate protection, going beyond mere information, especially in certain areas such as telecommunications, access to justice, food, financial services, etc.
in writing. − consumer rights and their protection in community law is one of the main pillars of the functioning of the internal market. i believe that adequate consumer protection and safety is fundamental to the proper functioning of markets and trade, which is essential for competitiveness and growth. however, some consumers, out of all consumers, deserve particular protection, since they are considered to be the most vulnerable for various reasons (children, adolescents, the elderly, people with disabilities, etc.). while i recognize this need, i also believe that strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers is essentially about strengthening the obligations to provide correct information to the market, taking into account the special needs of each group.
in writing. − this report follows on from a previous report by a gue/ngl rapporteur on consumer protection, focusing on the specific case of vulnerable consumers a complex concept, which it defines broadly and comprehensively. the rapporteur proposes that the european commission and the member states develop strategies to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers (in areas such as telecommunications, access to justice, energy, transport, etc.). suggestions are made, for example, for a strengthening of pre-contractual and contractual information requirements; a strengthened right of withdrawal if the seller does not transmit the information in a clear and comprehensible manner, among others. the concept of vulnerable consumers includes children, the elderly and women. special attention is proposed for specific conditions, such as those of people without access to the internet or those with disabilities. the commission also proposes tougher advertising rules, better informing on the risks and not overestimating any benefits, even referring to the particular case of financial products. we appreciate that the amendments proposed by our group have been accepted by a majority. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i believe that consumer protection is always a matter of concern to all of us, so that we can continue to build an increasingly balanced internal market. in this respect, it is imperative to create product safety standards and measures should be introduced to protect the rights and interests of consumers, especially against misleading advertising by offering the consumer an image of the product that is not compatible with reality. the most sensitive sectors are in particular the financial, food, transport and internet sectors. in addition, consumers should be given the means to enjoy the benefits of a liberalised market, allowing them to make informed choices. finally, to increase consumer confidence in the internal market, it is absolutely necessary to ensure better access to justice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of agreeing to the perspective of strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers by closely monitoring social habits and changes in social and consumer behaviour which may place certain groups and/or individuals in a vulnerable situation. this should be done in a balanced way and always in communication with all stakeholders.
in writing. − the promotion and protection of consumer rights are core values for the development of eu policies, in particular for the strengthening of the single market and the pursuit of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. within the general concept of consumers, however, there is a specific category, namely vulnerable consumers, to which special attention should be paid. the present report aims precisely to contribute to the creation of a strategy to strengthen the rights of the most vulnerable consumers, calling in this regard on the commission and the member states to adopt specific measures to ensure their adequate protection, especially in those sectors where the level of vulnerability has been shown to be highest (financial sector, food, transport, internet, access to justice, transport and energy) and specifically in the consumer agenda and the consumer programme for 2014-2020. i voted in favour.
in writing. − in november 2011, the european commission presented the proposal for a regulation on the consumer programme 2014-2020, aiming to put consumer rights at the heart of the single market. i am voting in favour of this report because it aims to stimulate consumer spending, which represents 56% of eu gdp, and thus make a decisive contribution to boosting economic growth and wealth creation. i believe that consumers should be protected from any commercial vulnerability, that the information available can be improved and that safety standards should be developed to ensure the effective functioning of the market. at a time of severe budgetary difficulties, i believe that it is necessary to protect the consumer from the financial markets, and that more economic regulation should be put in place and more information made available that leads to effective financial education.

in writing. − this report addresses the issue of euro coins, with the main concern being the introduction of binding rules and an integrated framework for the issuance of euro coins in all member states, as well as greater transparency and security in this process. the future weighting of the issue of 1 and 2 euro banknotes is suggested in this theme, taking into account the advantages that these would bring, in particular in increasing the handling and acceptance of the currency. on the other hand, the reduction in commemorative coins in circulation will also be an asset, as their value will increase due to their rarity. the report also includes a proposal for the commission to carry out an impact assessment on the continued issuance of euro 1 and 2 cent coins. in view of the timeliness and advantages of these proposals, i am in favour of this report.

in writing. - i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work and i fully agree with his position on the need to optimise the euro and reduce administrative costs.
in writing. − this report mentions that the lack of binding provisions for the issue of euro coins may lead to divergent practices in the member states and does not allow for the creation of a sufficiently integrated framework for the single currency. it therefore argues that, in the interests of transparency and legal certainty, it is necessary to introduce binding rules for the issuance of euro coins. it proposes, inter alia, to differentiate between current coins, which are intended for circulation, and collector coins, which by definition are not issued with a view to circulation, although they may be put into circulation at face value or higher. it is proposed that collector coins should be legal tender in all member states and not just in those where they are issued. although some of the provisions in the report are relevant, others raise doubts, such as the proposal which could call into question the continued issue of 1 and 2 cent coins.

in writing. − according to article 128 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the european central bank has the exclusive right to authorise the issue of euro banknotes within the union. the european central bank and the national central banks may issue these notes. i agree with this report because i believe that there should be general binding provisions for the issue of euro coins which aim to create a sufficiently integrated framework for the single currency. i also believe that it is good to study all the ways in which the single currency can be enhanced, and that the interests of the member states and citizens must be safeguarded, especially with regard to the costs associated with possible inflation resulting from the elimination of the 1 and 2 cent coins.
in writing. − this report mentions that the lack of binding provisions for the issue of euro coins may lead to divergent practices in the member states and does not allow for the creation of a sufficiently integrated framework for the single currency. it therefore argues that, in the interests of transparency and legal certainty, it is necessary to introduce binding rules for the issuance of euro coins. it proposes, inter alia, a distinction between current coins, which are intended for circulation, and collector coins, which by definition are not issued with a view to circulation, although they may be put into circulation at their face value or higher. it is also proposed that the commission should assess the continuation of the issuance of 1 and 2 cent coins. this proposal raises some concerns and doubts, particularly as regards the possibility of an increase in product prices as a result of the so-called rounding-offs, which, if confirmed, would have a more negative impact on countries such as portugal. in addition, an impact assessment of the issue of 1 and 2 euro banknotes was initially proposed as a way of increasing the value of collector and commemorative coins but this amendment was not incorporated into the final document.

in writing. − the publication of the internal market assessment panel has contributed to improving the transposition of the relevant legislation. despite considerable progress since its first publication in 1997, there is still a gap in the transposition of community legislation at member state level. some member states continue to fail to fully comply with their obligations as regards the correct and timely transposition of community legislation. the current average deficit of 1.2% is once again above the 1% target agreed by the heads of state and government in 2007. this report, which i have supported, advocates a coordinated and cooperative approach to improve the functioning of the single market by better transposing european legislation. it advocates the creation of support mechanisms for member states and urges member states to ensure adequate human resources in solvit centres and to strengthen the one-stop-shop systems with the aim of providing citizens with clear and practical information.

in writing. - as is already the case in other eu policies (e.g. neighbourhood policy or trade policy), it seems to me absolutely essential to condition our relations with third countries (even those that are candidates for accession) on strict observance of our fundamental values as a community of citizens and states. this report, which focuses on women's rights in turkey, is an important tool for framing and understanding the cultural, religious and historical reality of this candidate country, highlighting the latest developments, which allows an objective and clear analysis of the current situation, such as the creation of the ministry of family and social policies and the parliamentary committee on equal opportunities or the progress made in the education system and the labour market. however, there is still a long way to go as acknowledged in the report, in particular in the fight against gender-based violence and especially outside the large urban centres; in the implementation of the ambitious legislative framework already adopted and in the dialogue and monitoring of civil society on the implementation of these measures. i congratulate the rapporteur on voting in favour of this excellent own-initiative report.
in writing. - according to the report, the legislative framework in turkey on women's rights is largely established with legislation aimed at preventing violence against women, educating girls, eradicating illiteracy among women and increasing women's participation in the labour market. the rapporteur stresses, however, that the practical implementation of this legislation is not yet the most effective. it is important that turkey, as a candidate country, deepen its policies for the protection of women, by establishing genuine gender equality and ensuring the safety, protection and education of women in a society that provides equal opportunities regardless of gender.
in writing. - this report analyses and takes stock of what has been done in relation to equality between men and women in turkey. it also proposes a strategy to be followed in the field of inequalities between men and women in the country, violence between men and women, problems of women's access to education, the creation of shelters for women victims of domestic violence, the strengthening of prenatal and elderly care and institutions, data on the situation of women in turkey, among others. the commitments included proposals made by our group on the situation of kurdish women, women in rural areas, unemployed women and women living in poverty - which we value. how much we appreciate the paragraph calling on turkey to fulfil all its obligations under the ec-turkey association agreement and the additional protocol, which turkey has not yet implemented for the sixth consecutive year, because of the implications for the cyprus problem. for these reasons, we supported the report.
in writing. - turkey, as a potential candidate for membership, must respect the acquis communautaire and commit itself to respect human rights, including women's rights and gender equality. the pursuit of gender equality holds great potential for achieving the europe 2020 objectives by contributing to growth and full employment. progress has been made in turkey in improving and implementing the legislative framework to ensure equal participation of women in social, economic and political life. we are confident that turkey will continue on the right track with regard to gender equality; the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome, but it is a party to the treaty of rome.
in writing. the rapporteur has carried out an in-depth research on the situation of women in turkey, interviewing a number of people from the public sphere and ngos. the rapporteur concludes that the common claim expressed in all the contributions received is that of the need for a change of mindsets to transform the patriarchal structure of society into a structure based on gender equality. the rapporteur therefore makes a number of suggestions in this document to change attitudes. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - it is essential that the government of turkey respects and reinforces the principles of equality and women's rights by adopting and amending its legislative framework. i support the text adopted, which calls on turkey to fulfil all its obligations under the association agreement with the ec and the additional protocol, which turkey has not yet implemented for the sixth consecutive year. i welcome the increase in the number of female members of the turkish parliament.
in writing. - turkey, as a candidate country, must commit itself to respecting the acquis communautaire, in particular women's rights and gender equality. despite limited progress in the equal participation of women in social, economic and political life, there is still strong discrimination against women and the need to implement legislation already adopted to combat violence against women, including domestic violence, honour killings, and the fight against forced and early marriages. this report, in addition to analysing the situation of women in turkey, presents concrete measures to improve their situation. violence against women continues to reach alarming levels, and there are legal gaps and inconsistent enforcement among the authorities involved in protecting victims. illiteracy, low participation in politics and the labour market require the implementation of effective support measures, both at institutional and social level, in particular in changing mindsets and in the active participation of civil society in the implementation of these supports. i think it is extremely important that these issues are safeguarded in the new turkish constitution, and at the same time that awareness is raised of the importance of gender mainstreaming.
in writing. − this report analyses and takes stock of the progress made in promoting equality between men and women in turkey during the negotiation process for turkey's accession to the eu. it also suggests a strategy to be followed to combat the inequalities between men and women in the country, violence against women, and problems of women's access to education. it also called for the establishment of shelters for women victims of domestic violence to strengthen prenatal and elderly care and institutions, and stressed the importance of obtaining more data on the situation of women in turkey. we consider that the amendments we proposed and which referred to the need to pay special attention to the plight of kurdish women, women in rural areas, unemployed women and women living in poverty have been generally included in the final proposal of the report.
in writing. - i support this report because if we want to promote a citizens' initiative, i.e. for a group of citizens to be able to invoke the need for a piece of legislation at european level, it is imperative to ensure maximum transparency and democracy in this process. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that hearings should be held by the committees concerned at the same time as the participation in the petition. similarly, a single desk under the responsibility of the vice-president, which in turn ensures a stable environment, to deal with citizens' initiatives, would be a step forward. a legislative act initiated by citizens is an exceptional milestone in the progress made by the european union in developing democracy and we must therefore ensure that it is implemented in the best possible way.
in writing. − on 15 december 2010, the european parliament adopted the report on the proposal for a regulation on the citizens' initiative at first reading. the citizens' initiative will be an important tool available to european citizens, and aims to give citizens the same powers of political initiative as the council of ministers and the european parliament. in particular, it is intended to provide citizens with a means of being heard by allowing them to submit certain matters of interest to the european institutions. this initiative will complement the existing direct links between citizens and institutions. the ep can help to achieve these objectives by using all the means at its disposal to support citizens' initiatives, including public hearings. i therefore support this report.

in writing. − the european citizens' initiative should bring citizens closer to the european institutions. this new instrument of participatory democracy, provided for in the lisbon treaty, should give european citizens the opportunity to be heard and to contribute to the definition of the issues to be included in the eu's political agenda. the european parliament should contribute to the achievement of these objectives, in particular by organising public hearings, and parliament's rules of procedure will therefore have to be adapted. i support the rapporteur's proposals for the creation of a single desk to facilitate exchanges and dialogue with citizens, and for the organisation of hearings within the committees that are appointed to deal with this matter. these public hearings should take place when the citizens' initiative has collected more than one million signatures from citizens of at least seven member states, has been published in the register by the commission and sent to the ep, whose president should forward it to the committee responsible. the citizens' initiative will undoubtedly be a powerful tool to strengthen the citizens' europe by encouraging greater participation and the dynamic exercise of european citizenship.

in writing. - the observation that there is a gap between elected and electors, between citizens and decision-makers, in the european union, is repeated throughout europe. academics and political institutions are unanimous in their diagnosis even though there are disagreements about the best solutions to the problem. the european citizens' initiative is another attempt to bridge the gap and allow citizens to become more involved in european affairs, having been adopted by the treaty of lisbon. it is now up to us to put it into practice and to that end to amend the rules of procedure of the european parliament accordingly. without placing unreasonable hopes on this initiative in view of its actual scope and the limitations that result from it, i hope that a good use of it will enable it to achieve its intended purpose and promote participation and citizenship at european level. and while it does not replace representative democracy, it can nevertheless bring new voices and new initiatives to the political debate.
in writing. - this report deals only with the amendment of the rules of procedure of the european parliament to take account of the role assigned to parliament in the so-called citizens' initiative. while agreeing to hearings to discuss the issues covered by this figure, which the treaty of lisbon has created, it is worth recalling the contradictions and limits of the initiative itself. it is worth recalling, in particular, the demagogic way in which it was promoted: the attempt to whitewash the impoverishment of democracy by trying to make people forget that european officials prevented the people from expressing their opinion on the lisbon treaty. the procedure is now repeated in relation to the so-called budgetary treaty. it should be recalled that one million signatures from a significant number of member states are needed to simply invite the european commission to submit an appropriate proposal on matters on which these citizens consider a legal act of the union to be necessary to implement the treaties. in other words, after all the work of collecting signatures and meeting the requirements laid down in the proposal for a regulation, there is no guarantee that citizens will have their requests taken into account. the amendments to the rules of procedure are positive and they merely provide a framework for parliament's participation in this process.
in writing. − on 15 december 2010, a regulation was adopted allowing one million european citizens to ask the european commission to come forward with legislation on a given matter. the rules implementing the citizens' initiative, which was approved by the european parliament today, stipulate that signatories must come from at least seven member states. in the case of portugal, at least 16,500 signatures will be needed to support an initiative. the treaty of lisbon created a 'right of initiative for citizens' under which one million citizens can ask the commission to submit certain legislative proposals. today we are going to make the necessary amendments to the rules of procedure of the european parliament so that the 'right of initiative of citizens' becomes a reality.
in writing. − i have approved this report which calls for amendments to the rules of procedure to enable the european parliament to make an active contribution towards the achievement of the objectives of the citizens' initiative, in particular by making use of all the means at its disposal, including the organisation of public hearings.
in writing. − pursuant to article 11 of regulation (eu) no 211/2011 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 february 2011, it is provided that, following the registration of a citizens' initiative by the commission, the organisers will have the opportunity to present their initiative at a public hearing organised in the european parliament. the main purpose of this report is precisely to introduce the necessary amendments to the rules of procedure of the european parliament in order to regulate the organisation and conduct of these hearings. i voted in favour of the amendments because i agree with them.
in writing. − this new instrument will enable citizens, according to certain criteria, to put issues on the european agenda through the power of political initiative. at the same time, it will allow european citizens to be heard and european issues to be discussed at a cross-border level. in accordance with regulation (eu) no 211/2011, the organisers should be given the opportunity to present their initiative in a public hearing, with the broad technical support of the european parliament and the european commission. i would like to emphasize the creation of a single point of contact for dialogue and exchange between citizens, which will facilitate the applicability of the initiatives, the possibility of speakers taking part in the public hearings, and the possibility of reimbursement of transport costs, according to certain rules. despite the importance of this initiative, it should be stressed that not all initiatives will end up in a legislative proposal from the commission, but the possibility of debate on the european project has a crucial development with this instrument.
in writing. the report also calls for the european parliament to be given the right to vote in the european parliament elections. in our view, this initiative has several limitations. it was promoted in a demagogic way to whitewash the attacks on democracy that the european union has suffered. if the intention is to listen to the citizens, why have the people been prevented from expressing their views on the lisbon treaty and are they now being prevented from expressing their views on the budgetary treaty? what this initiative means is that one million signatures collected in a significant number of member states mean that the european commission can be asked to come forward with an appropriate proposal on matters on which these citizens consider a legal act of the union to be necessary to implement the treaties. in other words, there is no guarantee that citizens' requests will be taken into account. the amendments to the rules of procedure are only intended to regulate parliament's participation in this procedure.

levels, the european economy enters recession and more than seven of its member countries are experiencing negative growth. and yet, while greece is no more than a first stone that threatens to bring down the castle, the revival agenda seems to have been forgotten. at this point, that agenda is clear. the important thing at this point is not to give it an urgency character, but an emergency character, in a situation that threatens to explode. we must act urgently on a set of pillars. firstly, we must have a european marshall plan, with investment that promotes growth, employment and convergence. project bonds are one possible source. secondly, the interest rates at which countries finance themselves must be stabilized. let us at least prepare ourselves to coordinate sovereign mr president, the financial transaction tax should function as a means of controlling and discouraging high-risk speculative activities in the financial sector. it aims to reduce speculation and to increase healthy competition, which is the basis of the single market, and also to generate revenue. the podimata report attempted to bring the european commission's initial proposal closer to the well-known uk stamp tax. we have thus made this proposal more attractive to reluctant member states. it is hoped that the council will also understand the message. the commission proposal applied the tax to transactions by financial institutions located in the european union, but now it is proposed that transactions in european assets, even if carried out by non-european entities, should also be taxed. this will broaden the revenue base and reduce leakage. it is expected that the revenue from the tax will be considered as a source of own resources of the union or of the states, reducing the taxes of the member states, a question which is still to be decided. i would like to conclude, mr president, by congratulating the rapporteur on her excellent work, and i hope that this symbolic text... mr president, we have been advocating a tax on financial transactions on the stock exchange since at least the late 1990s. we think it is an important instrument to combat financial speculation, but it is not enough, because other more courageous measures would be essential, namely the end of tax havens and the most speculative financial products. but this is an important step. and yet we are concerned that the proposal under discussion treats favourably derivatives and other structured products, those where speculation is precisely the most intense, with the minimum rate of the proposal: 0.01%. on the other hand, it seems to us essential that the revenue from this levy should be used to combat poverty and not to replace national contributions to the community budget, which would maintain the same insufficient amounts in the budget and not contribute to the stated objective of increasing funds for social convergence and cohesion.
in writing. in this discussion on a common system of financial transaction tax, there are at least two aspects to be considered: the tax itself its technical characteristics and political implications and the destination of the revenue to be raised from it (which, according to the european commission's forecasts, could amount to eur 57 billion). as for the tax itself, we have long defended it. whether as an instrument of (some) fiscal justice, or as an instrument to combat financial speculation necessary but insufficient in itself (other measures, such as the end of tax havens and the end of the most speculative financial products, are required). despite the general agreement, the proposal raises some reservations and disagreements, such as the relatively more favourable treatment of derivatives and other structured products (precisely where the evidence of speculation is strongest). as regards the management of tax revenues, although the subject is beyond the scope of this directive, it is inseparable from the above discussion. we are opposed to the commission's proposal to channel revenue into the community budget by making a corresponding cut in direct contributions from the member states. this will benefit the large countries in particular and will further undermine the redistributive function of the budget.

in writing. − on 3 may 2010, the writer arturo pérez-reverte wrote the following in his weekly column patente de corso: durante años me crucé en el mar (...) con barcos (...) traídos para la faena. and so, by matching the boils with european legislation, by locating the tuna with airplanes, by surrounding it with ultra-modern technology, by searching ever further afield, in sicily and the libyan coast, and by taking it in cages to the places of concentration and slaughter, cuatro linces have become made of gold, while the bluefin tuna that for centuries has been crossing the strait of gibraltar, a silver and red treasure that has sprinkled its ancestral lake in our cupboards with greek, latin and arabic words, is extinguished without remedy. the transcription i have made is more accurate than any proper word i would add and well illustrates the present state of affairs. i believe that the european union can only try to make up for lost time and adopt measures which will enable it to act effectively to save bluefin tuna. i hope you get it.
in writing. − sustainable management of fisheries resources is one of the european union's (eu) concerns, especially when it comes to endangered species. this report, by raül romeva i rueda, is based on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 302/2009 establishing a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. since tuna is a highly sought-after species, legislation is needed to regulate its capture and not endanger the stocks of this species. in addition, illegal fishing is a serious threat to their recovery. although the international committee for the management of atlantic tuna (icat) has a recovery plan in place since july 2011, the measures have not yet been transposed into european law, undermining the eu's credibility. i understand, however, that the restrictions must apply to everyone and not just to european fishermen. i voted in favour of this report because it combines the economic consequences of the reduction in catches with the fight against illegal fishing and the need to ensure the future maintenance of the species.
in writing. − the main objective of this report is to transpose into eu law the amendments made by iccat, the multilateral organisation for the management of the tuna fisheries, to its multiannual recovery plan for the bluefin tuna stock. the rapporteur stresses the difficulty of establishing a bluefin tuna fisheries management plan. the rapporteur also believes that the difficulty in establishing a bluefin tuna management plan may be related to the lack of means (economic, administrative and technological) on the part of iccat to control the fisheries. noting that the iccat recovery plan is less ambitious than the eu internal legislation. concerns are raised about the lack of up-to-date statistical data on the bluefin tuna stock and its validity. the rapporteur approves the commission proposal, with the amendments it has made. we reaffirm the principle that decisions on the management of living marine resources should be based on scientific knowledge and that this should be supported by as sound data as possible. this report had that concern. that's why we're here. we would, however, like to stress the rapporteur's own reservations on the above points, which should be addressed in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution which provides for the reduction of fishing quotas and the strengthening of controls on the catches of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. there is evidence that illegal fishing accounts for more than half of the total catch in the european union, and new rules are urgently needed to oblige member states to ensure that their national observers monitor all active trawlers. previously, only 20% of ships were inspected. reducing fishing quotas and fleet size, extending protection periods for patrol vessels and increasing surveillance will help to deal with a species threatened by overfishing.

in writing. − at its 2010 annual meeting, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) adopted a recommendation to amend the multiannual recovery plan for the eastern bluefin tuna stock. the plan aims to strengthen measures to reduce fishing capacity and measures to control catches. the proposal for a regulation aims to transpose this recommendation of iccat, to which the european union is a contracting party, into european law. the proposed plan is less ambitious than eu legislation and iccat must also anticipate the important issues within its remit. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. the report, drawn up by dominique riquet, concerns the proposal for a recast of the european parliament and council regulation on the accelerated introduction of double-hull or equivalent construction requirements for single-hull oil tankers. every day, millions of barrels of oil are transported across the oceans. in fact, the sea route remains the main 'highway' for large oil tankers. the safety of hydrocarbons transported by sea is a matter of concern to citizens in general and environmentalists in particular. we all remember the ecological catastrophes caused by the black tides following the sinking of oil tankers such as the erika in 1999 and the prestige in 2002. since most tankers use the single hull system, which in the event of a spill immediately causes direct spillage into the water with serious consequences for marine flora and fauna, it is understandable that the most effective solution is to equip these vessels with a double hull. i therefore voted in favour, taking into account the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, which considers that the proposal is merely a codification of the existing texts without any substantive changes.
in writing. − the introduction of double-hull construction requirements or equivalent design standards for single-hull oil tankers is a matter of great importance, particularly in view of the well-known cases of the erika in 1999 and the prestige in 2002, which caused extremely serious ecological disasters. the objective of this regulation is therefore to reduce the risks of accidental pollution by hydrocarbons in water. in the event of damage to the chaparral as a result of collision or stranding, the contents of the cargo tanks are expected to be less likely to spill. this is a matter of obvious relevance and the steps are now relevant and necessary. that is why we supported the report. it also seeks to limit the duration of the commission's powers to adopt delegated acts to five years and to set out the conditions for the extension of those powers. a report is also requested so that parliament and the council have regular information against which to evaluate future proposals. as regards objections to delegated acts, parliament or the council will now have two months for the extension of the deadline, which will give a much more realistic total of four months to implement an objection.

in writing. - i approve this report, agreeing that both parties, the european union and mozambique, should conclude a new protocol, with the consent of the european parliament. this new protocol is a model for relations with third countries, since it imposes conditionality clauses that apply to the annual financial allocation, with particular emphasis on respect for sectoral support for the human rights support programme, which may imply its suspension.
in writing. − on 2 january 2012, a new protocol was concluded between the european union and the republic of mozambique. this protocol allows access to a total of 75 european union vessels. spain, france, portugal and the united kingdom are the member states concerned by these fishing opportunities. the agreement with mozambique is strategic in that it guarantees the continuity of the european fleet's fishing zone in the indian ocean and can be an excellent alternative, given the increase in piracy in other exclusive economic zones further north. the new protocol promotes responsible and sustainable fishing and allows the promotion of a cooperative relationship based on respect for the laws and regulations in force in the eu and mozambique in the field of fisheries. in accordance with the mandate received from the council, clauses on the conditionality of annual payments were added to the protocol, in particular as regards respect for the programming of sectoral support and human rights, and their application may be suspended in the event of non-compliance with the conditions laid down in the protocol. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that sustainable fishing practices, greater transparency in identification procedures and improved monitoring and control infrastructures for fishing activities in the exclusive economic zone of the republic of mozambique should be promoted. i believe that the joint committee should take concrete steps to increase the number of calls by eu vessels in mozambican ports and thus promote local employment. the joint committee should also ensure a fair distribution of the allocation of aid to mozambique's fisheries and maritime policy, to the development of coastal populations living off fishing and to the setting up of small businesses at local level.
in writing. - the balanced management of fisheries resources and consumer needs require the union to diversify its fisheries resources and, consequently, to conclude agreements with a variety of partners. mozambique has been among these partners since 1987. unlike other international actors who are only concerned with the prey of resources, the european union seeks to involve local fishing communities and contribute to their development. this social and community dimension must not be left out of european priorities, because only in this way can we ensure not only the renewal of fisheries resources through the adoption of good practices but also the support of the populations for european fisheries. mozambique enjoys a privileged position in the indian ocean and has very strong historical and cultural links with europe, particularly portugal, which can be important in a context where it is intended to implement a partnership that is operational, efficient and that holds all parties involved to account.
in writing. − the european union (eu) and the republic of mozambique have partnership agreements in various areas, including fisheries. in view of the mozambican territorial waters and their resources, this is a protocol of mutual interest. the eu, because its citizens can enjoy the species in those waters; mozambique, because it will benefit from the eu financial resources it badly needs to carry out the reform and development programme that the country badly needs. the recommendation under examination concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion of a new protocol laying down the fishing conditions and financial compensation provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of mozambique. the new protocol, which will apply from 1 january 2012 to 31 december 2014, will allow european shipowners (43 fishing vessels and 32 longliners) to continue to benefit from fishing licences for mozambican waters, while promoting a policy of sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. in addition, the republic of mozambique will receive a financial contribution of € 2 940 000.
in writing. - this report approves the conclusion of the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and mozambique. the agreement provides for a contribution of eur 980 000 per year, of which eur 520 000 relates to access for european vessels to the mozambique fishing zone and eur 460 000 to support mozambique's sectoral policy. the reference tonnage of 8 000 tonnes was also set, which was lower than the previous agreement. this allows access for a total of 75 eu vessels, of which 43 are purse seiners and 32 surface longliners. the member states concerned by these fishing opportunities are spain, france, portugal and the united kingdom. the rapporteur highlights the amendments to the protocol to reflect the latest developments in the mozambican national fisheries legislation. as regards the obligation to take on board mozambican seamen, it is further established that this includes, inter alia, freedom of association and effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining, as well as the elimination of discrimination in employment and occupation, and that the salary may not be lower than that of crews of national ships, nor than the ilo standards. we supported the conclusion of the agreement, but stressed the need to increase sectoral support and its results.
in writing. - i have tabled my vote in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the new protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of mozambique. the agreement states that despite the reduction in the fishing quota, the financial compensation paid to mozambique has increased from eur 250 000 to eur 460 000 per year to support the fisheries sector. it provides for the licensing of fishing opportunities for 75 european union (eu) vessels from portugal, spain, france, italy and the united kingdom. the agreement also emphasises sustainable fishing and control and obliges eu vessel owners to employ local seafarers.

in writing. - i support this ambitious proposal because i consider it to be an essential part of our way out of the crisis. the introduction of this system will make the global financial sector more stable, less time-based and more focused on financing the real economy. two important amendments introduced by us, the socialists and democrats in the european parliament, are undoubtedly those concerning the right of issue, which ensures that a non-european investor will be forced to pay this tax if he buys a financial instrument launched in the european union, and the second, concerning the right of ownership, which ensures that the instrument cannot be transferred unless the fee is paid.
in writing. − at a time when european citizens are facing significant tax increases as well as severe cuts in wages and pensions, the financial system, which is largely responsible for this crisis, remains virtually exempt from taxation of its activities and transactions. on the other hand, the serious financial difficulties faced by many member states prevent them from addressing future challenges, such as financing growth and sustainable development. we need tax alternatives that are fair and do not punish citizens any more. the european commission estimates that the financial transaction tax could generate up to €57 billion in revenue, allowing investment to shift from speculative transactions to growth-generating production. in implementing this proposal, some precautions need to be taken to prevent tax evasion and not to shift the costs onto consumers and citizens. given that this tax should be applied as widely as possible and that it benefits the eu as a whole, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - the current economic and financial crisis, which is slow to disappear, has, as we all know, its origins in the financial sector. a rogue industry that has bankrupted thousands of businesses and thrown millions of people out of work. if the financial crisis was triggered by the financial economy, it is only fair that this sector should also pay a share of the crisis and not just the citizens, as is happening at the moment. the report under discussion, which was prepared by anni podimata, deals with the proposal for a council directive on a common system of financial transaction tax (ftt) and amending directive 2008/7/ec. i voted in favour of this proposal because it improves transparency and relieves the citizens by means of a fair contribution from the financial sector. i hope that the ift will be approved at the next meeting of the eu's finance ministers in july.
in writing. − we generally support the proposal to create a financial transaction tax. we've been defending him for a long time. whether as an instrument of (some) fiscal justice or as an instrument to combat financial speculation, it is necessary, but not sufficient in itself. we have reservations and disagreements about certain specific aspects of this proposal. while these reservations and disagreements have not changed our vote, they could strongly influence our position at later stages of this debate, such as on the management of tax revenue (an issue which goes beyond the scope of this directive, despite the unacceptable consideration that it was included by the majority of parliament in this regard). the principle that tax revenue should replace part of national contributions to the community budget, reducing the direct contributions of the member states, is unacceptable to us. this principle will maintain a budget of poverty, while at the same time providing relief to the richest countries with higher gni (including those with a larger transaction market), thus calling into question the redistributive function of the budget and, with it, the proclaimed (but never implemented) principle of economic and social cohesion. we also disagree with the relatively more favourable treatment given to derivatives (which are more prone to speculation).
in writing. - i am opposed in principle to the introduction of a european tax which would override those of the member states and would also place a tax burden on more people than in many countries, where austerity has increased all contributions. in addition, taxation is an important instrument for governments from an economic and financial point of view, and i was against the idea of a european tax when i campaigned for the last elections for which i was elected.
in writing. − i obviously voted in favour of the creation of a financial transaction tax (rel. podimata), which i have long advocated, even when it was politically incorrect (as happened in the 2009 election campaign). firstly, it is a means of combating financial speculation, especially in the case of high-frequency financial transactions, which is a huge asset in these times of increasing global financialization of the economy. secondly, the tff can - and should - act as the union's own financial resource, thus partly strengthening the firepower of the community budget and partly reducing national contributions, which are currently a burden on national budgets, which are under enormous pressure from budgetary consolidation programmes. in short, it is a remarkable contribution to the strengthening of the financial and budgetary integration of the european union.
in writing. − according to european commission estimates, the financial transaction tax could generate revenues of up to €57 billion, allowing investment to move from speculative transactions to growth-generating production. i voted in favour of this report which envisages this alternative taxation, which no longer penalises citizens, is for application in the eu27 benefiting the eu as a whole and therefore aims to be fairer taxation.
in writing. − at a time when european citizens are facing significant tax increases as well as severe cuts in wages and pensions, the financial system (partly responsible for this crisis) remains largely exempt from taxation of its activities and transactions. on the other hand, the serious financial difficulties faced by many member states prevent them from addressing future challenges, such as financing growth and sustainable development. we need tax alternatives that are fair and do not punish citizens any more. according to european commission estimates, the financial transaction tax could generate revenues of up to €57 billion, allowing investment to be shifted from speculative transactions to growth-generating production. in implementing this proposal, however, some caution is needed to avoid disproportionately disrupting the european financial system, preventing tax evasion and not shifting the costs onto consumers and citizens. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is justified to introduce this tax.
in writing. the global financial crisis has spread rapidly to the real economy of countries, with profound consequences for the social, economic and even political systems of some countries. state intervention in some financial institutions as a last resort has necessitated large expenditures of public funds. for this reason, and because of the implementation of serious austerity measures that affect the daily lives of european citizens, i agree that the financial sector should contribute to the costs of this crisis. the application of a financial transaction tax has as its main objectives: to make the financial sector pay the costs of this crisis, as other sectors do; to discourage highly speculative and risky activities and to reorient the sector towards long-term productive investments; to implement a complementary measure to financial market regulation, avoiding future crises; and finally to generate additional revenue for eu own resources or associated with eu public policies and goods, in particular development aid, combating climate change. however, for it to have a multiplier effect, it must be implemented in as many countries as possible. the eu must therefore take the lead in applying this rate among member states, in order to create a progressively global dynamic.
in writing. the principle of this tax, which we have long advocated, is important in combating financial speculation. however, it will certainly be ineffective if it is not accompanied by other decisive measures such as the end of tax havens and speculative financial products, in particular derivatives. we have some concerns about this report and the commission's proposal for a directive. first, derivatives and other structured products, where the greatest volume of speculation is concentrated, are those to which the lowest rate applies. secondly, we are totally opposed to the possibility of the revenue from this levy being used to replace national contributions in the community budget, since this does not strengthen the community budget, but only relieves the budgets of the countries with the highest national contributions, which are precisely those which benefit most from the internal market and the liberalisation of markets. on the other hand, we think it would be fairer if the primacy of revenue were due to the states with which the products are primarily associated, irrespective of the tax residence of the institutions concerned. we are faced with a fair measure, but one which, dissociated from the necessary change in the economic policies of the eu, will have little or no effect.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering it essential to balance trade relations between two of the world's largest trading blocs: the european union and china, and the need for growth stated by the chinese authorities, based on the increase in living standards and the corresponding increase in domestic consumption, can bring great economic opportunities for europeans. however, we must not forget the main reason for this imbalance: european companies cannot invest in china today on the same terms as chinese investors invest in europe. in addition, there are still trade barriers to access to chinese markets, a lack of equality in public procurement, a lack of intellectual property protection that discourages european investors based on new technologies, and restrictions imposed by the authorities on chinese raw materials. i therefore support greater economic cooperation between the european union and china, but only if european companies have the same conditions in the chinese market as chinese investors have in europe, otherwise we will only be further aggravating the imbalances between the two economic blocs.

in writing. - despite the question mark in the title of the resolution, i believe that it is now clear that there is a real trade imbalance between the european union and china, which, despite the internal changes it is undertaking, is still far from being a market economy. the differences in access to their markets by external investors, as well as in workers' rights and levels of social and environmental responsibility and accountability, which have justified the relocation of formerly european-based industries, are also evident. in view of this clear disadvantage between the two, the european union should seek to ensure greater reciprocity in its trade relationship with china. it has the opportunity to give a clear signal of openness and to demonstrate the extent to which it is ready to work with the european union and other international actors to develop a freer and fairer economic order.
in writing. - for several years, we have heard that china was a sleeping giant. it turns out that this giant has woken up and is dominating the world commercially. its economic growth, and consequently its gdp, is among the highest on the planet. trade between the european union (eu) and china - although in the interest of both sides - is proving to be highly unbalanced with the balance of trade tilting towards the chinese side. although europe's export potential to china is high, the cost of factors of production, starting with labour, is unparalleled. furthermore, we cannot consider china a market economy. the rights of workers are not respected, nor are the rights of authors, and there are no concerns about the environment. therefore, china has been delaying its accession to the world trade organization (wto). while i am not in favour of closing the european market to chinese products, i believe that in the next partnership agreement we must demand reciprocity and respect for eu principles and values. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by marielle de sarnez and i hope for reciprocity in mutual market access.
in writing. - this report proposes to increase eu investment in the chinese market, which it considers to be blocked by non-compliance with the market economy criteria as defined by the wto. virtually the whole report is a critique of china's protectionist trade policies. it urges china to open its markets and allow trade liberalisation subject to wto rules. among other things, it criticises chinese export subsidies but refrains from doing the same with regard to europeans. as we said during the debate, this is a view and a path which we unequivocally reject. so, of course, we voted against this report. we cannot ignore the serious consequences of free trade. we cannot ignore the fact that the eu's common commercial policy has deprived the member states, especially those with weaker economies, of a very important instrument for defending their interests in trade. the offensive interests of the stronger economies and their economic groups have prevailed, leaving the weaker ones unable to safeguard specific, weaker interests and productive sectors. with china, or with any other country, trade relations should be oriented towards complementarity and not competition, which is the spirit of free trade.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this recommendation by the european parliament. the eu is the first destination for chinese exports, which increased by 39,5% between 2009 and 2010, with china being the eu's second largest trading partner. the increasing development of china's economy and its accession to the wto imply increased responsibilities to play a full and positive role in the world economic order. china joined the wto in 2001 and must respect wto rules by liberalizing trade and opening up its markets. however, their efforts in this direction are still not sufficient. china does not meet the market economy criteria as defined by the wto. the commission should apply the principle of reciprocity to the eu's common trade policy with developed and emerging countries, such as china, in order to restore fair competition. eu-china relations will develop on the basis of partnership and mutual benefit, not bitter competition.
