in writing. − this own-initiative report sets out the causes of trade imbalances and the main obstacles to trade, stressing that reciprocity on the part of the chinese authorities is the solution to ending the problems of access to the chinese market for european companies. the problems facing european investment in china are many, including: barriers to entry and protectionism; limited access to public procurement due to complex bureaucracy, lack of transparency and competition and rules contrary to international law; violations of intellectual property rights, protectionist measures on european participation in technology companies; restrictions on the export of rare raw materials; overvaluation of the yuan which leads to increased investment in europe and the purchase of advanced technologies and european sovereign debt. for there to be a true partnership, the principle of reciprocity must be accepted and applied by both sides. the same conditions of access and the application of international standards for the reinforcement of the cooperation agreement signed in 1985. i also think it is important that there should be more coordination between the member states so that bilateral agreements do not weaken the position that the eu must take in the face of these problems.
in writing. - this report is a criticism of china's protectionist trade policies, seeking to pressure china to open up its markets and allow trade liberalisation subject to wto rules. we voted against this report because of the disastrous and harmful consequences of free trade, which leaves the countries with the weakest economies without the possibility of defending their commercial interests and their productive sectors. we are in favour of a foreign trade policy which is not competitive but complementary and cooperative.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that in order to ensure a wide range of effective remedies, natural or legal persons other than institutions or bodies of the union and the member states should have a pre-litigation remedy before the european parliament, so that they can challenge decisions taken or in force. i also stress the need to respect the separation of powers in order to avoid abuses of legislative, executive and judicial powers, which must be kept separate from each other.
in writing. - the right of inquiry is an important aspect of the european parliament's power of scrutiny. the treaty of lisbon has changed the institutional balance and strengthened the political dimension of parliament. article 14 tfeu expressly provides that parliament exercises political control functions. the report, which i have supported, therefore argues that committees of inquiry should have the means to carry out their role of examining allegations of breaches or maladministration in the application of union law, in line with the case law of the court of justice. furthermore, all conclusions of an investigation should be based only on elements of evidentiary value. a committee of inquiry should therefore be able to carry out, within the limits of its mandate, any inquiry it deems necessary for the performance of its duties. it should also be able to summon any person whose testimony or knowledge is deemed necessary to support the investigation in question. finally, it is noted that witnesses duly summoned are required to respond spontaneously, fully and honestly to questions put by members of the commission. in the same vein, failure to comply with these obligations should entail the application of appropriate sanctions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because i consider that committees of inquiry should have the means to examine allegations of breach or maladministration in the application of union law; that all conclusions of an inquiry should be based solely on evidence of probative value; that committees may carry out any type of inquiry, provided that the rules are clear and established in advance; request documents, hear officials and other agents of the union or of the member states, call witnesses and request expert reports.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the methods of exercising the right of inquiry. the proposed improvements are linked to an appropriate legal framework to ensure that the political control exercised by the european parliament is serious and effective and is in line with the expectations of european citizens in terms of democratic accountability and good governance.
in writing. - the european parliament's powers have been strengthened by the treaty of lisbon. the logical consequence of this strengthening is the possibility of adopting a regulation which seeks to give operational substance to the role of committees of inquiry, to strengthen their potential scope of action and the means at their disposal so that they can operate with dignity, rigor and efficiency, in the light of what is already happening in other parliaments. i would point out that such committees must take account of the right of the respondents to contradict themselves. i would like to recall a few less encouraging incidents in the course of hearings of candidates for the post of commissioner, in which they were subjected to less than appropriate behaviour by some members who misused the statements made. i therefore hope that the desirable strengthening of the operation of these committees will be counterbalanced by a responsible use of this instrument which is both useful and fair.
in writing. - this report aims to create the conditions for strengthening the european parliament's (ep) powers of inquiry, which have been strengthened by the treaty of lisbon and the resulting removal of powers from the institutions of national sovereignty. the strengthening of the ep's powers of inquiry does not enhance its legitimacy, nor does it guarantee the political adequacy that should be associated with it. the examination of allegations of breach or maladministration in the application of eu law by the ep - an institution whose numerical composition expresses its dominance by the great powers - is from the outset doomed to serve the interests of the forces that dominate it. we cannot agree with the strengthening of the investigative powers of the ep, that is, with the interference of the ep, by forcing sovereign countries to hand over documents, calling witnesses, hearing officials and other agents of the eu and the member states; the obligation of citizens and member states to give the ep access to documents that the ep considers relevant; the application of effective sanctions to be decided by the ep and to be applied by the member states. although the report is in favour of the separation of powers (political and judicial), the confusion is evident and does not make the ep more democratic.
in writing. - with the adoption of the treaty of lisbon, the institutional balance in the union has been renewed and improved. this proposal for a regulation on the procedures for exercising the right of inquiry of the european parliament and repealing decision 95/167/ec, euratom, ecsc of the european parliament, the council and the commission confirms the right of inquiry as an important element of parliamentary scrutiny by conferring specific, legitimate and clearly defined powers on the committees of inquiry of the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to revise the european parliament's powers of inquiry (david martin report) because it strengthens parliament's power of scrutiny over the government and administration of the european union. this is a timely update of this parliamentary instrument following the treaty of lisbon, which gave the representative assembly of european citizens all the powers of a genuine parliament, in particular with regard to powers of control and political scrutiny. this is an important contribution to the building of a parliamentary democracy in the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the ways in which the european parliament exercises its right of inquiry. i would stress the introduction of the rule that committees of inquiry must fully respect the rights of the persons they ask to testify, in accordance with the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the eu charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. - the right of inquiry is a very important aspect of parliament's power of scrutiny. since the treaty of lisbon has strengthened the european parliament's political control functions, it is justified to strengthen its committees of inquiry by giving them the means to carry out fully their role of examining allegations of breach or maladministration in the application of eu law. the regulation proposed here is precisely concerned with the exercise of the right of inquiry by the european parliament, and it lays down a set of rules which are intended to help improve the functioning and effectiveness of future committees of inquiry. that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - the right of inquiry is an important aspect of a parliament's power of scrutiny. this right is exercised in very different ways by democratic parliaments around the world. the european parliament has used this right with great caution, but the treaty of lisbon explicitly gave parliament the right of initiative. since the procedure has changed, parliament does not amend the old ones but proposes a new regulation. the committees may therefore carry out any type of inquiry, in particular on-the-spot investigations, request documents, hear officials and other servants of the union or of the member states, call witnesses and request expert reports, and have access to all documents and information likely to facilitate their work. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report in plenary.
in writing. - the european parliament's (ep) inquiry exercise is an instrument that takes away the sovereignty of the national institutions, reinforcing the power of the ep. as we know, the ep has a majority of members from the great powers, so the suitability of this instrument is in doubt. it is the interests of the great powers that will be best defended here. we are totally against the strengthening of investigative powers, which are nothing more than interference in the affairs of other countries, against the fact that citizens and member states are obliged to hand over relevant documents to the ep, and against the application of sanctions by the ep.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i am pleased to have the opportunity today, on behalf of high representative/vice-president ashton, to discuss the situation in guinea-bissau, and i welcome the attention that the european parliament is giving to it. the current crisis in guinea-bissau clearly reveals once more an attempt by the military to get involved in civilian affairs and gain control of the political affairs of the country. the country remains one of the poorest in the world, ravaged by drug trafficking, and its problems directly affect europe through the drug trade. the way to a solution is to persuade the military to step aside and to reform the army. only then can the country be ruled by civilians legitimated by free and fair elections. the eu strongly condemned the military coup in guinea-bissau on 12 april 2012. we called for the immediate re-establishment of the legitimate government and for the completion of the presidential elections in compliance with the law. we welcome the adoption on 18 may of unsc resolution 2048/2012 on guinea-bissau, imposing individual sanctions on coup leaders and demanding the immediate restoration of the constitutional order, including a democratic electoral process, the return of the military to barracks and their withdrawal from political affairs. the un security council also underlined that those responsible for the human rights violations must be held accountable, and that any lasting solution to instability in guinea-bissau should ensure that those responsible for politically-motivated assassinations, other serious crimes and breaches of constitutional order are brought to justice. we reiterate our strong condemnation of the coup, and encourage all stakeholders to work within the framework of security council resolution 2048 with a view to agreeing on an inclusive road map with agreed benchmarks and a calendar for the return to constitutional order, the implementation of security sector reform, fighting against impunity, combating drug trafficking and the removal of any army grip on power. we stand ready to actively support mediation efforts in the current crisis towards the identification of an inclusive transitional arrangement. we renew our call for the immediate release of all illegally detained persons and for the immediate suspension of the military command’s prohibition on persons, including members of the former government, leaving the country. the eu has already adopted sanctions against six members of the military command and is ready to extend the list to other persons, military and political, who are de facto governing the country and may be responsible for human rights violations and abuses, including arbitrary detentions, ill-treatment during detention and violent repression of peaceful demonstrations, as well as looting and mismanagement of public funds. we already suspended most of our aid last year, and the primary condition for its resumption is local agreement to reform the security sector. we are also concerned about the deteriorating human situation and the constant risk of violence. moreover, we are concerned about the possibility of arrangements that would allow the current leaders of the armed forces to continue to threaten or control the civil powers. democratic stability in guinea-bissau requires the removal of the threat represented by the armed forces, and the reform of the security sector remains an urgent necessity. those responsible for anti-constitutional behaviour or crimes must be held to account; any agreement must be inclusive and democratic; the military must not be allowed, in any case, to dictate who does or does not participate in politics. we are monitoring the latest political and security-related developments in this light. the international community needs to stand united. in this regard, the high representative has encouraged ecowas and the au to bring the concerned partners of the international community together to mobilise coherent political and financial support for the roadmap for return to constitutional order and security sector reform. to this end, a contact group of the international community could usefully be launched.

mr president, the industrial societies are built on the consumption of enormous amounts of energy and increasingly scarce mineral resources. many of them are now strategic in nature and their management must be guided by the imperative of safeguarding the public interest, taking into account the needs of present and future populations. the reduction of consumption, reuse, recycling and the efficient use of resources are all imperative needs, but their pursuit cannot be left to the whims of the market and its expectations of profitability, as some seem to want. the sustainable and efficient use of resources requires a profound change in current production and consumption patterns. for example, we must question free trade and the unsustainable flows of energy and materials associated with it, we must focus on local production and consumption, short supply chains, public transport. what is not worthwhile is trying to paint a system green that has already revealed to society its unsustainability.
the only way to growth and jobs in europe is through a resource-efficient europe, as this increases its competitiveness and creates new sources of growth and jobs in a number of sectors of activity, many of which are not yet properly exploited in the eu. in addition, it generates greater cost savings through more efficient resource management, marketing and innovation processes in their life cycles. we must therefore support a europe which is increasingly efficient and competitive on the world stage. the eu must make better use of resources for the sake of the environment and its future economic growth. we have set ambitious plans to tackle this issue, it is now up to member states to rise to the challenge and strive for resource efficiency. this would mean economic growth, job creation and environmental protection. the member states should converge towards polluter-payer taxation, which would stimulate environmental protection and technological innovation and would allow for cuts in other taxes, such as labour taxes. inefficient use and waste of resources should be more severely penalized in order to help boost competitiveness while preserving the environment.

in writing. report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation laying down general provisions for the granting of macrofinancial assistance to third countries. the eu's macrofinancial assistance was launched in 1990 to provide assistance to third countries experiencing short-term balance of payments difficulties. to date, 55 decisions on macrofinancial assistance have been adopted for 23 countries, amounting to a total of eur 7.2 billion, in the form of grants or loans or combinations of both. since macrofinancial assistance is one of, if not the main source of external financing for many third countries, i believe it is essential to create a formal legal instrument for the granting of such aid, so that it is implemented in a harmonised and regulated manner.
in writing. - since 1990, macrofinancial assistance (mfa) has supported third countries in short-term balance of payments difficulties. this aid can take the form of grants or loans, or combinations of both, and has been given 55 times to 23 different countries. this report seeks to make the amf more effective and adopts and sets out clear rules and conditions for the payment of the amf. i agree that more effective and faster solutions should be sought for the use of this instrument, which is essential to help neighbouring countries in difficulty.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to create a formal legal instrument for the granting of macrofinancial assistance (mfa) to third countries and to create a faster, more efficient and harmonised decision-making process for each operation. this requires agreement on rules and conditions between the eu institutions, updating some of the rules on the geographical scope of the amf and harmonising decision-making with other external financial assistance instruments. parliament has today adopted a document, with my vote in favour, which states that the amf should generate added value from the eu and be granted only when the eu has the possibility of bringing something useful. for example, by decoupling the amf from the existence of an imf programme, the eu will have greater freedom to provide added value and can take a leading role in operations. therefore, in most cases, the eu contribution should not fall below a minimum percentage, ensuring such added value and facilitating countries' access to the benefits of the mfa.
in writing. − the eu's macro-financial assistance (mfa) was established in 1990 to provide resources to third countries experiencing temporary balance of payments difficulties. this assistance may be provided in the form of loans or grants or a combination of both. the eu assistance programme must always be linked to the financial assistance provided by the imf, which is about 10% of the imf programme. we voted against this report because macrofinancial assistance is linked to the imf criteria, the same criteria which condemn countries to poverty through financial discipline, structural adjustment and the economic and social conditionality required. the financial assistance is mainly intended to finance the imf's recommendations and its policy of structural adjustment, i.e. the same neoliberal policies that led to the economic and financial crisis and are aggravating it are being pursued. what is needed are policies of economic cooperation and not blackmail operations on countries in economic difficulties.

in writing. the resolution also calls on the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's external action is coordinated. it resumes its usual policy of interference and manipulation of facts, seeking to conform them to the view of reality that best serves the interests of the major powers of the eu. yulia tymoshenko was at the forefront of the colour revolutions in ukraine, driven by the support of the eu, the us and nato. the current, recalcitrant power refuses to fulfill the role that the great powers of the eu/usa/nato had reserved for the country's authorities. it is recalled that ukraine is a pivotal point for the geostrategic interests of some eu powers, particularly in the energy field. the process of liberalization and privatization has led to the unbridled enrichment of a few, in the shadow of the local oligarchy, while the vast majority of the ukrainian people have been left with the prospect of social regression. not a word about that in this resolution... the majority of the ep does not reserve a word.
in writing. − we are all aware that ukraine is a country of strategic importance to the eu, because of its size, its resources, its population and its geographical location, ukraine occupies a unique position in europe, which makes this country a regional actor of the greatest importance, with a significant influence on the security, stability and prosperity of the entire continent, and therefore it must assume its share of political responsibility. we cannot forget that ukraine's record on human rights, its respect for civil and fundamental freedoms and the rule of law, with the incorporation of fair, impartial and independent judicial processes, and the emphasis on internal reforms are fundamental requirements for the development of relations between the european union and ukraine. we must therefore condemn the position of the ukrainian authorities in the resolution of the yulia tymoshenko case, although there is at present a slight openness on the part of the ukrainian authorities.
in writing. - ukraine is a country of strategic importance to the european union. in the context of its foreign and neighbourhood policy, the european union intends to develop its relations with ukraine at various levels: political, economic and cultural. parliament deplored the conviction of yulia tymoshenko and stressed that strengthening the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary and an effective fight against corruption were necessary not only for relations between the european union and ukraine but also for the consolidation of democracy in ukraine. i therefore voted in favour of this joint resolution of the european parliament.
in writing. the resolution also calls on the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's external relations are not compromised by the threat of a nuclear war. the majority of the ep behaves as usual, promotes interference, manipulates facts, creates or exacerbates others, praises former or current allies. so too is yulia tymoshenko, a woman who was at the forefront of ukraine's color revolutions, propelled by eu, us and nato support, and who increased her wealth considerably during her time in power. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it should also be remembered that ukraine has a pivotal role for the interests of the us/main eu powers, notably in the energy field and in the geostrategic field for nato in its encirclement of russia.
in writing. − i approve this report, taking particular account of the findings of the european agency for fundamental rights in its report on homophobia, transphobia and discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity. these results demonstrate the need for the european commission to take appropriate action, in line with the proposal for an annual report on the implementation of the charter of fundamental rights. discrimination on the grounds of sex or gender must be combated, as the european union must defend the fundamental freedoms of its citizens and ensure their protection, guaranteed full respect by all citizens.
in writing. − the right to liberty and the principle of equality are concepts which have shaped western civilization and the rule of law. that is why these states guarantee in their universal declarations and constitutions that no one can be discriminated against on the basis of his or her sexual orientation. this was a fundamental advance in the fight against discrimination and against homophobia. but unfortunately we know that there are still many states which do not accept these principles and which practice true barbarism against men and women on the basis of their sexual orientation alone. that is why this parliament condemns and will always condemn acts of discrimination.
in writing. − the international covenant on civil and political rights prohibits any discriminatory legislation or practice related to sexual orientation. however, even in countries that have signed up to the pact, we have seen violations of the principle of non-discrimination, as recently happened in st petersburg, russia, with the violent attack on a bus carrying lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (lgbt) activists, and in kiev, ukraine, with the beating of two leaders of the gay pride movement. the joint motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 110 (2) and (4) of the rules of procedure, replacing the simple motions for resolutions tabled by the following political groups: epp, greens/efa, s&d, gue/ngl and alde - which i voted in favour of - deals with the fight against homophobia in europe. homophobia, like racism and xenophobia, undermines society and is contrary to the provisions adopted by this parliament, in particular the anti-discrimination and gender equality directives. no one may be discriminated against on the grounds of sexual orientation, either in the workplace or in any other place or member state. this is a fundamental right which must be respected as such, both inside and outside the european union.
in writing. − we believe that, in pursuing the objective of an effective equality policy, it is important to fight, create and strengthen measures and guidelines which, among other things, combat all types of discrimination, in particular on the basis of sexual orientation. this is a very important fight to eradicate homophobia and all acts or defence of acts of hate speech and incitement to discrimination, ridicule, verbal, psychological and physical violence, among others, which deserve our deep condemnation.
in writing. - i abstained from voting on this resolution because i do not agree with many of the points in it. at a time when europe is experiencing serious economic difficulties, i do not think it is appropriate to deal with this very fractious subject now.
in writing. − respect for human dignity is one of the fundamental pillars of society, so homophobia must be eliminated, since the right to difference and freedom of sexual orientation should also be unquestionable rights. i therefore criticise any and all discrimination and violation based on personal choices. i think it is extremely important that these premises be incorporated at the legislative level and, above all, at the institutional level, through education and raising people's awareness. no one should be humiliated, mistreated or discriminated against because of their sexual orientation.
in writing. − the fight for equality and non-discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is a fight of the utmost importance. the facts mentioned in the report deserve the most serious criticism and are part of a very worrying situation which requires reflection and action. we are fighting for another europe, of the workers and peoples, of sovereign nations, equal in rights and duties, where clearly homophobia cannot have a place.
in writing. - i support this proposal, considering that the only way to growth and jobs in europe is based on a resource-efficient europe, as this increases its competitiveness and creates new sources of growth and jobs in a number of sectors of activity, many of which are not yet properly exploited in the european union. in addition, it generates greater cost savings through more efficient resource management, marketing and innovation processes in their life cycles. we must therefore support a europe which is increasingly efficient and competitive on the world stage.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal because i believe it is the european parliament's responsibility to encourage the commission, the member states and industry to move towards a more ambitious agenda which does not simply follow the roadmap but initially defines its priorities and criteria for a new growth agenda. it also considered that at international level the eu should play a role of model by encouraging a new agenda for future growth at the rio+20 conference. the eu must use its political and economic strength to put other parts of the world on the same path towards a green economy. to ensure our well-being and that of future generations, we must respect the limits of our planet and decouple our economic growth from our use of resources.
in writing. − energy efficiency is one of the european union's flagships, the main lines of which have been detailed in the european commission's roadmap for a resource efficient europe. it is also one of the pillars of the 2020 strategy for growth and jobs. i therefore support all measures that can put europe on the path to optimising its energy resources, and even more so to contributing to the creation of jobs and the subsequent well-being of europeans in this sector of economic activity which is really expanding. i believe, however, that it is necessary to take full advantage of the legislative processes under way in this area before moving forward with new measures which may overlap and even destroy the effect of the currents.
in writing. - although some european countries are experiencing a population decline, the reality is that the world population is continuing to grow. in addition, gregarious societies continue to shrink and the number of people with more resources increases, so that the number of people belonging to the middle class is expected to double by the year 2050. this phenomenon entails an increased need for raw materials, which is estimated to increase by 150%. against this background, the need for an innovative approach is evident, which, while promoting european competitiveness and economic growth, provides for a reduction of environmental impacts and implements a green economy where natural resources are managed in a sustainable way. this requires close cooperation between the public and private sectors and better coordination with academic centres of excellence developing projects in the areas of food and energy efficiency. i voted in favour of this report on a resource-efficient europe because it is urgent and undeniable that we should work towards the creation of a green economy. the eu cannot lose its leadership but must instead seize this opportunity to create new jobs (green jobs) and increase its exports.
in writing. − we agree on the urgent need to increase resource efficiency. the report contains some recommendations and comments, which are undoubtedly positive. but unfortunately, like others, this report is a paradigm of a markedly commercial approach to environmental problems. the stated objective is positive. we are concerned about the paths chosen to reach it. and we disagree quite strongly with some of the positions taken throughout the report. for example, the creation of a common and solid agenda between the public and private sectors, which is aimed at opening the door to processes of liberalization of the waste market, with the privatization of waste management and collection. we also reject several of the proposals made in the tax field, as they are presented in this report. the logic of making citizens responsible is emphasised at various levels, both by internalizing the external environmental costs, in accordance with the polluter-pays principle, and by choosing products that are more sustainable, reducing waste and its impacts, stressing that what is really needed is to change the current production and consumption models and the economic system underlying them - capitalism - which is intrinsically unsustainable and predatory on the environment and its resources.
in writing. − europe faces challenges but also great opportunities in terms of resource use, as the eu has the opportunity to reap the benefits of the sudden increase in global demand for pm by enhancing the supply and efficiency of pm, while meeting the needs of european industry and the pm sector. the commission's leadership in 2008 on resource efficiency policy was therefore of the utmost importance, but the commission and the member states still need to move towards its swift implementation. i believe that resource policy and resource diplomacy are of great importance to the eu not only in terms of industrial policy and international trade but also as a cross-cutting issue for different areas of internal policy as well as foreign and security policy. the commission must therefore pay attention to this question, as well as to the energy question. i see here a working area for the european external action service (eeas).
in writing. − the european commission has published two proposals on resource efficiency, namely the roadmap to a resource efficient europe and the 'resource efficient europe - europe 2020 flagship initiative'. in view of the increase in the world population and the evolution of the consumption of goods by the newly developed countries, i believe that it is necessary to draw up an agenda for economic growth aimed at an efficient use of existing resources. i am voting in favour of this report which aims to achieve a resource-efficient europe, and where greater coordination is needed at local, regional and national level. increased sharing of good practice within networks of local and regional authorities related to the management of the structural funds should be encouraged. finally, i believe it is essential that work is carried out to improve the quality of life of the population and to ensure intergenerational solidarity, so that young people have a more prosperous future and a better chance of employment.
in writing. − while the stated objective of this report is positive, it approaches environmental problems in a mercantilist way. we do not agree with the creation of a common and solid agenda between the public and private sectors, which is aimed at nothing more than opening the door to processes of liberalization of the waste market, with the privatization of waste management and collection. the prevailing logic is that of making citizens responsible for the choice of their products. what really needs to be taken into account and changed are the modes of production and consumption inherent in the capitalist system, which exploits the environment and its resources for the benefit of a few.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering it imperative to work on strategies, economic and labour market policies to create more and better jobs for the youngest so as to combat precariousness. i would like to highlight some important proposals to combat unemployment in a strategy articulated at european level, analysing the national past of each member state in terms of labour market, education and training policies, the creation of a youth guarantee to guarantee the right of all young people to a job, apprenticeship or training complementary to work after a period of unemployment of up to four months, national campaigns to combat school leaving, improving the link between education systems and the labour market, adjusting supply to demand for young people or european recognition in terms of formal and informal learning. history has shown us europeans that austerity measures only worsen our economic and social situation, and at this moment the european union must be concerned about economic growth and employment, otherwise we are doomed to fail and to lose a generation of qualified young people.
in writing. - youth unemployment is one of the most terrible aspects of the crisis we are going through. the focus on education and training to improve the skills of young europeans is therefore a key objective and an essential tool for combating unemployment and encouraging entrepreneurship. the youth opportunities initiative is therefore to be welcomed, particularly in its support and encouragement of job creation for young people through specific programmes, and the european youth guarantee initiative which will allocate eur 4 million to the member states to assist them in setting up youth guarantee programmes. if europe is to successfully meet the ambitious goals of the eu 2020 strategy - with a strong focus on innovation, research and training - it will have to invest in better qualifying its young people, opting for education models that are more geared to future integration into the labour market.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution, tabled following the question with request for an oral answer on the youth opportunities initiative, deals with the need to increase the employment rate at european union level, especially as regards youth employment. the economic and financial crisis that has led to the bankruptcy of thousands and thousands of businesses has thrown millions of people out of work and has raised unemployment rates to unprecedented levels: the average rate in the eu is over 10%, with over 22% among young people. these rates vary from one member state to another, and are almost 50% in the countries most affected by the crisis, such as greece and spain. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu must act quickly. the european union has a duty to help the poorest of the poorest, and to help the poorest of the poorest. in addition, there is a need to strengthen support for smes, especially in terms of bank credit and reducing red tape, as smes may be the biggest contributors to solving this problem.
in writing. - youth unemployment in the european union is taking on shocking proportions. on average, it is 22.4%, although in some countries, such as portugal, it is much higher. this resolution - which contains positive aspects which we value - follows on from the letter from the president of the commission to the eight member states with unemployment rates well above the eu average, which includes portugal, and the dispatch of action teams with the aim of developing youth employment plans in those member states. it's shocking, too, this hypocrisy. youth unemployment in the eu is not due to any fatality. he's a political decision. a policy decision by those, like barroso, who impose policies that sow unemployment and poverty. there will be no job creation unless there is a decisive break with the so-called austerity policies which the majority of this parliament has been supporting.
in writing. - i voted in the belief that the alarming rise in youth unemployment is a threat to the economic and social future of many young people in the european union and is forcing them to pay a very high price for the crisis. i believe that the fight against youth unemployment requires greater investment in education and training in the eu and i see as a priority the development of a more coordinated strategy between national education and training plans and labour market needs.
in writing. − according to eurostat, in march 2012 the european union had more than 5.5 million young unemployed, with an unemployment rate of 22.6%. the most severe cases occur in greece (51.2% in january 2012) and spain (51.1%), with portugal having a youth unemployment rate of 36.2%. i would like to congratulate the ec on the initiatives of the leonardo da vinci programme, erasmus for the first job and erasmus for all. however, new measures are urgently needed to stimulate youth employment so that europe's young people have the opportunity to demonstrate their academic qualifications and professional skills. the €82 billion of community funds announced by the ec must be restructured to stimulate employment, boost financing for the economy and strengthen the single market. it is also important to adopt the new package of measures announced last month by the ec to create more job opportunities for young people and support entrepreneurship. in the next programming period (2014-2020), it is important to allocate a considerable part of the european union's financial resources to supporting the training and qualification of young europeans, as well as to stimulate the development of programmes that facilitate their entry into the labour market.
in writing. - this resolution follows president barroso's letter to the eight member states with unemployment rates well above the eu average (22.4%), including portugal, and the deployment of action teams to develop youth employment plans in these member states. we are not opposed to the proposals to combat youth unemployment the european youth guarantee, the reallocation of part of the unspent budget of the 2007-2013 structural funds to youth programmes and aid to smes, the increase in co-financing for these eight member states, the implementation of the maternity leave directive . however, on the other hand, the resolution also advocates the deepening of the single market as a potential for job creation, the inclusion of youth unemployment in the european semester, coordination between national education and training plans and the needs of the labour market, investment in labour mobility: measures which are profoundly contrary to the creation of jobs with rights, which we reject outright. there is no job creation unless there is a decisive break with the so-called austerity policies which the majority of this parliament supports through the economic governance policies of the stability and growth pact, the budget treaty.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account the latest studies which show that women earn about 16.4% less than men in the same jobs. although we think that the evolution of history has taken care of equality, we are mistaken, the truth is that inequality has actually been increasing in some member states. i agree with the need for the european commission to strengthen existing legislation by introducing sanctions in order to effectively implement a process of equality between men and women and, once again, the european union must set an example for the rest of the world.
in writing. - the principle of equal pay for men and women, enshrined in the 1957 treaty of rome, is still not fully respected in the european union. the latest available data indicate that on average european women receive about 17% less than men. the causes of wage disparities are complex and multifaceted: direct and indirect discrimination, as well as social and economic factors, the devaluation of women's work, inequality in work-life balance, as well as traditions and stereotypes. i therefore voted in favour of this report which stresses the need for the european commission to review directive 2006/54/ec in order to improve the effectiveness of european legislation, by making the concepts related to equal pay clearer and more detailed, by raising awareness among employers, by improving the availability of accurate statistical data, and finally by introducing the classification of jobs in order to identify possible wage discrimination.
in writing. - as a strong supporter of the principle of equality, i could not question initiatives aimed at protecting women's rights in the workplace, such as this report which advocates the legitimate principle that equal work should have equal pay. in addition to equity requiring equal rights for men and women, the law must also take into account gender-specific needs, which in the case of women is evident in areas such as maternity protection and reconciling work and family life. that is why, in addition to the just demand for equal pay, it is essential that women are not systematically penalized in the workplace solely on the basis of their gender and the fact that they are mothers.
in writing. - the present report, by edit bauer, focuses on a set of recommendations to the commission on the application of the principle of equal pay for men and women for work of equal value. the treaty of rome established the principle of equal pay for men and women. despite more than 40 years of legislation to this end, reality shows that much remains to be done. the wage gap is a reality which becomes more pronounced as people age, especially after the birth of their first child. this situation means that women at the end of their working lives receive pensions that are lower than those of men, thus increasing the risk of poverty among women. in an ageing europe with no measures to stimulate births, maternity and parental leave must not be taken to the detriment of women. the principle of equal pay for equal work must therefore be respected. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, and i hope that the member states, following the recommendations of the court of justice, will comply with and enforce the legislation in order to reduce this wage gap, which according to the oecd stands at 17.1%!
in writing. the report deals with a problem which is unfortunately recurrent, which is not dealt with quickly enough and which, on the contrary, is becoming more serious in many member states. it provides evidence of the gender pay gap in eu countries and proposes measures to tackle it, both in eu policies and in national programmes. we regret that several of the amendments we proposed to this report have not been accepted. they would substantially improve the document, which is thus incomplete in some areas. for example, this report acknowledges that individual hiring widenes wage disparities, but does not advocate collective hiring as the alternative. worse, it contains a paragraph proposing that we study how flexicurity can help to combat wage inequalities when it is well known that it deepens them. the report contains a number of proposals with which we agree: increases in women's wages, financial support for specific programmes to combat wage inequality, and so on. that's why we supported him.
in writing. - i consider that the application of the principle of equal pay for equal work and work of equal value is crucial to achieving gender equality, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − the european parliament has asked the commission to review directive 2006/54/ec by 15 february 2013 at the latest in line with the recommendations set out in the annex to this resolution, with regard to aspects of the gender pay gap such as: definitions, situation analysis and transparency of results, job evaluation and job classification, equality bodies and redress mechanisms, social dialogue, prevention of discrimination, gender mainstreaming, sanctions and simplification of eu regulation and policy. given that, despite the significant body of legislation in place for almost 40 years and the actions taken and resources spent to try to reduce the gender pay gap, progress has been extremely slow and in some member states the gaps have even widened, action by the european union is urgently needed. i voted for the document.
in writing. − this report contains a number of data demonstrating the existing gender pay gap in eu countries and proposals for measures to tackle it, both in eu policies and in national programmes. in this sense, and in view of the large wage gap in the eu 16.4% , it is clear that this report is relevant and necessary. we have proposed a number of amendments to the report, but several of them have not been accepted. the report has several shortcomings that have not been addressed acknowledges that individual recruitment widenes wage disparities, but does not advocate collective recruitment as the alternative; the commission is also proposing to study how flexicurity can help to combat wage inequalities, when no equality can be built by deepening precarious employment links. finally, it should be said that, despite the many reports on the subject, the so-called austerity policies supported by the majority of parliament are putting enormous pressure on wages to fall, which will only help to maintain and deepen wage inequalities.
in writing. - i approve of this report, agreeing with the position that the commission should indicate what actions have been taken with regard to the accompanying measures which have made it difficult for smes in the european union to provide services in switzerland and convince the swiss authorities to revoke the decision requiring foreign service providers to be required to demonstrate financial fitness. these obstacles to european companies by switzerland must be reviewed and corrected if not only the european union but also switzerland are to benefit mutually from the european union's internal market.
in writing. - the swiss decision is contrary to the convergence movement between switzerland and the european union and entails discrimination against nationals of member states in a way that does not appear to be appropriate or proportionate. it is for switzerland to clarify this situation fully and for the union to demand its elimination as soon as possible. the european parliament was right to speak out clearly against this measure. switzerland and the union have everything to gain by strengthening relations and coordinating policies and positions, and much to lose by opting for sterile differences.
in writing. - the restrictions imposed by switzerland on the entry of workers from eight eu member states (poland, lithuania, latvia, estonia, slovenia, slovakia, the czech republic and hungary) are not only highly questionable but also negative for eu-swiss relations. the agreement on the free movement of persons and goods is the cornerstone of the functioning of the european internal market and has been very beneficial for the swiss economy, helping the country to overcome the economic and financial crisis very quickly. with the measures taken, switzerland is in breach of european non-discrimination legislation and is preventing the family reunification of many european citizens. despite almost two years of negotiations, the results are very meagre, and the visit of the swiss president and the minister for foreign affairs to brussels has not accelerated the resolution of the problem, since the announced proposals have not yet been submitted. i voted in favour of this proposal because i do not agree with the discriminatory attitude of the swiss authorities and i urge the government to put an end to this behaviour which calls into question the concept of european citizenship as we approach the year 2013 declared the year of european citizenship.
in writing. - we cannot fail to follow the criticisms made in the report of the recent measures announced by switzerland. but we should point out that the report takes advantage of this denunciation to go on to defend the single market, showing that the concern is less about the democratic aspects and more about the deepening of the process of european integration.
in writing. − the resolution on swiss quotas on the number of residence permits to be granted to nationals of poland, lithuania, estonia, slovenia, slovakia, the czech republic and hungary condemns the decision of the swiss authorities to establish quantitative limits on long-term residence permits to be granted to eu citizens from eight member states that joined the eu in 2004, limiting the free movement of persons as provided for in the 1999 eu agreement. since i consider that the decision is not based on a reasonable legal basis, i have voted in favour of the text of this resolution.
in writing. - the imposition of unilateral quotas on the number of residence permits imposed by switzerland on 18 april on eight eu member states is contrary to the principles of the schengen acquis, as it differentiates between citizens of different nationalities, particularly those from central and eastern europe. the free movement of persons is one of the main achievements of the european area and should not be jeopardised by purely political considerations. in parallel, the safeguard clause of the free movement agreement, article 10, which offers the possibility of unilaterally reintroducing quotas by 2014, should be for all 27 member states. the same clause, on the other hand, applies only to employed and selfemployed persons and can only be applied if, during a year, the number of residence permits granted exceeds the average of the last three years by at least 10%. for these reasons, the swiss authorities cannot claim the application of the safeguard clause, as the above criteria have not been fully met. i think it is important that switzerland should review its position and eliminate all discriminatory aspects of its migration policy.
in writing. − the reality of migration differs between the countries of the european union, and the decision on this policy must respect the sovereignty of each member state, which obviously does not prevent the necessary cooperation in this field at eu level. however, despite the defence of the sovereignty of each member state, we cannot help but follow the criticisms made in the report of the recent measures announced by switzerland. what we cannot but criticise, however, is that the report takes advantage of this denunciation to make the case for the single market, showing that the concern is less about democracy and more about deepening the conditions for the process of european integration.

the six-pack was officially published in the official journal on 23 november 2011, the same day the commission published the two-pack. the two pack is another initiative to strengthen budgetary discipline in the euro area member states. now, after the six pack, the budgetary pact, conditions are being created for increased surveillance of countries even before they ask for aid, the budgetary targets they have to meet are being strengthened, the timetables for the budgetary process are being coordinated. budgetary discipline has been the alpha and omega of the commission's legislative initiative and work, workers and wages the adjustment variable. the basic fact is ignored that if all economies, including those with surpluses, are forced into austerity in a single market, the market will eventually and inexorably contract. all countries try to export to markets that meanwhile close, competing on the basis of crushing wages, the only variable chosen to do so. local demand disappears and unemployment spreads. the growing unemployment and the loss of tax revenue make it impossible to achieve the desired rebalancing of public finances, and the debt of the states is entirely at the mercy of financial operators. the two pack legislative initiative is being developed in this context, precisely when the fourth european economy has just shown its fragility, the representatives of the citizens cannot continue to co-legislate on initiatives that only target this aspect of discipline and austerity, it must be compensated, it must be rebalanced. it is therefore essential that the improvements introduced in the legislative text are now strongly endorsed and strongly supported, they ensure a balance between the short-term objectives and the medium-term needs for correcting imbalances. there is a greater respect for national democracy in the construction of the national budget and the recognition of the need for coordination between member countries, but also an additional respect for social concertation practices at national level. but it is also essential that the commission produces, in the very short term, the road map for the only possible breakthrough in sustaining sovereign debt, which is to manage the debt burden above 60% jointly through a medium- and long-term fund, some coordination in the short-term management of such debt issues and a road map leading to the actual and definitive creation of eurobonds. it is also essential to overcome the bottleneck in domestic demand and the lack of european countercyclical instruments, and an instrument of 1% of gdp for 10 years is therefore proposed to fill this gap precisely. thirdly, it is essential that strategic investment that enables countries to overcome their structural weaknesses is protected when assessing deficit and debt levels and imposing the rules that lead to budgetary rebalancing. we have been working, as is the task of our econ committee and this house, in writing. the european union has set up the european union solidarity fund to show solidarity with the people of regions affected by disasters. the solidarity fund is mainly used in cases of major natural disasters with serious repercussions on the living conditions of citizens, the natural environment or the economy of one or more regions of a member state or of a country applying for accession to the european union (eu). in exceptional circumstances, the eusf may also be mobilised for disasters considered to be 'regional' when a region is struck by a disaster causing damage affecting the majority of its population and having a serious and lasting impact on its living conditions and economic stability. italy submitted the request to mobilise the fund, in response to the floods in liguria and tuscany, which caused serious damage to homes and agricultural businesses, as well as disruption to important transport links and essential public infrastructure networks. the application complies with the eligibility criteria of regulation (ec) no 2012/2002, and i therefore voted in favour of mobilising eur 18 061 682 in favour of italy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of agreeing to the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund (eusf) to address the situation at hand.
in writing. - there has been a dramatic increase in the number and severity of natural disasters worldwide, such as forest fires, floods and landslides, earthquakes, etc. unfortunately, the eu and its member states are not immune to such disasters either, and given the increasing rate of climate change and the increased likelihood of more frequent and more intense natural disasters, maximum solidarity is needed, particularly in the area of assistance operations, as well as the rapid mobilisation of the instruments at the eu's disposal. the eu financial solidarity fund allows for assistance to the people of regions affected by disasters up to a maximum annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. following the floods which affected the regions of liguria and tuscany in october last year, a request for assistance was submitted by italy. the damage caused by this natural disaster amounted to some eur 722,5 million and affected housing, businesses, farms, transport and communications networks and public infrastructure. since there is no doubt as to the eligibility of this application, i support the decision to mobilise the amount of eur 18 061 682 from the solidarity fund.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up in the wake of the devastating floods that hit central europe in the summer of 2002 as a vehicle for expressing european solidarity with the population of eu regions affected by major natural disasters. it has been triggered 48 times and has awarded some €2.5 billion in aid. the torrential rains and floods which hit northern italy last october, causing serious damage to the coastal regions of liguria and tuscany, have left us perplexed and apprehensive, because of their extreme violence and strong destructive power. as a union of states and using the instruments at our disposal to help people affected by natural disasters, it seems to me self-evident to mobilise the eusf to alleviate the suffering of the people affected. a word of appreciation and acknowledgement to my fellow rapporteur josé manuel fernandes for the excellent and rapid work done in the preparation of this report.

in writing. − cooperation between the european union and the latin american region has always been of considerable importance at various levels, notably in development cooperation. it is a region with 180 million people living below the poverty line and with the highest levels of inequality in the world. despite progress, poverty levels remain very high and progress towards the millennium development goals, particularly poverty, job creation and social cohesion, is insufficient. we need to rethink and act more effectively in our policy of cooperation and development with latin america: to address the specificities of each country through a differentiated approach in line with our trade policy, making resources available through the icd for the improvement of living conditions and promoting equity, decent work, reform of judicial systems, the fight against violence and crime, the conservation of biodiversity and sustainable development of the region. to achieve these objectives, i believe that the full involvement of national authorities, regional blocs and civil society is necessary in setting priorities and in pursuing programmes.

in writing. − in a globalised world where money is king, those living in the underworld of crime and corruption find favourable ground in developing countries whose populations often live below the poverty line. some countries in africa, asia, and south america are in this situation. they have economies that depend on the cultivation of narcotics, often exploit sex tourism in clear violation of human rights, and they have a proliferation of parallel economies where fraud and corruption are rampant. the european union, the main donor of international aid to the countries of latin america, is attentive to this phenomenon and has been cooperating with other international organisations. it is worth noting the progress made in some countries which have shown growth of more than 4% of their gross domestic product and are now in a position to move from the poverty agenda to the development agenda. i voted in favour of this report on the definition of a new development cooperation with latin america which, while continuing to support countries living below the poverty line, changes some cooperation procedures from aid to partnership, bringing the relationship between the eu and these countries to a higher level.

in writing. − the lisbon treaty establishes that the union's action in the international context must be based on the principles of the universality and indivisibility of human rights, respect for human dignity and the principles of equality and solidarity. it also states that the union should seek to develop relations and create partnerships with third countries, supporting sustainable development in the economic, social and environmental fields of developing countries, with the primary objective of poverty eradication. it is essential that eu development cooperation policy and, in particular, coherence between union policies play a key role in achieving the millennium development goals and in fulfilling international commitments on human rights, food security and environmental sustainability. it is in the context of these objectives that cooperation between the eu and latin america, a rapidly developing region of the world, should be developed.

in writing. − volunteering plays a major role in the economic and social sustainability of europe. it embodies the core values of justice, solidarity, inclusion and citizenship on which the european union is founded. having successfully completed the european year of volunteering (2011), it is now necessary to pave the way for the development of this activity, which directly contributes to key eu policy objectives such as social inclusion, employment, education, skills development and citizenship. in addition to increasing people's tolerance, it creates human and social capital and plays a very strong role in the fields of humanitarian aid and cooperation, whether in post-crisis or disaster situations or in the sustainable development process across borders. i therefore believe that the commission and the member states should promote volunteering activities by establishing a clear and appropriate legal framework for volunteers, by removing bureaucracies and barriers such as the granting of visas to third-country nationals wishing to enter the union for the purpose of volunteering, by creating synergies with existing organisations, by creating a centralised eu portal for volunteering and the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, as provided for in the lisbon treaty.
