in writing. - voluntarism is, in its simplest definition, goodwill in action. it's free, it's generous, it's free and it's uncommitted. it is also a fundamental pillar of any society, with the work of thousands of volunteers, acting formally or informally in various areas, making a difference in thousands of lives every day. at the moment, there are 100 million european citizens engaged in various volunteering activities, which is a very significant number. the rapporteur now proposes to improve the conditions for volunteering by creating a centralised eu portal dedicated to volunteering, with a specific section on cross-border volunteering, the establishment of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps and the development of a european skills passport. i generally agree with the ideas put forward by the rapporteur, which are in line with the csf, which has always looked at the question of volunteering politically, recognising its undeniable social dimension and seeking to put forward concrete proposals to help volunteers, giving them the dignity and recognition they deserve. i believe, however, that volunteering should be kept as free and unregulated as possible.
in writing. − the report under review, by marco scurria, comes after 2011 was the year of volunteering and focuses on the need to recognise and promote crossborder volunteering activities in the european union (eu). in a european union (eu) that is increasingly fraternal and supportive, crossborder volunteering is becoming increasingly important, especially in view of the current economic and financial crisis and the lack of prospects for its end in the short term. first of all, i would like to welcome the importance which the european institutions intend to attach to this solidarity work, with a view to recognising it and creating the conditions for more citizens to be able to devote themselves to this noble cause in any of the following areas: social, environmental and heritage. since there is no volunteering without organisations, it is essential to adopt a legal framework to promote and encourage the activities of these ngos, in particular by exempting them from vat, simplifying procedures and creating a volunteering passport. i am aware that a big world is made up of small daily acts, so i am voting in favour of this report and i urge the member states to encourage volunteering and to measure its impact on the economy.
in writing. - this report is extensive, detailing various aspects of volunteering. without underestimating the importance and potential of volunteering - which we value highly - we do not fully follow the perspective on volunteering presented here, mainly because of what it may imply in terms of the disempowerment of the state and the underestimation of the role of public policies in a wide range of areas. some risks arising from the distortion and even subversion of the concept of volunteering are not adequately addressed. volunteering can under no circumstances be used to justify or legitimize situations of irresponsibility on the part of the state, such as lack of or poor training in schools, or to extort free work from young people, adults and the elderly. however, we appreciate the fact that almost all the amendments proposed by our group have been accepted. it is important to address some of the problems experienced today by volunteers and the ngos that promote it, such as funding difficulties, bureaucracy and lack of recognition of the activities that have been developed. the report has some good paragraphs on strengthening the financing of associations, collectives and the like. but we are rejecting proposals such as the european statute for associations, as formulated here.
in writing. − volunteering is an expression of active citizenship in all aspects of social life and is a key activity for the development of democratic values, human dignity, equality and subsidiarity. it should therefore be supported by all member states. the figures reveal a body of 100 million european citizens engaged in various volunteering activities, capable of contributing to the production of 5% of european gdp, and these activities being considered by 80% of citizens as an important element of democratic life and a meaningful way for citizens to participate in society. volunteering is thus a precious european heritage.
in writing. − i was actively involved in the european year of volunteering, which i chose as the theme for 2011, and i promoted actions in the azores and brussels. i am pleased to note that all these initiatives organised in the framework of the european year of voluntary activities (2011) have helped to demonstrate the importance of volunteering, a phenomenon involving some 100 million european citizens who are able to contribute to the production of 5% of european gdp. the times we live in and the need for budgetary consolidation threaten the financial sustainability of many ngos, so it is necessary to ensure adequate and stable funding and to simplify administrative procedures. in this context, the european parliament calls on the member states to make an effort in this direction. i also stress the call on the commission to negotiate visa facilitation for third country nationals and to create a centralised eu portal dedicated to volunteering. all these reasons justify my vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − recently, there has been a growing awareness among european citizens of the importance of volunteering. this awareness is reflected in the growing number of citizens who are drawn to this activity, which provides not only personal development and cultural learning but also contributes to the reinforcement of civic values, solidarity and participation in democratic life. member states are therefore asked to apply the provisions of council directive 2004/114/ec on the conditions of admission of third-country nationals for the purposes of studies, student exchanges, unremunerated training and voluntary service. in the same vein, the simplification of visa procedures for persons wishing to engage in volunteering activities, in particular in the framework of the european neighbourhood policy, should also be promoted. in this way, it is intended to increase cooperation between volunteers from eu countries and third countries, in particular in the context of the european neighbourhood policy, as volunteering can provide additional benefits, including the promotion of democracy and the rule of law in third countries. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − this report aims to take stock of the european year of voluntary activities promoting active citizenship (2011), and at the same time to strengthen measures to support volunteering in the eu and beyond. volunteering is an activity that instills essential values in the citizen, namely the promotion of solidarity and equality, which spreads the most humanistic side of the individual, through active participation in society, at all levels. it is therefore essential to remember the importance of the year of volunteering and the implementation of support measures. the rapporteur therefore proposes the creation of a 'european voluntary humanitarian aid corps' which would work in line with existing institutions and structures; a portal which would centralise all information relating to intra- and inter-eu volunteering; tax incentives, in particular for small organisations with limited financial resources; the creation of a special status for organisations which would facilitate cross-border volunteering; and the creation of a european skills passport, which would validate volunteering experience as part of informal training. volunteering is the purest form of active citizenship and a key element for the personal development of citizens that deserves to be supported and developed.
in writing. − volunteering activities face a number of problems both with volunteers and with the ngos promoting it, including difficulties in funding, various bureaucracies and lack of recognition of the activities carried out. these problems need to be solved urgently and this report points to some solutions. however, we cannot but disagree with views that see volunteering as an opportunity for employability, that encourage companies to promote volunteering among their employees and that support the recognition of volunteering as a professional experience. volunteering activities should be undertaken on their own initiative and not as a result of a lack of existing employment. on the other hand, they should never replace jobs and job creation.
in writing. − i welcome this report, as the growing digital innovations and information technology have made cybersecurity an increasingly important priority. i welcome the proposal here for a comprehensive eu cybersecurity strategy which should give priority to the security of critical information infrastructure protection and prevent attacks on systems, strengthening the eu's global cybersecurity engagement.
in writing. − with the increasing use of the internet and information technologies, internet security issues must remain a top political priority for the european union as well as the rest of the world. the data available on cybercrime indicate a significant increase in several european countries. this report, which has been supported by me, calls for the minimum standards of resilience to be updated regularly to protect against any disturbance, incident, attempted destruction and attack. calls on the european network and information security agency (enisa) to coordinate and implement the european cybersecurity awareness months annually; recommends that the commission propose binding measures to impose minimum standards on security and resilience and to improve coordination between national it emergency response teams (cert). the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to introduce a european-wide public education initiative focusing on educating and raising awareness among users of the potential threats posed by the internet. it called on the commission to present a legislative proposal to strengthen the criminalisation of cyberattacks. increasing the resilience of the internet is only possible with a system of international cooperation and international standards.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to strengthen the protection of critical information infrastructures in order to strengthen citizens' overall security, their perception of security and their confidence in the measures taken by governments to protect them, and this strengthening should enhance the lasting integration of european research in order to maintain and strengthen european excellence in this field.
in writing. − the internet and new information and communication technologies are now real drivers of social interaction, cultural enrichment and economic growth. however, the confidence of users in the use of icts depends on the guarantees given to them in terms of security and resilience, as well as on the fact that there is effective enforcement of legislation on privacy and data protection, net neutrality and protection of intellectual property rights. there has been a significant increase in cybercrime in several european countries. the recent cyber incidents and attacks against eu and member states' information infrastructures also clearly demonstrate the need to establish an effective, robust and innovative system for the protection of critical information infrastructures, based on full international cooperation and minimum standards of resilience between member states. it is essential to establish national cybersecurity contingency plans as well as a robust regulatory framework with appropriate procedures and mechanisms to ensure better coordination between national competent authorities and greater consistency in their actions. i support the creation of a critical infrastructure protection service that operates continuously in each member state, as well as the establishment of a common european emergency protocol.
in writing. − in recent years, our dependence on information infrastructures has increased exponentially, making us increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks, which are particularly severe when they target institutional infrastructures and businesses. recent attacks have exposed the vulnerability of institutions and networks that we would have considered to be properly protected, revealing the need for strategies that ensure cybersecurity. as the report states, 'the increasing use and deployment of innovative ict technologies such as the internet and fixed or mobile, high or ultra-high speed cellular networks, smart grids, but also internet services such as cloud computing and the internet of things, all depend on a simple but crucial aspect security, resilience and trust. " the use of all these technologies, which are becoming increasingly essential for institutions, businesses and citizens, depends to a large extent on the implementation of a clear strategy to ensure that these information infrastructures are secure.
in writing. − in the era of globalisation we live in and in view of the increasing use of new information technologies, it is understandable that internet security is a priority for the european union and its member states. from transport systems to industry, and from services - judicial, financial, military or otherwise - it is essential to ensure their security in accessing internet services, as these are critical structures whose collapse would jeopardise not only the functioning of that member state but the functioning of the european union itself. as no state is self-sufficient in this area, international political and regulatory measures are needed to ensure the functioning of the internal market and to increase the security of networks through cross-border surveillance and prevention mechanisms. despite the alert systems, we're aware of cyber attacks. it is imperative to protect ourselves not only from cyberterrorist attacks, but also from possible violations of citizens' privacy and the disclosure of confidential data that jeopardise the security of states. because i believe in and trust new technologies, i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr kalfin on the protection of critical information infrastructures for global cybersecurity.
in writing. − with regard to so-called global cybersecurity, the commission has defined a set of instruments, including the action programme for the protection of critical information infrastructures and the critical infrastructure alert network, which this own-initiative report endorses and promotes the implementation of. we recognise the importance of ensuring that people have the necessary security and protection when using the internet and the infrastructure that supports the service. however, we disagree with security-oriented strategies and policies that restrict freedom of expression and movement on the internet. the report proposes a strong role for the european external action service in this area. it intends to permanently integrate internet security issues into its external relations, including when awarding its various funding instruments, aligning policy orientation and legislative action with its us counterparts. on the other hand, coordinated positions are advocated in international forums under the umbrella of the promotion of fundamental values, in which nato, the un and the world bank, among others, participate. we cannot but point out that the so-called global cybersecurity is part of nato's new strategic concept, a vision which the majority of parliament supports. for all these reasons, we voted against this report.
in writing. − the role of technology has been expanding more and more in everyone's daily lives, from communication to finance and banking, from transport to energy, and from culture to entertainment and health. cybersecurity is thus one of the main concerns and political priorities of the eu and the rest of the world. however, the rapid advances in all information technologies, the emergence of new technologies and their development, make this task very difficult. every effort must be made at global level to protect critical information infrastructures.
in writing. − internet security remains a top political priority for the european union and the rest of the world. the europe 2020 strategy, launched in 2010, included the digital agenda for europe as a flagship policy, set to ambitious targets for the european union's technological development. the increasing use and deployment of innovative technologies depends on a simple but crucial aspect: security, resilience and trust. the rapid development of technology requires that the prevention of internet attacks, remedial responses and resilience of the global network be based on a comprehensive, responsive, flexible, innovative and long-term framework. emphasizing the call in this report for the european network and information security agency and the european commission to participate in the main stakeholder dialogues on the definition of technical and legal standards for cyberspace at international level, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − technology is becoming increasingly important in many sectors of the european economy and in the daily lives of citizens, and the european commission has launched the flagship initiative 'digital agenda for europe' as part of the europe 2020 strategy. i agree with this report which aims to introduce a high level of security and resilience in information and communication networks, services and technologies by adopting new security standards for critical information infrastructures. the aim is to improve protection and knowledge of security breaches in specific sectors of the european economy. i also believe that the european network and information security agency (enisa) should play a more prominent role in cybersecurity issues and should carry out more pan-european exercises to ensure greater security for businesses and citizens.
in writing. − we recognise the importance of ensuring that people are safe and secure when using the internet and the infrastructures that support it. however, we strongly disagree that this statement is part of a set of strategies and policies of a security nature and deeply damaging in terms of employment and freedom of expression for these same populations. these measures are closely linked to the work of the european external action services, which aim to permanently integrate internet security issues into its external relations, including when awarding its various funding instruments, aligning policy guidance and legislative action with its us counterparts. on the other hand, coordinated positions are being orchestrated in international forums under the umbrella of the promotion of fundamental values, in which nato, the un and the world bank, among others, participate. as regards these fundamental values, it cannot be overlooked that the so-called global cybersecurity is part of nato's new strategic concept and that, along with and in alternation with the usa, its central partner, they are orchestrating war after war, under the most diverse political and geostrategic arguments. for all these reasons, we voted against.
in writing. - i support this report, considering that greater coordination between the member states and the european union is urgently needed in order to work together to increase europe's influence in the world in the field of energy and to ensure its supply. it is necessary not only in the energy field, but also in all the other areas that we can call global, that the european union fulfils its duty to speak with one voice in the world, otherwise it will lose its negotiating power and its political credibility in the international arena.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to ensure reliable and cost-competitive access to global energy supply in order to support europe's competitiveness and security in the light of the eu's current policy objectives set out in the 20-20-20 package and the long-term commitment to decarbonise our economy by 2050; because i believe that pooling of efforts in r & d and innovation (rdi) at eu level will allow for better quality and more efficient, economical and dynamic research than if it were undertaken by individual member states; and because i support our continued efforts to seek cooperation with third countries on r & d with a view to maximising mutual benefits at international level.
in writing. − the availability of secure, sustainable and competitive energy is of paramount importance to the eu economy, industry and citizens and is one of the central objectives of european policies. it is worth noting that the eu imports more than 60% of its gas and more than 80% of its oil, facing increasing competition for fossil fuel resources, including from emerging countries and energy producers themselves. in addition, dependence on energy imports will tend to increase over the next decade due to the depletion of domestic resources. experience has shown that bilateral energy relations established individually between member states and third country or transit country suppliers may result in the fragmentation of the internal market rather than in the strengthening of the eu's energy supply and competitiveness. i therefore believe that a fully integrated european energy market, which operates on the basis of solidarity and responds to the challenges of energy supply, is vital. only a coherent and coordinated approach between the member states, the commission and the council will allow for a strong external position of the eu's energy objectives and guarantee a better negotiating position vis-à-vis third countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on cooperation on energy policy with partners beyond our borders, because i support the need for the eu to act in a coordinated way to define a common position in negotiations with third countries and thus guarantee the security of energy supply.
in writing. - the events of the so-called arab spring have made even more evident the energy dependence of which the european union is suffering today and the insecurity which some of its suppliers are experiencing. it is now clear that this over-dependence is a major strategic weakness and that without a coherent and common response by the member states to the challenges they face, they will be more easily constrained in their action and more subject to external pressures. the excessive reliance of some member states on a small group of suppliers increases their exposure and weakness. the diversification of internal and external energy sources and the creation of national and european energy pools, which include energy from a sufficient number of sources to allow competition, should therefore be encouraged. the importance of the energy question is such that it must increasingly be considered as one of the main european priorities and the pursuit of a common policy in this area must therefore be encouraged.
in writing. - the rapid technological evolution we have seen in recent years has led to a significant increase in global energy consumption. despite the growing emphasis on the exploitation of renewable energy sources, the truth is that we remain very dependent on so-called fossil fuels. the report by edit herczog deals with the issue of how to strengthen cooperation on energy policy with partners beyond our borders: a strategic approach to secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply. while our energy partnerships to the east and south are important, the european union (eu) cannot fail to look for other markets, always demanding compliance with community criteria, especially with regard to the exploitation of raw materials and environmental protection. these partnerships should take the broadest possible approach and ensure stable energy flows. i am aware of the importance of energy in all areas and i voted in favour of this report. i hope, however, that the eu will speak with one voice on energy and support the technological development of renewable energy and the installation of such equipment, thus contributing to the relaunch of economic growth and job creation.
in writing. − the whole of this report is based on the idea of implementing and strengthening the internal energy market, the undeniable negative consequences of which have been worsening, particularly since the creation of the energy community in 2006, which established the internal market for electricity and gas. this path is inseparable from the liberalizations and privatizations that have removed this important strategic sector of the economy from the public sphere, with all the constraints that this entails, especially for countries with weaker economies such as portugal. given the current energy dependence of the eu, and the trend towards an increasing population and consumption in the coming decades, this document does not hide concerns about future energy supply. it is vital for the eu powers and their economic groups to secure this supply. not for reasons of vital public interest, but for the old reason that determines their choices (and actions): to pursue capitalist accumulation. to do so, they must not disguise their unbridled imperial ambitions, in the service of which they want to continue to put the european union and its foreign policy, as they have always done, now with this important instrument, the european external action service, created by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. - the european union's energy dependence and the insecurity of some of its suppliers are increasingly worrying. it is becoming increasingly clear that over-dependence is bad if not well used, and that it can only be well implemented if there is a coherent and common energy market approach strategy by all member states. we must therefore commit ourselves to a genuine common policy on energy policy.
in writing. - i have approved this report which calls for closer cooperation on energy policy with partners beyond our borders. europe is a major buyer of energy in world energy markets. while this may be seen as a weakness, it can also be one of our strengths: we are the largest importer and if we take advantage of this fact, act in a coordinated way at eu level and take a firm and common position in negotiations with third countries, we will almost always be in a good negotiating position to exert our power as a strong player in the demand side market. a common negotiating approach, extending our sphere of influence beyond the borders of europe, in particular in the field of energy market rules, can be a plus for all. i have voted in favour of this procedure, highlighting this among other proposals.
in writing. − in september 2011, the european commission presented a communication on security of energy supply and international cooperation entitled 'eu energy policy: closing the gap with partners beyond our borders'. i support this report because i believe that the eu must have a strong and effective position on the international scene, ensuring the energy it needs for its economic activities. at a time when europe imports more than 60% of its gas and more than 80% of its oil, it is important to have better coordination at internal level and effective cooperation with the various international partners. in order to increase energy sustainability and reduce europe's dependence on certain international actors, i believe it is important to diversify the suppliers and sources of energy supply to the european union, and it will also be necessary to promote new forms of energy exploitation, with particular emphasis on renewable energies.
in writing. − the whole report is based on the idea of strengthening, analysing and implementing the internal energy market, the undeniable negative consequences of which have been worsening, particularly since the creation of the energy community in 2006, which established the internal market for electricity and gas. in the face of the current energy dependence of the eu and the trend of increasing population and consumption for the next few decades, this document points to solutions based on more of the same, i.e. more internal energy market, and its full implementation as the centre of all action. the square of the circle is also defended, while ensuring and enhancing security of supply, competitiveness and sustainability in a cost-effective way, continuing a policy of exploiting the energy resources of the eu as well as of third countries, with which the european external action services will take care to ensure that all multilateral and bilateral agreements of the eu [...] fully comply with the rules of the eu internal market. these solutions are being unmasked by those who suffer the disastrous consequences, such as the populations who see the price of energy bills constantly rising and, consequently, access to energy increasingly difficult.

mr president, i would like to make it clear that we regard the council meeting at the end of june as essential and that it is essential to find a european solution to this crisis. the problem, from our point of view, is that we have so far dealt with each of the issues that have arisen in isolation and individually. the time has come for a global solution for europe, a solution which, as president daul has made clear, requires more integration, more cooperation, closer alignment of european policies and a renewed appreciation of the community method. it is essential that growth should go hand in hand with stability, but that we should not abandon the concerns of stability. we therefore count on a european response as a whole, and not on a response divided up for each state or for each region in difficulty.
in writing. more than members of the european parliament, we are citizens of different member states who aspire to a better europe. the european response to the challenges of our time will only be effective if it is based on a robust budget ensuring adequate financing of the union's political objectives, a budget that is flexible, rational and dynamic in the application of the funds distributed among the various headings and a political agreement on the reform of own resources. this is a budget which will not cost the taxpayer more, but which is ambitious and innovative. i believe that only a simpler and more flexible budget will have an impact on the lives of europeans. in particular, i stress the importance of the role of science and innovation, which will contribute to the competitiveness of european industry, particularly smes.
in writing. the guidelines emerging from the european institutions on the direction of the integration process reflect a simple equation. on the one hand, they want to deepen all the things that have been leading to divergence between member states: free competition in the internal market; the stability pact, now strengthened; the liberalisation of international trade; common policies tailored to the needs of just a few. on the other hand, they want to weaken the instruments which could mitigate or, preferably, even overcome inequalities - in which the community budget has a central role. the result can only be one: more divergence, more inequalities between member states, less cohesion. it's a disgrace what's going on in the council. the biggest beneficiaries of the internal market and common policies now want to reduce their contributions to the community budget even further, forcing a squeeze on the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. they want to cut the budget and they want to cut the cohesion funds. and they want to get a bigger share of that cohesion money. this is what is meant by the proposals for conditionality, the 'transition regions' or the modification of the weighting coefficients associated with cohesion. for the others, for the weaker economies, the costs of this integration are increasing and the benefits are decreasing.
the multiannual financial framework of the european union for the period 2014-2020 is increased by eur 49 billion (5,04%), compared to the 2007-2013 mff. the budget for the cohesion policy will be eur 1.025 billion, the largest financial envelope, surpassing the common agricultural policy for the first time. some aspects are accepted by the european parliament and the committee of the regions, such as the intermediate regions, the increase in the budget for territorial cooperation projects, the creation of the common strategic framework and the cohesion fund, which will continue to support countries with a gni below 90% of the eu gni. it should be noted that the first discussion of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 and the new cohesion policy regulations will take place only at the june european council. i think it is essential that the value of cohesion policy is maintained at the same level as in the previous programming period (2007-2013) and that the outermost regions have a financial envelope in the additional specific allocation that is adequate to meet their natural constraints.

in writing. the european court of auditors (eca), made up of the national audit bodies of the member states, is responsible for checking that the community funds, which come from taxpayers, are properly managed in accordance with european law. the court shall consist of one representative of each member state, who shall appoint the president from among themselves. at the moment, it is chaired by the portuguese dr. vítor caldeira. this report, which was written by inés ayala sender, recommends that we approve the appointment of iliana ivanova as a member of the court of auditors. in view of the training and experience of the candidate nominated by the council and the opinion of the committee on budgetary control, i support the appointment of iliana ivanova of bulgaria as a member of the ect. given the importance of the ect's role in the transparency of european accounts, i hope that the new member will have a good mandate, aware that his success will be the success of all eu citizens.
in writing. − the court of auditors is an audit institution, which checks the legality and regularity of the european union's revenue and expenditure and the sound financial management, exercising its functions with complete independence. in this spirit, the appointment of the individuals who make up the committee must be governed by criteria of competence and independence. the council has therefore appointed several personalities from various eu countries to the court of auditors. the applicant submitted her cv, answered a written questionnaire and was heard by the committee on budgetary control, having presented sufficient arguments to justify her appointment to the court of auditors to perform her duties therein in a competent and independent manner. i therefore voted in favour of the name of iliana ivanova.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the appointment of iliana ivanova as a member of the court of auditors. all the data presented for this option, including the replies to the questionnaire for candidates for members of the court of auditors annexed to this report, justified my decision by indicating that the criteria laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union are met and that the members of the court of auditors must be fully independent, and i therefore welcome the appointment of iliana ivanova.
in writing. − section 7 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes the court of auditors as one of the european institutions. created in 1975, its objectives are to control the accounts and improve the financial management of the european union (eu). the court of auditors may carry out audits of any person or organisation responsible for the management of eu funds, and its findings are presented in writing in the form of reports which are sent to the commission and the governments of the eu countries. member states shall submit a proposal to the council which, after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt the list of members of the court of auditors. i am voting in favour of the appointment of iliana ivanova as she fulfils the conditions laid down in article 1 of article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. − i approve these recommendations, agreeing in substance on the eu's role in the un, in particular with regard to global governance, peace and security, security council reform, development issues including sustainable development, climate change, human rights, justice and support for democracy. it is regrettable, however, that no agreement has been reached on the establishment of a united nations parliamentary assembly.
in writing. - the united nations reflects not the reality of 1945 but one which the victors of the second world war still believed existed at that time. unable to change, the un will risk jeopardizing its very survival. while it is true that the worlds of the cold war and american unipolarity were able to coexist with a security council stripped of effective military, demographic, economic and cultural representation, greater doubts arise as to its appetite to continue at the present time. it points to the rise of powerful states in the south and east to the status of emerging powers, the speed and accessibility of the people to the media and calls for a new approach. the best symbolic expression of this new understanding could be the increase in the number of permanent members of the united nations security council and a strengthening of the way in which the european union operates within the un and the way in which its member states are organised within it.
in writing. the report, drawn up by alexander graf lambsdorff of the alde group, contains a proposal for a european parliament (ep) recommendation to the council on the 67th session of the united nations general assembly. the participation of the european union (eu) in the united nations general assembly is always a relevant moment of political intervention in a world-class coordination and monitoring institution and as such should be prepared in light of this enormous responsibility. i voted in favour of this report as it seeks to improve the conditions for eu participation in the un general assembly (unga), whose resolution 65/276 was widely supported and which strengthens the eu's observer status. in addition, it is essential to make known the commitments made by member states on the institution building package of the united nations human rights council (unhrc) and the outcome of the review process. i hope that the eu's participation will make a decisive contribution to the preparation of a post-2015 development framework in the context of the millennium development goals (mdgs), global sustainable development and international humanitarian aid to populations whose survival is at risk for political or climatic reasons.
in writing. - we are faced with a report which contains obvious contradictions. while it is true that international law, the un and its role in global governance are defended, this defence is hardly compatible with the defence positions of nato, the g8, the g20, the imf or the wto. these forums (and others) pervert the world order to which the creation of the un opened the door, with the aim of establishing a new order under the domination of the great imperialist powers. the defence of respect for, promotion of and protection of the universality and indivisibility of human rights is not compatible with support for or complacency in the face of the terrorism of the state of israel against the palestinian people, or the occupation and killing of civilians in afghanistan, among many other examples. we reject the old aspiration of some, expressed here again, to secure a seat for the european union in an enlarged security council, thus seeking to give it a state legitimacy which the eu does not have.
in writing. − in a time of crisis such as the one we are living in, the eu needs to strengthen its cohesion and be a key player in the international political context. given the importance of a strong and stable eu-un relationship for un activities, the eu must be on all fronts to strengthen the international criminal justice system, ensure greater protection and recognition of human rights, promote a culture of democracy and the rule of law, and take a leading role on climate issues by supporting biodiversity and climate protection in developing countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendations addressed to the european council by the european parliament at the 67th session of the united nations general assembly, as i agree with their content, in particular with regard to the recommendation to strengthen the coherence and visibility of the european union as a global actor in the un, meeting the expectations of un members regarding the eu's ability to act and deliver results in a timely manner.
in writing. - this report contains a proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on the 67th session of the united nations general assembly. the eu is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy. the aim is to further enhance the eu's role in this international organisation, either by increasing the representation of specialised agencies in its institutions or by developing stronger public diplomacy. in addition, the themes of maintaining and consolidating global peace and human rights are also focused. the first is to promote the role of mediation and to strengthen the international criminal justice system. as regards human rights, it is expected that there will be a greater effort at international level to ensure that all human rights agreed under the un conventions are considered to be universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated. finally, it calls for greater integration of eu development policies at all levels, with due regard for both human rights and environmental protection. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − in the document adopted today, the european parliament addresses a number of recommendations to the council on the european union's position in the united nations system, with particular attention to issues of global governance, peace and security, international justice, human rights, support for democracy, development and climate change, environmental protection and sustainability. it is also worth noting that the european parliament is urging the council to reach a common interpretation of the modalities of the european union's participation in the work of the general assembly and to move forward with a consensual reform of the security council in order to strengthen its legitimacy. for these reasons i voted in favour of the document in question.
in writing. - it is not possible to highlight all the important aspects of this report - and there are many - but we would like to underline the hypocrisy of those who claim to defend international law, the un and its role in global governance, while at the same time supporting its perversion and instrumentalization, in particular through the role of nato, the g8, the g20, the imf, the wto and other forums which aim to impose a setback on the democratic advance of international relations - represented by the creation of the un - and a world order over the domination of the great imperialist powers. once again, they hypocritically invoke respect for, promotion of and protection of the universality and indivisibility of human rights and the need to strengthen them at international level, when they violate them or are complicit in their violation every day, supporting the state terrorism of israel against the palestinian people and the occupation and killing of civilians in afghanistan, among many other examples. they support the responsibility to protect which can be expressed by the deepening of the processes of interference, aggression and violation of national sovereignty when the interests of the great world powers are at stake. and they defend a state legitimacy that the eu does not have, with the longstanding aspiration to obtain a seat on a larger un security council.
in writing. - i support this report because since 1971 the european union has been granting non-reciprocal trade preferences in the form of reduced duties for goods from developing countries imported into the european market through the system of generalised tariff preferences (gsp). in any case, it is particularly important to draw attention to the fact that the new legislative proposal aims to focus import preferences on the developing countries most in need. in practice, this means that preferences are withdrawn from certain countries, which increases the value of the preferences granted to those who remain covered by the scheme, a process which could be termed consolidation of preferences - this seems to me indeed the most appropriate approach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union should support developing countries which share a common development need and are at a similar level of economic development and which are not classified by the world bank as high-income or upper-middle-income countries or which have a very high or high human development index (hdi). the tariff preferences will certainly help those countries to reach higher levels of development. it will also make it possible to ensure greater consistency between the union's internal and external policies.
in writing. since 1971, the european union has been granting non-reciprocal trade preferences in the form of reduced duties for goods from developing countries imported into the european market through the generalised system of preferences (gsp). this approach is an integral part of its common commercial policy, in line with the general provisions governing the eu's external action. that is why, and because aid to developing countries in the form of reduced tariffs must cover as many countries as possible that need it, i advocate the maintenance of the calculation criteria which allow the beneficiaries to be identified, without change.
in writing. the united nations conference on trade and development (unctad) recommended in 1968 the creation of a generalised system of preferences (gsp) with the aim of the more developed countries supporting the developing countries by granting trade facilities. in 1971 the european community pioneered the implementation of a gsp which has become one of the main methods of cooperation in international trade to combat poverty. some 176 countries have benefited from this gsp, but it is necessary to revise it by introducing new rules, new conditions and more incentives. the report by mr fjellner deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the application of a new system of generalised tariff preferences. i voted in favour of this proposal because, without jeopardising the eu's economic interests, it supports developing countries which defend the eu's values by encouraging their exports. although its scope is now wider for tradable products, the new programme (spg+) contains more demanding requirements such as the 27 assumptions on respect for human rights and environmental protection.
in writing. − the eu has been guaranteeing developing countries the possibility to export products to the eu without reciprocity for decades. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this system of preferences has undergone developments and differentiations, seeking to benefit the least developed countries more. however, everything has been called into question by the subjection to the rules of the wto, one of the institutional pillars of neoliberalism on a global scale, and by the emergence of free trade as a means of colonizing the economies of developing countries. the new regulation now proposed will move the eu from the wider system of trade preferences between industrialized countries or blocs to the more restrictive system. many countries will be excluded from the system of non-reciprocal preferences, which is not without unacceptable pressures and blackmail to force acceptance of free trade agreements, as is the case with ecuador. on the other hand, in the interests of the eu powers, benefits are being extended to some countries, which could have negative impacts in countries such as portugal, with a significant share of sensitive sectors such as textiles and clothing. we voted against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this new legal gsp regime (general system of trade preferences for imports from developing countries) because it is a more balanced and more demanding regime than the current one. the main improvements are the halving of the number of beneficiary countries, concentrating benefits on the most deprived countries, and the more stringent requirements for gsp+, which is a more advantageous scheme. despite these positive aspects, i cannot but express my disagreement here with regard to the relaxation of the conditions for access to gsp+, which will allow large economies, such as pakistan, which is very competitive in some sectors, to access it (if the other conditions in the field of human rights and the rule of law are met), at the expense of the poorer countries and the european textile industry itself, and particularly the portuguese one.
in writing. the portuguese socialist delegation voted in favour of the new legal regime of the gsp (generalized system of trade preferences for imports from developing countries) because it is a more balanced and more demanding system than the one currently in force, firstly because it reduces by half the number of beneficiary countries, concentrating benefits on the most deprived countries, and also because it makes the requirements for benefiting from the gsp +, which is a more advantageous system, more demanding. this overall positive assessment does not, however, mean that the objections, which have been voiced from the outset, to the relaxation of the conditions for access to the gsp+ should be abandoned, which will allow large economies, such as pakistan, which is very competitive in some sectors, to access it (provided that the other conditions relating to human rights and the rule of law are met), at the expense of the poorer countries and the european textile industry itself. although the special safeguard clause for textiles and clothing, which the ep has obtained, allows for a satisfactory defence of european industry, we believe, as a matter of principle, that european generosity towards third countries cannot be at the expense of the economies of the least competitive countries in the union.
in writing. - as this is the first time that a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of a scheme of generalised tariff preferences has been adopted by the ordinary legislative procedure and in view of the major amendments proposed, i support the rapporteur's claim that it should be revised within five years of its entry into force and that it should be limited to a period of 10 years, as opposed to the indefinite period of validity proposed by the commission. this will indeed be a significant improvement on the current situation, and this period is sufficiently long to ensure stability and predictability for economic operators. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − since 1971, the european union has been granting non-reciprocal trade preferences in the form of duty reductions for goods from developing countries imported into the european market through the generalised system of preferences (gsp). the last scheme dates back to 2008 and it is now necessary to review it. this is the first time that this regulation will be subject to the ordinary legislative procedure following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the objective of this important trade instrument is to enable developing countries to participate more fully in international trade and thus generate additional export revenues to support income growth and the implementation of their own sustainable development and poverty reduction policy strategies. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − since 1971, the european union has granted non-reciprocal trade preferences in the form of duty reductions for goods from developing countries imported into the european market through the system of generalised preferences. the objective of this trade instrument is to enable developing countries to participate more fully in international trade and thereby generate additional export revenues to support income growth and the implementation of their own development policy and poverty reduction strategies. the proposal for a revision of this scheme provides for some important changes, including the reduction of beneficiaries to 80 countries, the exclusion of countries with an annual per capita income of more than usd 4000 for three consecutive years, the introduction of a grading system by product sector and the extension of the gsp+ to a greater number of countries. i support the proposed new architecture and have voted in favour of it in the european parliament.
in writing. - with the adoption of this regulation, the eu will move from a wider system of trade preferences between industrialized countries or blocs to a more restrictive system, which means that many countries will be excluded from the non-reciprocal preference system, which is not without unacceptable pressures and blackmail to force acceptance of free trade agreements. on the other hand, in the interests of the eu powers, benefits are being extended to some countries, which could have negative impacts in countries such as portugal, with a significant share of sensitive sectors such as textiles and clothing.
in writing. - i welcome the fact that, despite the austerity measures the commission intends to implement, great progress has been made, notably with regard to the non-obligatory reference of 0.5% of the deficit but only the stability and growth pact, the application of the multiclausel, where the social dialogue must be respected, the need for a thorough analysis of the procedures for macroeconomic imbalances and the obligation for the commission to ascertain the consequences of taxation, among other significant progress achieved by the socialists which ensure that austerity will not be unfair or as severe as proposed.
in writing. − the commission's proposals, which complete the economic governance package, aim to ensure that the conditions are met for enhanced surveillance and protection of states supported by financial assistance and/or threatened by difficulties or instability. the report draws lessons from the financial and sovereign debt crises that have hit europe and proposes solutions for stability and growth based on preventive measures that allow problems to be solved in advance rather than making up for errors that have already occurred. it is thus envisaged that when a member state is experiencing severe difficulties, it should have enhanced supervision (which will depend on the severity of the financial difficulties and the assistance granted to the countries) and everything should be done to avoid negative contagion to other economies. countries that fail to comply should also be guaranteed legal protection and have an adjustment programme which will be monitored by the commission and other competent bodies. i voted in favour of this report because it is a factor in strengthening stability and confidence in the euro area countries, which are key to a sustainable recovery and to laying the foundations for growth in europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the european economic governance (the so-called six-pack) adopted by the european parliament and the council in 2011 and because i believe that the serious economic and social situation in which some member states are currently found could have been avoided if early and specifically targeted action had been taken.
in writing. − the financial crisis has had serious consequences for financial stability and economic growth, contributing to a serious deterioration in the government deficit and the indebtedness of member states. unfortunately, the number of member states requiring assistance is increasing, and therefore there is an urgent need for increased supervision. it is a pity that this two-pack was not adopted earlier, because it would have been preferable to give priority to prevention with early and specifically targeted action that could avoid a state's indebtedness difficulties rather than to correction with strong austerity measures, which could have serious consequences for economic growth and job creation. in the context of the financial crisis and the sovereign debt crisis that we face, we have to draw lessons and propose solutions. the proposal is another initiative to strengthen budgetary discipline, which is intended to complete the economic governance package and provides that a member state in difficulty should be subject to enhanced surveillance, helping it to ensure its rapid return to a situation of normality. since the intensity of economic surveillance should be proportionate and appropriate to the seriousness of the financial difficulties, there should be a guarantee of legal protection and monitoring by the commission.
in writing. − this proposal, which together with the regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down common provisions for the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and for the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area member states, constitutes the so-called two-pack and strengthens the previously adopted economic governance package. this specific regulation aims to ensure the conditions for enhanced surveillance and protection of member states receiving financial assistance and/or threatened by difficulties or instability, using preventive measures to resolve problems in advance. another step in the right direction. more europe and greater integration, towards a common future and a path of economic and environmental growth and development, peace, prosperity and shared happiness, as it has been for the past 55 years. this is a reality which is not currently being grasped by the vast majority of european citizens, given the economic, financial and budgetary crisis in which we are living.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has forced member states (ms) to adopt restrictive measures on consumption, wage cuts and the raising of the retirement age. some eu member states were unable to recover from the crisis on their own and had to ask for financial assistance from the european institutions in order to obtain support from bodies such as the european stabilisation fund, the international monetary fund and the european central bank. the crisis is an octopus that threatens to spread its tentacles across several european countries. after ireland, greece and portugal, spain is next and italy hovers over. it is urgent to create mechanisms to prevent this progress, because we know that the consequences of the indebtedness of one member state can have repercussions on others and even on a world scale, since the effects of corrective measures are late. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability in the euro area, which lays down new procedures, such as the strengthening of the commission's powers and the introduction of the qualified majority rule.
in writing. - this regulation is part of the so-called two-pack, which is intended to complement the previous six-pack, thus completing the legislative framework of the so-called economic governance. provisions are laid down for the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance of member states whose currency is the euro and which are experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. what is amazing is the way in which it is assumed that it is transposing the provisions of the recent budgetary treaty into eu secondary legislation. it should be remembered that this treaty has not even been ratified yet and that it is, moreover, a legal aberration, a fact that has been outside the law of the eu itself, although it brings the institutions of the eu within it. the rapporteur considers that 'it is for the commission to take the necessary decisions, including the decision to place a member state under the enhanced surveillance procedure'. the intention, as in the case of the other report in this two-pack, is clear and self-evident: to further deepen control over the member states, in a line leading to the establishment of colonial-type relations. we obviously voted against it.
in writing. − with the vote on this report and that of ms elisa ferreira, parliament completes the package on european governance adopted at the end of 2011. the continuation of this crisis, which continues to afflict the whole of europe, requires the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance by the states to safeguard the stability of europe and especially of the euro zone. the adoption of these rules will strengthen the eu's power to intervene, allowing it to intervene when necessary and to have the most appropriate means at its disposal to do so.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree, in its broad outline, with the commission's proposal to provide that a member state whose currency is the euro should be subject to enhanced surveillance when it is affected or threatened by serious financial disturbances. these are measures to restore a normal situation quickly and to protect the other euro area member states against any negative consequences.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation on the economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability in the euro area is in the context of the financial and sovereign debt crisis currently facing the european union, drawing lessons from it and proposing possible solutions. the six-pack of legislative acts needs to be strengthened to ensure both financial stability and economic growth in the euro area. the aim is to ensure that a member state whose currency is the euro is subject to enhanced supervision when it is affected or threatened by serious financial disturbances, and to provide for a legal protection regime for a member state which is at risk of being in a prolonged state of default or default in the short term. the consequences of excessive indebtedness of states can be dramatic, both within these states and for the other member states of the european union. preventive action at an early stage is preferable to corrective measures that intervene late, perhaps too late, in the process.
in writing. - this report is part of the famous two pack in the field of economic governance. the report under discussion embodies the logic of the intergovernmental treaty which enshrines an ideological dogma and outlaws countercyclical policies in favour of a controversial and highly manipulable technical criterion of assessment. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. − in november 2011, the european commission presented a proposal to the european parliament and the council aimed at establishing provisions to strengthen economic and budgetary surveillance of euro area member states that are experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability and/or that are receiving or are likely to receive external financial assistance. i agree with this report because i believe that there needs to be stronger supervision of the euro countries in order to prevent the difficulties of one member state with regard to its financial stability from spreading to the rest of the euro area and, more generally, to the whole of the union. i believe that the member states should inform the commission and the council in advance of their plans to issue public debt, so that the european commission can coordinate better and work towards a more coordinated economic policy. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that the structural funds should not be suspended in the period 2014-2020 if a member state does not comply with its adjustment programme, and that other economic and financial mechanisms should be adopted for this purpose.
in writing. - as in the ferreira report on the other component of this two pack, this report also proposes several amendments to include the need for member states to take growth and employment into account in their policies and actions. these intentions are dead letter when they are inserted into the logic of the policies in which this two pack is inserted - the perpetuation of austerity policies through cuts in public investment, public services, cuts in wages and social protection, promotion of privatizations - which are precisely the opposite of the necessary growth of employment and the economy. on the other hand, the so-called enhanced surveillance procedure is nothing more than an anti-democratic blow against the institutions of national sovereignty and democratically elected, which are thus no longer able to decide on such important economic instruments as budgetary policy.
in writing. - i approve this report and welcome the introduction of a new chapter entitled 'establishing a roadmap for enhanced policy coordination, a growth facility and a framework to enhance debt issuance'. this chapter calls for the commission to submit a proposal for the countercyclical 1% of gdp instrument to boost growth, a report setting out a roadmap for the establishment of euro area stability actions, the immediate establishment of the requirement for member states to report ex ante on the issuance of their public debt and the establishment of the proposal for the redemption fund through a co-decision regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the amendments to the text proposed by the committee which establishes common provisions for the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and for the correction of the excessive deficit of the euro area member states.
in writing. − this report sets out measures to ensure greater coordination of the budgetary policies of the member states. it therefore stresses the need for sound public finances and financial stability as a means of strengthening price stability and sustainable and strong growth in order to achieve the union's objectives of sustainable growth and employment. ensuring that the economic policies of certain member states do not adversely affect the others and the smooth functioning of economic and monetary union is the priority identified and fully supported. the report is overall positive and consensual in its importance for the euro area and the union as a whole. i would just point out that some issues such as the mutualisation of european debt and concrete measures to promote investment and growth in europe, although fundamental, should be discussed in the context of the documents produced for this purpose and not in the context of this report. the two-pack adopted today represents one of the basic pillars for building economic and financial stability in europe, the foundation of a new policy generating prosperity and growth in the euro area and the european union as a whole.
in writing. the report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down common provisions for the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and for the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area member states. the concern of the member states for budgetary discipline and the correction of excessive deficits has led to a restraint on consumption and, consequently, to the bankruptcy of many companies, the loss of tax revenues, the increase in unemployment and, necessarily, the emergence of new poverty situations. i voted in favour of this report because, in addition to the reinforced surveillance which aims to prevent member states from becoming over-indebted and the contagion of the disease by monitoring and evaluating their plans, prevention is better than cure, even for the late effects of the measures adopted, points to the need to change the direction of the agenda, which has so far been oriented towards austerity, in order to promote economic growth and job creation. i therefore welcome the creation of eurobonds, the defence of an ambitious investment plan that is in line with eu 2020 and the strengthening of the community method that stimulates economic growth that is smart, sustainable and inclusive.
in writing. - this regulation is part of the so-called two-pack, which is intended to complement the previous six-pack, thus completing the legislative framework of the so-called economic governance. the aim is to control the budgetary and economic policies of the member states, while continuing the unacceptable draining of national sovereignty institutions. we are faced with an unusual and profoundly undemocratic concentration of economic and political power in the eu institutions, particularly in the commission. the usual protagonists are backing it: the right and the social democrats. the latter, with this report, is once again making its usual attempt to put the word 'growth' on policies and strategies which are themselves the negation of growth, but above all the negation of any prospect of sovereign, just and sustainable development. the proposals for the stability bonds (in the form already proposed by the commission, even adopting the same designation) and the rescue fund are, in this context, more propaganda than proposals with practical effect. at least, a practical effect other than to further elaborate the original commission proposal in terms of the obligations which the member states have to fulfil in relation to their budgetary procedures. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − by voting on this report and on the report by mr jean paul gauzès, parliament completes the package on european governance adopted at the end of 2011. the continuation of this crisis, which continues to afflict the whole of europe, requires the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance by the states, in order to safeguard the stability of europe and especially of the euro zone. the adoption of these rules will strengthen the eu's power to intervene, allowing it to intervene when necessary and to have the most appropriate means at its disposal to do so.
in writing. - i would like to commend the rapporteur for the commitment and dedication she has shown in implementing this report, seeking consensus at 27 but at the same time protecting the interests of her country of origin. the work done was necessary work, and there are a number of proposed measures which must now be implemented urgently and which we all hope will make a decisive contribution to improving the economic situation throughout the eu.
in writing. the report makes timid declarations of intent on a roadmap for the hypothetical introduction of eurobonds. i support these aspects of the proposal but at this rate of implementation they will clearly be insufficient to provide an alternative to austerity-based adjustment programmes. for these reasons i voted against.
in writing. − in november 2011, the european commission presented a proposal to the european parliament and the council with the aim of establishing provisions to improve the monitoring of fiscal policies in the euro area that are complementary to the measures already set out in the european semester, a system of multilateral surveillance of fiscal policies and a procedure for correcting a member state's excessive deficit. i agree with this report because i believe that it is necessary to strengthen the conditions for price stability and to promote increased financial stability which contributes to the achievement of the union's objectives in terms of growth and employment. i believe that it will be good to establish a common budgetary timetable between the euro area member states which will lead to increased synergies, facilitate the coordination of economic and financial policies and enable the european commission to draw up recommendations with a view to eliminating existing macroeconomic imbalances.
in writing. the commission's original proposal follows on from the previous six-pack and further strengthens economic governance. it is also an attempt by the european commission to incorporate the assumptions of the treaty on budgetary discipline into eu secondary legislation. this is a major infringement of community law, since the budgetary treaty was signed outside the eu's laws and is therefore not enshrined in eu law. but this setback does not seem to bother the ec or the majority of the ep. the aim is to ensure compatibility between fiscal policies and the procedures for preventing and correcting excessive macroeconomic imbalances through closer monitoring of national reform programmes. in other words, what is being depicted here is the continuation of the so-called austerity policies with all that this implies - cuts in public investment, public services, wage cuts, privatisations - in addition to the establishment of mechanisms that transfer to supranational institutions matters of budgetary policy which should be the exclusive competence of the member states and their sovereign bodies. the instruments for the com munication of debt proposed attempt to conceal the obvious blackmail and the unacceptable attacks on democracy contained in this package.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that its objective is to extend the geographical scope of the operations of the central bank for reconstruction and development to the countries located south and west of the mediterranean basin and jordan. this report is a response that the european union must have to the arab spring, so as to make it easier for the region to move towards stable and reliable democratic systems. the european union's objective of expressing itself as a bastion of peace and human rights must be applied in cases like this.
in writing. − the ebrd was set up to support the development of market economies from central europe to central asia following the widespread collapse of communist regimes. the ebrd is currently continuing its work to promote the transition to market economies, private enterprise and entrepreneurship in the countries of central and eastern europe, and to contribute to their economic progress and reconstruction. the bank's activities are now to be extended to the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean. in the light of the events in 2011 in the mediterranean partner countries, the commission and the high representative presented the eu's political and economic support to the region, which envisaged the possibility of extending the mandate of the ebrd to the southern neighbourhood countries, drawing on its extensive experience in promoting the transition to market economies. the european parliament and the g8 group have also invited the ebrd to amend its statute in order to be able to participate in this financial assistance process. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the experience of the ebrd can be put to use in the transition of these mediterranean countries by promoting the principles of multiparty democracy, pluralism and the market economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the amendments to the text proposed by the commission to the agreement establishing the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd), which extend the geographical scope of the ebrd's operations to the south and east of the mediterranean.
in writing. - last november, in my report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy (enp), (unanimously approved in this house), i stated that: appreciates the work carried out by the european investment bank [...] and the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) [...]; supports the amendment of the ebrd's statutes so that the countries of the southern neighbourhood are also eligible for aid, while seeking to establish between the eib and the ebrd [...] a fruitful relationship of cooperation, not competition. in my first report on the revision of the enp-southern dimension, dated 7 april 2011 (also adopted unanimously), we called on the ebrd to amend its statute in order to be able to participate in the financial assistance to these countries, as evidenced by the text of the resolution adopted today (recital 1-a). moreover, as president of the delegation for relations with the countries of the maghreb, i have also advocated this extension of powers in various fora, inside and outside the union. it is therefore with great personal satisfaction and with the pleasure of having actively and positively contributed to making this extension of the mandate of the ebrd to the countries of the southern neighbourhood (including jordan) a reality that i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the report aims to extend the remit of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the southern and eastern mediterranean regions. it should be recalled that when the ebrd was set up in 1990, its geographical boundaries were the countries of the former soviet bloc. however, in view of the latest developments following the arab spring, the union considered that the ebrd should also be able to operate in this area. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work and i fully agree with his position on pursuing projects which are aimed at energy efficiency and which are socially inclusive, always having respect for human rights as a cornerstone.
