in writing. − the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd), established in 1991, is the eu's first financial institution and was set up to support europe's economic development following the break-up of the soviet union. the ebrd mainly supports the development of the local sector: small and medium-sized enterprises, private individuals, municipalities, regional cooperation, innovation, job creation, energy, green projects, etc. this report, by mr binev, is on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision amending the ebrd constituent agreement to extend the geographical scope of the bank's operations to the south and east of the mediterranean. initially intended to support the countries of central and eastern europe, it is now intended, in the wake of the so-called arab spring, to extend its geographical area of influence to the countries of the southern and eastern shores of the mediterranean, including jordan, in order to support these countries in their transition to open market economies and in promoting private initiative. i agree with this enlargement and welcome it, as i said when the proposal to increase the ebrd's share capital from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion was approved.
in writing. the aim of the commission proposal is to extend the scope of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to the countries south and east of the mediterranean and jordan, in order to provide financial assistance to these countries. since its establishment in 1990, the ebrd has been assisting the countries of central and eastern europe in their transition to market economies and promoting private initiative and entrepreneurship. the ebrd has thus been instrumental in serving this desire: the expansion and consolidation of capitalist production relations in europe. now, in the wake of the arab spring, an unequivocal political response from the union is called for. and the commission has put forward this proposal, which is therefore part of the political response that is required. we support the establishment of cooperation relations and development aid measures with the countries south of and east of the mediterranean. these could include facilitating access to sources of finance that can support development-enhancing investments. but we are not ignoring the more general context (and this is evident in this report) of attempts to interfere politically and economically by the eu in these countries (through the ebrd) and to open doors to eu multinationals to new and promising markets.
in writing. − the recent events and social upheavals affecting the african and asian countries of the mediterranean basin make it necessary for the european union to support them, and adequate support for these countries is crucial as they play an important role not only in terms of political stability but also in terms of trade. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which seeks to extend the activities of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean.
in writing. − putting the ebrd's experience to use in the transition of the mediterranean countries, promoting the principles of multiparty democracy, pluralism and market economy seems to be a solution for the eu to contribute to the progress and economic reconstruction of these countries. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the commission in its report broadly supports the extension of the geographical scope of operations of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to the south and east of the mediterranean in order to encourage the transition of the countries in this region to market economies and pluralist societies. first, the bank is expected to foster the transition to market economies and to promote private initiative and entrepreneurship in countries that commit to respecting the principles of multiparty democracy, pluralism and market economy, while contributing to the economic progress and reconstruction of those countries. the commission is also calling for greater action in the field of energy efficiency, the fight against poverty and the protection of human rights, so as to achieve greater social cohesion. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) aims to foster the transition to market economies and to promote private initiative and entrepreneurship in the countries of central and eastern europe that commit themselves to respecting the principles of multiparty democracy, pluralism and market economy, while contributing to the economic progress and reconstruction of these countries. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the ebrd should now have a role in the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean similar to that which it currently has in the countries of central and eastern europe. the aim is to support more countries in their efforts to transition to open and market-oriented economies and to promote private and entrepreneurial initiative. i believe that the extension of the ebrd's activities is a symbol of the support that the european union gives to the transition of countries to a more democratic and pluralistic market economy. however, i believe that before any intervention is undertaken, the ebrd should carry out a detailed technical assessment of the economic and political conditions in the country concerned in order to maximise the financial assistance it will make available.
in writing. the commission's proposal aims to extend the scope of the ebrd's intervention to the countries south and east of the mediterranean and jordan in order to provide financial assistance to these countries after the so-called arab spring, stating that this means strong eu political and economic support for the region. we advocate that this support be implemented in the framework of solidarity cooperation, in which the objectives are those of an autonomous and sovereign development of the countries supported and not of political interference by the eu in these countries. in this respect, we do not support the premises of the report that the political and economic conditions of the country concerned should be assessed in detail, including possible gaps in the transition process in relation to the country's commitment to the principles of multiparty democracy, pluralism and market economy.
in writing. - i support this report because it stresses that the eu budget is an investment budget with a strong leverage effect, since 94% of its appropriations are intended to stimulate economic growth and employment and as such is a powerful instrument to increase strategic investment with european added value and to put the european economy back on track. today the eu budget has an even more fundamental role, as it can help to be an important complement to the budgets of national recovery policies on the road to consolidation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the multiannual financial framework and own resources because i believe that only with a sound community budget can europe overcome the crisis and achieve the objectives of growth and employment. i consider it necessary that an agreement on the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 also provides for a reform of the own resources system to include a financial transaction tax.
in writing. − taking due account of the union's current financial, economic and social situation, there is a growing need for the institutions to respond with responsibility and restraint to the demands of the very serious situation we are facing and to use rigorous budgetary management processes to achieve savings. it should be noted, however, that the union budget is an important lever for the european economy, since 94% of the appropriations are used to stimulate the economy and create jobs, and is therefore essential for the much needed revival of the european economy, in parallel with the fiscal consolidation carried out by the member states. it is also essential to improve the use of community funds, so that they are managed more efficiently and waste less.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled following the statements by the representatives of the council and the commission pursuant to rule 110 (2), by the political groups of the ppe, s&d, alde, greens/efa and gue/ngl, deals with the multiannual financial framework and own resources. on 8 june 2011, the european parliament (ep), in pursuance of the europe 2020 strategy, adopted a resolution entitled 'investing in the future: a new multiannual financial framework (mff) for a competitive, sustainable and inclusive europe'. part four, entitled 'organization and structure of the financial framework: a framework to reflect priorities', refers to the structure of the next mff which should facilitate continuity of planning and flexibility within and between headings and avoid the shortcomings of the current mff, in particular as regards shortcomings in categories 1a, competitiveness for growth and jobs, 3b, citizenship, and 4, external relations. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it directs the next mff towards growth and employment, through various directives and initiatives such as the six-pack and the two-pack, and it proposes a genuine system of own resources through the creation of a financial transaction tax.
in writing. - this resolution insists that 'the political positions agreed by the european council must be negotiated between parliament and the council (...) before the council formally submits its proposals, with a view to obtaining parliament's approval of the regulation on the multiannual financial framework'. it is the usual exercise of parliament, which is to prove its existence, even if it then resigns itself to its also usual role as a mere sounding board for the council. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. reiterates its faith in the neoliberal eu2020 strategy, which we reject and oppose; support and reiterate the political priorities of the european parliament's report on the financial perspectives 2014-2020, which we voted against; the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission. the commission is also proposing to reduce the contributions of the member states based on their gni by 40% by 2020, which we consider unacceptable because it undermines the redistributive role of the budget. more than enough reasons for our vote against.
in writing. - i support this resolution because we cannot allow european governments to completely exclude parliament from the negotiations on the financial perspectives 2014 to 2020. in this unprecedented crisis, when it is essential to affirm solidarity, the european council responds with one voice: austerity. parliament in this resolution defends its full right to participate in the negotiations; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. parliament reiterates its desire to put an end to the bargaining of the big states and the shameful correction and rebate mechanisms of britain and others. we need a financial transaction tax that will force those who caused the crisis to start paying it. what is not needed is austerity, which in this declaration is euphemistically called fiscal consolidation. what is not needed is a reduction in the member states' share of the european budget. what is needed is more and better europe, more solidarity.
in writing. − the european union has always aimed to achieve the best possible living conditions for its 500 million citizens. for this to happen, we need a budget that is innovative and that is concerned with the new realities of globalisation. in the aftermath of the crisis, governments, businesses and households in europe are more sensitive to how their money is spent. the european union, through the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, has to do the same, choosing carefully where to cut and where to invest for future growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i also believe that the objectives and policies of the multiannual financial framework should be agreed before the amounts are entered and that parliament and the council should start genuine negotiations on all aspects of the multiannual financial framework before the amounts are fixed and the final adjustments to the overall package of the multiannual financial framework are made.
in writing. - i support this resolution because we cannot allow european governments to completely exclude parliament from the negotiations on the financial perspectives 2014 to 2020. in this unprecedented crisis, when it is essential to affirm solidarity, the european council responds with one voice: austerity. parliament in this resolution defends its full right to participate in the negotiations; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. parliament reiterates its desire to put an end to the bargaining of the big states and the shameful correction and rebate mechanisms of britain and others. we need a financial transaction tax that will force those who caused the crisis to start paying it. what is not needed is austerity, which in this declaration is euphemistically called fiscal consolidation. what is not needed is a reduction in the member states' share of the european budget. what is needed is more and better europe, more solidarity.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union budget (2014-2020) continues to be rigorous. the overall amount proposed for the next seven years is eur 1.025 billion in commitment appropriations (1.05% of eu gni) and eur 972.2 billion (1% of eu gni) in payment appropriations. it should be noted that the budget is geared towards the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and that some 94% of the financial appropriations are directed towards supporting growth and employment, with particular emphasis on cohesion policies (eur 336 billion) and research and innovation (eur 80 billion). the connecting europe facility (eur 50 billion) will be extremely important for financing crossborder projects in the energy, transport and information technology sectors, and the erasmus for all proposal (eur 19 billion) demonstrates that the european union is concerned about the future of the new generations. finally, i would like to stress the importance of the adoption of new own resources (vat and financial transaction tax) which will make it possible to reduce by 40% by 2020 the percentage of member states' contributions to the european budget.
in writing. - the resolution is intended to state that the political positions agreed by the european council must be negotiated between parliament and the council (...) before the council formally submits its proposals, with a view to obtaining parliament's approval of the regulation on the multiannual financial framework. while this position may be important, we cannot but disagree with the establishment of the sure report as a basis for negotiation (which proposed the freezing of the community budget until 2020), with the reform of the own resources system with a view to reducing national contributions to the community budget, the legitimization of fiscal consolidation (austerity policies) and the recommendation of support for strategy 2020 as one of the ways out of the crisis.
in writing. the european union has a small budget, but a big impact on european citizens. the proposal for a multiannual budget for 2014-2020 responds to today's concerns but also to tomorrow's needs, by focusing on priority funding at eu level that generates real added value. i voted against this resolution because, unlike the rapporteur, i believe that the union budget fulfils the objective it was originally set to contribute to greater economic growth and job creation. i also support the proposals for own resources put forward by the european commission, in particular the financial transaction tax and the capital from vat.
in writing. - the multiannual financial framework shows a decrease in the amounts for the individual development of the regions (cohesion policy) but an increase in the overall funds for economic, social and territorial cohesion, due to the creation of the connecting europe facility. on the contrary, there has been a reduction in the funds allocated to the cap (agriculture and rural development), demonstrating that the european union's focus is on the economy of the first sector. i agree with the rapporteur that the eu budget is an investment budget with a strong leverage effect and can be a very powerful tool for increasing strategic investments with high european added value, in line with an approach to growth and job creation. i have voted against this motion for a resolution, however, because i disagree with the rapporteur on the own resources. i welcome the proposals for a financial transaction tax and a new eu own resource from vat.
in writing. - i approve this resolution on the european union's negotiations with japan, considering that the commission has insufficient reason to consider the opening of negotiations valid, simply on the basis of a report containing the level of ambition of both parties. i agree with the majority of members of the european parliament that we should not approve the opening of negotiations, considering that the commission's evaluation exercise in this process is not sufficient. i therefore propose that the council does not authorize the opening of trade negotiations until the european parliament has declared its formal position on a mandate proposed for negotiation on the basis of a report from the commission responsible, thus bringing the european union into line with the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
in writing. − the japanese authorities have been slow to negotiate and there have been repeated doubts about their willingness to reach a lasting agreement with the european union in the near future. i believe that this future agreement is very important for both sides and that the union should therefore do everything in its power to promote concrete progress on this issue. i think, however, that parliament cannot be left out of this process and its views on it ignored.
in writing. the resolution, which follows a statement by the commission, focuses on the negotiations between the european union (eu) and japan on a free trade agreement. the excellent relations between the eu and japan are very important to both sides. in fact, japan is the eu's sixth largest trading partner (€49 billion) and the eu is japan's third largest trading partner (€69 billion). given the trade deficit at the expense of the eu, it is essential that japan removes many of the obstacles it places in the way of european imports, notably non-tariff barriers, the non-opening of public tenders to eu companies, which is detrimental to our small and medium-sized enterprises, and protectionism to the japanese car industry. if there is no progress in the negotiations or if the results are not satisfactory, they should be terminated. i voted in favour of a new free trade agreement, but it is essential that the final result be mutually beneficial and not favourable to one side only, namely japan.
in writing. - the european parliament, more papist than the pope, has been asking the european commission to open negotiations with japan with a view to establishing a free trade agreement with that country. the european commission, in response to these requests, asked japan to meet certain conditions for opening up its market before the negotiations began. at the end of may, eu and japanese representatives agreed in brussels on a first definition of the scope and scope of the negotiations. the commission is now preparing to propose to the council a mandate giving it the green light for these negotiations. this resolution merely asks the council not to take a position on a negotiating mandate until parliament has defined its own position. but it is not difficult to imagine what that position will be. time will show more clearly the interests and contradictions at stake in this process. but in this case, unlike in other countries, the interests of the eu powers and their economic groups (such as the german automobile industry) may find in japan an undesirable competitor rather than good market opportunities. a factor which will certainly weigh on the evolution and outcome of the process.
in writing. − in 2010, the total amount of bilateral trade between the eu and japan, the world's third largest economy in terms of gdp, amounted to €120 billion; japan is the sixth largest trading partner for the eu and the eu is japan's third largest trading partner. however, there is a great deal of untapped trade potential and therefore a strong determination is needed to strengthen eu-japan trade relations by focusing on the removal of non-tariff barriers to trade and investment, including numerous restrictive rules and regulatory measures for european companies to access the japanese market. in this sense, the eu-japan fta has great potential to be beneficial for both economies. to this end, the eu should in due course make the necessary suggestions to the commission on the conditions which the commission considers necessary to include in the agreement to be negotiated.
in writing. - i abstained on the motion asking the council not to authorize the opening of trade negotiations with japan because it seems to me that it may have counterproductive effects and may be against the interests of parliament itself. in fact, if the commission has already announced that it will ask the council for a mandate, the council is more likely to ignore parliament's request and grant it, not least because there is a political commitment to do so. if this happens, parliament will not only be disregarded by the council, but it will also lose the opportunity it now had to tell the commission and the council in advance what substantive conditions parliament considers should be included in the negotiating mandate, which would then give it the authority to react if these conditions were not met (including the threat of not giving final assent to the treaty).
in writing. − at the 20th eu-japan summit, held on 28 may 2011 in brussels, summit leaders decided that the two sides would start talks to define the scope and level of ambition of these negotiations. to this end, a scoping group was set up to assess the common understanding on the scope and level of ambition of potential trade negotiations between japan and the eu. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution calling on the council not to authorize the opening of trade negotiations until parliament has given its opinion on the proposed negotiating mandate on the basis of a report from the committee responsible.
in writing. - the proposal for a resolution on trade negotiations between the eu and japan with a view to closer economic integration between these two strategic trading partners. following the 20th eu-japan summit held on 28 may 2011 in brussels, the leaders of the summit decided that the two sides would enter into talks to define the scope and level of ambition of those negotiations, which are mainly about the removal of regulatory barriers to trade by japan. since these negotiations could be an excellent window of opportunity for the eu, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the elimination of trade barriers is an essential condition for the success of any trade relationship between the two partners and is of particular importance in the launch of trade negotiations between the european union and japan. given that the opening of talks on trade negotiations was agreed at the brussels summit on 28 may 2011, parliament, with my support, now calls on the council not to open the negotiations until parliament has stated its position on the mandate.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that after the democratic elections, the president and the prime minister elected by universal suffrage were forced to evacuate the country following a coup d'état. i believe that the european union should give a clear signal of zero tolerance to attacks on democracy. the european union must intervene to demobilize the military and establish democracy, and this must be done in collaboration with international partners.
in writing. − on 12 april 2012, members of the armed forces of guinea-bissau seized power by force and arrested the interim president and the prime minister. this illegitimate military coup took place the day before the start of the electoral campaign for the second round of the presidential elections and was widely condemned by the international community. for several decades, guinea-bissau has been experiencing political instability, leading the country into a deep political, governance and humanitarian crisis. this resolution, which i supported, strongly condemns the illegitimate seizure of power by the armed forces of guinea-bissau and calls for the immediate restoration of constitutional order and the rule of law. it calls for the immediate release of all public officials and other citizens held by the rebel military and for an end to violence, looting and intimidation. supports the eu's willingness to cooperate with the west african states and their regional and international partners with a view to establishing an effective partnership contributing to the long-term pacification and stabilisation of guinea-bissau.
in writing. - on 12 april this year, a military force seized power illegitimately and by force in the republic of guinea-bissau, on the eve of the electoral campaign for the second round of presidential elections, deepening the political instability in the country and leading it to a deep crisis of governance with severe social, economic and humanitarian consequences for its citizens. i condemn in the strongest terms this illegitimate seizure of power by the military forces, which has plunged the country and its institutions into unprecedented instability, calling into question the democratic rule of law, and i condemn the interference of the military in political power and in the free choice of the legitimate representatives of the guinean people. it is essential that the european union, the united nations and the entire international community coordinate their efforts to bring normalcy and peace to guinea, so that constitutional order, the rule of law, the freedoms and fundamental rights of the guinean people and the democratic and sustainable development of the country can be restored. the settlement of the dispute should, as far as possible, be carried out by peaceful means, with the minimum of consequences for the well-being of citizens and without infringement of their guarantees and freedoms.
in writing. - on 12 april, the guinean military carried out a military coup which deposed the president of the republic and the prime minister. this joint motion for a resolution, tabled following a statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, replaces the motions for resolutions tabled by the following political groups: epp, ecr, alde, s&d, gue/ngl and greens/efa, on the military coup in guinea-bissau. first of all, i would like to express my solidarity with the suffering people of guinea-bissau, who have been tormented for years by the social and political instability that has cyclically plunged the country into civil war. the international community, and in particular the european union (eu), cannot remain indifferent to the situation in this country where the military are dismissing the legitimate representatives of the people, committing clear violations of human rights and allowing looting and drug trafficking. the eu maintains a partnership agreement with guinea-bissau, and i urge the european authorities to do everything possible to ensure that democratic legality is restored as soon as possible, that political prisoners are released, that the elected representatives are allowed to return and that the electoral process is resumed.
in writing. the resolution strongly condemns the military coup in guinea-bissau and sets out important principles and guidelines for overcoming the current situation: rejection of any attempt to legitimise the coup. it calls for the restoration of constitutional order and the completion of the electoral process interrupted by the coup, for the physical integrity of all public officials and other citizens subject to arbitrary detention and persecution to be respected, for the release of detainees and for an end to violence, looting and intimidation. in addition to all this, we also welcome the inclusion of the paragraph on the rejection of any external exploitation of the present situation which would jeopardize the sovereignty of the guinean people and the territorial integrity and independence of guinea-bissau, which we have proposed. but we reject the insistence of the other groups that some points should be included in the resolution which could conflict with this principle, in particular by opening the door to external interference in the country. the call for urgent aid measures to deal with the humanitarian situation in the country is also important. any mission in the country, whether in the framework of the pflp or other organisations, should have a clear and precise un mandate to support the sovereign institutions of the country, which respects its sovereign will, international law and the un charter.
in writing. - it is the eu's obligation to condemn the acts of the military in guinea-bissau, demanding the restoration of the democratically elected sovereign bodies and the resumption of the electoral process which was under way.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on guinea-bissau, in which i stress the call for the international community to take immediate concrete and appropriate aid measures in view of the humanitarian situation in guinea-bissau. in particular, the internally displaced persons and refugees are mentioned, as is the risk of epidemics and the danger to the food security and health of the guinean people.
in writing. the current political crisis in guinea-bissau arises from the seizure of power by force in guinea-bissau and the subsequent arrest of the interim president, raimundo pereira, and the prime minister, carlos gomes júnior. as is well known, the military leaders of guinea-bissau have repeatedly and intolerably interfered in the political life of the country, and this interference has had a very negative impact on the process of establishing democracy and the rule of law, as well as on the security of the population and economic development. the eu condemns this unconstitutional seizure of power by the guinea-bissau armed forces and calls on the international community to exert all the necessary influence to overcome this situation. this, of course, without any external exploitation of the present situation which would call into question the sovereignty of the guinean people and the territorial integrity and independence of guinea-bissau. the eu and the international community must be more committed if a democratic and stable state is to be built in guinea-bissau.
in writing. the european parliament condemned the military coup in guinea-bissau on 12 april and called for the freedom and respect for the physical integrity of all citizens detained by the military rebels. i voted in favour of this parliament resolution condemning the violent repression of peaceful demonstrations, urging all those involved to stop their illegal and violent actions immediately and also calling for the restoration of order, including through the completion of the electoral process.
in writing. - this resolution strongly condemns the military coup in guinea-bissau. it comes with a set of important principles and guidelines to help move beyond the current situation, such as: the refusal of any attempt to legitimize the coup and to recognize any self-proclaimed military command, national transitional council or transitional government, the advocacy of the restoration of constitutional order and the completion of the electoral process interrupted by the coup, respect for the physical integrity of all public officials and other citizens subject to arbitrary detention and persecution, the release of detainees and an end to violence, looting and intimidation. we welcome the inclusion of the paragraph on the rejection of any external exploitation of the present situation which would jeopardize the sovereignty of the guinean people and the territorial integrity and independence of guinea-bissau, which we have proposed. we reject the insistence of the other groups to include in the resolution some points which may conflict with this principle, in particular by opening the door to external interference in the country through the esdp. any mission in the country, within the framework of the pflp or other organisations, should have a clear and precise un mandate to support the sovereign institutions of the country, which respects the sovereign will of these institutions, international law and the un charter.
in writing. - i approve this report, expressing my extreme concern at the escalation of hostilities between sudan and south sudan due to the unresolved issue of post-separation issues, including the sharing of economic resources such as oil. the european union should work closely with regional and global actors to ensure the smooth implementation of the un resolution calling for an end to hostilities between sudan and south sudan and to pave the way for a comprehensive resolution to resolve the problems of territorial separation.
in writing. the region now occupied by the states of sudan and south sudan has been a martyrdom for many years, and is a real humanitarian disaster. the escalation of the conflict between the two states raises fears of a return to the same scale of violence and violations of freedom, democracy and the human rights of their populations. the european union must be at the forefront of efforts to prevent such an outcome and must ensure that both states take account of the interests of their peoples and come to terms with each other in order to ensure their survival and the peace that has been as rare as it is desirable. the european parliament, on the initiative of a member of my party, awarded the 2007 sakharov prize to salih mahmoud osman, who has revealed firsthand the tragedy in darfur and throughout the country. perhaps you'll be advised that we can take you in one more time and hear you again about what's going on there. we know what the consequences of the prolonged western silence have been for the sudanese. we owe them a renewed attention and a greater capacity for action today.
in writing. the joint motion for a resolution, tabled following a statement by the commission vice-president, catherine ashton, replacing the motions for resolutions tabled by various political groups, deals with the situation in sudan and south sudan. for years, these people lived through a civil war that left thousands and thousands dead and devastated the country. the european union (eu), seeking to contribute to peace in the oil-rich region, supported the independence process of the two countries. however, it has not been possible to establish peace, let alone create the conditions for the start of the process of transition to democracy. the eu remains committed to the peace process, having mobilised €285 million of special funds to support south sudan. however, human rights violations continue with south sudan bombing sudan. despite the african union (au) peace council calling for the withdrawal of troops from both sides, this recommendation was not heeded. i urge the parties to accept the roadmap for peace endorsed by the au peace council and adopted by the un security council (resolution 2046 of 2 may 2012).
in writing. - we have always warned of the dangers of supporting the referendum in south sudan. it's good to remember. it was encouraged and funded by the eu (including the majority of this parliament), the us and the un. we warned that support for the destruction of the unity of the country could lead to an escalation of confrontation and a climate of destabilization between the two sides, with potential effects for the entire region. unfortunately, the reality confirms this warning, with the return of the conflict between north and south over the definition of borders. the us and its allies took advantage of the conflict that existed until 2005, exacerbating poverty, social injustices, ethnic and religious differences (between the arab-muslim north and the african-christian south) and pushed the peoples to secede, for reasons of their own geostrategic interest and exploitation of the considerable oil reserves and various important minerals in the south. we advocate a peaceful political solution to the conflict, free from external interference, supporting dialogue between the parties and mutually acceptable solutions to the problem of defining borders and sharing oil revenues. the deployment of more un forces, as this resolution advocates, and their permanent presence may not be the necessary contribution to a genuine process of unity and peace for this region.
in writing. - any armed conflict must be duly condemned by the eu. in this particular case, it is already an open confrontation with obvious consequences affecting the populations, especially the most vulnerable, such as women, the elderly and children. a solution must be found quickly to put an end to this conflict.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the international community to honour the funding commitments to the region and in particular to help address the serious shortages of food aid, emergency shelter and protection, paying particular attention to the food security situation and taking action if the situation worsens.
in writing. − south sudan officially became an independent state on 1 january 2012. however, the lack of agreement on a transitional economic regime between the two countries, including on the use of oil, led to the seizure of south sudanese oil by khartoum and the decision by south sudan to suspend oil production, which has contributed greatly to the current crisis. it is therefore of the utmost importance that these two countries begin to show their political will to pursue the path of peace by resolving the security issues on both sides within the framework of the joint political and security mechanism, starting with the creation of a secure demilitarised zone along the border and the unconditional withdrawal of all their armed forces. with a view to ensuring long-term stability in the region, a new and unified global international strategy is required, in which the eu plays a role alongside other global and regional actors, including through financing for the region, in order to address the serious shortcomings in food aid, emergency shelter and protection.
in writing. − the independence of the republic of south sudan, declared on 9 july 2011 following a referendum in the country, did not bring the desired end to tensions between the two countries. the continuing conflicts on both sides have a dramatic impact on the possibility of implementing a genuine rule of law. despite the roadmap adopted by the african union and the un for the two countries, the recent conflicts in the oil-rich town of heglig have reignited old fears as both sides claim sovereignty over the territory. both countries have high rates of poverty and the worst development rates in the world. to look after the welfare of the populations, it is necessary to reach an agreement between the two. here the eu must work together with the african partners in the african union and the un. however, the authorities in sudan and south sudan must be open to dialogue and a full ceasefire.
in writing. - we have always warned of the dangers of supporting the referendum in the then southern region of sudan, which was encouraged and financed by the eu, the us and the un and by the majority of the ep. we warned that support for the destruction of the unity of the country would generate confrontation and destabilization of both sides, with potential effects for the entire region. unfortunately, reality confirms this warning with the return of the conflict between north and south over the definition of borders. the us, eu, israel took advantage of the conflict that existed until 2005, exacerbated poverty, social injustices, ethnic and religious differences (the north is arab-muslim and the south african-christian) and pushed the peoples to secede for reasons of geostrategic self-interest and exploitation of the considerable oil reserves and various important minerals in the south. it is necessary to advocate a peaceful political solution to the conflict, free from any external interference, supporting dialogue between the parties and mutually acceptable solutions to the problem of defining borders and sharing oil revenues. the deployment of more un forces, as advocated in this resolution, and their permanent presence may not be the necessary contribution to a genuine process of unity and peace for this region.
in writing. - i support the agreement, particularly because there are historical and cultural links and strong trade traditions between the eu and the countries concerned. in particular, i welcome the clear commitment of all parties to the promotion of human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law, confirmed by the inclusion in article 1 of the trade agreement of broad binding provisions on these fundamental principles.
in writing. it is with great personal satisfaction that i have seen this report voted in favour by 525 votes in favour (76.5%) and 64 abstentions (9.4%) before the european parliament gave its consent to the trade agreement between the eu and colombia and peru, for which i am the rapporteur here in the european parliament. the first word to the co-rapporteur (of this previous report), my german socialist colleague bernd lange, with whom it was possible to establish a basis of mutual understanding, which has given rise to this strong support for our report. in this previous resolution, we acknowledge and support the enormous efforts of the colombian and peruvian governments in defending human rights, labour rights, indigenous peoples and the environment in recent years and call for greater involvement of civil society in the practical implementation of these fundamental values on which we do not compromise and in accelerating the reforms underway, which we believe will improve the applicability and transparency of this agreement. while i ask, as an addendum to this resolution, for a road map from each of our andean partners on these matters, from a strictly personal point of view i believe that the mechanisms provided for in the agreement, if scrupulously implemented, would lead to the same results. in october we will vote to approve the trade agreement.
in writing. - i cannot but support the trade agreement with colombia and peru, countries whose language, history and culture are so close to those of the european union. for years, these countries have been plagued by guerrilla movements such as the farc and the shining path, and they have made an effort to adopt their practices in democracy and human rights without renouncing the fight against those who seek to undermine democracy and the rule of law. the eu is also considering a new trade agreement with the two countries, which is expected to be beneficial to both sides.
in writing. the resolution under consideration, tabled following a question with a request for an oral answer on behalf of the committee on international trade, concerns the trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru. for years colombia has been considered a haven for drug producers and traffickers. unscrupulous people took advantage of the poverty of the majority of the population to exploit them. thanks to international cooperation, these countries have embarked on a process of reform and the fight against drug trafficking with very positive results. colombia exceeded the forecasts of the international labour organisation in terms of the adoption of the measures advocated and peru implemented the united nations convention on labour. despite improvements in respect for human rights and the rule of law, both countries are aware of the need to continue to improve in this area. i voted in favour because i believe that this acp can help these countries to combat poverty and social exclusion and to promote the substitution of tradable consumer goods for the drug culture, thus improving exports to the eu, the main importer of goods produced in peru.
in writing. - another free trade agreement signed by the eu. this was the culmination of a difficult process in which the negotiations with the andean community were concluded only with colombia and peru. the so-called road map for human and labour rights aims to mitigate criticism of free trade and some of its most negative effects. but it obviously does not change the essence of this agreement. we'll be here to evaluate your practical results. between two unequal parties, free trade is always the protectionism of the rich. the pressure on countries which have hitherto benefited from the gsp system to sign such agreements cannot be ignored. on the other hand, the hypocrisy of the eu in human rights issues is once again demonstrated. a launching pad for countries that don't align with their interests, conveniently ignored when appropriate. this is now the case in colombia, where clear violations of human rights have been denounced by numerous social organizations, particularly trade unions. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement. we voted against it.
in writing. − as the eu is latin america's largest investor and second largest trading partner, and also the largest provider of development aid, we believe that these data are sufficient to have a clear and well-defined strategy for eu-latin america trade relations. a good way to achieve the aid that latin america needs is through the dynamisation of trade relations between the two blocs, which, if it comes to fruition, will be one of the main ones in the world. this is where the negotiations with colombia and peru come in. however, the outermost regions of europe, which may be affected by the import of certain agricultural products, must not be forgotten. we must find a balanced agreement which will enable these countries to develop, but which at the same time will not be detrimental to the various economic sectors of some member states, especially the agricultural sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which highlights the fact that colombia and peru have ratified the eight ilo core conventions plus three of the four governance conventions, as stated by the ilo representative at the international trade commission's public hearing on the trade agreement held on 29 february 2012 in the european parliament in brussels.
in writing. - it should be stressed at the outset that there is a clear commitment by all parties to the eu-colombia-peru trade agreement to promote respect for human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law, which deserves my full support. the aim of this agreement is to open markets for goods, services, public procurement and investment, to foster economic integration between the parties and to promote comprehensive economic development, with the aim of reducing poverty and creating new employment opportunities, improving working conditions and raising living standards through liberalisation and increased trade and investment between the territories. however, much remains to be done in colombia and peru, in particular with regard to the effective implementation of the new legislative framework aimed at addressing old problems that have not yet been fully resolved, such as poverty, violence and corruption, internal armed conflicts, illegal armed groups, drug trafficking and land expropriation. that said, this agreement can prove to be a key instrument in combating the kind of situations that plague that south american region.
in writing. − the trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru aims to liberalise the market for goods, services and investments and to promote economic integration between the various parties, with a view to reducing poverty, creating new employment opportunities, improving living conditions and standards. however, the agreement does not provide for a dispute settlement mechanism and sanctions are excluded in the event of a breach of the terms relating to trade and sustainable development. it is in this context that the european parliament is advocating the importance of maintaining a constructive dialogue with partner countries on the protection of human rights. regretting that the european parliament is not kept informed of the activities of the dialogue mechanism voluntarily established in 2009 between the european union and colombia, i voted in favour of this resolution which calls for the inclusion in the agreement of domestic mechanisms and dialogue with civil society.
in writing. - we voted against this resolution because free trade agreements, by opening up the markets for goods, services, public procurement and investment, do not lead to the alleged development of the weaker economies concerned by the agreement, but rather to the colonization of these economies. at the moment, the workers and peoples of peru and colombia are fighting a courageous struggle against the free trade agreement which, like the previous ones, will lead to the attack on the achievements of the workers and the sovereignty of the peoples, the appropriation by multinationals of natural resources and biodiversity, the increase in unemployment, the ruin of millions of small farmers with consequent threats to food sovereignty and security.
in writing. - i approve this report and congratulate the european union on this symbolic milestone. by having a single diplomatic front on human rights, with the creation of the post of european union special representative for human rights, we are finally speaking with one voice, even in a specific area, which i think is already a considerable reach. i think it is however appropriate to assess the importance and mandate of this new representative of the european union.
in writing. −while the appointment of the eu special representative for human rights (eusr) and the establishment of his mandate is formally a council decision based on a proposal from the eu high representative, i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider that the eusr should act and speak on behalf of the union, reflecting the indivisible and shared responsibility of all eu institutions and member states to protect and promote human rights worldwide.
in writing. − human rights and fundamental freedoms are the set of values and principles that distinguish us as human beings and on which our coexistence is based. they are universal, indivisible and interdependent. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty was undoubtedly an important step forward in terms of human rights, including the possibility of creating an eu special representative for human rights. the ep has called on numerous occasions for the appointment of this special representative in order to promote the visibility, efficiency, coherence and accountability of eu human rights policy. i welcome the fact that his appointment is scheduled for 25 june by the foreign ministers' council and the role of the ep in appointing and supervising his mandate. the mandate will be for two and a half years, renewable in order to ensure continuity, consistency and democratic accountability. while under the authority of the eu high representative for foreign affairs and cfsp, it should nevertheless have an independent, strong and flexible mandate, in the performance of which it should act and speak on behalf of the union, reflecting the shared responsibility at the level of the eu institutions and member states to protect and promote democracy and human rights worldwide.
in writing. - the european union has been playing the role of guardian and interpreter of human rights internationally and of honest broker between the parties concerned in many cases where their violation is at issue. it has a track record of action and deliberation which makes it a particularly cohesive and active political bloc on these matters, seen externally as exemplary. despite this cohesion, given the high standards required in this area and the european effort to live up to its practice and legacy, it is justified to appoint a special representative of the european union specially dedicated to these issues and able to represent it particularly when these issues have been on the agenda. i agree with the ideal profile of the candidate for the post proposed by mr salafranca and his description of what his duties should be and the means at his disposal. i hope that the first eu special representative for human rights will rise to the challenge and that his intellectual ingenuity and practical sense will ennoble the role and make it visible and respected in the international context.
in writing. − the european parliament's concern for respect for human rights is recognised worldwide and the sakharov prize for freedom of thought, awarded annually and intended to reward personalities or entities who have distinguished themselves in the defence of human rights and fundamental freedoms, is much appreciated. the report, drawn up by josé ignacio salafranca sánchez-neyra, focuses on the ep's recommendation to the council on the appointment of a european union special representative for human rights. the eu's structure is based on human rights, universal values which must be taken into account in all eu negotiations with third countries. in fact, the violation of human rights is still very much alive and well and i would like to highlight two cases: the self-immolation of monks in tibet and the continuing massacre of innocents in syria, which alone would justify this appointment. i therefore welcome the present recommendation to appoint an eu special representative for human rights who will work for human rights justice, for the abolition of the death penalty, for the defence of causes against impunity, for the defence of the rights of women, children, minorities and against any form of discrimination.
in writing. - we have repeatedly denounced the instrumental conception of human rights which is increasingly dominating european union policy in this area. the creation of the eu special representative for human rights cannot be dissociated from this process. the appointment of a face to this policy will give it increased visibility, but will not erase its fragility, contradictions and inconsistencies. unfortunately, what is at stake is more the defence of the eu's economic and geostrategic interests in the world - that is, its powers and its economic groups - than a genuine defence of human rights. we did not support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that respect for human rights is one of the main pillars of european policies. the eusr for human rights, as the sole spokesperson for democratic values, will strengthen the eu's role in the protection and promotion of human rights in its external policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation to the council on the eu special representative for human rights, in which the european parliament, recognising the exclusive competence of the council to appoint the eu special representative on the proposal of the high representative, urges that, in order to enhance the transparency and accountability of the mandate of the eusr, an exchange of views/hearing with the appointed eusr for human rights be held in the competent committee of the european parliament.
in writing. − the appointment of an eu special representative for human rights is a very important step towards enhancing the visibility and coherence of eu policy in this area and is considered a key part of its common foreign and security policy (cfsp). while the appointment of the eu special representative (eusr) for human rights and the establishment of his mandate formally constitute a council decision, on the basis of a proposal by the high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy, the eusr should act and speak on behalf of the union, reflecting the indivisible and shared responsibility of all eu institutions and member states to protect and promote human rights worldwide. i believe that this reaffirms the eu's commitment to promoting human rights and democracy in all its external action, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − human rights are a constituent pillar of the eu as expressed in article 21 of the eu treaty and their promotion and defence are an essential policy for common foreign and security action. following several calls from parliament, on the basis of article 33 teu, the council is asked to appoint the eu special representative for human rights (eusr) in order to make eu policies more effective and visible and in line with other international organisations already on the ground. the aim of this post is to give greater visibility to the eu's role in promoting human rights and democracy in the world. there should therefore be coordination with other services and institutions within the eu, and it should serve as a link with international, regional and non-governmental organisations. the eusr shall be a person of international standing and international renown in the field of human rights, and his or her mandate shall be for a period of 2 years, renewable after consultation of the ep.
in writing. - the appointment of an eu special representative for human rights underlines the importance the eu wishes to attach to this front, which is obviously instrumental. by creating a face, the eu wants to give greater visibility to a hypocritical policy that creates or uses processes of interference and aggression where and when eu interests are at stake. taking into account the eu's political practice, the appointment of a representative is not aimed at its effective defence - which should above all be a cross-cutting practice - but rather accentuates the manipulation and minimisation of human rights. it is to reinforce a policy which links various eu instruments, such as the european external action service, with all those who, in countries where the eu has geostrategic, economic and financial interests, are available to give expression to interference and the violation of the sovereignty of the people, defending the interests of the eu's great powers. as the eu crisis is demonstrating, big capital in the eu is trying to get out of its crisis by increasing the exploitation of workers and by dominating natural resources, energy, food and markets. it is towards this objective that the eu nominee's action will converge.
in writing. - i support this report, considering it essential that the european union has an effective, efficient and transparent domain in the field of arms negotiations, and should take into account that opaque, poorly controlled and regulated arms trade agreements can lead to irresponsible arms exchanges and cause unnecessary human harm. in view of this, a strong and clear set of parameters in which such agreements are made is urgently needed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i understand the need to seek to regulate the trade in conventional arms through an international legal instrument. despite this principled position, i cannot but express my scepticism both as regards its conclusion in the appropriate terms and as regards its effectiveness if it comes into force. the weight of the arms industry is well known and the european need to maintain, if not increase, member states' investment in their defence industries as part of the common effort to be undertaken within the framework of the atlantic alliance. but beyond this legitimate investment in these industries that generate jobs and create technical innovation, there is a hard-to-control side market that moves many millions of euros a year. we must seek to limit their action and combat their main agents. without this firm action at international level and a truly operational character, the treaty may at first be nothing more than a mere enunciation of hopeful words. but words are worth more than guns and, fortunately, produce effects that guns cannot always counteract.
in writing. - the arms trade is a matter which divides europeans between those who see it as just another form of trade with the resulting economic added value and those who see it as a commercial strategy enabling terrorist groups to achieve their aims. this treaty is crucial to prevent situations like those that have occurred in syria, with china and russia providing weapons that are used to kill innocent people. it is therefore essential that the united nations adopt restrictive measures and transparent rules on this type of trade. given that the value of arms exports by member states represents some 30% of world exports, and that they are among the world's largest arms producers, i welcome this initiative by the united nations to draw up an instrument which would legally bind all un members with regard to the manufacture, import, export and transfer of conventional arms. i welcome the measures proposed and hope that all countries will implement them as soon as possible so as to prevent these weapons from being diverted to illicit markets where they can be used for other purposes, including criminal activities or terrorist acts.
in writing. − the discussion on the arms trade treaty (att) began in 2006, when the un general assembly adopted a resolution that had the support of 153 countries. the united states was the only un member state to vote against the creation of this treaty. the implementation of this treaty is of great importance in a context of renewed arms race, with increased military spending, especially by the usa and the nato countries, which is increasingly revealing its aggressive nature. the eu, with the treaty of lisbon and the provisions on the european defence agency, is also entering this race. the regulation of arms imports, exports and transfers will be all the more effective if it is accompanied by a process of multilateral and reciprocal disarmament, in particular by dismantling the existing huge nuclear arsenals and the complete destruction of chemical and biological weapons. it is also important to attack the instruments, such as tax havens, which enable money laundering associated with arms trafficking. we appreciate that the reference to employment in the arms industry has been removed from the resolution. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. − the treaty should cover as many activities as possible in the conventional arms trade, including import, export, transfer (including transit and transhipment, as well as temporary import and export and re-export), foreign licensed manufacture, stockpile management and all related services, including brokering, transport and financing. the treaty should cover all aspects of the trade in conventional arms, including transfers between states, transfers between states and private end-users, commercial sales and leases, as well as loans, grants, aid or any other form of transfer. the treaty should also cover the widest range of conventional weapons, including small arms, light weapons and ammunition, transfers without the use of bodies, dual-use goods, components and technologies associated with their use, as well as the manufacture or maintenance of such weapons for military or security purposes and law enforcement purposes. i also think it is very important to pay particular attention to the marking and traceability of conventional weapons and ammunition in order to strengthen accountability and prevent arms transfers being diverted to illicit recipients.
in writing. − a poorly regulated, uncontrolled and opaque arms trade leads to an irresponsible arms trade, has already caused unnecessary human suffering, fuelled armed conflict, instability, terrorist attacks and corruption, has also undermined peace processes, good governance and socioeconomic development, and has led to the overthrow of democratically elected governments and the violation of the rule of law, human rights and international humanitarian law. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for the negotiation of a legally binding international arms trade treaty in july 2012 to be a landmark step towards progress through greater transparency and accountability, and to this end, to establish the highest international standards and criteria for evaluating decisions on the transfer, import and export of conventional arms.
in writing. the arms trade treaty aims to regulate and bind signatory states to the establishment of standards for the import, export and transfer of conventional arms with a view to reducing illicit trade in such arms. this illicit trade is directly linked to organised crime and criminal activities, to supporting terrorist acts, and to undermining global, regional and local stability and security. in the negotiations on this treaty, which are still ongoing this year, it is imperative to involve the majority of the states and not to forget that it must be in line with international human rights law and international humanitarian law. the eu must present a common and robust position, showing the other partners that transparency and accountability in the negotiation and ratification process is of the utmost importance for global stability and security.
in writing. − the debate on the establishment of the arms trade treaty (att) began in 2006 when the un general assembly adopted a resolution supported by 153 countries, with the us being the only un member state to vote against the creation of the att. the completion of this process is of great importance in a context where the arms race and military expenditure, the investment in new weapons by the usa, nato and the eu, is being relaunched, over the hypocritical talk of their reduction. however, it must be stressed that the regulation of the import, export and transfer of arms will be all the more relevant if it is accompanied by a process of multilateral and reciprocal disarmament, in particular the dismantling of the huge existing nuclear arsenals, starting with the world's largest nuclear powers - such as the usa - and the complete destruction of chemical and biological weapons.
in writing. - i vote in favour. i express my deep concern about the situation in the democratic republic of congo, where the re-election of president joseph kabila and the subsequent contestation of the election results by the opposition following the last presidential elections on 28 november 2011 have resulted in extreme clashes with serious violence. since then, the situation in the country has remained very unstable, with the continuing violation of human rights and the humanitarian situation being even more worrying, making a transparent democratization process involving all parties urgent.
in writing. - the elections in the democratic republic of congo, which were affected by a number of irregularities, demonstrate how the institutionalisation of democracy does not depend solely on the electoral act. the drc has not been a fully peaceful state for a long time, a state which respects democracy and human rights. there are many reports of this and many international attempts to prevent the situation from worsening. unfortunately, there are no tangible results worthy of more than a vague hope and which do not cause concern to observers and international partners. the stabilization of the democratic republic of congo is a major factor in the stabilization of a continent which cannot be achieved without the stabilization of its second largest country. its process of transition to democracy inspires the natural care and constant attention of the european union.
in writing. − the democratic republic of congo (drc), one of the poorest countries in the world, is a nascent democracy recovering from a very difficult past and therefore needs eu support to consolidate the reforms it has begun. this joint motion for a resolution, tabled in replacement of the motions for resolutions tabled by six political groups, concerns the monitoring of the elections in the drc, whose eu observation mission concluded that these elections were marked by a lack of transparency and credibility due to the fraud and irregularities found. in addition, there is a continuing violation of human rights by armed groups, confirming a serious problem of lack of governmental authority. the eu must continue to support the drc, in particular the victims of armed groups whose disarmament is essential and urgent for the establishment of a climate of peace and the implementation of much needed reforms in the country. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution and i hope that the situation will improve and that the next elections will take place in the normal way required so that all the human rights violations and crimes committed by elements of the army will end.
in writing. − the democratic republic of congo (drc), located in the heart of africa and bordering numerous countries in the central african region, has enormous potential in natural resources, particularly minerals. a potential unmatched in the entire african continent and even in the world. since its independence, the processes of interference and aggression have been continuous, either from outside or using actors within the country itself, pushing it into a series of conflicts that have almost continuously generated the immense contradiction that in this country of so much potential, the majority of the people live in a situation of extreme poverty. for our part, we will continue to support this struggle for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and right of the country to economic and social development. it is necessary to defend the sovereignty of the congolese people, to ensure that the people and the natural resources of the country can be used to achieve their interests and aspirations.

member of the commission. − mr president, a robust and systemic solution must be found – and very soon – to the financial and economic crisis. a major consequence of this crisis is the excessively high unemployment. unemployment now stands at 10.3% in the 27 member states of the eu, a level we have not seen since the 1990s. within the euro area, the level of unemployment is even higher, reaching 11% of the workforce. to find real solutions to europe’s current crisis, we need a jobs-centred approach. the employment package that the commission presented in april shows how employment policies can ensure that job creation drives economic growth. the package also outlines ways to rebalance eu economic governance by strengthening the coordination of employment policies. we need the strong support of the european parliament on both these issues. the commission package seeks to reorient european employment policy along three main lines. first, we support measures to create jobs and boost the demand for labour across the economy. we identified the green economy, information and communication technologies, and the health and care services as the three areas that can generate the most job opportunities and for which a detailed action plan is presented. we propose concrete demands and interventions to support job creation, such as hiring subsidies for newly created jobs, a budget-neutral tax shift from labour to environmental taxes and greater support for business start-ups, self-employment and last, but not least, the social economy. second, the package seeks to make labour markets more dynamic through balanced and fair reforms, notably investment in skills and the removal of obstacles to free movement of workers and worker mobility. we need to secure transitions in the labour market by making sure that transitions pay. a more dynamic european labour market will help to reduce existing skill shortages and mismatches. this is why we also need to invest in skills and to create new tools to anticipate and monitor skills development at the eu level. the commission is also committed to improving mobility by removing obstacles, such as those affecting the portability of pensions. we are also proposing to transform the current eures system into a genuine eu employment tool able to match jobs and jobseekers across borders. third, the package aims to strengthen eu governance of employment policies. in particular, we want to reinforce monitoring of member states’ employment polices so that employment and social concerns do not lag behind economic concerns. we also seek to involve the social partners in the process of implementing reforms and monitoring wage developments at the eu level. in addition, the package also sets out a stronger link between member states’ labour market reforms and investment through eu financial instruments and, in particular, the european social fund. parliament’s support for the package is critical. it will provide an additional political impetus for employment to be considered among the cornerstones of our ‘european growth pact’. i am looking forward to this debate today.
