in writing. − serious industrial accidents, such as those in seveso (italy, 1976), enschede (netherlands, 2000), toulouse (france, 2001) and buncefield (uk, 2005), have not only claimed many lives, but have also destroyed property and damaged the environment, causing irreparable damage. to reduce the likelihood and mitigate the consequences of these accidents, the eu adopted in due course the seveso i and ii directives. the aim is now to review these directives in order to integrate them with the provisions of regulation (ec) no 1272/2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (cer regulation). this review is necessary and the commission has chosen to maintain the level of protection and avoid substantial changes.
in writing. - industrial accidents usually have devastating consequences: human casualties, air pollution and groundwater pollution. the report under review, by jános áder, looks at the dangers associated with serious accidents involving dangerous substances in europe we have 2000 companies dealing with these matters - and aims to protect people, the environment and avoid wasting resources. in fact, serious industrial accidents have caused billions of dollars in damage. to reduce the likelihood of these accidents occurring and to minimise their consequences, the eu first adopted directive 82/501/eec (seveso i directive) and later directive 96/82/ec (seveso ii directive) which, although successful, needs revision due to the need to adapt to the ccr regulation. the new rules increase safety and apply equally to all businesses and in all eu member states. in addition, inspection rules are more detailed and public information is improved. i welcome the package of measures now approved, which will allow member states to improve safety conditions, thus contributing to a higher level of protection for people and the environment.
in writing. the new proposal for a directive repeals the existing directive 96/82/ec, known as the seveso ii directive, which aims to prevent major accidents (such as those at seveso, bhopal, schweizerhalle, etc.) involving large quantities of dangerous substances (or mixtures) and to limit the consequences of these accidents for man and the environment. the main reason for the revision of the seveso ii directive arises from the need to adjust its annex i to the regulation on the classification, labelling and packaging of dangerous substances and mixtures. some of the amendments are purely technical, although there is also provision for the right to information, prevention and emergency plans, and the extension of the scope of application, aspects with which we can agree. we voted in favour of this report, but we cannot fail to stress the points made by our group during the debate, in particular those relating to the need to improve the safety, training and working conditions of workers directly or indirectly involved in the production and/or use of dangerous substances. unfortunately, not all the proposals were accepted by the majority.
in writing. - the serious industrial accidents which have occurred in the past almost all over europe and which have had serious repercussions, such as loss of life, destruction of public and private property, as well as severe environmental damage, have forced the eu to adopt the seveso i and ii directives. the report aims to review these directives in order to integrate them with the provisions of regulation (ec) no 1272/2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (cer regulation).
in writing. - the proposed revision of the seveso ii directive on serious industrial accidents is necessary and the commission has rightly chosen to maintain the level of protection and avoid substantial changes in the scope. i voted in favour of this proposal and i stress the rapporteur's position that any amendments should only be authorised through the ordinary legislative procedure as the inclusion of new substances could lead to substantial changes in the scope with potentially important economic repercussions, and therefore the european parliament should be able to exercise its full powers in the decision-making process on the inclusion of substances.
in writing. − this report provides for a broader revision of the seveso directive, through the adaptation of the cre regulation on the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures, which applies the un globally harmonized system of classification and labelling of chemicals in the eu. this is a differentiated approach to the obligations of operators, whereby the strictness of the rules increases with the quantity of substances. in addition, in order to ensure an ever higher level of protection, greater access to information, greater public participation in decision-making and easier access to justice are proposed. i therefore voted in favour of this report, because i believe that it is an important step towards preventing accidents such as those which have occurred in italy, france and the netherlands, which have claimed a great number of lives, destroyed public and private property and damaged the environment, and caused billions of euros in damage.
in writing. − in order to reduce the likelihood and consequences of industrial accidents at all levels, the eu adopted the seveso i directive in 1985, amended in 1996 by the seveso ii directive, also amended in 2003, which, in addition to a list of establishments where dangerous substances or mixtures thereof are present in large quantities that may constitute a risk, includes a set of obligations for operators and responsible authorities in the member states and a major accident prevention policy. this report aims to validate the adaptation of this directive to the cre regulation, to implement the un globally harmonized system of classification and labelling of chemicals, to harmonise it with the aarhus convention and to strengthen the criteria for inspections. i support the rapporteur in that i disagree that the ec can adopt delegated acts in amending annex i, implementing the directive, and that the ordinary legislative procedure should be used as a basis where parliament will have a say on the inclusion of new substances. finally, i am in favour of the application of access to information and public participation in decision-making processes and access to justice in environmental matters.
in writing. the new proposal for a directive repeals the existing directive 96/82/ec, known as the seveso ii directive, which aims to prevent major accidents (such as those at seveso, bhopal, schweizerhalle, among others) involving large quantities of dangerous substances and to limit the consequences of these accidents for man and the environment. the main reason for the revision of the seveso ii directive arises from the need to align its annex i to the regulation on the classification, labelling and packaging of dangerous substances and mixtures. we welcome the fact that the council has agreed to include in annex i at least three of the most toxic substances in the acute toxic group. the right of the public to know the procedures for participating in the decision-making process, to be informed on how to use them, to have access to information and finally to have access to justice in environmental matters is also valued.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that food for certain nutritional uses is different from food for normal consumption and is manufactured to meet specific dietary requirements. the non-implementation of the dietary food framework directive is still very wide, which has made the implementation of this directive difficult and resulted in market distortions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the labelling of foodstuffs is not distorted.
in writing. − the commission presented this proposal for a regulation on food for infants and young children and food for medicinal purposes in june 2011. the purpose of this revision of the legislation is to simplify, also applied in the creation of a single list of substances that can be added to the foodstuffs covered by this proposal. the objective is to incorporate low calorie dietary products (dbtc) into the scope of this regulation by including them in the definition of food for medicinal purposes. it is essential that the faster and less costly notification process remains the rule, as a marketing authorisation decided at national level and the need to strengthen processes through additional rules on labelling and composition. this simplified legal framework, which provides greater protection, should be applied equally to imported and exported foodstuffs and facilitates the application of the precautionary principle. the proper functioning of the internal market depends on this. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the thorough revision of the legislation on foodstuffs intended for particular nutritional uses, by abolishing the concept of dietetic food, which in most cases no longer makes sense from a nutritional point of view, and also because i consider it essential to strengthen the legal security of industrial operators and food-vulnerable populations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on food for infants and young children and food for special medical purposes because it includes measures that help to ensure a high level of consumer protection in the eu, in particular through provisions on food for people intolerant to gluten and the use of pesticides.
in writing. − it is essential to promote appropriate regulation of food labelling. we cannot legislate on healthy eating, but we must ensure that consumers have the information they need to make an informed choice. this is particularly important in the diet for infants and children and for people with special medical needs. the proposal lays down stricter and clearer rules on labelling, presentation and advertising. these standards cover not only infant formula and food but also food intolerances and low-calorie diets. the labelling, presentation and advertising of these foods should be clear and easy to understand for consumers.
in writing. − the issue of food for those with special nutritional needs is a key area of eu legislation to ensure a safe and healthy food supply. the market niche for these foods has grown significantly in recent years, leading to a lack of clarity when trying to distinguish between everyday food and food intended for specific groups of people. the commission therefore proposes to revise the framework directive by removing the general rules on dietetic products but retaining some specific food rules adopted under the directive. i agree that it is right to limit the scope of this regulation to a limited number of specific foodstuffs. it is clear that infants, children under 3 years of age and certain patients for whom special diets are essential deserve special attention and harmonised treatment in the european union. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted for, because newborns and children need to be well protected, but it is also urgent to move forward with a proposal for a directive on so-called growth-promoting milk, since it was not included in this package.
in writing. − this report confirms the limitation of the scope of the regulation to a limited number of specific foodstuffs, with particular attention to infants, children under 3 years of age and certain patients for whom special feeding is essential. although it excludes from its scope meals intended to replace all or part of the daily diet and sports foods specifically for intense muscular effort, the regulation includes low-calorie dietary products, including them in the category of food intended for medical purposes, for the treatment, authorisation and medical monitoring of obese patients. the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the rules on the labelling of foodstuffs are complied with. we supported this report, although we regret that the right wing voted against the fact that we could have gone further in areas such as the defence of greater restrictions on the use of pesticides, or greater requirements and restrictions on the advertising of certain products, ensuring better and more complete information for consumers.
in writing. − the promotion of better regulation of food labelling is essential. it is important that consumers have the information they need to make an informed choice. for the most part, these concerns are more pressing in the case of food for infants and children and for people with specific medical needs. this regulation introduces stricter and clearer rules on labelling, presentation and advertising. the labelling, presentation and advertising of these foods should be clear and easy to understand for all consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which proposes a simplified legal framework for the rules on food for infants and young children and food for special medical purposes. this framework, which provides greater protection by means of the precautionary principle, should be applied equally to imported and exported foodstuffs. the proper functioning of the internal market depends on this, and the health of the most vulnerable cannot be ignored.
in writing. − this report follows a proposal for a regulation presented by the commission in june 2011 on food for infants and young children and food for special medical purposes. the primary objectives of this report include the incorporation of low calorie dietary foods (lcdf) into the scope of this regulation by including them in the definition of food for medical purposes, the increased legal coverage of people suffering from food intolerance, and ensuring that products for newborns and children are placed on the market free from pesticides and any other toxic substance. the main aim is to simplify the current legal framework, which should apply equally to imported and exported foodstuffs, thus facilitating the application of the precautionary principle. the proper functioning of the internal market depends on this, and the health protection of the most vulnerable cannot be left out of the picture.
in writing. - this proposal aims to create specific legislation for infants, children under 3 years of age and certain patients, who are considered vulnerable and therefore need high standards of protection, in relation to imported and exported foodstuffs. the commission proposal lays down a single list of substances which may be added to food and excludes certain specific features from this proposal, in particular sports foods and the concept of dietetic food. the commission is also proposing to simplify product labels so that they are clear and perceptible to consumers. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's position that this regulation should include an obligation to include gluten in products if they are intended for a low-calorie diet. i am voting in favour of this proposal because i believe that once again the european consumer is protected.
in writing. - this report is consistent with the commission's position of limiting the scope of the regulation to a limited number of specific foodstuffs, paying particular attention to infants, children under 3 years of age and certain patients for whom special diets are essential. although it excludes from its scope meals intended to replace all or part of the daily diet and sports foods specifically for intense muscular effort, the regulation includes low-calorie dietary products, including them in the category of food intended for medical purposes, for the treatment, authorisation and medical monitoring of obese patients. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the food supply. the committee also expressed concern about the need to ensure that products for newborns, young children and other vulnerable populations are free of pesticides as well as any other toxic substances. we voted in favour of these controls because we are in favour of them.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this text because it is a text which defends european citizenship. in this case, promoting access to eu documentation in all languages will stimulate more active participation in eu decision-making processes. the eu brings us rights and benefits, and this is certainly one of them.
in writing. − citizen participation is an essential element of democratic governance and well-designed, structured and well-communicated public consultations are an important instrument for the transparency of the european union, thus enabling european citizens to play an increasingly active role in the european construction process. the european commission should therefore take advantage of all available technological resources to actively communicate with citizens by disseminating public consultations. it should guarantee the right of every european citizen to address the european institutions in any of the official languages of the union and that there is no linguistic discrimination between consultations. finally, consultations should be easy to understand and should be carried out within sufficiently long time limits to allow greater participation by citizens. i therefore support this resolution.
in writing. - it is never too late to say that it is essential and urgent to bring the eu closer to its citizens and to make the decision-making process of the institutions closer, more transparent and more scrutinisable. to do this, all citizens must be able to address the institutions in all the official eu languages. this is particularly important in the context of public consultation procedures. they shall be available in all official languages and all replies shall be treated equally, without discrimination on the basis of the language used.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution tabled by the epp and s&d political groups following a statement by the commission on the public consultations and their availability in all the languages of the european union for the following reasons: meps represent the peoples of 27 countries who express themselves differently, but all have the same rights of access to documents dealt with in the european institutions; public consultations are excellent opportunities to share europe's ideas and should be moments of public participation and a true exercise of european citizenship; although multilingualism is very expensive, an effort should be made to provide the next budgets with resources to enable public consultations to be carried out in all the official eu languages; very special attention is given to citizens with disabilities who are expected to be consulted using accessible formats; finally, i welcome the fact that the commission has proposed that 2013 be the european year of citizens as a way of making all europeans aware of the benefits and rights conferred on them by european citizenship.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this resolution because all eu documents must be easily accessible and available in all the official languages of the european union. we have long been denouncing, repeatedly and in detail, the abuse of multilingualism by the european institutions. it is a condition of democracy in an eu with 23 official languages that all of them are respected and treated on an equal basis. which it doesn't. parliamentary work is an example of this. it is regrettable that the same political groups which now recognise the importance of ensuring respect for multilingualism in public consultation processes have approved cuts in the european parliament's translation and interpretation services, which compromise the same respect for the different eu languages. that was a criticism we included in our resolution. the statements by the european commission and some representatives of the most populous countries (especially the united kingdom) are worrying, openly saying that multilingualism should be respected as far as budgetary constraints allow. we will continue to be vigilant in the future, fighting against any and all limitations and attempts to undermine democracy (even more) by the european institutions.
in writing. − public consultation of documents, and access to them in all eu languages, is essential if all citizens are to feel fully integrated into the eu. for that reason, there should be no worries of any kind for that objective to be a reality. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the aim of this motion for a resolution is to enhance the role of public consultations within the eu, as they are one of the main instruments for the implementation of the eu's transparency policy. in order to address the lack of communication and information between citizens and the union, it is intended to enhance the full use of existing communication channels to distribute the consultations to the general public and to conduct them, in a selective manner, together with ngos and other stakeholders. it also aims to ensure that the right of every citizen of the union to address the european institutions in any of the official languages of the union is fully respected and applied, while ensuring that all public consultations are treated equally, so that there is no linguistic discrimination between consultations. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that citizen participation is an essential element of good democratic governance.

in writing. - this resolution is based, among other documents, on the single market act and the resolution on aspects of private and commercial law, which are covered by the stockholm programme. the express aim is to create an eu regulatory framework that facilitates companies to operate across borders, in particular with regard to the transfer of their headquarters, and their ever deeper integration into the single market and european markets, allowing for more effective competition and protecting creditors, shareholders, members and, last but not least, employees. the commission is proposing to adopt the statute for a european private company, which minimises the role of employees in company decisions, and proposes a legislative initiative laying down measures to facilitate the cross-border mobility of companies within the eu, which can be deeply damaging to the interests of member states and employees.
in writing. - i approve this report because i consider it of the utmost importance that an employment package be adopted to restore employment. i agree with a framework for a european employment strategy to identify opportunities that can help create jobs and to establish european union funds that can be used in the long term as an investment in human capital. i am aware of the importance of this european framework for employment, but i believe it is pertinent that this plan will only be possible to achieve through the coordination of a european investment plan, a coherent european industrial strategy and investment in public services based on new revenues, including new financial transaction taxes and eurobonds, giving priority to investments that promote a sustainable economy, quality jobs and social justice in order to combat inequalities.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on defective silicone gel breast implants manufactured by the french company pip, because it includes proposals to develop a legal framework to ensure the safety of breast implants and medical technology in general throughout the eu, including by banning advertising of cosmetic implants.
in writing. − the pip breast implant scandal has exposed the flaws in the current eu medical device certification system. breast implants are classified as active implantable medical devices. in order to be placed on the market, according to directive 2007/47/ec, they have to fulfil three cumulative requirements: they must meet the requirements laid down by the legislation in force, bear the ce marking and be subject to a conformity assessment by a health authority. the ce marking is, as we see, a prerequisite for placing medical devices on the market and is also a guarantee of compliance with the applicable legislation, attesting that the medical device is fit for its purpose and safe. it turns out that this whole procedure failed in the case of pip breast implants and may have failed in countless others, putting the health of europeans at risk. it is therefore essential that in the next revision of the medical devices directive a common procedure is ensured which ensures first of all the safety of medical devices and the absence of risks to the life and health of patients.
in writing. - pip, a french medical device company, has sold 470,000 breast implants which have been placed in women in 71 countries. some of these implants have caused health problems and had to be removed, causing harm to patients who had allowed them to be placed. the motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled following questions with oral questions by representatives of all the political groups in the european parliament, concerns defective silicone gel breast implants manufactured by pip. i welcome the adoption of a directive on medical devices which prevents misleading advertising and holds companies producing medical devices accountable. when working with humans, all stages of the production process, from research to laboratory testing and mass production, must be subject to continuous monitoring, as human life is at stake. permanent traceability is required to increase the security and confidence of citizens. i voted in favour of this resolution because the health of patients must be at the forefront and we cannot allow any kind of fraud, let alone when it involves medical devices.
in writing. - following the scandal in france involving pip's silicone breast implants, this resolution refers to the need to strengthen cooperation between member states and to increase market surveillance, surveillance and inspection to provide a better guarantee of patient safety in medium and high risk medical devices. for inspections, annual frequency and without prior notice across the supply chain and suppliers is suggested, as well as the move towards a system of pre-market authorisation, in particular for the mentioned categories. the exchange of information between national authorities on adverse effects of medical devices and their withdrawal from the market can improve the current picture, both in terms of rapid response at national level and in terms of reducing impacts on patients. the commission is also proposing a single european database to bring together information on medical devices on the market, the record of economic transactions, surveillance and market surveillance initiatives, which should not be used to promote economic interests rather than patient safety or to jeopardise the vital protection of patients' data. we supported this resolution.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i would like to begin by thanking mr seeber for the good work he has done and for the good cooperation he has had with the shadow rapporteur. the problem of water scarcity and drought is not new but has been growing. in the last 30 years, the areas and people affected by drought have increased by almost 20 percent. the total cost of droughts over the last 30 years is about 100 billion euros. in 2003 alone, drought affected more than 10 million people, one third of the union's territory, and cost the european economy €8.7 billion. water scarcity is no longer limited to southern european countries and is likely to worsen as a result of climate change, threatening important sectors of the economy such as energy and agriculture. climate change is expected to have a negative impact on precipitation patterns and hydrological cycles with very significant effects on water quantity and quality. for example, in my country, portugal, at the end of february, about 70% of the territory was in severe drought. the proposal to set up a european drought observatory therefore makes perfect sense. european policies must focus on savings and efficiency. wastewater must be reused and recycled. water is a public good, scarce, not a commodity. we all have to contribute to it being a preserved resource.
i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the european union. on the one hand, there are the defenders of the water business, those who ignore or misrepresent the resolution of the united nations general assembly which recognized the right to drinking water and sanitation as a human right, those who, by claiming to defend the right of access to water, open the way to the interests of the transnational water cartel, whose greed inevitably clashes with the effective guarantee of the right to water and sanitation that many europeans are still deprived of. those who insist on treating water as a market commodity, subjecting it to the rules of the internal market, even in contradiction to previous resolutions of this parliament. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the water supply is not reduced to the level of the community's water resources, and that the community's water resources are not reduced to the level of the member states. this is the way in which european union legislation has been opening up doors. that is where this report comes in. on the other side of this debate are those who consider water to be a common good of mankind, a public good essential to life, which, for that very reason, should not be a source of profit in commercial exchange. those who believe that market rules cannot apply to water or water services and who therefore advocate the exclusion of water from the internal market. those who fought for the adoption of the un resolution and who are fighting for its implementation, so that the right to safe drinking water and sanitation is guaranteed to all, without exception, as a human right essential to the full enjoyment of life and all human rights. those who fight for public ownership and management of this precious commons. we are on this side, and this is the alternative resolution we are proposing. we shall see which side each of the other political groups in this parliament is on.

mr durão barroso, for the first time the question of growth and employment has been put on the council's agenda and for the first time a pact for growth and employment has been put forward. now, if we really look at what has been proposed, we can only conclude that the mountain has given birth to a mouse. if we compare both the content and the amount, we are talking about 120 billion euros. what we have found is that if we compare it with the aid that has been given to the banks and the recapitalisation of the banks, we are talking about a ridiculous package and so i would very much like you to be able to explain to the citizens why when it comes to banks the amounts are higher, the support is higher, the conditions are much lower and the counterparts, why don't you explain this to the citizens? why don't they explain that when we talk about aid, they're the ones who will pay again. it was important to clarify these questions because we are tired of austerity.
this european council was another step on the way to the establishment of a political and institutional framework which would force the eu institutions to exercise a tight control over each country, undermining national sovereignty and defying the most basic democratic principles and values, all in order to intensify exploitation, attack the rights and living conditions of workers and peoples and prolong the extortion of national resources. the so-called 'european semester' was concluded with the adoption of the 'country-specific recommendations which member states will integrate into their future national decisions on budgets, structural reforms and employment policies'. if we look at these 'recommendations' which the european commission has published and which they now want to implement, we will understand the meaning and the objectives of this 'european semester'. in portugal, the commission advocated a reduction in wages and the duration of unemployment benefits. in a country with one of the lowest wages in the eu, unemployment is at historic levels and long-term unemployment is increasing as a result of policies imposed by the eu and the imf. it was the interests of the economic and financial groups that were once again on the table, as is also shown by the decision on the possibility of direct support for banking.

in writing. − solvency ii directive 2009/138/ec establishes the regulation and supervision of insurance and reinsurance undertakings in the european union. these new rules are essential to ensure the soundness and safety of the insurance sector. the deadline for transposition of this directive is 30 october 2012. however, the commission has recently proposed an amendment to that directive with the aim of adapting it to the new architecture of insurance supervision, also proposing to extend the deadlines for transposition, repeal and application initially provided for. the proposal to extend this deadline to 30 june 2013 is essential as other rules will have to enter into force before this directive and there is no certainty that these deadlines can be met, as is the case with the omnibus ii directive. taking into account that supervisors and (re) insurance undertakings need some time to prepare for the application of the new legislation, it is also proposed to extend the start date of application of the solvency ii package to 1 january 2014. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the measures proposed.

in writing. − this report focuses on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament (ep) and of the council amending directive 2009/138/ec as regards the dates for transposition and application and the date of repeal of certain directives. the deadline for transposing the directive laying down new rules on the regulation and supervision of insurance and reinsurance undertakings in europe, in order to ensure the soundness and safety of this sector, allowing it greater stability and strengthening consumer confidence, expires on 31 october. in january 2011, the commission adopted an amendment to the abovementioned directive, namely the creation of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa) and the extension of the deadline for transposition, repeal and application, taking into account the need for prior approval of the omnibus ii directive. i voted in favour of postponing the transposition of directive 2009/138/ec to 30 june 2013 and the entry into force of the solvency ii package to 1 january 2014, avoiding a legal vacuum from 31 october next and ensuring the timely preparation of its operationality.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to propose a directive postponing the dates for transposition of directive 2009/138/ec (solvency ii) and the repeal of the existing insurance and reinsurance directives to 31 october 2012. this is because the commission adopted in january 2011 a proposal to amend directive 2009/138/ec in order to take account of the new architecture of insurance supervision and in particular the creation of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa), called omnibus ii. as the omnibus ii trilogue is still ongoing, the commission considers that the entry into force of directive 2009/138/ec without the major adaptations provided for in the omnibus ii directive could impose heavy burdens on member states. it also considers that these rules are important for a smooth transition to the new regime. in order to become operational, solvency ii requires the inclusion of delegated and implementing acts by the commission. the report therefore calls for the postponement of the transposition of directive 2009/138/ec (solvency ii) and the repeal of the directives to 1 january 2014. the content of this report is therefore eminently technical. in view of our critical position towards eiopa, we abstained.

in writing. − the present report concerns the proposal for a council decision amending council decision 2001/822/ec on the association of the overseas countries and territories with the ec, following the request made by the french republic under article 355 tfeu and in a letter dated 30 june 2010 asking the european council to decide in favour of changing the status of the island of saint barthélemy from 'outermost region' to 'overseas territory associated with the european union'. the rapporteur believes that this change in status 'meets the needs and specificities of the territory of são bartolomeu, without prejudicing the interests of the union', while maintaining the euro as currency and its inhabitants being considered 'european citizens'. saint barthélemy becomes the 26th country and associated territory of the eu. i voted in favour of this proposal as it meets the legitimate aspirations of the people of st bartholomew's, enabling them to strengthen partnerships with neighbouring states acp countries and the outermost regions of the caribbean and does not harm the interests of the eu.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the european council may, on the initiative of the member state concerned and acting unanimously, amend the status with regard to the eu of the french, danish and dutch overseas countries and territories. france has therefore asked the european council to change the status of the island of saint barthélemy from an outermost region to an overseas country and territory associated with the european union. consultation of the european parliament is a necessary step in this process. the rapporteur believes that the change in the statute responds to the needs and specificities of the territory of são bartolomeu. we respect the wishes and the legitimate and sovereign choices of the peoples of these territories. we must not forget the struggle that many of them are still waging against european colonialism, and we stand in solidarity with them. a struggle for the possibility of being able to freely and sovereignly decide their own destinies.

in writing. - i support this proposal, considering that macro-regional strategies can bring enormous benefits to the regions, which also involves several member states and their regions, as was the case with the danube and baltic sea strategies. i think that this type of strategy is certainly working, but on the other hand the european union must strengthen multi-level governance in all its institutional procedures, not only within the framework of the strategies but in the framework of all political action, in order to facilitate the creation of new macro-regional strategies, such as the possible atlantic strategy, which could bring enormous benefits to the regions. in the specific case of the mediterranean, as the rapporteur points out, the fact that several states and regions share the same basin, natural environment and historical linkage along the coast could bring great benefits not only in the synergies to be created between the member states of the european union, but also with neighbouring states.

in writing. - i was pleased to see that this owninitiative report in the committee on regional development was perfectly in line with the strategy for the european neighbourhood policy (enp) previously defined by this parliament, for which i was the rapporteur in the afet committee. highlighting the importance of the mediterranean basin as a decentralised and more comprehensive area of cooperation in enhancing transregional decision-making/sharing of good practice, it proposes the development of a macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean basin (similar to the strategy for the baltic for example) in a broader framework including the western mediterranean, the adriatic and the eastern mediterranean. it also considered that a comprehensive policy for the whole mediterranean basin could be implemented, complementing the priorities defined by regional and international organisations (e.g. the union for the mediterranean) and applying good practices that could contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the eu strategies. the focus on civil society participation, the principles/areas of action to be developed and deepened and the updating of the approach to migration in the face of the 'arab spring' also seem to me to be an excellent complement to the two enp reports for which i was rapporteur in the european parliament.
in writing. - the macro-regions, the baltic being the first, are the logical consequence of the growing interdependence of the countries and their similar or common characteristics, and are based on belonging to a particular geographical and cultural area which, although it crosses borders, is nevertheless delimited by them. the macro-regional approach allows common problems to be faced, shared problems to be tackled, cohesion to be promoted and solutions to be sought whose effects can benefit all actors and give the european union an overall vision that allows it to develop its action more appropriately. i believe that this option, if it is well managed and skillfully articulated with the states, respecting their sovereignty and promoting and respecting their specificities, can be successfully replicated in a number of areas. the mediterranean, in the face of the current turbulent times, must merit intelligent involvement by the union and the search for stabilising solutions involving both its shores.
in writing. − as with the macro-regional strategies for other geographical areas of europe, such as the danube basin and the baltic sea, macro-regional strategies for the mediterranean, more specifically for the adriatic and ionian seas, are now presented. the experience gained with the implementation of the baltic macro-region shows that it is a good initiative and a development booster for the peoples of these regions. the economic policy of the european union is based on regional cooperation. it is therefore clear - especially after the so-called 'arab spring' - that it is in the best interests of the union to maintain good relations with the peoples of the southern mediterranean and to promote trade and tourism development by exploiting existing resources, in particular maritime traffic and sustainable energy. it is also an excellent opportunity to promote interregional cohesion and strengthen relations between peoples. i voted in favour of the report by mr françois alfonsi on the eu's macro-regional strategies for the mediterranean and i hope that, with the support of the next multiannual financial framework, the eu will continue to cooperate in the process of democratization of the african countries of the mediterranean basin in order to achieve greater stability and economic growth in the region.
in writing. − we believe that it is essential to promote policies that promote effective economic and social cohesion in the european union, especially in a situation of deep structural crisis and of great social inequalities and regional asymmetries. the promotion of cohesion can and should involve cooperation between countries and regions with different affinities, which provides for interventions in the territory aimed at preserving the ecological balance and promoting fair, balanced and sustainable development. this view is partly reflected in the report and its approach to macro-regional strategies. however, the eu often subverts the concept of cohesion, for example by renationalising the costs of eu policies, by under-spending on cohesion or by imposing conditionality, by tying countries to strategies (such as eu 2020) whose aims and objectives are contrary to the desired cohesion. this report sets out a list of intentions which we value, but we cannot help but express our concern about these points. we also have serious reservations about certain points in the report which are close to the vision of the eu as a hegemonic power in the mediterranean region, denoting unconcealed imperial ambitions.
in writing. - i agree that the development of macro-regional strategies should be part of a global reflection aimed at identifying the problems on the ground, in order to avoid projects that are hesitant or arise from mere political and immediatist considerations. i agree with the idea that each macro-region needs a 'pre-setting phase', which organises a round table of the partners involved, which sets out the first strategic priorities and also lays the foundations for future governance, as the rapporteur has said, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this report looks at the evolution of the eu's macro-regional strategies, particularly in the mediterranean, and advocates a macro-regional approach that would allow the union to define a global project in this area, which is vital for the future of the union, in order to emerge from the current crisis and meet the expectations of its neighbours, particularly those in the southern mediterranean. this approach makes perfect sense to me, since the mediterranean area is a coherent whole, forming a single cultural and environmental basin, sharing several common characteristics and priorities: the same agricultural production, the abundance of renewable energy resources, in particular solar energy, the importance of tourism, the same risks in the face of natural disasters (fires, floods, earthquakes, scarcity of water resources) and the same risks in the face of human activities, in particular marine pollution. a dynamic development around the mediterranean can be, in addition to being a driving force for the whole european economy, a powerful encouragement for the development of new active neighbourhood policies, since the so-called 'arab spring' has highlighted the strategic potential of the geographical, political and economic links between the two shores of the mediterranean.

in writing. - i welcome and welcome this report, which highlights the extent of the negotiations between the european parliament and the council, which have brought about fundamental changes, particularly in services relating to the railway sector, particularly in the direction of its modernisation and interconnection. more important is the ultimate objective of this proposal, which is the opening up of the national passenger market and the separation of transport management infrastructures, which will undoubtedly not only bring us all closer together in europe, but also mean consolidating the principles of the free movement of persons in the european area.
in writing. − since january 2012, a european parliament delegation has been in informal negotiations with the council and the commission to prepare a second reading agreement on the single railway area. this recommendation supports the amendments adopted at first reading in plenary, in order to defend in the ongoing trilogues with the council the position of parliament which was adopted by a large majority. it advocates the need for independent regulatory bodies to achieve equal conditions of competition between large and small railway undertakings. the commission is proposing that in the long term a european regulatory body be set up to supervise cross-border transport. it rejected the council's proposals to reduce the duration of the multiannual contractual agreement to three years and proposed a duration of seven years. it advocates the need for transparent rules on access to connected rail services or service facilities to ensure that transport operators are able to provide their services. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. − the existence of independent regulatory bodies is crucial to achieving a level playing field between large and small railway companies. the decisions of national regulatory authorities shall be reliable and timely. in the long term, a european regulatory body should be established to oversee cross-border transport. in the meantime, national regulatory authorities should develop their networking activities. parliament adopted amendments to increase the transparency of financial flows, in particular in integrated companies providing transport and infrastructure management services. the text of the legislation currently in force has led to wide discrepancies in interpretation and, consequently, to several cases pending before the european court of auditors. the need to improve the text on this point in order to ensure greater clarity has thus become urgent. i agree with the above and with the other proposals of the european parliament mentioned in this document, and therefore i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'single european railway area', which reflects the good results of the negotiations with the council and the commitments made, particularly in the areas of access to rail transport services, such as the creation of an independent national network of regulatory bodies and the increase in the transparency of financial flows between the infrastructure manager and rail transport companies in integrated undertakings.
in writing. − the need to establish a single european railway area is part of the decline in rail transport, and aims to reverse this trend and promote this means of transport of people and goods which is faster, safer and less polluting than those using fossil fuels, in particular air transport. member states should closely monitor the implementation of this european railway area and promote the use of this means of transport internally, as well as enhance connectivity between railway lines in the various member states. a europe with a single railway area will tend to be more environmentally friendly and better supplied with goods and services. after many months of discussion, it has now been possible to reach an agreement with the council and i therefore congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on the work they have done on this dossier.
in writing. - deborah serracchiani presents a recommendation for second reading following the council's position at first reading, with a view to the adoption of a european parliament (ep) and council directive establishing a single european railway area (recast). the construction of a single market at the level of the european union (eu) implies a vast set of standardisation standards, which often require the removal of technical barriers, as is the case with railway infrastructure. in fact, it is discouraging and a reason for not using this type of transport that, when travelling between member states, we have to change trains when we reach a certain border. it is therefore urgent to standardize the gauges of the european rail networks. i welcome the fact that after long and difficult negotiations it has been possible to reach an agreement on the creation of a single european railway area. the liberalisation of rail services will be an asset for european citizens and businesses. i welcome the adoption of this report because it is a proposal which will make the single market work and bring enormous benefits to citizens and businesses. it can also be an excellent alternative to road traffic with enormous energy and environmental benefits.
in writing. − this directive is another piece of the ongoing attack on the public rail service. the direction is clear: privatize what is profitable and leave to the state the areas where large amounts of funding are needed such as the construction and maintenance of infrastructure. the proposed fragmentation is tailored to the multinationals in the sector, which are taking over rail transport and colonizing the markets for associated services in several countries. those who have adopted this directive today will be responsible tomorrow for the workers who will lose their jobs, for those who will see their working conditions degraded, their wages reduced and their hours increased. they will also be accountable to the populations, who will be deprived of services considered less profitable, who will pay more for a service of poorer quality. they will also have to respond, finally, to the disturbing threats to railway safety, which is the imposition of the subordination of safety standards set by the national authorities to the rules of competition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the serracchiani report on the recasting of the union's rail transport legislation because it consolidates two fundamental objectives: (i) to make progress in creating a cross-border european rail market, without which there is no real internal market; (ii) to strengthen the conditions for rail transport's efficiency and enable it to compete with road and air transport (which, moreover, do not internalise their environmental over-cost). i also believe that a single european railway market cannot be effectively regulated in a fragmented way through national regulators, requiring the creation of a pan-european regulator. the proposed solution of a council of national regulators chaired by the european commission should therefore be seen as an intermediate solution towards a future union railway regulator, without prejudice to the continued existence of national regulators as decentralised entities at national level.
