in writing. − this proposal for a directive establishing a single european railway area merges three existing directives and contains provisions on adequate financing for railway infrastructure, conditions of competition in the railway market and the organisational reforms necessary to ensure adequate market surveillance. in very general terms, this recast was designed to ensure the improvement of the investment framework in the railway sector and to ensure better rail transport services for passengers and freight users, increasing competition in the railway market and strengthening the authority and powers of national regulators. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the creation of a single railway area depends on coherent, transparent and simplified legislation, which fosters a competitive business environment. after the trilogue negotiations, the council proposal significantly lowered the ambition of the proposal submitted by the commission and parliament. the rapporteur's recommendation therefore seeks to reinforce the objectives already discussed and approved by parliament in order to reach an agreement at second reading. the rapporteur wants to strengthen access to rail services, infrastructure financing, infrastructure charges, the strengthening of the powers of the regulatory body, the full independence of the management of the network and financial transparency. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road. i support this recommendation because i consider it vital to simplify the existing legislation in order to achieve the objectives set out in the transport white paper - horizon 2050.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that it is an extraordinary advance not only in technology but also in improving road safety and working conditions on the one hand, and safeguarding the privacy of citizens on the other. if well implemented, this new technology could bring significant results in improving road safety in europe, provided that individual privacy is protected, with the ultimate aim of monitoring and preventing disasters and negative consequences for road transport users.
in writing. - since 1969, the european union has introduced social provisions in the field of road transport in order to improve road safety and the working conditions of drivers and to ensure fair competition between transport undertakings. the aim of this revision of the tachograph regulation is to make fraud more difficult, to improve the application of social legislation and to reduce administrative burdens by making full use of new technologies and introducing some new regulatory provisions. this report, which i supported, proposes two important measures: to encourage the development of an application through the harmonised tachograph interface, which provides interpretation and guidance to drivers, and to introduce the approval of the software used by control officers to interpret the data recorded on the tachograph. none of the present objectives of the proposal will be achieved if member states do not commit themselves to improving the level of implementation of this regulation.
in writing. − since 1969, the european union (eu) has introduced social provisions in the field of road transport with the aim of improving road safety and the working conditions of drivers, as well as ensuring fair competition between transport companies. the eu has developed a comprehensive policy on supervision and enforcement based on two pillars: - directive 2006/22/ec on minimum requirements for roadside checks and on-the-spot checks to be carried out by member states. - council regulation (eec) no 3821/85, hereinafter referred to as the 'tacograph regulation'. the commission has identified two main problems today that require an eu-wide response: - problem 1: violations of social rules still very frequent: on average 9% of the vehicles inspected do not comply with social rules; - problem 2: the use of the tachograph system is not sufficiently optimized: the way in which the tachograph, especially the digital tachograph and its additional functionalities, facilitate the driver's work and promote transport efficiency can be improved. i voted in favour of the amendments to the regulation because i believe they will help to solve the problems identified.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the introduction of a recording equipment in road transport, as i believe that the new regulation will improve the functions of the digital tachograph by applying stricter rules on driving and resting time, thus contributing positively to the protection of drivers and road safety.
in writing. − road transport safety is a particular concern of the eu, which is why it has developed legislation to harmonise maximum daily and weekly driving times and minimum daily and weekly rest periods for drivers. these rules are intended to ensure road safety and protect workers by ensuring fair competition between companies in the sector. to this end, the tachograph regulation (control device for data on driving, working and resting times recorded for each operator and driver) was adopted in 1985. it is this regulation that the commission now intends to review and update in order to make fraud more difficult, improve enforcement of the legislation and reduce the administrative burden by using the new technologies at its disposal.
in writing. - the transport of goods by road without well-defined rules and without strict control of the drivers' rest periods increases the risk of accidents with sometimes very serious consequences, both in terms of personal injury and material and environmental damage. the report by silvia-adriana ţicău is on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (eec) no 3821/85 which made the existence of a control apparatus in the field of road transport compulsory, and regulation (ec) no 561/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. the new proposal for a regulation, which follows the evolution of new technologies, provides for the introduction of a control device (digital tachograph) in all new heavy-duty vehicles from 2015 and its generalization to heavy-duty vehicles from 2020. the new apparatus, equipped with gsm transmission, will allow much faster and more efficient control and can be extended to other functions beyond speed and rest time control, contributing to a reduction in bureaucracy and greater economy since data transmission can be done at zero cost.
in writing. the rapporteur proposed two important measures: to encourage the development of an application, through the harmonised tachograph interface, which provides interpretation and guidance to drivers and to introduce the type approval of the software used by control officers to interpret the data recorded by the tachograph. in agreeing with these measures which will benefit drivers and transport efficiency, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european union has been introducing social provisions in the field of road transport since 1969 with the aim of improving road safety and the working conditions of drivers, and of ensuring fair competition between transport companies. as part of the european policy on the supervision and enforcement of social legislation in the field of road transport, this proposal aims to strengthen the existing legal framework and to extend the functionalities of the digital tachograph substantially by introducing new technological developments, thus giving rise to a new type of digital tachograph (the so-called 'smart tachograph'). member states should also commit to improving the level of implementation of this regulation by promoting greater harmonisation in the training that control officers receive across europe and by certifying the acquisition of appropriate technical competence through an examination, as well as by providing control officers with the appropriate equipment and approved software to take full advantage of the new possibilities that the smart tachograph will provide for improved control.
in writing. - regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on tachographs aims to improve road safety and therefore lays down a set of technical standards and standards for the use, typeapproval, installation and inspection of tachographs, which are binding on manufacturers and authorities, but also on transport undertakings and their drivers. the rules concern the driving, working and rest times recorded for vehicles of 2,8 tonnes gross vehicle weight for freight transport and for drivers of passenger vehicles with a capacity of 9 or more. this revision of the 1985 regulation is intended to strengthen controls on fraud, improve the application of social legislation and reduce the administrative costs of technological progress. the focus will be on enhancing the functionalities of the digital tachograph, the so-called 'smart tachograph', which will allow remote communication for control, automatic recording of precise location data and complementarity of the tachograph with intelligent transport applications. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take a more active role in the fight against fraud.
in writing. - i support this proposal, considering that in a globalised economy intellectual property has become a very important factor in european competitiveness. protecting knowledge is protecting europe's investment in research, innovation and jobs. at the same time, infringements of intellectual property rights and the resulting global trade in counterfeit goods is a growing concern, both in terms of the economic consequences for europe's industry and the risks to the health and safety of its consumers. considering that customs rules and practices play a crucial role in effective action, the commission's proposal to revise the current regulation (ec) no 1383/2003 on border controls with the aim of increasing the control of imps and streamlining customs procedures is timely and desirable.
in writing. − intellectual property rights (ipr) are central to innovation, a key priority of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. given the increase in ipr infringements and in the international trade in counterfeit goods, economic growth and jobs depend to a large extent on effective enforcement of ipr legislation. customs authorities are in a relatively good position to effectively control the application of ipr legislation at the eu's external borders before goods enter the internal market. once goods are dispersed across the different member states, it becomes much more difficult and costly to trace them and to initiate proceedings. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the commission's proposal to revise regulation (ec) no 1383/2003 in order to strengthen the control of the application of ipr legislation by customs authorities and because i agree with the recommendations put forward by the rapporteur.
in writing. - artistic, scientific, industrial and cultural creation deserves protection and that is why there are internationally recognised intellectual property rights (ipr). these ensure the integrity of the creation/invention and must protect it against counterfeiting and piracy. however, modern technologies - notably the internet - have made piracy and counterfeiting easier and more accessible. therefore, adequate and effective ipr protection is increasingly essential for the protection of industries (in particular creative industries) and is an essential part of the eu2020 strategy on innovation and entrepreneurship. piracy and counterfeiting represent an estimated annual cost to european businesses of eur 250 billion and as such it is of paramount importance to establish and activate the most effective mechanisms to combat piracy and counterfeiting.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis has reinforced the need to focus strongly on economic growth and job creation. all employment opportunities, concentrated mainly in small and mediumsized enterprises, must be exploited. in this context, the fight against the shadow economy, especially tax evasion and counterfeiting, plays a crucial role. the trade in counterfeit products on european markets represents losses of around eur 250 billion annually and has a negative impact on labour markets of 185,000 jobs. in addition, consumer protection and the quality of the products traded are at stake, as is the protection of intellectual property rights. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities because it will strengthen existing legislation, increase legal clarity, better protect the economy and the rights of european consumers (health and well-being are at stake: health, food, technological, industrial products, etc.) and meet the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy: smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. - this report is based on a proposal for a regulation which intends to give customs authorities an increased role in the 'war' against counterfeiting, pirated goods, infringement of trademark/copyright, etc. we are not opposed to greater supervision and control of this type of goods, and it does not seem inconsistent that once this decision has been taken, it should be made compulsory for the customs authorities to play a more active role in this matter. however, the report does go some way in some areas that we cannot follow up. the rapporteur goes further than the commission has proposed. the commission is therefore proposing that this regulation should cover all infringements of intellectual property rights, generic medicines and non-commercial imports. it also proposes a definition of 'small shipment', which we have many doubts about, which can be taken as universally valid.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the creutzmann report on the customs protection of intellectual property rights (ipr) because i share the view that the protection of ipr in external trade relations is essential for the european economy, whose competitiveness is based on innovation and the differentiation that trade marks, patents, copyright and geographical indications guarantee. the union customs authorities have the primary responsibility for preventing the entry of pirated or counterfeit goods into the internal market. i also agree that customs controls on goods in transit should not be excluded, at least in cases where there may be reasonable grounds for suspecting that they are destined for the internal market. i also believe that it is pointless to deprive the european union of the right to seize goods infringing iprs protected in the union (european trade marks, etc.) simply because they are intended for another market, since the damage caused to european companies holding such rights is no less serious. the case of generic medicines in transit to developing countries under the relevant wto trips waiver clause is not at issue precisely because there is no infringement of iprs by european pharmaceutical companies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider intellectual property rights (ipr) to be fundamental to innovation and a key priority of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. as i have said, it is important to combat piracy and counterfeiting, which are already costing european companies an estimated eur 250 billion a year.
in writing. − given the increase in infringements of intellectual property rights and in the international trade in counterfeit goods, economic growth and jobs depend to a large extent on effective enforcement of intellectual property rights legislation. in order to reverse this situation, this report provides for the revision of regulation (ec) no 1383/2003 in order to strengthen the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities and to increase legal clarity by adapting the provisions of the regulation to new developments. the main aim is to strengthen the role of customs authorities in both monitoring and enforcing intellectual property rights legislation at the eu's external borders, i.e. before goods enter the internal market, as it becomes much more difficult and costly to trace and prosecute goods once they have been dispersed across the member states. as i consider intellectual property rights to be fundamental to innovation and a key priority of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, i voted in favour.
in writing. − intellectual property rights are fundamental to innovation, a key priority of the europe 2020 strategy. given the increase in violations of these rights and in the international trade in counterfeit goods, economic growth and jobs depend to a large extent on effective enforcement of counterfeit legislation. procedures should therefore be established to enable customs authorities to prevent the movement of goods suspected of infringing intellectual property rights. for the reasons i have mentioned, i voted in favour of the document in the european parliament.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that a holistic approach to the protection of water resources is needed. the protection of water resources, in particular drinking water, should be considered in a global perspective, taking into account all the ecosystem services supported by water. controlling pollution at source is of key importance to prevent the entry of hazardous substances into the environment and to reduce the pressure placed on wastewater treatment. climate change adaptation and mitigation policies should systematically take into account the impact on water resources and the eu should take a comprehensive approach to the problem of water scarcity and droughts. significant gains in water resource efficiency are possible and desirable. resource efficiency is a flagship initiative of europe 2020 and water efficiency plays a central role in the strategy. moreover, the quantity and quality of water are inextricably linked.
in writing. - water is unquestionably the most important of all public goods. with the adoption of the water framework directive (wfd) in 2000, the european union has a solid framework for sustainable and efficient management of water resources. however, the pace of implementation of the eqf in european countries and regions has been slow. in order to respond to current and future water challenges, the commission will present a plan to preserve europe's water resources in november 2012. this report, which is the european parliament's contribution to the european commission's plan, advocates that the regional and local dimension should be strengthened, communities and local stakeholders should be involved and actively involved in all stages of the policy-making and implementation process. it also advocates a holistic approach to the protection of water resources, particularly drinking water, and that water should be integrated into all areas of intervention at european, national and regional level. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − water is a common good of mankind and access to water should be a fundamental and universal right. sustainable water use is an environmental and health necessity and plays a central role in the climate regulation cycle. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that special attention should be paid to the specific activities and objectives of the horizon 2020 framework programme on better sustainable management of water resources and aquatic environments in the eu and its neighbouring countries.
in writing. - water issues are a legitimate concern for european decision-makers. the idea that we have water in quality and quantity should not distract us from the fact that desertification is affecting more and more regions of europe. taking water resources for granted and not protecting or trying to conserve them are the first steps to losing them. if there is one issue that touches upon the most basic of our survival and that crosses multiple areas of our existence, it is that of water. it is therefore up to the union to tackle it in a comprehensive, intelligent and effective way. i hope that the european conscience will really wake up to the need to safeguard the supply and rational use of water by the people and that the legislation that will be adopted will reinforce the need to preserve it, thus ensuring the survival of future generations and of european ecosystems.
in writing. - never has the maxim "water is life" made so much sense as it does today. in fact, water can be both a war breeder and a peacemaker. so some claim that the next world war will be fought over the possession and control of water resources. as it is an essential resource for mankind (human consumption, agricultural and industrial activity), it must be treated with all the precautions it deserves. aware of this, the european union (eu) adopted the water directive in 2000, which established a reasonable framework for water protection and use. after 12 years, there are areas where improvements are needed, both in quality control and in management at regional and sometimes macro-regional level. another aspect that requires urgent attention from the managing authorities is the optimisation of supply systems, since it is estimated that around 70% of these losses are incurred. i voted in favour of this report which improves the quality and preserves our water resources and i urge the commission to include in the cohesion fund for the next mff appropriations to optimise water treatment and supply systems.
in writing. - this report makes some very serious proposals, such as the inclusion of water in the internal market - a clear change of position from previous ep resolutions, which considered that the management of water resources should not be subject to the rules of the internal market, a position which has also been advocated by numerous organisations and trade unions, including the european federation of public services unions. the ep now calls for the rules of the internal market to be adapted to the specific characteristics of the water sector, a move which is another step towards privatising the water sector and water services. we regret the rejection of our alternative motion for a resolution - a motion which focuses on defending the right to water and the public management, possession and ownership of this precious com mon good and the services associated with it. the report opens the door to the interests of transnational water companies and to the privatisation and commercialisation of this unique and irreplaceable resource. these are the interests which the right wing and the social democrats represent in this parliament defend. we obviously voted against it.
in writing. - this report considers water to be an inalienable public good essential to life and that it is a common good of humanity and that access to water should be a fundamental and universal right. it also proposes measures to ensure that everyone can enjoy this vital public good more effectively and efficiently. this is an important position from the european parliament at a time when attempts are being made to turn water into a commercial asset. for these reasons i voted in favour, considering that water is a human right and a public good. i am, however, opposed to an internal market in water technology. i advocate for public investment and knowledge in water and for the effective transfer and sharing of that knowledge by the people of the world. it's a matter of avoiding water control by the few and making it a resource of all for all. i also believe that this is a resource that should be at the service of the community and the planet.
in writing. − considering that decisive action at eu level is needed to address the current and future water challenges facing our continent, i voted in favour of this report. i agree with the rapporteur's request to the commission to incorporate the strategic recommendations contained in this report into the formulation of the 'plan to preserve europe's water resources' as an important contribution to a more effective and better integrated water policy and to the promotion of a level playing field for its implementation at international level.
in writing. − sustainable management of water resources is vital to ensure that all ecosystems receive sufficient quantities of good quality water for their proper functioning and to be able to provide essential services in terms of food safety and quality, health and the economy. the 2000 water framework directive sets the objective of achieving 'good ecological, chemical and quantitative status' of european water bodies by 2015. however, the pace of implementation of the directive in the countries and regions of europe has been slow and uneven. while the main concern should be the implementation of current legislation in the water sector, there are specific gaps that need to be filled, either by adapting existing legislation to water priorities or by developing new legislation to address the impact of specific activities or sectors, and the importance of cooperation between different economic operators and other stakeholders for the sustainable management of water resources should be taken into account at this level. i voted in favour of this because i believe that we must move towards a more effective and integrated water policy.
in writing. − water is a public good that needs to be protected and its proper use ensured. more than 800 million people still lack access to safe drinking water, and the un targets for basic sanitation remain far from being met. for these reasons, this report analyses and identifies the challenges and obstacles to the correct implementation of the 2000 water directive in the member states, in particular the objective of 'good ecological, chemical and quantitative status' of european water bodies by 2015. i support this report which sets out a number of ideas to be included in the 'plan to preserve europe's water resources', to be published later this year. i would like to highlight a few key ideas: the importance of effective participation of the regions in policy-making, there is no single policy; water should be a cross-cutting issue in all eu policies, with a holistic approach to all water resources; there must be an eu policy on water reuse and recycling; enhanced research and innovation, particularly in regions with water scarcity; and international cooperation for sustainable water development.
in writing. - i support this proposal, considering that the greatest advantage of the ecall system will be the reduction in the number of deaths and the severity of injuries caused by road accidents, due to the faster arrival of emergency services at the scene of the accident. this faster arrival of rescue teams, police and trailers will allow for faster clearance of the accident site, thus allowing ecall to reduce congestion time and contribute to the efficiency of road transport in europe and to a reduction of external costs. the authorities consider that the advantages of ecall are mainly evident in the reduction of the medical consequences of an accident, the risk of other accidents at the same location and the impact of an accident on the flow of traffic. it should however be recalled that for the automotive industry, the mandatory introduction of an eu-wide public ecall system in all newly type-approved vehicles will open up new opportunities for the deployment of additional value-added services using the ecall telematics platform.
in writing. − from 2015, all cars sold in the european union will have to have an emergency call system in case of a serious accident. the system will automatically transmit the data on the location of the vehicle and the time of the accident to the nearest emergency service. the adoption of this report will help to reduce the number of deaths and the severity of injuries caused by road accidents by allowing emergency services to arrive at the scene of an accident more quickly. the faster arrival of emergency aid will also reduce the medical consequences of accidents, reduce the risk of further accidents at the same site and reduce traffic congestion. it is emphasised that any applications introduced in the vehicle and based on the ecall platform should fully comply with the relevant data protection and privacy regulations. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − the ecall service is a service that automatically makes an emergency call when a serious road accident occurs. for this to happen, the vehicle must be equipped with ecall. ecall does not prevent accidents but it improves the efficiency of emergency services. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the installation of the ecall service should be mandatory and should not be based on or dependent on the existence of a positive commercial justification for an autonomous ecall service, since the advantages it brings to society as a whole must also be considered.
in writing. − the launch of the ecall service, based on the 112 emergency number, should ensure automatic notification of emergency services in the event of an accident, thus making a decisive contribution to reducing the number of fatalities on european roads and the severity of the consequences of injuries through faster, qualified and properly equipped assistance. this pan-european vehicle emergency call service should be operational in all member states and european states joining this initiative and should be available in any vehicle, regardless of the brand, country and actual location of the vehicle. initially, it was planned that this service would become fully operational in 2009. unfortunately, progress has been too slow and the roll-out of the pan-european ecall service is still lagging behind. it is therefore urgent to ensure that this system, considered to be one of the most efficient and cost-effective for road safety, can be implemented in a timely and harmonised manner throughout europe, as 80% of the citizens surveyed would like. i support this initiative which allows for the establishment of a regulatory framework for the deployment of this service, which will make it possible to speed up the process by making the installation of ecall devices compulsory in all new vehicles type-approved in europe.

in writing. - in portugal we have the proverb 'a minute in life is worth more than life in a minute' which, i suppose, should be echoed in similar sayings in other countries. however, this advice to be calm and cautious is often countered by the need to act quickly, especially in emergency situations. there, a minute can make the difference between life and death. the ecall service aims to meet this need in the case of road accidents. in an age when mobile phones are a pervasive technology, it is hard to understand why alert and rescue solutions are not being studied and applied that are aware of their existence and that take advantage of their full potential. the automatic nature of their activation raises some doubts as regards the privacy of vehicle occupants and the traceability of journeys. these doubts do not call into question my overall favourable assessment of the initiative or my desire that its implementation can actually help to save lives. unfortunately, my country has a high rate of road accidents. i hope that ecall will lessen this scourge.
in writing. − active and passive safety for motorists has improved significantly over the last few decades: seat belts, airbags, energy absorption zones, sensors, lighting, etc. everything that can be done for the preservation of human life must be done. the report under review, by dieter-lebrecht koch and olga sehnalová, focuses on the introductory regulation of the ecall service. the aim of this measure is to save lives and it consists in making it compulsory to introduce in motor vehicles an alert system which, in the event of an accident, and as is already the case in some high-end vehicles, automatically calls the emergency services and provides the coordinates of the location of the vehicle involved. how many people could not be alive if they had been treated at the time of the accident? how many were imprisoned, often in inhospitable and/ or hidden places, bleeding to death without being able to call for help? i voted in favour of this report because i believe that ecall will be an added value that will save many lives and many resources from 2015 onwards and as such it should be considered a public service accessible to all.
in writing. − it is essential that medical assistance in the event of road accidents reaches the accident site as soon as possible, and that it responds adequately and effectively to the variety of situations that may require its presence. the proposed service, known as ecall, is a system to be installed on all vehicles which, in the event of an accident, automatically calls the nearest emergency centre with information on the time, exact location and direction of the vehicle. during this call, the emergency service operator will be able to speak and hear what is happening inside the vehicle. this technology allows access to a set of geographical, location and trajectory data collected and monitored in real time by satellite. without forgetting other details concerning possible limitations of the system, this last aspect of access to data places us before obvious requirements concerning a high level of protection of personal data and the guarantee that individual freedoms are guaranteed in all their dimensions. unfortunately, the report does not adequately address these requirements.

in writing. − the ecall system aims to improve assistance in the event of an accident by automatically calling the emergency services with information on the accident location, time, precise location, description and direction. ecall can thus reduce the number of fatalities and the severity of injuries. this service, already introduced by the ec but on a voluntary basis, is now imposed as compulsory for all vehicles from 2015. the member states are therefore asked to define the infrastructure that will receive emergency calls and to incorporate this system into their networks, so that calls are a public service and free of charge, like 112. furthermore, it must be interoperable with existing private systems and the sharing of data must be strictly necessary for the specific purpose. i support this report because i consider it to be a valuable addition to the european citizen and at the same time to open up new opportunities for the automotive industry, since it can be used for new applications and services.

the rapporteur. - the report on my responsibility, which is being discussed here today in this context, concerning the controls by the member states of operations forming part of eagf financing, reflects comagri's understanding of the alignment of this dossier with the provisions on delegated and implementing acts introduced by the treaty of lisbon. for implementing acts, the procedures have been introduced in accordance with regulation (eu) no 182/2011 laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by the commission of the exercise of implementing powers. the delegated acts were adopted in accordance with the progress of the informal negotiations between the three institutions. it is therefore essential that parliament confirms this position by the vote that will take place tomorrow, a vote which i hope will be as wide as possible, and which is intended to reaffirm parliament's position on its role as co-legislator. i would therefore like to call on the commission and the council to give a strict interpretation of the lisbon treaty so that we can make progress in our work, particularly in the context of the reform of the cap. time is of the essence. the treaty of lisbon transforms the old comitology procedure to introduce, in my view, a clear distinction between administrative acts, i.e. implementing acts, and on the other hand to give the european parliament a strengthened right of veto over these acts on an equal footing with the council, i.e. the right to revoke the delegation of an act to the european commission. there remains an institutionalised procedure whereby the commission continues to be assisted by the specialised committees for implementing acts and consultation of member states' experts for the preparation of delegated acts is unavoidable. it is certainly necessary to strike a balance between what can be categorised in a basic act as a delegated act or an implementing act whenever the boundaries between the different provisions leave room for interpretation and it is in the spirit of this balance that i reiterate my call for a strict interpretation of the wording of the treaty in which parliament is invested with new powers. i am not asking the european parliament to replace the executive of the union, the european commission, let alone the governments of the member states. i only ask for the european parliament to have a power of control over the new comitology which, without promising the effectiveness of decision-making, is commensurate with its new role as co-legislator.

in writing. - with the lisbon treaty, regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 on the single common market organisation (single cmo) needs to be adapted to the distinction between delegated and implementing powers established by articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). article 290 allows the legislator to delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of a legislative act. article 291 tfeu allows member states to adopt all measures of national law necessary to implement legally binding union acts. the aim of the proposal we are now voting on is to adapt the single cmo regulation, including some amendments to make it more understandable and effective.
in writing. - all alignment exercises are essentially technical exercises but they contain a certain political sensitivity and always raise some controversy. i am therefore pleased that this issue has been discussed in the european parliament (ep) before the debate on the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap). the lisbon treaty changed the old comitology system (strengthening the powers of the ep which now has a veto on delegated acts) by replacing it with a two-tier structure of delegated acts and implementing acts, thus necessitating a new alignment of the current legislative body. the report, which was drawn up by mr de castro, analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products (single cmo regulation). i voted in favour of this report which calls for the strengthening of the powers of the ep conferred by the lisbon treaty and calls on the council to share more responsibilities, which will be to the benefit of all citizens.
in writing. − insertion of the alignment by the treaty of lisbon, which consists of the adoption of delegated and implementing acts empowering the commission to exercise implementing and enforcement powers and without consulting parliament, the report inserts this update in the regulation establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and specific provisions for certain agricultural products. the legislature is thus empowered to define the objectives of market intervention measures, production limitation systems and aid schemes, as well as the establishment of a system of import and export licences, the basic elements of the marketing and production rules and the principle of the application of penalties, reductions and exclusions. the report focuses on technical adaptation, but there are important positive aspects raised by the rapporteur: the facilitation of cross compliance checks, reducing the administrative burden on member states; the rejection of discrimination against producers in the fruit and vegetables sector; and the eligibility of vat for the eafrd.

in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) establishes the distinction between delegated and implementing powers. article 290 allows the legislator to delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of a legislative act. article 291 tfeu allows member states to adopt all measures of national law necessary to implement legally binding union acts. in the proposal which we are now adopting, the commission has made a strict distinction between provisions of a more general nature, laying down additional elements (article 290) and elements of a technical nature which are closely linked to the power of decision which the member states enjoy in implementing measures (article 291). therefore, no amendments are proposed to the proposal for regulation (ec) no 834/2007 on organic production and labelling of organic products as regards the classification of delegated and implementing acts.

in writing. − the conclusion of this agreement is a step forward long awaited by the economic groups of the major eu powers. the process of russia's accession to the wto entails a process of liberalisation and privatisation in several areas, notably in the services sector, opening its market to foreign investment. the services market in russia began to develop only in the 1990s, after the end of the soviet union and after the victory of the counterrevolution which dismantled an important public service sector. with this agreement, russia renounces part of its sovereignty and undertakes to ban virtually all national preferential treatment in order to allow eu economic groups access to its services market. the beneficiaries of this agreement signed by the eu are the same as always: the major economic groups of the major powers who see this as creating additional business opportunities in an area where they can have a competitive advantage. the usual winners and losers of this agreement are the same: workers in this sector threatened with redundancy, smes threatened by competition from the large monopolies in the sector and working-class consumers who see prices rise and quality fall. so we can only vote against.

in writing. - this agreement is another example of the contradictory process of russia's accession to the wto. russia has committed itself to ensuring that by 2018 trade in eu automotive parts and components into russia does not jeopardise the industry in certain regions of the country. the commission has therefore decided to maintain the existing regime for the automotive sector by continuing to restrict access to the russian market for manufacturers of motor vehicles and components beyond the requirements of the russian domestic market. the eu, for its part, is pressing for russia's accession to the wto and is demanding compensation mechanisms to ensure that the profits of its exporting economic groups are not jeopardised. in the immediate future, it is positive that russia tries to anchor and defend this industry in regions where it has traditionally anchored, maintaining production and employment at least until 2018. at the end of this period, their domestic production will be exposed to external competition, particularly from eu production, whose installed capacity may be at an advantage, leaving many jobs and production at risk of disappearing in many regions.

in writing. - the accession of the russian federation to the world trade organisation has a very positive effect, as it establishes a regulated multilateral trading system. however, its foreign investment regime in the automotive sector, initiated in 2005 (trim 1) and extended in 2006 to automotive components, became more restrictive in 2010 (trim 2) to the extent that, at the time of the accession of the russian federation to the wto, it could be declared to be contrary to the agreement on trade-related investment measures. thus, the need arose for the eu to conclude bilateral agreements with russia for the legal guarantee of additional and complementary bilateral trade concessions. in this context, the eu negotiated this bilateral agreement to have a mechanism for compensation of manufacturers of automotive components, to be applied in case of realisation of the risk of falling exports of these products to russia resulting from the implementation of the russian automotive investment programme until 2018. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − for several years russia has been trying to attract foreign manufacturers of motor vehicles and related components to its territory in order to compensate for the decline of the domestic automotive industry and to provide employment for the workforce in this sector. with the accession of the russian federation to the wto, it would be possible to declare this investment contrary to the agreement on trade-related investment measures of this organisation, which prohibits investment measures in the production of goods that cause trade distorting or restrictive effects. however, under the conditions of russia's accession to the wto, this automotive investment programme will be exempted from the obligation to ensure that all laws, regulations and measures relating to trade and investment applied in the russian federation are consistent with the provisions of the wto. in this context, the eu negotiated a bilateral agreement to have a mechanism for compensating manufacturers of automotive components to be applied in case of a realisation of the risk of falling exports of these products to russia resulting from the implementation of the russian automotive investment programme until 2018. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the agreement in the european parliament.

in writing. − due to the internal process of struggle and the necessary combination of interests between the different sectors of capital in russia, russia is seeking to postpone the future impacts of the mandatory liberalisation of important sectors of its economy, taking into account the process of its accession to the wto. this agreement allows russia, in a not entirely clear manner, to retain sovereignty over the definition of export duties currently applied to exports of raw materials. the report states that this agreement is not enough and that more needs to be done. you can see the ambition. russia accounts for more than 10% of the world production of these raw materials or more than 10% of world exports. the eu has important current or potential import interests. a binding agreement or the guarantee of a more rapid liberalisation process could be more advantageous for large eu capital which would thus see reduced import costs for products which are in many cases crucial for industry in many eu countries. we support the inalienable right of russia or any other country to exercise sovereignty over its resources, including natural resources, and to impose export duties as it sees fit in its own interests, irrespective of the provisions of the wto.
in writing. - as this is a measure which is considered to bring added value to the eu economy, i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the russian federation on the introduction or increase of export duties on raw materials.
in writing. − this bilateral agreement with the russian federation was negotiated in the context of its accession to the world trade organisation. in this context, the russian federation undertook to gradually reduce or eliminate the export duties currently applied. according to the bilateral agreement, the russian government undertakes to make every effort not to introduce or increase export duties on raw materials listed in the annex to the agreement, as these are raw materials in respect of which the eu has significant current or potential import interests and in which there are risks of global supply stress. in this way, if russia intends to apply export duties on these products, it will consult the european commission at least two months in advance in order to reach a solution that takes into account the interests of both parties. the eu is therefore expected to make a firm commitment to the reforms required immediately by wto accession, as well as to reciprocate and engage in negotiations for a new mutually beneficial agreement, particularly in the fields of energy, trade and investment.
in writing. − this bilateral agreement with the russian federation was negotiated in the context of its accession to the world trade organisation, in which the russian federation has undertaken to gradually reduce or eliminate the export duties currently applied. this undertaking on export duty rates was included in the russian goods leniency and commitment schedule. there are numerous products which are not included in the said schedule and this agreement presents a rather long list, covering very important raw materials which are not listed in the said list but for which russia holds more than 10% of the world production or more than 10% of the world exports. these are raw materials in which the eu has important import interests and in which there are risks of global supply stress. they include agricultural products and seeds, numerous chemical, ferrous and energy products, minerals, cotton derivatives and animal products, among others. these are raw materials for which the russian government undertakes to make every effort not to introduce or increase export duties. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the agreement.
in writing. - i vote against this draft agreement, mainly for reasons associated with the definition of 'commercial scale', the use of criminal sanctions as the treaty suggests, excessive policing of the internet, the potential disregard for privacy and indeed individual freedoms, among other matters. i understand that other measures will have to be taken to protect intellectual property.
in writing. the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) is a new international agreement designed to establish a general international framework to combat counterfeiting and piracy. the problems acta seeks to tackle are real and growing, and in the case of intellectual property rights in europe, they have cost european businesses €250 billion a year and destroyed 185 billion jobs in europe. however, the acta text has unintended consequences, is not sufficiently precise as regards individual criminalisation, the definition of 'for commercial purposes', the role of internet service providers and the possible disruption of the flow of medicines. moreover, acta, in its aim of combating piracy and counterfeiting, should and must include in its negotiations countries such as india, china and brazil, where the greatest violations of intellectual property occur. the benefits of acta are thus clearly outweighed by the potential threats to individual freedoms. in view of the above, and because the european parliament cannot ensure adequate protection of the rights of european citizens, i am voting in favour of this report which recommends that acta should not be approved.
in writing. - i agree with the need for a new international agreement to combat counterfeiting and piracy. in europe alone, the cost of infringement of intellectual property rights is estimated at eur 250 billion and the loss of 185 billion jobs every year. acta, by pretending to be all-inclusive, confuses commodities and goods with the free exchange of data on the internet. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat piracy and counterfeiting, and it is therefore important that the commission should be able to take action to combat piracy and counterfeiting. the benefits of acta are thus clearly outweighed by the potential threats to individual freedoms. for these reasons, and in the belief that this is the best way of defending the rights of european citizens, i am voting in favour of the martin report which recommends that acta should not be approved.
in writing. - acta sought to solve real problems, which have worsened in recent years, with the global trade in pirated and counterfeit goods estimated at over eur 250 billion. however, acta raised some doubts as to its scope, in particular with regard to infringements in the digital environment and the role of internet service providers in identifying such infringements. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. i voted against this agreement (and therefore in favour of the report), but i think it is absolutely necessary to start a broad discussion now with a view to a new agreement involving so-called 'civil society' which should use this text of acta as a basis, obviously revising the part on 'protection of intellectual property rights in the digital environment' as the only way to protect our most innovative industrial sector. why not split acta in two and start the legal procedures now for the discussion and approval of the chapters that do not include the 'digital environment'? we'd gain in time and efficiency...
in writing. − the fight against counterfeiting is a priority and international cooperation is essential to achieve this objective. however, the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) has raised important questions about possible violations of fundamental rights and threats to individual freedom that cannot and should not be dismissed. therefore, and given that the european commission has referred acta to the court of justice for a review of its compatibility with the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights, i considered it appropriate that parliament should await the court's decision before voting to approve or reject acta. for that reason, and out of respect for the decisions of the courts, i abstained from voting on acta.
in writing. the recommendation under consideration, drawn up by mr david martin, concerns the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) between the european union (eu) and its member states, australia, canada, japan, the republic of korea, the united mexican states, the kingdom of morocco, new zealand, the republic of singapore, the swiss confederation and the united states of america. while the preservation of intellectual property rights - the raw material of many european citizens - is essential and the fight against piracy and counterfeiting of products mainly from emerging economies is a priority, the present proposal for an agreement is critical in terms of the violation of fundamental rights in access to the internet. i believe that the eu should have first revised the ipr directive and adapted eu law to the internet environment before negotiating this agreement. it should be noted that the acta, which aims to combat piracy and counterfeiting, did not include in its negotiations countries such as india, china and brazil, where the highest violations of intellectual property occur. for these reasons i voted against acta.
in writing. - the long acta process is thus (for now) over. this process has triggered a remarkable mobilization of citizens throughout europe (and beyond), promoting public debate on acta and denouncing some of its dangers and consequences. the european commission has conducted the whole process in a manner that has avoided democratic debate and scrutiny, and the negotiations have been conducted in a highly secretive manner, which is reason enough to be suspicious of their content. we believe that it is necessary to combat counterfeiting, particularly counterfeiting with which the eu has been associated, of products such as port wine (and others) or textile products, which affect portugal so much, and which is inseparable from the eu's own policies, for example in the agricultural and commercial fields. but we cannot agree - and we strongly reject - to an agreement which establishes measures for the surveillance and spying of citizens, ranging from the surveillance of computer data, through internet service providers, to the search of personal luggage. this is an unacceptable violation of citizens' privacy, which violates the free flow of information and knowledge. an agreement which, moreover, could have implications in areas as diverse as access to medicines or seeds.
in writing. - having rejected the postponement, i voted in accordance with my understanding of the merits of the treaty which brings an indispensable international dimension to the protection of iprs guaranteed in the eu and of the insubstantiality of the objections against the treaty in the field of individual freedoms. first, iprs are fundamental rights protected by the tfeu. second, as generous as internet freedom is, it does not include freedom from piracy and counterfeiting. third, acta does not affect the freedom of internet users, but only the freedom to provide pirated or counterfeit material on a commercial scale. finally, acta is not self-executing, does not create rights or obligations for anyone, nor does it criminalize anything: it can only be operated by internal law.
in writing. - before the vote on this report, a colleague of mine suggested that this document be returned to the european commission, as he considered it to be worthy of improvement. such return was rejected. this document contains two issues which should be kept separate: the serious problem of counterfeiting and the issue of online content (online piracy). since the root document should have been structured differently, i voted in favour of its return. in the final vote i abstained on a matter of principle on the serious problem of counterfeiting, which has cost european companies 250 billion euros a year. the european union is also destroying 185 billion jobs a year.
in writing. − the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta) aims to combat counterfeiting for commercial purposes and online piracy by coordinating the global enforcement of existing copyright infringement laws. counterfeiting and piracy have increased substantially and this increase continues. the consequences of the growth of these illegal activities range from economic damage to health and safety hazards. the european union is seriously hampered by the absence of effective global coordination of copyright protection. however, the intended benefits of this international agreement are far outweighed by the potential threats to individual freedoms. given the vagueness of some aspects of the text and the uncertainty of its interpretation, the european parliament cannot ensure the adequate protection of the rights of european citizens under acta. in addition, acta, in its efforts to combat piracy and counterfeiting, should and must include in its negotiations countries such as india, china and brazil, where the highest levels of intellectual property infringement occur. i therefore voted in favour of this report recommending that acta not be approved.

in writing. − from 2014, new support schemes for farmers will be implemented as part of the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) 2014-2020. this report analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 73/2009 as regards the application of direct payments to farmers in respect of 2013, the last year of application of the current schemes. the purpose of this proposal is to define the net maximum amounts that farmers will be able to receive in the year 2013, which should take into account the compulsory modulation that was applied in 2012. in addition, some financial provisions are circumscribed to the end of 2012 and the calendar year 2013 corresponds to the financial year 2014. direct payments to farmers shall be settled by 31 october each year. however, the rural development budget was frozen and this situation needed to be unlocked as the sector is in crisis and faces a lack of support from member states. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i voted in favour of, since without this commitment some farmers would receive less, by about 20%.
in writing. − this report sets out the rules for the current system of direct payments to farmers for the year 2013, as some financial provisions are limited to 2012. the next cap - whose reform is currently under discussion - for the period 2014-2020 will only come into force in january 2014. additional legislation is therefore needed to provide for direct payments during this hiatus. this proposal sets net ceilings for direct payments through an adjustment mechanism similar to the compulsory modulation applied in 2012. despite the technical justification of the proposal, our abstention reflects our fundamental disagreement with the current system of direct payments. a system of granting subsidies based on historical values - with colossal inequalities between producers, productions and countries - and without any obligation to produce. the intensity of the modulation, now known as the adjustment, is not changed, with reductions of 10% for amounts between eur 5 000 and eur 300 000 and reductions of 14% for amounts above eur 300 000. a mechanism would be required whose maximum value would be well below the proposed one. it would be necessary to support those who actually produce, linking direct payments to production and balancing the unfair distribution of aid that is taking place today.

most decisive. the dominant economic and social system on a world scale is proving incapable of satisfying the most basic needs of millions upon millions of human beings, and yet it is consuming and degrading the planet's resources at a rate far in excess of their natural regenerative capacity. breaks are inevitable. in view of this, some may feel that it is time to pull a rabbit out of its hat. they called it the green economy. the vagueness and ambiguity of the concept has served all opportunism, even that of those who say they want to save the environment without interfering with the system that degrades and threatens it, who say they want to combat hunger and other social ills without going to their root causes, a genuinely sustainable development based on a sustainable relationship between man and nature will not be possible without questioning the laws and dogmas of capitalism, however much they want to paint it green. we must break with a growth which sacrifices natural resources and labour, the creative and transformative energy of the human being, to the growing accumulation of profit, to the private appropriation of the social wealth produced. we must safeguard natural resources, but also their democratic use, defend local production by reducing the breadth of production and consumption cycles, stop the liberalisation of world trade, which is an incentive to increase energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, despite their serious economic and social consequences, protect natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems, recover degraded ecosystems by enhancing their role in regulating the carbon cycle, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, but through a regulatory approach and not through mechanisms that leave these objectives to the taste of market sentiment. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that the fight for a healthy planet is inseparably linked to the fight for a fairer world, for the appreciation of those who work and for a society which raises the principles of democracy above the laws of the so-called market economy.

in writing. the court of justice of the european union is composed of seven judges. the temporary absence of one of these judges for health reasons could have a profound impact on the functioning of the court and contribute to delays in pending cases. this initiative thus introduces the possibility of associating temporary judges with the specialised courts. it is envisaged that the council will draw up a list of three persons who are fit to sit as judges of the civil service tribunal and who may be called upon to act as judges acting in their capacity whenever it is necessary to replace a judge who is prevented from acting for health reasons for at least three months. these temporary judges shall be appointed for a term of four years (renewable) and shall exercise the prerogatives of the permanent judges in dealing with the cases for which they have been appointed, that is to say, they shall have strictly judicial functions but shall not be able to take part in decisions concerning the administration of the court or in the election of the president or presidents of the chambers. i have therefore supported this regulation because i believe that it seems to be the most logical solution to deal with situations which may eventually constitute an obstacle to the pursuit of the judicial mission of the court.

in writing. − the european union civil service tribunal (eupst), set up on 2 december 2005 by the council of the european union, is composed of seven judges and hears disputes between the communities and their servants (article 236 of the ec treaty and article 152 of the eaec treaty). it is a specialised court and its decisions are subject to appeal to the court of first instance. in recent years, there has been a significant increase in the number of pending cases that need to be dealt with urgently. the current statute of the eupt does not allow for the replacement of a judge during temporary absences for health reasons, which implies a backlog of pending cases. to remedy this situation, it is proposed that temporary judges be appointed from among former judges of the court of justice of the european union for a renewable term of four years. although i regret that the 'vote of the day' was not included, i voted in favour of this proposal to amend the statute of the feutc, as the creation of a vice-president and the possibility of replacing a judge absent on grounds of illness will not only improve the work of the court but also contribute to improving the quality of life of citizens.
in writing. − this report concerns a draft regulation which will allow the appointment of temporary judges to the european union civil service tribunal, and lays down their rights and obligations, as well as the conditions under which they perform their duties and the circumstances in which they are terminated. the civil service tribunal may decide to appoint an acting judge whenever it finds that a judge is or will be prevented from sitting on the case on grounds of ill-health and that such a hindrance will or may be expected to last for at least three months. the rapporteur considers that the court of justice's proposal is a sensible solution to a specific problem which could be disruptive to the functioning of the civil service tribunal. it also added that the proposed amendments were purely technical and replicated those put forward by the commission in its opinion. however, we do not dissociate these issues from the evolution of the integration process itself, nor from the growing progress on the sovereignty of states and their institutions that is associated with it, also in the area of justice.

in writing. − the existence of modern and efficient infrastructure is important to achieve the europe 2020 objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as well as to reduce unemployment through the completion of the internal market. investment needs in transport, energy and information and communication technology (ict) infrastructure are estimated at eur 1.5 billion for the period 2010-2020. although much of this investment is private, the truth is that a public component is still needed, here in the form of project bonds. these are a debt instrument issued by private project companies, supported by an eu/eib contribution, to make bonds safer and more attractive to capital market investors. this first step is essential to test how the project bond issue is received in the markets.

in writing. - this proposal is based on a real need. in the context of large transfers of public funds to plug holes in the financial system, with the prospect of a prolongation of the restrictive financial policies for several years, with credit being scarce and the risk of default increasing, a number of major infrastructure projects, whose financial requirements are colossal, are now seriously compromised. but the logic behind these major projects is not to benefit the countries and their peoples - which would require, first of all, a break with the policies of plunder and exploitation that are in place. in fact, the only concern of this proposal is with the large projects, those involving mainly large german or french capital, which dominate these sectors - transport, energy, telecommunications. it is significant that investment in smaller scale infrastructure, which is of great importance because of the greater incorporation of national production it enables and the incentive it provides to smes, with the consequent creation of employment, is simply ignored. moreover, the proposal maintains all the dogmas associated with the existing policies budgetary control, deficit reduction, austerity. these long-term bonds are nothing more than a public investment to reduce private risk and thus increase private profit.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending decision no 1639/2006/ec establishing a framework programme for competitiveness and innovation (2007-2013) and regulation (ec) no 680/2007 laying down general rules for the granting of community financial support in the field of the trans-european transport and energy networks, by agreeing to it.
in writing. the ec has presented the connecting europe facility (cef), a financing instrument for transport, energy and ict infrastructure, as vital for the development of the european economy, with particular attention to cross-border links. since investment needs are so great, it has simultaneously proposed a new project bonds instrument to encourage private sector financing, which would not normally invest in this type of project. project bonds are debt issued by private companies for a specific project, with the eu and eib safeguarding it, making it more attractive and secure. along with other innovative instruments, this pilot phase of project bonds can be combined with other public and/or private financing. the eu will contribute up to eur 230 million. i support this initiative and hope that at the end of the pilot phase in 2013, this instrument will be implemented as another opportunity for states to finance themselves, for the development of energy, transport and ict infrastructure.

in september, year after year, many of us in this house raise our voices to speak about the fires in southern europe, the deaths of people, the loss of property, the destruction of forests and agricultural fields. the damage is hard to calculate. sometimes it is criminal hands and careless hands, but it is also high temperatures and worsening drought that create the conditions for fires, and are also the cause of them. in portugal, for example, 80% of the territory is in severe drought. the area burned in 2012 is already twice the average of the last ten years. the possibility of using the european civil protection mechanism is important to alleviate the disaster, but it is also urgent to strengthen existing community instruments and create others to minimise the occurrence of fires and control their spread and devastating effects by, firstly, promoting a forestry policy appropriate to the geographical and climatic diversity of europe, and, secondly, mechanisms for joining forces and means of fighting fires for rapid and massive action.

in writing. − in the framework of the european globalisation adjustment fund, the european commission adopted on 4 june 2012 a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of denmark to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. this is the fourth application to be examined under the 2012 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 455 104 from the egf for denmark. it concerns 981 redundancies, 550 of which were potential beneficiaries of support, at odense steel shipyard as the parent company and four suppliers and downstream producers in denmark during the four-month reference period from 1 may 2011 to 31 august 2011. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that ambitious policies are needed to combat climate change and resource scarcity. energy efficiency has proven to be the cheapest and fastest way of reducing co2 emissions. i also believe that it is essential to take measures to reduce the eu's external energy debt and to increase the geopolitical independence and energy security of the european union, as well as to keep energy costs under control and to achieve sustainable growth in the european union.
in writing. − this directive is an opportunity for europe to deliver on the commitments made by heads of state on energy and climate in march 2007 and february 2011. the aim is to achieve a 20% increase in eu energy efficiency, which will lead to a reduction of 368 million tonnes of oil equivalent (toe) by 2020 compared to the current trend. i believe that the european union cannot fail to achieve the energy efficiency objective; if it does not, it will also fail in relation to climate change, energy security, environmentally friendly growth and social protection. the renewal, every year, of 3% of the total surface area of 'heated and/or cooled buildings' owned by the state or occupied by the central government, as well as the installation of smart meters that help consumers to improve their energy efficiency behaviour are some examples of what this directive aims to introduce towards greater energy efficiency. i would stress that this directive encourages member states and regions to use the structural funds and the cohesion funds to invest in energy efficiency measures.
in writing. - we believe that it is imperative to take significant steps to increase energy efficiency and, in general, to rationalise energy consumption. this requires profound changes, which must involve a change in the dominant economic model on a world scale. continuing the principles that have guided energy policies in the eu, such as the liberalisation of energy markets, will not achieve this. in the so-called market economy the aim is to produce and sell, increasing supply, inducing demand, which underlies unsustainable energy consumption. this will partly explain why efficiency is the poor relation of european energy policy. the report highlights several positive aspects, including the fact that energy efficiency is an essential element in achieving the sustainability of the use of energy resources, the issue of smart meters, the energy efficiency of buildings and concern for smes. but what is missing is the essential thing: the break with neoliberal policy to allow energy efficiency that does not come under the influence of the crisis and the increasing energy poverty in europe.
in writing. − it is widely accepted that policies are needed to combat climate change and resource scarcity. in agreeing with the objective of keeping energy costs under control and achieving sustainable growth in the european union, i voted in favour of this report. in fact, experts consider energy efficiency to be one of the most efficient and least costly ways of reducing co2 emissions. in this respect, i consider this policy to be important, as do the adoption of measures leading to increased energy independence for the union and making it possible to reduce the union's external debt in the field of energy.
in writing. − the european commission has presented the 'energy 2020' initiative, putting energy at the heart of the union's energy strategy for 2020. the communication also stresses the need for a new energy efficiency strategy that would enable all member states to decouple energy consumption from economic growth. the european union has been leading the global negotiations on how to achieve greater energy efficiency, as all actions and measures taken will have an impact on climate change, energy security, environmentally friendly growth and social protection. i agree with this report because i believe that the eu must take a common approach to strengthening energy saving and energy efficiency by focusing on new innovative products and services, economies of scale between companies and reducing the bureaucratic burdens that exist in all member states. i also believe that european efficiency policy will be based on existing and successful regional and national policies, and that there should be sufficient flexibility to adapt to the needs and specificities of member states and regions.
in writing. - we agree with the general objective of increasing energy efficiency. it is, however, regrettable that the much-vaunted 20% target by 2020 - one of the five main objectives of the failed europe 2020 strategy - is far from being achieved. it is not surprising that, based on the continuity of the principles that have guided energy policies in the eu - such as energy market liberalisation and private and subsidised production from renewable sources - this objective will be difficult to achieve, as the so-called market rules have little effect on energy efficiency. the neoliberal functioning of the economy implies producing and selling, increasing supply, inducing demand, and not intervening to reduce the consumption of the goods produced. the report points to several positive aspects - the issue of smart meters, energy efficiency in buildings and concern for smes. however, if the aim is to help consumers in a time of crisis, then regulation of energy prices by energy service companies, which make huge profits, would be necessary. the report does not interfere with the interests of these monopoly companies, placing the burden of efficiency solely on the consumer.
