in writing. − i approve this report, recalling that the european union has committed itself to completing the creation of a common european asylum system (ceas) in 2012 by creating a common area of protection and solidarity based on a common asylum procedure and a uniform status for beneficiaries of international protection. i consider the echr to be an evolutionary step in european policy, bringing about a harmonisation of protection standards which is under way through the amendment of member states' legislation and the strengthening of practical cooperation through the work of the european asylum support office (easa). it is now necessary to tackle the third pillar of the esdc head-on, giving substance to the concept of solidarity and shared responsibility, enshrined in article 80 tfeu, which constitutes an essential horizontal component of the esdc. the esdc is specifically important because, in other words, it aims to be a comprehensive solidarity framework in which member states receive support to improve the quality of their asylum systems with a view to ensuring full respect for asylum seekers, which will in turn ensure the proper application of the asylum acquis.
in writing. − the european union has committed itself to completing the creation of a common european asylum system (ceas) by 2012, based on three pillars: harmonisation of protection standards through closer alignment of member states' asylum legislation; practical and effective cooperation with the necessary means; and greater solidarity and a sense of responsibility, not only between member states but also between the eu and third countries. it is important to ensure the smooth functioning of the ees, especially when migratory flows are often mixed, including migrants, asylum seekers, refugees and vulnerable persons. in this context, this report argues that member states, local authorities and civil society should be informed about the various european funds that can be used in the field of asylum. the asylum system of the member states should be regularly and frequently assessed to identify good practices and weaknesses. member states should show solidarity with each other and share responsibility, in particular as regards the joint processing of asylum applications and the relocation of beneficiaries of international protection. i therefore support this report.

in writing. - this standardisation proposal was the first of 12 measures launched by internal market and services commissioner michel barnier as part of his strategy to relaunch the single market. european standardization is, in my view, the sine qua non for the effective functioning of a european market which is to be called a single market. a single market which is transparent and uniform in its rules and in the classification of the products traded on it was one of the main objectives of the founding fathers of the union when they created the then ecsc/eec. no more english, german, french, spanish, italian or swedish standards (for example for industrial products) competing with each other (and surprise!) with the european standards themselves created for the entire eu area! it is also surprising that in a so-called 'single market' the imperial system and the metric system still exist! i am therefore in favour of all legislative measures leading to the creation of common market rules. only in this way can we move towards a true union of peoples and states, which is obviously intended to be free of any technical or other barriers.

in writing. the rapporteur believes that standardisation contributes to increasing the competitiveness of enterprises, in particular by facilitating the free movement of goods and services, and also to increasing competition and lowering production and selling costs. standardisation is thus seen as a step towards deepening the single market, free competition and, therefore, the resulting divergences and asymmetries. another issue of concern is the intention to develop european standards in the services sector, as provided for in the services directive, which will lead to greater harmonisation in this sector, increase the transparency, quality and competitiveness of european services, this is an integral part of the intention to liberalize the services sector. this liberalization of services is, in turn, inseparable from the attack on public services and the social functions of the states, and can have very serious implications for several countries, particularly those with more fragile social situations, and is even more serious in a crisis situation such as the one we are experiencing, particularly in portugal. we obviously recognise the importance of standardising products and processes in contemporary economies and societies. but it is the whole commercial philosophy behind this report that bothers and worries us.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative proposal on the revision of the standardisation regime (commission report) because it represents a major step forward in the convergence and harmonisation of product and service specifications within the union, removing barriers to movement and competition in the internal market. it is actually a piece of the so-called single market act announced by the european commission last year, which aims to deepen the internal market. standardisation establishes a level playing field in competition between undertakings, eliminates national borders, widens markets for undertakings, reduces production costs, better protects consumers and increases the external competitiveness of the union economy. in addition, internal standardisation leverages the union's initiatives and efforts to extend standardisation internationally, either through bilateral trade agreements or through bilateral instruments. international trade is increasingly dependent on the convergence of regulatory standards and the elimination of non-tariff barriers.

in writing. - food safety is a concern of european citizens which we must ensure. consumer information must be clear, objective and the result of a simple, non-bureaucratic process. optional labelling of beef is of obvious importance as it prevents the proliferation of misinformation to consumers on sensitive issues such as breed, breeding and meat processing, which the consumer information regulation should address. beef is a very sensitive product in the community market, which is very much under pressure from third countries with lower standards of animal welfare and production systems. i believe that the labelling system should be improved, but with concrete rules and a clear and equal control system for all member states, always in the spirit of a community system which prevents different practices that distort competition, that is, it should be mandatory for all member states, similar to what currently exists for poultrymeat or eggs.
in writing. − this regulation aims to pave the way for the abolition of the provisions on voluntary beef labelling by laying down general rules to provide a framework for and protect consumers, public health and public confidence, by means of objective information which is verifiable by the competent authorities and understandable to consumers. our group did not follow the proposed amendments because it considered that they weakened the consumer's right to information. we welcome the recognition of the differences in agricultural systems and practices and in the organisations of the sector between member states, and therefore they should be able to decide whether or not to introduce fdi in their territory, including the beef organisations in the discussion and taking into account small farmers and potential impacts. some concerns and doubts remain as to the implications for the process of receiving direct aid. we do, however, appreciate the fact that care should be taken that in cases of defective electronic identification, the failure of the technology does not lead to the imposition of financial penalties on farmers. the report acknowledges that there are practical problems which continue to impede the effective functioning of fdi, especially as regards the accuracy of the technology.
in writing. - although i voted in favour of the report as a whole, i voted against the proposals for amendments to the regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 as regards the electronic identification of bovine animals. the purpose of this regulation is to abolish the provisions on the voluntary labelling of beef and veal. i consider this system to be very important, since it makes it possible to specify and value aspects such as those relating to breed, diet and production systems, aspects which are as important for consumers as they are for farmers who use these terms for commercial purposes and also derive dividends from them. in the case of portugal, the effort made by producers who saw in the implementation of such voluntary schemes (which require approval of specifications by the competent authorities, specific control and labelling) an added value for national production, could be frustrated if the same schemes cease to exist.
in writing. - i supported the position of the rapporteur who received the commission's proposals on the introduction of electronic identification of bovine animals on an optional basis. i believe that it is necessary to adapt the legislation in order to recognise electronic identification as an official means of identifying bovine animals, taking into account how technology and its use in this field develop and become widespread. such technology will bring a number of benefits to those who wish to use it, particularly in the areas of traceability and workforce management. however, it is important that as the use of electronic identification of bovine animals becomes more widespread, technical standards are harmonised throughout the european union.

in writing. the report under review, by colleague linda mcavan, is on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2001/83/ec as regards pharmacovigilance. in december 2010, the european parliament and the council agreed to review the rules applicable to pharmacovigilance by adopting directive 2010/84/eu and regulation (eu) no 1235/2010. the package of measures adopted with this new legislation will lead to an improvement in the safety of medicines at eu level, thanks to the reinforced role of the european medicines agency (ema) in terms of collection and response following detection of signs and increased cooperation between member states. i believe that patients in europe should be better informed about the medicines they take and their side effects. the new pharmacovigilance legislation provides, among other measures, for the creation of a european web portal and national drug and device safety portals so that patients can notify national authorities when adverse reactions occur. in this respect, the added value of working with 500 million people is clear compared to the work of individual member states.
in writing. − pharmacovigilance has been under review since december 2010 with a view to its implementation this year, with the aim of improving the safety of medicines at eu level by strengthening the role of the european medicines agency (ema) in the assessment, detection and prevention of adverse reactions to medicines, and enhancing cooperation between member states. as we have stated in previous reports on this same subject, there are aspects of the changes under way which could improve the functioning of this mechanism for the assessment, detection and prevention of adverse reactions to medicinal products. this need for improvement was made evident by the tragic outcome of the mediator case, a diabetes drug that is estimated to have killed between 500 and 2,000 people. pharmacovigilance is undoubtedly of unquestionable importance, especially when adverse reactions to medicines are the fifth leading cause of hospital death, with an estimated 197 000 deaths per year in the eu. we stress the key role that the member states must continue to play in the community pharmacovigilance system. the competent authorities of the member states should continue to act as the screening centre for all spontaneous reports of adverse reactions to medicinal products.

in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the use of the market information system (mis) for administrative cooperation is a tool available to the member states which is best suited to protect the rights of european citizens, its purpose being to establish rules for the use of the mis which include a process for the exchange of personal data of european citizens between the competent authorities of the member states and the commission. this report aims to improve the conditions for the functioning of the internal market by creating a more effective and user-friendly tool to facilitate the implementation of administrative cooperation and the exchange of information. the proposal goes further with the s&d group amendments, which ensure further limitation on the purpose of using personal data, protecting citizens, and ensuring the proper application of the new provisions.
in writing. − the internal market information system (imi) is a free service provided to member states to improve the exchange of information in the internal market, and has been in use since 2008. it is a fast and secure means for cross-border exchange of information and administrative cooperation. currently used for the exchange of information on the recognition of professional qualifications and internal market services, imi continues to operate without a single legal instrument, which is considered one of the main obstacles to further expansion of the imi system. in this sense, this report, which i voted in favour of, supports the creation of a single legal framework for the imi system and a set of rules to ensure its proper functioning, thus allowing for the future expansion of imi to other areas of european union legislation.
in writing. - i consider it essential to improve the exchange of information within the internal market. since 2008, this exchange has been ensured by the internal market information system (imi) which has over 6 000 registered authorities from all eu member states and eea countries. but imi operates on the basis of a commission decision and recommendation and therefore lacks a single legal instrument, which has been identified as one of the main obstacles to further expansion of imi. i voted in favour of this report because i support the establishment of a common set of rules for the operation of imi with a view to making imi a more comprehensive tool for the citizens and the european internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on administrative cooperation through the internal market information system, as i consider that these amendments will make it possible to extend imi to other areas of eu legislation in the future and thus establish a clear set of rules in terms of its operation and data protection processing.
in writing. − the internal market information system (imi) is used as a free service provided to member states to improve the exchange of information within the internal market. the specific purpose of this regulation is to establish a single legal framework for the functioning of imi in order to contribute to the further expansion of this instrument. it also aims to enable the future extension of imi to other eu legislative areas and to establish a clear set of rules, including data protection processing. the imi is nothing more than an instrument designed to deepen and develop the internal market. that is how we evaluate it and take a stand on it. that is why we do not support this report. the question of data protection is another problem raised in this regulation. first, they want to open up imi to external actors, which could jeopardise the security and protection of personal data. secondly, the commission is not explicit about maximum retention periods for personal data in imi.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to establish a set of common rules for the operation of the internal market information system. i am convinced that the commission is doing its best to ensure that the single market is not simply a matter of a single market, but also a single market in which the citizens of the union have the right to know what they want. the internal market information system has already proven to be a reliable and efficient tool in the two areas where it has already been working the professional qualifications directive and the services directive and the proposal under consideration will therefore allow the full potential of the system to be further exploited with clear benefits for citizens and the internal market.
in writing. - article 26 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that 'the internal market shall comprise an area without internal frontiers in which the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital is ensured in accordance with the provisions of the treaties'. in addition, the union is responsible for adopting measures to establish the internal market or to ensure its functioning. to improve the exchange of information within the internal market, a free service for member states has been set up, the internal market information system (imi). i agree with this report because i believe that the system is a fast and secure means of cross-border exchange of information and administrative cooperation, with over 6 000 registered authorities at present. i would also like to stress that all personal data and information that circulates between the various competent authorities must be collected, processed and used for strictly legitimate purposes and in accordance with data protection rules.
in writing. − the internal market information system (imi) is used as a free service provided to member states with the stated aim of improving the exchange of information within the internal market. thus, this regulation has the specific purpose of establishing a single legal framework for the functioning of imi in order to contribute to the further expansion of this instrument. it also aims to enable the future extension of imi to other eu legislative areas and to establish a set of rules such as data protection processing. the imi is therefore nothing more than an instrument designed to deepen and develop the single market, which we have criticised. data protection is also one of the major concerns raised by this report - the opening of imi to external actors may jeopardise the security and protection of personal data, as it may make the system accessible to the private sector. secondly, the commission is not explicit in setting maximum retention periods for personal data in imi, considering that retention periods should not go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objectives of this regulation, which leaves room for an indefinite retention period.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that four years after the outbreak of the financial, economic and social crisis, it is essential to have a clear understanding of the direction in which the member states are moving, taking into account all possible solutions to bring europe back on the path of growth and development. on the one hand, it is essential to create and initiate new common policies with the help of which we will be sufficiently united and strong to avoid a crisis in the future. on the other hand, in difficult times like the present, it is also necessary to rethink existing policies and commitments and, if necessary, to test them to assess their relevance and adequacy to the challenges ahead. the council directive on a common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states has been amended several times over the last few years, but there are still technical improvements to be made as also mentioned in the commission communication in the name of clarity and accountability.
in writing. − council directive 2003/49/ec regulates the common taxation regime applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states. however, problems remain with regard to the functioning of the internal market, in particular the effect of the corporate tax: transactions between different member states are subject to higher interest and royalty rates than the taxation of the same transactions within the domestic market. the objective of this council directive is thus to ensure greater harmonisation between the charges paid within and between different member states, by eliminating certain problems such as double taxation, tax fraud and evasion and the possibility of involuntary non-taxation, which cause many damage to the proper functioning of the internal market. the european commission is also urged to define a minimum value for the fees paid by companies within the european union, taking into account factors such as tax competitiveness between certain countries and in a way that does not prejudice the sustainable consolidation of member states' national budgets. i have supported this report because i consider it an important step in the process of building an efficient, competitive and truly value-adding internal market for european businesses and citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it important that every effort be made to reduce the possibilities of involuntary non-taxation, double taxation or tax evasion and avoidance between member states, as these phenomena cause significant damage to the proper functioning of the internal market, as indicated in the recently adopted motion for a resolution on concrete means of combating tax evasion and avoidance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the common tax system applicable to interest and royalty payments. cooperation between the tax systems of the different member states is increasingly desirable. i consider this proposal to be positive, since it aims to exclude any possibility of tax evasion, tax substitution or illegitimate tax exemptions.
in writing. − the common tax regime applicable to the taxation of interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states is the subject of this council directive (2003/49/ec). the aim is to avoid double taxation of income. this can be achieved in two ways: taxing income in the member state where it is produced or in the member state where the head office of the company benefiting from it is located. the proposal is to tax interest and royalties in the member state where the company receiving them has its registered office. it is known that associated companies, which are often separate branches of the same organisation, have various mechanisms at their disposal to reduce their payment of tax on profits, in particular by manipulating the prices of goods or services they trade with each other. in this way, they shift profits to where they are least taxed. under article 1 (1), interest and royalties are exempt from tax in the state in which they are paid if the beneficial owner is a company from another member state or a permanent establishment situated in another member state. whether the company is associated with the paying company or not.
in writing. - i abstained on the report on the proposal for a council directive on a common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states (recast) because, although the principle of harmonising rates in the european union has been enshrined, this harmonisation has not been enshrined in the directive. the report also misses the opportunity to make progress in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion in this area, under the cover of the discourse on the elimination of double taxation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on a common tax system for interest and royalty payments between associated companies of different member states. i would stress the importance of updating this system in the light of the lessons learned from the financial crisis and would stress, among the rapporteur's amendments, those relating to 'taxable persons' and 'permanent establishment' which are intended to exclude any possibility of tax evasion, tax substitution or illegal tax exemptions.
in writing. − over the last few years, successive amendments have been made to the council directive on a common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states, and some additional measures could be taken to improve its effectiveness. i support this report because i agree that the european commission should introduce a minimum rate for corporate taxation, and that rate will reduce tax competition and strengthen the freedom of member states to tax companies. i also think it is a good thing that interest and royalties are taxed in a single member state, thereby restoring fairness among european citizens. finally, i believe it is essential to put in place effective mechanisms to prevent tax evasion, tax substitution or illegal tax exemptions, thus strengthening economic transparency within the european union.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on voluntary and unpaid tissue and cell donation because i believe it is important to increase public support and the rates of tissue and cell donation. member states should work towards developing, in a transparent manner, tissue and cell banks that respect ethical principles and ensure the safety of donors and patients.
in writing. − this report reinforces the view that tissue and cell donations should be voluntary and carried out on a non-profit basis and in a transparent context. given that healthcare is largely a matter for the member states, the proposed recommendations aim to complement existing practices in the member states and to take advantage of areas such as crossborder giving. altruism is a key word when we talk about tissue and cell donation. that is why i agree that compensation for the grant should be managed and defined carefully by the member states and should be limited to covering strictly the costs incurred by the grant. in these matters it is very important to consider the legal and ethical problems raised by the existence of numerous websites allowing people to buy and sell gamete cells online. in this regard, member states should consider adopting legislation to regulate this area in order to prevent the possible emergence of an online black market. i believe it is important to increase the supply of tissues and cells through the exchange of good practice in joint operations, ethical standards and awareness raising for donation through greater collaboration between member states.
in writing. - i welcome the presentation of this report which reinforces the position the european union has always held on organ, tissue and cell donation, that is to say, as the name implies, it must be absolutely free. the fundamental values for organ, tissue and cell donation, shared by all member states, are those of altruism and solidarity and must remain so, resisting the economic interests that have been developing in this field and thus combating the commercialization of the human body and the instrumentalization of the person.
in writing. − this report presents a set of recommendations on voluntary and unpaid donation of tissues and cells, complementing the practice of member states with exclusive competence in this area. the aim is that donations should be voluntary and made on a non-profit basis in a context of transparency and security, allowing for a small compensation to cover the costs incurred. the proposals concern only multiple tissues and reproductive and non-reproductive cells. it excludes in vitro fertilisation, stem and embryonic cell research and cloning. the rapporteur calls on the member states to take account of the existence of websites selling tissues and cells and the potential for a parallel market. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that cooperation and the exchange of good practice can increase transparency and the flow of donations between member states and thus improve the quality of life of people.

in writing. − i approve this report, considering that in 2010 in the european union in the service sector, the overwhelming majority of jobs are held by women and almost 50% of women are concentrated in 10 of 130 service sector occupations. these facts are particularly worrying at a time of economic crisis and especially when we also consider the fact that women are paid 16.4% less than men. i therefore support this proposal which aims to give a boost to the improvement of working conditions for women, as this will not only help europe to emerge from the crisis earlier, but also to achieve the 2020 targets more effectively. this proposal includes measures such as the need for the commission to collect data on the impact of austerity on women in the service sector and to call for projects whose underpinnings are aimed at helping women's employment situation.
in writing. - in recent decades, the european union has made great strides in integrating women into the labour market. the employment rate for women is 62%, up from 55% in 1997. on the other hand, women represent almost 60% of all university graduates in the european union. despite the fact that more and more women are highly qualified and their participation in the labour market is increasing, they continue to be largely outnumbered by men in positions of responsibility in the political and business fields, particularly in top positions. there is also a gender division of labour based on stereotypes that assume the existence of male and female jobs. on the other hand, wage disparities are still a reality in the european union. despite the various legal initiatives for equal pay, the gap persists and progress is extremely slow. i voted in favour of this report, which sets out a series of measures, particularly in the field of reconciling work and family life, to improve working conditions for women in the service sector.
in writing. - about half of women in employment are concentrated in 10 of the 130 occupations listed in the international typology of occupations. this horizontal segregation is based on stereotypes rooted in society which presuppose the existence of male and female jobs. most people hired for flexible working hours are women. parttime and temporary employment are still predominantly female. in the eu, women earn 17.1% less than men, although the gender pay gap ranges from 3.2% to 30.9% in the member states. although 60% of university graduates are women, only one in seven board members of the most important european companies is a woman (13.7%). the weight of the informal economy in female employment in the service sector is higher than in male employment. harassment, sexual abuse at work, and other forms of violence against women are of particular concern. i voted in favour of this report because it denounces these situations and points to measures to improve the working conditions of women in the service sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the implementation of measures which help to reduce the segregation of women in the service sector. the level of education of women, which is on average higher than that of men, is rarely accompanied by a rise in the professional hierarchy or an improvement in their employment conditions. it is necessary to implement measures to ensure greater representation of women on boards of directors and to ensure the effective application of the principle of equal pay between men and women.
in writing. - from the middle of the last century, women in modern societies have been emancipated, mainly because their level of education has increased and has rapidly overtaken that of men. in fact, today, 60 percent of college graduates are women. whereas in the past women were said to belong in the home, today there are many professions where they are in the majority, such as the service sector. in the european union, 69.4% of all jobs in this sector are held by women, but this figure falls to 5.2% in agriculture. despite the fact that the employment rate at european level is converging between men and women, the truth is that many women continue to be discriminated against by employers because of their maternity. they therefore work mostly on flexible or parttime hours, which results in a gender pay gap. it is therefore imperative to eliminate gender inequalities in order to prevent all forms of violence against women, which affects all social, cultural and economic strata, with sexual harassment and abuse being prevalent in the service sector.
in writing. − this report highlights the poor working conditions of women in the service sector, including wage discrimination, parttime work, temporary employment, irregular and unpredictable working hours, the scarcity and irregularity of days and rest periods, harsh working conditions. among the many positive proposals in the report, we would stress the need to implement measures to ensure equal pay, combat precarious employment, convert precarious workers into actual workers, strengthen and safeguard workers' rights and working conditions, and ensure that companies implement effective maternity support schemes, among others. the report encourages member states to ratify immediately ilo convention no 189 on domestic workers, with the aim of ensuring decent working conditions. it also stresses the need to create free, quality public social facilities and services to support children and dependants. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. we voted in favour.

madam president, lady ashton, as we point out in this report, the consistency and coherence of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) requires political leadership and coordination, ensuring that european policies such as trade and development are in line with cfsp principles, values and strategic interests. ethiopia – an acp partner, a major recipient of eu aid, the second most populous country in africa and headquarters of the african union – has been without a government since the dictator meles zenawi died in july, much earlier than the totalitarian clique announced to the people of ethiopia. this delay allowed them to secretly engineer the perpetuation of their oppressive regime. fortunately yesterday two swedish journalists imprisoned by meles were finally released. but we did not hear the eu pressing for their release, and we did not hear it pressing for the release of all the other thousands of ethiopian political prisoners, including eskinder nega, recipient of pen america’s ‘freedom to write’ award. what can you tell us about your endeavours in that regard? why is the eu so silent or at least so discreet in calling for the liberation of ethiopians? and can you tell us what the eu is doing to press for an inclusive political dialogue involving all opposition parties, including the armed ones, so that ethiopia may remain unified and not fall into violence, so that ethiopia may now find that genuine road to democracy to which its people aspire and not go on oppressed by these totalitarian forces? ethiopia is too important for africa and for the world for us to continue to turn a blind eye to what is going on there. (the speaker agreed to take a blue-card question under rule 149(8))
answer is "blue cardboard". madam president, my question is precisely: what have we done? i am glad that we have worked for the release of these two swedish journalists. but what about the thousands of journalists and other ethiopian dissidents who are in prison? what are we doing in the face of this situation and to push for a truly democratic solution for ethiopia? ethiopia is too important to be neglected as it is by all of us and by our governments, in particular.
on behalf of the green group in the european parliament ladies and gentlemen, once again we are in one of those typical debates in parliament, a very dilemmatic debate. the situation in syria is complex, the situation in syria is problematic. what do you mean? president-in-office of the council. − mr president, let me first thank the four rapporteurs, mr gallagher, mr stevenson, mr torvalds and mr salavrakos, for their presentations and for their outstanding work. i would also like to greet commissioner damanaki and her commitment and ambition in advancing the reform of our fisheries policy. it is a great honour for me to be here today to present the council views on the very important topics that we plan to discuss. these include of course, as we said, the reform of the common fisheries policy. i look forward to working very closely with you in the codecision procedure as we advance a very important legislative agenda with a significant impact on eu citizens. therefore i would like to stress my commitment to making our joint work successful and rewarding. concerning the common fisheries policy reform, the council launched its debate horizontally in july last year. that debate took into account the commission communications on which mr haglund and mr salavrakos have prepared reports. since then, the council has focused on the common market organisation and the regulation on the common fisheries policy, reaching a general approach in june of this year. in addition the council agreed on conclusions for the external fisheries policy in march of this year. the council’s position on the common market organisation enlarges the role and responsibility of producer organisations towards promoting more sustainable fishing activities, taking on tasks related to fisheries management and on handling unwanted catches that fishermen will have to land after the implementation of the discard ban. on public market interventions the council agrees with the commission that these interventions should be scaled down. storage aid should be the only remaining intervention and member states are not yet in agreement on whether these should be completely phased out over time. on consumer information the council agrees with the commission that product labels should have to report on whether the fish has been defrosted before marketing, but the council disagrees with the commission’s proposal that the date of catch should be mandatory as well. on the reform in general, the council’s position can be summarised as follows: management of fish stocks needs to achieve maximum sustainable yield by 2015, where possible, and by 2020 at the latest. new multiannual plans should better reflect the interdependence of fish stocks and fisheries and apply the maximum sustainable yield policy to all stocks which are significant in the area of the multiannual plan. discard reductions should be at the forefront of the fisheries reform, accompanied by a landing obligation which will be phased in according to a timetable. i would like to welcome the european parliament’s support for a more regionalised common fisheries policy with better involvement of stakeholders and reinforced advisory councils. the council agrees with this pillar of the reform, and its general approach contains procedures for putting regionalisation into practice as well as reinforcing the role of advisory councils. with regard to transferable fishing concessions, many member states are cautious concerning their effectiveness in fighting over-capacity and are concerned about possible unintended consequences. the general approach therefore foresees the introduction of transferable fishing concessions on a voluntary basis, while improving the existing mechanism to report on over-capacity and to take measures for fleet capacity adjustment. the link between fleet capacity and the european maritime and fisheries fund will be further explored by ministers during their september meeting in two weeks’ time, preparing for a partial general approach at the october council. i do not need to stress that the emff’s role in the reform will now be the focus of our discussions, in particular its importance for growth, boosting aquaculture, creating more jobs and helping to implement the new common fisheries policy. with the new council conclusions on the external dimension, the council has set a more detailed framework for bilateral fisheries agreements, based on sustainability, and has given policy directions for the union’s work in regional and multilateral fisheries organisations. last but not least, as a testimony to the success we can achieve together, i would like to thank mr gallagher for his outstanding work on the trade measures file which is expected to be adopted by our two institutions by the end of this month. this is a far-reaching piece of legislation which will enable the european union to adopt effective measures against third countries allowing non-sustainable fishing. of course the most recent such case that comes to our minds is the situation of the north-east atlantic mackerel stock. we all know that unfortunately the latest attempt to find a solution acceptable to all did not succeed last week in london. i would like to recall the july council’s desire to find a suitable compromise for this very unfortunate situation, but not at any price. thanks to this legislation we now have an additional instrument to use against such non-sustainable management practices.

answer under the 'blue card' procedure. our response is very clear and has been expressed in the numerous amendments we have tabled to the various reports under discussion. we believe that local management is in the best interests of the resources and the fishermen. this proximity management we advocate is the antithesis of the centralised management we have had for the last 20 or 30 years, a centralised management which the lisbon treaty has unfortunately deepened by making the management of living marine biological resources an exclusive competence of the european union. we are now faced with the negative consequences of this, firstly because of the limitations which the commission itself says it has in going further in decentralising the common fisheries policy and in promoting the local fisheries management which we advocate.
the committee on regional development has also adopted a number of amendments. - mr president, commissioner, the future common fisheries policy must give priority to its environmental, economic and social sectors, in a synergistic and non-hierarchical way, for the sake of sustainable development and in line with the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth of the eu 2020 strategy. as rapporteur for the regi opinion, i would like to highlight the particularity of certain regions, such as the outermost regions, whose economies are heavily dependent on the fisheries sector. in these regions, the reform of the common fisheries policy must seek to ensure the survival and future prosperity of their small-scale and artisanal fishing fleets, thus safeguarding and defending the jobs that depend on them. i agree with the european commission's position that there is a need for an adjustment of this policy and for specific measures which should take account of the different realities of the fisheries and aquaculture sector in the various coastal regions. i would urge that this policy focuses on regionalization as a form of governance through greater involvement of the various stakeholders so that in future it can respond more adequately to the needs and sensitivities of each sea basin.
the reform of the common fisheries policy has now begun to take shape with the presentation and voting of some of the reports under discussion today, for which i congratulate the respective rapporteurs and shadow rapporteurs and thank them for their work. we all know that reform must be deep and that resource sustainability is our lowest common denominator. we also know that the reality of the sector has to change, so the challenges it faces will be tough. it is up to all of us to work towards ensuring that fisheries and their fish stocks are maintained by promoting the sustainability of resources. it is up to us all to respond positively to the different interests at stake, accepting the complexities of dialogue and consensus-building and not, in a complacent and irresponsible way, to pursue the simplest solutions, as seems to be the fashion today, or seeking the applause of the masses, to give in to the populist forms of which we have become hostages. we are members of the committee on fisheries and the commissioner is the one responsible for maritime affairs and fisheries. let us not forget it! and there is no reform, neither superficial nor profound, as we want it to be, that can be done against the sector or without the sector. other politicians have fallen into this error. they lost, they lost in sectors where nothing has changed and we all lost too. an effective reform must involve those it is addressed to in order to win their collaboration, without which it will be doomed to failure. today's reports are a testimony to the change that must be made and to the dialogue that must be held because change is taking place. i hope we can continue along this path.

in writing. - i approve this report because it seeks to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union. i consider the proposal to create a set of common rules for victims of crime in all the member states of the european union to be extremely important and useful, as rights such as the right to be heard, to be informed, to understand and be understood, to have victim support services at one's disposal, to make it easier to identify vulnerable victims and to protect victims during questioning or criminal proceedings are essential. such a set of rules should be able to increase confidence in the criminal and justice systems of all the member states of the european union and at the same time ensure greater judicial cooperation in a climate of mutual understanding and promotion of fundamental european values. for all these reasons, i support this proposal in favour of victims of crime who deserve more help, assistance and information from the competent authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which was presented on the symbolic date of 11 september and which allows us to remember and honour all the victims of crime and their families. europe needs a common and transparent justice system and must ensure that the rights and protection of victims of crime are strengthened. this directive constitutes an important step in the construction of the european area of freedom, security and justice. all victims of crime, regardless of the degree of harm suffered, are covered by this directive and should be offered support and protection in their country as well as in other member states. increased cross-border interinstitutional cooperation, including the effective sharing of information and good practice, is essential.
in writing. − i fully support the establishment of minimum standards on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime, regardless of their nationality or the place where the crime occurred. i consider it of the utmost importance to strengthen the rights of victims in general and in particular of victims with special needs and those who have suffered a particularly horrific experience, as well as to ensure the protection of the privacy of the victim, regardless of the nature of the harm suffered. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this directive is part of a package of legislative measures aimed at strengthening the rights, support and protection of victims of crime in the eu. the eu therefore needs an integrated and coordinated approach in this area which can ensure that the rights and needs of victims of crime in all their aspects can be respected and fulfilled. it thus establishes minimum standards applicable to cases where crimes have been committed in the eu and to criminal proceedings pending in the eu, thus strengthening trust in the criminal justice systems of all member states, which should contribute to more effective judicial cooperation in a climate of mutual trust and should also promote a culture of fundamental rights in the eu. i therefore support this initiative, which should make it possible to strengthen and complement the existing instruments. it is also good that an agreement was reached at first reading. i hope now that the member states can do their part and transpose it in time over the next three years.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it sets minimum standards for the rights, support and protection of victims of crime. i consider proposals relating to victim support services to be of high importance, as they are particularly at risk of further harm, intimidation or repeated victimisation during criminal proceedings.
in writing. - i consider it to be elementary justice that, in an area which is unique in so many respects, there are standards of protection for victims which are common to the whole of the union. this protection, as the commission also argues, must be granted irrespective of the nationality of the victim and the place where the crime was committed. in this parliament last december we passed measures which aimed to guarantee all defendants some basic rights in criminal proceedings. the same protection must now be afforded to victims of crime, who for that very reason often feel helpless in the face of a process they do not know and do not understand, especially when such a process is taking place in a foreign country. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of victims of crime is a step in the right direction.
in writing. − the aim of the european union (eu) is to make all citizens feel that they are brothers and sisters in a project of well-being and security. the free movement of persons and goods can only be fully enjoyed if we feel that our rights are safeguarded in any member state where we are. it's vital that we know that wherever we are, there's always someone who cares about us. when a terrorist attack occurs, there is a great concern to identify its perpetrators and bring them to justice. it's all about the criminal. often, it is international organizations that sponsor the defense of terrorists and defend the rights of prisoners. however, most victims and their families are forgotten. which, in addition to being unfair, is inhuman. i welcome the presentation of this proposal which clarifies the rights of citizens when they are victims of gender-based violence, trafficking, rape, terrorism, etc. in any eu member state. i congratulate the rapporteurs on their excellent work on behalf of european citizens, especially those who, for whatever reason - and this can happen to any of us - may become victims. this is how the people's europe is built. a europe that does not abandon us when we are most vulnerable.
in writing. - the report proposes measures to support and protect victims of various forms of violence against people: domestic violence, discrimination on grounds of sex and sexual orientation, trafficking in human beings, exploitation in prostitution, sexual and moral harassment, female genital mutilation, among many others, are some of the forms of violence mentioned. the need for specialised staff involved in these support and protection processes is also mentioned. we value these proposals, although we do not support the proposals for transferring more power to the eu through new legislation. that is why we abstained. some other considerations: we also believe that the right to be heard by minors should be safeguarded. we consider it fair that the offended party should be able to request a review of decisions taken by the competent authorities.
in writing. − i welcome the adoption of this report on the commission proposal for a directive on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime, which is part of a package of legislative measures aimed at strengthening the rights of victims in the eu and which includes a proposal for a regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters and a communication entitled 'strengthening the rights of victims in the eu'.
in writing. − strengthening this directive is of the utmost importance to increase the rights, support and protection of eu victims of any crime within the eu. i consider this report to be an important measure that extends the rights of victims of any type of crime by applying minimum standards throughout the eu. i would like to highlight some of the points in the report, namely the protection of victims with special needs, adopting the methods and support taking into account the type of harm suffered, individual assessment and training of the competent bodies, understanding the gender dynamics of victims' rights and increased cooperation and coordination for the protection of victims between member states. this protection must be extended to the family and the support provided must take place throughout the legal process and victims must be informed in a clear and discernible manner. an area of freedom, justice and security must have the citizen at its core.
in writing. − we support this report in its call for integrated protection against the various types of violence against people: domestic violence, discrimination on grounds of sex and sexual orientation, trafficking in human beings, exploitation in prostitution, sexual and moral harassment, female genital mutilation, among many others. however, as a matter of principle and judicial sovereignty, we do not agree with a greater transfer of power in this area to the eu. in many of the areas mentioned, portugal already has adequate legislation, in particular as regards the protection of victims of domestic violence, the right of the child to be heard and the protection of minors. the reality facing portugal is rather that of a lack of public investment in the implementation of practical measures to support the victim.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the purpose of this commission proposal is to bring council regulation (ec) no 774/94 opening and providing for the administration of certain community tariff quotas for certain meat and cereal products into line with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which gives the commission (ec) the power to adopt the necessary implementing measures and to amend this regulation if the volumes and other conditions relating to the quota system are adjusted, in particular by decisions concluding agreements with third countries. as a member of the european parliament, i support the rapporteur's position that these powers should be brought into line with the post-lisbon regime of delegated and implementing acts by conferring relevant implementing powers on the ec, which should be exercised in accordance with the provisions of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council, so that there is a real involvement of the european parliament. we must never forget that the european parliament is the institution which represents the citizens of europe, and therefore it must have the power to limit the commission's action.

in writing. - the main objective of this report is to align the above-mentioned council regulation with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). the rapporteur introduces a number of amendments aimed at limiting the commission's powers in relation to the delegation of powers and advocating greater involvement of the european parliament in the preparation and implementation of delegated acts. we appreciate the provision which gives parliament more time to object to a delegated act. however, this report cannot fail to be examined in its deepest meaning, taking account of the positions of principle on the treaty and its provisions on commercial policy. the lisbon treaty stipulates that trade policy is an exclusive competence of the eu. in other words, the states have been deprived of an essential instrument of economic policy. the interests in the commercial field are, of course, different from country to country, because the respective economies, fragility and potential of each country are different. the overlapping of the interests of the strongest with those of the weakest, in this as in other areas, entails tremendous damage to weaker economies, as is the case with portugal. the effects of free trade policies on the restructuring of important national productive sectors are to be seen...

in writing. the commission proposal aims to bring council regulation (ec) no 774/94 opening and providing for the administration of certain community tariff quotas for certain meat and cereals products into line with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. that regulation confers on the commission the power to adopt the necessary implementing measures and to amend that regulation in the event of adjustments to the volumes and other conditions relating to the quota system, in particular by decisions concluding agreements with third countries. these powers should be aligned with the system of delegated and implementing acts established by the lisbon treaty, and in this context the rapporteur proposes greater involvement of parliament, limiting the delegation to tacitly extendable five-year periods, extending the period for a possible objection to four months and modifying the implementation of the written procedure. it also advocated that the text of the regulation be made compatible with the 'trade omnibus' regulations.
in writing. - i approve this report because, for reasons of consistency of trade legislation, the rapporteur proposes two amendments to the commission proposal which reflect the changes resulting from the two 'omnibus regulations', in particular with regard to the addition of two new recitals concerning the implementing/delegated acts in the basic legal acts and the involvement of the european parliament. the commission proposal also refers, for the three regulations, to the committee procedure provided for in the adjusted regulation establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products (single cmo regulation). the rapporteur proposes that this reference be deleted and that a new provision on the committee procedure be added to each of the amended regulations. this can ensure the amended application of the written procedure resulting from the trade omnibus regulations. for all these reasons, i would point out once again that a more active role for the european parliament is always more favourable to the european citizens and to the harmonious development of the european union as a whole.

in writing. the commission proposal aims to harmonise the three council regulations on imports of olive oil and other agricultural products from turkey with the post-lisbon treaty regime for implementing and delegated acts provided for in articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. for reasons of consistency of trade legislation, the rapporteur proposes amendments reflecting the changes resulting from the two 'omnibus regulations', such as increased involvement of the european parliament in the preparation of delegated acts, limiting the delegation of power to the commission to a period of 5 years, tacitly extendable for an equal period, extending the possible extension of the time limit for objecting to a draft delegated act from 2 to 4 months, and changing the detailed rules for the application of the written procedure. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the proposed parallel agreement amending the agreement on mutual recognition (mra) with australia is important as they are agreements on the mutual recognition of conformity assessment of regulated products. the report thus proposes that the arm should seek to remove technical barriers to trade while safeguarding the health, safety and environmental objectives of both parties. the arm provides in its main body for general rules on the establishment of conformity assessment bodies as well as specific rules applicable to the various sectors covered.
in writing. − mutual recognition agreements (mras) allow for conformity assessment of regulated products, which give both parties authority to test and certify products based on the other party's regulatory requirements, on their territory and before export. it aims to remove technical barriers to trade while safeguarding health, safety and environmental objectives. this agreement amending the arm with australia was negotiated by the european commission with the aim of simplifying the operation of the arm and entered into force on 1 january 1999. the amendments are intended to allow for increased flexibility in the structure of the sectoral annexes to the arm, to remove unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties, to reduce the administrative burden related to the management of the agreement and to facilitate and clarify the functioning of the arm. i therefore support this recommendation calling on parliament to approve the agreement.

in writing. the document under consideration, for which mr vital moreira is responsible, concerns a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement between the european union (eu) and australia amending the agreement on mutual recognition (mra) in the field of conformity assessment, certificates and markings between the european community and australia. the agreement now being negotiated by the commission aims to simplify the arm which has been in force since 1 january 1999 and whose purpose is to enable the parties to assess the conformity of regulated products. the amendments introduced will increase the flexibility of the structure of sectoral annexes by removing unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties. in addition, the restriction on rules of origin for industrial products, which was considered unnecessary, will be removed, and the text will be updated with regard to institutional and procedural changes, the withdrawal of recognition and suspension of conformity assessment bodies, etc., without neglecting matters relating to health, safety and the environment. i voted in favour of this recommendation because, in addition to having no financial implications, it brings a significant set of improvements to the applicability of the existing mutual recognition agreement.

in writing. - i support this report, firstly for reasons of fairness, because i do not consider it fair that while there are regions like mine that practice sustainable fishing, at the same time other member states do not meet the same requirements and may even put the stocks of different european marine regions at risk. any blatant lack of good will to work in obedience to agreed measures must be counterbalanced by firm action. as a lucrative destination market for fishery products, the eu has a special responsibility to safeguard the sustainability of the sector and to respect the shared management of straddling and highly migratory fish stocks. it is therefore necessary to provide the eu with effective means to act against any state that is unwilling to assume this responsibility, or that does not cooperate in the adoption and implementation of agreed management measures to discourage unsustainable fishing. i therefore wholeheartedly support the commission's proposal to use trade and other measures in situations similar to those described, but also to send a clear political message that includes a clearer approach and stronger and more effective measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu has a special responsibility to safeguard the sustainability of the fisheries sector and to respect the shared management of highly migratory and straddling fish stocks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'measures against countries engaging in unsustainable fishing for the conservation of fish stocks', as i considered it necessary to provide the eu with the means to take effective action against states which do not adopt the agreed management measures, and thus discourage the continuation of this unsustainable fishing.
in writing. − the organisation and functioning of fisheries and aquaculture product markets have implications for the sustainability of fisheries resources and marine ecosystems, as well as for public health and food security. the new provisions are intended to strengthen the role of producer organisations and to soften the marketing rules for fresh produce. the current consumer information requirements for fresh products (trade name, scientific name, indication of catch or production area, words 'caught' or 'cultivated', defrosted if applicable) are supplemented by the indication of the date of catch or production; or the word 'fresh' or 'frozen'.
in writing. - we all know that the planet's resources are not inexhaustible. this aspect becomes much more relevant when we are talking about resources directly linked to human food. the increase in the world population requires more and more resources and we cannot allow the degradation of ecosystems. the report by pat the cope gallagher, an expert on responsibility, deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of certain measures to states which engage in (or permit) fishing which is not environmentally sustainable and which jeopardises the maintenance of fish stocks. the absence of a sustainable fisheries policy, particularly as regards the capture of carp, is at issue. it is not acceptable what has happened to iceland (and others) which has unilaterally increased its catches. there must be agreement between the member states, because each one cannot do as it pleases. i voted in favour of the rapporteur's proposals because i agree that fishing, both within and outside the european union, must be sustainable.
in writing. − the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the united nations fish stocks agreement require coastal states and states whose fleets fish in adjacent high seas fish stocks to cooperate in managing, in a responsible manner, highly migratory and transboundary fish stocks and stocks in adjacent eezs in order to ensure their long-term sustainability, either through direct mutual consultation or through the regional fisheries management organisations (rfmos). as a relevant and lucrative destination market for fishery products, the eu has a special responsibility to ensure that this cooperation obligation is fulfilled. this proposal aims to establish a rapid and effective mechanism to enable trade-related and other types of measures to be used against states which do not respect their obligations. we are following the rapporteur's proposals. the trade measures to be implemented should not be limited to imports of 'stocks of common interest' and 'associated species', but should apply to all imports of fish and fishery products of all species originating in countries that accept the existence of unsustainable fishing.
in writing. − responsible management and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources should be a priority for the eu and all member states. in this context, the protection and conservation of stocks plays a crucial role. in particular, the eu has a special responsibility to safeguard the shared management of highly migratory and transboundary fish stocks. the eu therefore needs effective means to act against states that do not cooperate in the adoption and implementation of agreed management measures to discourage irresponsible and unsustainable fishing activities. i agree with the reasons given and therefore voted in favour of this report on the adoption of measures against countries which allow unsustainable fishing.
in writing. − the european union must have an appropriate legal instrument to enable it to react to the behaviour of states that do not cooperate with the rules of the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the united nations fish stocks agreement, as well as with the requirements imposed by regional fisheries management organisations for the responsible management of fish stocks. the european union has a special responsibility to safeguard the sustainability of the sector and to observe the shared management of highly migratory and transboundary fish stocks and should therefore be provided with effective means to act. those measures should apply to all imports of fish and fishery products of all species originating in countries that accept the existence of unsustainable fishing.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the reformed cfp should strengthen producer organisations so that they play a more significant role in the day-to-day management of fisheries under a more regionalised system, and that the creation of transnational producer organisations should be encouraged with a view to creating a level playing field for all those involved in the fisheries sector. the future cfp must also contribute positively to a dynamic development of the eu aquaculture sector to better respond to the increase in demand for fish in a context of declining wild fish stocks. the use of modern technology to improve market intelligence should be promoted in the framework of the future european fisheries and maritime fund. the proposed intervention mechanism on the eu market is limited to a single storage system. however, any system which interferes with the free market must be treated with great care and must be implemented on a cooperative basis involving all the ops and allowing the greatest possible flexibility, while protecting the interests of the marine and island regions heavily dependent on fisheries, in particular the outermost regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to strengthen and internationalise producer organisations (po), which counterbalance the power of retailers and are effective in ensuring realistic prices for the catches landed by their members.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to stress the importance of this own-initiative report as a reflection of the european parliament's (ep) opinion on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) currently under way. the commission will not vote on the regulation of the ep and the council on the reform of the cfp until next november (as is expected). however, this method of presenting 'early reports', although more laborious and potentially more time-consuming, seems to me to be quite effective in 'post-lisbon' europe, where the search for intra- and interinstitutional consensus has become paramount so that the legislative documents produced can actually see the 'light of day' within a reasonable time. that said, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the excellent work he has done and wish my colleague ulrike rodust (rapporteur on the joint regulation) the best of luck in the complex work she is doing. as a personal note on this reform, and although i am not a member of the committee on fisheries, i would just like to highlight: the absolute importance of pursuing the objective of 'balancing the three dimensions of the cfp' - social, environmental and economic; the maintenance of support for fleet renewal and the search for a more regionalised model for the management of the cfp.

in writing. - for the european union, and especially for a country like portugal, with a maritime and fishing vocation, with a strong fishing and canning industry, it is essential to maintain fishing as a viable and sustainable economic activity. portugal needs fisheries and as such it needs the sea to maintain its capacity to give us fish and for species to maintain their reproductive capacity intact. it is therefore clear to me that there must be an appropriate legal instrument to prevent behaviour which will result in a considerable depletion of fish stocks, with significant losses for fishing activity in the union.
in writing. − the european citizen, as a result of his environmental awareness, is a demanding consumer who is aware of his rights. it is therefore essential that the european union, also in this sector, adopt measures which are in breach of its marketing standards. this report, by mr struan stevenson, analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down the common organisation of the market in fishery and aquaculture products. first, very special attention should be paid to the information provided to the consumer by clear, simple but informative labelling. the citizen must know the origin of the product, the date of catch, thawing, supply chains and that its catch respects sustainable fishing practices; secondly, fishermen's organisations should be supported and sustainable fishing practices rewarded; in addition, it is necessary to promote sustainable management of fisheries resources by avoiding the capture of juvenile species and their subsequent return to the marine environment. last but not least, a fair income for fishermen must be ensured, who must be supported in stabilising stocks with a high degree of predictability.
in writing. - the current fisheries cmo is far from guaranteeing stability in fisheries markets and fair incomes for producers. in this context, a thorough and ambitious reform of the cmo was needed, strengthening public intervention and market regulation instruments with a view to ensuring the sector's income, the stability of the markets, improving the marketing of fishery products and increasing their value added, with an increase in the prices at first sale of fish. this report points to a weakening of the current cmos, dismantling some of the (few) remaining regulatory instruments. the aim is to achieve increasing liberalization and 'market orientation'. in the current context of the sector, this path will prove disastrous for numerous segments of the fleet, especially for small-scale fishing segments. we regret the rejection of many of our proposals, such as: • adopting measures to increase the price at first sale of fish, such as the introduction of maximum intermediation margins along the value chain of the sector; • introducing a 'management option' which would allow member states to retain the power to take key decisions (now vested in producer organisations) at the level of their administration. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. the common market organisation (cmo) is a key component of the common fisheries policy (cfp). in this report particular emphasis has been placed on the future role and objectives of producer organisations, which are expected to play a more significant role in fisheries management and therefore need tools to regulate the activity of their members more effectively. labelling is another key issue in this report, with the argument that the consumer has a right to better and clearer information about the fishery products he buys, in particular the dates of catch and landing. i voted in favour of this report but disagreed with the inclusion of the date of the fish catch. i believe that more important than the date of the catch is the proper conservation of the fish and the maintenance of its quality, both on board and after landing.
in writing. − in the context of the reform of the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products, special emphasis is placed on the future role and objectives of producer organisations. producer organisations should play a more significant role in the day-to-day management of fisheries, within a more regionalised system, and their internationalisation or the creation of transnational associations should be encouraged. the future common market organisation must also contribute positively to a dynamic development of the eu aquaculture sector to better respond to the increase in demand for fish in a context of declining wild fish stocks, and the use of technology should be promoted in the framework of the future european fisheries and maritime affairs fund. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − this document refers to the report to be submitted by the european commission to the european parliament and the council on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources and member states' measures to adjust fishing capacity before the end of 2012. in addition, it was also required to submit a report on the fishing restrictions in the 12 nautical mile zone by 31 december 2011. the commission considers that the efforts made by member states to improve conservation and restore stocks have been insufficient and that little progress has been made in reducing fleet capacity. the fishing limitation regime in the 12 nautical mile zone was working well and could be extended to a 10-20 mile regime. in its position, parliament states that despite the general acceptance of multiannual recovery plans, overfishing has not been sufficiently reduced. it considers that a general definition of overcapacity at european level and a specific definition at regional level is necessary. it also recognises that the principle of relative stability has led member states to focus on their national share rather than on collective long-term benefits.

this legislative initiative by the commission raises two questions. the main question is whether the union should withdraw the unilateral trade preferences enjoyed by the acp countries on a transitional basis to those countries among them which do not negotiate and ratify economic partnership agreements with the european union, as provided for in the cotonou agreement. subsidiary question: what timeframe should we give the countries concerned to negotiate and conclude the agreements in question, since the 2007 regulation unfortunately contained no deadline. the answer to the question at issue can only be a decidedly positive one. first, the 2007 regulation was obviously transitional; second, the wto waiver expired in 2007 and therefore the trade preferences in question are unlawful and in breach of the union's obligations under the world trade organisation; thirdly, to maintain these unilateral trade preferences would be unfair both to the least developed non-acp countries, which do not enjoy the same preferential treatment, and to those acp countries which have already concluded economic partnership agreements with the union. the commission also found that the commission had not provided any evidence that the measures were necessary to restore the viability of the union industry. it is a more balanced and reasonable solution in principle. on the other hand, proposals to extend this deadline even further, extending the existing illegal and unfair situation excessively, are no longer worth supporting. in short, the martin report must be approved in its entirety by this house.
