the measures to promote the recognition and protection of the quality of certain agricultural products are positive and undoubtedly play an important role both in enhancing the value of production and thus the income of producers and in informing consumers and promoting healthy consumption habits. but what quality systems cannot be is the panacea for the many problems facing agriculture and the rural world today, especially in the less developed regions. in the context of the continuation of the policies of liberalization and deregulation of agricultural product markets, it will be very difficult to ensure the continuity of many high-quality productions of great importance for the cohesion of the rural economic and social fabric. the same can be said of the persistence of policies that crush the incomes and purchasing power of the general population. there are a number of policies that need to be changed.
i congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteur on the way they have conducted this process, which has now culminated in the vote on this proposal at first reading. i hope that we will thereby contribute to greater simplification and transparency in certification systems for both producers and consumers, and that they will become less costly and more flexible to innovation. farmers will certainly continue to focus on quality, but they expect us to create the conditions necessary for them to get a fair return on their investment, bearing in mind that imposing such high production standards in terms of food safety, animal welfare and environmental sustainability has the effect of raising the final price of the product. the consumer who demands quality from the european producer ends up buying imported products of lower quality and cheaper. this is our challenge, to invest in quality, to guarantee a fair return to producers and to provide a reasonable choice to the consumer.
european agriculture offers a wide variety of food, with production methods that respect the environment and rural communities. the regional diversity of food, traditional production methods, the emphasis on safety and good environmental conditions mean that the quality of european food is one of the highest in the world, which we must reciprocally demand from third-country products entering the eu. farmers and consumers need to be aware of the special characteristics of food. this quality-oriented approach can therefore help to reward the best quality products both domestically and in international markets. these labels and quality certification schemes recognise the high value characteristics of products and also their regional specificities. the current certification schemes: pdo, pgi, gats, organic and rural products, all of which have their logos, bring a high added value for farmers and consumers. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's initiative to press the commission to make these more comprehensible and extend them to 'island products'.
the discussion on the permissible uses of orphan works should be guided by the principle of access to culture and the arts as citizens' rights and important instruments for cultural, as well as social and economic development and dynamism. the use of orphan works for non-commercial purposes can indeed be an economic and social asset for society as a whole, although we believe that the principles of copyright should be safeguarded. since there can be no direct remuneration of authors, artists or creators in the framework of orphan works, it will be essential to have compensation that reverts to copyright protection bodies or other state bodies if it is used for commercial purposes. but, again, the aim of this recognition should never be to promote the dissemination of works in the context of the deepening of the single market and competitiveness between companies, thus creating a monopoly of ownership of these works, but should be exclusively in the service of the dissemination of cultural heritage in the various member states and in the european union.

in writing. − the management of classified information is necessarily complex, and caution and description are recommended, as is a strict understanding of who should have access to it and how they use it. this problem is exacerbated when information must be passed between institutions which, by their nature, have very different structures and modes of operation. this is the case with the european parliament and the council. together they should be able to ensure that information considered to be classified in this way remains and at the same time that the right of members of the european parliament to information should not be inappropriately and disproportionately restricted. this balance between the rights to information and the reservation of information, which is necessarily unstable, must be continually assessed by the two institutions. the interinstitutional agreement is a major joint effort in this direction.

in writing. − the smart regulation programme represents a renewed opportunity for the european institutions to fully embrace good governance on the basis of a sound policy-making process in which impact assessments and ex post control play a crucial role. the aim is to consolidate efforts to better legislate, simplify eu law and reduce administrative and regulatory burdens. however, the 2003 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making has become inadequate in the current legislative framework created by the lisbon treaty. this report, which i supported, calls for the 2003 interinstitutional agreement to be renegotiated in order to adapt it to the new reality created by the lisbon treaty. it stressed the need for legislation that was clear, simple, easy to understand and accessible to all. it stresses the need for the commission to ensure the consistent application of the 'sme test' and encourages the member states to do the same in their national decision-making processes. finally, it calls for an independent study of the issue to be commissioned by the european commission, which should clarify the role of regional or local parliaments in the context of subsidiarity control.

in writing. - following the cotonou agreement, the acp countries have access to the european market with a duty exemption granted by the eu. this benefit, granted almost unilaterally, presupposes that the countries take steps to ratify the economic partnership agreements. 17 of these countries have not done so and the commission proposes that, as from 1 january 2014, those countries which have not yet signed or ratified their agreements will be removed from the list of beneficiaries. the european commission argues that the current situation is not compatible with wto rules, but is also a matter of fairness, both for those countries which have fulfilled their obligations and ratified their agreements and for developing countries which are not acp partners. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the issue should be resolved while safeguarding the underlying objective of the economic partnership agreements, which is that the agreements contribute to deepening the process of regional integration and to promoting economic growth and development in all the countries and regions concerned.
in writing. − the cotonou agreement provides for the conclusion of economic partnership agreements (epas) between the members of the acp group and the eu, known as the market access regulation, which lays down the conditions applicable from 1 january 2008 to products from the acp group. the regulation lays down the eu import regime applicable to the 36 acp countries which signed the epas in 2007. this was the provisional solution found for those countries which were not yet in a position to apply the epas awaiting ratification. the regulation in question anticipated, in a virtually unilateral manner, the duty-free access granted by the eu in those agreements. however, 17 countries have not yet ratified the agreements. the european commission therefore proposes that these countries be removed from the list of beneficiaries of the regulation as from 1 january 2014, a move which fully supports the principle of equality between countries benefiting from these exceptional trade conditions.
in writing. - the report under review, by david martin, is on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending annex i to council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 as regards the exclusion of a number of countries from the list of regions or states which have concluded negotiations. in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the preferential discrimination which the european community granted to countries with which it concluded cooperation agreements ended in 2007. in 2008, the cotonou agreement was signed, which provided for support for developing countries through certain rules. after concluding negotiations with half the acp countries, the eu, believing that all of them would sign the new agreement, adopted a regulation exempting them from paying customs duties and tariff quotas. however, some 18 countries did not sign the convention. it is therefore imperative to force these states to sign cooperation agreements with the eu as soon as possible. i agree with the commission's proposal to require that the new agreements be signed by 1 january 2014, since we cannot continue with transitional arrangements to the detriment of third parties.
in writing. - as we said during the debate in plenary, this proposal for a regulation is an unacceptable form of pressure and blackmail on the acp countries which resist - for justified reasons - signing the so-called economic partnership agreements, which are nothing more than free trade agreements between the eu and acp countries, which could have disastrous consequences for the fragile and poorly diversified economies of these countries, opening the door to the colonization of their markets and the deepening of relations of dependence and subordination at economic level. our group proposed that the proposal be simply rejected, which unfortunately was not accepted by the majority of parliament. the agreement between the socialists, greens and liberals has made it possible to postpone for two years the end of the trade preferences granted to these countries. but the idea behind this delay (which is a defeat for the european commission, which opposed it with its well-known fundamentalism in this field) is quite clear: to give the countries more time to sign the agreements. that is to say, to give the acp countries more time to continue to have the sword of damocles on their heads. this is unacceptable.
in writing. - i voted against the proposal put forward to reject outright the european commission's proposal to exclude a number of countries from trade preferences as this would have harmful consequences for those countries. although the report makes improvements to the ec proposal, i consider that it has some important negative aspects, and i therefore abstained in the final vote.
in writing. the main objective of the economic partnership agreements (epas) included in the cotonou agreements is to strengthen regional integration between acp countries and thus to enable the regions to grow and develop economically. these agreements will also be in line with wto rules. several countries have not yet completed negotiations or ratification of the epas and the ec has put forward a proposal for a regulation which would exclude countries such as haiti and mozambique from trade preferences and exemptions. i think that the date set by the ec for ratification of the epas, 1 january 2014, is quite short, since we have to take into account the particular characteristics of these countries. we have the example of haiti, which is still suffering from the aftermath of the 2010 earthquake, or regions in the african continent where regional integration and stable relations between states are sometimes non-existent. moreover, many of the agreements concluded in 2007 were concluded with countries rather than with regions. for these reasons, i am in favour of extending the deadline until january 2016, given the importance of the negotiations in question.

in writing. - the economic and financial crisis in which we are living forces us to pay special attention to social issues. maximising the existing financial resources is the watchword. we have to do more with the same or even less. social enterprises are an example in this field. they also create social links through the integration policy of people with problems and those in need. i welcome the adoption of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european social entrepreneurship funds. for the first time we have a european regulation on social entrepreneurship to support companies that pursue social objectives and implement innovative programmes. we must not forget that 10% of european companies are active in the social field, which is fundamental to the european economy. we are faced with a text which aims, on the one hand, to promote development based on solidarity and, on the other, to diversify the sources of financing for social enterprises, which are currently financed mainly by subsidies.
in writing. − this proposal, together with the proposal on european venture capital funds, is designed to promote and finance projects of social interest within the framework of the commission's social business initiative. the aim is to harmonize the means of access to and redistribution of funds for social entrepreneurship by creating a mechanism to link companies with interested investors, the composition of the portfolio of such funds, the investment instruments to be used and the categories of eligible investors. it should be noted that these enterprises, usually smes, account for 10% of european enterprises and employ some 11 million people, making it essential not only to harmonise the new rules but also to ensure that investors and enterprises are properly informed. i would like to congratulate my colleague, sophie auconie, on her excellent work in an area which can make a major contribution to the creation of more smes.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation establishes the legal framework under which the different types of investment funds can obtain the status of 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and the corresponding 'passport'. its objective is to create a european sector for investment in legal persons engaged in non-profit-making activities aimed at achieving various social objectives. i agree that funding for social enterprises should be increased, using all available resources, including private ones. however, the current trend is that public investment in these matters is increasingly being replaced by private funds that are less stable and profit-oriented to the detriment of social impacts. i have some reservations in this respect that this regulation should not become another step towards privatisation and/or external contracting in areas which are the responsibility of the state. for these reasons i abstained.
in writing. the final vote on this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european social entrepreneurship funds has been postponed. the regulation does not call into question existing national arrangements for investing in social entrepreneurship but complements those arrangements at union level.
in writing. − in october 2011, the european commission presented a proposal for european social entrepreneurship funds (esfs) which aims to support the social enterprise market by improving the effectiveness of mobilising investment funds targeted at such enterprises. according to eurostat, in july 2012, the european union had an unemployment rate of 10,4%, while in the eurozone the unemployment rate reached 11,3%. the eu-27 thus had 25.2 million unemployed, of whom some 18.1 million were in the euro zone. i believe that it is essential to take measures to tackle this social scourge affecting thousands of people, and social entrepreneurship is a good solution, given that social enterprises cover a wide range of entities whose main objective is solidarity. i agree with this report which sets out uniform rules on the nature of esi funds, in particular on the portfolio companies in which esi funds are allowed to invest and which investment instruments to use.
in writing. − this regulation aims to create uniform rules for the financing process of social enterprises, in the framework of the european commission's social entrepreneurship initiative (2011). the aim of the regulation was to create funds which, by having the same rules, could increase investor confidence in investing in such funds. the definition of 'social enterprises' covers a 'wide range of enterprises with different legal forms, which provide social goods or services to vulnerable or marginalised people' including all enterprises 'which use a mode of production of goods and services that pursue a social objective'. while these funds may be useful for financing the so-called third sector, i.e. collective management companies such as cooperatives, it cannot be overemphasized that in a context where the troika (integrated by the ec and the ecb) encourages states to publicly divest and privatise public services, this solution presents a perversion in that the eu supports the transfer of social services to the private sphere, dismantling the social role and public assets, while at the same time supporting the financing of private companies to replace public services.
in writing. − this proposal, presented together with the social entrepreneurship fund, aims to implement efficiently in the european union a financing model for companies which, at a very early stage, have an ambitious business model. the aim is to create the conditions for investors with venture capital funds to do so in accordance with the participation requirements, for example by allowing them to benefit from a european passport, and thus boost the financing of smes.
in writing. - this report analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european venture capital funds. the economic and financial crisis requires us to pay particular attention to the question of investment. maximising the existing financial resources is the watchword. we have to do more of the same! for a long time, some economists argued that finance was not used to boost the economy and support businesses. no one thinks that today. we must put finance at the service of people in order to boost the economy, economic growth and job creation. if each of the 22 million small and mediumsized enterprises in europe were supported in creating a job, we would have solved the problem of unemployment in the eu. for this, venture capital is very important. i welcome the fact that the eu now has a new legislative framework unique across europe that will make it easier to raise money from donors, which will be essential to get us out of the current crisis. finally, i would like to draw attention to the need to step up the fight against tax evasion and the flow of money to tax havens.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation lays down the legal framework under which the different types of investment funds can obtain the status of 'european venture capital fund' and a 'passport' for venture capital funds. its objective is to create a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises. while it is true that financing for smes is problematic in the union, the solution cannot be to rely solely on private funds which are primarily aimed at making a profit, thus relieving the state of its responsibilities to support growth and employment. i abstained.

in writing. − at a time when the capital available by banks to support business investment is becoming scarcer, other sources of finance are becoming more prevalent. in this sense, venture capital funds provide financing to companies, generally very small, which are in the early stages of their development and which show a strong potential for growth and expansion. i support this report because i believe that venture capital funds provide companies with valuable inputs in terms of knowledge and skills, contribute to job creation and capital raising, foster the creation and expansion of innovative companies, increase their investment in research and development and promote entrepreneurship, innovation and competitiveness in line with the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. i believe that the process of setting up a european venture capital fund should be speeded up as quickly as possible in order to alleviate the costs of introducing new funds into the market.
in writing. − the objective of this regulation is to create a european venture capital investment sector targeted at small and medium-sized enterprises. the express purpose of the capital funds is 'to provide financing to companies, generally very small, which are in the early stages of their development'. sme financing is undoubtedly a real need and one that must be met. in portugal, however, the growing difficulties faced by smes are the result of the continued policy of public disinvestment and the increase in recessive austerity policies. the problems of portuguese smes are the result of a policy of abandonment and destruction of our production and productive apparatus, of an internal market strangled by the ever-decreasing purchasing power of workers, of a tax policy which penalizes work and small enterprises. privatizations, which have placed in the hands of large economic groups, energy, banking, telecommunications or transport companies, suppliers of essential goods and services at monopoly prices, are one of the causes of the economic strangulation of smes. this is the policy that needs to be reversed and which led to 46.7% more companies declaring bankruptcy in the first half of the year than in the same period of 2011.

in writing. − in march 2011, following a difficult process, the european commission signed a trade agreement with colombia and peru. many social forces in these two countries and in europe opposed this agreement. countries such as bolivia and ecuador have decided to abandon the negotiations, accusing the eu of wanting nothing more than a free trade agreement. as a matter of fact, it is. the consequences - profoundly negative - will be felt on both sides of the atlantic. in the banana sector, the agreements anticipate the damage to european producers. they therefore provide for a safeguard clause which, as experience has shown, will not prevent such damage. the opinion of parliament's committee on agriculture itself recognizes this. there are several weaknesses in this clause. with unacceptable hypocrisy and intolerable cynicism (for those who, after all, endorsed the agreement), it is proposed (as the commission has done) to extend the globalisation adjustment fund to these farmers, recognising the doom to ruin they have decreed. portugal, and in particular the autonomous region of madeira, where banana production is of considerable importance, will also be affected.

in writing. − on 19 january 2009, the council authorised the commission to open trade negotiations with the andean community member countries, which eventually led to a trade agreement with colombia and peru. the agreement was initialled on 23 march 2011 and signed on 26 june 2012. the agreement provides for the reduction and elimination of customs duties in bilateral trade between the partners. it also contains a safeguard clause under which tariff preferences may be suspended or removed if such trade liberalisation causes an unexpected increase in imports, harming the position of european industry competing with those imports and affecting employment in the european producing sector, as may happen in the weaker economies of the outermost regions.
in writing. − bananas are one of the main export products of several ibero-american countries to the european union and are of enormous importance to their economies. despite the european desire to contribute to the stability, progress and development of exporting countries, it is worth remembering that bananas are also produced in the union. it is of the highest quality and comes from the outermost regions whose economies, because of their specific circumstances, deserve particular attention and protection from european decision-makers. the agreements concluded for this product must take account of this and provide for mechanisms to protect european interests. i hope that it will not be necessary to use it, but i recognize the need and the desirability of guarding against this need.

in writing. the european commission has signed a free trade agreement with six central american countries - costa rica, el salvador, guatemala, honduras, nicaragua and panama. this agreement liberalises trade in certain agricultural products in whole or in part. the banana is the main agricultural product in all these countries' exports, and the american multinationals are the main producers, in vast areas of monoculture where the working conditions of local peasants are close to slavery. for these reasons, numerous organizations have denounced the social, labour and environmental dumping resulting from this agreement, and more generally from free trade and the subjection of agriculture to the rules of the world trade organization. the safeguard clause and the stability mechanism proposed here will be worthless. the weaknesses of the cap are numerous and its ineffectiveness is pointed out in the opinion of the committee on agriculture itself. the stabilisation mechanism will not be automatic, since the european commission will be free to apply it or not. parliament here acknowledges its inability (and we add: unwillingness) to oppose the commission, despite all the propaganda that has been made about its increased role in trade policy.

in writing. − on 23 april 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with certain central american countries. the negotiations, concluded at the eu-latin america summit in madrid in may 2010, led to an agreement establishing an association between the eu and central america, initialled on 22 march 2011 and signed in tegucigalpa on 29 june 2012. the council approved its celebration on 10 july 2012. the agreement includes a bilateral safeguard clause providing for the possibility of reintroducing the most-favoured-nation tariff rate in cases where, as a result of trade liberalisation resulting from the agreement, imports are made in such increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause, or threaten to cause, serious injury to union producers producing similar products or in direct competition, as is the case in the outermost regions, in particular as regards the banana sector.

in writing. - with the extraordinary technological progress of recent years, access to culture has changed radically. today, people can read on their mobile phones, tablets and e-readers, and the relationship of citizens to books is not the same as it was 10 years ago. that is why i think it is relevant and important to make available, through online access at european level, works for which not all the rights holders have been identified (orphan works). this is a step towards preserving and disseminating the diversity of european culture, making it accessible to all.
in writing. - man is a social being who has always lived in society and can only survive in society. this implies that there are standards of conduct and laws to be observed. the truth is, we live in a society where everything is regulated. the report by mrs lidia joanna geringer from oedenberg deals with the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the use of works which are 'orphan', i.e. whose author or authors are unknown. in fact, thousands of works are lying in national, municipal, castle and other archives, with no possibility of being disclosed without the knowledge of the intellectual property rights holder. the proposal for a directive under consideration aims to address this issue through a new legislative framework. i welcome the adoption of this proposal because, thanks to digitisation and dissemination via the internet, it is possible to make this work available to the public concerned without any fear of the appearance of its author, thus avoiding its destruction while promoting the identification of its authors. i voted in favour and i consider that this is a measure of great cultural and scientific significance.

in writing. − the discussion on the permissible uses of orphan works should be guided by the principle of access to culture and the arts as citizens' rights and important instruments for cultural, as well as social and economic development and dynamism. the use of orphan works, not for commercial purposes but for political dissemination, could thus constitute an economic and social asset for society as a whole. however, we fear that the purpose of this recognition is to promote the dissemination of works in the context of the deepening of the single market and competitiveness between companies, creating a monopoly on the marketing of these works, creating a lucrative business for the large digital distribution companies.

in writing. − at the european council on 28 and 29 june, euro area leaders agreed on the need to move towards a strengthened economic and monetary union, i.e. the need to complete the legal framework for economic and monetary union (emu). they also agreed, as i have been advocating, that to achieve this final stage of emu, it will be necessary to work on four essential pillars: a banking union, a budgetary union, an economic union and a political union. the european commission has therefore put forward a proposal yesterday to move towards a banking union which, despite its merits, is based on article 127 (6) tfeu. the article in question is designed to limit the european parliament's participation in the drafting of this piece of legislation, forgetting one of the pillars which the european leaders have set themselves: that of political union and democratic legitimacy. it is therefore essential that the participation of the only democratic european body be reviewed immediately.
in writing. - over the past few months, several voices from european policy makers, starting with the president of the european commission, mr barroso, have warned of the need to move urgently towards a strengthened economic and monetary union on the path towards the already established economic and monetary union. now, durão barroso is moving forward with a new proposal: the creation of a european banking union not just for eurozone countries, but for those outside the eurozone who wish to cooperate. the strength of the euro implies the existence of union-wide supervision, guaranteed by this new legislative framework and implemented by the ecb. this would ensure that citizens' deposits are protected and that, in the event of a financial institution going bankrupt, it is not the taxpayers who pay for it, as is the case today. i voted in favour of this proposal because it responds to the main challenges facing the euro area: to end the banking sector's link to sovereign debt and to create a single and effective european supervisory mechanism that will support the member states. there will also be a single book on banking, which should apply to the 27 member states.
in writing. the majority of this parliament wants banking supervision to be transferred from the national authorities to the ecb. it wants this sector, which is fundamental to the financing of national economies, to be moved from being directly controlled by the states to being directly determined by the ecb. the ecb, without any political and democratic control, has fulfilled the triple role of hindering the refinancing of large capital by promoting the dependence of the states for its financing , of the financial sector (the so-called markets) and of promoting the exploitation of workers by covering the loss of purchasing power of wages by credit. countries such as portugal, which have no currency and cannot intervene autonomously in monetary policy, are also limited in the regulation of the financial sector. what economies like portugal need to grow is the nationalisation of commercial banking, putting it at the service of the national economy. portugal needs a public bank to finance the increase in national production and a reindustrialization programme, a fundamental instrument for creating jobs with rights, raising wages, reducing the country's external dependence, and thus solving the problems of the deficit and public debt.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which proposes a concrete step towards solving the current problems of the european economy.
in writing. − several eu member states are facing a serious financial crisis, most often caused by the lack of existing banking supervision which has led to the approval of support mechanisms by national governments. greece, ireland and portugal have received large amounts to support their banking systems, demonstrating that there is a widespread problem in the european banking sector and that action at european level is urgently needed. in this respect, i am in favour of creating a banking union in which the european central bank is the sole body responsible for banking supervision, and there should also be greater transparency and accountability of these institutions to the european parliament. finally, i support the existing proposals on capital requirements for the banking sector, deposit guarantee and bank resolution which aim to ensure greater sustainability of banking in the medium and long term.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to begin my remarks this afternoon by welcoming the agreement reached between the council and parliament on this important issue. the designation of 2013 as the european year of citizens is an important signal that we want to increase public awareness of the rights and responsibilities of citizens across the european union. we hope, in particular, that it will highlight the rights of citizens to move and reside freely within the european union. these issues are all the more important in the run-up to the european elections of 2014. it was this parliament which first proposed this initiative at the end of 2010. at that time you highlighted the need to stimulate discussion on union citizenship and to inform union citizens of their rights, in particular those resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. we are happy that the idea was taken up and moved forward by commissioner reding. the treaty on european union first introduced the concept of citizenship of the union, so next year will mark the 20th anniversary. it is therefore particularly appropriate that 2013 will be designated as the year of citizens. the cyprus presidency, building on the work of the danish presidency, was able to conclude negotiations on this proposal in the first few weeks of its term in office. i would like to thank in particular the rapporteur, mrs papadopoulou, for her enthusiasm for this initiative and for her willingness to negotiate in such a cooperative manner with the council. i welcome the vote that will be taking place this week on this proposal and have no doubt that the initiative will be strongly endorsed by this parliament. the general objective of the european year of citizens in 2013 is to enhance awareness and knowledge of the rights – but also of the responsibilities – attached to union citizenship. as is clear from the legal basis chosen by the commission, the proposal aimed first and foremost to help citizens to make full use of their right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. however, in the context of free movement, the european year will also provide an opportunity to promote other rights. the free movement of persons is one of the four basic freedoms, but at the same time there is clearly also a way to bridge the gap between what the rules state and how they operate in practice. citizens still encounter difficulties when moving to another member state, whether as workers, students, entrepreneurs, job seekers or consumers. it is therefore essential that all citizens are fully aware of their legal rights. this initiative will also provide an opportunity to raise awareness of other rights related to free movement, such as the right to vote and stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament and in local elections in the member state of residence, the right to petition the european parliament, the right to apply to the european ombudsman and the right to address eu institutions, as well as a wide range of other rights, such as the free movement of goods and services, consumer protection and public health, equal opportunities and equal treatment. we very much hope that this proposal will play an important role in encouraging and empowering citizens to uphold their right to engage actively at european level, not least in view of the 2014 european elections. of course, the european year of citizens is not a one-off event. it now needs to seek the launch of a longer-term process of building awareness and encouraging participation. i know this parliament has a pivotal role in ensuring that this is the case. we also look forward to the 2013 european union citizenship report, which will assess progress in this area and propose further initiatives to remove the obstacles which prevent citizens from fully enjoying their rights. this is an important decision which serves the interest of all our citizens. all of us – this parliament as well as our own national governments and parliaments – have a role in helping to increase awareness of what it means to be a citizen of the european union. we are ready to play our role. i have no doubt that the european parliament will be very active, not just in 2013 but also beyond, in highlighting this message. thank you for your attention.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, on behalf of the commission i wish to thank very much the rapporteur, mrs papadopoulou, and the members of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and all the committees involved in shaping what is now, finally, a solid basis for compromise in this area that should suit all parties. the european year of citizens 2013 will take place in a very special context, as next year also marks the 20th anniversary of eu citizenship, as introduced by the maastricht treaty. this is an opportunity to illustrate, with concrete examples, the benefits of eu citizenship in the daily lives of students, residents, tourists, workers, private individuals and businesses. the commission is ready to provide the second so-called ‘citizenship report’ on how to remove the remaining obstacles and barriers which make it difficult, in daily life, for european citizens to move around europe. the year also falls on the eve of the european elections. therefore, it is a good opportunity to remind people that participation is legally possible wherever citizens may reside in the european union. as mentioned already, this is a matter of raising awareness of the real value of citizenship, going beyond participation in the democratic life of the european union, as already described on many occasions, to the rights to consular protection and to petition the european parliament, address the institutions and apply to the ombudsman. last but not least, this is an opportunity to highlight the prerogatives of this assembly, which is an assembly of people elected by the people. i am happy now that we have a solid basis between the institutions, and i am sure that together we can make the european year of citizens a real success.

mr president, the european union's development policy is in fact in need of substantial changes, first of all it lacks sufficient means, at least in line with the commitments it has made and the objectives it has set at international level, particularly in the framework of the un, and it lacks the changes that would make it possible for the developing countries to better appropriate the aid that promotes their sovereign development. we are concerned about trends and directions such as a shift from budget support and public subsidies to so-called blending mechanisms which weaken and distort aid and introduce uncertainty where predictability is needed. we are also concerned about the imposition, under the guise of so-called good governance, of practices and policies in a number of areas such as economic organization, taxation, justice and others, policies which must be the result of the choices and options of developing countries, taking into account their specific situation and conditions and not being exported from europe. finally, much more in-depth consideration is needed of the question of whether sectoral policies are consistent with development objectives or not.
mr president, the european leaders continue to insist on budgetary discipline and i ask, budgetary discipline, so let us get to it, because what exactly are we talking about when we talk about budgetary discipline? i believe that budgetary discipline means respecting the contracts with pensioners and not abandoning the commitments of the state halfway, i believe that budgetary discipline means respecting the contracts of those who work and not inventing extraordinary taxes or cuts in subsidies, budgetary discipline means respecting commitments in health, education and culture and not closing down services or closing down and cancelling projects halfway, discipline means putting the banks in order and not taking from the taxpayers to put it in the hands of speculators to save their banks. this is the budgetary discipline i would like to see implemented in the european union and we should not continue with this market party. if we need an example, the budget being discussed in portugal under the auspices of the troika is the perfect example, it violates all the commitments that any state must have to its citizens not to violate the agreements made behind closed doors that are ruining europe and its countries.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is not very encouraging to speak to an empty room at this time of night. however, even if it is just for the record, for the record, let me present my report on economic and trade relations with the united states of america. this report was approved by a large majority in the committee on international trade. as the permanent rapporteur of the committee on international trade for economic and trade relations with the united states, i am personally very pleased with the content of this report. firstly, because it sends a strong message of support for deepening economic and trade relations between the union and the united states, and secondly because the report sets out the most important elements of offensive and defensive action for the union without, however, setting preconditions for the opening of negotiations. the report is primarily political in nature. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. this report seeks to answer two crucial questions. firstly, does a trade and investment treaty between the union and the united states make sense? the answer to this question is almost unanimously yes. first, all the existing studies and analyses show the enormous growth potential that mutual liberalisation of trade and investment would bring to both sides. second, both economies face common challenges that can only be properly addressed together, rather than separately. among them are the low growth they suffer from, the eruption of new emerging economies, particularly china, the growing protectionism in some relevant economies like argentina, brazil, russia, south africa. thirdly, since the doha round for a multilateral treaty on global trade openness has failed, the only way to do this is through bilateral channels. secondly, will it be possible to reach an agreement between the united states and the european union within a reasonable time? let's start by saying, right now, that it's not going to be an easy task. there are considerable divergences of interest in some important areas, especially in agriculture and in air and sea transport, to name just two examples. there are important regulatory divergences from technical standards, for example in the automobile sector. there are deep-rooted cultural differences such as the one between the european precautionary approach to food and environmental safety and the american risk-based approach. there are a number of irritating elements, for example, genetically modified organisms (gmos), meat from the offspring of cloned animals, again, just to name two examples. it is simply that these difficulties, although great, are not insurmountable and should not, even less, be regarded as obstacles to a successful agreement. first, there must be agreement, especially since it covers all sectors and removes most barriers to trade and investment; secondly, the advantages at stake in such an agreement are so great that it is worth making the mutual concessions necessary to reap the benefits of substantial trade and investment liberalisation between the two parties. i therefore invite parliament to support my report so that parliament's voice can be heard now and taken into account in the initiatives of the commission and the council on this matter.
mr president, the single european sky project is, from the outset, inseparable from the intention to liberalize the air transport sector. the underlying vision is not the development of the sector according to a logic of the prevalence of the public interest, but rather the alignment of airspace management with the interests of the large airlines and the monopolistic concentration taking place in the sector. the arguments which have been advanced over the years in favour of a single european sky are subsidiary to this objective and are without foundation, whether in terms of safety, employment or environmental issues. it is in the context of public ownership and management of the sector that all these issues can best be balanced and not in the context of the liberalisation which they want to promote at all costs. let us not forget the steps that have been taken and those that can still be taken to achieve better coordination and better use of airspace, while maintaining the sovereignty of each member state over its national airspace, an essential issue for the defence of the specific interests of each country, whether in the field of commercial aviation or in the field of defence.

mr president, how is it possible that the european council did not pay any attention to the imf’s admission of errors in calculating fiscal multipliers and the impact of austerity, with the consequent tragic costs in terms of the recession endured directly by the peoples of portugal, ireland, greece, spain and italy, and the indirect weakening of the eurozone and the union’s economic outlook as a whole? how come the commission, which is supposed to be the promoter of european interests and which is part of the troikas in bailout countries, is not pressing those troikas to reassess the adjustment programmes in the light of these mistakes, which have been admitted by the imf, and of director lagarde’s clear recommendations to allow more time and reasonable interest, in order for those countries to adjust? how can the council and commission continue to insist on ‘perpetual imprisonment in austerity’, as french president françois hollande has so rightly put it, for eu bailout countries, which has such dangerous economic and political consequences for the whole of the european union?
in writing. at a time when we are still suffering the effects of the economic and financial crisis, it is understandable that the european council has focused on economic issues, in particular the need to invest in growth and job creation and the need to deepen economic and monetary union. it is imperative to restore european competitiveness, encourage investment and create jobs, and the number of unemployed in the eu is already around 25 million. we therefore need a growth-oriented budget. it is also essential to restore confidence in the euro area and to ensure the eu's long-term stability by ensuring economic convergence. but it is not just emu that needs a boost, the union of citizens and the creation of a common european identity in an area without internal frontiers are also under threat. we must urgently reach a compromise here too, because the europe of which we are proud is not limited to the common market, it goes far beyond that, putting people first in european policies. i regret that in all these areas the council has simply repeated decisions already taken and postponed others, without bringing hope to the european citizens.
in writing. this meeting marks an unmistakable deepening of the economic, social, political and institutional crisis in which the eu is plunged. the repetitive and tedious formulation of guidelines and proclamations - on growth, employment, reforms, consolidation, the single market and other trash that is a regular presence in the conclusions of the european council meetings - does not hide the growing tensions and contradictions, especially those that oppose germany to france, spain and italy, among others. in the face of the massive destruction of productive forces, unprecedented levels of unemployment and the prospect of severe and prolonged recessions, there is growing disagreement about the extent (and location) of this destructive process. the contradictions surrounding the banking supervision mechanism and the direct financing of banks by the esm are a clear example of this. against this background, attacks on the rights and sovereignty of peoples and on democracy itself continue. after economic governance and the fiscal compact/budgetary treaty, the idea arises of concluding contracts between the states and the european institutions, obliging the former to comply with a previously agreed reform plan, in line with the recommendations of the european semester. despite the differences, a concertation determined by class interests still prevails, aimed at intensifying the exploitation and theft of workers and peoples.
the last european council in brussels had the opportunity to discuss three subjects considered central to the future of the european union, namely the growth pact and economic and monetary union. the council also referred to the difficult economic and financial situation in greece. i am in favour of the rapid implementation of the new growth and employment package worth eur 120 billion, the capital increase of the european investment bank by eur 10 billion, the adoption of the transeuropean networks in the field of energy and transport, the deepening of the internal market or the strengthening of the amounts for research and innovation or industrial competitiveness. i also criticise the lack of agreement between the member states on the entry into force of economic and monetary union, and it has been decided that the european central bank will only strengthen its powers in the area of supervision of all european banks next year. i would also like to stress that if any member state receiving external financial support can make the adjustment period more flexible, or if the amounts of bank recapitalisation do not affect the budget deficit, all other countries should be entitled to exactly the same treatment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as in the light of article 9 of the protocol and the relevant provisions of the rules of procedure of the european parliament and of the austrian constitution, the committee on legal affairs has concluded that there is no reason not to waive the immunity of mr martin ehrenhauser.
in writing. − this report, by bernhard rapkay, concerns the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of martin ehrenhauser mep following a request made on 21 march 2011 by the public prosecutor's office in vienna, austria. the prosecutor's office intends to bring proceedings against the mep, who is suspected of illegally accessing a computer system, thus violating the austrian penal code in relation to the secrecy of communications, improper interception of data, use of a communications interception device and data protection offences. the prosecutor's office, on the basis of statements and a set of documents from another mep, suspects that martin ehrenhauser illegally accessed hans-peter martin's private e-mail system, copying and disclosing his private and professional data. in this connection, and in view of the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs recommending the waiver of mr martin ehrenhauser's parliamentary immunity, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. the request for waiver of immunity is made by the public prosecutor's office in order to allow the austrian authorities to carry out investigations and bring criminal proceedings against martin ehrenhauser. the request for the waiver of the immunity of martin ehrenhauser concerns a suspicion of an offence relating to unlawful access to a computer system pursuant to article 118oa of the austrian criminal code, of an infringement of the secrecy of communications pursuant to article 119 of the austrian criminal code, of an improper interception of data pursuant to article 119oa of the austrian criminal code, of an improper use of a recorder or an interception device for the interception of communications pursuant to article 120 (2) of the austrian criminal code, and of an infringement of article 51 of the data protection act 2000. so i'm in favor of lifting the immunity of martin ehrenhauser.
in writing. - the european parliament was asked to waive the parliamentary immunity of mr martin ehrenhauser, mep, in an action for unlawful access to a computer system under article 118a of the austrian criminal code, for breach of the secrecy of communications under article 119 of the austrian criminal code, for misuse of data interception under article 119 of the austrian criminal code, for misuse of a recorder or a device for intercepting communications under article 120 (2) of the austrian criminal code, and for breach of article 51 of the data protection act 2000. considering that the facts of this case, as presented in the documents submitted to the committee on legal affairs, do not indicate that the alleged events have a direct and obvious connection with the performance by martin ehrenhauser of his duties as a member of the european parliament, it was decided to waive the parliamentary immunity. on the basis of these arguments, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the request for the waiver of the immunity of mr martin ehrenhauser, member of the european parliament, since the vienna public prosecutor's office intends to bring proceedings against him, given the suspicions contained in this report.

in writing. − the delicate situation of national economies reinforces the role that the eu budget should play: primarily as an instrument to support these economies. in this context, the eu budget must be approached carefully and responsibly, given the importance of its implementation. the council also adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, which calls for the immediate release of all political prisoners and the immediate release of all political prisoners. it may be possible to reduce some appropriations in some categories of the draft budget, but if we agree with the council's reading, the eu will risk not honouring its debts. i do not want to make the mistake of appearing inflexible about the council's strategy, and i am aware that the eu's institutional credibility is at stake, but i cannot help but say that the response to the crisis must be 'more europe' and not 'less europe'. i therefore support the commission's draft budget which follows parliament's priorities for programmes and initiatives to be taken into account in order to achieve these objectives. therefore, the priorities for the 2013 budget should be to support sustainable growth, competitiveness and employment, in particular for smes and young people.

in writing. - this report, drawn up by mr giovanni la via and mr derek vaughan, concerns the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013 - all sections. it regrets the council's position, which has once again given us the usual approach of horizontal cuts in the draft budget. in fact, the council, in response to the commission proposal, cut eur 1 155 million in appropriations for commitments (da) and eur 5 228 million in appropriations for payments (pd). this cut in payment appropriations would lead to the need for amending budgets next year, a practice which leads to instability and demonstrates a lack of rigor. the mff is coming to an end and the concentration of project implementation in the member states is leading to an increase in the funds needed to pay for projects. i therefore support the ep's strategy of providing sufficient funds for payment expenditure, particularly in the area of sustainable growth, competitiveness and employment, smes and youth.
in writing. − the adoption of the european parliament's position on the eu budget for 2013 repeats the strategy of previous years. the majority in this parliament is confined to the traditional institutional game in which the initial differences eventually fade and the three institutions (ep, commission and council) and the political forces that dominate them always agree on the fundamental: to reduce the eu budget. the justified concern about the likely shortage of funds to deal with debts already incurred in several programmes and the fact that 2013 is the last year of the current multiannual financial framework does not hide the complicity of the majority of parliament in the deepening of social and inter-country asymmetries, rampant unemployment and the huge increase in poverty in the eu. the majority in parliament is limited to cosmetic and other purely propaganda changes, keeping the main guidelines and priorities of the eu budget unchanged, making it manifestly insufficient in the face of the urgency of countries like portugal in this period of deep economic and social crisis. the basis for negotiation between parliament and the council is far below existing needs and even below the figure set in the multiannual financial framework (1.15% of gni).
in writing. − the eu's general budget for 2013 should have as priorities, as detailed in its abovementioned resolution of 4 july 2012 on the mandate for the trilogue, support for sustainable growth, competitiveness and employment, especially for smes and young people. in my view, the commission's draft budget reflects parliament's priorities as regards the programmes and initiatives to be strengthened to achieve these objectives. we are all aware of the serious difficulties caused by the state of national economies and the need for a responsible and realistic reading, but we cannot accept the approach whereby the eu budget becomes the basis for possible savings in the same proportion and logic as is applied to national budgets, given the substantial difference in their nature, objectives and structure. the reduction of eu resources could result in a lack of investment and liquidity in the member states which will exacerbate the problems they face, and that is what we cannot allow to happen.
in writing. − in voting on the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013, i voted in favour of an amendment to remove the subsidy for tobacco cultivation. i believe that the maintenance of these aids to tobacco production is inconsistent and incompatible with the union's health policy and with the objectives of reducing tobacco consumption, especially among young people. the money you waste could be used instead to fight smoking and the evils of tobacco. i also voted in favour of an amendment to exclude bulls specially bred for participation in bullfighting from the payment of premiums for beef production. first, the rearing of those animals is essentially motivated by objectives which are outside the scope of beef production and must therefore be considered to be outside the scope of the payment of that premium. on the other hand, i believe that subsidising the breeding of these animals means encouraging and promoting a barbaric and degrading spectacle which is offensive to the values of present-day society.

in writing. the committee on budgets of the european parliament has decided to adopt a budget with eur 151.2 billion in commitment appropriations and eur 137.9 billion in payment appropriations. those figures represent an increase of 2,2% and 6,82%, respectively, compared to the union budget in 2012. the budget adopted by the committee on budgets restored all the budget cuts proposed by the council in the amounts allocated to cohesion for growth and employment. the amounts entered under the heading of cohesion for growth and jobs are of paramount importance in view of the economic and financial situation in the member states. the adopted budget for the european union will support smes and respond in a more robust and articulated way to youth unemployment and allow alignment of cohesion policy with the europe 2020 objectives. the regions, especially those in countries under the imf, ecb and ec structural adjustment programmes, will benefit from an important crisis-fighting tool, as this budget will address the lack of investment in them. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − this interim report aims to facilitate and accelerate the adoption of the mff for the period 2014-2020. european citizens place great hope in the achievement of the priorities set out in the europe 2020 strategy: smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. only then will it be possible to overcome the crisis and develop the european economy. in this context, i would stress the importance of cohesion policy. all the studies show its added value. in the face of the enormous disparities between eu regions, the need to maintain this policy is clear and it should never be the adjustment measure for other policies such as those resulting from the eu 2020 flagship initiatives. cohesion policy is the only policy that can simultaneously contribute to the 5 eu 2020 objectives in the areas of education, research and innovation, climate change, employment and the fight against poverty. the eu budget depends on more than 80% of direct contributions from national budgets. this leads each member state to seek a 'juste retour' and leads to an unhealthy distinction between net contributors and recipients. that is why it is important to have real own resources. the eu should therefore seek other revenue such as the application of a financial transaction tax and vat revenue in the manner proposed by the commission.
in writing. - this report is yet another expression of the support of the majority in parliament for a path of successive budget cuts as advocated by the major eu powers - the major beneficiaries of the single market and the policies and guidelines in place. they say they want to influence the negotiations on the next financial framework, but there are a number of points - as in the case of cohesion policy - on which they support the council's unacceptable positions. the majority supports the subordination of the eu budget to the eu 2020 strategy (orientation towards privatisation, liberalisation and the destruction of public services) and the foreseeable transfer of funds from the cohesion fund to the deepening of the single market through the 'connecting europe' mechanism, transferring public money to large transport networks which, in the context of the prevailing relations within the eu, will accentuate the dependence and subordination of countries such as portugal in the face of the great powers, which will not only have the outflow of their production facilitated, but also access to the resources of our country. we, for our part, support the need to increase the community budget to at least double the present amount, reinforcing its redistributive function.
in writing. − i am aware that the negotiations on the mff for the period 2014-2020 are taking place in a very adverse social, economic and financial context, in which member states are making considerable efforts to adjust their national budgets with a view to the sustainability of public finances and the stability of the banking sector and the single currency. i believe, however, that the eu budget is part of the solution that will enable europe to overcome the present crisis by promoting investment in growth and jobs and by helping member states to tackle, collectively and in a concerted way, the current structural challenges, namely the loss of competitiveness and the increase in unemployment and poverty. we therefore need to present a mff 2014-2020 that upholds the objectives set out in the eu 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, namely promoting employment, improving conditions and increasing public spending in the fields of innovation and research and development, meeting our climate change and energy objectives, improving education levels and promoting social inclusion, in particular through poverty reduction.

in writing. the report stresses the political importance of the european union budget in overcoming the economic crisis by ensuring the necessary level of financial investment throughout the union. the mff negotiations are taking place in a difficult context, in which only european concepts of solidarity and mutual assistance can help member states to tackle, collectively and in concert, the structural challenges facing europe: loss of competitiveness, rising unemployment and poverty. however, the commission's proposals represent a budget freeze for the mff and are therefore deficient. the report also calls for the council to clearly and publicly disclose which eu projects and priorities should be abandoned. i voted in favour of this interim report because we all depend on the leverage effect of the eu budget to trigger and catalyse actions with clear added value in boosting growth and employment which the member states alone are not capable of delivering.

in writing. − revenues from the european union (eu) budget come to more than 80% of the gni-based share of member states (ms) directly from their national budgets. this means that, contrary to the treaties, the eu budget is not financed from genuine own resources. this leads to the logic of the 'juste retour' and the undesirable distinction between net contributors and recipients. the new challenges and commitments of the eu in tackling the crisis and delivering on the europe 2020 strategy led the commission, on 29 june 2011, when presenting the proposals for the new multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020, to include a set of proposals on the reform of the eu's own financial resources system, which envisages the abolition of the vat own resource as it stands and its replacement by an eu vat. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr dehaene because i believe that the new eu vat, being more transparent, stable and reliable, is a step forward in the reform of eu resources and a way of lowering the contribution of each member state.
in writing. - we strongly disagree with the proposal of the majority in parliament to reform the own resources system to include a new 'eu vat' as an 'own resource'. we are faced with a federalist proposal which is a gross manipulation based on the false 'reduction of the share of contributions from the member states'. as is their custom, the majority in parliament do evil and make a mess of things. it is trying to take advantage of the serious economic and social crisis facing countries like portugal (in which the eu has a great deal of responsibility) to advocate a shift from a system of contributions based, above all, on the product of each country, to a system that will increasingly be based on the most blind and unjust of all taxes, vat, penalizing the weakest and most unprotected. this proposal is all the more manipulative because, by invoking 'the consolidation efforts of the member states', it seeks to create the idea of inevitability. but, as we have proposed, another path could and should be followed, improving the current regime by changing the national contribution key in proportion to their gni, so as to ensure that the countries with the highest gni contribute proportionately more to the eu budget, with the introduction of profound changes in their redistributive function and their priorities.
in writing. − on 29 june 2011, the commission presented its proposals for a new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, together with a set of proposals on the reform of the union's own resources system. these include the proposal for a seventh own resources decision (odr), which calls for the abolition of the current vat own resource and its replacement by a new eu vat resource. the proposal for a regulation aimed at making the vat own resource available is necessary to define the method to be used by the member states for the calculation of this new resource and the procedures to be followed for its transfer to the eu budget. the proposal for a new eu vat own resource is undoubtedly a major improvement on the current system and has the potential to become a genuine stable and reliable own resource for the union budget. the vat own resource should be part of a reform of the own resources system, which should substantially reduce the overall level of national contributions by member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation on the methods and procedure for making available own resources based on value added tax. the european commission has said that the current vat own resources should be abolished and a new eu vat own resource created.
in writing. − the commission's proposal to abolish the current system of own resources and to create a new eu vat own resource streamlines the current taxation system so that it evolves into a stable and reliable own resource for the union budget. the vat own resource aims to reform the eu's own resources system in order to reduce the level of national contributions by member states, and one of the key criteria for a genuine vat own resource would be that it should be paid directly to the eu budget without being collected initially by national administrations.
in writing. − the multiannual financial framework sets out the community budget for the period 2014-2020. in june 2011, the european commission put forward a proposal for €1.083 billion of expenditure, corresponding to 1.11% of european gross domestic product and an increase of 5% over the current programming period (2007-2013). in order to reduce the member states' contribution to the community budget by 40%, the european commission has put forward the possibility of creating own resources, which are enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in this connection, i believe that the introduction of the financial transaction tax and the modernisation of vat should be considered appropriate, and that the current european resource of a part of national vat being collected by the member states should be abandoned. i am in favour of creating these own resources, provided that firms and households do not have to pay more for the products or services they purchase. i therefore agree with the statement by the president of the european commission that 'it is not a question of increasing the eu budget, but of giving it a stronger basis and reducing direct contributions from the member states'.
in writing. the creation of a new 'eu vat' as an 'own resource' is another federalist proposal which is a gross manipulation based on the false 'reduction of the share of member states' contributions'. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. what we are advocating is that the countries with the highest gni should contribute proportionately more to the eu budget, introducing profound changes in their redistributive function and their priorities. this would be the most solidary way of obtaining own resources for the eu.
