in writing. - this report, drawn up by ingeborg gräßle and crescenzio rivellini, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the financial provisions applicable to the annual budget of the european union (eu). the budgetary principles and rules governing the establishment and implementation of the general budget of the eu are laid down in regulation (ec, euratom) no 1605/2002, but the implementing provisions were laid down in commission regulation (ec, euratom) no 2342/2002 of 23 december 2002 on the financial regulation applicable to the general budget of the european communities. at present, all regulations have to comply with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in these terms, and taking into account the report of the committee on budgets and the committee on budgetary control and the opinions of the committee on foreign affairs, the committee on industry, research and energy and the committee on regional development, i am voting in favour of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the financial provisions applicable to the annual budget of the european union.
in writing. - the commission proposal concerns the establishment of the legal framework for the establishment and implementation of the eu budget in all areas, both expenditure and revenue. among other things, it defines the scope of parliament's action on the establishment of the eu budget and deals with the evaluation and accountability of parliament as one of the two arms of the eu's budgetary authority. although we consider that greater transparency and accountability in the implementation of the eu budget is important and necessary, some of the articles in the proposal adopted today cannot be accepted by us. the european stability mechanism is introduced, thus providing guarantees for its financing. the final proposal extends the scope for public-private partnerships. the commission is also proposing to make the implementation of the budget more transparent and to make it more transparent. it also proposes the transfer of appropriations relating to projects financed under the connecting europe facility, which has project finance obligations as one of its financial instruments.
in writing. − the financial mechanisms available to the european union and the citizens of the member states must function efficiently to enable the implementation of european policies, while ensuring maximum transparency in the use of taxpayers' money. it is therefore essential that they are simple and transparent and that they reduce the administrative and bureaucratic burden faced by all beneficiaries of european funds. the amendments now made to the commission proposal, which are supported by the ppe group, bring about major improvements to that text and achieve the objective that everyone wants of a more agile, more dynamic and at the same time more transparent european union when it comes to the application and provision of the funds at its disposal.
in writing. - having regard to the report of the committee on budgets and the committee on budgetary control and the opinions of the committee on foreign affairs, the committee on industry, research and energy and the committee on regional development, and having no objections, i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the financial provisions applicable to the annual budget of the union.
in writing. − the regulations lay down rules for financial instruments, including the definition of their scope, control and reporting on the mechanisms and financial risks to the union budget. this refers to the eu, which, although one of the world's largest donors, has only been contributing to existing funds, whether the un or the world bank, resulting in little visibility of the union in terms of its performance and priorities. these new provisions thus give the commission autonomy to establish investment funds as an instrument of international cooperation - tools of the utmost importance for disaster relief and development aid operations. the budget rules also include a new feature, the 'incentive awards', which are an instrument to stimulate research projects. the report also calls for an extension of the reporting obligations of eu member states, especially as regards the use of the structural funds. the commission is given more rights and duties over national paying agencies and over the supervisory authorities. the audit rules and penalties for irregularities will also be improved, with a view to harmonising the complexity and number of financial rules. i voted in favour.
in writing. - article 317 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union stresses the importance of simple and transparent mechanisms, providing a catalytic effect for non-eu budgetary resources and at the same time reinforcing the european commission's accountability for budget implementation. i support this report because i agree that the rules and procedures for the european union's research framework programmes should be further simplified and harmonised, and that a risk of error should be indicated to promote sound financial management and adequate controls in the area of cohesion policy. finally, i believe it is essential that the budget should include the entry in the budget of the guarantee for borrowing and lending operations carried out by the european union in the framework of the management of the european financial stability facility (efsf) and the european financial stability mechanism (efsm), as well as the entry in the budget of transfers to the guarantee fund for external actions.
in writing. − we consider that greater transparency and accountability in the implementation of the eu budget is important and necessary, objectives which should of course guide this regulation. however, there are some aspects of this report which we strongly oppose: the european stability mechanism is introduced, giving it legitimacy and thus guaranteeing its financing. the final proposal also extends the scope for public-private partnerships by proposing that the commission 'entrust the implementation of the budget to public-private partnerships'. the introduction of this possibility is, in our view, unacceptable.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am the rapporteur for this report, but it is not my report, because i voted against it in the inta committee, which i chair. having made that statement, i shall briefly present the various issues involved with the utmost objectivity. the basic question is whether we should approve the trade agreement with israel under the mutual recognition of conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products, which this protocol already applies to pharmaceutical products but which allows it to be extended to all other products subject to conformity assessment and acceptance. the inta committee was divided between two irreconcilable views. first, a position against approval, in the name of the coherence of the union's external policies towards israel. it is pointless, this position argues, on the one hand to condemn strongly israeli policy towards the occupied territories and on the other hand to strengthen trade relations with israel. it is pointless to watch israel's contempt for our condemnation and then give israel the valuable prize in trade policy. it is pointless to be shocked by the deliberate policy of destroying the conditions for a two-state solution, as the union advocates, and then to support and encourage israel in relation to these same policies. the other position in inta was that, firstly, the protocol merely gives effect to the trade mechanism already provided for in the association agreement and that we should not mix the foreign policy and foreign trade policy plan. this is the position which won in inta against my draft report, albeit by a small majority. it is now up to the plenary and each of us to decide definitively on the question of substance. in addition to this basic question, there are two additional questions. the first concerns the territorial scope of the protocol. unfortunately, the protocol was not carefully negotiated and it is not clear whether or not it excludes products from the occupied territories. we must clarify this point, otherwise we will be breaking a red line of the european union, namely the non-recognition of the israeli integration of these territories. the proposal to ask the council for an interpretative statement on the subject is therefore justified. only the council can do that, because it is the council which, on behalf of the union, is bound by this protocol. our role here is only to give our assent to that council decision. so we can only ask the council to do so. however, without the council's clear commitment today and here (and by the way, i do not see the council here) that it will make that interpretative statement, our vote on this issue is irrelevant and ineffective. in any case, we are called upon to vote on this interpretative statement or this request for an interpretative vote. the third point relates to article 3 of the draft council decision which concluded the agreement on behalf of the union. in that provision, the council delegates to the commission the power to amend the agreement, including with regard to the products covered, without any further approval by parliament or the council. this is a genuine authorization to amend an international agreement, which we have voted on. however, the council still wants to keep control over these amendments through an ad hoc committee, while parliament will have no further role in the amendment of the agreement we are going to vote on here. there are three problems here, firstly, does it make sense to allow the commission to amend a trade agreement in such a substantial way? secondly, what is the legal basis in the treaty for the ad hoc committee which the council is proposing to monitor the commission in this matter? thirdly, and with this in mind, is it permissible for parliament to be ignored either in the delegation, in the control of the exercise of the delegated power or in the assessment of the amendments to the protocol which the commission is to negotiate with israel? the socialist group has already announced that it will ask the commission to withdraw this case in order to examine this matter. and this is an important point, and i do not think we can allow a precedent to be set in this matter.
blue-card question. – mr president, my question is a very simple one. article 2 of the association agreement to which this protocol is an additional arrangement says ‘relations between the two parties are based on respect for human rights’. does the house believe that israel is respecting the human rights of palestinians – stealing their lands, expelling them from their homes, preventing them from free circulation in their own land? is this respect for human rights? does the house feel that the conditions for an association agreement are being fulfilled by israel?
blue-card question. – madam president, i appreciate the experience of mr zahradil in this parliament and his serene and usually very balanced participation. i would like to put to him an objective question regarding the qualification of this agreement as a technical one. this is a not a technical agreement because, while it is about the removal of technical barriers to trade, the removal of some technical barriers is quite political. it will mean, for example, the removal of assessment controls and mutual recognition, which constitutes a high level of partnership and means that israeli exports will be fully integrated into the internal market. let me ask mr zahradil whether he does not agree that the benefits that israeli exporters will reap from this agreement will give them a significant edge over other exporters to the union. is that not a privilege?
the rapporteur. - mr president, two concluding remarks: first, there is not a day's delay in this proceeding due to any unilateral statement, position, or decision on my part. i was not the first rapporteur in this procedure, i was a rapporteur malgré moi and all the decisions, all the conduct of this procedure was made with full transparency and with the full agreement of the committee. the accusation made against me by a representative of the israeli interests in this parliament is not only stupid, it disqualifies the person who made it. secondly, my objection to this agreement, my initial position as rapporteur, has nothing to do with israeli policy, it has to do with ours and with the consistency which the treaty requires of our foreign policies to be consistent with each other. my position has always been that it is the coherence of the union's external policies that is at stake and i do not see how it is possible that we can at the same time condemn israel for what israel is doing in relation to the occupied territories and then when we have an opportunity to put pressure on israel to comply with our condemnations we give it a prize of this nature. tomorrow israel will laugh, and with pleasure, at our political positions because it knows that it is only libre service, it is hypocrisy and when it comes to carrying them out we are not capable of carrying them out. finally, a personal statement: i do not belong to any anti-israel movement, i do not belong to any association of friends of the palestinians, i do not owe anything to any of the parties, i repeat, i do not owe anything to any of the parties, and i would like those who have spoken in this debate to be able to say the same with the same frankness.
in writing. − i voted in favour because i consider that draft amending budget no 4 to the 2012 general budget has a triple objective, namely the creation of four budget lines to reallocate up to 10% of the appropriations allocated to the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund 2007-2013 to risk-sharing mechanisms, a revision and budgeting of the own funds forecasts, which results in a change in the distribution of their contributions to the eu budget among the member states. in addition, draft amending budget no 4/2012 provides for the possibility for amounts recovered or remaining from union support for risk-sharing mechanisms financed under cohesion policy to be added in the following year, at the request of the member state concerned, to its financial allocation for cohesion policy. however, i would stress that any transfer of cohesion policy appropriations to the financial mechanisms to be defined must be duly justified and well controlled, as provided for in regulation (eu) no 423/2012.

in writing. − on 1 december 2011, the european parliament (ep) finally adopted the general budget of the european union (eu) for the financial year 2011. we all know that budgetary executions never fully correspond to the amounts approved, either because of the unpredictability of the revenue collected or because of unforeseen expenditure. to avoid these situations, there are so-called amending budgets which allow the initial appropriations to be corrected. draft amending budget no 4 to the general budget of the eu for the year 2012 provides for the creation of four budget lines in order to reallocate up to 10% of the appropriations allocated to the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund for 2007 to 2013 to 'risk-sharing mechanisms, a revision and budgeting of the capital estimates', and to replace the 'pass' entered under the payment appropriations of budget line 16 03 05 01 (preparatory work) 'euroglobe' by a pro memoria entry (p.m.) to enable a transfer to be made. the draft is in line with the amendments to the financial regulation agreed between the ep and the council, and i therefore vote in favour of this report by mrs francesca balzani.
in writing. − the adoption of this amending budget (no 4/2012) aims to provide budgetary cover for the provisions which have enabled the creation of a 'risk-sharing mechanism', based on an authorisation for a transfer of capital from the structural and cohesion funds from the member states to the european commission, i.e. the transfer of part of the financial allocations made available to countries in difficulty which thus reduce the remaining global allocations. the majority of parliament thus supports the concentration of capital in the european investment bank to cover the expected and unforeseen losses resulting from loans and guarantees. the so-called risk-sharing is established between the eib and other national or international financial institutions, public or private, which will grant the loans to project sponsors and banks, with a view to providing private co-financing for projects implemented with the contributions of the structural funds and the cohesion fund. other avenues existed and could have been followed to overcome the existing constraints on the private investment side. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as we have already pointed out in the debate on this mechanism, we are faced with another exercise of european 'solidarity' sui generis.
in writing. − draft amending budget no 4 to the 2012 general budget has a threefold objective, namely the creation of four budget lines to reallocate up to 10% of the appropriations allocated to the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund 2007-2013 to risk-sharing mechanisms, a revision and budgeting of the own funds forecasts, resulting in a change in the distribution of their contributions to the eu budget among the member states. i think it is important, however, that parliament should be regularly and fully informed about the operational programmes whose appropriations are being reduced, the financial mechanisms to be implemented and the projects to be supported.

in writing. − raising awareness among the general public of the rights and responsibilities associated with union citizenship is essential if both the rights and duties arising from european citizenship are to be effectively fulfilled. only by exercising these rights can the remaining obstacles to this level be identified and eliminated. it is therefore up to the european citizens themselves to play a key role in strengthening these rights through their participation in civil society and democratic life, and it is up to the european institutions to promote awareness-raising campaigns such as this one on the european year of citizens. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report, while deploring the drastic cut in the budget for this initiative, which is a key issue for the democratic culture of the union.
in writing. − the year 2013 will be designated as the european year of citizens, the overall purpose of which is to ensure that all citizens of the union are aware of the rights which they enjoy, in a crossborder context, by virtue of their status as european citizens. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. while member states have the primary responsibility for raising awareness, appropriate action to address this problem requires multilateral collaboration, information exchange, union-wide experience and the dissemination of transnational best practices. this awareness-raising campaign, which aims to remove the many obstacles still remaining to the exercise of the rights of european citizenship, is of great importance. only more and better information can help europeans to make use of their rights. i voted in favour.
in writing. - article 20 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union establishes citizenship of the union, stating that 'a citizen of the union is any person who is a national of a member state. citizenship of the union shall be additional to, and not replace, national citizenship.' over the last few years, a number of problems and obstacles to citizens' civic participation in activities related to the construction of the european project have been identified. it is essential to promote projects that increasingly involve citizens in general and young people in particular in the civic and political component. i support the proposal to establish 2013 as the 'european year of citizens' with the general objective of raising citizens' awareness of the rights linked to union citizenship in order to help them make full use of their right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. however, i think the designation 'european year of citizenship' is more appropriate and i think it is essential that the budget of eur 1 million allocated to the initiative be substantially increased.
in writing. − this report supports the establishment of the european year of citizens (2013) with the stated aim of raising awareness of citizenship rights in the eu. in our view, the celebration of the european year of citizens (2013) is nothing more than a strategy of the eu to try to legitimize the idea of the eu as an area of democracy, equality, solidarity and citizen participation at a time when the european institutions lack public credibility. the eu is not really a place where people can move freely, and this initiative, albeit in a disguised way, is an apology for the single market as a place of freedom. in view of the difficult situation facing workers today and the need for emigration to cope with unemployment in their home countries, we introduced in the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs the idea of the need to defend workers' rights in the field of social security and trade union rights, and that the movement of workers should not be interpreted by certain employers as an opportunity to reduce wages, social protection or to degrade working conditions in general.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the assumptions and content of the report.
in writing. the report under review, by mrs kristiina ojuland, concerns the proposal for a european parliament (ep) recommendation to the council on the establishment of common visa restrictions for russian officials involved in the sergei magnitsky case. sergei magnitsky was a brave russian lawyer who died in a russian prison, the victim of mistreatment, where he was detained after being arrested for fighting corruption in russia. despite all efforts by the russian government to have this case properly investigated and those responsible tried by an independent tribunal, the truth is that despite the promises made by the rulers, nothing has been done and this case continues to be part of the summits with that country. this image of lack of freedom and credibility undermines the consolidation of the democratic process, driving away investors, consolidated by russia's accession to the world trade organization (wto). i voted in favour of this report and i urge the russian authorities to resolve this human rights violation quickly in the interests of the russian community itself.
in writing. - the debate and adoption of this report is another step in the process of interfering with the legal and constitutional system of a sovereign country, which raises serious reservations and is hardly acceptable in the context of normal and healthy relations between independent and sovereign states. whatever one may think of the political and social situation in russia, this is the use of a court case to attack that country and its sovereignty at a political moment when that country, in the framework of the un security council, is opposed to military aggression against syria, and therefore constitutes a clear form of blackmail and political retaliation.
in writing. the european parliament has also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's external action is coordinated. the detention, conditions of detention and subsequent death in prison of sergei magnitsky are evidence of the disregard for fundamental human rights by a member state of the council of europe, which has committed itself to full respect for fundamental rights and all the principles inherent in the rule of law. i therefore consider that the restriction on the issuing of visas to russian officials involved in the case described here is a necessary and entirely legitimate foreign policy instrument, a political signal of the eu's concern about the frequent violations of human rights in russia.
in writing. - on the assumption that this is an exceptional measure, and without prejudice to the assumptions and content of this report which justifies and substantiates the exceptional nature of this measure establishing common restrictions on the issuing of visas to certain individuals, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − without the russian authorities' respect for the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, as noted in the tragic case of the death of sergei magnisky, it is not possible to develop a stable and reliable partnership between the eu and russia. while the restrictive measures proposed in the report do not constitute traditional judicial sanctions per se, they should nonetheless serve as a political signal of the eu's concern, a signal sent to a wider public, aimed at hopefully awakening the russian authorities to develop genuine and renewed efforts to approach, hopefully, the rule of law issue in russia in a more concrete and convincing way.
in writing. - the magnitsky case is another example of the violation of the rule of law in the russian federation, as there was a clear abuse of power, in particular of the judicial authorities. following several appeals by the eu and the osce to establish the true facts, russian judicial authorities acquitted the officials involved and sentenced sergei magnitsky posthumously, in clear violation of international and national law. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. − regardless of whether the detention of any citizen in any country in the world is justified or not, we believe that it is up to each country and its judicial system to guarantee its citizens access to the law and to the courts to defend their legally protected rights and interests. the detention, conditions of detention and subsequent death in custody of russian citizen sergei magnitsky are inserted in this principle. we are faced with a clear interference in the legal and constitutional system of a sovereign country which we cannot and must not accept in the name of cooperation between independent and sovereign states. this is the use of a judicial case to attack russia and its sovereignty at a political moment when russia, in the framework of the un security council, is opposed to military aggression against syria, and therefore constitutes a clear form of blackmail and political retaliation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the recent commission document on 'the implementation of the single sky legislation'. the urgent need for progress should be highlighted, as well as the greater need for political support, in order to ensure a successful and timely implementation of the ess legislation. other key issues in this report include the implementation of functional airspace and the blocks to the deployment of sesar technology, both of which are essential for the functioning of the single european sky.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the full and timely deployment of the ees will bring significant benefits to the member states, as all indications are that it should have positive effects on the economy, employment and the environment.
in writing. − at present, european airspace is one of the busiest in the world, with over 750 million passengers using eu airports. in the face of the continuing increase in air traffic, it is essential to complete the single european sky legislation as soon as possible in order to avoid congestion of european airspace and to ensure a high quality of air services for european citizens, while also enabling significant savings in economic, environmental and safety terms, creating a more sustainable aviation sector and a more effective air traffic management system at european level. while there has been much positive progress in the right direction, much remains to be done to achieve full and timely implementation in order to avoid any operational or safety risks caused by increasingly intense flows, outdated technologies and the fragmentation of european airspace. timely implementation should also allow the eu to maintain its competitiveness, foster new momentum in this area, foster growth and jobs, especially in the aeronautics and aviation sectors, and contribute significantly to the reduction of co2 emissions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the single european sky legislation, which stresses the need for concrete measures to overcome the obstacles and ensure the timely implementation of this legislation.
in writing. − at present, each member state manages its airspace in conjunction with neighbouring countries. this uncoordinated management of european airspace has an estimated cost of four billion euros per year. the european union has been focusing for many years on the need to implement a centralised management of european airspace with obvious consequences for everyone: safety, speed and economy. in 2004, the european commission launched a very ambitious initiative to reshape air traffic, creating the sesar programme, the technological pillar of the single european sky. after these years, it is clear that progress has not been as expected, and it is therefore urgent to raise awareness among member states so that they can overcome the difficulties in implementing it. the european technological and economic development is at stake (job creation, reduction of co2 emissions, greater security, increased tourism, more competitive industry, etc.). i voted in favour of the report by my colleague jacqueline foster on the implementation of the single european sky legislation because we need a well-organised airspace - where safety is the order of the day - and because the implementation of this legislation will make an important contribution to the future of europe.
in writing. - this report aims to accelerate the process of creating the 'single european sky', identifying the need to set 'binding deadlines' for its implementation. the report is based on two main principles: 1. clear pressure on member states to implement the legislation on the 'single european sky', even going so far as to propose that the commission take punitive measures against countries which have not yet met the deadlines. 2. an excessive propaganda campaign on the alleged advantages of the 'single european sky': the european parliament has been a very active participant in the debate on the future of the european union. the absence of any justification for these alleged advantages is manifest and confrontational. the report conceals the real aims of the single sky: national subordination, reduction in the price of labour and increase in the profits of the large companies. it also states that progress in the field of better coordination and use of airspace can and must be achieved within the framework of maintaining the sovereignty of each state over its own airspace - an essential issue for the defence of the specific interests of each country, whether in the field of commercial aviation or in the field of defence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the single european sky legislation. the single european sky will contribute to the creation of a more sustainable aviation sector and a more effective air traffic management system at european level. it will have competitive gains across the eu and even globally, boosting growth and jobs, especially in the aeronautics and aviation sectors. i believe that this issue should be given increased priority in order to develop efforts to develop and implement the legislation in question.
in writing. - the desired legislation on the single european sky (ses) should be implemented. the studies indicate that the ses will bring economic and competitive advantages, benefiting all actors, including the final consumer, i.e. the passenger, through reduced user charges. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - one of the most urgent challenges to be tackled is the fragmentation of european airspace. the industry providing air traffic control closely mirrors the geographical boundaries of its countries, each of which has at least one air navigation service provider (asp). this fragmented national approach needs to be replaced in order to increase efficiency and reduce congestion. the report supports public-private partnerships, and the favourable relationship between both parties along the entire sector chain, using incentives to encourage commitment, and bringing numerous socioeconomic benefits.
in writing. − the achievement of the single european sky (ses) will bring the entire aviation sector, and directly and indirectly related sectors, competitive advantages and significant growth for a turbulent period in europe's history. if single european sky traffic management (sesar) is implemented, it is estimated to have a cumulative impact on eu gdp of €419 billion, create 328 000 jobs and reduce 50 million tonnes of co2. on the other hand, air traffic is about to reach its maximum capacity, putting aviation operations and safety at risk. it is time to apply all the investment made in ses and sesar to the modernisation of european aviation and to the elimination of the fragmentation of airspace, which is still divided like the borders of european countries. a strong and efficient european aviation, capable of competing internationally, will bring enormous economic advantages to the member states.
in writing. - the process of creating the 'single european sky' is under way. that is, an attack on national sovereignty, more national subordination, predictable reduction of the workforce and increase in profits for the big companies. what also worries us about this project are the militaristic designs involved, when it refers to 'the military community as one of the main actors in the framework of the single european sky', which may mean that this process has, in addition to the economic objectives of privatising the 'sky', objectives of military control in the service of the interests that command the destinies of the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i agree with the specific passenger rights listed in the communication as a step forward in building fundamental rights across all modes of transport. the establishment of guidelines on the application and implementation of these rights is one of the main calls for improving their implementation in the short term. a single transversal regulation on passenger rights as a whole remains a medium-term vision. passenger rights are at the heart of our transport policy and there is a need for better information and transparency for citizens on these rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to strengthen the application of the existing provisions on passenger rights and to improve them where necessary.
in writing. − over the last 10 years, we have been creating a set of eu passenger rights, regardless of the mode of transport, to ensure a minimum level of protection, facilitating mobility and at the same time creating a level playing field for carriers. unfortunately, we do not always see the full and correct application of these rights, either by the carriers or by the national authorities. it is therefore urgent to review the legislation in force in order to make it clearer and to strengthen passengers' rights, in particular the right to information on their rights and how they can exercise them. the effective and efficient enforcement of these rights can only be ensured if there is active and effective control by the national enforcement bodies. passenger rights are thus based on three pillars: non-discrimination, accurate, timely and accessible information, and prompt and proportionate assistance. i therefore support this initiative, which, as one of the measures provided for in the communications on a single market act, lists the rights and principles applicable to all modes of transport, taking account of the distinctions due to the specific characteristics of each mode of transport, and identifies the areas where greater convergence should be achieved, as well as the existing gaps.
in writing. − mobility is one of the pillars of modern society and has been strongly encouraged, not only among young people see the success of the erasmus programme but also in business terms (de-location and internationalisation) and as a way of overcoming the economic and financial crisis. in fact, over the last few years there has been a significant increase in passengers carried with a highlight for aviation due to the concept of 'low cost'. with the increase in the number of passengers carried, we are seeing an increase in problems in this sector. every day we see hundreds of cancelled or delayed transport that put passengers (workers, students, tourists, etc.) in very complicated situations. sometimes passengers are not aware of their rights, perhaps through negligence on the part of the carriers themselves, particularly in relation to assistance services in the event of cancellation of a journey or transport. also, information is not always correct, clear and available in several languages. i voted in favour because i agree with the need to implement a regulatory framework which guarantees respect for passenger rights, in particular facilitated access to information and support services.
in writing. − the document sets out a set of passenger rights applicable to all modes of transport, to ensure a minimum level of protection in the eu. it addresses the criteria for compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or significant delays, and the liability of airlines in the event of baggage problems. it is also intended to ensure the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility in air transport with regard to access, information and appropriate training. in rail transport, improvements are being made in the protection of passengers and their luggage, as well as in the area of delays and accidents. however, it is worrying that these rights could be called into question, for example, considering that it is considered 'essential to balance the need to respect passenger rights in bus services in rural areas and ... to ensure that the charges are not so considerable as to render such services unviable in the future'. the absence of a single reference to public transport services - an essential means of ensuring the maintenance of the transport needed to link isolated regions and localities and to guarantee the full rights of passengers and the population - is symptomatic.
in writing. − for some years now, the eu has been developing a set of eu passenger rights, regardless of the mode of transport, in order to achieve a higher level of protection, facilitate mobility and, at the same time, create conditions for a competitive market for all carriers. however, full use of all these rights has not always been possible, largely due to the fault of the actors, carriers and national authorities. we must therefore review this legislation to make it clearer, thereby strengthening passengers' rights, particularly as regards the right to information on their rights and how they can exercise them. passenger rights must be based on three pillars: non-discrimination, accurate, timely and accessible information, and immediate assistance.
in writing. − this report refers to the commission's communication which sets out a list of rights applicable to all modes of transport, which, taken together, ensure a minimum level of protection for passengers (in the broad sense) in the eu. this report considers the strengthening of the application of the existing provisions on passenger rights and the need to improve them where appropriate. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the report calls for improvements in several areas, calling in particular for the creation of a single cross-cutting regulation on passenger rights for all modes of transport, to be implemented in the medium term. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's airspace is not used for illegal purposes. the rights of citizens with reduced mobility or disabilities are also considered in this report. i voted in favour of the proposed measures.
in writing. − access to information on passenger rights should be simple, clear and transparent, from the moment of booking or purchase to the end of the journey. it is important that passengers have all the help they need in the event of problems with their travel or loss or damage to their luggage. information on costs and prices of services shall be clear and accessible from the beginning of the procedure. we cannot but support measures which promote and facilitate information and transparency and thus ensure passenger rights.
in writing. − passenger rights in the eu have been evolving steadily and progressively. the air and rail passenger rights are already in place, and those relating to sea/river and bus transport will come into force in december 2012 and march 2013 respectively. what i would like to stress in this document is the need for transparency of the information provided, from the moment of booking until the end of the journey. in any mode of transport, there must be a point of contact. on the other hand, companies should be held liable in the event of insolvency and the concept of 'extraordinary circumstances' should be better applied. finally, it is important to emphasise the rights of persons with reduced mobility, who should receive a service adapted to their needs.
in writing. − this report aims to identify some of the rights of passengers in all modes of transport, such as the criteria for compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or significant delays, and the liability of airlines when there are problems with luggage. it is also intended to ensure the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility in air transport with regard to access, information and appropriate training. these, like other aspects, are essential. however, it is extremely worrying that there is not a single reference in the whole report to public transport services, which are an essential means of ensuring the maintenance and guaranteeing of the right to non-profit-making mobility, providing transport in isolated regions and localities for the benefit of the population.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are facing a serious financial, economic and social crisis, with rising unemployment as one of the main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 2 696 382 from the egf for ireland to support the 493 potential beneficiaries of the 592 workers made redundant by talk talk broadband services and three of its suppliers in ireland.

in writing. − this report concerns the proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) and falls within point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the ep, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2012/001 ie/talk talk, ireland). the egf was set up in 2006 to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in world trade patterns brought about by globalisation. ireland submitted an application on 29 february 2012 to the egf, following the dismissal of 573 workers from the talk talk broadband services (customer centre), for support of eur 2 696 382. on 27 july 2012, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision to grant the requested support. this is the seventh application to be examined under the 2012 budget. the commission's conclusion is that the application fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions for the mobilisation of the egf. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's recommendations and vote in favour of this proposal for a decision.
in writing. - this application concerns 592 redundancies in the telecommunications sector, 432 of which are potential recipients of assistance, at the company talk talk in ireland. the commission has decided to mobilise eur 2 696 382 to assist workers made redundant as a result of outsourcing to the united kingdom, india, the philippines and south africa. these layoffs are not inevitable. they are the result of political choices. we're approving palliative care that's necessary, but we need to go further. we must attack the root of the problem: the break with the neoliberal policies which are driving us into the abyss without discerning, however faintly, a small ray of hope for the millions of workers who are being deprived of their right to work and to a decent life.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to ireland which has submitted a request for assistance for 592 redundancies, 432 of which are potential beneficiaries, in talk talk broadband services (ireland) and three of its suppliers in ireland.
in writing. − under the european globalisation adjustment fund, the european commission adopted on 27 july 2012 a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of ireland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. this is the seventh application to be examined under the 2012 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 2 696 382 from the egf in support of 592 redundancies, 432 of which are potential recipients of assistance, in talk talk broadband services (ireland) and three of its suppliers in ireland during the four-month reference period from 7 september 2011 to 7 january 2012, and six more outside that period but related to the same collective redundancy process. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − following ireland's request for assistance in respect of 592 redundancies, 432 of which are potential beneficiaries, at talk talk broadband services (ireland) limited and three of its suppliers in ireland, the commission proposes to mobilise the amount of eur 2 696 382 from the european globalisation adjustment fund, set up in 2006 to 'provide additional support to redundant workers suffering from the consequences of structural changes in world trade patterns'. i voted in favour.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. i agree with the request for the mobilisation of the egf made by ireland in respect of 592 redundancies, 432 of which were potential beneficiaries of support, in talk talk broadband services and three of its suppliers. i believe that the european commission should mobilise eur 2 696 382.00 to help the vocational integration of workers in irish telecommunications companies. the financial package now approved should be channelled to support measures in the area of vocational guidance, individual training and general information provided through specific employment channels.
in writing. - in this plenary session alone we will be voting on eight calls for mobilisation of the globalisation adjustment fund, which reflects well the path of economic and social disaster that capitalist and neoliberal policies are leading the eu countries on. this application concerns 592 redundancies in the telecommunications sector, 432 of which are potential recipients of assistance, which occurred in the company talk talk in ireland and in six of its suppliers, in connection with the same collective redundancy. the commission has decided to mobilise eur 2 696 382 to assist workers made redundant as a result of their relocation to the united kingdom, india, the philippines and south africa. we're approving palliatives that may be temporarily important but we have to attack the evil at its root: it is imperative to break with the neoliberal policies which are driving us into the abyss without any glimmer of hope for the millions of workers and their families who are being deprived of their right to work and to a decent life.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are facing a serious financial, economic and social crisis, with rising unemployment as one of the main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 4 325 854 from the egf for sweden to support the 700 potential beneficiaries of the 987 workers made redundant at the pharmaceutical company astrazeneca.
in writing. − the globalisation of markets on the one hand, and the expiry of patents and the growing market share of generic medicines on the other, have brought about major changes in the pharmaceutical industry, forcing it to make adjustments in an already difficult environment in order to remain competitive. it also notes that investment and biotechnology research are becoming increasingly important worldwide and that the situation of r & d in the eu is a cause for concern in the face of the austerity climate in europe. in the face of new strategies and investment patterns in life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals or medical technology initiated by third countries, european companies, even those considered successful examples such as astrazeneca, have been forced to adapt their production to meet the new challenges. i therefore voted in favour of this report which makes available eur 4 325 854 through the mobilisation of the egf in favour of sweden.
in writing. − the european union (eu), recognising the very serious social consequences of the current economic and financial crisis, has set up the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to provide additional support to workers affected by structural changes in world trade. this report is based on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of the egf, in accordance with point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the ep, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2011/015/se/astrazeneca, sweden). on 16 july 2012, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of sweden to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global crisis, following the abovementioned application submitted on 23 december 2011. this is the sixth application submitted under the eu budget for 2012, mobilising eur 4 325 854, and aims to mitigate the social impact of the dismissal of 987 workers from the swedish company astrazeneca. i voted in favour of this proposal as it meets all the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation.
in writing. - this report approves the mobilisation of the egf to the amount of eur 4 325 854 to support the reintegration into the labour market of 987 workers made redundant by the swedish company astrazeneca in the pharmaceutical industry as a result of 'structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation' - always the same talk... - to outsourcing and also to cuts in r & d investment at european level. unlike asian communities, which increased investment in r & d during the recession, europe, obsessed with tackling deficits, is restricting public support for r & d, which could continue for several years, with inevitable consequences for employment and medical research. every new mobilisation of this fund must be condemned and denounced in the strongest possible terms. this is the result of the policies which the eu has been imposing on europe. a new course is being set.

in writing. - the proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) under point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament (ep), the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2010/015 fr/peugeot', france). on 21 august 2012, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of france to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global crisis. this is the 11th application examined under the eu budget for 2011, and was submitted to the commission on 5 may 2010 for the mobilisation of eur 11 949 666. it is intended to mitigate the social impact of the dismissal of some 2 089 workers at psa peugeot citroën and voluntary redundancies at the same company. i am therefore voting in favour of this application, since it fulfils the conditions for the mobilisation of the egf, and i hope that the economic fabric of the affected region will be restored quickly.
in writing. - in addition to our usual position on this matter, this request for mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund has specific features which make further critical assessment essential. the request was made by france for 5 100 workers made redundant by the psa peugeot citröen group, of whom more than 41.55% are over 55 years of age. this raises questions (and concerns) about the type of support that will be provided and the future of these workers, who traditionally have more difficulty finding new jobs. moreover, peugeot, in the redundancy plan negotiated with the workers, included the support of the egf as an integral part of the package to compensate the workers made redundant, an action which uses the fund with a functionality for which it was not created - but to which it is clearly suited. we maintain our position of solidarity with workers made redundant as a direct consequence of eu policies and the structural crisis of capitalism, although we can never agree to the mobilisation of this fund as a way of 'negotiating' conditions of redundancy with workers.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to france which has submitted a request for assistance for 2 089 redundancies, all potential beneficiaries, 649 of which occurred in two subsidiaries of the psa peugeot citroën group (peugeot citroën automobiles and sevelnord) during the reference period from 1 november 2009 to 28 february 2010, and 1 440 other workers were made redundant by the same companies before and after the reference period under the same voluntary redundancy scheme.
in writing. − in the framework of the european globalisation adjustment fund, the european commission adopted on 21 august 2012 a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of france to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis due to globalisation. this is the 11th application to be examined under the 2012 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a global amount of eur 11 949 666 from the egf in favour of 2 089 redundancies of workers, all of whom are eligible for assistance, at psa peugeot citroën during the reference four-month period from 1 november 2009 to 28 february 2010, as well as redundancies resulting from the same voluntary redundancy scheme, also at psa peugeot citroën, but outside the reference period. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − france has submitted an application to mobilise the egf, in respect of redundancies in the psa peugeot citroën group in france, and supplemented it with additional information by 13 april 2012. this application complies with the requirements for determining the financial contributions laid down in article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006. the commission is therefore proposing to mobilise eur 11 949 666. i voted in favour.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. france submitted an application to mobilise the egf in favour of 649 workers made redundant in two subsidiaries of the psa peugeot citroën group (peugeot citroën automobiles and sevelnord) during the period from 1 november 2009 to 28 february 2010, and of a further 1 440 workers made redundant under the same redundancy scheme based on voluntary redundancies. i agree to the mobilisation of eur 11 949 666.00 to support the reintegration of workers, in particular vocational training measures aimed at creating high value-added jobs, thus avoiding the off-shoring of knowledge acquired in this industrial sector.
