in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the export or transit situation through the european union of dual-use items, taking into account that dual-use items are products and technology. given that they can be used for both peaceful and military purposes, it is imperative to establish a set of standards in place to identify and regulate this type of product. this regulation lays down the conditions under which these items are exported and more transparency is needed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider it important to ensure non-proliferation without restricting competition and competitiveness and because i consider that the commission's proposal is in line with the objective of ensuring that eu checklists are updated as soon as possible, allowing for improved speed and flexibility, rapid adaptation to changing external circumstances and avoiding the proliferation of emerging threats, thus ensuring that european industry is not placed at a competitive disadvantage.
in writing. - dual-use products, goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, such as chemicals which can be used for fertilisers or to prepare bombs, computer technology but used to guide missiles, are today a highly sensitive matter. the control of exports of dual-use items and technologies at european level aims to ensure compliance with the international commitments of the eu and its member states on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and the proliferation of conventional weapons. the proposal aims to simplify the procedures of the eu export control regime by introducing delegated acts for regular updates of annex i and amendments to annex ii to regulation (ec) no 428/2009. these updates improve the speed and flexibility of control, allowing for rapid adaptation to changing external circumstances to address the proliferation of emerging threats.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr christofer fjellner, relates to the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishing a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items. over the past few years, the european union has taken a number of measures to prevent these dual-use materials (those which can have a use not only for civilian but also for military purposes) from being used in the manufacture of weapons, in particular weapons of mass destruction. the main eu control instrument is regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 5 may 2009, which focuses on brokering activities and the transit of these materials, but needs to be amended to avoid differential treatment between member states. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to update the existing regulation in order to facilitate the control of exports of dual-use goods and technologies in order to limit the risk of their use for non-peaceful purposes and without affecting legal trade in such goods.
in writing. - this report follows two legislative proposals already adopted by this parliament on export control issues for dual-use items which will amend regulation (ec) no 428/2009 on the export control system for dual-use items and its annexes, which contain lists of controlled items and destinations. we reiterate the objections we raised when this was approved. this report relates to the commission proposal for updating the annexes to the regulation. at present, updates to the regulation are made through the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission proposes to introduce delegated acts for regular updates of annex i and amendments to annex ii. the rapporteur supports the commission's position, and the main reason for this change of procedure is that the ordinary legislative procedure is 'costly and time-consuming' and the late implementation of decisions on strengthening controls 'affects the competitiveness of european exporters'. our group co-signed several amendments to the report which would improve it. unfortunately, they were not approved.
in writing. − the eu controls exports of products which are civilian in nature but which can be used for military purposes under regulation (ec) no 428/2009. annex i to the agreement contains the community list of controlled products, which reflects decisions taken by consensus in international export control regimes. the products under control may not leave the customs territory of the eu without an export authorisation. the general export authorisations listed in annex ii cover exports of certain products of the lowest risk to certain destinations. the dual-use export control framework serves a dual purpose: it aims to limit the risk of proliferation and military use without harming legitimate trade. therefore, it is of the utmost importance to strike a fair balance between these concerns.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the objective of ensuring that eu checklists are updated as soon as possible, improving speed and flexibility. this will allow for a rapid adaptation to changing external circumstances to address the proliferation of emerging threats and ensure that european industry is not placed at a competitive disadvantage.
in writing. − the eu controls the export of goods of a civilian nature, which can however be used for military purposes, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 428/2009. the framework for export controls on goods and technologies serves a dual purpose: to limit the risk of proliferation and military use, without, however, blocking legitimate trade. it is therefore vital to strike a fair balance between these concerns. in this regard, the commission is now proposing amendments to regulation (ec) no 428/2009 with a view to simplifying the procedures in the export control regime. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − the existence of civilian products and technologies which can be used for military purposes requires the european union to regulate and control their export. this export control aims to limit the risk of proliferation of weapons, without this limit affecting legal trade. in the context of such control there are two annexes to the export regulation, which list all dual-use goods and technologies. however, rapid technological advances require that the annexes be updated periodically through the costly and time-consuming ordinary legislative process. in view of the need to honour, as soon as possible, the international commitments made by the member states of the european union with regard to safety-related matters and the need to ensure the competitiveness of european exporters, it is necessary that the process of updating the annexes be carried out as soon as possible. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the document, which expressly proposes to delegate to the european commission the power to update the lists annexed to the regulation on dual-use goods.
in writing. - this report follows two legislative proposals already adopted by this parliament on export control issues for dual-use items which will amend regulation (ec) no 428/2009 on the export control system for dual-use items and its annexes, which contain lists of controlled items and destinations. the rapporteur supports the commission's position, which we do not agree with. the eug co-signed several amendments to the report which would have improved it but were rejected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the collection of data on the seafarer profession at european level. there is an unequivocal need for a more complete picture of the employment situation in this sector.
in writing. − the commission proposal is mainly a transposition of the amendments already accepted by the member states to the nfcsq convention at the imo in order to align european legislation with the amended nfcsq convention. i believe that the amendments introduced in the transposition serve the purpose of improving the wording of the legislative text for reasons of clarity or to update the text to take account of the most recent developments. i agree with the determination of all member states to provide information on seafarers' patents annually in order to obtain a more accurate picture of the seafarer's profession in europe. i also agree with the updates to the legislative text concerning the new comitology provisions introduced by the treaty of lisbon. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − it is essential that there is a minimum level of training for ship crews to ensure their safety at sea or in ports. it should be ensured that crews performing the same duties have the same level of competence required to perform the same duties, regardless of whether the training was carried out in another member state. the training and certification of crews shall follow the parameters of the convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers (the 'nfcsq convention'), adopted in 1978 by the international maritime organisation. the nfcsq convention was amended in 2010 in manila and entered into force on 1 january 2012. it is essential to consistently transpose the manila agreed changes into eu law by amending directive 2008/106/ec. in order to avoid compromising safety on board ships, the opinion provides for a minimum period of rest for the crew. i therefore support this proposal, which seeks to avoid the danger of fatigue by not allowing derogations from the daily rest period. derogations shall be permitted only with the consent of the social partners of all member states in respect of a weekly rest period of 77 hours.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'minimum level of training for seafarers', because it will bring european legislation into line with international conventions on the certification of the training of ship crews.
in writing. - the advent of the era of globalisation, with the elimination of frontiers and the increased mobility of people, means that workers of different nationalities are increasingly working in the same company or company, as is the case with workers on the same ship. the training and certification of seafarers (nfcsq convention) entered into force in 1984 and was significantly amended in 1995 to require a minimum level of training for this category of workers. currently, eu law is embodied in directive 2008/106/ec, which was adopted in november 2008 under the co-decision procedure. on 1 january 2012, a set of relevant amendments agreed at the conference of the parties to the nfcsq convention held in manila in 2010 entered into force. the commission proposal aims to transpose into european law the amendments agreed at the conference of the parties to the nfcsq convention in 2010. i therefore support the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2008/106/ec on the minimum level of training of seafarers.
in writing. − the proposed amendment to the directive on the minimum level of training of seafarers aims to establish a minimum level for the training and certification of seafarers, including the theoretical and practical component, ensuring adequate qualifications to ensure the necessary safety and protection and to respond to hazard and emergency situations. portugal has the technical and administrative capacity to meet the new training requirements. however, it is necessary to ensure that the minimum training requirements do not fall behind current technological developments and scientific advances - which we fear may not be the case. the proposal also includes the designation of a minimum number of hours of rest and minimum ages for young applicants, as well as mandatory minimum requirements for certification as seafarers in the mastery and seamanship. however, in portugal the work intensity on board is already high and tends to increase greatly because of the tendency to reduce staff. it would be essential to ensure that these workers do not work more than 8 hours - which is not the case with this report.
in writing. − it is essential that crews who are trained in different countries and under different systems but who work on the same ship have the necessary skills to perform their duties in the same way. training plays an important role in the field of maritime safety. the training and certification of seafarers is governed by the convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers (the 'nfcsq convention'), which was adopted in 1978 by the international maritime organisation. it entered into force in 1984 and was significantly amended in 1995.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which is based on the commission proposal which essentially deals with the transposition of the amendments already accepted by the member states to the nfcsq convention at the imo, in order to bring european legislation into line with the amended nfcsq convention. the amendments introduced in the transposition have improved the wording of the legislative text, making it clearer and updated to the latest developments in the subject. i am pleased that all the member states are determined to provide information on seafarers' patents annually, so as to obtain a more accurate picture of the seafarer's profession in europe.
in writing. − seafarers trained in different countries and under different systems, but working on the same ship, must have the minimum skills necessary to perform their duties with equal excellence. such competencies play an important role in the field of maritime safety. the legislation adopted, taking into account the rules of the international maritime organisation, introduces changes to european legislation in order to bring the union's rules on the training and certification of seafarers into line with international rules. i voted in favour.
in writing. − this report aims to transpose the amendments agreed in manila in 2010 to the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers, adopted in 1978. i am in favour of this, stressing the importance of minimum rest periods and limits on the possibility of derogations from the hours of rest for seafarers on room service. at a time when the blue economy has incredible growth potential, we must invest in training and qualifying seafarers.
in writing. the proposal to amend the directive concerns the regulation of the minimum level of training of seafarers. however, we think it is necessary to ensure that the minimum training requirements do not fall behind the current technological development and scientific advances, which we believe is the case here. the proposal also includes the designation of a minimum number of hours of rest, but it does not guarantee something fundamental: that these workers do not work more than 8 hours.
in writing. - the recommendation under consideration, drawn up by my colleague and compatriot vital moreira, concerns the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the state of israel, of the other part, on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products (caa). trade relations between the eu and the state of israel have existed for several years, although the eu has never recognised the legitimacy of israel's occupation of palestinian land, notably in the gaza strip. the protocol to the association agreement now approved aims to facilitate the import of safe and low-cost medicines, so-called generics, through mutual recognition of certification powers for certain products. i consider this agreement to be very important, not only because it represents a step forward in trade cooperation with israel, but also because of the advantages it brings to european and israeli consumers and producers. in addition, this protocol has obliged israel to bring its legislative framework closer to that of the european union, which is of great interest to the eu.
in writing. - the approval of this agreement is deplorable and illustrates the eu's hypocritical stance on human rights. the eu's closer trade relations with israel - based on the elimination of technical barriers to trade through the standardisation of legislation and infrastructure (the principle underlying the acaa) - come at a time when israel's systematic violations of the most basic rights of the palestinian people are deepening. a few days after israel, in blatant defiance of international law and numerous un resolutions, advanced to new settlements. human rights violations in the occupied territories are a daily occurrence. territories from which some of the products covered by this agreement may originate. the eu is turning a blind eye. business comes first. the policy of double standards is particularly visible when, in relation to other states, sanctions of various kinds are imposed precisely because of human rights violations. this is the case of iran recently, where the 'nuclear threat' has also been invoked. to be conveniently forgotten now in the case of israel - the only nuclear power in the region which even recently refused to participate in the un conference in helsinki on "a middle east free of nuclear weapons".
in writing. - an 'upgrade' in relations between the european union and israel, a country which violates international law and human rights in the occupied palestinian territories, is unacceptable. even if it ignores the violation of human rights, this protocol does not have the appropriate mechanisms to monitor and stop the industrial goods that are illegally produced in the settlements, which constitute a violation of the fourth geneva convention. since the european union has been awarded the nobel peace prize, freezing this protocol would be an incentive for israel to make a significant contribution to the peace negotiations. by accepting this protocol with israel, the european union is silently agreeing to the occupation and the war.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ep legislative resolution on a draft council decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products. the protocol will allow eu exporters to have their industrial products subject to a single check and certification before export against the same standards and criteria and to access the israeli market without any further certification requirements, with the same requirements applying in reverse on the same assumptions. however, i would stress that the eu's trade policy must be conducted on the basis of the objectives of the union's external action, the principles on which it is based, in particular, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, as enshrined in the treaty.
in writing. - i voted against granting new trade advantages to israel because i believe that, as the teu requires, there must be coherence between the union's external trade policy and its external policy towards israel. the strengthening of the eu-israel trade partnership is not in line with the eu's firm condemnation of israeli policy towards the palestinians, in particular the economic blockade of gaza, the illegal settlements in the occupied territories, the annexation of east jerusalem and the violation of the fundamental rights of the palestinians, namely the right to their territory, freedom of movement, work and, of course, their right to self-determination. the eu cannot afford two contradictory policies towards israel. we must have a single, coherent political message, namely that there will be no strengthening of bilateral relations as long as israel continues to ignore the eu's condemnation of israeli policy on the palestinian question. while israel, in defiance of the union's positions, is systematically destroying the conditions for a peace agreement, giving it this commercial 'gift' is not exactly a sign of consistency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i welcome the determination that eu exporters who so wish can submit their industrial products to a single check and certification before export against the same aligned standards and criteria and thus access the israeli market without any further requirements for certification of conformity.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, it is a privilege to present the report on the 20 concerns of citizens and businesses about the functioning of the single market, precisely in this debate with commissioner barnier, which marks the 20th anniversary of this market. firstly, i would like to thank my colleagues from all the political groups, and in particular the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteur, for their constructive contributions and positive attitude. it was a pleasure to work with all of you and the report has benefited greatly from our joint effort. we are well aware and proud that over the past 20 years the single market has been the engine of great economic and employment opportunities in europe that have transformed the lives of european citizens and european businesses. travel, residence and work in the union are freedoms that are available to all citizens of the 27 member states. for european consumers, the single market means more choice and lower prices. for our companies the single market means more business opportunities with access to 500 million consumers, which means more economic growth and more job creation. to illustrate the progress that the single market has made in europe since its creation in 1992 until the crisis in 2008, it is enough to look at the 2.7 million jobs that have been created and the 2.13% of additional gdp growth. today, it is 13% cheaper to make or receive a phone call when travelling in europe than in 2005. the free movement of persons finds its most eloquent expression in the erasmus programme. more than two and a half million students have benefited from this european programme of educational exchange and mobility. in the last five years, companies have also benefited from a 25% cut in administrative posts due to single market legislation. but one question remains: is the single market doing well? no, not everything works out. the economic and financial crisis that we are experiencing has had a negative impact on the functioning of this market. our citizens, in some countries living with the drama of unemployment and faced with austerity measures, have become sceptical about europe and negative about the internal market. people still do not know or understand their rights sufficiently and do not know where to find information or help. on the other hand, many member states are unduly delaying the transposition of european directives and legislation on the single market, thus undermining its full potential. in certain areas of citizens' daily lives, things as simple as reimbursing medical expenses after a temporary stay in another eu country, opening a bank account for an erasmus student, changing energy supplier, transferring retirement pensions, recognising qualifications and registering a vehicle in another member state are still very complex, difficult or costly. these problems need to be addressed. that was my concern as rapporteur. the message in the report is therefore very clear: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. finally, i would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the european commission, in the person of mr barnier, on the presentation of the single market act ii: 12 priority actions for new growth, which i am sure marks a new step forward.
madam president, commissioner barnier and dear colleague regina bastos, my congratulations on your already successful efforts. the single market of the union was created in 1992 when jacques delors was president of the european commission. the three basic principles of the single market were summed up by mr delors: competition that stimulates, cooperation that strengthens and solidarity that unites. twenty years later, the economic and financial crisis has reignited the threat of national protectionism and it has become clear that the internal market is not a finished product. the celebration of these 20 years must be used to relaunch the single market with the aim of putting the market at the service of the citizen and not the citizen at the service of the market. to do that, we must set priorities, and i would like to speak about one in particular. a common policy for producing and distributing energy at affordable prices to consumers, with a high level of energy efficiency through the european energy market, served by cross-border infrastructure with the possibility of community leverage of the investment representing european added value, is essential. the common market will also be played out in the energy sector, madam president.
the single market, mr president, is used for recurrent propaganda about its alleged contribution to employment, growth and, indeed, economic and social cohesion. only reality, stubborn as it is, insists on contradicting this wonderful vision. the fact is that the single market has gone hand in hand with the weakening of the economically most vulnerable countries, the destruction of productive capacity and the increase in their external dependence. these 20 years have meant the predominance of business over the public interest. the market has advanced in almost all spheres of economic and social life, in public services, with liberalization and privatization, generating inequalities, poverty, exclusion. the single market has opened the way to monopolistic concentration in a number of sectors of activity. consider the case of transport. as for the so-called free movement of persons in this single market, it is now clear that it serves not to harmonize progress but, on the contrary, to bring living and working conditions in europe down to a level. this is the balance of the 20 years that reality has imposed on us.
the single market is one of the greatest achievements of the european union and certainly one of the strongest pillars of the development of the union, its member states and its regions. however, to be effective and fair, it must base its policies on equal opportunities for citizens and all regions, while promoting the union's internal cohesion. in this context, it is essential to recognise that we can only achieve greater development of our outermost regions, such as the outermost regions, by integrating them more fully into the single market. regions like the azores need to continue to increase their competitiveness by improving their conditions of competition, but we will never be able to do that unless we solve our problems of accessibility in the area of transport better. we can do this by means of specific instruments which are better suited to the problems posed by our isolation. we therefore argue that the commission should consider a specific programme, such as posei transportes, as an essential instrument for the integration of such regions into the internal market.
mr president, there are reasons for celebrating the 20th anniversary of the internal market. but the internal market in goods, services and investment should be accompanied by a single labour market, also removing barriers to the mobility of workers. without a single labour market there is no true internal market. secondly, the single market means free competition, but free competition presupposes fair conditions and not regulatory dumping, tax dumping and social dumping. market integration must be accompanied by regulatory integration, tax integration and social integration.
the rapporteur. - madam president, first of all i would like to thank you very much for this excellent debate. it was a very constructive debate and it was a debate which demonstrated that the single market is indeed a great achievement of the european project. i welcome the presence of mr mavroyiannis and his participation in this debate, i thank all the members for their constructive attitude, some of them with a skeptical attitude, which is understandable, and i thank commissioner barnier very much for the commitment and enthusiasm he puts into discussing these issues, these problems of the internal market and the political will to solve them. we have a lot to answer to the citizens. the citizens are dissatisfied, they are disappointed and they expect more from us, they expect more from the council, they expect more from the commission, they expect more from the member states. this balance is very useful, this balance of 20 years is important, but, as many have said here, it is important to open the door to look into the future. and the future is seen through many of the issues that have been raised here and through many of the measures that have already been announced by the european commission. the digital single market, the mobility of citizens, the reform of the eures portal, the european energy market are all eloquent examples of the fact that we still have an important way to go in the future and that this way is very important and vital to respond to the crisis we are living in. the citizens are suffering, the citizens expect a lot from the politicians and the answers that the politicians can give to the adverse conditions they are suffering. it is therefore important that the single market is one of the answers to the great challenge of competitiveness, employment and economic growth. i am sure that after this 20th anniversary celebration, we are all better equipped to give the answers our citizens need.
madam president, we all know that youth unemployment is twice as high as that of other generations, and we all recognise that the erasmus programme enriches students academically, professionally and in terms of acquiring new skills, which enhances their prospects for employment. we all know that the council has made commitments to erasmus. it would therefore be unacceptable for the council to adopt the slogan 'we do not pay'. the council must pay on time and honour the commitments it makes. the council must be credible, trustworthy and exemplary. we hope that this priority programme, which has been absolutely fundamental to the affirmation of the european project, will continue and that the council will not in future raise any doubts as to whether or not it will pay what it has committed to and what it has undertaken.
the erasmus programme started 25 years ago and has already had about 3 million participants. it is one of the most popular and successful programmes in europe, and it is extremely important that it continues to be so. it is a symbol of the eu and, if it is in danger, it is the very unity of the eu that could be weakened. it is essential that a level of funding be agreed to ensure the continuity of this programme, because all the money that is applied will never be wasted but invested. this is an investment in the skills, the intellectual and cultural training of the young people who will be the future of europe. it is therefore unacceptable that the erasmus programme is in danger, as it is one of the most effective weapons to combat unemployment in europe. the future of europe and the credibility of the european union are at stake. erasmus is a fight to be fought. debts have to be paid and grants made available; it is necessary to qualify young people and to place them in the labour market. i call on the three institutions to make every effort to reach a satisfactory solution as soon as possible. and i call on the council to set an example of rigour. payments due for projects which were budgeted and for which the relevant legal authorization existed cannot be denied.
the erasmus programme is one of the most successful programmes at european level but is currently at risk due to a lack of community funding. at a time of serious difficulties for young people, it is essential to continue to support the mobility of thousands of students between different countries. during the negotiations on the community budget for 2012, the council decided to reduce payment commitments by eur 3 billion and also committed to unlocking the funds if necessary. during the year, the council and the european commission approved numerous projects in different areas such as the projects of the qren, the common agricultural policy, the fisheries, research and innovation fund (fp7) or the erasmus programme. in order for the eu to cover all its financing needs in the most diverse areas of economic and social activity, the community budget needs to be increased by approximately eur 8.3 billion, and the european commission has already put forward a proposal to this effect. i believe it is essential to respect the commitments made to the beneficiaries and to finance the projects that have been approved by the european institutions. we cannot put the erasmus programme in question, a programme which has taken years to consolidate and which is fundamental to the future of the younger generations.
rapporteur. − mr president, i have something important to say and i will be brief. first of all, as rapporteur, i call on the house to consent to this agreement because it is a good one and should be welcomed as a template for future agreements on the same subject. i am hoping for your unanimous support. however, in approving the agreement we are not voting to accept the council decision on this matter while it includes a provision establishing a comitology mechanism allowing the council to control commission decisions on the application of the agreement. in my view, parliament should not accept the council deciding unilaterally on something which, by definition, ought to be co-decided by this house – let alone accept the council abusing comitology to control, unduly and unilaterally, the commission’s powers in relation to application of the agreement. therefore, let it be clear that we are not endorsing the draft council decision on this matter, and that if the draft remains unchanged – which i hope will not be the case – we will not allow it to be considered as a precedent for future international agreements. unfortunately there is no council representative here, but i am sure this message will reach the council.

in writing. - the main objective of this report, like others on international trade, is to bring legislation in this area into line with the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon which have an impact on this area. the amendments tabled by the rapporteur are designed to bring the report into line with the provisions amended by the trade omnibus i amendments to the regulations on the stabilisation and association agreements and the interim agreements. but we cannot fail to appreciate the deeper significance of this report, in the light of the principle positions it takes on the treaty and its provisions on trade policy. the lisbon treaty stipulates that trade policy is an exclusive competence of the eu. the interests in the commercial field are, of course, different from country to country, because the respective economies, fragility and potential of each country are different. the overlapping of the interests of the strongest with those of the weakest, in this and other areas, is detrimental to weaker economies, as in the case of portugal, which is in the hands of the commercial interests of the economic groups of the eu powers, especially germany, which are often opposed to the interests of the national productive fabric.

in writing. - the fisheries sector is vital to the european union (eu), not only for food but also for the environment. sustainable management of fisheries resources is therefore a concern of the eu, especially for endangered species. the european parliament (ep), aware of the importance of this sector, has frequently debated this matter. in 2009, it adopted resolution (206) on the need to conserve fisheries resources in the atlantic ocean and the north sea. it is widely acknowledged that the common fisheries policy has been a failure on the whole. while the management of fisheries within the 12-mile zone, by the member states, has been a success, outside this zone and by brussels it has been a disaster. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the rapporteur on the two aspects mentioned in his conclusion: on the urgency, since the current 12-mile zone regime, although functional, will expire on 31 december, requiring an extension for another two years; and on the framing of this debate in a broader context, namely in the process of reforming the common fisheries policy of the european union.
in writing. the report extends the period of application of the current 12-mile zone access regime (exclusive access reserve). within the framework of existing legislation, article 17 (2) of the current regulation provides for a derogation from the principle of equal access within the 12-nautical-mile zone of each member state. this derogation has been in force since 1 january 2003 and expires on 31 december 2012. since it is more than likely that the reform of the cfp will not be completed by the end of 2012, the commission was forced to present the current proposal in order to avoid the termination of the still existing scheme - of which the commission itself has a very positive assessment. we voted for the report. however, we believe that the principle of reserving access should be permanent and that the area should be extended beyond 12 miles (whereas in the case of the outermost regions this area should include the whole of the exclusive economic zone, i.e. from 100 to 200 miles). the rapporteur has also taken this into account, and we have therefore supported his position. unfortunately, the right and the social democrats have joined forces to make this amendment unworkable, allowing only the extension of the current derogation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy. regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 introduced rules limiting access to fishery resources in the 12-nautical-mile zone, which contributed to its conservation. these derogations would expire on 31 december 2012, and the amendment of that regulation is therefore of the utmost importance at a time of discussion on the common fisheries policy.
in writing. the 12 nautical mile zone was established in 1983 by the first regulation on the common fisheries policy (cfp). council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 provides for a derogation from the principle of equal access within the 12-nautical-mile zone of each member state. as this derogation expires on 31 december 2012, this report proposed a two-year extension to avoid the end of the 12-mile regime, with the intention of extending it until 31 december 2014. the current 12-nautical-mile regime has worked well and has provided protection for the fishing activity of coastal communities. i agree with the reasons given and the urgency of this extension, and therefore i voted in favour of this report on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy.

in writing. - i approve this report, as it expresses parliament's opinion on the proposal for a council directive on the consular protection of citizens of the union abroad, in the context of a consultation procedure. the aim of the proposal is to enable eu citizens to seek help from the diplomatic and consular services of all states when in a third country if their country has no consular representation. the level of protection provided shall be equivalent to that provided by the member state to its own national citizens. it is essential for european union citizens to know that where their member state is not represented in a third country, union citizens can now safely rely on the protection and assistance of the consular services of other member states or european union delegations. this proposal will help to strengthen the sense of belonging to the european union among european citizens throughout the world.
in writing. − under european law, any citizen of the union enjoys, in the territory of third countries where the member state of which he is a national is not represented, protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state, under the same conditions as nationals of that state. in order to facilitate citizens' access to their rights, including the right to protection in third countries, a new legislative instrument is necessary and this directive therefore aims at repealing directive 95/353/ec. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that in crisis situations the european union delegation should be responsible for coordinating and providing assistance in terms of crisis preparedness and coordinating all cooperation, including contingency plans between member states and evacuation, and ensuring that all eu citizens, including unrepresented citizens, are covered by the contingency plans. the union delegation shall have the necessary financial means to carry out the coordination. in order to facilitate future consular protection, member states should consider setting up a 'trust fund' for consular protection.
in writing. − pursuant to article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), any citizen of the union shall, in the territory of a third country where the member state of which he is a national is not represented, be entitled to protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state on the same conditions as nationals of that state. this principle is enshrined in article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights. i believe that to facilitate eu citizens' access to their rights, including the right to protection in third countries, appropriate legislative instruments are needed. it is essential to ensure consular protection at local level and in crisis situations. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − despite the fact that an increasing number of union citizens live and work outside the union, consulates of all 27 member states can be found in only three third countries. the fundamental right, inherent in the concept of european citizenship, that every citizen of an unrepresented member state may obtain assistance from the consular authorities of other member states represented in that third country is therefore important. in order to facilitate access to their rights for eu citizens especially in view of the difficulties they have encountered in practice, in particular in the case of large-scale crises such as the 2004 tsunami, the arab spring in tunisia, egypt and libya, or the 2011 earthquake in japan, which have highlighted the need to provide consular protection to unrepresented citizens , it has become necessary to adopt a new legislative instrument establishing a common approach. i therefore support the adoption of this directive which establishes common concepts and identifies two levels of protection: local consular protection for day-to-day matters, which is left to the member states; and consular protection in crisis situations, where there should be cooperation between member states, under the coordination of eu delegations.
in writing. − consular protection is an integral part of eu policy and a fundamental right conferred by eu citizenship as defined in the treaties. and so i am voting in favour of this report which introduces measures of coordination and cooperation between the member states and the eu, harmonising consular protection concepts and practices and thereby facilitating the lives of european citizens in third countries. i would remind you that under the treaty of lisbon, solidarity between member states provides that a citizen of an unrepresented member state may seek assistance from the consular authorities of other member states who are represented. i welcome the commission's proposal that, by defining accessibility to the embassy or consulate as the time needed to reach and return to the point of departure on the same day, access to consular services is made easier and more accessible to all european citizens, because, whether or not they are represented in the third country, they can go to the nearest service. another example of how 'more europe' means more protection for its citizens. the eu delegation is now responsible for the coordination and provision of consular assistance in crisis situations, another step in the effective implementation of the european external action service!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'consular protection of union citizens abroad' because i regard as positive the possibility for eu citizens not represented in third countries to be able to benefit from consular protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of another member state, in accordance with the principle enshrined in article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. − consular protection of european union citizens outside the eu, in cases where there is no diplomatic representation of the third country of which they are nationals, may be provided by the representation of any other eu member state present there. this applies both to conflict situations and to everyday situations where a citizen needs consular assistance or protection. this is fundamental to guaranteeing the rights of european citizens abroad and an essential element of coordination and solidarity between member states.
in writing. − according to article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, 'all citizens of the union shall enjoy, in the territory of third countries where the member state of which they are nationals is not represented, protection by the diplomatic and consular authorities of any member state, under the same conditions as nationals of that state'. this same right is enshrined in article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). this report, by colleague edit bauer, looks at the proposal for a council directive on the consular protection of citizens of the european union (eu) abroad and provides for two levels of consular protection: at local level in everyday life (loss of identity documents, arrest, detention or death) and in crisis situations. in order not to place a financial burden on the assisting member state (member state), each member state should set up a 'trust fund' from which it can draw the amount needed to cover the costs of supporting the foreign national, which is then reimbursed by the member state whose nationality the supported citizen is. i voted in favour of this report because i recognise the advantages for european citizens in implementing this directive.
in writing. − we agree with the principle of cooperation between states with a view to ensuring better consular protection for citizens of the different european countries. it is well known that the representation of member states in third countries is very uneven and that at the same time there has been a significant increase in the number of europeans travelling and residing outside the eu. the commission proposal is in line with article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights, which states that any citizen of the european union shall enjoy protection in third countries where his member state is not represented by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any other eu member state under the same conditions as nationals of that state. while we support the extension of this directive, we regret that in your proposal the rapporteur has introduced unjustified and unnecessary amendments to the objective of the proposal. changes we cannot support.

in writing. - anti-dumping duties result from an investigation carried out by the commission following a complaint from one or more community producers, if they suspect dumping by certain countries/companies. where, as a result of an investigation, the commission finds that dumping is taking place and that the community is being injured, definitive anti-dumping duties are adopted, normally for a period of five years. however, during this period, the measures may be amended or even repealed. the sampling technique for the purpose of determining met claims was considered to be inapplicable by the court of justice of the european union. this decision should be taken into account and the related legislation should be amended accordingly. the protection of the european economy from unfair practices distorting fair competition must guide the union's action and guide its positions in international trade relations. the commission cannot fail to bear this need in mind.
in writing. - the european union (eu) is a territory with some 500 million consumers, making it a market that is highly attractive to the major economic powers, namely the so-called brics (brazil, russia, india and china). many of the products flooding european markets seek to evade customs controls and avoid recognition and certification processes. in order to prevent european consumers from being misled, the european parliament adopted council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009. this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community. article 1 (2) of the abovementioned regulation provides that 'a product is dumped if its export price to the community is lower than the comparable price of a like product established in the ordinary course of trade for the exporting country'. because i consider it essential to increase legal certainty in defending products from the member states against imports, and in view of the opinion of the committee on international trade, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − this report aims to amend regulation (ec) no 1225/2009. the proposal to amend this regulation follows a judgment of the court of justice of the eu in case c-249/10 p brosmann footwear (hk) and others v council of the european union, which annulled regulation (ec) no 1472/2006 imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty and collecting definitively the provisional duty imposed on imports of certain footwear with uppers of leather originating in china and vietnam. in this judgment, the court of justice ruled that the sampling technique provided for in article 17 of regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 cannot be applied in this case and concluded that the cooperating producers not included in the sample are entitled to have their met claim analysed, whether or not an individual dumping margin should be calculated for these non-sampled companies. the commission considers that this decision would impose a disproportionate administrative burden on the investigators. it therefore considers that regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 should be amended, in particular as regards the three-month time limit. we are not looking at the introduction (now) of any anti-dumping duty. this is the procedural part of the application of regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 before the change of form.

in writing. - in the interests of legal certainty and the principle of good administration, i voted in favour of this report as it is absolutely necessary that these amendments be applied as soon as possible to all new and pending investigations into possible dumping.

in writing. − policy coherence for development (pcd) is enshrined in article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which calls for the reduction and, in the long term, the total eradication of poverty as the number one objective of european development policy. the cpd therefore has a political and human value to which the legal value is added. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu-us joint action on the prevention of and fight against the illicit trade in human beings and the illicit exploitation of sexual and reproductive resources. the eu will not only be contributing to poverty reduction, but will also be encouraging developing countries to build their own trading structures, creating jobs and eventually competing as trading partners of the eu.
in writing. the report under review, by birgit schnieber-jastram, is concerned with the european union (eu) report on policy coherence for development. the aim of development policies is to eradicate poverty throughout the world so that all people have a minimum quality of life, both in terms of security and comfort. to this end, a number of countries have taken a stand and adopted measures to tackle the poverty that should be the shame of so-called modern societies. the millennium development goals, the treaty on the functioning of the european union and, more recently, the europe 2020 strategy, all give priority to reducing and eventually eradicating poverty, which, as we know, mainly affects the most disadvantaged groups, children and women. in view of the opinions of the committee on employment and social affairs, the committee on fisheries and the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i am voting in favour of this report and hope that the recommendations contained in it will be taken into account.
in writing. - we have often drawn attention in this parliament to the problem of policy coherence for development (pcd). we strongly condemn the inconsistency of the eu's sectoral policies with the stated objectives in the field of development cooperation. this report draws attention to several important aspects, which we value, such as: the lack of funding in the area of health; the failure of a substantial part of the fisheries agreements, in particular the weak results achieved in the fields of scientific and technical cooperation and sustainable development of the sector (an aspect which we pointed out in the opinion of the committee on fisheries, for which we were rapporteurs); the importance of policies to promote equality between men and women; the recognition of the right of each country to define its own policies, priorities and strategies in a democratic way. unfortunately, other aspects are either forgotten or not properly addressed. the problem of brain drain (not taking into account the effects of the 'blue card' in developing countries); the persistence of tax havens and the capital flight and economic crime to which they open the door; the question of access to raw materials from developing countries without taking into account the objectives of local development and poverty eradication. these are just a few examples. that is why we abstained.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because: it recognises the inconsistencies that have existed in the policies between the eu and developing countries (dcs) on trade, fisheries, agriculture, energy, migration and climate change, and that have affected the development objectives; it calls for the eu to respect the economic, social and cultural rights of peoples; calls on the commission to include in all eu trade agreements provisions on social matters, full employment, decent work, respect for workers' rights and gender equality, and the promotion of collective bargaining. the eu is called upon to respect the human rights of migrants in its migration policies and not to make development aid dependent on the performance of the developing countries in reducing migration flows. on arms exports, it calls for the eu to require more reliable information from member states and for a legally binding eu code of conduct on arms exports to be developed. the european parliament is called upon to ensure greater political coherence and greater control by the european parliament in the service of development.
in writing. − article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union enshrines the reduction and, eventually, the eradication of poverty, as defined in the european consensus on development, as the first objective of eu development policy, and that the union shall take development cooperation objectives into account in the policies it implements and which are likely to affect developing countries. the eu's efforts in policy coherence for development (pcd) insist that pcd is not just a legal obligation, but responsible, transparent, human rights-based and inclusive policy-making; providing an opportunity for the eu to establish sustainable and equitable partnerships with developing countries, going beyond mere development cooperation. it also stresses that policies aligned with the dpc give governments and societies in developing countries the opportunity and responsibility to generate success for themselves. that is the role of the eu in relation to the cpd, hence my vote in favour.
in writing. − policy coherence for development is not just a legal obligation, but the design of responsible, transparent, human rights-based and inclusive policies that provide an opportunity for the eu to establish sustainable and equitable partnerships with developing countries, while also giving governments and societies in developing countries the opportunity and responsibility to generate success for themselves. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − we agree with some of the 'calls for attention' in the report: the lack of funding in the area of health; the failure of a substantial part of the fisheries agreements, in particular the weak results achieved in the fields of scientific and technical cooperation and sustainable development of the sector; the importance of policies to promote equality between men and women; the recognition of the right of each country to define its own policies, priorities and strategies in a democratic way. on the other hand, the report omits or devalues aspects which we consider essential when we are dealing with the coherence of development policies, namely: the problem of 'brain drain'; the persistence of tax havens and capital flight and economic crime; the question of access to raw materials from developing countries without taking into account the objectives of local development and poverty eradication.
mr president, the european institutions continue to speak emphatically about partial aspects of financial regulation, in this case in relation to the markets associated with commodities. however, does this approach live up to the expectations that the european commission itself created when it came to accepting the end of derived products themselves from 2008 onwards? we are convinced that it is not, that the fight against financial speculation is far short of what is necessary and cannot be done in a partial way, because what would be socially and economically just would be a total fight against the speculative system itself, attacking not only the form but also its content. in this sense, we must not hide the essential facts, but must defend the end of the derivatives market and tax havens, and a truly effective control by political power over financial power. what you're doing here is just putting a tiny grain of sand into a gear that will continue to work in the essentials.
the report by mr gauzès, together with the report we are going to draw up on the annual growth prospects for the union at the end of this year, and which will precede the spring council, are two essential parts of the so-called european semester. this report deals with the recommendations made to each of the member states by the council, on a proposal from the commission, and these recommendations form, as has just been said, with the six pack and the future two pack, an extraordinarily strong body which strengthens european control over the economic and budgetary policy of the member states. the balance between this control and autonomy and legitimacy at national level is not easy to find and it has fallen to a level of imposition, above all, of discipline and, in the last resort, may even give rise to a serious package of sanctions. i would like to make a brief comment on the two pack, namely that it is important for the council, which is absent today, to give its negotiators a negotiating mandate compatible with the ambition to conclude this package, this two pack, quickly. but more european coordination, to return to the subject, means less control by countries over their own destiny, which requires a subtle balance but also an increased demand with the quality of the recommendations that are made to countries in at least three or four dimensions. first, it is important to ensure coherence between the medium and long-term objectives, which include growth, employment and real convergence, and the short-term recommendations, which focus mainly on discipline and nominal convergence; secondly, there must be consistency with the conclusions to be drawn from the analysis on macroeconomic imbalances, in particular on the asymmetric impact of common policies and negative externalities, the indirect effects of some national policies on other countries; thirdly, we must agree that there is a minimum threshold of social, economic and labour rights which cannot be exceeded by these recommendations, and lastly, it is important that the quality of the recommendations be measured in terms of the results achieved, which has not been the case so far. i would like to conclude, mr president, by thanking mr gauzès for his spirit of cooperation and hope that he will take a further step in that spirit, so as to widen the basis of consensus around his report and that this spirit will also remain with regard to the next report we are going to discuss.
i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european semester is not delayed. we all know that the treaties impose limits on trade surpluses, and we all know that germany does not comply with them. that is a fact. there is no lack of recommendations from the european commission in this respect and germany does not follow the recommendations, and frankly, i do not hear anyone saying anything about this. my question is, where are the sanctions? on the other hand, it is proposed that sanctions should be accepted as a matter of course for countries which do not meet the deficit and debt targets laid down in the treaties, and everyone seems to agree on this. it's that they're all too strong for the weak but too weak for the strong. as long as no sanctions are applied to countries which have trade surpluses because they have violated the treaties, and we agree that they would be better able to pay them because their violation is to accumulate surpluses, i think it is immoral to take for granted that countries which have violated the treaties should also be automatically made to pay for accumulating deficits, and even for that reason they have much more difficulty paying. this is not democratic. even as regards compliance with the deficit and debt, the rule does not apply to everyone, because we know very well that it is immediate for the countries which are under troika intervention, but the same does not apply to the countries of central or northern europe which do not meet the same criteria. and this is not democratic! and finally, only when we can bring some justice to all this will we achieve the much-needed real economic coordination. until then we shall always be putting more emphasis on the implementation of measures which are based exclusively on budget cuts, privatisation of public services and blatant tax increases. this is the revenue, without adding or subtracting, and i will end here, mr president, this is the revenue, without adding or subtracting, which is being applied to the state budgets of the countries under intervention. and for these citizens the european semester is synonymous with injustice and poverty, in portugal, in a single european semester, we have managed to go back decades in terms of rights.
the joy with which the majority of this parliament speaks of the european semester can only be the result of an exercise in denying the reality that is out there. we cannot even speak of the fact that the elected bodies of national sovereignty are prevented from deciding sovereignly on the destiny of their country, a decision which no one has ever asked the people to make, but let us first discuss the content of these recommendations. the rhetoric of the need for growth and jobs is often repeated, but what is certain is that the recommendations themselves in the framework of the european semester are the ones that require a reduction in public investment, privatisation and, in several countries such as portugal, a reduction in the level of wages, when already one third of portuguese people earn less than 600 euros. in other words, what the commission and the council are recommending is more recession, more unemployment and more poverty. reality is out there, and you can prove it. you just don't want to see it, you don't care to see it.
in writing. the european semester, which the right wing and social democrats praise, was set up to 'coordinate economic policies'. something "fundamental" in these times of crisis in the eu, they say. almost everyone speaks of "coordination" as an end in itself. they hide the essential: coordination around what and by what means? the commission is trying to answer that. the recommendations for portugal are clear: lower wages (in the country with the lowest wages in the eu); reduce the duration of unemployment benefits (when they reach historical levels and when long-term unemployment increases); more measures to 'flex' labour relations (i.e. to raise the level of exploitation to the level of the 19th century). we also know what the means are: reducing national parliaments - the power structures closest to the citizens and best controlled by them - to mere words to fill in, puppets of the european institutions, to whose examination they have to submit their budgetary options, subjecting themselves to prior censorship. the objectives of this 'european semester', which represents a dangerous attack on democracy (even if it is understood only in a purely formal sense), are clear: to 'coordinate' a violent retreat of civilization in europe, levelling living and working conditions on the continent.
in the first half of the 1990s, the european commission carried out a number of studies which set out minimum values for the community budget in order to achieve the objective of cohesion. these studies said that a budget of at least 2% of the european union's gdp was needed. almost 20 years after the biggest enlargement in the history of the european union, which has increased internal differences significantly, the budget is half that and there are still those who want to reduce it. they now want to ensure that, by some miracle of the multiplication of loaves, even by reducing the budgetary appropriations, more funds can be made available. there are many questions that arise with these financial instruments. the report also acknowledges the failure of the public financing of private profits and risks to be applied in cohesion policy in many countries. we should not waste time inventing apparently innovative instruments which only increase differences, inflate financial markets and hide the real ways in which the necessary increase in the community budget could and should have been implemented long ago.

in writing. - the recommendation under consideration, by béla kovács, concerns the proposal for a council decision on the signing and conclusion of the agreement between the government of the united states of america (usa) and the european union (eu) on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment. the existing agreement between the eu and the us expired on 31 december 2011. however, the previous month, bilateral negotiations to continue the energy star programme for another five years had been concluded. this programme, created by the us environmental protection agency, aims to improve the energy efficiency of office equipment and was applied to the eu in 2006 when the eu/us agreement on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment was renewed. however, the us decided to shift the certification to third parties, and the principle of mutual certification no longer applies. given the extreme importance of environmental issues, particularly in terms of energy saving, and given that the energy star programme has proven to be very effective in making changes to office equipment to increase its energy efficiency, i am voting in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. the report approves the conclusion of an agreement to extend the energy star programme, set up by the us environmental protection agency (epa) to improve the energy efficiency of office equipment. since 2000, the eu and the us have agreed to coordinate their labelling programmes for five years, renewing it for a second period in 2006. the programme was managed by the european commission and epa, including cooperation in the development of product specifications and mutual recognition of eu and us registered products. the rapporteur, while agreeing to the extension of this programme, notes, however, that the principle of mutual recognition will no longer apply, due to the introduction of third party certification in the usa. the european commission considers, however, that this will not have a particular impact on european smes (the commission guarantees that european manufacturers tend to sell in the european market in the vast majority and that large exporters have already registered their products in the us), and it is therefore preferable to keep the simpler procedures of self-certification in the eu in order to avoid additional costs for manufacturers, in particular smes. the report was adopted by consensus in the committee on industry. we voted in favour.
in writing. − the energy star programme was set up by the united states environmental protection agency (epa) to improve the energy efficiency of office equipment. in 2000, the eu and the us signed an agreement on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment. the agreement, which was renewed in 2006 for a second five-year period, provides for the implementation of the energy star programme in the eu. thus, the programme was managed jointly by epa and the commission, including cooperation in the development of product specifications and mutual recognition of products registered in the eu and the us. under the new agreement, there will be two independent product registration systems in the eu, which retains self-certification by manufacturers, and the us, which has decided to move to third party certification. the principle of mutual recognition therefore no longer applies. the provisions concerning the respective responsibilities of the commission and the member states for the implementation of the programme have also been clarified. there are no other significant changes to the current text. hence my vote.

in writing. − this proposal uses the already open window for transferring unused funds from the eu budget to the creation of the so-called financial instruments (fi), to give them a more instrumental role in the priorities for the next financial framework. the ifs are nothing more than instruments for the transfer of funds that were public (such as the cohesion fund) to the financial (and speculative) sphere. the majority of meps want to go further than before, by extending its scope to 'projects, groups of projects or parts of programmes which will generate profits' through public-private partnerships (public funding and private profit). these instruments and the funds - the commission estimates that €1.6 trillion will be needed by 2020 to tackle the seven thematic initiatives of the eu 2020 strategy - will be used to finance major infrastructure projects, which will serve to consolidate the 'single market' and its beneficiaries. in parallel, the eu's direct participation in the capital of infrastructure projects is advocated. the chronic shortage of the community budget is now being compounded by other risks, such as the even more unequal distribution of its resources, with (even greater) weakening of the objectives of cohesion.

in writing. − the european ombudsman is competent to receive complaints concerning maladministration in the activities of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. on 22 may 2012, it presented its 2011 annual report, which showed that it had helped more than 22 000 citizens, of whom 2 510 had lodged complaints, 1 284 had requested information and 18 274 had obtained advice through the interactive guide. the significant reduction in requests for information received in recent years demonstrates the success of the interactive guide. it is also worth noting that the number of investigations opened against parliament has decreased significantly compared to 2010. despite the success, the number of complaints processed in 2011 was again relatively modest (around 27%). more comprehensive and proactive citizen awareness projects should therefore be envisaged, all eu actors are urged to act in accordance with the european code of good administrative behaviour and the ombudsman should continue to ensure the best use of resources. the full exercise of rights by eu citizens, including the right to complain, is seen as essential to the realisation of the european project. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − in the common effort to bring the european institutions closer to the citizens, the european ombudsman plays a key role. the greater clarity and openness of the european administration is a win-win for its action and citizens have the assurance that their rights are defended, their complaints heard and their doubts clarified also at union level. the annual report of the provider shall reflect this effort and the initiatives taken to this end. i record their number and their quality and how they knew how to interpret their function. however, there are still doubts about the scope of its powers which need to be clarified.
in writing. − the european ombudsman's role is to receive complaints about maladministration in the activities of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and to deal with them as he sees fit. it submits an annual report on its activities to the european parliament (ep). the annual report for 2011 was handed over to the president of the ep, martin schulz, on 22 may. according to the same, we found that there was a slight decrease in the number of complaints submitted, 2 510 (less 157 than in 2011), of which only 698 (27%) fell within their competence. i welcome the work of the european ombudsman and welcome the innovations introduced, in particular the success of the interactive guide available on the website, which allows citizens to obtain the information they want in real time, without leaving their homes and without a formal request. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by my colleague erminia mazzoni and i congratulate the ombudsman on all the efforts he has made to bring his procedures closer to the citizen.
in writing. − the european ombudsman's annual report 2011 gives an account of his work, presents statistics on complaints received, numbers of inquiries carried out, among other information. the total number of complaints received was 2510, which led the ombudsman to launch 396 inquiries, of which 58% were directed at the european commission and 11% at the european personnel selection office. the average duration of the investigations was 10 months. in addition to these complaints, 1 284 people requested information and 18 274 obtained advice through the interactive guide on the ombudsman's website. the ombudsman's mandate has been extended - an inseparable process from the (undemocratic) concentration of new powers and competences in the eu, to which the lisbon treaty paved the way. it has now included possible maladministration in the context of the common foreign and security policy, including the common security and defence policy. the main types of alleged maladministration were questions of illegality, including refusal of information, bias, unsatisfactory procedures, avoidable delay, discrimination and letter replies in a language other than that of the complainants. in general, the ombudsman's intervention was useful, and the efforts made to facilitate the submission of complaints, which the report rightly points out, were noteworthy.
in writing. − the 2011 annual report was presented to the president of the european parliament, martin schulz, and subsequently to parliament's committee on petitions, the committee responsible for relations with the parliament. since there is nothing to object to or point out by the committee on petitions, i voted in favour of this report which gives an account of the european ombudsman's activity throughout 2011.
in writing. − the european parliament approved the annual report 2011 presented by the european ombudsman, noting that the ombudsman helped over 22 000 citizens, of whom 2 510 lodged complaints, 1 284 requested information and 18 274 obtained advice. i welcomed the fact that the number of inquiries opened by the ombudsman against parliament had decreased by more than half compared to 2010, and i voted in favour of the document.
