in writing. - i approve this report. the texts deal with various aspects of the structure of financial markets, the instruments and the actors, and in my view they represent a very important step towards increasing transparency and ensuring a good price formation process on european stock exchanges. we must ensure that transparency requirements are increased for high-frequency trading firms so that everyone is aware of their technical trading. another very important issue is the so-called commodities and agricultural derivatives: this is an important policy issue and it is important to have provisions to reduce speculation in food markets. there should therefore be more transparency requirements and stricter rules for the rights of asset managers vis-à-vis their clients, and strict limitations should be introduced for the practice of so-called 'incentives'. on this last point, member states will have the option of prohibiting incentives. this is a text with a good compromise and a strong starting point for starting negotiations with the council. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the financial interests of the union.
in writing. − this directive aims to regulate the provision of investment services in financial markets by banks and investment firms or others regularly engaged in investment activities on a professional basis. the european commission proposes a revision of the mifid directive to promote more efficient, resilient and transparent financial markets and strengthen investor protection. achieving these objectives requires the establishment of common regulatory requirements for investment firms in the european union ensuring the full functioning of the single market. this directive will bring numerous benefits by creating more structured and robust markets, better managing the framework for technological innovation in the functioning of capital markets, increasing transparency and facilitating the supervision of capital markets. all these measures will make it possible to better protect investors in the market. in this connection, and considering that the adoption of this legislation is a fundamental step in the regulation of the eu's financial markets in order to correct its shortcomings and improve the transparency and regulation of financial markets, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. − following the profound changes in financial instruments markets in recent years, and in response to the declaration by leaders at the g20 summit in 2009, the european commission has put forward a set of proposals to strengthen the rules applied to these markets. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the organised trading systems (otfs) which are playing an increasingly active role in these markets are now regulated, and it has been decided to create a separate brand for capital markets, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, to facilitate access to alternative financing. these proposals will allow for more transparency in financial markets, strengthen the role and power of national supervisors and esma, and allow for more accountability of investment institutions through the introduction of corporate governance principles. finally, i would like to congratulate and follow up the conclusions of my colleague, markus ferber, on this important dossier.

in writing. − the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid) has been in force since 2007, but since then the emergence of new products and the financial crisis in 2008 have highlighted gaps in the functioning and transparency of these markets, leading to the need for a review of the legislation. in this regard, the new legislation aims to increase the transparency and supervision of unregulated markets, otfs and mtfs, such as the regulation of high frequency trading, the introduction of limits on the trading of derivatives that are now carried out on regulated platforms, as well as the revision of investor protection measures, the consolidation of information and provisions on existing products. while much remains to be done in financial regulation, this proposal allows for greater regulation of new trading platforms and financial products, which was almost non-existent until now. i voted yes.
in writing. − in recent years, the number of investors present on financial markets has increased, offering them an increasingly wide and complex range of services and instruments. in view of these developments, the legal framework of the european union should cover the full range of investor-oriented activities. to that end, it is essential to provide for the degree of harmonisation necessary to provide investors with a high level of protection and to allow investment firms to provide services throughout the european union within the framework of a single market on the basis of home country supervision. the financial crisis has revealed shortcomings in the functioning and transparency of financial markets. developments in financial markets have highlighted the need to strengthen the regulatory framework for markets in financial instruments, including situations where trading in those markets is conducted over-the-counter, in order to increase transparency, better protect investors, enhance confidence, address unregulated areas and ensure that supervisors are given appropriate powers to perform their tasks. that is the aim of this regulation, and that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − i approve of this report, considering that the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid), in force since november 2007, is one of the cornerstones of eu financial regulation and i recognise the need for a revision of the current mifid (hereinafter referred to as mifid ii) in order to correct its shortcomings. since then, however, two developments have occurred which have revealed the need for improvements: firstly, financial markets have evolved, for example with the emergence of new products. second, the 2008 financial crisis and the period that followed have highlighted shortcomings in the functioning and transparency of those markets, as well as in the ability of mifid to address them. drawing the necessary lessons, the european commission has proposed that mifid be revised. i hereby approve the proposed new legislation, which consists of two different legal instruments, a directive (mifid) and a regulation on markets in financial instruments (hereinafter referred to as mifir), which should be examined together. i would like to note that i agree with the rapporteur's view that in future discussions more attention should be paid to the impact of the mifir regulation on non-financial corporations.
in writing. − together with the mifid directive, this regulation forms the legal framework governing the requirements applicable to investment firms, regulated markets and data service providers in order to enhance transparency and improve the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments. the application of a regulation ensures that the requirements are directly applicable to investment firms and provides a level playing field for all, avoiding divergent national requirements resulting from the transposition of a directive. the rules will therefore be applied uniformly throughout the european union and to all market players. financial instruments will be able to be traded on regulated markets through multilateral trading facilities (mtfs) and organised trading facilities (otfs), also bringing more transparency to the market. ensuring a more efficient and assertive functioning of the high-frequency markets will also be an advantage of this new legislation. in view of the advances and improvements in the market brought about by this legislation, i am voting in favour of this report.

in writing. the new regulation on markets in financial instruments is intended to take a further step towards greater regulation and supervision of markets. the main objective of this proposal is to establish uniform requirements in all member states for the public disclosure of trading data and the reporting of transactions; the commission will also be able to use the new rules to ensure that the rules on the trading of derivatives are applied in a transparent manner. this regulation provides for the introduction of position limits or alternative arrangements in relation to derivative financial instruments associated with commodities (e.g. food and energy goods), which could facilitate price formation and the efficient hedging of price risks to which producers and consumers are exposed and thus prevent and correct asset bubbles and other distortions. although much remains to be done in financial regulation, this proposal allows a large number of products which until now were traded on unregulated markets to be subject to stricter rules. i abstained.

on behalf of the s&d group, mr president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr jan mulder, on his demanding guidance, perseverance and the interaction he has maintained throughout the process with all the shadow rapporteurs. this regulation on the marketing and use of explosives precursors represents a step forward in the safety of europeans, because it limits and seeks to control access to dangerous substances used for the domestic manufacture of explosives. unfortunately, examples of terrorist attacks with these homemade bombs are on the rise in europe. it is therefore incredible that the council, that is to say our member states, took so long to reach a conciliatory position with the european parliament to adopt this regulation on the basis of the proposal, even though it came from the commission. after the breivik attack in norway last year, using precisely a homemade bomb, one would think that the council would take the safety of citizens more seriously. instead, bureaucratic chapels and corporate interests prevailed. interestingly, germany is the only country to be exempted, albeit temporarily, from a tight licensing system for the purchase of these chemicals that could be used in the manufacture of homemade bombs on the grounds that its registration system works very well. the message from parliament is clear: the safety of citizens must be given priority. terrorists exploit our vulnerabilities and it is therefore urgent that this regulation should enter into force quickly, that member states should transpose it into national law and that they should adapt their control and security systems to the new european standards governing access to explosive precursors. legitimate and justified access to these chemicals is guaranteed by this regulation, but the aim here is not to protect the right to market and buy dangerous substances. the ultimate objective of this regulation is to raise the security standard in the accessibility and use of explosive precursors for criminal purposes by ensuring their traceability and ensuring that tragedies such as norway in 2011 or london in 2005 are not repeated.

mr president, the crisis is inseparable from the deepening of economic and monetary union and the single market, which has had profound consequences in destroying the productive apparatus of the countries with the weakest economies, in accentuating and creating production deficits, which have generated budget deficits, and in increasing public debts. in other words, contrary to the propaganda around the euro and the economic and monetary union, these instruments have not only proved to be a shield against the crisis, as they said, and a weapon to confront capitalist globalization, but have revealed with great clarity their true purpose - their instrumental character to face the growing world competition between capitalist monopolies. the destruction of the sovereignty and independence of countries has proved to be inseparable from the process of fusion of economic and political power, which has accentuated the differences and the deepening of uneven development that particularly affects countries with peripheral economies. the report seeks to centralize these powers even further, and it also argues that the european supervisor should be able to put an end to financial institutions, that is, to manage the process of monopolizing financial capital as he sees fit. we need a monetary instrument for economic growth and employment, for the benefit of workers.
emu is a project of european big business, aiming at the reduction of unit labour costs (the real objective behind price stability), a greater liberalisation of capital movements and, consequently, a greater mobility of multinational capital in search of better conditions for the exploitation of labour and domination of markets within the european area. the consequences are obvious: deterioration of living and working conditions; a decrease in the weight of wages in national income; the destruction of production systems and marked deindustrialization in the peripheral countries, as they become consumers of the surplus production of the central countries. emu is inseparable from the increase in macroeconomic imbalances between the different countries of the euro area, inseparable from the indebtedness of net importing states. the path has proved unsustainable, but those who have benefited from it do not want to do without it. so in a real leap forward, they want to delve deeper into the instrument that has served their interests so well. it is typical of the eu: each new step in integration seeks to legitimize the previous one and justify the next one. and what follows is more centralization of political and economic power, new steps in the development of a monopoly capitalism on a european scale, more attacks on the sovereignty of the peoples and on democracy.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the brussels i regulation provides clear rules for access to justice and is of great importance to citizens and businesses. in an increasingly globalised world, where european citizens live and work outside the european union, it is vital to uphold their fundamental right of access to justice and to avoid discrimination on the basis of domicile. i would also like to stress our efforts as s&d group members to introduce proposals for a new rule of jurisdiction for disputes relating to industrial action, individual employment contracts, and disputes relating to the infringement of privacy and the right to personality. these proposals reinforce an essential aspect, because in a globalised world, apart from the simple rights of citizens, there is a need to analyse labour disputes and the socioeconomic consequences for workers, in order to move towards a fairer europe.
in writing. - after two years of intense and complex negotiations, i am pleased that an agreement has finally been reached, which i consider to be generally positive. the brussels i regulation of 2002, which is the foundation of judicial cooperation in civil matters in the eu, is thus revised to determine the most appropriate jurisdiction for the settlement of cross-border disputes and to ensure the easy recognition and enforcement of judgments given in another member state. despite the enormous improvements introduced by this regulation, there are still gaps that need to be addressed in order to facilitate cross-border litigation and the free movement of judicial decisions in the eu, with a view to developing a genuine european area of justice, serving citizens and businesses. there is no doubt that among the 27 member states sharing the single market, the exequatur procedure has become a mere formality, and it makes crossborder litigation more time-consuming and costly. i therefore agree with its abolition, without any exceptions for the sake of legal certainty, although it is essential that the safeguards for the protection of the rights of the defence be maintained. i also believe that the effectiveness of the agreements on the allocation of powers has been substantially improved.

in writing. - i am aware of the enormous importance of council regulation (ec) no 44/2001 in the field of private international law and of the need for an appropriate legal framework to enable the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the recognition and enforcement of decisions outside the issuing member state is essential for the protection of the interests of citizens and businesses and for legal certainty in the internal market.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr tadeus zwiefka, deals with the proposal for a recast of the european parliament and council regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the right to enforce a judgment is fundamental as a guarantee of the protection of citizens' rights. there is no point in going ahead with the initiation of a judicial procedure, taking into account the financial and time costs, when, after having been informed of the judgment, it is not possible to enforce it. i therefore welcome the adoption of this regulation on the approximation of national judicial systems by the ep after three years of debate and hope that the process will be completed at the next european council in december, which will allow the free movement of judgments and thus help to consolidate the european union (eu). the extension of the right to citizens of third countries is very important as it will increase the efficiency of the courts by simplifying procedures and reducing costs. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which is intended to reform the judicial systems by making justice quicker and less burdensome.
in writing. - the commission proposal proposes amendments and recasting of the current regulation (no 44/2001), removing certain parts which it considers to be obstacles to the free application of judicial decisions in line with the principle of mutual recognition. in this connection, it proposes - and the rapporteur supports - the abolition of the exequatur procedure, i.e. that a judgment given by a court in one member state should be recognised by another member state without recourse to any other procedure. this is a further step towards the harmonization of legislative procedures which call into question the independence of national courts. we have to be very careful not to let the commission and the council of ministers get involved in this.
in writing. − for the protection of the interests of citizens, businesses and the legal certainty of the internal market, the recognition and enforcement of decisions outside the member state is essential. the adoption of this report is therefore essential for the existence of a legal framework allowing for the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters.

in writing. − i approve this report, as the purpose of this regulation is to restrict access by the general public to chemicals of high risk and with the potential to be used for the production of household explosives. i believe that in these times it is increasingly necessary to adopt a preventive attitude to protect european citizens. the crisis and austerity, as well as the international climate and the geostrategic situation in europe, force us to take precautionary measures aimed at the welfare of the general population. we cannot ignore the reality in europe and the world: some fear, frustration and unrest, because instability has taken over the economy and thus the whole of society in much of europe, which is living under extreme austerity measures. in addition, it should be stressed that europe, as an international actor with a foreign policy, must take account of the need to take account of attacks and other acts of terrorism or attacks on the general population on the basis of political and cultural principles, values and ideas. we must therefore safeguard the immunity and well-being of the peoples of europe at all costs.
in writing. the commission's proposal aims to limit the general public's access to specific substances for general use, but which can also be misused as explosives precursors, and thus reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks. professional users of these materials and sales between companies will not be affected. i voted in favour of this report because i support the measures to combat terrorism and i agree with the overall rationale of the proposal.
in writing. - i support the commitment reached at first reading with the council that it should make a significant contribution to reducing the risks of illicit use of certain chemicals which are widely available on the market and within the reach of the general public. in 2006, we adopted the reach regulation for chemicals from a safety perspective, but safety issues related to chemical precursors for explosives were, exceptionally, left out of its scope. we must not forget that homemade explosives, made from certain chemical precursors that are easily accessible to the public, are, according to europol, the preferred instrument for carrying out terrorist attacks. a common european approach is therefore urgently needed to avoid different levels of regulation, which lead to gaps in safety and distort the functioning of the internal market. only in this way will we be able to significantly reduce the risk of misuse of certain chemical precursors for the production of homemade explosives by prohibiting the unauthorised sale to the public of certain chemicals above certain concentration thresholds. this regulation should also be accompanied by a whole range of measures to be taken by manufacturers and retailers to improve safety and raise awareness throughout the supply chain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the application of measures which help to reduce the risks and limit access to a range of highly concentrated chemicals by the general public. it is necessary to control access to certain items, such as precursors of homemade explosives, which are not only dangerous but are also commonly used by terrorists and other criminals in their attacks.
in writing. the proposal we are voting on today is a regulation which limits the general public's access to specific substances which could be misused as explosives precursors. while i tend to favour legislative frameworks which do not restrict individual freedom, i believe that in some circumstances the protection of public security recommends some restrictions on that freedom. this is the case here, where the protection of citizens against terrorism recommends that restrictions be imposed on the marketing and use of products which can be used in the manufacture of explosives.
in writing. - with the spread of new information technologies and the advent of the internet, we are only a click away from a set of data which, manipulated by unscrupulous people, can jeopardise the safety of people and property. we all remember the massacre (85 dead) in norway, more specifically on the island of utøya, of young people attending a labour party summer camp, and the car bombing that killed seven people in the norwegian capital just two hours earlier. the ease with which we access inside information and certain dual-use items is conducive to terrorist activity and it is urgent to restrict such access, as the security of states and citizens is at stake. i voted in favour of the report by mr jan mulder on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the marketing and use of explosives precursors, because measures are needed which are widespread in all member states and which prevent indiscriminate and uncontrolled access to substances which can be used in the manufacture of weapons of home origin. because terrorism and crime are cross-border, i am aware that this will be a major step in order to prevent further terrorist attacks within the european union.
in writing. - there are important steps to be taken in the field of marketing and use of explosives precursors. the commission has taken steps, in particular, to improve safety levels for workers and to protect the environment. this report aims to move in this direction, but not without limitations and contradictions. we welcome the provision of a safeguard clause to allow any member state that so wishes to apply stricter measures in respect of certain substances or mixtures of substances, as well as to decide that it will not allow private individuals to have access to any of the substances in question. once again we criticise the view of the free movement of chemicals and mixtures in the internal market and the need to correct the distortions of competition underlying the report.
in writing. - i am not in favour of legislation which may restrict individual freedom, but in some cases it is necessary. this is the case with this report which limits the general public's access to certain substances that could be misused as explosives precursors. the protection of citizens against the practice of terrorism is at issue here, hence the restrictions approved here on the marketing and use of certain products which may be used in the manufacture of explosives.
in writing. the commission proposal is a regulation which limits the general public's access to specific substances for general use, but which can also be misused as precursors to explosives. in order to protect the free movement of goods, eight substances listed in annex i may continue to be placed on the market in a concentrated form, subject to the holding of a licence issued by a national competent authority for a documented legitimate purpose or, in the absence of a licence, at concentration levels which render them unfit for the manufacture of homemade explosives. in view of the balance of the well-founded proposal, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the aim of this proposal is to restrict the general public's access to high-risk chemicals which could be misused in the production of homemade explosives. the aim is to reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks by limiting access to raw materials and by reporting suspicious transactions involving substances that, in high concentrations, can be used in the manufacture of explosives. the proposal therefore provides for a ban on the sale to the general public of certain chemicals at concentration levels above the established limits. sales of higher concentrations will only be allowed to users who can document a legitimate need to use the chemicals. the report also proposes a set of obligations on the sale of these chemicals and their mixtures, including the notification of suspicious transactions. the annex to the regulation clearly distinguishes between substances and their maximum concentration limits. this is a proposal in line with the community policy objectives set out for the eu counter-terrorism strategy, the eu action plan to improve the safety of explosives, and the stockholm programme an open and secure europe serving and protecting the interests of citizens. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − on 18 april 2008, the council decided to set up a standing committee on precursors to consider the measures to be taken and to prepare some recommendations on the legislation applicable to explosives precursors available on the market, taking into account the cost-benefit effects. the committee identified some explosives precursors that could be used in terrorist attacks and urged the european union to take appropriate action. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary for member states to adopt legislative measures concerning certain substances which are used in unlawful circumstances, thus ensuring protection against the unlawful use of explosives precursors of a similar or higher grade. i also believe that this regulation is fundamental to regulating european standards with regard to placing on the market, possession, use and introduction into the eu. it is positive that these resources are limited to the public and that proper reporting of suspicious transactions is ensured throughout the supply chain.
in writing. − in a context where the private monopoly of their production persists, it is difficult, if not impossible, to improve the free movement of chemicals and mixtures in the internal market and to correct distortions of competition while ensuring high levels of worker safety and environmental protection. it has long been known - and reality has shown - that the pursuit of maximum profit is incompatible with the necessary rationality in the production and distribution of production by human beings. explosive precursors are not off the hook. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the right to vote on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. we are, however, pleased that a safeguard clause is included in the framework of liberalisation, allowing any member state that so wishes to apply stricter measures to certain substances or mixtures of substances, and to decide that it will not allow private individuals to have access to any of the substances in question.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the consumer credit directive, a directive which pursues two objectives: a high level of consumer protection and the strengthening of the crossborder internal market for consumer credit. the level of consumer protection has been greatly increased in europe through the partially exhaustive harmonisation of some essential components of credit law. however, the increase in the contraction of consumer credit appears to be insignificant. this may be due to the fact that only a few credit institutions offer credit to cross-border consumers and that in recent years the market has been in recession due to the financial market crisis. moreover, obstacles to cross-border consumer credit are more due to language problems or the lack of a personal contact with the financial institution than to the legal area. the present review aims to put an end to some problems identified during the review, namely: publicity, pre-contractual information, contractual information, right of withdrawal, early reimbursement and calculation of the annual overall effective rate of charges.
in writing. − the consumer credit directive has two objectives: to achieve a high level of consumer protection and to promote the strengthening of the crossborder internal market for consumer credit. if, on the one hand, we see in europe an increase in the level of consumer protection through the harmonization of rules on the right to credit, on the other hand, we also see that cross-border taking out of consumer credit has not increased since the entry into force of the directive. this can be explained by the effects of the economic downturn on consumption and the shortage of institutions offering credit to cross-border consumers. the commission should therefore, before proposing to parliament any necessary amendments, review the transposition and put pressure on member states to implement the directive, and present to parliament and the council an evaluation report on the implementation of the directive and a comprehensive assessment of its impact on consumer protection, taking into account the consequences of the financial crisis and the new eu legal framework on financial services.

in writing. − the global art market is estimated to be worth around usd 12 billion by 2012, and its creators or heirs should be fairly compensated. it sometimes happens that a work of art is successively traded increasing its value exponentially without any benefit to its author or heirs. the report under review, by marielle gallo, deals with the application and effects of the right of way directive. the 'right of succession' is the prerogative which any author of a work of art has to share in the price of successive sales of his work. the exercise of this right at european union (eu) level was harmonised on 1 january 2006. although there has been a breakdown in the european art market, a causal link with the entry into force of this directive cannot be established. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims, on the one hand, to ensure that authors of graphic and visual artworks have a financial share in the successive transactions of their works and, on the other, to harmonise the application of copyright law throughout the eu.

in writing. - rule 70 of parliament's rules of procedure, on interinstitutional negotiations in legislative procedures, provides as follows: '1. negotiations with the other institutions for an agreement during the legislative procedure shall be conducted in accordance with the code of conduct for the negotiation of ordinary legislative procedures; 2. before entering into such negotiations, the committee responsible for the subject-matter shall, in principle, take a decision by a majority of its members and adopt a mandate, guidelines or priorities; if the negotiations lead to a compromise with the council after the committee has adopted the report, the committee shall in any event be consulted again before the vote in plenary.' the conference of committee chairmen, after extensive discussion and after receiving input from the secretaries-general of the political groups, asked the committee on constitutional affairs to review the above-mentioned article. whereas this proposal to amend rule 70 of the ep's rules of procedure aims to make the procedures 'more efficient, more transparent and more inclusive by incorporating some key elements of the code of conduct for the negotiation of the ordinary legislative procedure', i voted in favour.
in writing. - the amendments to the rules of procedure of the european parliament introduced by this report seek to legalise an interinstitutional negotiating process which has been abused and which is in the interests of the major political groups: the right and the social democrats. the concertation between these forces undermines the transparency of the discussion processes. this is not a democratic change in the way parliament works - which would be very necessary - but rather a change in the rules of procedure which, among other things, allows, where the committee responsible deems it duly justified, for negotiations to begin before the report has been adopted by the committee responsible. in other words, negotiations are started in the trilogue without groups like ours having had the opportunity to put forward any proposals. the big groups are in agreement, everything is moving forward. this is an amendment which limits the ability of groups like ours to intervene, propose and denounce, breaking with this consensus which also dominates the other eu institutions and which is, after all, responsible for the process of civilizational regression that is taking place in europe today.
in writing. − the revision of rule 70 aims to make the procedures more effective, more transparent and more inclusive by incorporating some key elements of the code of conduct for the negotiation of the ordinary legislative procedure into the binding part of the rules of procedure. these amendments make the legislative process more transparent, which is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the committee on constitutional affairs was asked by the conference of presidents of the european parliament to revise rule 70 of the rules of procedure with a view to making the procedures more effective, transparent and inclusive by incorporating some key elements of the code of conduct for the negotiation of the ordinary legislative procedure into the binding part of the rules of procedure, and in particular the parts on: the decision of a committee to open negotiations; the decision on the composition and mandate of the negotiating team; the regular provision of information to the committee concerned on the progress and outcome of the negotiations, including the agreement reached and the re-consultation of the committee on the agreed text, before the vote in plenary. the public nature of debates and votes is linked to democratic accountability: if voters cannot know what their elected representatives have said, and cannot know the meaning of their vote, they cannot hold them accountable in the next election. the transparency measures proposed here are to be commended and i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − since the financial crisis began in 2007, the g20 has decided to take a number of regulatory measures to make the financial system safer and more sustainable. much legislation has been developed within the financial sector, but the shadow banking system has fallen behind the developments in the rest of the financial system, remaining outside the regulatory perimeter. the european commission has therefore launched a green paper which opens up the debate on the regulation of this sector, which involves activities such as repurchase transactions, securities lending and securitisation operations. the activity of the shadow banking system can create a lot of instability in financial markets if it is not regulated and supervised and in this regard the commission is committed to producing guidelines that increase the full transparency of the activities of this sector and keep under control the potential for increased systemic risk. the european commission is also urged to set up mechanisms to better analyse risk transfer in the financial sector. i voted in favour of this report because it is clear that there is a need to establish rules to supervise and define the rules for the functioning of the shadow banking system and to support greater stability, soundness and transparency of the financial system.
in writing. − since the financial crisis began in 2007, the g20 has decided to take a number of regulatory measures to make the financial system safer and more sustainable. among other measures, capital requirements for financial institutions were tightened, a first step towards stricter regulation of credit rating agencies was taken and a new architecture for financial supervision was developed. despite these new regulatory frameworks, or perhaps because of them, a large part of the intermediation of credit operations remains insufficiently monitored and regulated. thus, the shadow banking system operates through financial entities or contracts that create a combination of functions identical to those of banks but outside the scope of regulation, or in a regulatory framework that is weak or addresses issues other than systemic risks, with no access to central bank liquidity facilities or credit guarantees offered by the public sector. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to promote better monitoring and regulation of the shadow banking system.
in writing. - the concept of 'shadow banking' does not necessarily derive from an unregulated or illegal aspect of the financial sector. however, their innovative nature may constitute a systemic risk to taxpayers and the financial system. all their harmful practices must therefore be eliminated to ensure financial stability. given that some of the components of the shadow banking system are central to the financing of the real economy, it is important to define the scope of new or existing regulatory measures. it is therefore absolutely vital that there should be cooperation on a global scale in order to achieve full transparency of the phenomenon of the shadow banking system. a comprehensive view and more effective monitoring will enable supervisors to know the level of repurchase agreements, securities lending and all charges and mechanisms of institutions. i therefore call for a rational and comprehensive approach to regulation in line with the recommendations of the financial stability board.

in writing. - according to the report, the shadow banking system represents 25-30% of the total financial system and half of the banks' assets. few practices of this system have disappeared since 2008. the report points out the dependence of the normal banking sector on the shadow system and that it may threaten the stability of the financial system. it is even recognised that it is impossible to regulate, assess and audit when credit risk distortions or cash flow changes are caused. the report is a good one, but the proposals made in the report, pretending that something has to change, leave everything the same. the problem is not in alleged excesses in the functioning of the shadow banking system, but in its very existence and essence, which is purely speculative. this is a system dominated by large investment banks with financial instruments in their portfolios which exceed several times the gdp of some countries (even the so-called rich countries) and which have developed the most speculative instruments, in particular with the public debts of the states. a system that uses the surplus value created in the productive sphere (by the workers) to create instruments (papers) that sells and resells, and then passes the bill to the workers and the people when in the speculation chain someone does not pay.

in writing. - i consider the thyssen report towards a genuine economic and monetary union to be one of the most important reports adopted by the ep on european integration since the start of the banking crisis in 2008, which then turned into an economic and then a budgetary crisis in several countries and which has tested the strength of the european union. 2. the key message of the report is that the crisis arose and developed largely from a lack of european integration in the construction of emu and that the solution to the crisis lies in a genuine emu in all its dimensions - fiscal, economic and banking union - and in strengthening the social and political pillar of european integration. the problems of integration can only be overcome by further integration. i also note that the report does not ignore the need to limit competition and tax dumping within the union, because it is contrary to the logic of the internal market. the report therefore deserves the broad support it has received and deserves to be considered as a reference for the future.

in writing. − this report is a response to the proposal of european leaders (council, ecb, european commission and eurogroup) for the redefinition of a genuine economic and monetary union (emu), which sets out its basic pillars, the steps to be taken to consolidate it and the implications in terms of the treaty amendments needed for its full implementation. in view of the serious economic and financial crisis facing the european union, and taking into account the objectives of promoting stability, consolidating public accounts, sustainable and balanced growth and deepening the internal market advocated by emu, this proposal is intended to be a response by the european union to restore confidence in its currency and economy. the proposal is based on four fundamental pillars: banking, fiscal and economic union and strengthening democratic legitimacy and accountability, including proposals such as the creation of a single supervisory mechanism, strengthening fiscal harmonisation and decisively implementing structural reforms in the economy. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that decisive steps must be taken to strengthen integration and deepen emu.
in writing. - prosperity and stability in the european union (eu) increasingly depend on one of its cornerstones, economic and monetary union (emu). the economic and financial crisis has exposed the weaknesses of emu. strengthening emu is therefore fundamental to the eu's future socioeconomic well-being. i therefore support the proposals put forward by marianne thyssen in her report, since they aim to strengthen emu by adopting concrete measures to enable a real banking, budgetary and economic union to exist, guaranteed by democratic legitimacy and accountability. however, if a fiscal union is to exist, it should take into account the derogations in the treaties in respect of the outermost regions. the proposals contained in the report, to be implemented in an articulated manner, will ensure a coherent and comprehensive framework capable of ensuring the eu's long-term stability and sustainable economic growth.
in writing. - this report contributes to the mystification of the debate on emu and the euro by evading the responsibilities of the majority which adopted it. the reality here is that, contrary to the propaganda around the euro and emu and the eu itself , these instruments have not only failed to prove to be a shield against the crisis and a weapon to confront capitalist globalisation, but have clearly revealed their instrumental character for the accumulation of profits by capitalist monopolies. there is no solution or reform possible for emu. the strengthening of emu will lead to a further destruction of the productive apparatus of countries with weaker economies by accentuating productive deficits which will generate larger budget deficits and the growth of public debts. what is required is an immediate radical change in the statutes and guidelines, as well as in the false regime of independence of the european central bank, which guarantees the equal participation of the states represented on its council, so as to ensure, on the one hand, effective political control of the ecb by the member states and, on the other hand, control by each participating state over its own national central bank and its national monetary policy, with a view to promoting economic growth and employment.

in writing. - the report, by mr norbert neuser, focuses on the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2011. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly is composed of the member states of the european union and 78 african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries signatories to the cotonou agreement and meets twice a year to discuss development-related issues. during 2011, it met in budapest (hungary) from 16 to 18 may, where it adopted three reports and resolutions of the standing committees on the democratic uprisings in north africa and the middle east and on the situation in côte d'ivoire, and in lomé (togo) from 21 to 23 november, where it adopted three resolutions of the standing committees on the lisbon treaty, debt and persons with disabilities. in addition to the regular meetings, it held a regional meeting in yaoundé, cameroon, and two fact-finding missions, one to east timor and another to the fourth high-level forum on aid effectiveness in busan, south korea. i voted in favour of this report and welcome the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, whose quality of work makes it a key player in north-south cooperation.

it is true, madam president, and it has been said many times here, that there is a great deal we do not know about the extraction of shale gas. but there are also many we already know, and it is good not to forget them. we know, for example, that each operation to extract shale gas uses more than 19 million litres of drinking water, which is enough to supply 1 000 european citizens in terms of their needs in a year. we also know that every shale gas extraction that is done, in each of the operations that are pumped into the ground 300 tons, can go up to 300 tons of chemicals, about 80 percent of which remain in the ground and do not come out. we also know that every shale gas extraction releases radioactive elements and heavy metals into the ground which, together with the evaporation of the toxic waste resulting from the process, constitute a real threat to public health. this is a danger of contamination of drinking water resources and it is a contamination that is real and that is imminent. we know that shale gas extraction is also a seemingly easy answer, which only thinks about the immediate, industry and profit, ignoring the people, the future and the environment. but this is also a europe which knows, in this house, that water is an essential, vital and important resource, which knows how to protect the health of its citizens and which must protect it, which seeks to make agreements to avoid emissions and to propose energy efficiency, because we know that environmental standards are important - environmental and health standards. so when you don't know everything, being prudent is the least you can do. and you may want to do that, but you're not doing it on our behalf or on behalf of the citizens we're here to represent. (the speaker accepts the answer to two questions on the 'blue card' (rule 149 (8)).
answer according to the "blue card" procedure. i think it is interesting that you put this question to me, because you are asking me to choose between two uses of water which i find absolutely unacceptable. we're talking about water as an essential good, we're talking about water as an essential good for humanity, and drinking water, that's what we're talking about. so i can't even compare the nuclear industry and shale gas extraction, because, if you want my opinion on both, i think it's a total waste of water, when we can use it for much more useful purposes for humanity. with regard to the examples given by mr goebbels, it is not by chance that he only mentions two examples, one concerning the recycling of water and the other concerning the non-addition of chemicals, because in the overwhelming majority of farms that exist, in the overwhelming majority, what we are seeing is a total waste of drinking water and the addition of chemicals that remain on the land. what i've said and i'll say it again is that we don't know everything, there are some things we do know. our obligation, and the minimum, is to respond to what the needs of the people and the environment are, and this is a care we must take, on our behalf and on behalf of those we represent.
mr president, it is the most elementary common sense to at least immediately impose a moratorium on the exploitation of shale gas and oil. the environmental impacts associated with the exploitation of these deposits are significant and very negative. the associated techniques, hydraulic fracturing, the injection of polluting, possibly toxic chemicals into the rocks, necessarily lead to a huge instability of these rocks and the degradation of underground water resources or the water courses draining these rocks. these impacts alone would be enough to ban the exploitation of these resources, but at a minimum, a moratorium is required. the commission notes that the extraction of the raw materials is not an economic activity. it would be interesting to know if they exist, and if they do not, it would be interesting to know if this assessment, the results and the methodology of an energy return on investment assessment were made. an energy return on invested energy assessment covering the life cycle of each of these projects in order to verify the economic balance of this technique.

in writing. - i support this report, as i consider sis ii to be an essential instrument for increasing the security of the schengen area and at the same time for more effective intergovernmental management of the system, which considerably improves data protection and citizens' fundamental rights. this report thus enables the european union, its citizens and the schengen states and citizens outside the european union to benefit as quickly as possible from the benefits of this new system.
in writing. − the schengen information system (sis) is the backbone of a europe without borders and of the area of freedom, security and justice. the second generation of sis (sis ii) will allow the introduction of new data, including biometric data, new types of alerts and new functionalities that will enhance security and a more intelligent use of information. the migration to sis ii is scheduled to start at the beginning of january next year. sis ii is an essential instrument for strengthening the security of the schengen area and for ensuring the intergovernmental management of the system. for several years the european parliament has been advocating the need for a clearly community solution, rejecting the continuation of an intergovernmental architecture. this is one of the reasons for supporting sis ii. despite support for the european commission's proposal, this report, which has my support, considers it essential to strengthen data protection rules and the need to ensure effective supervision of this complex migration.
in writing. − despite the numerous problems and delays that the sis ii project has been experiencing over the last few years, the ep has always supported sis ii, supporting the need for a clearly community solution and rejecting the continuation of an intergovernmental architecture. sis ii should also contribute to enhanced security and provide a higher level of data protection than currently exists. parliament accepted the council's proposal to split the commission's initiative by creating a second proposal which more adequately reflected the situation in the united kingdom and ireland, which meant that the ep had to give its opinion on this proposal as well. the specific situation of the united kingdom and ireland stems from the fact that these member states only participate partially in schengen, in particular as regards measures in the framework of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. both countries do not participate in the current sis 1+, but will participate in sis ii, and it is therefore necessary to clarify their special situation, as they will not be able to participate in the aspects covered by the sis ii regulation (ex-1st pillar), but only in the aspects covered by the sis ii decision (ex-3rd pillar).
in writing. the schengen information system (sis) is the most important tool for the security of the schengen area. sis ii (the second generation sis) makes it possible to add new data, new types of alerts and new functions that could increase security and lead to a more intelligent use of information through linked alerts. the migration of sis 1+ to sis ii is governed by two legal instruments: regulation 1104/2008 in the former first pillar and council decision 2008/839/jha in the former third pillar. the commission's proposal seeks to merge the two legal acts into one in order to reflect the abolition of the pillars. the council asked for the original proposal to be divided into two parts, one of which would include the united kingdom and ireland in order to respect their specific positions. that's the one we voted for here. it is never too much to stress the importance of the schengen information system for the security of europeans and the need for this migration to take place with the utmost caution and care, in respect of the rights of citizens.
in writing. - we are seeing the development of new features in the schengen information system, we are seeing its deepening. the migration to sis ii implies that new authorities will have access to sis ii, linking alerts together, adding new categories of data (such as the arrest warrant, biometric data such as fingerprints and photographs) and a technical platform for sharing information with the visa information system. the report also calls for further devolution of member states' powers by migrating to sis ii, thus underlining its federalist character. this process will add new elements to a database that is accessible to several people, without any guarantee of confidentiality or of non-sharing of this data with other people or organisations. we reiterate our longstanding condemnation of the serious threats to the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens arising from the creation of the schengen area. the migration from sis i to sis ii confirms this trend and deserves our firm rejection.
in writing. - the sis (schengen information system) is the most relevant instrument for the security of the schengen area and is rightly considered the backbone of a europe without borders and of the area of freedom, security and justice. sis ii (the second generation of sis) will allow the introduction of new data (in particular the introduction of biometric data), new types of alerts and new functionalities, allowing for enhanced security and a smarter use of information through the interconnection of alerts. sis ii is an essential instrument for strengthening the security of the schengen area, for putting the intergovernmental management of the system in charge and for considerably improving data protection and the fundamental rights of individuals. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report so that sis ii can come into force as soon as possible in the eu, including the uk and ireland, as desired. i congratulate my colleague carlos coelho on his work.
in writing. − an area of freedom, security and justice between member states, part of the schengen agreement, is only feasible if it has effective instruments, such as the 1st and 2nd generation schengen information system. i am voting in favour of this proposal to migrate from sis i to sis ii, because i consider it essential that it should move from an intergovernmental system to a union system, where the protection of citizens' data must remain an essential element of the proposal.
in writing. − i approve of this report, beginning by congratulating the commission on this proposal, which clarifies the legal framework applicable to the migration from sis 1+ to sis ii and i particularly welcome the application of the sis ii legal framework from the moment the first member state completes the transfer of its system. this proposal, in my view, increases legal certainty and avoids unnecessary expenditure in the various member states. i also welcome the possibility of community co-financing of any expenditure that member states may have to bear in the context of the migration process. however, i regret the delay in the commission's presentation of this initiative.
in writing. − the schengen information system (sis) is the backbone of a europe without borders and of the area of freedom, security and justice. the second generation of sis (sis ii) will allow the introduction of new data, including biometric data, new types of alerts and new functionalities that will enhance security and a more intelligent use of information. the migration to sis ii is scheduled to start at the beginning of january next year. sis ii is an essential instrument for strengthening the security of the schengen area and for ensuring the intergovernmental management of the system. for several years the european parliament has been advocating the need for a clearly community solution, rejecting the continuation of an intergovernmental architecture. this is one of the reasons for supporting sis ii. despite support for the european commission's proposal, this report, which has my support, considers it essential to strengthen data protection rules and the need to ensure effective supervision of this complex migration. given the political relevance of the matter and its importance in budgetary terms, it is regrettable that parliament is only consulted.
in writing. − despite the numerous problems and delays that the sis ii project has been experiencing over the last few years, the ep has always supported sis ii, supporting the need for a clearly community solution and rejecting the continuation of an intergovernmental architecture. sis ii should also contribute to enhanced security and provide a higher level of data protection than currently exists. these proposals ensure greater legal clarity and avoid additional costs, where the sis ii legal framework should apply from the moment the first member state completes the transfer. it also provides for the possibility of community co-financing to ensure timely migration by member states. the commission has introduced amendments to strengthen data protection rules, ensuring efficient supervision of this complex process and a smooth transition to the new system, ensuring that the ep is kept informed throughout the process as well as the final outcome, and ensuring data quality and accuracy by ensuring the deletion of any data that has not been transferred. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. the schengen information system (sis) is the most important tool for the security of the schengen area. sis ii (the second generation sis) makes it possible to add new data, new types of alerts and new functions that could increase security and lead to a more intelligent use of information through linked alerts. the migration of sis 1+ to sis ii is governed by two legal instruments: regulation 1104/2008 in the former first pillar and council decision 2008/839/jha in the former third pillar. the commission's proposal seeks to merge the two legal acts into one in order to reflect the abolition of the pillars. the council asked for the original proposal to be divided into two parts, one of which would not include the united kingdom and ireland. that's what we're voting on here. despite the criticism it has received, the schengen area is an important achievement for europeans. having an information system that effectively ensures security within it is a contribution to its durability.
in writing. - in this case, the participation of the united kingdom and ireland is not taken into account. but our position is, of course, the same as that expressed in the previous report (in which these two countries took part). we voted against it. the migration to sis ii entails the development of new features in the system, extending its access to new authorities, interlinking alerts between them, adding new categories of data (such as the arrest warrant, biometric data such as fingerprints and photographs) and a technical platform for sharing information with the visa information system. these are elements of increased concern for a system (and the space it serves) which from its origins has entailed serious threats to the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens.
in writing. − this report covers the same subject as a7-0368/2012 but does not include the united kingdom and ireland. in fact, following discussions between the member states, the council considered it more appropriate to divide the commission proposal into two texts: one in which the united kingdom and ireland participate and another in which they do not. sis ii (the second generation of sis) will allow the introduction of new data (in particular the introduction of biometric data), new types of alerts and new functionalities, as well as enhanced security and a smarter use of information through the interconnection of alerts. the sis is also recognised as an essential instrument for strengthening the security of the schengen area, for putting the intergovernmental management of the system in place and for considerably improving data protection and the fundamental rights of individuals, which is why i am voting in favour of this report. i congratulate the rapporteur, my colleague carlos coelho, on the work he has done here.
in writing. - for reasons of legal certainty, the council decided that this proposal should be divided into two parts, one containing the participation of the united kingdom and ireland and the other not. an area of freedom, security and justice between member states, part of the schengen agreement, is only feasible if it has effective instruments, such as the 1st and 2nd generation schengen information system. i am voting in favour of this proposal to migrate from sis i to sis ii, because i consider it essential that it should move from an intergovernmental system to a union system, where the protection of citizens' data must remain an essential element of the proposal.
in writing. − the migration to sis ii entails the development of new features in the system, extending its access to new authorities, interlinking alerts between them, adding new categories of data (such as the arrest warrant, biometric data such as fingerprints and photographs) and a technical platform for sharing information with the visa information system. the report also calls for further devolution of member states' powers by migrating to sis ii, thus underlining its federalist character. this process will add new elements to a database that is accessible to several people, without any guarantee of confidentiality or of non-sharing of this data with other people or organisations. we have always been and continue to be among those who have denounced the high risks to the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens which arise from the creation of the schengen area. the migration from sis i to sis ii confirms this trend and deserves our rejection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that a clear community solution to the matter in hand is necessary, rejecting the continuation of an intergovernmental architecture, and because the implementation of the sis ii legal framework will strengthen legal certainty and avoid the burden of costs on the individual member states.
in writing. - i would like to start by congratulating my colleague carlos coelho on the excellent work he has done in preparing the reports on the proposal for a council regulation on the migration from the schengen information system (sis+1) to the second generation schengen information system (sis ii). the sis is the most important instrument in the security of the schengen area, which enhances the existence of a europe without borders, i.e. an 'area of freedom, security and justice'. sis ii is a system for checking our borders which will replace the current system by introducing a set of new functionalities (such as the use of biometric data) in order to respond to the increase in requests and to resolve complaints. this is a more secure system and allows for more efficient use of available data.

in writing. - as the european union is a legal structure based on treaties and legislative acts, it is essential that these are applied correctly and uniformly in the 27 member states. however, we know that the member states often fail to apply or transpose the rules of european union law on time, or apply or transpose them poorly or incompletely. it is therefore essential that member states do not underestimate the value of the correct and timely application of eu law and that the commission keeps parliament duly informed on the state of implementation of eu law. it is also essential that national courts in the member states play their fundamental role in the application of eu law and that judicial training for national judges and other legal professionals be improved and coordinated so that they have an adequate knowledge of eu law, which is a key step in ensuring uniform and proper application in the various states.
in writing. - we all know the herculean effort that each rule adopted by this parliament requires, from simple contacts to negotiations, commitments, votes, etc., all for the improvement of the quality of life of the european citizens who elected us. however, when we compare all this work with the time that elapses between the adoption of a regulation or a directive by the european parliament and its transposition by all the member states (ms) that are bound by these regulations, we get the feeling that this effort is not properly valued. i voted in favour of the report by mrs lichtenberger on the 28th annual report on the monitoring of european union (eu) law for the year 2010, because it draws attention to some reprehensible practices by member states in failing to transpose community directives into national law or in failing to transpose them in due time, thus encouraging the commission to impose financial sanctions. european citizens and consumers are at the heart of the application of community law and demand that it be applied swiftly. there is no justice if it is not done in a timely manner.
in writing. − this report advances an assessment of the commission's communications on the application of eu law (2010). the 'infringements of the internal market' are the most frequently reported, and are the starting point for the usual and unacceptable procession of pressure on member states to transpose into national law the directives which pave the way for the deepening of the internal market, however harmful they may be to their interests, to the interests of the overwhelming majority of their populations (and they often are). the report advocates financial sanctions for member states that are late in transposing a directive, by taking the matter to the european court of justice. in other words, blackmail outright on the member states to force them to accept taxes regardless of the position and interests of their citizens. this is unacceptable! we voted against it, of course.
