in writing. - i approve this report, considering that although the extraction of shale gas and shale oil is highly profitable and is already common practice in the united states, canada and europe, it is still at an experimental stage, which makes it essential to take preventive measures, given the high environmental impact of this activity. since many studies and even european public opinion associate this activity with water and soil contamination, i believe that the measures outlined in this report are appropriate, insofar as they present a demanding environmental package, which respects the essential environmental concerns.
in writing. - the extraction of shale gas and shale oil can give rise to a number of different impacts over time, such as during the initial phases with diesel or natural gas fuelled engines to power drilling equipment and pumps, and during extraction by pumps and compressors. disturbances are minimised from the start of extraction, thanks to a surface production equipment that covers a few square metres and silences the production. unlike many other extractive and industrial processes, the decommissioning of shale gas and shale oil wells leaves no trace on the surface landscape. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the environmental impacts of shale gas and shale oil extraction should be taken into account and that public participation should be ensured by means of appropriate public information campaigns before the exploration phase and by means of a public consultation in the pre-exploration phases.
in writing. − gas is expected to play a key role in the transformation of the global energy system, as it contributes to reducing emissions. shale gas and other unconventional gas sources have become potential and important sources of supply in europe and surrounding areas. the 'shale gas revolution' is spreading globally at a relatively rapid rate. according to some estimates, the total shale gas reserves in the eu exceed 56 billion cubic metres, of which some 14 billion cubic metres are technically recoverable. i believe that greater public involvement and awareness of unconventional fossil fuel activities is needed to allow for public understanding, acceptance and confidence in these activities. i believe that this extraction of fuels, provided it respects environmental standards, is a great opportunity to strengthen the economy and increase employment and development in certain regions of the eu.
in writing. − the report is concerned with the prevention of environmental impacts associated with the exploration and extraction of unconventional shale gas and oil, through planning, testing, use of new technologies and best practices, data collection and monitoring. in our view, at the very least, a moratorium should be imposed on the exploitation of shale gas and oil fields, given that these are techniques with large environmental impacts and quite controversial, involving drilling at high depth, bursting the shale layer and injecting water, chemicals and sand at high pressure to obtain the extraction of gas and oil. the environmental impacts of this process are significant and very negative, in terms of groundwater contamination or water courses draining from existing masses, due to the leakage of chemicals resulting from the injection. in addition, it can generate instability in the rocky masses and release methane leaks into the atmosphere. the amendment tabled calling on the member states to adopt this moratorium on hydraulic fracturing operations, which we support, taking into account the principles of precaution and preventive action, as well as the risks to the environment and public health, has unfortunately been rejected.
in writing. − given the rising price of oil and the need to reduce emissions of other greenhouse gases, the use of renewable energy and other non-conventional energy sources is becoming inevitable. given that conventional gas production is declining and that this will make the eu even more dependent on energy imports from third countries, the focus on extracting unconventional gas and oil, in particular shale gas and oil, is important. the diversification of energy sources will contribute to greater security of supply and lower energy prices. currently, some eu member states are engaged in exploration and extraction, with the eu having around 14 million cubic metres of potential to be extracted. however, advanced methods of shale gas extraction may prove to be environmentally harmful, in particular hydraulic extraction. i therefore voted in favour of the report, since it proposes to the commission that the rules on the liability of transnational companies, in particular hydrocarbon extracting companies, for environmental and social rights should be strengthened, as well as possible means of enforcement.
in writing. − this report says it wants to mitigate the environmental impacts associated with the exploration and extraction of unconventional shale gas and oil, through planning, testing, use of new technologies and best practices, data collection and monitoring. in our opinion, that is not enough. at a minimum, a moratorium should be imposed on the exploitation of shale gas and oil fields, given that these are techniques with large environmental impacts and highly controversial, involving drilling at high depth, blasting the shale layer and injection of water, chemicals and sand at high pressure to obtain the extraction of gas and oil. we support an amendment tabled calling on member states not to authorize any hydraulic fracturing operations, taking into account the principles of precaution and preventive action, as well as the risks to the environment and public health, which was rejected by the majority of the ep. we therefore voted against the report.
in writing. - i approve of this report because it not only points to the positive aspects of this type of activity, but also considers an environmental package, voted in parallel, which provides for preventive approaches in industrial and energy exploration and others linked to shale gas and oil. i should also like to stress that we must take account of the benefits of this new type of activity, which is still under-explored in the european union, while taking into account that the environmental aspects have been well safeguarded.
in writing. − i believe that shale gas production has a role to play in the eu in the medium to long term, contributing to the eu's target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels, in the context of reductions by the developed countries group, while ensuring security of energy supply and competitiveness, which is the basis of the energy roadmap 2050. i urge the commission to come forward with recommendations for all shale gas wells in the eu to reduce evasive methane emissions. i believe that the 'polluter pays' principle should be applied rigorously to shale gas and oil exploration activities, particularly in relation to waste water treatment, and that companies should be fully liable for any direct or indirect damage they may cause. for these reasons, and because i agree with the assumptions of the report, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - with the increase in world energy demands, oil, which for decades was the main source of energy, began to show signs that its reserves were running low. this has led to an exponential increase in its price and has encouraged countries to explore alternative sources such as wind, solar, wave, geothermal, etc. but human ingenuity is constantly searching for and exploring other types of fuel. at the moment, attention has been focused on the exploitation of so-called shale gas and oil, a fuel that is widely exploited in the united states and whose stocks on american soil guarantee the energy supply of that country for the next 45 years. at eu level, although its existence is confirmed in several countries in central and eastern europe, there are still many reservations about the value added of this type of fuel, mainly due to fears of the side effects of its exploitation in the areas of health and the environment. i do not think, however, that the eu can afford to miss the train of new energy resources. it should therefore look at all the positive factors, such as the impact on the economy, but also the negative ones, especially in the areas of health and the environment, and look for ways to eliminate or substantially reduce them.
in writing. the report aims to promote the exploration and extraction of unconventional shale gas and oil, citing industrial policy and energy market objectives put forward by the european commission in the context of the desired transition of the energy system to the so-called decarbonised economy. the development of the sector's infrastructure and industry is advocated, and concern is expressed that this should be financially sustainable, aspects which not only give rise to reservations but also exclude the necessary environmental concerns. the capture of shale gas is now a highly controversial technique, which poses major environmental risks, including contamination of ground and surface water, as well as the inherent risks of rock instability. moreover, the return on energy consumed by this extraction method has not been proven to be positive. it would be important to carry out life-cycle energy return on invested energy (eroi) assessments of each of these projects in order to check their economic balance sheet. this is a matter on which a moratorium was at least called for.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on industrial, energy and other aspects of shale gas and oil. this document considers a stable regulatory framework to be essential both for creating the right environment for gas companies to invest in areas with shortcomings such as infrastructure and research and development, and for avoiding market distortions. it is also proposed, and i welcome this, to promote the exchange of information and best practice between the eu member states, but also between the eu, the usa and canada. in addition, the twinning of european and north american cities and municipalities that have discovered shale gas is particularly encouraged with a view to transferring knowledge on shale gas development from industry to local communities.
in writing. − this report analyses a wide range of issues relating to the development of shale gas and oil in the european union, including the following: potential reserves in some member states; the impact of shale gas development on the eu market and decreasing dependence on russia; the role of shale gas in energy security; shale gas development in the context of the transactional back-up plan for a decarbonised economy; the licensing framework; public opinion; and, finally, the importance of using best available practices and technologies. i think that this is a matter of great importance and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the eu has about 14 million cubic metres of shale oil and gas that can be extracted. however, advanced methods of extracting shale gas and oil, in particular hydraulic extraction, may prove to be environmentally harmful. i voted in favour of the report because it proposes that safety and environmental standards be respected, taking as a reference matrix the good practices and legislation already in place in the united states of america and canada (in particular those in the province of british columbia and the province of alberta), countries where shale gas extraction has been taking place for a longer time. in addition to the above, i also consider it important that the commission and the public authorities of the member states review and improve the regulatory frameworks in order to ensure that the exploitation, extraction and marketing of this energy source is done in an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable way in the long term.
in writing. − the report aims to promote the exploration and extraction of unconventional shale gas and oil, taking into account industrial and energy market aspects, in line with the european commission's objective of placing gas as a substantial element in the transformation of the energy system towards the so-called decarbonised economy. the development of the sector's infrastructure and industry is advocated here, and concern is expressed that this is financially sustainable, aspects which not only give us reservations but also exclude the necessary environmental concerns. shale gas capture is today a highly controversial technique due to the environmental impact and complexity of the operation, involving drilling to high depth, bursting the shale layer and injecting water, chemicals and sand at high pressure to provide extraction of the gas and oil. this process poses major environmental risks, including contamination of groundwater or watercourses draining from existing landfills, due to the chemicals resulting from the injection. it also generates instability in the rocky masses and release of methane leaks into the atmosphere. this is a matter on which a moratorium was at least called for. we voted against the report.
in writing. - gas will play a key role in reducing emissions. in this context, shale gas and other unconventional gas sources are becoming potential and important sources of supply in europe, and could bring about radical changes in global energy markets. it is noted that shale gas, which in 2000 represented 1,4% of the us gas market, rose to 17% in 2011. according to some estimates, the total shale gas reserves in the eu exceed 56 billion cubic metres, of which some 14 billion cubic metres are technically recoverable. their exploitation must therefore be studied and all conditions must be created for exploration, extraction and use that is as environmentally neutral as possible and in compliance with all safety standards relating to gas extraction activities.

in writing. − one of the fundamental rights of european citizens is to exercise, individually or in association, their right to petition the ep (article 227 of the treaty on the functioning of the eu tfeu) on any matter relating to the activities of the eu and directly affecting them. during 2011, almost a thousand petitions were submitted, of which about 400 were outside the competence of the committee on petitions and were therefore forwarded to other services or archived. this is why there is an increasing number of petitioners whose issues do not fall within the eu's remit. the most common subjects covered in the petitions were: 1. violation of fundamental rights; 2. the functioning of the internal market and 3. attacks on the environment. as for the country of origin, germany is the country with the highest number of petitions, followed by spain and italy. interestingly, the countries targeted in the petitions are, in descending order, italy, spain and germany. i welcome the work carried out by this commission in constructive cooperation with the european ombudsman, who plays a key role as an intermediary between the citizen and the ep and helps to motivate citizens and to build their trust in the european institutions.
in writing. − this report covers the activities of the committee on petitions of the european parliament during 2011, providing a statistical breakdown of the petitions submitted a total of 998, of which 649 were forwarded to the european commission and the remaining were deemed inadmissible. the report covers the most common topics in petitions by citizens or groups of citizens, such as breaches of eu law in the fields of the environment, justice and the internal market, with a significant number of cases concerned with complaints about decisions taken by national authorities or judgments of national courts. taking into account the comparison between 2009, 2010 and 2011, there is a steady decrease in the number of petitions lodged, from 1924 to 1655 and 998 respectively in 2011, i.e. a decrease of 52% compared to 2009 and 60% compared to 2010. this development will be more related to the discrediting of the policies of the european union and its institutions than to a reduction in the reasons for citizens' complaints and dissatisfaction. we will continue to follow closely the complaints that reach the committee on petitions and to do everything in our power to increase the level of complaints and to demand solutions to the legitimate problems raised by citizens.

mr president, commissioner, two issues that would be worth discussing in depth as we prepare for another climate change conference: the first is the carbon market. the european union, eager to create another haven for financial speculators, to bet on the creation of another billion dollar machine for generating fictitious financial assets, has opted for a market approach instead of a regulatory approach which it could and should have followed. the question is: when will the perversity of market instruments be recognised? the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. secondly, trade liberalization and deregulation. the same european union that is very concerned about climate change is pursuing trade liberalization and deregulation in the rest of the world, which significantly increases the flows of energy and materials and, consequently, the co2 emissions associated with the satisfaction of the most basic human needs. when will this intractable contradiction be resolved?
in writing. bridging the gap between the available scientific data and the current commitments of the parties to the framework convention on climate change is urgently needed. according to a united nations study published this week, greenhouse gas emissions levels continue to rise and are 14% above 2020 targets, with a temperature increase of 3 to 5°c predicted this century in the absence of rapid action. all governments meeting in doha need to raise the bar by ensuring that a legally binding global agreement is finalised to limit global warming to 2°c. the costs of inaction are documented and will be higher if emissions reductions are delayed for decades. the crisis must not therefore reduce the level of ambition in doha. the eu must give a new impetus to international climate negotiations and invest in the transition to a green economy, showing that it is possible to reduce emissions without losing competitiveness and jobs.

mr president, the recession cannot justify the member states' disinvestment in security and defence in this world which is more dangerous because it is deregulated. it is precisely because of the crisis and the challenges we face on a global scale that the european union has to coordinate and integrate security and defence policies, resources and capabilities. this implies moving forward in the permanent headquarters and gathering and sharing human resources, equipment but also financial means. the 'cost-benefit rule' prevents some states from contributing more civilian and military forces and capabilities to csdp missions. the recommendations of this parliament in the reports here - the operationalization of the solidarity clause, cyber defence, the security implications of climate change - are essential for the european union to have strategic autonomy and also serve europeans in this way to assume the commitments they have within nato, the un and other strategic partnerships as security providers on a global scale.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, this report is not about finnish. finning is an abhorrent practice of catching sharks for the removal of fins and the discarding of the body, banned in the european union since 2003. the commission proposes to eliminate the derogation, not to finning, but to the cutting of fins on board, which is permitted by a special authorization, and the shipowner must keep, land and market all parts of the captured animal. the ship owners want to keep cutting the fins on board. why would you do that? by cutting the fins they can store fins and bodies separately, which saves space for on-board storage, and allows for increased duration of each trip and available fishing time. so it reduces shore visits, thereby saving fuel and reducing pollutant emissions, it prevents the shark from partially thawing on land to separate fins and bodies, which have distinct markets, and then later being refrozen. this preserves the quality of the fish, safeguards the health of the consumer and does not reduce the value of the fish. these arguments were legitimate for the commission in 2003. what's changed? why did the commission think of taking this initiative? why does the european fleet practice finning? i'm not going to. in 2005 and 2006, the commission and parliament confirmed the absence of finning, and today, often called upon to provide evidence of finning, neither the commission nor the ngos have been able to do so. at a workshop in may, the shark alliance representative publicly stated that it was not the european fleet that was finning. so why are the species that the european fleet catches at risk? i'm not going to. 90% of european catches are of the bluefin tuna, a species with unparalleled biological productivity. the commission has said that it is to put an end to finning, deliberately creating confusion in public opinion. at the same time, urged to justify it, it says that they are suspects after all, and dares to attempt to legislate on the basis of suspicion. despite the absurdity of this position and the serious precedent it sets, i have tried to put forward proposals which would respond to all the concerns raised. if there's any suspicion of finning, we'll step up the surveillance. i propose that the simultaneous landing of fins and bodies be made compulsory in all ports and that shipowners appoint an independent body to monitor landings in ports where control is not ensured. if the problem is the waiver, let's narrow it down. i proposed that the derogation should apply only to freezer vessels, excluding fresh-water vessels. if the concern is shark stocks, let's create the conditions for scientific data. i proposed the basis of a shark action plan, with mandatory extensive data collection on all species caught. the commission said no to everything. however, in your strange drive to push this proposal forward, you forgot to assess the socioeconomic impacts. the sector did, and in a very small estimate it calculated 14 million losses a year to the iberian fleet. the commissioner's proposal is unjustified, harmful and the proposals i have put forward in their entirety fully answer all the suspicions and concerns. so why do these proposals not get unanimous support instead of being voted down by parliament tomorrow? it is here that it is important to denounce forcefully the campaign of disinformation launched by the commission and militantly pursued by the ngos, which, in this particular case, have forgotten the nobility of their citizenship and have resorted to half-truths that lead to false conclusions, to outright lies, to the pressure of the constant presence of e-mails and circulars, but also to the political terrorism of the persecutory identification of those who think differently and their personal defamation on social networks. the pressure from ngos and the national disinterest in this fishery leads many members to opt for the comfortable vote. we all lose. on the eve of the cfp reform, which will inevitably lead to high economic and social costs, the fleet is penalized with an additional loss. the commission is deluding itself into thinking that it can reform the sector, which sees it as a second environment commissioner and sees itself as an orphan, rebelling in the future with the means at its disposal. the ngos that are supposed to protect sharks are losing out because they are breaking the existing excellent relationship of the shipowners with the scientists and making extensive data collection and a shark action plan unfeasible. meps who vote for convenience are increasingly held hostage by ngos. i'm sorry for all of you.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, this report on small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing was necessary for two reasons. firstly, while the disaster of the current common fisheries policy is relatively consensual, we must not forget that this disaster is felt particularly keenly today by the weakest segments of the fleet, by small-scale fishing and by the coastal communities most dependent on it. secondly, because the european commission's proposals for the reform of the common fisheries policy not only do not solve these problems but contain new elements of concern and threat to the future of small-scale fishing. this report sought to contribute to a more favourable overall approach to the reform of the cfp for small-scale fisheries, to a better consideration of what its problems are, but also of its potential, so as to exploit it as fully as possible. on the other hand, concrete proposals of varying scope are being put forward to support small-scale fishing. let me highlight some of the points in the report and some of its proposals. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european fisheries fund. a local management system that puts an end to the centralised management system that has prevailed for the last 30 years with the known results. the rejection of a single management model for all member states, such as transferable fishing concessions. increased community co-financing for the acquisition, processing and provision of biological data. the promotion of positive discrimination against segments and operators using more selective gear and equipment, with less impact on marine resources and the marine environment, and with greater benefits for the communities in which they operate in terms of job creation and the quality of that employment. the need for a financial instrument for the outermost regions which retains the principle of increasing the intensity of support. the european fisheries and maritime fund also finances actions. actions in the following areas: improving safety and working conditions on board, fish conservation conditions fishing and enhancing activities carried out on land. other proposals include the creation of support mechanisms for emergency situations such as natural and man-made disasters; forced stops of activity, determined by plans for the rebuilding of stocks or sudden increases in fuel prices; the introduction of financial compensation during periods of biological standstill; the possibility of reserve areas of exclusive access for small-scale fisheries; the defence of the public instruments for regulating the markets still in existence; the defence of mechanisms that promote a fair and adequate distribution of added value along the value chain of the sector. all of these are proposals in this report, among others. these are some of the most relevant ones, for which i ask your support. some of them correct serious flaws in the commission proposal. it is not enough to make loud proclamations in defence of small-scale fishing. these proclamations need to be translated into a concrete commitment to support the measures needed to help solve the serious problems facing small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing today.
i would like to say a few words about the external dimension of the common fisheries policy. in my final speech i shall have the opportunity to return to small-scale fishing and to give mr davies a new development: the management of living marine biological resources is an exclusive competence of the european union. it is not even a competence shared with the member states. but we'll be back. as regards the external dimension of the cfp, the current cfp also lacks major changes in its external dimension. the current fisheries agreements with third countries require major changes. the rapporteur has advanced some of them, which we appreciate. a substantial part of the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreements has not been achieved. these agreements have generally been a transfer of funds to developing countries in exchange for the exploitation of their fisheries resources. this is a restrictive view, which we deplore and which runs counter to the spirit and objectives of these agreements. cooperation in the fisheries sector should, in the medium term, promote the exploitation by developing countries of their own resources, both for internal consumption and for export, thus increasing the share of the wealth generated that remains in the country. we stress once again the importance of the formulation of maps, with targets, actions and indicators to monitor the implementation of fisheries agreements in a spirit of partnership. this monitoring shall include the adoption of corrective procedures to be articulated with the third country whenever a departure from the objectives set is noted. a final word on the proposal for a regulation on technical measures. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his willingness to accept the amendment we have tabled. the previous regulation provided for heavy and discriminatory measures against the portuguese fleet fishing for redfish - measures which lacked a scientific basis. we therefore welcome the fact that this amendment has been introduced.
mr president, small-scale fishing should be given special protection under the common fisheries policy, not only because it promotes socioeconomic cohesion and ensures the livelihood of many families, but also because it is a factor in the attachment of these communities to coastal areas. their economic and social sustainability should be an objective, ensuring that they are subject to a differentiated fishing regime that gives priority to access to resources, allows for proximity management and protects the fishing rights enjoyed by the fishermen of those communities against transferable fishing rights. it is also important for their sustainability to take account of the regime of access to waters, especially in regions with marine biogeographical basins, with a small continental shelf and scarce resources, concentrated in seamounts and fisheries that must have protected access. in a context of liberalisation and crisis, which is weighing on fragile regions, it must also be ensured that products from international trade meet the same requirements as those imported by the union.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i share the commission's concerns about enforcing the 'finning' ban and collecting scientific data for good management, and also because i believe that the legitimate economic and social interests of the sector must be safeguarded and the protection of shark stocks guaranteed.
in writing. - i agree that the derogations or exception to the regulation which already prohibits the practice of removing the fins of sharks on board ships and then returning the rest of the animal's body to the sea should be abolished. i believe that the practice of fining is unacceptable from an environmental point of view because it threatens the sustainability of some of the shark species targeted by this practice, from a social and economic point of view because it involves the waste of a food commodity with commercial value, and also from a moral point of view because it is an act of total disregard for animal life. it is therefore necessary to condemn this practice unequivocally and to take the appropriate measures to ensure that it remains banned from european waters and from the activities of the community fleet, in particular to move towards the monitoring of the prohibition of this practice in order to eliminate any suspicions.
in writing. - this is one of those issues where it is required that policy decision should be supported by a strong scientific basis. the scientific opinion of the portuguese institute of the sea and the atmosphere (ipma) pointed to the maintenance of the existing derogation, that is, that it would continue to be possible to cut the fin on board, although tightening the means of control, in view of the current legislation. in addition to considering that adopting the commission proposal will entail obvious economic losses, which are not justifiable given the current state of conservation of the resources, ipma advances on grounds relating to the quality of fishery products (avoiding freezing, thawing and re-freezing of material), and on the losses this proposal will entail by calling into question the good and cooperative relationship between researchers and the sector for the collection of information necessary for scientists to provide the administration with their opinions, for effective fisheries management and thus ensure the conservation of these resources. our vote was based on this opinion.
in writing. - the european commission proposal provides for the abolition of the current article 4, i.e. the derogation from the prohibition on the removal of shark fins on board community fishing vessels, which is currently allowed by issuing special catch licences granted for this purpose, duly regulated by the articles of this diploma. the rapporteur of this document has decided to maintain the derogation contrary to the commission's proposal. since this proposal was not accepted in plenary, i voted against the final document because it no longer corresponded to the original version and the author of the rapporteur.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering first of all that the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of great importance, since it establishes a system which allows the cooperation of the participating states with a view to finding a solution to international child abduction, determining the competent courts and the applicable law for the purpose of deciding on the child's place of residence. in addition, recalling the role that the european union has already assumed in terms of exclusive external competence in the field of international child abduction, i believe that for this reason the council should promote the necessary measures as soon as possible to adopt the decisions proposed by the commission, in particular the immediate consultation of parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution for urging the member states to sign the declaration, in the interest of the european union, which will allow eight countries to accede to the convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the council must proceed without delay with the adoption of the abovementioned draft decisions and in this process parliament should have a say in the eight draft decisions.
in writing. − the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of great importance as it establishes a system which allows for cooperation between the participating states with a view to finding a solution to international child abduction by determining the competent courts and the applicable law for the purpose of deciding on the child's place of residence. it is therefore urgent that the council take the necessary steps to accept the accession of eight new states to the convention.
in writing. the resolution, tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure, following a question with a request for an oral answer tabled by a number of members on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, concerns the declaration by the member states (me) of acceptance, in the interest of the european union (eu), of the accession of eight third countries to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the increased mobility of citizens at european level has increased the number of relationships between people from different countries. as a consequence of this increase, there has also been an increase in the number of separations between couples with children, who end up fighting over custody of the children. often, court decisions are not respected and children are abducted by one of the parents. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution - which was blocked in the council almost a year ago - because it is essential that in the above cases the international community should put the interests of children first and not those of the parents, which is not always the case with some institutions. in the case of international kidnapping, the eu has external competence.
in writing. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction establishes a system which allows for cooperation by participating states with a view to finding a solution to international child abduction. this convention applies only between countries which have ratified it or acceded to it, and acceptance of accession is therefore of the utmost importance. the interests of children are of paramount importance and their protection must take precedence over any other interest. we believe that it is essential and urgent to establish the most effective ways of ensuring the immediate return of a kidnapped child to the state of his or her habitual residence. hence our vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the declaration by the member states, in the interest of the european union, of acceptance of the accession of eight third countries to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, in which the council is recommended to proceed without delay with the adoption of the abovementioned proposals for decisions, and to this end it should consult parliament on the eight proposals for decisions and in the interest of the european citizens who will benefit from the adoption of these decisions.
in writing. - having regard to the importance of the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction, which establishes a system enabling the participating states to cooperate in order to find a solution to international child abduction by determining the competent courts and the applicable law for the purpose of deciding on the child's place of residence, the european parliament recommended that the council proceed without delay with the adoption of the proposals for a decision on the subject submitted by the commission. it therefore reminded the council that it should consult parliament on draft decisions and that, in the interests of the european citizens who have benefited from the adoption of these decisions, it should refrain from obstructing the proper functioning of the european union by invoking spurious legal grounds. for the reasons i have given, i supported the adoption of the document.
in writing. − i approve this report, starting by urging the council and the commission to ensure that any changes to the itr are compatible with the eu acquis and further the eu's objective and interest of advancing the internet as a genuine public space, where human rights and fundamental freedoms are respected, in particular freedom of expression and assembly, and ensuring respect for the principles of the free market, net neutrality and entrepreneurship. on the other hand, it is important to preserve the development of online services and access to them for end-users, as well as the digital economy as a whole.
in writing. − issues surrounding internet access and management are increasingly central to the debate on international telecommunications. i believe that the common position of the epp and the alde group has reflected a prudent and balanced line on this matter, seeking to ensure that the european position at the next world conference defends freedom of use and access to this medium, human rights and respect for the community acquis. unjustified restrictions would only set back the way we communicate today, which has had the merit of bringing people closer together and of making information and trade flow more freely. while recognising the need to be alert to the crimes that may be committed through the internet, i nevertheless believe that the starting point should be freedom of use and access to the internet and not its limitation or the introduction of economic barriers to its use. i hope that the conclusions of the conference will take up this position.
in writing. - the joint motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 110 (2) and (4) of the rules of procedure, replacing the motions for resolutions tabled by the epp and alde groups, concerns the next world conference on international telecommunications (wcit 2012) of the international telecommunications union, to be held in dubai, united arab emirates, from 3 to 14 december 2012, during which the possible extension of the scope of the international telecommunications regulation will be discussed. i hope that the participation of the european union (eu) and the member states (ms) in this conference will be properly articulated since only ms can negotiate the proposals submitted so that no changes are made which could harm eu interests or limit the development of the acquis communautaire. in dubai, europe must speak with one voice and defend the freedom of internet access that some states would like to curb. i support the revision of the international telecommunications regulations in the framework of the wcit 2012 because it is a good opportunity to improve cooperation between countries in order to raise levels of economic and social development.
in writing. − this resolution seeks to ensure that the council and commission amendments to the regulation are in line with the 'eu's objective and interest in advancing the internet as a genuine public space', without any reference to the importance of truly universal, democratic and inclusive access. the resolution calls for respect for 'human rights and fundamental freedoms, in particular freedom of expression and assembly'. we agree. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. concern is expressed that 'itu proposals include the creation of new profit mechanisms ... raising prices and hindering innovation', which falls short of the necessary rejection of such profit mechanisms and a reversal of these policies, as some of their harmful effects are recognised. in the alternative, we signed a resolution which we regret was not adopted, as it was the only one to say that 'telecommunications and the internet are and should remain public goods, as this is the only way to ensure universal access to both and their democratic control'.
in writing. the resolution also calls on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's telecommunications policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. among the concerns raised, i would highlight the call on member states to prevent any changes to the international telecommunications regulation that could harm the openness of the internet, net neutrality, universal service obligations, creative content online and participatory governance by multiple actors such as governments, supranational institutions, non-governmental organisations, small and large enterprises, the technology community and internet users and consumers in general.
in writing. − the amendments to the international telecommunications regulation (itr) should be compatible with the eu acquis and should further the objective and interest of the internet to progress as a genuine public space, respecting human rights and fundamental freedoms. i am voting in favour of this resolution because i believe that the internet should remain free and open to citizens, that it should be multilateral and bottom-up, and that online services and the digital economy should be promoted. finally, the internet should be a space of freedom, ensuring respect for the principles of free markets, net neutrality and entrepreneurship.
in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that the fight against climate change must remain a priority, both at european and international level. i believe that the fight against climate change, in addition to its objective in itself, also contributes to sustainable growth, more employment and less dependence on imported energy sources. the european union must therefore show leadership at this conference, speaking with one voice, representing the 27 member states of the european union, in the pursuit of progress towards an international agreement.
in writing. − with just a few days to go until the cop 18 climate change conference in doha, 26 november to 7 december, it is relevant to know what steps the council is taking to ensure that the un framework conference on climate change produces concrete progress and results, especially with regard to the necessary modifications to the kyoto protocol, before the second commitment period which will start on 1 january 2013. equally important is to set an example by respecting your commitments in terms of funding and meeting the objectives you set.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure, following a number of questions for oral answer, concerns the conference on climate change to be held in doha, qatar, from 26 november to 7 december 2012. the recent natural disasters that have affected several countries, including italy, the united states of america (hurricane sandy) and portugal, and caused not only dozens of victims but millions of euros in damage, should lead governments to take the necessary environmental measures to prevent the average temperature of the globe from continuing to rise with the consequences we all know. although the cost of reducing greenhouse gas emissions may be high, it will always be far less than the consequences of not taking these measures. i therefore hope not only that the kyoto protocol will be extended, but that its objectives will be increased, that it will be extended to include developing countries and that it will be ratified by the largest emitters of greenhouse gases: the united states of america, china and india.
in writing. - this resolution aims to set out guidelines for the eu's mandate at cop 18. a reinforced approach is proposed in the run-up to the second commitment period of kyoto, calling for increased ambition by 2020 and seeking new sources of funding. the aim is to introduce robust accounting rules for 'land use', land use change and forestry, as well as for the reduction of emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, in particular with regard to the technical assessment of forest reference levels. while we agree on some points, we strongly disagree on others: the advocacy of creating a global carbon market, with "links between the eu emissions trading scheme and other emissions trading schemes", at a time when the ineffectiveness and perversity of this market approach is clearly visible; the advocacy of assigning a bargaining value by assigning a price to the "goods and services" provided by biodiversity; the halfway point towards the commodification and private appropriation of nature and its resources; the removal, as a result of the plenary vote, of the reference to patents (saying that developing countries will not be obliged to purchase them). that is why we voted against the report.
in writing. - the ep is calling for the adoption of a new directive on the protection of the environment and for the protection of the environment from harmful substances and their by-products.
in writing. − the doha conference (cop 18) should build on the momentum achieved in durban to ensure that a legally binding global agreement is finalised in 2015. this agreement should be consistent with the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities' and should recognise the need for all major emitters to adopt ambitious and sufficient targets and corresponding policy measures for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. the european parliament welcomes the establishment of the ad hoc working group on the durban platform for enhanced action, noting that decision 1/cp 17 requires the working group to start work on a legally binding document under the convention, applicable to all parties, as a matter of urgency and to conclude this work as soon as possible, and at the latest by 2015. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i approve the report because i believe that we need to reaffirm our support for the european union's external policies and recent enlargement processes, and we must always learn from all processes. i also think it is important to stress the social role complementary to the economic role of the applicant countries, and civil society in the european union and the applicant countries should be given the opportunity to express their views. i therefore welcome the proposal to include civil society organisations, trade unions and other beneficiaries of the pre-accession instrument fund in the enlargement process, as a key step towards better addressing social issues, labour rights and sensitive historical issues relating to ethnic and religious minorities. all this effort is necessary if we want a european union based on the values on which it is founded. in addition, the european parliament, in my view, must send a clear message that, despite the economic crisis, the eu must continue its enlargement policy which has proved to be a tool in consolidating democracy and stability in the candidate countries.
in writing. − the enlargement policy must take account of the particularities of the applicant and strictly respect the criteria and principles of the european union. in order to remain a credible process, access to the union must be transparent, balanced and fully respect the merit of the applicant. it is essential to pay the utmost attention to judicial reform and the fight against corruption and fraud from the very beginning of the evaluation process. i voted in favour of this report because i think the commission's decision is in the direction i have indicated.
in writing. − a well-planned enlargement policy could prove to be a successful strategy for the eu's economic development. since 1973, when the eu was first enlarged, it has been growing. this policy has been beneficial for the european union as a whole. it allows for the creation of conditions to address global challenges, prevent conflict, foster stability, stimulate reforms and consolidate peace. any state wishing to join the eu will have to commit itself to the values of freedom, equality, democracy and respect for human rights; the european union is built on these values. the enticing prospect of eu accession has had significant impacts on the candidate countries; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. candidate countries should be subject to an evaluation process where their own merit and compliance with the established criteria are at stake. the union is responsible for facilitating integration and for analysing the european aspirations of the applicants. however, it is important to be cautious about whether the union is able to successfully integrate new countries, which is particularly sensitive in a context of economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - believing that the european union should continue to support the accession process of the candidate countries provided that they are willing to accept the legacy of the community acquis and to meet the criteria imposed by the accession process, i voted in favour of this report. as i have had the opportunity to argue, to overcome the dramatic crisis we are experiencing, we need more europe. walk to a federal solution! greater economic, monetary, fiscal, social and political harmonization we have a critical mass of 500 million citizens, a trade surplus that overshadows the united states and china, a currency that in a decade has become the second largest in the world (hence much of the reason for the attacks of the commonly called "markets"), and a social model that is the envy of all other continents (which we will have to reform, however, because its sustainability is compromised). i also believe that we need, as a political entity, a genuine common foreign and defence policy. only then will we project our economic weight.
in writing. − the 2012 nobel peace prize was awarded to the european union (eu) for its contribution, over more than 60 years, to the advancement of peace and reconciliation, democracy and human rights in europe. the six founding states have been joined by 21 others, and others are interested in joining. the report, by maria eleni koppa, focuses on the enlargement of the eu to other countries, taking account of the eu's policies, criteria and strategic interests. everyone recognises that countries have significantly improved their quality of life by joining the eu. however, the applicant countries will have to prove their respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law and that they are not involved in conflicts. i welcome the adoption of this text, which is intended to maintain and strengthen the eu's enlargement policy - one of the most successful policies - and which proves the openness of the european project, based on the criteria of the copenhagen treaty. i would like to see no budgetary cuts in the enlargement chapter, but i understand that the financial situation requires it. we must therefore spend eu resources better.
in writing. − the enlargement of the eu to new countries, if it is to take place, must be the result of a sovereign decision of the peoples and countries concerned and respect their right to economic and social development. this report does not guarantee that these requirements will be met, and that is why we voted against it. the report also defies the principles of the united nations charter and international law. the 'new negotiating approach' advocated in the report is even more intrusive, imposing economic and social models and models of political systems and democracy that clash with the right of peoples to self-determination in accordance with their interests and aspirations. the majority of meps believe that the 'general interests of the eu' should prevail over the interests of the people and over 'disputes' between countries wishing to join. in the 'case of inability to reach a bilateral agreement', these countries must submit to a 'binding arbitration mechanism of their choice', i.e. the attempt to impose the eu's interest on sovereignty disputes. in particular, it is an attempt to force serbia to accept the secession of kosovo, which is advocated by the eu and nato, and cyprus to accept the accession of turkey, in a framework in which turkey maintains its occupation of the northern part of the former.
in writing. − the european project, as a project to promote peace and economic and social equity among peoples, is part of the very notion of enlargement. in this context, i am in favour of the progressive enlargement of the european union to include other countries and other peoples. in any event, i believe that this enlargement must take account of the european union's own capacity to integrate new states while maintaining the standards of respect for human rights and the promotion of social justice. in the present economic and social crisis, this imperative is even stronger. in this context, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - parliament strongly supports the enlargement process. it is important for the eu and the candidate countries to see that all obligations are fulfilled and respected, ensuring that the necessary conditions are created for a successful future enlargement. parliament considered that the copenhagen criteria should remain the fundamental basis for future enlargements. the committee on foreign affairs proposes a new approach for future negotiating frameworks that gives priority to issues related to the judicial system and fundamental rights, as well as justice and home affairs. any acceding state (albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, iceland, kosovo, montenegro, serbia and turkey) must also resolve its main bilateral problems and major disputes with neighbouring countries, particularly those relating to territorial issues, before it can join the union. the possibility of developing an arbitration mechanism to settle possible disputes between these states and their neighbours should therefore be considered.
in writing. − it is of vital importance for the eu and the candidate country that all obligations and commitments arising from the accession process are fulfilled by both sides. the accession/enlargement process should be carefully assessed, and the socioeconomic effects for both parties should be taken into account. the union should take into account not only the social implications of accession in the candidate country, but also its capacity for integration. in this context, it is important that the union maintains and strengthens the mechanisms for monitoring and socioeconomic support during the accession process. the new approach to be introduced in the new negotiations, giving priority to issues relating to justice and internal administration and insisting that new applicant countries should only join after they have resolved territorial disputes and/or other bilateral problems with their neighbours, helps to avoid deadlocks within the union itself. i also agree with the rapporteur's call for the commission and the council to set up an arbitration mechanism to settle bilateral and multilateral disputes. for the reasons set out above, i voted in favour of this report.
