in writing. − issues involving common security and defence, because they touch at the heart of member states' sovereignty, have evolved in a prudent way, but not always in a way that adequately responds to actual geostrategic challenges. in the face of global threats and the strategic devaluation of the atlantic area for the benefit of the asia-pacific region, it is clear that we must seek to respond to them by increasing the capacity and coordination of means and the actual and potential projection of forces. unfortunately, there are areas of tension and instability near the union's borders, which cannot but cause apprehension and motivate military vigilance and readiness. in this context, it is particularly important that the union should not only provide itself with the means but also strengthen its alliance with the united states and increasingly take on the burden-sharing part of the common effort to protect democracy and human rights. european society, fortunately largely free of armed conflict for some time now, has become accustomed to downplaying the importance of security and defence. policy makers should seek to reverse this trend and promote respect for and the need for the armed forces and the military condition.
in writing. - the enlargement of the european union (eu) to the east has brought peace to a large part of europe which was still, if not in an explicit conflict, at least in a latent one. the fall of the berlin wall and the end of the union of soviet socialist republics has emptied the role of military organizations such as nato. in reality, europe has never been so prosperous, secure or free as it is today. the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy (csdp), drawn up by mr arnaud danjean on the basis of the annual report from the council to the european parliament (ep) on the common foreign and security policy, draws attention to the need to improve our action, given the economic crisis member states are experiencing and the focus of nato's attention on a part of the world (africa and asia) other than europe. i welcome the adoption of this report, which i supported, which contains a very positive approach to the csdp, especially in times of budgetary austerity, because i agree that the eu cannot leave its defence to nato alone. the eu should therefore increase cooperation between member states and establish synergies between the csdp and other policies.
in writing. the majority of parliament advocates eu military autonomy through investment in defence and military armaments, 'sharing' and 'mutualization' of resources, permanent structured cooperation between 'countries with more ambitious criteria in terms of military capabilities', strengthening the role of the european defence agency, increased operability of rapid intervention groups, closer relations with nato. these developments are inseparable from the needs for access to and control of natural and energy resources on which the eu monopolies depend. the majority of the european parliament makes its ambition very clear here: the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. a policy that finally fulfils the eu's role as the european pillar of nato. it is only a position of the european parliament, but it highlights the need for democratic breakthroughs in the eu, with a process of demilitarisation and disarmament, the dissolution of nato and the creation of a collective security system which respects and ensures the sovereignty of states and the free choice of peoples.
in writing. − the eu is intended to be a global political actor in the international context, promoting international peace and security. in the context of this responsibility, which includes the security of its citizens, i voted in favour of this report, which sets out a new strategic framework for the common security and defence policy, arising from the many changes at the geostrategic level.
in writing. − the major changes taking place in the geostrategic context of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the csdp, in particular following the turmoil in the middle east and north africa (including revolutions, conflicts and/or regime change in libya, tunisia, egypt, syria) and the emergence on the international scene of new players with regional and even global ambitions, as well as the reorientation of the us defence policy priorities towards the asia-pacific region, imply that the eu should develop its civil and military capabilities by implementing practical measures to enable it to respond appropriately to these new challenges. the main aim is to enable the eu to assert itself as a global political actor in the international context, and to be able to assume its responsibilities in the face of international threats, crises and conflicts, especially in its neighbourhood. i voted in favour.
in writing. − the geostrategic environment in which the european union (eu) finds itself and the challenges it faces are forcing the institutions, in particular the council, to rethink the common security and defence policy. it is a fact that the eu's main partner, the united states of america, is giving increasing importance to the pacific to the detriment of europe. i agree with the rapporteur that the eu external action service needs to be strengthened in the area of crisis management and that greater cooperation between member states on common defence policy needs to be encouraged. greater cooperation in defence, including in terms of technology, military industry and intelligence sharing, should be promoted. such measures should be adopted within the framework of a strategy drawn up in advance, because only then will a real implementation of the lisbon treaty be possible, namely: permanent and structured cooperation, the application of the mutual assistance and solidarity clauses and a more active role for the european defence agency.
in writing. - i welcome this report because it is not about creating a new instrument but about bringing together and better coordinating different instruments to enable an effective response, so that appropriate solidarity can be provided when a member state sees its capacities exhausted. i also believe that in a time of financial crisis it is essential to identify solutions for joint investment and joint development of the member states. the need for a rapid response combined with a contribution from each country within a flexible framework may well meet many defence needs in the european union area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu should develop a policy of prevention and rapid response to any and all identified threats to the union or to any member state.
in writing. − the mutual defence and solidarity clauses are two mechanisms based on the same idea of union and solidarity between member states in times of particular adversity such as military interventions, terrorist attacks or natural disasters. the use of appropriate and available means to assist a state in a crisis of this nature is a natural consequence of the idea that in a united europe, the problem of one must be the problem of all, and where it is not possible to solve it individually, it must be sought collectively. as i have written, in addition to being united in diversity, the union must remain united in adversity. the clarification of the scope of these clauses and the provision of means to enable them to be used quickly and flexibly, if necessary, should be in the minds of key policy-makers who should stimulate synergies, cooperation and the exchange of information. the idea that the european union should cooperate actively with nato, and that nato today has aspects which go far beyond its purely military component, expands the potential sources of solidarity in the event of a crisis but also requires a serious commitment on the part of everyone.
in writing. the european union, as an area of free movement of people and goods and where the functioning of an increasingly prosperous single market is to be sought, must assume the role of a unifying entity and a catalyst for an ever stronger feeling of territorial cohesion. we need more and better europe, not just on paper but above all in practice. the treaty of lisbon reinforces this aspect: we need a genuine common security and defence policy (csdp) that protects european citizens and strengthens solidarity between member states. sometimes we have the means to act, but we lack the motivation from some institutions. to strengthen solidarity, of which the european globalisation adjustment fund is a good example, it is necessary to provide it with financial resources as a way of responding to natural disasters more efficiently. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr ioan mircea paşcu. i welcome the commission's greater technical and political commitment and hope that we will soon be able to move forward with the operation of the eu headquarters to have a greater capacity for intervention.
in writing. - under the lisbon treaty, the 'mutual defence clause' transforms the eu into an alliance with a stronger military bond, and the 'solidarity clause' paves the way for military interventions on eu territory. the explicit 'obligation' to respond 'by all means' in the event of aggression against a member state goes even further than the nato clause, since it also includes unarmed attacks. under the solidarity clause, military support is requested in the event of terrorist attacks and natural or man-made disasters (whose scope is unclear: social unrest, resulting from strikes? protests?), which implies the conduct of military operations on eu territory. the solidarity clause can also be activated in the event of cyberattacks, pandemics and power cuts. this report is inseparable from the crisis in the eu, the looting of countries like portugal, the exploitation of workers and people, the regression in rights, the loss of sovereignty and the regression in political and democratic freedoms. but it is at the same time inseparable from the growth of the struggle and the fear that the capitalist monopolies and the political forces at their service have of the emergence of processes of emancipation of the peoples.
in writing. − considering that the security of eu member states must be shared and that all european citizens must have the same security guarantees and an equal level of protection against conventional and unconventional threats, i voted in favour of this report on eu mutual defence and solidarity clauses: political and operational dimensions.
in writing. the common security and defence policy has two important principles underlying it: the solidarity clause and the mutual defence clause. these two clauses have different implications when 'activated', but both require member states not only to cooperate more closely but also to develop their military capabilities. an integrated approach to attacks and/or disasters which may affect the european union as a whole has to be created by creating a system of coordinating means of response to the most diverse types of crisis. only then will the union be able to realise the full potential of the provisions of the treaties. for the reasons set out above, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − i welcome this report, drawing attention to the need for better coordination and coherence in cybersecurity and cyber defence. only in this way will we be able to better meet your challenges, which in my view require member states to develop their own cybersecurity and cyber defence plans, alongside an approach of their own to this issue by the european union as a whole. i think the european union should be careful, starting to deal directly with the private sector for a faster exchange of information, always respecting the anonymity of private sector partners, ensuring a balance between security measures and the defence of fundamental rights and freedoms. in particular, the european union should invest in its transatlantic relations with the united states in order to strengthen cooperation in this area.
in writing. − cybersecurity is a colossal challenge for the european union. cyberattacks are an undeniable threat to the defence, stability and competitiveness of the european space. the rapporteur notes that the digital sphere is becoming increasingly aggressive and stresses that the vast majority of threats in this area are currently politically motivated. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the eu must take measures to ensure the safe use of information and digital technologies and to provide reliable services and infrastructures for cybersecurity and cyber defence.
in writing. − dependence on information and communication technologies and on cyberspace is a reality at virtually all levels of society. an attack on some of these most important assets risks having practical consequences in terms of the security and defence of populations and the infrastructures that serve them, compromising communications and transport, rendering health systems unable to act, triggering the activation of military arsenals, exposing and misappropriating defence and trade secrets, allowing the diversion of funds, among many other negative possibilities. in short, it is putting at risk the free and peaceful coexistence of citizens and the survival and balance of their communities and the environment around them. it is well known that real wars are now fought at the computer level and that cybersecurity issues call for a real cyber defence of the key points of member states' systems and a relentless fight against cybercrime. the european union and its member states cannot ignore the urgency of this fight and must provide themselves with the best human and technical resources to develop it and coordinate their action among themselves and with nato.
in writing. - the era of globalisation has invaded the modern world. what happens thousands of miles away can also affect us, and much so. today, the "information highways" are filled with a remarkable amount of data that, if used well, can do much to improve our quality of life. however, when accessed by those with bad intentions, it can have highly damaging effects. the report by tunne kelan focuses on the issue of cybersecurity and cyberdefence. this is a matter of great interest to which not all ms are aware, as evidenced by the fact that only 10 ms have adopted a prevention strategy against high-damaging aggressors. piracy and cyber attacks against public administrations are common and will certainly increase as the social and economic crisis worsens. we must therefore protect our structures against this kind of terrorism which does not use explosives. i voted in favour of this report which highlights the need to improve our cohesion and to establish a regulatory framework which not only punishes cybercrime but also protects citizens - children and young people in particular - and public and private institutions from the threats posed by the misuse of the internet.
in writing. − we recognise the importance of ensuring that people are safe and secure when using the internet and the infrastructure that supports the service. as the report points out, there are 2 billion connected users worldwide. the internet is a powerful medium for spreading ideas, democratizing access to knowledge and facilitating a growing set of services. but this report is alarming because it is part of a security strategy which is deeply damaging to the freedom of expression of the people and their democratic rights. it brings into the pseudo-justifications for the application of the eu's solidarity and mutual defence clause (lisbon treaty) the "cyberattacks". it also calls for cybersecurity to become an active capability of the common security and defence policy, i.e. the militarisation of control over the internet. it advocates the establishment of public-private partnerships in this area, thereby transferring public resources to software and hardware monopolies through the european defence agency. he also called for the eu and nato to pool and share resources. the icing on the cake is the proposal that juvenile offenders convicted of cyberattacks be rehabilitated and integrated into defense agencies and bodies.
in writing. − considering that the strengthening of trust between the private sector and the security forces and services, defence institutions and other competent authorities is of the utmost importance for the fight against cybercrime, i voted in favour of this report which presents forms of action articulated between these entities.
in writing. − this report aims to strengthen the safe use of digital and information technologies and to strengthen the resilience and reliability of information services and related infrastructures. the rapporteur therefore calls for the development of a comprehensive cybersecurity and, where appropriate (at eu and member state level), a cybersecurity and defence strategy that can respond to cyber emergencies, through the development of national emergency plans. the report encourages member states to create dedicated cybersecurity and cyberdefence units integrated into their military structures and to make research and development one of the key pillars of cybersecurity and cyberdefence, encouraging the training of engineers specialised in the protection of information systems.
in writing. − the concept of security extends beyond land borders and countries as nation-states. for these reasons, a strategy to combat cybercrime is necessary at union and member state level. a cybersecurity and cyber defence strategy requires coordinated action between the union and the member states. the development of information and digital technologies now allows any citizen to challenge a government system or access sensitive data. i therefore support the union's proposal to develop a common strategy and complementary actions with the main eu partners. however, i would also like to stress that the concepts of cybersecurity and cyber defence should not call into question respect for the rights and guarantees of european citizens.
in writing. - i support this report because i believe there is a clear need for stronger multilateral cooperation and better global governance on climate security. in my view, the european union, as a major global player in the environment, should start thinking about mitigating the main effects of climate change in its most important security strategies. the european union must also, as a symbol of innovation, make its mark on the world stage as a champion of the use of green technologies for military purposes, since we are already clearly behind the united states in this respect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that climate change and natural disasters have an impact on the security and stability of societies, both economically and politically, and that the eu should take these factors into account in its foreign policy.
in writing. - several observers point to the climate issue as one of the main likely causes of future conflicts. the european union must take this into account when formulating its security and defence policies. some regions of the globe will be particularly prone to such conflicts. the european union will have to devise ways and means of meeting the challenges it faces. you already have a number of tools at your disposal which you should make full use of. the question of the union's energy dependence is particularly important and cannot be left out of this reflection and our future action.
in writing. - recent natural disasters, which are occurring more or less everywhere, such as the recent hurricane sandy in the united states of america (usa), emphasise the growing need to equalise climate change mitigation measures. this report, by indrek tarand, focuses on the role of the common security and defence policy (csdp) in climate-related crises and natural disasters. we might be tempted to think that climate change doesn't affect us because we live far from the coastline and sea level rise won't hit us, nor do we build on water lines or inconsistent soils, etc. this is not only a selfish position but also a wrong one. the consequences of climate change affect all people, directly or indirectly. it is therefore urgent to improve preventive measures and our climate security, especially in the most vulnerable areas. we must not forget that climate change has a direct impact on security and the economy, and can lead people to emigrate to other parts of the globe. finally, a word to stress the need for cooperation at international level, particularly with the usa and emerging countries responsible for high greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. the report starts by manipulating legitimate fears about crises caused by more or less extreme weather events and natural disasters, to elevate them to the category of 'the greatest threat to security in the world'. it thus seeks to justify the deepening of the eu's militarization process, the development of military capabilities by the european defence agency, the strengthening of coordination between nato and the eu in the field of 'meeting and sharing' and 'intelligent defence' projects while respecting the 'specific activities' of both organisations. these priorities confirm what we have been saying: that the process of militarization of the eu is making the eu the european pillar of nato. the real aim is to respond to the intensifying global struggle for access to and domination of the regions from which the eu monopolies depend on the energy resources and key raw materials. the emergence or threat of conflicts in third countries due to climate phenomena will only be effectively resolved if their causes are properly identified and addressed. there can be no solution unless neo-colonialism, the destruction of national sovereignty, the economic domination of capitalist monopolies are put to an end, that is, unless a dominant production system based on the exploitation of nature and man is defeated.
in writing. − complex crises must be prevented through a comprehensive approach with policies making full use of the instruments available under the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the common security and defence policy (csdp), as well as humanitarian and development aid policies. i believe that this approach can have a positive effect on combating climate-related crises and natural disasters, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − climate change and its socioeconomic consequences pose challenges to the common security and defence policy. the conflicts that have emerged in the horn of africa and the sahel have been triggered by climate change in these regions. the high representative should therefore take climate change into account by placing it at the heart of risk analyses for civilian and military missions. the need to take account of climate change should be a cross-cutting issue for the entire external action service of the european union. an integrated approach must be created by establishing a system for coordinating the means of responding to the most diverse types of crisis, a system which should be in permanent contact with the un, nato and ngos. for the reasons set out above, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i approve this report because i consider a strengthened partnership with kazakhstan to be extremely useful, both because of its geostrategic situation and because through our partnership we can implement important processes of civil, institutional and political reform. however, i consider it essential to stress the need for kazakhstan to demonstrate a deep commitment to show progress on universal rights, democracy, the rule of law, labour and social rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with its assumptions.
in writing. − kazakhstan has played an important role in central asia, in developing good relations with neighbouring countries and in the peaceful settlement of bilateral issues. the eu has also been active in the fight against terrorism, and has been active in the fight against organised crime. however, the tragic events of december 2011 (repression and detention of opposition members) and the irregularities visible in the course of the 15 january 2012 elections allow us to infer that kazakhstan still has a long way to go. in the framework of the negotiations on a new partnership and cooperation agreement, a constructive dialogue is under way between the eu, representatives of kazakhstan and representatives of civil society on issues of mutual interest. the eu is the largest investor in kazakhstan and relies significantly on imported natural phosphorus for agricultural production, making maintaining good trade relations even more relevant. i therefore support the strengthening of the eu-kazakhstan partnership and welcome the political efforts made by that country and its openness to fruitful negotiations on a future partnership and cooperation agreement.
in writing. - the countries of central asia have long been seen as failed states, remnants of the ussr's disintegration and without particular strategic interest. i think this approach is deeply wrong and i believe that from the point of view of cooperation, security and defence and access to energy sources and raw materials, these states now have a relevant position vis-à-vis the european union. the country in question, kazakhstan, has a long, rich and varied history and has repeatedly demonstrated its desire to move closer to the european union and develop a stable partnership with it. i welcome this wish and hope that kazakhstan can actually converge more and more with the eu, in particular on issues related to democracy and human rights i hope that kazakhstan will take concrete steps to demonstrate this accession and that the negotiations now being held by parliament will be beneficial to both parties and their peoples.
in writing. the report by ms jaakonsaari contains parliament's recommendations to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the negotiations for a partnership and cooperation agreement (acp) between the european union (eu) and kazakhstan. although kazakhstan is the most open economy in central asia and the european union's (eu) most important partner in the region, we cannot dissociate scrupulous respect for human rights from our partnership agreements. if kazakhstan wants to remain an eu trading partner, it must move forward with the ongoing internal reforms in full respect for freedom of association, assembly, expression and religion. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the eu-kazakhstan negotiations in the framework of a new partnership agreement must include respect for eu values and a set of reforms towards the establishment of a democratic regime. if there is a violation of human rights, the agreement must be suspended. given that kazakhstan has applied for membership of the world trade organisation, which has the support of the eu, i agree that the agreement in preparation will only be concluded after accession.
in writing. the recommendations adopted by the majority of parliament constitute an inadmissible process of interference in kazakhstan's internal affairs and sovereignty by defending the incorporation of clauses in its constitution. it is not a question of incorporating the demands and demands of its people, at the time and under the conditions defined by it, but of forcing this country to face up to internationally established norms. they are taking advantage of a worrying situation with regard to workers' rights and democratic rights to try to justify the eu's pressure and interference in internal processes in the life of this country which, however worrying, are the responsibility of the people of kazakhstan alone to change. the aim is not to help improve the working and living conditions of these people. the real objectives are the liberalization of trade relations, invoking the wto agreements, and access to the energy resources of which this country is fertile. the real concern of the majority in parliament is to force a negotiation in which they will use all the tools and arguments to obtain the advantages that the eu monopolies currently demand.
in writing. − the partnership and cooperation agreements are part of a geostrategic policy of major importance to the eu. it is important that this eu-kazakhstan partnership and cooperation agreement takes the form of a comprehensive framework for the development of relations, addressing all the priority areas that allow for a closer and more cooperative relationship between the two parties, including human rights, the rule of law, good governance, youth and education, economic development, trade and investment, energy and transport, environmental sustainability and water, as well as the fight against common threats and challenges. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european union and kazakhstan aim to deepen and broaden their relations and their citizens should mutually benefit from closer cooperation, so the conclusion of the negotiations on the new partnership and cooperation agreement should provide a comprehensive framework for cooperation based on human and democratic rights, as well as opportunities in terms of socioeconomic development and the necessary political and economic reforms. the european parliament therefore welcomes the political will and practical commitment of kazakhstan to strengthen the partnership with the eu and the opening of negotiations for an eu-kazakhstan partnership and cooperation agreement. i have voted in favour of the document, stressing the importance of political dialogue and cooperation, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms and economic cooperation.
in writing. - because the crisis in the fishing sector particularly affects small-scale fishing, it is important to remember that it ensures the livelihood of many families and is a factor of fixation of fishing communities along coastal areas. it is therefore important to ensure the economic and social stability of their communities. and this must be done from the outset by promoting fisheries management by marine biogeographical territories, for fair and informed local management of small-scale fisheries with little autonomy and freezing capacity on board and which do not operate outside their exclusive economic zone. the current regime for access to waters should therefore be adjusted, with particular attention to regions with a sea basin with few fisheries resources in the interests of their sustainability.
in writing. - the allocation of a minimum amount of resources from the new emff to small-scale fisheries; - priority should be given to projects with integrated solutions which benefit all coastal communities as widely as possible, rather than those benefiting only a small number of operators. - the creation of mechanisms to ensure that the so-called positive externalities generated by small-scale fishing and not remunerated by the market are recognised, both at the environmental level and at the level of economic and social cohesion of coastal communities; - the creation of specific support mechanisms to be used in emergency situations such as natural disasters, stoppages of activity caused by stock replenishment plans or sudden increases in fuel prices.
in writing. - i agree with the concept of 'small fishing' explained in this report. i believe that it was necessary to go into the details of this explanation for the good and benefit of the cfp, but also for all those who work in the sector. these characteristics are usually associated with small-scale fishing and include: the strong link to the economy, social structure, culture and traditions of coastal towns and communities. i therefore believe that, as stated in the european parliament resolution of 25 february 2010 on the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy, small-scale fishing should be treated differently and be subject to management schemes or models adapted to its specific characteristics and problems.
in writing. - mr joão ferreira has presented an excellent paper on coastal fishing, small-scale fishing and the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). we have already discussed here on several occasions the failure of the present cfp. support for the slaughter of many vessels has not contributed to improving fisheries resources and has thrown thousands of fishermen, most of whom come from small communities, into unemployment. it is therefore essential that the new cfp exploits the potential of small fishing communities, not only in tackling the social and financial crisis by fixing families who are in danger of leaving their villages, but also by contributing in a sustainable way to the conservation of resources and the conservation of the marine ecosystem. they must therefore be protected from large-scale fishing. i voted in favour of this report because i support a significant increase in support for small-scale fishing, especially in the outermost regions, decentralised management of this sector and the use of more selective gear. the improvement of infrastructure and safety conditions on board vessels, the encouragement of young workers and the organisation of the sector are other areas which deserve very special attention under the new cfp.
in writing. - we welcome the adoption of this report which proposes a more favourable overall approach to cfp reform for small-scale fisheries (which account for about 90% of the portuguese fleet), with better consideration of their problems but also their potential. with this report, the european parliament takes, in some cases for the first time, important positions in defence of small-scale fisheries and advances with concrete proposals of various scope, such as: a significant decentralisation of fisheries management; transferable fishing concessions; the defence of positive discrimination between segments and operators using more selective fishing gear and equipment; increased community participation in the financing of the acquisition, processing and provision of biological data; the need for a financial instrument for the outermost regions; the financing of actions by the future european fisheries and maritime affairs fund; the creation of support mechanisms for emergency situations; the establishment of financial compensation during periods of biological standstill; the possibility of defining exclusive access areas for small-scale fisheries; the defence of existing public regulatory instruments; and mechanisms that promote fair and fair value added and distribution along the value chain of the sector.
in writing. − this report lists and emphasises numerous specific features of small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing which should be duly taken into account in the ongoing reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). small-scale fishing includes a wide variety of fisheries, fleet types and fishing gear, which vary widely between member states and depending on the areas of operation. however, regardless of its geographical location, small-scale fishing activity has a certain set of common characteristics, including close links with local communities, the prevalence of family units, micro and small enterprises, fishing relatively close to the coast and with short stay at sea, the use of more selective fishing gear with less impact on marine resources and the marine environment, among others. i voted in favour of this report because of the wide spread and enormous socioeconomic importance of small-scale fishing along large stretches of eu coastline and because i agree that the particular characteristics of small-scale fishing justify a different treatment for this fishing activity.
in writing. − the types of fisheries and fisheries covered by the concept of 'small-scale fishing' are very different from each other, varying according to the member states and fishing zones. the european commission, in conjunction with the member states, should carry out a more rigorous characterization of small-scale fishing. this information supports knowledge-based management, which is essential to increase the community effort in financing the acquisition, processing and provision of this information. the rapporteur is putting forward a set of concrete proposals to support small-scale fishing. given the structural weaknesses of small-scale fishing and its increased vulnerability, this segment is more exposed to certain types of external shocks or sudden changes in the availability of resources than fleet segments considered to be more competitive. the possibility of setting up specific support mechanisms to be used in emergency situations should therefore be considered.
in writing. − small-scale fisheries should be treated differently and be subject to management schemes or models adapted to their specific characteristics and problems. the rapporteur therefore considered that changes were needed in small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing as part of the reform of the common fisheries policy. the definition of 'small fisheries' should take into account a set of criteria in addition to the strict criterion of size. the reform of the cfp should also ensure the conditions for effective local fisheries management, which is the best way of meeting the needs of small-scale fisheries. the reform of the cfp should also encourage improvements in the environmental, economic and social sustainability of the fleet and encourage developments that will bring greater benefits to communities, in particular in terms of job creation. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i approve this report, starting by stating that the external dimension of the common fisheries policy is, in my view, an essential element of this policy. the european union is one of the main markets for fishery products and the world's largest importer of fishery products, consuming some 11% of the world's fishery products in terms of volume and importing 24% of all fishery products in terms of value, while still accounting for only 8% of the world's catches. in my view, the need for a clear reinforcement of the external dimension of the european union's common fisheries policy is clear. in this connection, i would like to stress that in a context of liberalization which is weighing on fragile regions, it is necessary to ensure that products from international trade meet the same requirements as union products and that the commission should carry out impact studies, particularly where the outermost regions are affected by bilateral agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to strengthen the optimisation of eu policy with regard to the objectives of development, trade and fisheries policies.
in writing. − as a member of this parliament from one of the countries with the largest exclusive fishing economic zone in the world, i believe that the objectives which should guide the external action of the common fisheries policy (cfp) should be to defend the eu's fishing interests, whenever in line with the eu's external policy. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common organisation of the market in fishery products, which is to be adopted by the council on 1 january 1999, is intended to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not deprived of its fishing opportunities.
in writing. the european market depends on imports for about 60% of its fish consumption needs. most of the rest is provided under the partnership agreements. as the world's largest consumer market for fish, with a share of 11% of the world's fish, the eu has a major responsibility in restoring fish stocks and, at the same time, in the recovery and revitalisation of the eu's fishing industry. it is essential that the eu not only cares about the marine resources in its waters, but also presents a global concern in this area. to achieve improvements in international fisheries, the eu must lead in environmental and management terms through a plan that is consensual for long-distance fishing and for which it must obtain the agreement of third countries. it is therefore imperative to collaborate and work with the fishermen of these countries in order to standardize vessels. in our view, the best management is not that which favours individual agreements but regional ones, with full respect for the conservation of existing resources. because we are faced with a good report which can change the behaviour of this sector at global level and which will ensure sustainability in all international waters, i voted in favour.
in writing. the external dimension of the common fisheries policy needs to be radically changed. the fisheries agreements, hitherto known as 'partnerships', which the commission now wants to designate as 'sustainable fisheries' (sfa), are still in need of major changes. we have made concrete proposals during the debate in plenary, taking up some of the proposals we made in the opinion on policy coherence for development. we generally welcome and support the rapporteur's approach, including proposals to decouple financial compensation from development aid, to involve third countries more closely in agreements and to strengthen scientific and technical cooperation. we appreciate the fact that the unacceptable paragraphs on eu foreign policy and the military operation 'atlanta' in the somali area have been removed to cover the long-running plundering of resources in the region. we regret the paragraphs on the compatibility of the ppas with wto rules.
in writing. − the external dimension of the common fisheries policy (cfp) is complex and covers a variety of parameters, including catching fish by the eu fleet operating outside community waters, importing fish into the eu from other geographical areas, exporting fish caught in community waters, and so on. it is therefore important that these diverse activities are properly regulated so that the eu's fishing interests are pursued in a framework of full legality and sustainability at environmental, economic and social levels. on the other hand, it is also necessary to ensure that the eu fleet maintains its strategic and competitive presence in third country waters, while strictly complying with the requirements of environmental sustainability, social responsibility, respect for fundamental human rights principles and operating in accordance with the standards applied to operators in the eu fishing sector. i voted in favour of this report because i recognise the enormous importance of the external dimension of the common fisheries policy and i agree in general with the proposals presented, albeit with several reservations in certain respects which i considered excessive, notably with regard to the fisheries partnership agreements (fpas).
in writing. − the external dimension of the common fisheries policy contains many areas, such as bilateral fisheries agreements and regional fisheries management organisations. in addition, there are a number of issues which are not regulated by european union law and which are still 'grey areas'. the reform of the common fisheries policy thus aims to contribute to the promotion of the long-term sustainable development of the sector, to obtain high-quality scientific advice and to contribute to better governance and management of financial assistance to the sector. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document.

rapporteur. − madam president, this trade agreement with our friends from colombia and peru includes a human rights clause stating that the failure to respect human rights and democratic principles would constitute a material breach which, under public international law, could give rise to the adoption of appropriate measures, including the possibility of terminating or partially or totally suspending the agreement. it also enshrines a chapter on sustainable development and labour rights, and the creation of domestic mechanisms and dialogue with civil society which will involve citizens, whether individually or in an organised, collective manner, such as trade unions, employee representatives or other relevant stakeholders such as ngos. regardless of all these clauses and mechanisms, some political groups and members refuse to accept the new reality due to old problems – which are being gradually resolved in both andean countries – relating to longstanding problems of poverty, violence and corruption, internal armed conflict, illegal armed groups, drug trafficking, impunity and land dispossession. this happens due to old stigmas, preconceived ideas and prejudices which no longer correspond to reality and to the new political, social and economic atmosphere in these countries. it is clear that there is a genuine and indisputable commitment by both states and governments to a higher level of human welfare and wellbeing in their countries. here are a few examples: - the dialogue with civil society; the dialogue with the unions; the peace talks with farc; the reduction of poverty; water preservation; indigenous peoples’ rights; strengthening of fundamental labour rights shown, for example, by the ratification of the eight ilo fundamental conventions and three of the four governance conventions;- in colombia: the comprehensive and ambitious action plan on human, environmental and labour rights up to 2014, with clear and verifiable targets; the high-level dialogue on human rights between colombia and the eu; the fight against impunity; the witness protection programme; the creation of the ministry of labour; the regulation of the actions of worker cooperatives; the new restitution and victims’ law. - in peru: the national strategy for the prevention and the eradication of child labour; the national plan on environmental action; the act and regulation on prior consultation; and the new high-level institutions where civil society is now participating. it was an astonishing surprise to realise the level of impressive changes that these two countries have gone through in recent years. it was almost like rediscovering them. actually i think some of us did. others do not want to. last june, in a resolution that we passed in this house, we requested a roadmap for the improvement of human and labour rights, better environmental protection and a more efficient monitoring and scrutiny by civil society of the implementation of the pre-established goals. both governments freely and voluntarily answered us positively, showing us how highly committed they are to these three objectives. i highly value both government plans which, more than answering our requests, are proposing major and binding action plans for a better future for the two nations. that is why i hope to count on your sincere and large support for this consent recommendation so that we will vote positively on it tomorrow, being sure that our principles and our fundamental values are duly respected.
there are two good reasons for supporting this trade agreement between the european union and colombia and peru. the first reason is that it is a good agreement from a trade point of view, with great potential for creating growth and jobs. this is important from the point of view of the european union, especially in view of the current crisis in the european economy. we need to take advantage of the opportunities that foreign trade gives us. just last week, eurostat showed that exports are the only sector currently contributing to the growth of the european economy. and colombia and peru are now two vibrant economies with enormous growth potential, and colombia may soon be the second largest economy in south america. secondly, the second big reason to support this agreement is that this agreement is not just a trade agreement: it can be a powerful instrument for improving the situation of human rights in general and workers' rights in particular. first, there is the chapter on sustainable development with an advanced definition of the core label standards, which have to be defended. secondly, for the first time, as has already been pointed out here, the safeguard regulation includes monitoring of social conditions in colombia and peru. and finally, a precedent of enormous scope: this european parliament was able to obtain from colombia and peru the road map with very precise commitments to improve this situation. contrary to what i have heard here from some of the critics of this agreement, ratification of it does not mean an endorsement of the violation of workers' rights in colombia and peru. on the contrary, it means an endorsement of the positive changes that are already taking place, and it means an endorsement of a powerful lever that is to use international trade to improve the rights of workers in colombia and peru. and that is why, as a social democrat, i am very proud to vote in favour of this agreement.

rapporteur. − mr president, first of all i want to express my gratitude to all the shadow rapporteurs and give a particular mention to all the work done in cooperation with the rapporteur on the safeguard clause, my friend bernd lange, as well as with commissioner karel de gucht and his team. i would also like to give a special word of thanks to the very numerous civil society organisations, from labour unions to ngos, that we heard and discussed with in the course of this long and widely-participated process of ratification. but in democracy the political power lies in the constitutional institutions elected by the people for the people. until now, it has been time to debate, to listen to civil society and to consolidate ideas. now it is time to act, to decide. when it is time to decide, it is up to the democratic parliaments or congresses, both here or in bogotá and lima. i am sorry to be so blunt, but it is us, not ngos or trade unions, that represent all citizens. also, we cannot forget that, according to an independent study, this agreement will boost colombian gdp by 1.3 % and peruvian gdp by 0.7 % in the long term. this deal will result in total tariff savings of more than eur 500 million per year. this is how much we – consumers – may save. in times where economic growth and employment creation should be two of our main objectives as politicians, this trade agreement is a new and important tool for all the 29 nations involved. approving this trade agreement is also a way for the eu to show its support for the ongoing talks for peace and conciliation in colombia. finally, let me emphasise to all colleagues the very good news from last friday when, after 11 years on the blacklist for the violation of human rights, colombia was withdrawn from this blacklist by the inter-american commission on human rights.
the rapporteur. − this is one of the most important regulations we have voted on so far in the area of international trade, as it implements and gives effect to one of the most important innovations in the lisbon treaty. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted by the introduction of the euro. and since the union has exclusive competence in matters of common commercial policy, this means that from now on only the union can legislate and adopt legally binding acts in this area, including the negotiation of treaties to protect the union's external investment. the member states can now do this themselves only if and when they are authorized by the union to do so. however, when the treaty of lisbon entered into force three years ago, the member states had concluded numerous bilateral investment agreements with third countries: more than 1 200. the main purpose of these agreements is, as you know, to provide protection for investments made abroad against arbitrary actions, expropriation, for example, by the governments of the countries receiving the investment. the lisbon treaty did not lay down any explicit transitional provisions for existing agreements, which henceforth fall within the exclusive competence of the union. this regulation was therefore necessary to ensure a transition as smooth as possible, in order to reduce the legal uncertainty which results from this transitional period as regards the status of the existing treaties. according to this regulation, which was negotiated at length with the council, bilateral agreements negotiated between member states and third countries before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon remain in force until they are replaced by an investment agreement of the union or otherwise expire, unless they are contrary to union law, in which case they must be reviewed or cancelled by the member states concerned on the initiative of the european commission. secondly, the regulation also legalises bilateral investment treaties negotiated by member states illegally after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, provided that they comply with the strict conditionality laid down in the regulation. that was the price parliament demanded for legalizing these agreements. thirdly, this regulation also sets out the conditions, strictly random, under which member states may henceforth be authorised to amend or conclude new international investment agreements in cases where the union obviously has no interest in negotiating them itself. the commission will present a report to the european parliament and the council on its implementation no later than 10 years from now, and then the situation can be assessed and any necessary amendments proposed. it's been a long road to get here. as rapporteur for this dossier, i have to say that i consider the agreement to be fully satisfactory and that the fundamental objectives of the european parliament have been achieved for the good of the union and for the good of our businesses and our investments.
the rapporteur. - mr president, allow me to join in praising the seriousness and responsibility of commissioner de gucht. that is probably why he has so far rarely lost an initiative in the european parliament, with the exception of the failed acta agreement. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this is a happy ending to a negotiation that was anything but easy. member states were slow to become convinced, first, that foreign direct investment had become an exclusive competence of the union, second, that existing bilateral treaties could only remain in force if they were not an obstacle to the development of the union's investment policy and, third, that there was an invaluable added value in a common external trade policy rather than a policy fragmented among the 27 member states of the union. as we come to the end of these difficult negotiations, it is important to stress the commitment, the seriousness and the responsibility of the three institutions. it would not have been possible without the contribution of the polish presidency of the council, which opened the negotiations, and the danish presidency, which concluded them, and without the mediation of the commission, without whose contribution we could hardly have reached an agreement. let me remind you of the leading role played by the deputy director-general, mr joão aguiar machado, who was unrivaled in his attempt to find satisfactory solutions between the council and the european parliament, and finally by my fellow shadow rapporteurs, in particular pavel zalewski, who did not compromise on their commitment to reaching an agreement, however difficult it might have seemed at first. i therefore ask this house to adopt this regulation with broad support. it is a huge step towards greater integration of the union's external trade policy and external investment policy. from now on, the union will be closer, an ever closer union, also here in the field of external trade and foreign investment.
the rapporteur. - i guess today's my day. i have no good news to give parliament this time, but i ask again that you support my position and the position of inta, the parliament's committee on international trade, in our position to fight the council on this matter. the committee on international trade, of which i am the chairman, proposes that this house approve the commission's proposal, submitted in december 2011, to make available macro-financial assistance to the kyrgyz republic up to a maximum amount of eur 30 million. the report adopted at inta, for which i am rapporteur, only approved a minor amendment to remove from the recitals the justification for adopting the advisory procedure on comitology as regards the control of the commission's implementing powers by the member states. unfortunately, it was not possible to reach an agreement with the council on this matter. the view of the committee on international trade in this house, supported by a large majority, is that if there is a need for comitology, which can be and has been disputed, then the consultative procedure should be used in the case of the memoranda of understanding on macrofinancial assistance, as happened in previous cases with ukraine and moldova, and not the examination procedure, as proposed by the council, which gives the member states, as we know, that is to say the council, through the member states, a veto power over the commission's implementing powers. the council considers that the examination procedure should be used as a general rule and that the advisory procedure should be exceptional and should be adopted only on the basis of special case-by-case justification. once again, the council has clearly changed its position on this matter, as it had previously accepted the consultative procedure in the agreements on macrofinancial assistance to moldova and ukraine. it should be clear that the point of contention between parliament and the council on macrofinancial assistance to kyrgyzstan, as well as to georgia, is not a matter of substance and whether or not this country fulfils the conditions to deserve such assistance. we certainly support the granting of financial support to kyrgyzstan. there are two interlinked political issues at stake: an institutional question, which is what degree of control member states should have over the commission's implementing acts in this area, and a related political question, which is whether the european parliament can accept increased control by the council via the member states over the commission when the parliament does not have, or would not have, the same power of control over the commission. this is an issue on which parliament must remain firm in defending the balance of powers established in the lisbon treaty and make it clear that we do not accept the council's instrumentalisation of comitology to enable it to recover the powers which the lisbon treaty requires to be conferred on the commission and shared equally with the european parliament. it is important to make it clear to the council that this strategy cannot be vindicated and that it is also unacceptable for the council to sacrifice the interests of kyrgyzstan and georgia for a sectarian position on institutional matters.
the rapporteur. - mr president, there are two good reasons for supporting this commission proposal. firstly, macrofinancial assistance is not a gift, it is on the one hand a loan and on the other hand an investment which the union is making in economic stabilisation and democratic transition in kyrgyzstan. macro-financial assistance can and should also be subject to relevant conditions, in particular the rule of law. this is the case here, because article 5 of this regulation specifically states that there must be conditions in the fight against fraud and corruption. so the question is whether the union should reject this financial assistance on the basis of the situation in kyrgyzstan or whether it should give it just to leverage its capacity to press for and demand progress in the rule of law and democratic transition in kyrgyzstan. i have no doubt, once again, that the correct choice on our part is the second. i therefore call for our support for this commission proposal and for macrofinancial assistance to kyrgyzstan.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, direct investment has ceased to be a competence of the member states and has become an exclusive competence of the european union and an integral part of the european union's external trade policy. i think this is a positive objective, because it will boost trade and increase the competitiveness of the european economy as a whole. at the same time, i am pleased that this regulation does not mean that member states will no longer be able to have bilateral trade agreements. this report thus makes an important contribution to the further development of the european union's role as a global actor. the new regulation stresses that this role should be developed in line with the objectives of external actions (development, human rights, etc.).

in writing. − at the time of the entry into force of the lisbon treaty (tl), member states had concluded some 1 400 bilateral investment agreements with third countries. however, the tl did not define any transitional mechanism for existing agreements, which are now the exclusive competence of the union. this regulation was therefore necessary to ensure a transition as smooth as possible, in order to reduce legal uncertainty during the transitional period as to the status of the existing treaties. i therefore voted in favour of this important regulation on international trade, which will make it possible to implement and give effect to one of the great demands of the tl! i would remind you that with the entry into force of the tl, foreign direct investment has been integrated into the common commercial policy. since this is an exclusive competence of the eu, this means that only the eu can legislate and adopt legally binding acts in this area, including the negotiation of treaties to protect the union's external investment. the member states can now do this themselves only if and when they are authorized to do so by the union.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, in accordance with articles 206 and 207 tfeu, foreign direct investment becomes an exclusive competence of the union. the commission should also be able to provide information on the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to third countries, including the union's macro-financial assistance to third countries, in accordance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. the transitional measures now adopted do not constitute a precedent for the union to empower member states, in the framework of future regulations, to legislate and adopt legally binding acts in areas of the union's exclusive competence.
in writing. the recommendation under consideration, drawn up by mr vital moreira, concerns the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries. the aim of this regulation is to reduce the legal uncertainty that exists with regard to the protection of investments made outside the eu, since the lisbon treaty (tl) did not provide for any protection. there are currently around 1,400 bilateral agreements in force which will be replaced by eu agreements giving greater transparency to these instruments and a high level of protection to eu investors. the proposal for a regulation is the result of a satisfactory agreement between the ep and the council, which took account of the ep's objectives, sets out the conditions under which new agreements can be negotiated and provides for their review within 10 years.
in writing. − trade policy is another area where the member states have been stripped of their powers and the eu has become exclusively competent in this area, with the known consequences for portugal. this is the basis of this proposal for a regulation, namely the application of article 207 (1) tfeu, which provides for the exclusive competence of the eu in the field of foreign direct investment in the framework of the common commercial policy. it is clear that the specific interests and constraints of certain countries have been ignored or even dealt with by the eu in the exercise of this competence. the damage caused by trade and investment policies which take account not of the particularities of the portuguese economy and its complementarities but of the interests of the major economic groups (in particular industry and services) of the major eu powers is therefore evident in the case of portugal. this evidence is the basis for our vote on this report - which approves a regulation which seeks to give the commission the power to withdraw authorizations, to ask member states to negotiate or to denounce bilateral investment treaties and to approve new ones. we voted against it, of course.
in writing. - this report on transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries was adopted by a large majority in the committee on international trade. i voted in favour of the agreement because i consider it to be a positive overall approach.
in writing. − articles 206 and 207 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union place foreign direct investment (fdi) under the exclusive competence of the eu, including the ability to conclude fdi agreements covering market access conditions and rules on investment treatment and protection in the pre- and post-establishment periods. the fact that fdi was previously the sole responsibility of the member states makes it necessary to create a regulation establishing a transitional period between the new and the old system. the regulation proposed by the european commission lays down the conditions for this transition, while ensuring the protection of investments already made in the eu and setting criteria for negotiations initiated by member states that are still ongoing. the regulation thus aims to ensure legislative coherence during the transition to the new system over which the eu has exclusive competence. although the eu now has exclusive competence in relation to fdi, member states remain responsible for the promotion activity for fdi. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the report which proposes the application of the regulation confirming the new powers of the european commission in relation to fdi.
in writing. − trade policy is another area where member states have been removed from competence and the eu has become exclusively competent in this area. this is the basis of this proposal for a regulation, namely the application of article 207 (1) tfeu, which provides for the exclusive competence of the eu in the field of foreign direct investment, within the framework of the common commercial policy. it is clear that the specific interests and constraints of certain countries have been ignored or even ignored in the exercise of this competence by the eu. the damage caused by trade and investment policies which take account not of the particularities of the portuguese economy and its complementarities but of the interests of the major economic groups (in particular industry and services) of the major eu powers is therefore evident in the case of portugal. this evidence is the basis for our vote on this report approving a regulation which seeks to give the commission the power to withdraw authorizations, to ask member states to negotiate or to denounce bilateral investment treaties and to approve new ones. it is an interference in the commercial policy of the member states with which we are deeply disagree ing.
in writing. - i approve this report because, in line with the european union's commitments at the 2008 donors' conference, we must financially assist the state of georgia so that this country can overcome the adverse effects of the global crisis. i think it is positive that this assistance is intended to support georgia's economic reform agenda and help reduce its financial vulnerability in the short term. more importantly, it has been stipulated that in order to provide financial assistance to georgia, the country and its authorities must postpone the structural reforms to be carried out.
in writing. − the impasse over the approval of macrofinancial assistance to georgia is similar to that for the kyrgyz republic and concerns the differences between the european parliament and the council over the comitology rules to be applied to the agreement. parliament advocates the use of the consultative procedure, while the council advocates the application of the examination procedure, which gives it greater scope for using comitology. in line with this, and for the same set of reasons as those i put forward in my explanation of vote on macro-financial assistance to the kyrgyz republic (see explanation of vote report a7-0208/2012), i voted in favour of this report and reaffirmed the importance of turning words into action with regard to the effective implementation of the lisbon treaty. it is difficult to understand why, three years after its entry into force, we are still faced with resistance to the new division of powers between the european parliament, the council and the commission.

in writing. - georgia has not escaped the present financial crisis unscathed, with trade and budgetary weaknesses. the european union has not renounced its role as the world's largest donor and has sought to reach out to that country. however, there is no interinstitutional agreement on the way in which this aid should be adopted, and it has therefore become necessary to adopt an interim solution which, by not binding the institutions for the future, makes it possible to make the aid promised feasible. i hope that the aid will be made available soon, that georgia can regain the stability that has been affected in the meantime and that the european institutions can come to an understanding on a permanent basis so as to avoid situations like the one we are facing.

in writing. - this regulation approves, at second reading, the mobilisation of eur 46 million of macro-financial assistance for georgia, covering the second part of the assistance promised in 2008, following the armed conflict with russia and as a consequence of the global crisis. this eu macro-financial assistance is intended to contribute to meeting georgia's external financing needs identified in cooperation with the imf in the context of the imf stand-by arrangement of usd 1,17 billion in force since october 2008. this assistance will be provided half in the form of grants and half in the form of loans and should contribute to helping georgia cope with the economic consequences of the conflict with russia and the global crisis and support the economic reform programme of the government of georgia. the principle of cooperation and genuine development aid, which must be developed further, in respect for the sovereign will and choices of each state, is not in question. however, this type of assistance is typically accompanied by demands for 'structural and macroeconomic reforms', which we reject.
in writing. − relations between georgia and the european union are developing within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy. the macro-financial assistance is considered an appropriate response to the request of georgia, given the current exceptional circumstances and with a view to supporting economic stabilisation in conjunction with the imf programme. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council's position at first reading and with a view to adopting the decision of the european parliament and the council granting additional macrofinancial assistance to georgia.

in writing. - i support this report because the debate on the creation of a unitary patent is as old as the internal market. in times of economic and social crisis, i declare my support for the european resources initiative, which i consider to be the greatest opportunity to harness innovation in europe in intellectual property since the creation of the european union patent. i also believe that the creation of the unitary patent puts an end to a long decade of fruitless negotiations. in my view, patent unity should be ensured in the member states based on a single application which could reduce applicant costs by 70%. furthermore, i argue that patent holders should pay a renewable annual fee so that the patent unit is successful.

in writing. − patent granting in europe is governed by the european patent convention an intergovernmental agreement between the 38 european states, including all 27 member states but not the eu itself. today, a 'european patent' application is nothing more than a set of national patents to be validated in each state where the applicant wishes protection. once the patent has been obtained, it shall be translated into the official language of each member state. and in the event of a dispute, it has to be heard in the various national courts. the cost of validating a patent currently ranges from eur 22 000 to eur 26 000 for eu-wide coverage, with an estimated eur 205 to 230 million spent by eu companies on patent costs. we are faced with a system that is too complex, too costly and where costly litigation in various jurisdictions can even result in conflicting decisions. the creation of a european patent system is now more than a necessity, it is an evidence for creating more favourable conditions for investment in r & d, boosting innovation and creating jobs. i therefore vote in favour of this report.

in writing. the report under review, by bernhard rapkay, deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament (ep) and of the council implementing enhanced cooperation in the field of the creation of unitary patent protection. because of the cost of patent recognition, many smes did not proceed with their recognition as their costs were about 20 times higher than those of the united states of america and 11 times those of japan. smes had to register in all the member states where they wanted to operate and spent €4,000 on translations alone. this is a regulation vital to the future competitiveness of the european union and which will catalyse economic growth and job creation. smes will be able to compete with their products throughout the eu without the need for recognition in each member state. i regret that it has been necessary to resort to enhanced cooperation, but the urgency of the matter requires it, and i hope that it will be implemented as soon as possible, as it will have a very positive impact on business and investment.
in writing. the aim of this regulation is to create a mechanism for the 'automatic' licensing of a patent throughout the european area, thus going beyond the current obligation to translate/register in each country. we recognize the need for the procedural requirements for registering a patent to be within the reach of a micro, small or medium-sized enterprise, a small university or even an individual inventor. but as we said during the debate in the plenary, we have a number of concerns about this specific proposal for the creation of a european unitary patent. firstly, a wider and necessarily longer public debate was required, which did not take place, leaving the impression that the whole process is being driven by the big industrial interests of a few more industrialized countries, leaving the public interest behind once again. the proposal to set up a unified patent court and the consequent loss of sovereignty and national capacity to intervene in this area are clearly dangerous. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment.

in writing. − this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing enhanced cooperation in the field of the creation of unitary patent protection aims to make it possible to grant a european patent with unitary effect in respect of all or part of the territories of the participating member states. i am in favour of this proposal and therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − there are currently two ways of registering a patent: through the national institute of industrial property (or the equivalent institute in another member state) or through the european patent office (epo), based in munich, federal republic of germany. however, the registration in the epo has to be validated separately in all the member states in which protection is sought, implying that the registration has to be translated into the respective official languages of the member states in which patent protection is sought. given the existence of translation requirements, the cost of registering patents in the eu is extremely high, complex and, in the event of a dispute, can lead to conflicting decisions, depending on the member state where the dispute is initiated. this prevents the existence of a 'true european patent', which may discourage potential investors. i therefore share the rapporteur's view that a patent should be created which would enjoy the same benefits in a unitary manner in all the member states which have decided to adopt the 'single patent', and the person who submits the patent will be able to choose whether or not it will be protected in all the member states. however, i voted against the report because of the linguistic solution adopted for the single patent.

in writing. − there is widespread recognition of the competitive disadvantage faced by european companies due to the absence of european patent protection with unitary effect, which the union has so far been unable to create. this proposal, which establishes the enhanced cooperation procedure, builds on the existing european patent system and provides for the conferral of unitary effect to european patents granted in the territories of the participating member states. unitary patent protection will be optional and should coexist with national and european patents. i have no doubt that the present system needs to be simplified and that administrative burdens and costs, especially with regard to translation requirements, need to be reduced. to do this, it would be advisable to adopt only one language, english. i am totally opposed to the solution which has been found, which establishes an unacceptable distinction between the european languages, with the choice of english, german and french over the others. i also express my concern about the model chosen, which raises doubts as to legal certainty by denying the possibility of appeal to the court of justice.
