in writing. − in october 2011, the european commission sent a proposal to the european parliament to incorporate the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas into eu law. the proposal constitutes the legal instrument necessary to implement such measures and to provide a legal framework for operators on the banana market. the central america agreement includes a bilateral safeguard clause providing for the possibility of reinstating the most-favoured-nation tariff rate in cases where imports are made in such increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause, or threaten to cause, serious injury to eu producers producing like or directly competing products. this agreement is therefore necessary to maintain the protection of the rights of eu banana producers.
in writing. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas of the agreement establishing an association between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and central america, of the other part. the document in question contains a safeguard clause designed to protect european producers against unfair competition. it must be an effective safeguard clause which requires respect for human rights, social rights such as compliance with ilo recommendations, environmental rights, etc. we must, however, pay particular attention to the eu's outermost banana-producing regions so that they do not see their jobs threatened, and i hope that the safeguard clauses will be a guarantee for european trade.
in writing. the compromise from the committee on international trade introduces amendments to try to offset the 'deeply negative' consequences that this free trade agreement will have for the six central american countries that signed it and for the eu countries. this agreement liberalises trade in certain agricultural products in whole or in part. the banana is the main agricultural product in all these countries' exports, with the us multinationals being the main producers, in vast areas of monoculture where the working conditions of local peasants approach slavery. for these reasons, numerous organizations have denounced the social, labour and environmental dumping resulting from this agreement, and more generally from free trade and the subjection of agriculture to the rules of the world trade organization. the safeguard clause and the stability mechanism proposed here will be of little use. the stabilisation mechanism will not be automatic, since the european commission will be free to apply it or not. parliament here acknowledges its inability (and we add: unwillingness) to oppose the commission, despite all the propaganda that has been made about its increased role in trade policy.
in writing. − being constantly aware of the negative effects that this type of trade agreement, in this particular case between the eu and the countries of central america, may have on european agriculture, i voted in favour of this report on the implementation of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas in the eu-central america trade agreement, as i consider them useful instruments to mitigate the potential disruptive effects on the eu market resulting from these types of agreements. the more general bilateral safeguard clause provides for the possibility of reimbursing the most-favoured-nation duty rate in cases where imports resulting from these agreements are so increased in quantities that they threaten to cause serious injury to eu producers; the stabilisation mechanism for bananas applies until 1 january 2020 and is activated when, in a given calendar year, the trigger volume (determined specific volume of imports) is reached, giving the eu the right to suspend preferential imports until the end of the year, albeit only for a period of 3 months.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a regulation today aimed at implementing the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas under the association agreement between the european union and central america. in this context, the production and economy of the outermost regions should not be adversely affected by increased imports of bananas from third countries. the document aims to establish appropriate safeguard instruments to prevent significant damage to the union's banana crops, a sector with a significant weight in the agricultural production of many outermost regions, in accordance with article 349 tfeu. those safeguard measures should be established as soon as the product concerned, imported into the union, causes or threatens to cause injury to producers in the outermost regions of the union producing like or directly competing products. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − the european commission has achieved the objectives of eliminating high customs duties, tackling technical barriers to trade, liberalising services markets, protecting valuable eu geographical indications (gis), opening public procurement markets, including commitments to effectively enforce labour and environmental standards, and providing effective and rapid dispute resolution procedures, thereby ensuring a level playing field with competitors in the region, such as the united states. for all these reasons, and in congratulating the rapporteur, my colleague mario david, i voted in favour of this report. i am particularly attentive to agreements of this kind because of the real risk of serious damage to certain portuguese productive sectors, in particular agriculture.
in writing. the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and colombia and peru, on the other, is part of a longstanding relationship between the union and the andean community. the scope and ambition of the agreement are in line with eu policy on free trade agreements. the agreement eliminates virtually all customs duties after a transitional period and extends commitments on services far beyond the general agreement on trade and services (gats). it also includes provisions on non-customs barriers, such as technical barriers to trade and sanitary and phytosanitary measures. the agreement strengthens the protection of intellectual property rights while reflecting the needs of colombia and peru and includes institutional provisions such as dispute resolution, monitoring committees and a mechanism for the rapid examination of regulatory and non-customs barriers. it also contains an enforcement clause on human rights and a title on sustainable development, which comprises the core labour standards of the international labour organisation (ilo) and multilateral environmental agreements. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − i approve this report, expressing my personal concern that microbial resistance is a vital challenge to public health in general, which is in turn aggravated by the decline in the development of new antimicrobials. with this in mind, i am in favour of concerted and assertive action, including legislative measures, to prevent the spread of microbial infections and to increase our resistance as humans to these elements. it is essential to stress that prudent use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine is extremely important to maintain the availability and efficacy of antimicrobials.
in writing. − since the discovery of penicillin, antimicrobials have been revolutionizing medical and veterinary practice, leading to significant reductions in mortality rates, while paving the way for the widespread use of innovative invasive surgeries. however, medical progress in the age of antibiotics is in danger of being jeopardized by the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance (amr). ram does not have a single, simple solution; a multifaceted approach is needed. the following are essential: - prudent use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine; - the need for effective measures to prevent the emergence and spread of drug resistance; - the development of new antimicrobials or alternative treatments; - the need for an exchange of best practice and better communication, education and training of therapists in the human and veterinary health sectors; - an international approach to this issue, as infectious diseases know no borders; - the need for accurate and timely data, which makes the existence of surveillance systems at european level necessary. for these reasons i have supported this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it imperative to: ensure the prudent use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine; take more effective measures to prevent the emergence and spread of drug resistance; encourage the development of new antimicrobial agents; create a european surveillance system; encourage the exchange of best practice and ensure better communication, education and training of therapists in human and veterinary health; address this issue at international level.
in writing. − over the past 80 years of widespread use, antimicrobial medicines have played an essential role in the treatment of many microbial infections in humans and animals. however, this situation is being seriously compromised by the emergence and spread at an astonishing rate of microbes resistant to these drugs, rendering them ineffective in the treatment of these infections. for example, in some countries, resistance rates for certain bacteria are already over 25 percent. although the development of drug resistance is a natural and unavoidable consequence of treatment, it is being seriously aggravated, not only because there is a considerable decline in the development of new antimicrobials, but also because of their excessive and indiscriminate use in human and veterinary medicine, coupled with poor hygiene and insufficient infection control. efforts are urgently needed to curb this growth by controlling the use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine and by seeking to maintain the efficacy of existing antimicrobials through their responsible use and at the correct therapeutic level, only when prescribed and strictly necessary, for a specified period of time. i therefore support this concerted and multifaceted approach which should ensure prudent use, promote prevention, focus on research and development and encourage cooperation and information.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'the microbial challenge - the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance', because, given that infectious diseases know no borders, concerted and transversal measures are needed to ensure, in particular, the prudent use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine, the prevention of the emergence and spread of drug resistance, and the development of new antimicrobials or alternative treatments.
in writing. − antimicrobial resistance refers to the inability of certain antimicrobial agents (antibiotics, for example) to act effectively on organisms (bacteria, viruses and other micro-organisms) that were previously sensitive to them, because they have developed resistance. antimicrobial resistance has become a public health threat in europe (and the rest of the world) as it results in longer and more complicated treatments and the risk of failure to respond with potentially fatal consequences (e.g. 25,000 people die in the eu every year from infections caused by resistant micro-organisms). this means that there is an urgent need for global action to prescribe and use antimicrobials more prudently, ensuring that these treatments are only followed when they are actually needed, and for the pharmaceutical industry to research and develop new antimicrobials as a way of treating patients infected with resistant micro-organisms.
in writing. − the report points to the ineffectiveness of the council's objectives on the prudent use of antimicrobial agents in human medicine. the aim is to commit member states to implementing recommendations that go beyond the commission's five-year strategic action plan. in particular, there is a need for better and more effective coordination between the human health sector and the veterinary sector. this is a pertinent question which needs to be studied and further developed, as the report also states. the consequences of the prophylactic use of antibiotics in livestock should be better understood by investigating their relationship to the emergence of resistance in humans. a comprehensive response from health systems to the problem of antimicrobial resistance is required, including a range of preventive practices, both at the primary healthcare and hospital levels. this will only be possible in the context of public health services. there is also a need to strengthen public r & d in this area. the report is generally positive in its many recommendations and warnings, but this is one of the weak points of the report, which prefers to focus on the development of public-private partnerships.
in writing. - unfortunately, an amendment has been introduced to article 28 which seeks to classify 'medicinal foods' for animal use as 'pharmaceuticals', with the express purpose of monitoring them, via pharmaceutical legislation and their official inspections, and ensuring that their use falls within the 'prescription only' category. these medicated feeds are based on medicated premixtures, which are subject to authorisation by the veterinary regulatory authorities and which are classified and approved as veterinary pharmaceutical products (article 2 of directive 2011/82/eu, as amended by directive 2004/28/ec). all veterinary pharmaceutical products, including medicated premixtures for medicated feedingstuffs, are included in the category 'presciption only' and require a veterinary prescription for their administration to animals. medicated feed is only a channel for the administration of veterinary medicinal products, like drinking water. thus, amendment 82 (to article 28) in seeking to classify the medicinal food as a pharmaceutical product has relevant implications which may be incompatible with various legal instruments, considering that all constituents of the medicinal food, namely cereals (corn, wheat, barley, soybeans, etc.) may be included in the parameters and requirements necessary for pharmaceutical products, which is obviously unenforceable. that is why i voted against this amendment.
in writing. - according to data provided by the european commission, 25,000 people die every year due to the growing resistance of microbes to antimicrobial treatments. in addition to the number of lives lost, there is an additional cost of 1.5 billion euros. the growing resistance to antimicrobial treatments is due to the use of antimicrobials in cases where the disease is not clearly identifiable and to the fact that treatment is stopped prematurely. these situations occur, according to the european commission, in medicine and veterinary medicine. there is therefore a need to prohibit the online sale of antimicrobials, to separate the right to prescribe from the right to sell in the case of veterinary medicine and to improve access to information on their correct use. the report by anna rosbach, mep, contains important measures that must be implemented as soon as possible to prevent and combat the threat of growing antimicrobial resistance to public health. in view of the foregoing, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the report points to the ineffectiveness of the council's objectives on the prudent use of antimicrobial agents in human medicine. the aim is to commit member states to implementing recommendations, calling in particular for better and more effective coordination between the human and veterinary health sectors. the consequences of the prophylactic use of antibiotics in livestock should be better understood by investigating their relationship to the emergence of resistance in humans. a comprehensive response from health systems to the problem of antimicrobial resistance is required, including a range of preventive practices, both at the primary healthcare and hospital levels. this will only be possible in the context of public management of health services and not in the development of public-private partnerships, as the report argues.

for the gue/ngl group what we have here is an agreement that can finally put into practice and move forward with the taxation of the financial sector. i must say that i think the vote on this proposal is 30 years late, but better late than never. we voted here in may on the political proposal and i hope that tomorrow we can vote in favour of 11 countries starting to implement this measure. this tax is of the most elementary justice: finance capital has to pay. we are not talking about an overpayment, as has been demanded of european citizens, but about a residual payment. we are not even talking about a payment that is paid, for example, in everyday transactions. imagine: a family in portugal, who wants to do christmas shopping for their dinner, if they go to buy olive oil, cod, other things, will pay for every 100 euros invested, at least 6 euros in tax. a speculator in the financial markets, if he invests that same 100 euros, will pay, with this tax, about 10 cents or even 1 cent. so we are talking about at least 60 times less than what any ordinary citizen pays for basic necessities. that's why i think it's so important to ask the question: how is it that after we all know the impact of the crisis, there are still 16 countries that think that taxing the financial sector at 0.1 or 0.01% is an abuse? how can you ask so many sacrifices from people who have almost nothing and still think you can't touch the financial markets? we know very well that this rate does not solve the problem of speculation, we know that there are many securities which remain out of the transaction, but we also know that this rate can generate extra resources and that these resources should be used to reach the most disadvantaged sectors of the european population. that is the challenge which is also left to the countries which are going to put forward this proposal which we are seeking to adopt here tomorrow.

the european council's agenda includes the deepening of emu. the proposal put forward by the european commission to this end includes, among other things, the single banking supervisory mechanism and the creation of the new 'convergence and competitiveness instrument' to provide financial support for the implementation of the 'structural reforms' contracted between the eu and the member states. as far as banking supervision is concerned, it is accepted that a supranational body can terminate national banking institutions. in other words, we will have processes of merger/concentration of financial capital which are directly determined and organized by supranational institutions controlled, as we know, by this same financial capital. it is another giant step in the assault on the sovereignty of states and the intolerable subjugation of political power to economic and financial power. the new financial instrument (for convergence and competitiveness) will probably open the door for cohesion funds, which are now cutting into the budget, to be used to finance redundancies/measures to make labour market more flexible, liberalization of new sectors, so-called 'structural reforms' or perhaps to cover the costs of debt servicing. the commission's proposal is to be seen as a step in the right direction, and it is not a step in the right direction.
over the last few years, a number of measures have been taken to deepen european integration, such as the creation of the euro, the strengthening of the internal market and new solidarity mechanisms. however, i believe that the process of european integration must be deepened, and that it must be accompanied by an increasing economic, banking and financial union. i hope that the council meeting will finally move forward with the proposal for a banking union with the european central bank to supervise all banking institutions, regardless of their geographical location or relevance to the economy. europe must strengthen its internal project and promote greater integration at political and economic level, investing increasingly in the development of the regions and in improving the quality of life of the people.

in writing. - we all know that a budget always contains a forecast of revenue and expenditure which is subject to change during its implementation. however, it is essential to be vigilant as revenue develops so that commitments are not made on the expenditure side which cannot be covered by revenue. when we approved the 2012 budget, we already knew that the payment appropriations were not enough. without the adoption of this amending budget, commitments already entered into and expenditure already invoiced, amounting to eur 9 billion, would not be paid. this included some of the eu's most successful policies, such as the erasmus programmes, lifelong learning, and research programmes. i welcome the fact that it has been possible to reach an agreement between the institutions to avoid a large part of the financial responsibilities being left unaddressed, which would be a blow to the eu's credibility. but i regret that the payment of eur 2.9 billion under cohesion policy has been delayed.

in writing. - saab was, until recently, a solid brand in the european automotive scene, a company which employed many workers and was a factor of development and stability in the regions in which it operated. unfortunately, this situation was reversed and the company experienced serious difficulties which resulted in its declaration of insolvency. recent news reports suggest a potential recovery of the company and the brand, possibly through the production of electric cars, but even if this happens, the number of employees will remain very small compared to previous periods. the trollhattan region has been particularly hard hit by unemployment. i would like saab to be able to reinvent itself and contribute again to the progress of sweden and, above all, to support the workers who have lost their jobs in the short term and to ensure that the fund's aid contributes to a stable return to the labour market.

in writing. - this proposal to mobilise the egf concerns redundancies in saab automobile sa, one of its subsidiaries and 16 of its suppliers. we are facing the dismissal of 3,748 workers and the mobilisation of the sum of 5,454,560 euros, a dismissal which has generated a 20% increase in unemployment in the trollhattan region. as usual, the justification for further attacks on labour rights lies in so-called 'significant structural changes in world trade patterns' - world trade patterns that the eu influences with its policies of deregulation and liberalisation of international trade. the number of units produced in the eu decreased significantly. when wages are lowered, when unemployment is promoted on a large scale, when precarious employment is promoted, when public services are destroyed, this is the result: the internal market shrinks as a result of a feeling of insecurity about the future. in the famous words of an american trade unionist, "machines don't buy cars yet". more than these funds, what workers need is the implementation of investment policies that create and maintain jobs with rights.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be given to sweden which has requested assistance for a total of 3,748 eligible redundancies, 1,350 of which are potential beneficiaries of assistance for workers in saab automobile sa, one of its subsidiaries, saab automobile powertrain ab, and 16 of its suppliers in sweden.
in writing. − under the european globalisation adjustment fund, the european commission adopted on 19 october 2012 a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of sweden to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. this is the 14th application to be examined under the 2012 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 5 454 560 from the egf in favour of the 3 748 workers made redundant, 1 350 of whom are potential beneficiaries of assistance, including 3 239 redundancies at saab automobile ab and its subsidiary saab automobile powertrain ab during the four-month reference period from 19 december 2011 to 19 april 2012, and a further 509 redundancies at 16 subcontractors before the reference period but related to the same collective redundancy process. the swedish authorities confirmed that all these redundancies had taken place. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − regulation no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. sweden has submitted an application to mobilise the egf in respect of 3 748 eligible redundancies, of which 1 350 are potential beneficiaries of workers' compensation benefits for saab automobile sa, one of its subsidiaries, namely saab automobile powertrain ab, and 16 of its suppliers. i agree to the mobilisation of eur 5.454.560,00 to support the reintegration of workers into the labour market, in particular vocational training measures aimed at creating high value-added jobs, thus avoiding the off-shoring of knowledge acquired in this industrial sector. it should also be noted that the egf should not replace the legal and financial responsibilities of swedish companies, as it is complementary support provided by the european union to alleviate the social difficulties that workers will face.
in writing. - we are looking at the mobilisation of the egf for redundancies in saab automobile sa, one of its subsidiaries and 16 of its suppliers. we are faced with the dismissal of 3,748 workers, the mobilisation of the sum of 5,454,560 euros, a dismissal which has generated a 20% increase in unemployment in the trollhattan region. as usual, the justification for this further attack on the right to work lies, on the one hand, in the major structural changes in world trade patterns and, on the other, in the decline of the units produced in the european union, which passes to 26% of world production in 2011, compared to 34.1% in 2005. when wages are lowered, large-scale unemployment is promoted, precarious employment is promoted, public services are destroyed, this is the result: the internal market shrinks as a result of a feeling of insecurity about the future. these funds 'legitimize' the policy of redundancies and support employers in this decision. what workers need is investment policies that create and maintain jobs with rights. only a break with the policies currently being pursued by the eu will be able to stop this path of social and economic disaster.
in writing. − i approve this report, which gives the green light to this application concerning 1,106 redundancies, 500 of which are potential recipients of assistance, in 423 enterprises operating in the manufacture of processed metal products, except machinery and equipment in the basque country region in 2011. in my view, the metal products sector is a key supplier to a wide range of manufacturing industries, in particular shipbuilding, construction and the automotive sector. all these sectors have suffered a significant impact across the european union caused by the economic crisis, as previously acknowledged by the commission. to make matters worse, spain is among the member states most severely affected by the global economic and financial crisis. the manufacturing industry, on the other hand, is among the most affected sectors, with the situation deteriorating. the gloomy outlook for the industry as a result of the global economic and financial crisis has led to a reduced demand for and therefore lower production of metal and metal products, which has led to more redundancies since 2011, which leads us to consider the need for this support.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are facing a serious financial, economic and social crisis, with rising unemployment as one of the main consequences, the eu should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly in terms of support for people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report concerning the mobilisation of eur 1 299 545 from the egf for spain to support the 500 potential beneficiaries of the 1 106 redundancies in 423 enterprises ('manufacture of metal products other than machinery and equipment') in the basque country in spain.

in writing. - the production of metal products is intended for many manufacturing industries which, due to globalisation and the economic and financial crisis, have been particularly affected. this has meant less demand and less capacity to maintain production and labour levels, and reduced the number of workers in their service. in spain, the production of the sector fell by 24,6% and the production of metal products by 23,3% in 2009 when compared to the previous year. in the basque country, 1,106 redundancies in 423 companies gave rise to the application for the fund which we are now examining. the province of biscay was the most affected by redundancies in this sector, accounting for 57% of the total number of redundancies. i support their mobilization, as i have done in other cases, and i am concerned about the spread of these applications in the various countries which indicate the generalization of the crisis, and i hope that the european union and the member states will have the ingenuity and the art and the appropriate institutional architecture to reverse this worrying situation, which has no obvious end in sight for the time being.

in writing. - i approve of this report because i question the methodology used, particularly as regards the type of questions asked, some of which are sensitive, which raises doubts about the added value created and the sincerity of the answers. for example, questions about the interviewee's possible drug problems, possible gun possession, and fear of terrorism could give rise to misinterpretations. without wishing to start a debate on statistical methods in general, it is up to the commission to propose a fully coherent and clear instrument which does not reveal methodological problems and inconsistencies. victimization surveys are a 'subjective' type of survey that assess a person's level of victimization and their feelings about crime. as such, questions should be formulated in a clear and precise manner, with the aim of ensuring that the answers are as informative as possible and that their analysis can be used to develop policy in the future. the answers should leave as little room for divergent interpretations as possible, since the 'statistical fear of crime' can be quickly misinterpreted.

in writing. − ground handling services cover all ground activities (at airports) related to aviation. the revenue generated amounts to some eur 50 billion and employs more than 60,000 people in europe. the efficient provision of these services is essential for airports, air carriers, passengers and also for the optimal use of air transport infrastructure and for the performance of the aviation system in general. in view of the successive crises affecting air transport, the rapid growth of air traffic, the increase in the number of air carriers and the increasing capacity constraints at airports, it became necessary to replace the 1996 directive, which at the time constituted a first step towards the progressive opening and harmonisation of access to the groundhandling market. i believe it is essential that ambitious measures can be taken which can bring about real improvements in the current system, which is why i support the motion to refer the report back to the commission, allowing negotiations to resume which can help to reach more acceptable commitments during the first half of 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on groundhandling services at airports in the union, as i considered that the rules proposed by the european commission for the liberalisation of handling services would have very negative social costs and are therefore unacceptable.
in writing. − the ground handling services are crucial for the smooth operation of airports. there are eleven categories of ground handling services: (1) ground administration and supervision, (2) passenger handling, (3) baggage handling, (4) cargo and mail handling, (5) runway operations, (6) aircraft cleaning and servicing, (7) fuel and oil handling, (8) in-line maintenance, (9) air operations and crew management, (10) ground transportation and (11) catering. the provision of these services represents a revenue of eur 50 billion and employs 60,000 people in europe. i am not a strong advocate of protectionist policies and tend to support the liberalisation of markets, since i believe that competition is generally synonymous with a higher quality of service and a higher level of satisfaction for the end-customer, in this case the passenger. in this sense, i am in favour of the commission's proposal to liberalize this market.
in writing. the report which has reached the plenary, following the vote in the committee on transport and tourism, rejects the european commission's position. this position points to an increase in the number of providers of assistance services at eu airports, changing the existing reference threshold in directive 96/67/ec, i.e. deepening the liberalisation that this directive has established. although the european commission has numerous studies and evaluation reports showing the damage caused by liberalisation for workers and passengers, taking into account the reduction in wages and benefits, the increase in job insecurity, the degradation of the quality of services and the training and specialisation of workers, with consequent increased risks in terms of safety and although only airlines have benefited from the reduction in costs, the commission shows once again that interests are served. we welcome the rejection of the commission's proposal, but we cannot help but point out the hypocrisy of the social democrats. the commission's proposal is not a new one, but it is a new one, and it is not a new one. they also show, after all, what interests they serve.
in writing. - in recent decades, with the rise in the average standard of living of citizens, the reduction in air travel costs and the emergence of low-cost airlines, we have seen an exponential increase in the number of passengers in transit through airports and the recovery of many runways, some abandoned since the second world war, for the secondary market. artur zasada reports on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on groundhandling services at airports in the european union (eu) and repealing council directive 96/67/ec. in a globalised world where life is a constant rush - so many requests we don't want to miss - delays at airports, whether in check-in, in the departure of the plane or in the disruption that the loss of a piece of luggage always causes, call into question the quality of services that are required.

in writing. - after the rejection of this report by the committee responsible, tran, by only two votes, i think that the motion to refer the matter back to the committee is the best way of finding the necessary consensus for the correct application of this directive. i also think that the complete rejection of a proposal from the european commission which substantially updates existing legislation is unjustifiable, since most member states have already incorporated this same liberalisation. the 1996 directive already allowed the liberalisation of groundhandling services at airports. the difference in this report is that the minimum number of service providers is increased from 2 to 3. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams in 2004 was signed on the same day as the agreement between ryanair and ams in 2005. the controversy surrounding this report requires that it be referred back to the committee responsible in order to reach a broad consensus on this important aspect of the airport sector.
in writing. the report which has reached the plenary, following the vote in the committee on transport and tourism, rejects the european commission's position. this position points to an increase in the number of providers of assistance services at eu airports, amending the existing reference threshold in directive 96/67/ec, with the aim that member states may 'limit the number of providers to no less than two per category', further opening the sector to the market and leading to further liberalisation. the arguments behind this move refer to an alleged inefficient assessment of the provision of groundhandling services. what is not said is that these measures will further aggravate a scenario of constant social dumping used to blackmail and pressure workers through dismissals, the admission of new workers with lower wages, wages below inflation, more insecure jobs, more temporary work, degradation of the level of skills and training of staff, and with the consequent degradation of the quality of the services provided. the workers in this sector have been fighting against these measures with great vigour.
in writing. - i approve of this report which maintains that the series of slots to be retained by airlines would be 80% of the currently used slots, and i am in favour of a position against the commission proposal which redefines the length of the series of slots to 85%, although i support the commission proposal which allows for the secondary exchange of slots with or without monetary compensation, which i believe is beneficial because it will allow member states to allocate part of the revenues generated from the slots to finance the optimisation of airport infrastructure and services. i also support the intention to introduce the principle of applying sanctions to airlines which do not respect the schedules allocated to them. in my view, these measures will increase the rates of use of the time slots, one of the main objectives of this regulation, without harming the industry associated with the procedures for establishing the allocation of time slots.
in writing. − under the legislation in force, slots are allocated to carriers on the basis of an administrative system established by council regulation (eec) no 95/93 of 18 january 1993 on common rules for the allocation of slots at community airports, as amended by regulation (ec) no 793/2004. this allocation system has proved to be inefficient and does not ensure full use of airport capacity. one of the great challenges facing europe is the overcrowding of airports. according to eurocontrol's long-term forecasts published in december 2010, at least 10% of air transport demand in 2030 will not be met due to lack of capacity, even taking into account the infrastructure reinforcement currently planned. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it imperative to increase efficiency in the use of existing airport capacity by revising the timetable regulation and improving it so as to reconcile capacity with air transport demand in all segments (long haul, regional links, cargo transport, etc.).
in writing. - the demand for slots by airlines currently exceeds the capacity available at airports. depending on the characteristics of the airport, slot allocation may be necessary at certain times or during periods of heavy traffic. it should also be done in such a way as to ensure that access to congested airports is organised according to fair, non-discriminatory and transparent rules, allowing for the optimum use of airport capacity and the existence of fair conditions of competition. the current regulation is based on the iata global guidelines and has contributed to a considerable improvement in the allocation of slots at congested european airports and to the creation of the internal aviation market. however, the enormous growth in air traffic, with the number of intra-eu connections doubling and the number of long-haul flights from europe increasing by 150% over the last decade, has made it essential to amend this regulation, which is proving to be inefficient at the moment. i therefore support the proposed amendments which i hope will help to make this regulation an effective instrument for managing limited capacity, safeguarding the necessary guarantees for its effective application, ensuring the necessary transparency and allowing greater band mobility, in particular through secondary band trading.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the allocation of slots at airports in the european union, as it includes measures to ensure that airport capacity is used as efficiently as possible, while ensuring that the connection of european regions, including the outermost regions and islands, to the major central airports in europe and to the world air traffic network is not affected.
in writing. − the current system of slot allocation at eu airports has proved inefficient and does not ensure full use of airport capacity. according to eurocontrol and aci europe, one of the major challenges facing europe is the saturation of airports, pointing to long-term forecasts. at least 10% of air transport demand in 2030 will be unmet due to lack of capacity. it is therefore necessary to review the time-series regulation to determine to what extent it can be improved to match capacity with air transport demand, thus increasing airport capacity without ever compromising air transport and passenger safety.
in writing. - we all agree on the role transport plays in our lives by enabling fast and efficient connections. with the advent of low-cost air travel, many airports became congested and in many cases flights had to be moved to secondary airports. the commission has also proposed that the aid be granted to the airport operator in the form of a reduction in the number of passengers and a reduction in the number of aircraft. the way to solve this problem and increase airport capacity is to use so-called secondary lanes along with greater use of alternative transport such as high-speed rail. however, when allocating new slots, the exchanges need to be transparent and properly regulated so that companies do not use those slots for long-haul flights to the detriment of domestic flights.
in writing. − the overall objective of the report is to ensure optimum allocation and use of slots at congested eu airports by proposing to strengthen slot allocation and use mechanisms and ensuring their effective application. the amendments proposed in the report will allow airlines to sell slots they do not use and member states to introduce fines for carriers who return unused slots late, preventing new allocation. the report advocates the promotion of competition between operators, advocating access to secondary timetable trading and the integration of the timetable allocation system into the reform of the european air traffic management system the single european sky. the exhaustive rambling of the rosary of arguments in favour of sacrosanct free competition thus comes, as one might expect, into line with the design of the 'one sky'. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this. it is also suggested that a 'single european coordinator' associated with the time slot allocation process should be set up after the completion of the so-called 'single european sky'. we voted against it.
in writing. − improving airport efficiency is essential for further optimisation of eu airports where the time band regulation applies. in view of the various interests involved in this process, the amendments proposed are therefore intended to ensure greater independence and impartiality in the role of the coordinators, also thanks to a more balanced presence of the interested parties within the coordination committee. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, the overall objective of which is to ensure the optimal allocation and use of slots at congested airports in the european union. the majority of the amendments tabled by the european parliament to the proposal submitted by the european commission seek to strengthen the content of certain provisions in terms of effectiveness and clarity of presentation. the new elements presented relate specifically to the independence of coordinators, which will bring greater transparency, and to the secondary trading of time slots, which can be decisive in presenting better conditions to consumers.
in writing. - this report aims to ensure fair and non-discriminatory access to the allocation of take-off and landing slots, at a time when congestion at european airports is becoming a real problem. the aim is therefore to optimise the allocation and use of slots by means of the 80-20 rule and the minimum size of a 5-week series as set out in the current legislation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions, including the european parliament, the council and the commission. the amounts from secondary time-span trade may be used to improve infrastructure and passenger services. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of this report, which is intended above all not to create any more obstacles for companies in areas facing a period of crisis.
in writing. − the objective expressed in this report is to ensure optimum allocation and use of slots at congested eu airports by proposing to strengthen slot allocation and use mechanisms and ensure their effective application, while promoting 'fair competition and stimulating competition between operators', aspects of which we are concerned about. the aim is to open up access to secondary time-span trade and to strengthen competition by integrating the allocation system into the reform of the european air traffic management system (the single european sky). the real aims of the single european sky are being obscured: national subordination, the reduction of the price of labour and the increase in profits for the large companies, a process with which we disagree. it is also suggested that a 'single european coordinator' associated with the time slot allocation process should be set up after the completion of the so-called 'single european sky'. the proposed amendments would allow airlines to sell slots they do not use and member states to introduce fines for carriers who return unused slots late, preventing new allocation.

in writing. - we have all had bad experiences with excessive noise. although humans have an enormous capacity for adaptation, particularly to noise, the truth is that their continued exposure to high decibel sounds causes serious and often irreparable injuries. the report by jörg leichtfried analyses the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the establishment of rules and procedures for the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at european union (eu) airports within a balanced approach and repealing directive 2002/30/ec of the european parliament and of the council. the aim of this regulation is to update the existing measures in order to improve the noise environment of those living near an airport. there are people complaining about chemical and noise pollution, especially from night flights. noise at airports is a serious problem that must be addressed urgently. according to the civil aviation organisation, within a few years, some five million people will be affected by airport noise in the eu.
in writing. the commission has put forward a proposal to establish rules and procedures for the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at airports. the stated objective is to respond to the protests of the populations living near airport areas. the fear of undermining the sacrosanct 'free competition' by introducing distortions in the market led the commission to call upon itself to 'control the decision on the restriction of operation before its application'. if the commission considers that the decision does not comply with the requirements of the regulation, it may even suspend the decision. we reject this solution, which is an intrusion into the competence of the member states, whose decisions must be made on the basis of assessments of the different impacts on the areas concerned. the report also mentions cost-effectiveness as an aspect to be taken into account in the assessment of noise pollution at airports, weighing the economic benefits and the impact on people's health and quality of life, including a new concept of the overall efficiency of operating restrictions. it is an approach which we also reject. for these reasons we voted against.
in writing. − the purpose of this proposal is to update existing measures to enable local authorities to improve the noise environment around union airports, within the framework of the icao's international balanced approach to noise management. the balanced approach must be applied consistently. the balanced approach covers the full range of noise mitigation measures: 1) reduction at the source of aircraft noise; 2) land-use planning and management measures; 3) operational noise reduction procedures (using runways, routes or specific procedures) and 4) operating restrictions. the economic benefits and the impact on the health and quality of life of people living in the vicinity of airports should also be considered when assessing noise pollution at eu airports.

in writing. - the protection of animals during transport has been a subject of debate in the european parliament since the 1970s. we agree on the importance of ensuring the protection and welfare of animals during transport. as the report acknowledges, the transport of meat and other products derived from it is preferable to the transport of live animals for the sole purpose of being slaughtered, whether for ethical reasons or for technical reasons. it is also recognised that animals should, in principle, be slaughtered as close as possible to their place of rearing, reducing as far as possible long-distance transport. these principles are called into question by the systematic closure of farms and slaughterhouses, most of which are small, especially in the more isolated regions (the interior of portugal is a good example), concentrating them in large population centres, progressively more distant from the place of production. the existence of these essential infrastructures ensures not only better product quality but also that a greater proportion of the added value generated in the chain remains in the regions of origin, generating jobs and enhancing local production. in addition, of course, to better observance of animal welfare principles.

in writing. − the union is founded on a community of values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, solidarity, the rule of law and respect for human rights, for all persons living in the territory of the european union, including those belonging to minorities, stateless persons and persons temporarily or illegally on its territory. the protection of fundamental rights should be an overarching objective of all eu policies, including in its external dimension. the obligation to protect, promote and fulfil fundamental rights requires an institutional commitment through the development and strengthening of a genuine culture around them. it is therefore necessary for the institutions to assume fully their responsibilities for the full and proper implementation of the mandate and competences of the european union in this area, in particular on the basis of the charter of fundamental rights. while it considers the report to be generally positive, it contains some controversial points which are relevant to the principle of subsidiarity. for the reasons i have given, i abstained from voting on this document.
in writing. − the situation of fundamental rights in the european union (2010 and 2011) is examined in this report through the exhaustive analysis of the proper application of the charter of fundamental rights by the commission, the council and the member states. it is important to note that this charter was formally adopted in nice in december 2000 and fell far short of the rights guaranteed in the european convention for the protection of human rights and the european social charter, in particular as regards economic, social and cultural rights. in view of the current structural crisis of capitalism and its impact on the people, their rights and freedoms, it is contradictory that the report calls for 'an urgent strengthening of the european mechanisms guaranteeing respect for democracy and the rule of law' while at the same time gradually removing one of the fundamental pillars of a democratic state, its sovereignty. but if the aim of the report is to appeal for the defence of rights, it would be better if the meps of the majority in the ep did not constantly approve political lines of 'budgetary consolidation' which, in the portuguese case, call into question the rights enshrined in the constitution of the portuguese republic.
rapporteur. − mr president, i will first say a few words in english before i pass on to my mother tongue, portuguese, because i want to offer my condolences in my name, but i believe also in the name economists but also to students of political science. he was a theoretician of development; the first economist to show that development was not growth – and i think that is interesting for our colleagues in the committee on development – but even before he wrote his main books he was an anti-fascist freedom fighter in the spanish civil war and during world war two. one of the founders, with a writer. - mr president, looking ahead to the economic situation of the economic and monetary union in 2013 is an exercise that must be done with truth and objectivity. self-justification and ideology cannot overcome the toughness of numbers. since 2008 we have been trying to combat the crisis and since 2010 strong policies of so-called consolidation and discipline are being applied, particularly violently, in the weakest economies. we've got results today. the forecast a year earlier was for greece to grow by 0,7% in 2011. it ended with a recession of -6.9%. portugal has scrupulously complied with the troika's recommendations, with growth expected to be 0.7% in 2011. it ended with a recession of -1.7%. as we predicted two years ago, synchronised austerity policies, covering countries with surpluses by choice and deficit countries by obligation, do not generate fiscal consolidation. they set off a general recessive spiral. little by little, even the strongest economies are slowing down and the eurozone, which this year was expecting growth of 0.5%, will end the year in full recession, with a loss of wealth of -0.4%. unemployment affects 25 million citizens, young people are desperate and, in the face of constant errors in forecasts, citizens do not believe that the sacrifices are worthwhile. enough experimentation, first of all, we must change the speech of sin in some and virtue in others. we all now recognise that there are missing pieces in the architecture of economic and monetary union. we are on the way to fulfilling them, but we must revised, the consolidation deadlines must be extended, budgetary consolidation must be done. but it must be realistic, made with interest rates reduced to the bare minimum and which do not include remuneration for those who finance the countries. when an economy goes into recession, the dose of austerity has to be adjusted, it has to be reduced, and european legislation allows that to be done. been done. the situation is too serious and this seriousness, the unemployment, the loss of prospects, requires us to seriously review the recipes we have been following.

in writing. − tatjana ždanoka presents us with a recommendation on the draft council decision establishing a multiannual framework for the european union agency for fundamental rights (fra) for the period 2013 to 2017. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union states in article 1 that 'the dignity of the human being is inviolable'. it must be respected and protected. as this is the flag of the european union (eu), it is essential that the institution responsible for monitoring compliance with this principle in the member states be equipped with the means to operate. adfue has done commendable work, particularly in the integration of the roma community and against discrimination against gays, lesbians, bisexuals, transsexuals and transgender people (lgbt). the proposed multiannual framework for the five-year period 2013-2017 is proving difficult to negotiate because the council, instead of accepting the inclusion of new areas such as the monitoring of the rights of persons with disabilities, intends to reduce competences.
in writing. − a coherent and consistent policy in the defence, promotion and enhancement of fundamental rights is developed in a transversal way and should preside over all policy actions and proposals. but the eu's actions and policies are the opposite of this logic, and run counter to the interests and aspirations of workers and people, as the situation in portugal today shows. these are policies that infringe on the fundamental rights of citizens, in particular the rights contained in the universal declaration of human rights and, in the case of portugal, the rights enshrined in the constitution of the republic (which adopts the former). the eu charter of fundamental rights, when compared with these two documents, has a restrictive and impoverished view of these rights. the definition of the thematic areas for the agency's work programmes expresses a very minimalistic view of what fundamental rights are. it expresses a hierarchical and separating view of civil liberties and social rights, in order to weaken and manipulate the indivisible and universal character of fundamental rights. it advocates a minimalist "democracy" based on formal processes and stripped of effective informed and enlightened participation, disregarding national sovereignty and the right of peoples to self-determination.
in writing. − this report aims to approve the new multiannual framework for the eu fundamental rights agency for the period 2013-2017. multiple stakeholders were involved in the consultation process during the preparation of the new multiannual framework. from july to september 2011, all the bodies participating in the platform for fundamental rights were consulted, namely 108 bodies. most bodies support the work of the agency in the current thematic areas and the continuation of its activities, in particular in the areas of discrimination, asylum and migration, racism and xenophobia and access to justice. there was strong support for the agency's future work in the field of social rights and social security. several bodies have highlighted, amongst the additional areas to be prioritised, the rights of persons with disabilities and the importance of intensifying work in the policy areas of the former 'third pillar'. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the european union agency for fundamental rights started its work on 1 march 2007. the multiannual framework presented is not very ambitious. i voted in favour of this report which asks the commission to assess and propose the revision of the agency's tasks, areas of activity and working methods for 2013 in order to ensure effective monitoring and implementation of the eu charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. − the multiannual framework of the eu fundamental rights agency expires at the end of 2012, and it is therefore necessary to determine the thematic areas of the agency's activity by defining a framework for this purpose, which provides for the work programme. i agree with the proposal for the future multiannual framework, where the rapporteur not only proposes to continue current efforts in the areas of discrimination, asylum and migration, racism and xenophobia, but also considers the introduction of access to justice and, in this respect, the inclusion of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the list of thematic areas of the multiannual framework of fundamental rights. the council should therefore be urged to explicitly declare the inclusion of these areas in the agency's framework of intervention in order to ensure the full protection of fundamental rights in the eu as provided for in the lisbon treaty.
in writing. − on 15 february 2007, the council adopted regulation (ec) no 168/2007 which established the european union agency for fundamental rights. the agency started its operations on 1 march 2007. the current multiannual framework expires at the end of 2012. this proposal aims to establish the multiannual framework of the agency for the period 2013 to 2017 as provided for in article 5 of the regulation. in the coming period, the agency needs to focus on new thematic areas to ensure the continuity of its activities. the european parliament therefore expects the commission to assess and propose a revision of the agency's tasks, areas of activity and working methods for 2013 in order to ensure effective monitoring and implementation of the charter of fundamental rights. in addition, the council will need to give its consent to the inclusion of the areas of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the list of thematic areas. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - we do not share the concept of fundamental rights which is associated with eu policy in this area, namely the eu charter of fundamental rights, and which enshrines a loss of rights compared to that laid down in the constitution of the portuguese republic. we do not share the need or the political assumptions for the creation of an eu fundamental rights agency. in our view, a coherent and consistent policy for the defence, promotion and enhancement of fundamental rights is developed in a transversal way and should preside over all political actions and proposals. the action and proposal of the majority of the ep, as well as of the eu in general, are at the opposite end of this logic, deepening more and more policies which are contrary to the interests and aspirations of the workers and the people as evidenced in the situation in portugal. the definition of the thematic areas for the agency's work programmes expresses a very minimalistic view of what fundamental rights are. it expresses a hierarchical and separating view of civil liberties and social rights, in order to weaken and manipulate the indivisible and universal character of fundamental rights. it advocates a minimalist "democracy" based on formal processes and stripped of national sovereignty and the right of peoples to self-determination.
in writing. - i support this report because i support the distinction between written statements which are not legislative in nature and written statements which have a major impact or concern an interesting or important solution. i think it should be clear to parliament that the primary focus must be on its legislative role, and obviously, as is already the case under european law, statements on non-legislative proposals can be used to initiate a legislative proposal, as under the right of initiative that the european parliament has, with at least 10 members from three political groups.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the amendments to rules 123 and 42 of parliament's rules of procedure.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur's proposal to restrict the possibility of members making written statements. i do not deny the usefulness of statements, but i think their use should be rationalised and the terms in which they can be effectively promoted better defined. if this figure made sense in a house devoid of significant legislative powers, i believe it will do much less today, given the current wide and diverse framework of european parliamentary powers, which must be fully exercised by its members. i therefore welcome this initiative to define better the contours of a regimental figure which, for the most part, had no practical consequences and i hope that this definition will strengthen its future effectiveness and importance.
in writing. - the european union (eu) is an area of peace, freedom, justice and democracy. among the european institutions, the european parliament, given its pluralism, is the one in which citizens place their greatest trust. it is not surprising, then, that the committee on petitions has been successful. the report under discussion, drawn up by rafał trzaskowski on behalf of the committee on constitutional affairs, concerns the amendment of rule 123 (written declarations) and rule 42 (initiative pursuant to article 225 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union) of the rules of procedure of the european parliament. the european parliament (ep) whose members are elected by direct universal suffrage has seen its powers extended, particularly since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon (teu), thanks to the new co-decision methodology, which allows it to influence the decision-making process within the eu. meps can use written statements to defend the interests of their constituents, the best way for a member to ask the european institutions and their bodies for explanations.
in writing. - the possibility of a written statement 'being delivered by a maximum of five members' being replaced by the possibility of it being delivered 'by a minimum of 10 members from at least three political groups' is a loss of a right of members and groups like ours. the loss of democratic rights is something we must strongly criticise and vote against. to withdraw the members' powers of intervention is to withdraw the power of intervention and political action of the people who elected them. and to force at least 10 members of parliament from at least three political groups to submit a written declaration is a blatant attempt to reconcile the irreconcilable (class) interests of the different political groups. these amendments seek above all to condition the action of political groups which, like ours, are the bearers of proposals which are truly alternative to this eu of big capital and the big powers. step by step, the majority of the ep is creating rules that limit or prevent the action of our group, limit or prevent the democratic right of the representatives of the interests of the workers, to eliminate contradictions and impose the agenda of interests of the eu monopolies.
in writing. − the adoption of this report is intended to propose amendments to the presentation of written declarations and legislative initiatives. we hope that these amendments will give greater impact and visibility to such initiatives, which are mostly concerned with matters of public interest.
in writing. - written declarations have a very limited impact on both the agendas and the decisions taken by the institutions and can give a misleading impression of their effectiveness. in addition, some of the issues addressed in the written declarations do not have parliamentary dignity, and sometimes they seem to be more aimed at self-promotion to the detriment of the european construction project than they should be a separate instrument. however, when used properly, they continue to be valuable as a tool of popular campaigning. proposals calling for legislative action give each member an opportunity to influence union legislation and to incorporate a particular proposal into the work of parliamentary committees. i voted in favour of this report, which amends the rules of procedure of the european parliament to make written declarations and proposals for legislation more effective.
in writing. − while it is true that written declarations retain some usefulness, the truth is that, in the face of the increase in the strengthening of the european parliament's powers and the recent introduction of the european union citizens' initiative, their importance is considerably diminished. in this respect, the introduction of these amendments to the rules of procedure, which are essentially aimed at restricting their use and ensuring that they are properly handled and followed up by the institutions to which they are addressed, is to be welcomed. in particular, the amendments to rule 123 (1) of the rules of procedure are noteworthy, which set more stringent requirements for the submission of written statements (minimum of 10 members from at least three political groups) and specify that such statements must concern matters of exclusive competence of the eu and cannot call for legislative action, contain decisions on matters for which the rules of procedure provide specific procedures and competence and/or address matters relating to procedures already in progress.
in writing. - the possibility of a written statement 'being delivered by a maximum of five members' being replaced by the possibility of it being delivered 'by a minimum of 10 members from at least three political groups' is a loss of a right of members and groups like ours. the loss of democratic rights is something we must strongly criticise and vote against. to withdraw the members' powers of intervention is to withdraw the power of intervention and political action of the people who elected them. and to force at least 10 members of parliament from at least three political groups to submit a written declaration is a blatant attempt to reconcile the irreconcilable (class) interests of the different political groups. these amendments seek above all to condition the action of political groups which, like ours, are the bearers of proposals which are truly alternative to this eu of big capital and the big powers. this is how democracy within the rules of the ep has various conditions and limitations which the majority of this parliament corroborates and elaborates.
in writing. − i approve this report, welcoming the contributions made to the need to strengthen the european union's human rights policy and to speak with one voice, the promotion of key parameters in the framework of industrial relations under free trade agreements, greater control over exports, transfers, stock exchanges and transit of dual-use items. i also agree with the direction to call on member states to put an end to discrimination and intolerance in all areas, including gender, race, age or sexual orientation, religion or belief. finally, the protection of the rights of women and children must be given priority in european policies. despite these advances, i think that more can be done, notably in the areas of trade unions, the role of the european union after a high status at the united nations, the need for the european union to speak with one voice, the establishment of regional human rights offices and the prevention of maternal morbidity and mortality.

in writing. - it is very important that the european parliament does not give up its assessment of democracy and human rights in the world and of the european union's action, and that it is as objective as possible. the european union has played a decisive role in promoting these values, demonstrating that it does not only want to ensure that they are respected internally, but rather that it believes in their non-blocking character and the need to ensure that they are also adopted and pursued externally in order to ensure freedom, security and the right to expression and political participation for other populations and to abandon the death penalty and torture. the calls for coherence in the policies developed, for efficiency in action and for the good use of human and material resources in their service are not new. i believe that much remains to be done, but that significant steps are being taken to ensure improved results. the union delegations in third countries are of fundamental importance in this respect. i regret that the rapporteur has used his position to advocate policies which are not even consensual in european terms.
in writing. - respect for human rights has been the issue most addressed by this parliament, which does not hesitate to condemn, whether in europe or in any other part of the world, all those who violate these rights. the european parliament (ep) has been publishing reports on this subject for more than ten years. the european parliament has adopted several resolutions condemning the agreement, and in all cooperation agreements with third countries where these rights are not respected or where there is suspicion of a breach, a safeguard clause is always included providing for the denunciation of the agreement for disregard of human rights and the primacy of democracy. i would like to commend the work done by the commission in this area, in particular the work of the high representative of the european union for foreign affairs and security policy and vice-president of the european commission, catherine ashton, who has been involved in contacts in the defence of human rights and the implementation of democracy in the world. despite this effort by the eu, much remains to be done. as an example, i refer to the cases of the civil war in syria, the conflict between palestine and israel, the lack of respect for minorities, the existence of the death penalty, etc.
in writing. - in our parliamentary intervention, we have frequently denounced the apparent contradiction between the recurrent discourse of the eu and its institutions, which seem to be concerned with human rights, and the instrumental character they attribute to it, with a view to the implementation of a policy of neo-colonial contours. a policy of exploitation of labour and domination of markets and natural resources. let the people of libya, syria, iraq and afghanistan say so, who are seeing their countries destroyed and their living conditions increasingly degraded by military aggression that hypocritically invokes democracy, the 'responsibility to protect' and the 'defence of human rights'. let the workers and the portuguese people say so, who feel the brutal violence of the policy being imposed on them, being denied their right to work, education, health and housing. the instruments referred to in the report are not new. the intention is to give them greater articulation and effectiveness in denying the right of peoples to progress, social justice, peace and self-determination. if necessary, by imposing collaborative schemes with eu interests.
in writing. − the annual report on human rights and democracy should be an important tool for communicating the eu's work in this area and help to improve the visibility of eu action in this area. it would be important in the future that the hr/vp, when preparing future annual reports, actively and systematically consult parliament and report back to parliament on how parliament's resolutions have been taken into account. the adoption of the eu strategic framework on human rights on 25 june 2012 was important. it is now time for the eu institutions to work together to ensure its proper implementation and thus credibly deliver on the commitment enshrined in the eu treaty to pursue external policies based on human rights, democratic values and the rule of law, with respect for the principles, without any doubt of the eu's important role in the world.

in writing. − the european parliament welcomed the adoption of the eu annual report on human rights and democracy in the world in 2011, which it sees as an important tool for communicating and making the eu's work in this area visible. the support for eu action in the united nations and eu policy on international criminal justice and the fight against impunity is noteworthy. in addition, the union's action in the field of humanitarian law, the european neighbourhood policy and support for democratization and elections are mentioned. human rights dialogues with third countries, as well as human rights and democracy clauses in eu agreements, freedom of expression and thought, religion, conscience or belief, and eu support for civil society and human rights defenders are also addressed in the document. the eu action against the death penalty, torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, against discrimination against women and children in situations of armed conflict, and for the rights of women and children are also mentioned. i therefore voted in favour of the document.
