in writing. − i approve this report and welcome the strategic framework and action plan, which aims to improve the effectiveness and consistency of the european union's human rights policy. i would also like to stress the role of the european parliament in its implementation, with its new role in the context of the reformulation of this policy and its strategic framework. i believe that the strategic framework should insist on the universality of human rights, the promotion of human rights in the european union's external policies and their implementation, and the union's future work with bilateral partners, in multinational institutions and in its own institutions to promote human rights. i also think that we should learn from past lessons, such as the arab spring, which demonstrated the ineffectiveness of the european union's foreign policy and the clear need to involve more actors and players in its dialogues and negotiations, in addition to the official authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider that: the universal human rights and freedoms as set out in the universal declaration of human rights apply to all human beings, irrespective of any circumstance or situation, religion or belief, sex, racial or ethnic origin, age, disability, sexual orientation and gender identity; the strategic framework and the action plan form the basis of the eu's human rights policy; eu member states must take a firm and coherent approach to human rights violations worldwide.
in writing. − the member states of the european union have a long experience of implementing and defending human rights. the european union must take advantage of this experience and ensure that its positions do not conflict with the concrete legal systems of the member states, let alone that certain interpretations of human rights are used to subvert or condition them. that said, i believe that the greatest possible consistency is needed in the way european policies and actions on this subject are perceived externally and that it is advantageous to have closer coordination with the member states when designing and implementing them. the creation of the post of european union special representative for human rights could play an important role in this. the european union must put human rights at the heart of its external action. it will benefit from being developed in close contact with those on the ground who promote its agenda without such contact implying confusion of roles or reciprocal instrumentalisation.
in writing. - "the dignity of the human being is inviolable. it must be respected and protected.' human rights are at the heart of the creation of the european union (eu). the recognition we have achieved in the world, embodied in the award of the nobel peace prize 2012, makes us even more responsible. not only within the eu, but also beyond our borders. we cannot remain indifferent to reports of certain human rights violations, such as the use of the death penalty, female genital mutilation, women who are divorced and stoned for committing adultery, honour killings and the persecution of ethnic and religious minorities. i therefore welcome the appointment of a human rights representative, and i wish him the best possible performance.
in writing. − this report on the review of the eu's human rights strategy does not, unfortunately, avoid the eu's traditional instrumental and restrictive approach to human rights issues. it is instrumental because it often invokes human rights to justify the pursuit of economic, political and geostrategic objectives and because it is based on a hypocritical policy of double standards, as was made clear this week with the approval of the agreement with colombia or as is clear in the face of complacency and complicity in the systematic violations of human rights committed by the state of israel. just to give two examples. restrictive because it gives rise to a hierarchical view of human rights, with the division between civil liberties and social rights, which results in a regression in the universal and indivisible character of the human rights it claims to defend. despite the mild and even mystifying references to the internal situation of the eu countries, the lack of criticism of the imposition of the ongoing civilizational regression in the eu prevails.
in writing. − the eu is founded on the principle of respect for human rights and has a legal obligation, laid down in its treaties, to ensure that all eu and member state policies, without exception, as well as all international agreements, focus on human rights. dialogues between the eu, its member states and third countries must be preceded by concrete measures designed to ensure that human rights remain at the heart of eu policies. despite the crisis we are going through, we cannot forget that the defence of human rights is part of the eu's dna.

in writing. − eu intervention must be guided by the legal obligation, laid down in its treaties, to ensure that all policies of the union and the member states, as well as all international agreements it concludes, focus on human rights. this reverence for the quality of human dignity that is at the very genesis of the eu has led to a series of instruments aimed at establishing a policy framework that supports the obligation described. unfortunately, the multiplicity of such instruments has resulted in a fragmented approach which today jeopardises the implementation of a coherent framework for all eu actions. the report therefore considers the need for a strategic framework and the related action plan, which should be given sufficient visibility in order to increase its legitimacy, credibility and accountability to citizens, and be able to define the agreed guidelines, instruments and positions and the various financial instruments, in particular the european instrument for democracy and human rights, of the eu human rights strategy.
in writing. − the report highlights the importance of coherence and cooperation between the european union and the member states in the field of human rights policy. in this respect, the key role played by national strategies and the importance of their being communicated to members of the european parliament should be emphasised. parliament also called for human rights clauses to be an integral part of agreements concluded by the union with third countries, insisting on the need to assess their potential impact on human rights in those countries before the negotiations. the european parliament also advocates a new european neighbourhood policy which puts the spotlight on young people and civil society. for these reasons, and because effective institutional cooperation on this matter is recommended, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - this report advocates the deepening of a hypocritical and instrumental policy of interference, pressure, aggression and war developed by the major powers of the eu and nato. although we find some contradictions in the report, a hierarchical view of human rights prevails, with the division between civil liberties and social rights, which translates into a regression in the universal and indivisible character of the human rights it claims to defend. despite the mild and even mystifying references to the internal situation of the eu countries, there is a lack of criticism of the imposition of policies aimed at a civilizational setback in the human rights of workers and peoples in countries such as portugal. the myth of introducing clauses for the 'defence of human rights' in free trade agreements prevails, when it is known and acknowledged that the implementation of these agreements has led to the greatest pressures and the destruction of human rights. the eu's interests are being undermined by interference - and the possibility of military aggression - in internal processes, which deny the peoples' right to self-determination. the prevailing interest is to impose collaborative regimes with the eu's neo-colonial interests in domination of the labour force, natural resources and markets on which the eu's monopolies depend.

in writing. - russia is a strategic partner for the eu with which it has several trade agreements. its accession to the world trade organisation (wto) after almost two decades of negotiations, which was formalised on 22 august, has strengthened multilateral trade and, at the same time, committed it to a number of wto principles and laws. although early steps indicated that russia was on the right track toward a truly democratic state, the truth is that it has not. and like the rapporteur, i too am disappointed by the lack of democracy in russia. the last elections were marred by many irregularities, they cannot be considered free and fair, non-governmental organisations are prevented from carrying out their work and accused of being agents of foreign interests, the ministers of the interior and justice refuse to engage in dialogue and there are several allegations of human rights violations. the good eu-russia relationship is not at stake, but a new agreement must require a shared set of principles in terms of defence, strategic vision and human rights.

in writing. - i approve this resolution, beginning by expressing my deep concern at the israeli government's announcement of the construction of some 3 000 new housing units in the west bank, including east jerusalem. i think that this expansion may call into question the prospects of a viable palestine with jerusalem as the shared capital between palestine and israel, and that in the light of international law, israeli settlements in the west bank and east jerusalem are illegal. i therefore call for an immediate, total and permanent halt to israeli settlement building and expansion activities and for a halt to further orders to evict palestinian families and to demolish palestinian homes. i also condemn the statements by the political leader of hamas, khaled meshaal, who rejects the recognition of the state of israel and clearly rejects any israeli presence in jerusalem, and i call on hamas to recognize israel's right to exist.
in writing. - i have just recently expressed my deep regret for the victims of a conflict which threatens to continue unless two conditions are met: the security of the state of israel and its inalienable right to protect its population, on the one hand, and the right of the palestinian people to build their own state peacefully and freely, on the other. the expansion of settlements in the west bank calls into question the construction of a palestinian state and does nothing to contribute to the security of israel and its population. i would like the israeli authorities to reconsider their attitude to approving new construction and to return to negotiations as a matter of urgency. i would remind you that the portuguese government recently supported the recognition of palestine as an observer state in the united nations in order to give it the means to seek political solutions to its problems. just as this decision puts greater responsibility on the shoulders of the palestinian authorities, so international support for israel's freedom and security requires that its representatives be prepared to take concrete steps towards peace.
in writing. - there are many aspects of this resolution which we value. we stress the denunciation of the announced expansion of settlements by israel in east jerusalem, as well as the recognition of the illegality of the settlements and the "call" for their "immediate, total and permanent suspension". we also stress the denunciation of the israeli government's withholding of palestinian tax revenues and the 'request' for their immediate transfer. the approach adopted is, however, condescending towards the israeli authorities - which we regret. it is incomprehensible that there has been no firm and consistent condemnation of the continued violations of the most elementary rights of the palestinian people. it is incomprehensible that it does not mention, even once, that these actions constitute an intolerable retaliation by the israeli authorities for the recognition of palestine as a non-member observer state of the un. successive un resolutions have recognised the national rights of the palestinian people, in particular the right to the establishment of a sovereign and independent state of palestine within the pre-1967 borders, with east jerusalem as its capital. they demand the end and dismantling of all settlements and the separation wall, the right of return of all palestinian refugees to their homeland and compensation for the palestinian people for more than six decades of occupation. all this should be included in this resolution.
in writing. − for the very important resumption of direct israeli-palestinian peace talks to take place, all parties must avoid taking any unilateral steps that could compromise or hamper peace efforts. we must encourage the parties involved to settle all outstanding financial disputes under eu mediation. the statement by the political leader of hamas, khaled meshaal, that he rejects the recognition of the state of israel is to be condemned: hamas must recognize the right of israel to exist and to palestinian reconciliation. as long as palestinian leaders maintain this stance, it will be very difficult to find a path to full peace in this sacrificed region of the globe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the palestinian authority and the israeli government to relaunch the middle east peace process.
in writing. − having regard to the fact that on 2 december 2012 the israeli government announced its intention to build some 3 000 new settler houses in the west bank and east jerusalem, the european parliament expressed its deep concern at this announcement, stressing that this expansion could jeopardise the prospects for a viable palestine with jerusalem as the shared capital between palestine and israel. the joint resolution by the various political groups in the european parliament also stresses that israeli settlements in the west bank and east jerusalem are illegal under international law and calls for an immediate, total and permanent suspension of israeli settlement building and expansion activities and for the enforcement of new orders to evict palestinian families and demolish palestinian homes.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information and communication networks, including the european information and communication networks (eics). we also stress the denunciation of the israeli government's withholding of palestinian tax revenues and the 'request' for their immediate transfer. the language used is, however, quite condescending towards the israeli authorities. it is incomprehensible that these actions by israel are not expressly condemned. it is incomprehensible that it does not mention once that these actions are a revenge by the israeli authorities for the approval by the un general assembly of the status of a non-member observer state of the united nations, which are actions revealing the disregard with which israel continues to vote on successive un resolutions which recognize the national rights of the palestinian people, namely the right to the establishment of the state of palestine, sovereign and independent, in the pre-1967 borders, with its capital in east jerusalem. resolutions calling for the end and dismantling of all settlements and the separation wall, the right of return of all palestinian refugees to their homeland and compensation for the palestinian people for more than six decades of occupation.
in writing. - i approve this resolution calling on the ukrainian authorities to investigate the problems that occurred during the elections and the cases of violation of electoral law. i think it is urgent that the president of ukraine, the government and parliament step up and strengthen the process of modernisation and reform in order to bring the country closer to the parameters of the european union, stressing that many of these reforms can be done in cooperation between ukraine and the european union. i think that the european union has always shown its clear intention to associate itself politically with ukraine, and that ukraine should therefore give the same signal with the reforms it is calling for.
in writing. - ukraine is one of the most important centres of slavic culture and history, an inseparable part of european history and culture as a whole. the fact that a significant ukrainian community has settled in portugal, and lives and works there, has helped to make the country's political life less distant and the geostrategic issues affecting it more perceptible even to those who view them from the other end of europe. if we are to support ukraine's desire to converge with the european union and to see that country as a potential partner, we must nevertheless promote internal changes and reforms that will enable it to establish itself firmly as a democratic state governed by the rule of law. i hope once again that ukraine will demonstrate in practice its effective adherence to the values, principles and ideals which guide the life and action of the european union.
in writing. - we are faced with yet another regrettable exercise of interference, denoting the unconfessed aims of domination and control of a region and a country of great importance, for well-known reasons of a geostrategic nature. if the 'orange wave' were the political force most aligned with the interests of the major eu powers, the reaction would certainly be quite different. but it wasn't. the european parliament now calls for 'improvement of the electoral code of ukraine'. the epp's weak reactionarism (of bad memory) and primary anti-communism is highlighted in its attempt to introduce an amendment to the text of the resolution calling on the elected 'pro-democratic' parties not to establish links or agreements with the communist party of ukraine (which got almost 15% of the votes). as at other times in history, attempts are being made to criminalize the struggle against oppression and exploitation, the struggle for democracy and freedom, of which the communist ideal is the highest expression, with the help of a few little words. the political heirs (of various shades) of the former 'black shirts' feel, at bottom, the same threat as their predecessors. the threat that the struggle for social justice poses to the maintenance of the unjust and unjust social order that they defend and that sustains them. they won't get through!
in writing. − effective cooperation between ukraine and the european union can only be developed on the basis of a clear will on the part of the ukrainian authorities to introduce and implement the necessary reforms, in particular the reform of the legal and judicial system, aiming at full adherence to the principles of democracy and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, minority rights and the rule of law. the institutions of the european union, the council of europe and the venice commission need to give active and effective support to this reform process. ukraine should put an end to the practice of selective administration of justice at all levels of administration and allow opposition parties to participate in political life on equal terms. the political opponents targeted by the persecution, including yulia timoshenko and yuri lutsenko, must be released and rehabilitated.
in writing. − the neighbourhood policy is part of the union project. in this resolution, which i vote for, i welcome the signing of the amended visa facilitation agreement between the european union and ukraine, which introduces clear improvements to the issuing of visas to ukrainian citizens compared to the agreement currently in force.
in writing. − the elections held on 28 october 2012 in ukraine were marred by allegations of electoral irregularities by several international bodies, including the osce and the report of the european parliament's election observation delegation in that country. i therefore consider the recommendations made by the european parliament to be important in the attempt to achieve a genuine rule of law, in which the judiciary is independent of the political power and the public administration fulfils its objectives of the common good of ukrainian society. it is therefore essential that the union reinforce its engagement in relations with ukraine with a view to deriving comparative advantages and actions that benefit ukrainian citizens. the question of visa liberalization is an example of a measure which should be on the negotiating table.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the country. it would be interesting to see if the ep would have made this issue as visible if it had been the political force of the so-called 'orange revolution', more aligned with the eu's economic interests, that won the elections. the eu is also calling for the abolition of the death penalty in all eu countries. the epp also tried - and failed - to include an oral amendment urging the elected 'pro-democracy' parties not to establish links or agreements with the communist party of ukraine (which won almost 15% of the vote), similar to the reference to the fascist svoboda party in the resolution's base text. it is yet another attempt by forces in the european parliament to try to equate communism with fascism and to criminalise communist forces. when communists and their liberating ideal are criminalised, democracy and the freedom to choose an alternative project to capitalism are condemned, and the eu will thus be the most undemocratic example in the world.
in writing. - i approve this resolution, reiterating my full support for the future accession of albania to the european union and sharing the commission's assessment of this country, which argues that it should be granted the status of candidate country, provided that it meets the objectives of the planned reforms in the areas of justice, public administration and with regard to the revision of the rules and procedures of the national parliament. i also stress the importance of the forthcoming elections, so that they are conducted in a free and fair manner, which will be a true test of the maturity of democracy in albania and a demonstration of the ability of the political forces to embark on a european agenda for the country. i therefore call on the council to grant the status of candidate country to albania without delay, subject to the fulfilment of the key reforms which must be carried out more easily with greater inter-party cooperation involving the opposition and the government.
in writing. - albania is geographically, historically and culturally part of europe. the eu has also been active in the fight against terrorism, and has been active in the fight against organised crime. but before that happens, albania will have to carry out structural reforms in the areas of public administration and justice, which are being implemented by the country step by step, and this is to be welcomed. the albanian political forces must continue to adopt reforms for the benefit of their citizens, through constructive dialogue (essential in democracy), in order for the country to move forward on the path to accession. the albanian people must understand that democracy and the rule of law are the two main standards of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the authorities need to take further measures to ensure full independence, transparency, freedom of expression, judicial efficiency, fight against corruption and abuse of public funds. i hope that albania will continue to progress and to develop good neighbourly relations, particularly with the balkan countries. i urge the albanian government to take steps to solve the problem of unemployment and extreme poverty and to compensate former political prisoners. i believe that albania will soon be able to meet the conditions necessary for membership of the union.
in writing. − in 2010, i warned of the political crisis in albania, which threatened to undermine the reforms undertaken in the meantime and which were largely aimed at a growing rapprochement with the european union, and expressed my doubts about the few guarantees given by that country as regards respect for the rule of law and individual freedoms. more than two years later, i acknowledge that the situation has improved since the agreement of november 2011. i welcome the reforms undertaken and the efforts made. despite this improvement and the 'european path' that the government and opposition say they want to follow, it must be said that much remains to be done before we can judge albania fit to join the union. i wish that would happen.
in writing. − albania is a country of significant geostrategic importance as it is situated on the periphery of europe but with strong links to the middle east and asia via the hellenic peninsula. during 2012, he chaired the council of ministers of the council of europe, which allowed him to increase credibility among the member states. albania's governments have expressed their intention to join the european union (eu), and in 2010 a set of reforms were established that albania should undertake in order to be granted the status of a candidate country for accession. the 2011 monitoring report concluded that four priorities were met and is about to conclude two more. relations between the government and the opposition improved, the immunity of high-level officials and judges was lifted, and various reforms were initiated in order to transition to democracy. although much remains to be done to achieve political maturity, particularly in the fight against corruption, organised crime, tax fraud and evasion, i congratulate the albanian people on the progress made and urge the government to continue the reforms under way towards full eu integration.
in writing. - this resolution is not very different from other resolutions on the applicant countries. they share a common matrix: the imposition of the political, economic and social model that corresponds to the interests of the eu's powers and monopolies; the imposition of the state's conformity to the 'market economy', that is, to the rules of capitalist society. the implementation of the acquis communautaire is the eu's trojan horse, which requires full implementation by these countries. its implementation has led (and is increasingly leading) to the destruction of a very significant part of the national productive sectors of the countries which have joined the eu, paving the way for the domination of the monopolies of the great powers. it has forced the privatisation or dismantling of key public services, or the destruction of thousands of small and mediumsized enterprises and thousands of small and mediumsized farmers and the destruction of millions of jobs. the resolution makes little or no reference to the socioeconomic impacts and consequences of the implementation of the acquis communautaire and the measures needed to deal with it. although this assessment is critical, we hope that the sovereign right of the albanian people to decide - free from any outside interference or pressure - whether or not to join the eu will be respected. we abstained.
in writing. − countries seeking to join the union must demonstrate, at all stages of the accession process, their capacity to strengthen the practical implementation of the values on which the union is founded; establish and promote, from an early stage, the proper functioning of the institutions fundamental to democratic governance and the rule of law, from the national parliament to the government and the judiciary, including courts and prosecutors, as well as law enforcement agencies. the eu accession process should become a driving force for further reforms and the main factor in ensuring constructive and responsible cooperation between the country's political apparatus. since the november 2011 agreement between the ruling party and the opposition, clear progress has been made on the reform agenda. however, the remaining challenges must be met in order to move forward on the path to eu membership. albania, thanks to its reform efforts, and provided that the albanian people so wish, can move to the next stage of the accession process in 2012, i.e. to assume the status of a candidate country for accession, provided that it achieves the critical mass of concrete results in the main outstanding areas of the ongoing reforms.
in writing. - the determined efforts of the government and the opposition to cooperate on reforms after a long impasse are highlighted in this resolution, which i therefore vote in favour of.
in writing. − albania is located on the eastern edge of the balkan peninsula, covers an area of 28 748 km2 and has a population of approximately 3 million citizens. albania is implementing fundamental reforms in the areas of public administration and justice, revision of the parliament's rules of procedure, judicial reform and development of civil society-government dialogue. i am voting in favour of this motion because i believe that albania is making significant progress towards meeting the political criteria for accession to the european union.

in writing. - i support this resolution because i believe that the european parliament should strive for consensus on a common plan for the restructuring of the steel industry at european union level, improving its competitiveness. at the same plenary session we discussed requests for support from the european globalisation adjustment fund arising from the sharp decline in this sector, which is due to the collapse of the construction and manufacturing sectors as a result of the crisis. the steel sector, in my view, is just one of several sectors that are being adversely affected by the lack of competitiveness of the european single market. europe needs a strong steel industry, as the competitiveness of this sector reflects the competitiveness of various economic sectors.
in writing. the steel industry plays a central role in the economy and is the cornerstone of the development and creation of numerous industrial sectors, which are indispensable to economic and social well-being. the crisis of capitalism has aggravated the process of weakening the steel industry in several member states and the impact on the population has been devastating, particularly in regions that depend on this industrial sector and other downstream industries. it is worth recalling that in portugal, following accession to the eec, this important industrial sector was dismantled. this resolution not only fails to denounce the real culprits behind the present state of the steel industry in each member state and in europe, where privatisations of the sector have led to its real decline, but it insists on the same european policies which have determined the social and economic pit into which this industry has been pushed. the fundamental aspect that none of the resolutions that were voted on understood, and that the resolution proposed by our group advanced, is that, by means of 'financial market rules which destroy employment and the production apparatus', it is essential to demand the 'renationalization of the steel industry' and that 'only public control of the steel industry can guarantee both the future of the sector and the rights of workers'.
in writing. − eu steel exports reached 33.7 million tonnes in 2010 (worth €32 billion), with turkey, the us, algeria, switzerland, russia and india being the largest markets for these exports, while steel imports to the union in the same year amounted to 26.8 million tonnes (worth €18 billion), with russia, ukraine, china, turkey, south korea, switzerland and serbia being our largest suppliers. the current crisis is creating a huge social shortage for the regions and workers affected, and companies undergoing restructuring must act in a socially responsible manner, as experience has shown that successful restructuring has only been achieved through a lot of social dialogue. high-tech industries such as the steel sector are seen as a model of technological know-how and must therefore be protected by immediate action to prevent their relocation outside the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the commission to provide, in the short term, a clear picture of the situation with regard to the main changes in the steel industry in europe and to monitor closely the developments under way in order to safeguard europe's industrial heritage and the workforce involved.
in writing. the steel sector remains central to the economic growth of the european union. however, the recent economic and monetary crisis has also had a negative effect on demand for this sector, leading to increased unemployment in this sector and in most directly or indirectly associated sectors. the importance of the steel industry to the european economy requires the commission to take measures to ensure the security of energy supply and to avoid relocation outside the territory of the union. i welcome the commission's initiative to present an action plan as early as 2013, but i believe that a detailed analysis of the situation of the steel industry in europe should be made a priori in order to safeguard the technological heritage and the skilled workforce.
in writing. - the current crisis of capitalism has aggravated the process of weakening the steel industry in several member states and the impact on the population has been devastating, particularly in regions that depend on this industrial sector and other downstream industries. this resolution not only fails to denounce the real culprits behind the present state of the steel industry in each member state and in europe, where privatisations of the sector have led to its real decline, but it insists on the same european policies which have determined the social and economic pit into which this industry has been pushed. the fundamental aspect that none of the resolutions adopted included, and which our group's resolution advocated, is that it is essential to demand the 'renationalization of the steel industry' and that 'only public control of the steel industry can guarantee both the future of the sector and the rights of workers'. the resolution, which was tabled by the socialist and socialist group, also proposes solutions for 'the retraining and vocational retraining of workers' and the use of 'eu financial instruments such as the european social fund and the european globalisation adjustment fund', solutions for those who already anticipate more dismissals and relocations of companies.
in writing. - i approve this motion for a resolution, considering that the petitioners have strongly expressed their concerns regarding the extremely high levels of dioxin emissions from the ilva steel plant in taranto, which have had and continue to have a significant, harmful and lasting impact on the health of the local population. some 20 000 families have members who worked in the steel industry or in ancillary sectors and the contamination rates of the local population have led to unacceptable and intolerable levels of illness and chronic disease. and on the other hand, considering that the steel industry, which employs some 360 000 workers, is a crucial economic sector of the european union and that parliament has the duty and responsibility to openly express its solidarity with the workers of the ilva steelworks and their families who have borne the effects of this completely unacceptable situation, i urge the commission and the council to develop a new policy for the steel industry which will boost growth and employment in times of economic crisis and which is compatible with the health and safety of all citizens and residents of the european union.
in writing. - given the current economic context, the eu cannot afford to lose opportunities to create jobs. the commission must therefore develop a new policy for the steel industry that will boost growth and employment and is compatible with the health and safety of all eu citizens and residents. as regards the petition which gives rise to this proposal, its authors have strongly expressed their concern at the extremely high levels of dioxin emissions from the ilva steel plant in taranto, italy, which have had and continue to have a significant, harmful and lasting impact on the health of the local population. this has direct and indirect implications for 20,000 families whose members worked in the steel industry or in ancillary sectors and whose contamination rates of the local population have led to unacceptable and intolerable levels of illness and chronic disease. i believe that the ep should take a position urging the italian authorities to ensure, as a matter of urgency, the environmental rehabilitation of the polluted site of the steelworks for the sake of the environment, but also for the jobs involved.
in writing. the resolution under discussion, tabled by erminia mazzoni on behalf of the committee on petitions following a petition by an italian citizen, deals with the need for the european union to work towards developing a new steel industry which is sustainable and competitive. at eu level, the steel industry is a strategic sector employing some 360 000 people and in need of revitalisation. from the 1980s to the 1990s, due to the increase in energy and raw material costs, this industry entered a crisis. many companies have relocated to other regions, notably to the asian continent, and those that remain are struggling with financial problems that prevent them from modernising and being environmentally and financially sustainable. the case reported in the report of the ilva steel plant in taranto, italy, perfectly reflects the problems mentioned above: decapitalization, privatization, environmental pollution, closure and unemployment.
in writing. - this resolution is based on a petition received expressing concern about the extremely high levels of dioxin emissions from the ilva steel plant in taranto, italy. the document states that 20000 families have members working in the steel industry or in auxiliary sectors and that the contamination rates of the local population have led to an unacceptable increase in illnesses and chronic diseases. the resolution states that the precarious and dangerous condition of the factory has caused "critical environmental degradation and damage" as well as serious economic and social problems in southern italy. it also stressed that the privatisation of the steelworks had not led to any improvement in environmental or worker safety and that it was essential to prevent further relocations of steelworks and steel production units, ensuring 'the safety of the workforce'. the resolution calls on the italian authorities to ensure the environmental rehabilitation of the site polluted by the plant, which we believe is the right thing to do.
in writing. − it is important to develop a new policy for the steel industry that will boost growth and employment in times of economic crisis and is compatible with the health and safety of all eu citizens and residents. the commission and the council should seek to work together with all stakeholders to ensure that this policy achieves a coherent link between economic objectives and social and environmental priorities in order to build a modern, competitive and sustainable european steel industry in full compliance with eu environmental legislation.
in writing. − in this resolution, which i vote for, the european parliament calls on the commission and the council to work together with all the parties concerned to ensure that the union's industrial policy achieves a coherent link between economic objectives and social and environmental priorities, in order to build a modern, competitive and sustainable european steel industry, in full compliance with eu environmental legislation.
in writing. the steel industry is of the utmost importance for the competitiveness of the european union, especially in a recessionary context. several high-end sectors are directly associated with the steel industry and therefore the implications of a breakdown of the sector should be assessed. the strategy presented by the commission on the need for a new industrialisation policy for the union should take account of this sector and present measures and actions to provide leverage.
in writing. - this resolution follows a petition received expressing concern about the extremely high levels of dioxin emissions from the ilva steel plant in taranto, italy. the document states that 20000 families have members working in the steel industry or in auxiliary sectors and that the contamination rates of the local population have led to an unacceptable increase in chronic diseases. the resolution condemns the precarious and dangerous condition of the factory as having caused "critical environmental degradation and damage" as well as serious economic and social problems in southern italy. it added that the privatisation of the steelworks had not led to any improvement in environmental or worker safety and that it was essential to prevent further relocations of steelworks and steel production units, ensuring 'the safety of the workforce'. the resolution calls on the italian authorities to ensure the environmental rehabilitation of the site polluted by the plant, which we believe is the right thing to do. however, we think it is unacceptable to recommend that 'the costs of prevention and remediation be borne in accordance with the polluter pays principle', which exempts some from responsibility in this area.
